title: Gate baseline has no HEAD binding: a path committed then re-dirtied is silently subtracted from the bound change set
description:
The gate baseline records pre-existing dirt as PORCELAIN LINES with no binding to
the commit it was captured at. So a path that is committed and then re-dirtied
within one baseline generation is silently subtracted from the change set, and the
approval binds a set that omits it.

FOUND LIVE at the i8cx wave-1 gate, 2026-08-26, by QA before approving.

THE SEQUENCE (all three steps are ordinary)
 1. A baseline is captured while some paths are dirty. Here: captured at head
    6d0011f by the 6im2 approve, listing ` M .claude/scripts/qa-gate.sh`,
    ` M .claude/scripts/tests/run-tests.sh`, and 7 fixture qa-gate copies.
 2. Those paths are COMMITTED (ed45abe). The dirt is gone; the baseline still
    names the same porcelain lines.
 3. The next wave of work re-dirties the SAME paths - normal, because the hot
    files of one phase are usually the hot files of the next.
Now `comm -12` between current status and the baseline body matches on the
porcelain line, so those paths are classified pre-existing and subtracted.

WHAT IT WOULD HAVE COST HERE
9 reviewable wave-1 paths would have been subtracted, INCLUDING
.claude/scripts/qa-gate.sh - the core file of units U3/U4. The approval would have
bound a change set with the wave's principal file missing, and nothing anywhere
would have reported the shortfall. The approval record would have looked complete.

WHY THE EXISTING REFUSAL DOES NOT CATCH IT
94d.1's `change_set_reconstructed` refusal fires on an EMPTY tracker. Here the
tracker was non-empty - merely incomplete. qa-gate.sh (~:3700) already names this
exact case as the honest limit of the mechanism, in a comment: it is reported, not
refused. So the limit was known and documented, and had never been measured
against a real cycle until now.

REPAIR APPLIED THAT CYCLE (disclosed, not silent)
QA appended the 9 masked paths to changed-files.txt before `enter`, kept a
pre-repair snapshot, and recorded the action in the approval comment, in review
artifact claude-workflow-plugin-i8cx-r1.json (finding R1-F1), and in the qa-plan
doc. Post-repair reconcile reported subtracted=0 and the bound set was all 8 real
files (the 21 fixture copies are workflow-denylist-excluded by design and were
verified byte-identical to canonical).

THIS RECURS ON THE VERY NEXT WAVE
The post-approve baseline (head ed45abe) re-lists the same script paths. Wave-2
edits to them will be masked again. So either land the fix before wave 2, or repeat
the manual repair at every gate - and a manual repair that must be remembered is
the failure mode this whole release is about.

SUGGESTED DIRECTION
Bind the baseline to the commit it was captured at, and invalidate or re-derive it
when HEAD moves. A porcelain line is not an identity; ` M path` at 6d0011f and
` M path` at ed45abe are different facts about different content. Anything that
compares them as equal is comparing a string, not a state.

PAIRING (this is a CHECK, so it needs one): capture a baseline while a path is
dirty, commit it, re-dirty the same path, run the gate, and assert the path IS in
the bound change set. Negative control: the same flow WITHOUT the intervening
commit must still subtract it correctly, or the fix has simply disabled baselining.

title: Second systemic root cause: no pipefail - 1085 pipelines + 17 process substitutions mask upstream failure (sibling to uopo)
description:
SECOND SYSTEMIC ROOT CAUSE, sibling to claude-workflow-plugin-uopo. Found at
D4b review round 8, after a round-7 fix ESCAPED uopo's class and landed directly
in this one.

MEASURED 2026-08-25 on v5/design-phase (working tree):
  scripts setting pipefail ........ 0 of 4
    epic-gate.sh 0, qa-gate.sh 0, review-check.sh 0, verify-before-stop.sh 0
    command: grep -cE '^[[:space:]]*set -[a-z]*o[[:space:]]+pipefail' <file>
  pipelines in the decision path .. 338
    epic-gate.sh 77, qa-gate.sh 179, review-check.sh 82
    command: grep -cE '\|[[:space:]]*(jq|grep|sort|awk|sed|wc|head|tail)' <file>

THE DEFECT
Without `set -o pipefail`, a pipeline's exit status is the LAST command's status.
Every upstream failure is masked. `set -e` does not help: the pipeline succeeded.
So a failed producer reads as a successful empty/partial result - the same family
as uopo, through a different channel.

REPRODUCED (R8-F2, epic-gate.sh:1943, the round-7 "jq-free" multiply-bound decision):
  arr=(U1 U1); n=$(printf '%s\n' "${arr[@]}" | sort -u | grep -c .)
  with a sort shim that copies stdin and exits 9:
    entries=2 distinct_count=2 pipeline_rc=0  -> duplicate branch SKIPPED
  A multiply-bound unit therefore disappears, from_entries collapses one child,
  and the clean plan can report parallel_safe:true.
Also R8-F4 (design-unit-bind-parity.test.sh:249): a printf|sed|awk parser where a
failing sed is masked by a successful nonempty awk, silently dropping a required
flag from the census.

WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN ITS SIZE SUGGESTS
uopo and this task are EACH OTHER'S ESCAPE HATCH. Round 7 fixed a fail-open jq
(uopo's class) by rewriting the decision as a shell pipeline - and thereby created
a fail-open pipeline (this class). Neither rewrite direction is safe while both
channels are unguarded. That is the mechanical reason D4b took eight review rounds
and why the same defect family kept reappearing after each fix.

NOT A ONE-LINE FIX - this is why it gets a phase, not a patch:
`set -o pipefail` across 338 pipelines changes behaviour wherever a pipeline
legitimately has a non-zero stage: `head` closing a pipe (SIGPIPE 141), `grep -q`
short-circuiting, `grep -c` returning 1 on zero matches mid-pipeline. Enabling it
globally without auditing those is how you turn a masked failure into a spurious
one, which is the opposite mistake and just as damaging to trust in the gate.

SCOPE
  1. Audit all 338 pipelines and classify: must-fail-closed / legitimately-nonzero.
  2. Enable pipefail per-script (or scoped per-pipeline where a stage is
     legitimately non-zero), starting with the decision paths.
  3. Pair every change: a mutation making an upstream stage fail must turn the
     result into a REFUSAL, with a restore control and a leg running the shipped
     artifact.
  4. Prefer restructuring a pipeline into guarded steps over a scoped exemption
     wherever the pipeline is making a SAFETY decision.

SEQUENCING
Take this WITH or BEFORE uopo, not after. Fixing uopo's jq sites by rewriting them
as pipelines - the natural move - is unsafe until this lands.

UNTIL THIS LANDS: any pipeline in a safety decision can report a benign result for
a failed computation. In-scope instances found at round 8 are being fixed
individually; the other ~336 are not.
notes: WAVE 1 GATED: qa-approved at change_set_hash b5fe335f (2026-08-26). Task stays OPEN for waves 2-3 (9 units, ~36 must-fix sites). See qa-plan doc: R1-F1 tracker-repair warning applies to the NEXT gate cycle too (post-approve baseline re-masks the same script paths). Review artifact: docs/reviews/claude-workflow-plugin-i8cx-r1.json (artifact_hash 62034b9b).

comments.author: username
comments.text:
SCOPE QUESTION for this task's owner, raised by a specialist under the round-8 stopping rule (reported, not fixed).

A THIRD masking channel exists that a pipeline census will NOT find:
process substitution discards the producer's exit status entirely.
  while IFS= read -r x; do ...; done < <(producer)
On bash 3.2 there is no checkable status for `producer` at all, so a partial or
failed write silently shrinks whatever the loop builds. Structurally identical to
the pipefail masking this task covers, one level down — but `< <(cmd)` is not a
pipeline and would be missed by the filed census command.

MEASURED 2026-08-25, occurrences of `< <(` in the shipped scripts:
  $(basename $f)             $(grep -cE '<[[:space:]]*<\(' "$f")
  $(basename $f)             $(grep -cE '<[[:space:]]*<\(' "$f")
  $(basename $f)             $(grep -cE '<[[:space:]]*<\(' "$f")
  $(basename $f)             $(grep -cE '<[[:space:]]*<\(' "$f")
  command: grep -cE '<[[:space:]]*<\(' <file>

DECISION NEEDED: widen this task's scope to include process substitution, or
exclude it explicitly with a reason. Leaving it unstated would reproduce the exact
failure this task exists to fix — a channel nobody counted.

Concrete instance already found: design-unit-bind-parity.test.sh loads
REQUIRED_FLAGS through `while read ... done < <(printf ...)` AFTER rc-validation,
so a partial producer write would shrink the set unseen. For an in-memory printf
that is practically unmeasurable, which is precisely why it needs a stated
decision rather than a silent pass.

comments.author: username
comments.text:
SCOPE CORRECTION — the filed numbers were measured over THREE scripts and
presented as the whole. Re-measured across all 29 shipped scripts, 2026-08-26.

FILED (wrong denominator):        338 pipelines, 7 process substitutions, 0 scripts with pipefail
ACTUAL (all .claude/scripts/*.sh): 1085 pipelines, 17 process substitutions, 3 scripts already
                                   using SCOPED pipefail (epic-gate 2, tree-lease 2,
                                   verify-before-stop 6) - so precedent exists in-tree
  command: for f in .claude/scripts/*.sh; do
             grep -cE '\|[[:space:]]*(jq|grep|sort|awk|sed|wc|head|tail|tr|cut|uniq|xargs)' "$f"; done
This is the same enumerated-denominator failure the release keeps finding
(z7ni), committed by this task's own author while filing it. Recorded rather
than quietly amended.

TOP SCRIPTS BY PIPELINE COUNT
  qa-gate.sh 314, verify-before-stop.sh 158, review-check.sh 94, epic-gate.sh 91,
  model-select.sh 60, workflow-doctor.sh 60, codex-review.sh 42, session-start.sh 37

THE SCOPE IS SMALLER THAN 1085 - IT DECOMPOSES
Terminal-command distribution: jq 357, grep 113, tr 101, head 78, sed 59, cut 35,
sort 28, awk 28, tail 20, wc 5, xargs 1.

  1. LOW RISK, ~273 sites: the `printf '%s' "$x" | jq ...` idiom.
     The producer is printf on an in-memory string - it cannot meaningfully fail -
     and jq is last, so jq's status IS the pipeline status. Masking is not
     reachable here. Candidate for explicit EXEMPTION with a stated reason rather
     than mechanical conversion. Confirm the producer really is always in-memory.
  2. THE REAL TARGET: decision-path pipelines with a FALLIBLE producer - a real
     command feeding another, where the upstream failure is masked. This is the
     R8-F2 shape exactly:
       n=$(printf '%s\n' "${arr[@]}" | sort -u | grep -c .)
     with a failing sort -> count reads as "no duplicates" -> a multiply-bound
     unit disappears -> parallel_safe:true.
     Sizing signal: 513 pipelines are assigned to a variable, 178 appear in a
     conditional. Those are where a masked failure changes an outcome.
  3. SIGPIPE / INTENTIONAL-NONZERO HAZARDS, 162 sites, why this is NOT a
     one-line fix: 76 `| head`, 20 `| tail`, 52 `| grep -q`, 14 `| grep -c`.
     Enabling pipefail file-wide over these converts masked failures into
     SPURIOUS ones - the opposite mistake, equally damaging to trust in the gate.

REVISED APPROACH
  a. Classify per script: fallible-producer-on-a-decision-path (fix) vs
     printf-producer (exempt, stated) vs intentional-nonzero (scope or restructure).
  b. Prefer restructuring a safety decision into guarded steps over a scoped
     exemption. Prefer scoped `( set -o pipefail; ... )` over file-wide where a
     file carries SIGPIPE idioms - the in-tree precedent (epic-gate :1990,
     design-unit-bind-parity :268) is exactly this shape and bash 3.2 has no
     `local -`.
  c. Pair every change: a mutation failing an upstream stage must turn the result
     into a REFUSAL, with a restore control and a leg running the shipped artifact.
  d. Sequence before uopo, unchanged and now better evidenced: uopo's natural fix
     rewrites fail-open jq sites, and 273 of these pipelines already ARE that
     rewrite target.

comments.author: username
comments.text:
AUDIT COMPLETE — 141 sites examined across 19 scripts by six independent auditors,
40 classified must_fix, 13 implementable units (6 high risk, 5 medium, 2 low).
A synthesiser spot-checked 12 of the highest-blast-radius claims by reading source
at the named file:line; all 12 confirmed.

THE FOUR THAT MATTER MOST — each is a failed read releasing or binding something:

1. verify-before-stop.sh:3197 and :5362 (THE STOP HOOK)
   `reviewable_changes` feeds two release points, and BOTH callers structurally
   discard the function's rc: `done < <(reviewable_changes)` then
   `if [ "$CODE_CHANGES_DETECTED" = false ]; then echo "{}"; exit 0`. A failed
   sort/git/comm inside it yields an empty change set, so the session RELEASES.
   A return code cannot carry the failure through a process substitution.

2. impact-report.sh:270 + :288 (THE APPROVAL BINDING)
   `canonical_changed_files()` ends `done < <(sort -u "$TRACKING_FILE" 2>/dev/null)`
   - proc-sub, rc unobservable, loop simply runs zero times. `change_set_hash()`
   has no status check. Generator AND checker share the function, so a failed read
   yields the SAME empty-set digest e3b0c44298fc... on both sides and the freshness
   comparison MATCHES. An approval binds to a change set that was never read.

3. qa-gate.sh:327 — the error handler is DEAD CODE
   `status_out=$(git ... status --porcelain 2>/dev/null | LC_ALL=C sort) || { log_sync_error ...; return 1; }`
   sort is last, so git's failure never reaches the handler the author wrote.

4. review-check.sh:1417 — reviewer independence
   An empty `impl_lines` short-circuits the `-n` conjunct, so INDEPENDENT stays
   "true" and the `reviewer_not_independent` refusal never fires. A failed read
   makes a NON-independent reviewer look independent.

Also: beads-ledger.sh partial `record_meta` rows fall through to `db-ahead`, the
verdict that unblocks the destructive export; post-edit.sh:449 lets a partial sort
install a TRUNCATED tracker.

MEASURED — why file-wide pipefail is the wrong instrument:
  ( set -o pipefail; printf '' | grep -c . )        -> rc 1 on the HEALTHY zero-match case
  ( set -o pipefail; seq 1 100000 | head -1 )       -> rc 141 (SIGPIPE)
  ( set -o pipefail; seq 1 3 | head -1 )            -> rc 0
So the head trap bites only when the producer outruns the reader - nondeterministic
by data size, the worst kind of spurious failure.

MEASURED — why pipefail is wrong for the Stop hook specifically:
  set -e; set -o pipefail; f(){ echo tracker; c=$(false|sort); echo got; }
aborts AFTER the tracker half has been emitted, handing the caller a silently
TRUNCATED change set - strictly worse than today's empty one. U1 therefore
restructures into rc-guarded steps instead, copying the shape this same file
already uses correctly at :5504/:5516.

`set -e` INVENTORY (changes the fix shape per file):
  present: qa-gate, verify-before-stop, epic-gate, post-edit, current-task,
           subagent-start, workflow-manifest, bd-github-link, statusline,
           intent-router, lessons, tech-debt
  ABSENT:  impact-report, review-check, beads-ledger, model-select,
           worktree-sweep, codex-review, workflow-doctor
In the `set -e` files every rc capture needs `|| rc=$?`; in the others a bare
capture is safe as written.

IN-TREE TEMPLATES to copy rather than invent:
  epic-gate.sh:1992  scoped `( set -o pipefail; ... ) || rc=$?` with the rc branch
                     degrading BEFORE any arithmetic  (correct; one site, not two)
  workflow-manifest.sh:617  scan_declared_dir already captures find's rc and dies
                     with text saying an empty answer and a failed one must not
                     look alike - scan_flat/scan_tree simply never got it
  verify-before-stop.sh:5504/:5516  producer split onto its own line with an
                     explicit rc, then an rc-guarded comm

Full per-unit plan (approach + paired test + risk) in the session scratchpad at
i8cx-plan.txt.

machine inside a checker that must be more trustworthy than what it checks.

<!-- BD-MCP-DOC: qa-plan v1 -->
# QA plan — i8cx WAVE 1 gate (2026-08-26, approved at change_set_hash b5fe335f)

## Scope gated
Wave 1 only (U1 Stop hook, U2 approval binding, U3/U4 gate chain, + the verify-before-stop half of U7 that rode along). Task stays OPEN for waves 2-3 (9 units, ~36 must-fix sites). The approval binds the change set, not task completion.

## Review modules executed
- Regression impact scan (3a): mechanical impact report read (8 then 9 files, server=code-graph); impact_of on write_gate_baseline (callers: cmd_enter/cmd_approve/cmd_baseline_capture/cmd_choose, mirrored in fixtures); manual caller sweeps for sha256_file (exactly 2, both guarded), reconcile_tracker (soft at enter, hard at approve), reviewable_changes (exactly 2 consumers, both sentinel-aware).
- SECRETS: clean. INJECTION-class shell review: quoting/case-pattern/herestring semantics of the new code traced; sentinel \001 collision argument verified (porcelain C-quotes control bytes; forged sentinel can only block).
- Empty-vs-unreadable audit (the orchestrator's named judgement): SOUND. Absent tracker, empty readable tracker, clean tree, missing baseline, non-git dir all proven non-refusing (test legs 7.3/7.4, gbv2-8.1/8.3, clean-sandbox {} control + code trace). Every induced read failure refuses loudly with a recovery recipe. get/get-repo exit 0 empty on absent markers, so no spurious I8 arming and no sync-error flood on ordinary Stops.

## Tests run (live, this tree)
change-set-undeterminable 53/53 rc0; impact-report 95/95 rc0; qa-gate-pipefail 61/61 rc0; component gate-baseline-v2 standalone 159/159 rc0. Assertion arithmetic 4853+53+56+61=5023 confirmed (three deltas measured live; 4853 base accepted from the acceptance record). Full L1/L2/lint/e2e rc values accepted on the recorded four-tier run per orchestrator constraint.

## Findings (review artifact docs/reviews/claude-workflow-plugin-i8cx-r1.json, artifact_hash 62034b9b)
- R1-F1 medium: stale gate-baseline (head=6d0011f) masked 9 wave-1 paths incl. qa-gate.sh from the change set; repaired by appending them to changed-files.txt pre-enter (snapshot kept); post-repair subtracted=0. Pre-existing design limit (94d.1 honest-limit comment), not a wave-1 regression.
- R1-F2 low: U7 verify-half mislabels a whitespace-only current-task marker as read-FAILED; degrades safely; fold into the deferred U7 helper half.
- R1-F3 info: U7 verify-half present beyond the briefed 4 units; disclosed in spec headers, absent from acceptance comment unit list.
- R1-F4 info: impact-report---change-set-hash.json / ---list.json in .qa-tracking = historical flag-as-task-id argv wart.

## WARNING for the wave-2/3 reviewer

title: v5 phase: extract guarded json_emit/json_read primitives - 208 emitter call sites, 29 inline encoders, 101 fail-open readers
description:
OPERATOR DECISION 2026-08-24: patch D4b's in-scope findings now; this extraction
becomes its own v5 phase and goes through the new design -> reviewed -> implement
pipeline that v5 itself is building (dogfooding the release).

THE DEFECT (one root cause, not N bugs)
No single guarded, validated JSON construction/read primitive exists. Every site
rolls its own, and two failure shapes recur:

(a) CONSTRUCTION. Emitters build JSON as
      printf '{"ok":%s,"error_key":%s,...}' "$ok" "$(printf '%s' "$k" | jq -Rs .)" ...
    Under set -e a failing inner jq substitution yields empty, the OUTER printf
    still returns 0, and malformed JSON prints with a SUCCESS status.
    Proven: bash -c 'set -e; printf "{\"x\":%s}\n" "$(false)"; printf "rc=%s\n" "$?"'
      ->  {"x":}   then   rc=0
(b) READING. Readers collapse "could not read" into a benign literal
    (|| x="{}" / "[]" / "" / 0), making a failed read indistinguishable from a
    genuine empty result.

MEASURED SCALE (measured 2026-08-24 on v5/design-phase)
  emit_error_json call sites .......... 169   grep -cE '\bemit_error_json ' qa-gate.sh
  emit_json       call sites ..........  34   grep -cE '\bemit_json ' qa-gate.sh
  readers collapsing to benign literal .  46   36 qa-gate + 6 review-check + 4 epic-gate
  unguarded jq in array-append/printf ..   8   epic-gate.sh
  total shipped bash in the 3 scripts .. 12366 lines
Construction sites verified by hand at review-check.sh:640-648,
qa-gate.sh:2230-2235 and qa-gate.sh:2687-2692 - all three identical in shape.

EVIDENCE THIS IS ONE CAUSE
Across D4b rounds r1-r5 and h2r1-h2r2 this class produced findings in SIX
CONSECUTIVE ROUNDS: R1-F2, R2-F1, R3-F1, R4-F1, R5-F2/F5/F6, H2-F1,
H2R2-F1/F2/F3/F4/F5. Each fix round patched instances; the next found more,
because the sites are independent by construction.

THE FIX IS ALREADY PROVEN LOCALLY
Three independent fixes converged on the same pattern without coordination:
  - print_envelope_checked (qa-gate.sh:8600-8613) - one guarded jq -nc, then
    check rc + non-emptiness + parseability, else a caller-data-free literal at
    exit 2.
  - the single guarded jq -ce pass (review-check.sh:878-941) computing AND
    shape-validating in one program with one refusal sink.
  - _pb_degrade simplification (epic-gate.sh) - 7 jq sites -> 2, both guarded,
    wrong-order fallback DELETED so the defect became unrepresentable.
The pattern works; it simply is not global.

SCOPE
  1. json_emit() - build in ONE guarded jq -nc; validate rc + non-empty +
     parseable; on failure print a caller-data-free literal and RETURN NONZERO so
     callers cannot continue after an encoder malfunction.
  2. json_read() - explicit rc-3 "unreadable" channel, distinct from a
     successfully-read empty result. An absent value must yield the SAFE answer.
  3. Convert the 203 emitter call sites and the 46 fail-open readers.

RISK / SEQUENCING
A 203-call-site mechanical change inside an 8800-line gate script carries real
regression risk and needs its own review rounds - which is exactly why it gets a
design artifact and a design review instead of being smuggled into D4b. Consider
taking it AFTER D1/D2 land so it becomes the first change actually governed by
the design phase.

UNTIL THIS LANDS the class stays live at ~240 sites. That is the accepted,
stated risk of the chosen option, not an oversight.

title: design-unit-bind has no caller: D4a shipped the binding mechanism with no producer, so design-conform consumes a record nothing writes
description:
Found by the D4b scope-audit workflow; VERIFIED by the orchestrator before filing.

EVIDENCE (all at HEAD 6d0011f):
  $ grep -rln 'design-unit-bind' .claude/agents/ docs/ skills/ | grep -v plans/
  docs/reviews/claude-workflow-plugin-fkm.6-r2.json      # the review artifact ITSELF — no agent, no doc
  $ grep -cE 'design-unit-bind|unit_id|task per unit' .claude/agents/orchestrator.md
  0
  $ grep -c 'DESIGN-UNIT v1' .beads/interactions.jsonl
  0

So at HEAD: no agent prompt invokes design-unit-bind, orchestrator.md does not know the concept exists, and no task in the store carries a binding.

WHY THIS MATTERS. claude-workflow-plugin-fkm.6 (D4a, committed 6d0011f) shipped BOTH halves of a two-part mechanism: design-unit-bind writes the DESIGN-UNIT record, and design-conform reads it to decide whether a task's changed files match the unit it implements. The reader is fully built, twice-reviewed, and covered by 183 assertions. It resolves a binding that NOTHING PRODUCES. In practice every design-conform call on a real task therefore takes the unit_not_in_design path — the fail-closed branch — so the feature is not merely inert, it is uniformly refusing.

This is the same shape as the gap D4a itself discovered: D1-D3 built, reviewed and gated the design artifact and all three passed, because nothing yet CONSUMED the units. Here the mirror image — a consumer exists and no producer does. The machinery is correct and unreachable.

WHAT IS MISSING. The orchestrator must, when it opens one task per design unit, record the binding for each:
  bash .claude/scripts/qa-gate.sh design-unit-bind <child-tid> --design-task <design-tid> --unit-id <U-n>
That is a step in orchestrator.md's decomposition flow, plus almost certainly a line in the workflow-engine SKILL.md so the rule lives in the canonical source rather than only in a prompt.

DO NOT FIX THIS WITH PROSE ALONE. LESSONS.md:84 is this repo's own measured finding that prose cues do not drive subagent tool use. An instruction in orchestrator.md is necessary but not sufficient; the enforcing consequence is design-conform refusing at approve — which is DELIBERATELY NOT WIRED YET (qa-gate.sh:8116-8118 records the deferral). So closing this properly means deciding the enforcement wiring too, or accepting that the binding is advisory until D5.

PAIRING. A prompt-only change needs the parity check this repo already uses for agent-prompt contracts (see completion-contract-parity.test.sh's approach: assert each carrier names the invocation). A leg asserting orchestrator.md contains the design-unit-bind invocation is cheap and catches silent removal.

P0 because it makes a just-shipped, fully-reviewed feature inert, and because plan-batches (D4b) depends on the mapping existing: its unit->task resolution path cannot be exercised on real data until bindings are written.

prerequisite, not incidental — leases carrying owner identity and heartbeat, stale-lease reclaim, no fixed
/tmp paths, and no measurement of a tree another writer can touch without a lease or quiesce.' D4 is the
phase that actually spawns parallel implementers, so this lands first.

j7kk already shipped the CHEAP half — skip-when-unchanged, which removes the redundant-run case. Measured
twice since: it does NOT subsume ownership. On both occurrences of the log collision below the tree HAD
moved, so the skip correctly declined, and the collision happened anyway.

MEMBERS, each with measured evidence:

1. FIXED SHARED PATHS. verify-before-stop.sh:40-41 write TEST_LOG and LINT_LOG to fixed paths in the
   tracking dir. FOUR measured occurrences this arc of the gate asserting 'Tests failing (exit 2)' and
   pointing at a log that DOES NOT EXIST, every time with a concurrent suite live. The gate declares a
   failure and cites evidence for it that is not there. Task bjen is the same shape one tier down:
   specs/model-select.sh writes fixed /tmp/ms-*.err paths that two concurrent component runs collide on.
   -> per-run paths, or a lease covering the tracking dir.

2. THE UNEVIDENCED-FAILURE TAIL READ. Beyond the path, the reader must say 'the log is absent' rather than
   presenting an unevidenced red as measured. Note the asymmetry this arc already found: j7kk's store
   canary faces the identical ambiguity and HEDGES ('either this spec wrote, or another process wrote
   concurrently'); QA ruled that hedge load-bearing and it has now protected EIGHT-PLUS innocent specs.
   The Stop hook, facing the same ambiguity, asserts. Same system, opposite honesty.

3. 7tfe's ROOT CAUSE, now established and NOT blocked on an operator decision. There are TWO telemetry
   flushers and the disarm covers one: run-tests.sh exports BD_DISABLE_METRICS=1 for bd's send-metrics,
   but bd EMBEDS dolt and the embedded engine spawns its own 'dolt send-metrics', which that variable
   cannot touch. MEASURED: dolt config documents a metrics.disabled key; nothing in the tree sets it; a
   live specimen was running when checked. I previously flagged the fix as needing an operator decision
   because 'dolt config --global' mutates the user's machine — but 'dolt config --local' EXISTS and writes
   inside .beads/embeddeddolt/beads/.dolt/, which is UNTRACKED. So a repo-scoped disable is available
   without reaching outside the repo. Verify that by driving before relying on it.

4. rd2 — test-runner contention across tiers, where '1nz's CLASS survived its own fix'. Read it; it is the
   generalisation of the other three.

5. THE LEASE ITSELF. Owner identity, heartbeat, stale reclaim. This is what D4 needs and what nothing above
   provides: skip-when-unchanged removes redundant work, per-run paths remove collisions, but neither
   answers 'who owns this tree right now'.

MEASURED CONTENTION COSTS FROM THIS ARC, so the work is sized against evidence rather than fear:
  approve-idempotency.sh   853s contended vs 753s uncontended, identical bytes
  a 97-minute L2 run       discarded on a corrupted stability signal
  two component specs      transient failures, never reproduced in 3x isolated re-runs
  8+ store-canary firings  every one naming an innocent spec
  two acceptance runs      contended by the orchestrator's own Stop hook and reported with the window named

NON-GOALS: do not widen timeouts. That hides contention rather than resolving ownership, and was ruled out
explicitly when this was first scoped.

RELATED, NOT MEMBERS: 9xl4's own headline hazard (a timed-out Codex MCP call leaving a live writer) is
currently UNREACHABLE — three consecutive review requests measured 1,251,966 / 2,216,056 / 1,817,089 bytes
against a 100,000 cap and refused at exit 7 before any MCP call was made. It becomes reachable again the
moment the packet-size finding is fixed, so the lease design must cover it even though it cannot fire
today. qj7v and 4d.1.1 are gate-state adjacent and should be read but not necessarily fixed here.

comments.text: SELF-FOUND regression (round 3, before reporting): the R3-F3 heartbeat daemon added to all three participating runners (`run-tests.sh`, `component/run.sh`, `verify-before-stop.sh`) spawned its background subshell without redirecting its own stdin/stdout/stderr. Measured directly with a minimal byte-for-byte reproduction of the spawn shape: `kill "$HEARTBEAT_PID"` only terminates the subshell wrapper — the `sleep 30` it is blocked in at that instant is a separate child process, gets re-parented to pid 1 rather than killed, and keeps holding whatever fds it inherited for up to its remaining ~30s. In `verify-before-stop.sh` this means the hook's own JSON envelope stdout stayed open (from the perspective of any caller reading it as a stream, the same constraint bash's own `$(...)` has) for up to 30s after the actual decision was already written — every Stop hook invocation that reached this heartbeat would have appeared to hang. Fixed by redirecting the subshell's own fds at spawn time (`</dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1`) in all three runners. Added a new component-spec test (`vbs-r3fix` in `verify-before-stop.sh`'s spec) that drives the real hook through a dispatch, times a stdout-pipe capture, and proves a redirect-stripped mutant measurably hangs the same capture (pairing requirement satisfied). Full write-up and command-cited measurements in CHANGELOG.md's R3-F3 entry and in LESSONS.md. Currently verifying end-to-end via `.claude/tests/component/run.sh --filter verify-before-stop.sh` (background, ~30min) before final report.

comments.text: Follow-up on the fd-leak regression comment above: the new `section 18` test I added to `runner-completeness.test.sh` for run-tests.sh/component/run.sh initially FAILED on its first real run (4 assertions) — for the wrong reason, appropriately for this round's theme. Root cause (confirmed via `bash -x`): both runners source `tree-lease.sh` relative to their OWN script location (`dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}"/../tree-lease.sh`), not relative to `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR`. My mutant copies lived bare in a scratch dir with no sibling `tree-lease.sh`, so `TREE_LEASE_AVAILABLE` silently stayed 0, the heartbeat block never ran in either leg, and "does the mutant hang" failed because there was nothing to hang on. Separately, my non-vacuity check (`grep -c '^    ) &$'`) coincidentally matched an unrelated pre-existing `) &` at run-tests.sh:913, an unrelated backgrounded block, giving a false "2 not 1" mismatch. Fixed both: mutants now get a real sibling `tree-lease.sh` at the correct relative depth, and non-vacuity is now a diff-based exact-one-line-changed check, immune to unrelated coincidental matches. Re-ran clean: 344/344 assertions (`bash .claude/scripts/tests/runner-completeness.test.sh`), and the full `verify-before-stop.sh` component spec is 258/258 (`bash .claude/tests/component/run.sh --filter verify-before-stop.sh`, 1937s), including `vbs-r3fix` and its negative control. **Investigated 15.10 per your request — established, not assumed. Short answer: neither of your two options; a third.**

Re-read the R2-F7 mechanism in full (`_dolt_send_metrics_argv_pids`/`_dolt_pid_cwd`/`_dolt_send_metrics_pids_at`/`poll_for_dolt_flusher`). The attribution (cwd + pre/post-drain snapshot) is sound against a FOREIGN process — confirmed structurally, and confirmed empirically: the META assertions ("finds a real process at its own cwd" / "does NOT attribute that same process to a different directory") passed in every run, including the two where 15.10 itself failed. So it isn't "the attribution isn't attributing."

It also isn't "the disarm genuinely failed" in the sense of the `metrics.disabled` config not taking effect — I have no evidence of that; every time the probe read both calls correctly (the overwhelming majority of runs), the disarm worked exactly as designed.

**What I found instead, with direct repro:** the probe's own fixed polling budgets (3s to detect a new spawn, 5s per drain) are not validated against real contention, and I reproduced a LOAD-TRIGGERED FALSE RESULT on demand:
- Isolated, no load: 15/15 clean (`bash repro1510.sh 15`, extracted verbatim from the shipped functions).
- Isolated, under synthetic CPU saturation (10 busy-loop processes pinning all cores): 13/13 clean before I hit a tool timeout (all load processes were reaped automatically when the timeout killed the group — verified clean afterward, nothing left running).
- Two REAL copies of the repro running concurrently (matching "a concurrent make test" more closely than synthetic CPU spin): runner A showed 2/12 trials misread — but as `15.9=not-seen` (a false NEGATIVE on the positive control), not the `15.10=seen` false positive that actually occurred in my clean single-file re-run. Runner B: 12/12 clean.

So I can confirm the mechanism IS load-sensitive in the direction you're worried about (a real, on-demand-reproducible false result under real dolt/bd contention), but I have not pinned down the EXACT race that flips `15.10` specifically rather than `15.9` — the two failures I've now observed (yours in the full-file run, mine in the concurrent-runner repro) are the same root cause (fixed timing budget vs. genuinely async external process spawn) but different specific manifestations, and my clean re-run of the whole file had NOTHING else running concurrently, so whatever triggered it there was internal to the file's own ~9 minutes of prior real dolt/process activity, not an external contender.

This is the same risk class `claude-workflow-plugin-7tfe` already named in its own root-cause comment: "the spawn needs a bd call that reaches the embedded dolt engine AND a slow enough metrics endpoint... neither is reliable on a quiet machine; both are likely under load." My finding extends that: the DETECTION probe itself inherits the identical load-sensitivity, on top of the spawn it's trying to observe.

**Recommendation:** this is a test-instrument timing-budget question, not a shipped-code defect, and it's outside R4-F1..F5's scope. Per the task's own non-goal ("do not widen timeouts... was ruled out explicitly when this was first scoped") I'm treating that as applying to shipped gate/lease thresholds, not necessarily this L1 test probe's internal polling loop — but I don't have total confidence in a fix shape yet (widening the window is the obvious lever and the one most likely to just lower the failure's frequency without addressing why a previous call's own delayed spawn can still be live when the next call's baseline is captured). Not patching without that confidence. Recommend a dedicated follow-up task rather than folding it into this round — happy to file one if you want it tracked separately from 7tfe (which is about the shipped disarm itself, already fixed and driven-verified) rather than reusing it.

Investigating 18.4 (my own R4-F3 L2 control) next with the same discipline — isolated repro passed clean, so it's something specific to running deep in this file; a third full run with a diagnostic dump I just added (prints the actual captured L2 runner output on failure, not a re-guess) is in progress now.

## 1. Deleted vs added, net terms

Per-file deltas, each measured by `wc -l` before my first edit this round vs now:

Net additions (real fixes, not journey-narration):
| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `.claude/scripts/qa-gate.sh` | R5-F3 fix inside `wipe_iteration_state` — no pre-edit isolated count captured for this function specifically (honest gap, not hidden); current file 7700 lines / 452,605 bytes total |

**Verdict: yes, this round shrank the batch.** The two heaviest deletions (run-with-timeout.test.sh -290, runner-completeness.test.sh net -402 despite two real additions inside it) come from removing controls whose mechanism no longer exists, not from trimming comments. The two real additions (qa-gate-lock-recovery.test.sh +198, the qa-gate.sh fix itself) are both fixes with paired tests, not journey narration.

## 2. `run-with-timeout.test.sh` — kept vs removed, and why

**Kept** (6 assertions, all passing — `bash .claude/scripts/tests/run-with-timeout.test.sh`):
- **Section 0** (0.1, 0.2): the awk extraction defines `run_with_timeout` and parses. True of any shape of the function, including the restored one.
- **Section 1** (1a-1d): quick success (rc=0), quick specific exit code (rc=13) preserved exactly, log genuinely captures stdout, logging command itself returns 0. These exercise the property the restored `timeout`/`gtimeout`/`else` dispatch actually has — passthrough and capture — with zero dependence on heartbeat or group-kill machinery.

**Removed** (sections 2-4 + their METAs, ~290 lines):
- Section 2/META 2 (R4-F1 group-vs-wrapper kill check): targeted the literal `kill -0 -- "-$child_pid"`. Confirmed absent from the shipped function (`grep -c` = 0) — the restored dispatch has no manual kill-0 loop at all, it just calls `timeout(1)` and returns. Verified the survivor would have been a **false pair**: re-running the mutant construction against current code, the sed matched nothing (mutant byte-identical to original, non-vacuity guard would read 0 not 2).
- Section 3/META 3 (R4-F2 heartbeat sync/async): the restored function calls no `lease_heartbeat` anywhere — confirmed by reading it, it's the 8-line shipped-and-reviewed shape (`: > "$log"`, three `if/elif/else` branches, nothing else).
- Section 4 (heartbeat firing + `set -m` restoration): same reason — no heartbeat call, and no `set -m` manipulation in the restored function at all (it never backgrounds anything itself; `timeout(1)` runs in the foreground of the call).

**Survivors are NOT guarding absent machinery** — I checked each by grep count against the current shipped function before deciding to keep it, and ran the file standalone to confirm all 6 pass for the right reason (log content genuinely differs per test, not a vacuous "everything returns 0" pass).

**What I did NOT do**: add a new leg proving `run_with_timeout` returns 124 for a genuine (non-backgrounding-trick) hang. Filed as `claude-workflow-plugin-v4jn` rather than fixed — the correct test needs skip-when-`timeout`/`gtimeout`-absent handling (this box has **neither** on PATH, verified directly: `command -v timeout` → not found, `command -v gtimeout` → not found, `brew --prefix coreutils` resolves a prefix but the formula isn't linked), and designing that gate correctly is new machinery this round was told not to add.

## 3. R5-F3, R5-F5, R5-F6 — closed or not

All three **closed**, each with a `resolve-finding` comment on this task citing fix ref + test ref (visible in the task's comment stream now).

- **R5-F3** (qa-gate.sh ownerless stale lock): closed. Fix: `qa-gate.sh:1113-1131` (`wipe_iteration_state`) — the `case "$_gl_holder" in ''|*[!0-9]*)` branch was a bare no-op; now reclaims after exactly one retry's grace (`[ "$_gli" != "1" ]`) rather than never, covering BOTH the missing-pid-file case (crash before the printf) and the empty/garbage-pid-file case (interrupted write) as one state. Test: `qa-gate-lock-recovery.test.sh` sections 4-6 + a surgical META (reverts only this branch, not the whole R4-F4 mechanism) — **24/24**, `bash .claude/scripts/tests/qa-gate-lock-recovery.test.sh`.
  - Side-effect finding, also fixed: verifying that META surfaced that the **pre-existing** R4-F4 META (a different, earlier control) was ALSO broken by my own fix — its awk transform hardcoded "skip 14 lines" to consume the old loop body, which my fix grew to 19 lines, so it was leaking the old loop's tail into its own mutant (diff read 17, not 13; mutant failed `bash -n`). Fixed by re-anchoring on the loop's own `done` line instead of a line count.

- **R5-F5** (dolt-flusher `15.10` false-green): closed. Fix: `runner-completeness.test.sh`, `poll_for_dolt_flusher` (section 15) — the post-drain loop already polled the same pid-attribution primitive every iteration but only checked for emptiness; now it also runs the identical new-pid check the sampling loop uses, so a flusher visible only during post-drain sets `hit`. Test: new META-TEST in section 15 (5 assertions) using a **deterministic, call-counted stub** of the attribution primitive (empty for the 62 calls the shipped loops make before post-drain begins, a fake pid from call 63 on) rather than a real timing race — I explicitly avoided a wall-clock-timed decoy after confirming it would be racy to construct correctly. Real function reports "seen", a `declare -f`-derived mutant with just this check removed reports "not-seen" for the identical scripted scenario.
  - Known residual, disclosed not silently accepted: a flusher that spawns and fully exits inside one ~50ms poll gap is still invisible; that needs an event-based mechanism, not a tighter interval.

- **R5-F6** (`STOP_TIMEOUT_FILE`/`read_stop_timeout`): closed. **Restoring the `timeout(1)` dispatch did NOT give them a caller — they were already dead code with no caller before I started**, and I confirmed via `git diff HEAD` that they were deleted (not by me — by the round-6 `run_with_timeout` revert that happened earlier in this session, before I picked the task up) alongside the in-process rewrite they belonged to. I corrected the header to name the fixed timeouts (1200s/300s/600s) and point at `settings.json`'s actual fixed 1320000ms Stop-hook timeout. Test/verification: repo-wide `grep -rln STOP_TIMEOUT_FILE\|read_stop_timeout` outside `.claude/tests/e2e/fixtures` returns empty; `bash -n verify-before-stop.sh` clean.

## 4. Vacuity sweep result

Found **one new instance** beyond the six R5 already named, plus two bugs in my own new controls (caught before shipping, not survivors):

- **7th instance (new, found by the sweep, not by review)**: `runner-completeness.test.sh` section 16 (16.6, 16.6b-d) asserted the OLD four-value lease grammar directly — a stale lease "reclaimed" (expecting the file gone) and a fresh-mtime dead pid reading UNCONFIRMED (surfaced as a distinctly-worded notice, never reclaimed). Both properties the round-6 collapse removed. Running the file after my other fixes caught this as two real FAILs (16.6 expected "no" file, got "yes"; 16.6b expected notice count 1, got 0) — not assumed safe because the change looked confined to `tree-lease.sh`/`qa-gate.sh`. Fixed by asserting the CURRENT invariant (a dead-pid lease behaves identically regardless of mtime — never surfaced, always survives) rather than deleting the age-comparison coverage outright, since proving age no longer matters is a real property of the collapse.
- **Bug in my own new control #1**: my R5-F3 META's anchor (`grep -nF "''|*[!0-9]*)"`) matched my OWN explanatory comment (which quotes the same literal) before the real code line — caught by actually running the test, not assumed correct. Fixed with `grep -Fxn` (exact whole-line match).
- **Bug in my own new control #2**: see R5-F3 above — the pre-existing R4-F4 META broke as a side effect of my own fix.
- **Full repo-wide grep** for `UNCONFIRMED|LIVE-BUT-OLD|dead_grace_s|stale_s` across every `.claude/scripts/tests/*.sh` and `.claude/tests/component/specs/*.sh`: one more hit investigated and ruled out — `packaging-parity.test.sh` matched on `mcp_stale_suffix()`, an unrelated install.sh function about MCP package versioning, not lease staleness (substring collision on "stale_s", nothing to fix).

Confirmed it now leads with the shipped mechanism, not the journey: the `tree-lease.sh` bullet opens with **"This paragraph describes the FINAL, round-6 shape, not an intermediate one"**, states the two-value LIVE/STALE grammar with no threshold up front, then points to history below for readers who want it. Added a "Fix round 5" section (all 6 R5 findings) and a "Fix round 6: DESIGN COLLAPSE" section stating the operator's decision and, verbatim, **the report-only trade you asked me to confirm**: *"a lease whose owner crashed now lingers in `<dir>/leases/` until something else removes it — there is no accumulation problem in practice (a handful of small text files), and `lease_reclaim_stale` remains defined and directly callable by an operator who wants to sweep them... just never invoked on anyone's behalf."* Every earlier passage that still described the daemon/in-process rewrite/heartbeat as shipping is now flagged **"Not current"** in place, naming what superseded it, rather than silently rewritten (matches this file's own established "Rationale corrected" convention from earlier rounds).

## 6. `make lint` + what's still open

`make lint`: **clean, rc=0** — but only after I fixed 3 shellcheck SC2016 findings in my OWN new `qa-gate-lock-recovery.test.sh` additions: 2 were legitimate single-quote uses needing a `# shellcheck disable=SC2016` comment, 1 was a **real bug** — I'd written `\$` (backslash-escaped) inside single quotes in a grep pattern, which is a no-op there (backslash isn't special in single quotes) and happened to still match only because grep's BRE treats a bare `\$` as a literal dollar sign — fixed properly with `grep -F` instead of relying on that coincidence.

**Open, named plainly:**
1. **R5-F1 (HIGH) is NOT resolved or arbitrated by me, deliberately.** It's a real, valid finding (a `setsid`'d child can still escape the restored `timeout(1)` dispatch's supervision, so `run_with_timeout` can under-report completion) that the operator explicitly decided to accept as a trade when directing the round-6 collapse — not a code defect I can fix without reopening the five-round chain this batch exists to stop. Per my own standing instructions, arbitration is the orchestrator's call, not mine. It needs: `bash .claude/scripts/qa-gate.sh arbitrate claude-workflow-plugin-gsfd R5-F1 overrule '<rationale>'`, citing the operator's own decision (quoted in the CHANGELOG's round-6 entry) as rationale, before the review-separation gate will treat it as cleared for approval.
2. **`claude-workflow-plugin-v4jn`** filed (discovered-from this task): no test anywhere proves `run_with_timeout` returns 124 for a genuine non-trick hang. Not fixed this round per your own scope discipline.
3. **Unrelated, out-of-scope observation**: `reap_respawn_orphans` pairing (top of `runner-completeness.test.sh`, j7kk's own mechanism) FAILED once on my first standalone run of the file, then passed clean 100% on a second full run and within this `make test` aggregate — did not reproduce, did not investigate further (unrelated subsystem, zero proximity to anything I touched).

title: Evidence-layer stabilization: the gate's own substrate corrupts, contends with, and misreports the evidence it depends on
description:
OPERATOR-DIRECTED BATCH, 2026-08-15. Four filed defects that share one root: the machinery that RECORDS
evidence is not isolated from, coordinated with, or honest about the machinery that PRODUCES it. Closed by
one uninterrupted make test-component run as the acceptance measurement.

MEMBERS
  39cy riders  bd version pinning; doctor binary-vs-schema check; the status false-success; bd-mcp env key;
               issues.jsonl vs CLAUDE.md's ground-truth claim
  L1 census    both directions - see below - plus a STRUCTURAL harness guard
  9xl4 (grown) leases covering the gate's OWN verification, not just D4 implementers, PLUS skip-when-unchanged
  resolver     SessionStart auto-apply writing tracked files into an unrelated change set
  yj2, ha16    folded in: same family (harness isolation and harness accounting)

THE L1 CENSUS IS TWO-DIRECTIONAL. The contamination ALREADY HAPPENED, so a prospective sweep alone
under-scopes it:
  FORWARD   which of the 39 L1 specs can reach the real store at all
  BACKWARD  which comments already IN the store were test-authored; whether any fed a round count, a label,
            or an approval; and MARK them, so the evidence base is not silently mixed
Prevention must be STRUCTURAL, not per-spec: a harness-level guard that FAILS any spec whose environment
points at the production store. A per-spec fix can be reintroduced by the next spec author.

9xl4's CHEAPER STRUCTURAL HALF, to land now: the Stop hook must not re-run verification when the change set
AND the tree are unchanged since the last full run - reusing the escalated state's existing precedent of
reusing a last recorded result. Leases resolve OWNERSHIP; skip-when-unchanged removes most of the contention
outright. NO TIMEOUT WIDENING - that hides contention instead of resolving it.

WHY P0. D2 adds a second evidence-bearing record type (DESIGN-REVIEW) to this store, with its own binding
and label lifecycle. Building that on a store unaudited tests can write to, read by a gate that competes
with the work it gates, is how we end up debugging a design review no reviewer performed.

ACCEPTANCE: one uninterrupted make test-component run, alone, nothing competing. It is also the uncontended
baseline the skip-when-unchanged work needs. Treat a SIGTERM truncation as its own finding UNLESS a
truncated run already fails loudly - a duration ceiling that stops at 17 of 43 and reports anything other
than failure is the same family this batch fixes.
