The strongest single case: qa-claude censused design_foreign_paths as clean — correctly, for the newline round-trip class it was auditing — and sol-codex found a live bug in the same function by asking a different question, which entity are we classifying. Two sound audits, one bug between them. Allocate the second family by FAILURE-MODE SILENCE, not surface novelty. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-fkm.3 --> <!-- tags: evidence, process --> <!-- recorded: 2026-08-13 -->

Observed on fkm.3 — rounds 1 through 5 found mechanism defects, rounds 6 through 8 found a false sentence, a leg passing for a new reason, and a redundant-by-construction line. That transition is the signal to close, not the count of rounds or the count of findings. Make it a rule rather than a judgement call, because the orchestrator's judgement at that exact point proposed a filter that would have replaced a true disclaimer with a false closure claim. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-fkm.3 --> <!-- tags: process --> <!-- recorded: 2026-08-13 -->

The safety argument in the header said "can only ADD a hit" and was quoting the rule for the wrong operation. Two consequences worth carrying: state the invariant as NEVER REMOVE A REDUCTION, ONLY ADD ONE, so a substitution has to justify itself as a deletion; and when a header claims monotonicity, check which of its lines were added and which were REPLACED, because the replaced ones are where the claim is doing no work. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-mdnc --> <!-- tags: evidence, testing --> <!-- recorded: 2026-08-13 -->

The 6h-style legs drove the shipped classifier; the section-9 METAs compared the shipped bytes against a region-stripped copy of THEMSELVES; neither ever loaded the version being replaced. The fix is a differential leg with a FROZEN, sha256-pinned copy of the old artifact checked in beside the test, plus a `git show HEAD:` arm that is live exactly while the change is uncommitted, which is when a reviewer reads it. Pin the baseline's digest: without it, "refresh the baseline to match what we ship" is a one-line change that deletes the invariant and leaves every assertion green. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-mdnc --> <!-- tags: testing --> <!-- recorded: 2026-08-13 -->

# Default rubric (v2)

Applies to every task graded under the rubric-grader QA loop (spec Phase A). Each criterion below is a pass/fail assertion the grader evaluates from the grading packet: `bd show` for the task, the SPEC doc, the diff of the files listed in `.qa-tracking/changed-files.txt`, the F7 completion contract returned by the specialist, and `LESSONS.md`. One-line justification per criterion. No numeric score theater — pass or fail.

The criteria are intentionally short and checkable. Where the criterion needs context (boundary-mock fidelity, F7 fields), the "Evidence that satisfies it" line names the artefact the grader looks at.

## Criteria

### C1. Behavior matches the task description and SPEC.

The shipped diff implements the behavior the task description asks for, and matches the goal + acceptance criteria stated in the attached SPEC doc (read via `bd_doc_read(task_id, name="spec")`). Out-of-scope behavior the SPEC explicitly excludes is NOT in the diff.

Evidence that satisfies it: a 1-2 sentence walk-through that maps every user-visible behavior in the SPEC to a code path in the diff (or to a deliberate, documented deferral in the F7 `decisions` array). A diff that adds plausibly-related behavior the SPEC does not name fails this criterion — that is scope creep.

### C2. Tests added exercise user behavior rather than implementation.

Where the diff introduces new behavior, the diff also introduces tests that assert against the user-visible contract (return shape, side effects, error envelope, accessibility role, status code) rather than against the implementation's private structure (function-name mocking, line-coverage gymnastics, internal control-flow assertions).

Evidence that satisfies it: at least one test in the diff that would still pass if the implementation were rewritten while keeping the user contract identical. A test that asserts only against private symbols, internal call counts, or framework boilerplate fails this criterion.

### C3. The F7 completion contract carries all seven fields with substantive `llm_observations`.

The specialist's structured completion payload includes `task_id`, `files_changed`, `tests_added`, `decisions`, `blockers`, `llm_observations`, and `context_coverage`. `llm_observations` is non-trivial narrative — what surprised the specialist, what was unclear, what they noticed and did not act on. A boilerplate one-liner like "no observations" fails this criterion (principle 9: `llm_observations` is mandatory and substantive).

Evidence that satisfies it: each of the seven fields is present and the `llm_observations` paragraph is the kind of thing a human engineer would say at a stand-up. C3 scores presence-of-seven plus the quality of `llm_observations`; the quality of `context_coverage` is C8's job, so a payload can pass C3 on presence and still fail C8 on substance.

### C4. No unrelated scope in the diff.

Every file the specialist touched serves the task. Drive-by refactors, formatting churn on untouched lines, and "while I'm here" cleanups that exceed the task brief fail this criterion — they should be filed as paired follow-up Beads tasks instead.

Evidence that satisfies it: the diff's file list maps cleanly to the SPEC's deliverables; any incidental change is either trivial (one-line typo fix) or explicitly justified in the `decisions` array.

### C5. J26 modules relevant to the diff are addressed.

Where the diff touches a domain covered by the J26 security taxonomy (SECRETS, INJECTION, AUTH, CONFIG, DEPS, AI, MOBILE, DATA — see `docs/AGENTS.md`), the diff demonstrates that the relevant modules were considered. Untouched J26 domains are out of scope.

Evidence that satisfies it: the `decisions` array (or the SPEC) names which J26 modules apply, and the diff shows defences in those modules (input validation at the trust boundary, parameterised queries, narrow CORS, audited logging, etc.). A diff that touches user input handling without naming INJECTION fails this criterion.

### C6. Docs updated where behavior changed.

When the diff changes user-visible behavior, the documentation that describes that behavior is updated in the same change. This includes `CHANGELOG.md`, README sections, `docs/*.md`, command help text, and SPEC docs the diff renders out of date.

Evidence that satisfies it: a docs-only file in `files_changed` paired with each behavioral change, or a deliberate `decisions` entry stating why a doc deferral is correct (e.g. an internal refactor that ships without user-visible change). A behavioral change that ships with no doc update and no deferral note fails this criterion.

### C7. Boundary-mock fidelity (LESSONS.md lesson 2).

When the diff introduces or modifies mocks of boundaries the project does not control (third-party HTTP APIs, external SDKs, system calls, message-bus payloads), every such mock derives its shape from a fixture extracted from the real downstream producer's spec (OpenAPI, proto file, SDK source, vendor docs). The fixture's source is cited in a comment, the `decisions` array, or `llm_observations`.

**Automatic needs_revision:** circular pass-through assertions are an immediate fail. A mock that feeds `body.error` so a test can assert `body.error` proves nothing — it tests the test's own setup, not the production behavior. Cite `LESSONS.md` lesson 2 in the justification.

Evidence that satisfies it: every new boundary mock points at a fixture file (`.fixtures/`, `__fixtures__/`, `testdata/`) carrying a snapshot of the producer's payload, and the fixture has a comment naming the source (URL, commit, SDK version). Tests assert against the producer's contract, not against the mock's own input.

### C8. `context_coverage` names what was read, what was skipped, and the largest unknown.

The F7 payload's seventh field records three things, in order: the sources the specialist actually read to ground the change; the sources they deliberately did NOT read, and why; and the largest remaining unknown the work ships on. It fails on the same three-way taxonomy C3 applies to `llm_observations` — **empty**, **boilerplate** ("read the relevant files", "full context gathered"), or **detached from the work**: sources named that the diff plainly does not depend on, or the file carrying the diff's central change missing from the list. A coverage note with no deliberate omission in it is boilerplate by construction, because there is always one.

This is not a new principle. It is the evidence-before-fix discipline (`docs/AGENTS.md`) applied *before* the change rather than after — that protocol arms only on bug-typed tasks, and the ordinary feature work that produced the motivating 14-PR speculative-fix chain never gets typed as a bug at all.

Evidence that satisfies it: named files or artefacts (paths, doc names, task ids, log lines) in the "read" part; at least one explicit omission carrying its reason; and an unknown concrete enough that a reviewer could act on it. Grade it against the diff, not against its own confidence — the sources named should be the ones the change actually depends on.

# DevOps rubric (v1)

Applied additionally when the task carries the `devops` label. Default criteria still apply; these add domain-specific checks pulled from `.claude/agents/devops.md`. The leverage is default + bugfix — these are the few devops-specific failure modes that recur.

## Criteria

### D1. Scripts are idempotent and re-runnable.

Install, uninstall, hook, and CI scripts in the diff produce the same end state when run twice in a row. A second run of `install.sh` does not double-write hooks, clobber prior settings, or fail because a directory already exists. A migration script that exits non-zero on its second run fails this criterion.

Evidence that satisfies it: every new script uses `mkdir -p`, conditional inserts, and idempotent label operations (`bd label add` returns success if already present); the `decisions` array documents any deliberately non-idempotent step (e.g. a one-shot data migration) and pairs it with a guard (lock file, completion sentinel) so a re-run is detected.

### D2. Graceful degradation on missing optional tools.

When the diff depends on an optional tool (gitleaks, shellcheck, a particular bd version, a specific CI runner image), the missing-tool path is handled: log a structured warning, fall back to a safe default, exit zero where the workflow allows. A hook that exits non-zero because `gitleaks` is not installed fails this criterion — that is not a developer-machine-portable failure mode.

Evidence that satisfies it: every new tool dependency is probed (`command -v tool >/dev/null`); the fallback path is documented in the script comments and tested at L1; the `decisions` array names the dependency and its installation hint.

### D3. No new permission prompts; autonomy preserved.

The diff does not add `permissions.deny` rules to `settings.json`, narrow specialist tool lists below the broad allow set, or introduce any user-facing approval step the plugin previously ran without. Principle 3 of the v3 plan is "full autonomy, no permission prompts" — every deny rule becomes a future approval prompt and breaks the workflow.

Evidence that satisfies it: a diff of `.claude/settings.json` shows only `permissions.allow` expansions, never `deny`; specialist tool frontmatter is unchanged or expanded; the `decisions` array calls out any new tool the broadened allow set covers.

### D4. Secrets and PII stay out of source, logs, and history.

Hardcoded API keys, tokens, passwords, private keys, committer emails, and PII are absent from the diff. Logs that the diff adds redact sensitive fields before writing. A commit that introduces an `.env` file with values, a personal email address in a script header, or unredacted PII in a log line fails this criterion (extends C5 / SECRETS + DATA).

Evidence that satisfies it: secrets read from a secret manager or environment variable at runtime; PII fields in new log lines are redacted (`***@`, `user_id=***`); a `gitleaks`-equivalent pass on the diff is clean, and the `decisions` array names the secrets the diff touches.

title: The SessionStart resolver auto-applies pins, writing tracked files into a change set it does not own
description:
PROMOTED from a session correction to a filed defect by operator ruling, 2026-08-15: same shape as R4-F1,
same remedy.

OBSERVED, 2026-08-14T04:58:10 local. A SessionStart fired workflow-model-apply.sh, which rewrote FOUR
TRACKED FILES - .claude/agents/{backend,devops,frontend}.md and .claude/settings.json - all four carrying
the identical mtime, the signature of one script run rather than hand edits. It applied D0's declared
implementer=sonnet-class, which was correct in itself. The defect is WHEN and INTO WHAT.

The write landed in the middle of an OPEN, UNRELATED change set (mdnc's), hours after that task's last
write and after its measurement runs. No files_changed list claimed those four paths. Had they been
approved with the rest, the approval would have attested to bytes no specialist produced and no reviewer
read - and the only reason it did not is that the discrepancy was noticed by hand.

THE RULING, applied from R4-F1: an automatic path must not write into a tree it does not own.
DETECT-AND-WARN, with an EXPLICIT APPLY step. The resolver should report 'the declared role map and the
applied pins disagree; run <command> to apply' and exit without writing. This is the same argument the
plan already makes for prevent-orchestrator-edits.sh: the structural guarantee beats the well-behaved
automatic action.

SECOND-ORDER, worth stating because it made a real finding harder to see: D0 shipped a tree whose declared
role map (model-roles: implementer=sonnet-class) and whose applied pins (agent files: claude-opus-5)
DISAGREED, and nothing surfaced that gap - which is task wyv. So the auto-apply was silently compensating
for a defect nobody could see, and doing it inside someone else's change set. Fixing the auto-write without
fixing wyv leaves the tree inconsistent instead; both belong in this batch.

WHY THIS IS P1 RATHER THAN UNTIDY:
- Every component spec goes to real lengths to isolate (mk_fixture, mktemp -d, per-fixture .beads). L1
  evidently does not, and nothing declares that difference. A reader who knows the component tier's
  discipline will assume it holds one tier down.
- The Stop hook runs make test on EVERY orchestrator turn. So this fires repeatedly and unattended, and
  its writes land in the same store the gate reads for review rounds, labels and approvals.
- It corrupts the evidence base of this very release. bd comments are the durable record - the thing
  0in1, 46w9 and rqer all made load-bearing. A test that writes comments to real tasks means the record
  can contain entries no agent authored.
- It compounds the gate-contention defect (39cy): the Stop hook's suite is not only competing for CPU
  with in-flight work, it is WRITING to shared state while doing so.

NEEDS: L1 must not touch the project's beads db. Either point model-roles.test.sh at a fixture db the
way the component tier does, or make model-select.sh apply refuse to write comments when a test
environment marker is set. Prefer the first - a production-code guard keyed on a test marker is the
harness the plan forbids.

ALSO WORTH ESTABLISHING: whether any OTHER L1 spec writes to the real store. This one was noticed only
because a MODEL SWITCH comment appeared on an unrelated task during an unrelated review. A census of L1
specs for real-db writes is the actual scope.

DISCOVERED-FROM: rqer QA round 2.

title: The gate has no resilience to bd version skew, and it half-fails: status keeps answering while the review-accounting reader goes dark
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-15 at HEAD 9488c69, live on this machine, not hypothetical.

THE STATE. .beads/ is at Dolt schema v65; the only bd binary on the box (/Users/edk0/.local/bin/bd) is
1.2.2 and understands up to v53. bd's own message names the cause: 'This database was migrated by the
accidental, untested v1.2.0/v1.2.1 release.'

SEQUENCE (established, not inferred): bd self-upgraded 1.1.2 -> 1.2.1 mid-session (already recorded on
omwx), 1.2.1 migrated the database to v65, bd then self-upgraded again to 1.2.2 which knows only v53.
NOT the daemon - it last logged a shutdown 2026-08-10T02:35:39Z, days before the skew, and no bd daemon
process is running. Exactly one binary exists.

THE PRODUCT DEFECT, WHICH IS THE POINT OF THIS TASK. Under skew the gate does not fail cleanly - it
half-fails, and the half that keeps working is the half that looks reassuring:

  qa-gate.sh status <tid>        -> {"ok":true, ... "status":"not-entered"}   rc=0
  review-check.sh gate <tid>     -> {"ok":false,"error_key":"bd_unavailable"}

review-check.sh gate is the reader that computes rounds, independence, open findings and the design
binding. With it dark, no review can complete: approve refuses. Meanwhile status answers cheerfully, so
a casual check says the gate is up.

bd_unavailable IS handled correctly - it carries no rounds key and is never read as 'zero rounds', which
is the discriminator review-check.sh:45-55 documents. The gate fails CLOSED, which is right. The defect
is that nothing in the plugin detects, reports, or survives the condition, and no script sets the
vendor's documented bypass:

  grep -rn 'IGNORE_SCHEMA_SKEW' .claude/ (excluding tests) -> no matches

RECOVERY IS BLOCKED ON A MISSING DEPENDENCY. The vendor guide
(github.com/gastownhall/beads/blob/v1.2.2/docs/RECOVERY-1.2.1.md) is reversible, loses no issue data,
and rolls the cursor v65 -> v53 - but step 2 requires the Dolt CLI, which is NOT INSTALLED here. So the
only path available today is BD_IGNORE_SCHEMA_SKEW=1, which bd itself offers and calls verified safe for
this schema range.

NEEDS, in order:
1. A session-start check that detects skew and says so LOUDLY, rather than letting the first
   review-check.sh call fail mid-flow. session-start.sh already carries a warning ladder; this is
   another rung.
2. A decision on whether the plugin sets the bypass itself. Argument against: it hides a real
   condition. Argument for: without it a mid-session tool upgrade silently disables the gate, and this
   arc has now watched bd self-upgrade THREE times unprompted (1.1.2 -> 1.2.1 -> 1.2.2).
3. A doctor check pairing the bd binary version against the database schema version, in the same shape
   as the existing DOCTOR_TOOL_COUNTS pinning.

DATA IS SAFE: 173 open / 12 in_progress read cleanly under the bypass, and a full 770MB .beads copy plus
a 391-issue export are snapshotted outside the repo.

RELATED: rbi (.beads/issues.jsonl is stale and fails silently with zeros) is CONFIRMED by this incident -
the tracked JSONL holds 354 issues dated 2026-08-11 while the live DB holds 391. CLAUDE.md calls that
file ground truth. It is not.

DISCOVERED-FROM: the rqer implementation round.

comments.author: username
comments.text:
TWO ADDITIONS, measured 2026-08-15 during the rqer fix round.

1. bd-mcp IS UNUSABLE UNDER SKEW, AND THE FIX SLOT ALREADY EXISTS. A specialist reported that every
bd-mcp tool call failed for the whole round because the MCP surface offers no way to set
BD_IGNORE_SCHEMA_SKEW=1; it fell back to shell bd throughout. But .mcp.json ALREADY declares an env block
for the server and it is empty:

    "bd": { "type": "stdio", "command": "node",
             "args": ["${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-.}/.claude/mcp/bd-mcp/bin/bd-mcp.js"],
             "env": {} }

So the remedy is a one-key change in a slot that exists, not new plumbing. Note the blast radius this
already had: every agent granted bd-mcp silently lost its task-tracker surface and had to discover the
shell fallback on its own. Two did. Nothing warned them.

2. THE GATE'S OWN VERIFICATION COMPETES WITH IN-FLIGHT SPECIALIST WORK — a separate defect, filed here
because it was found chasing this one.

The Stop hook runs the FULL L1 suite (make test, now ~29-32 minutes) on every orchestrator turn. Specialists
run their own suites concurrently. Nothing coordinates them. Measured consequences this session, all
previously attributed to other causes:
  - a specialist observed a second concurrent instance of approve-idempotency.sh it did not start
  - approve-idempotency.sh took 853s for one agent vs 751s for another on identical bytes
  - two component specs showed transient failures that did not reproduce in isolation (3x each)
  - QA recorded its own make test run as 'partly contended by the root session's own Stop-hook L1 run'

This is the same family as 9xl4 (no lease protocol) but it is NOT the same instance: 9xl4 is about
parallel implementers under D4. This is the gate competing with the work it is gating, on every turn,
today, with no D4 required. It also interacts with 7x33 (L2's slowest spec at 1.12x headroom against its
cap) - a cap sized on an idle run is the wrong cap when the Stop hook is running a full tier beside it.

NEEDS: either the Stop hook detects in-flight specialist work and defers, or measurement acquires the
lease 9xl4 will introduce. Do not fix by widening timeouts - that hides the contention rather than
resolving ownership.

DISCOVERED-FROM: the rqer fix round.

comments.text:
RECOVERY EXECUTED AND VERIFIED, 2026-08-15, by operator decision.

  dolt 2.3.0 installed (brew)
  backup taken first: 803MB full .beads copy OUTSIDE the repo, plus a 391-issue export
  cd .beads/embeddeddolt/beads
  dolt sql -q "DELETE FROM schema_migrations WHERE version > 53; CALL DOLT_ADD(...); CALL DOLT_COMMIT(...)"
  dolt commit regqllv34lbnkgdm56tasalg14gddbah

BEFORE                          AFTER
  max_version 65, 65 rows         max_version 53, 53 rows
  issues 397                      issues 397  (preserved)
  exactly 12 rows >53 (54..65)    none

VERIFIED WITHOUT THE BYPASS (env -u BD_IGNORE_SCHEMA_SKEW):
  bd list --status open                    -> 179 open, no skew error
  review-check.sh gate <rqer>              -> ok:true, rounds=2, rounds_basis=cycle, reviewer=qa-claude
  qa-gate.sh status <rqer>                 -> ok:true, status=approved
  git status --porcelain                   -> 0 (embeddeddolt/ is untracked; only its gate.lock is in git)

THE DARK READER IS LIT, AND ITS FIRST ANSWER CONFIRMS 0in1. rounds=2 / basis=cycle is rqer's two review
rounds counted correctly across a change set that moved between them — the exact accounting 0in1 shipped
and that nothing could observe while the reader was down.

THE FOUR RIDERS REMAIN OPEN and are the real work; the rollback only removed the symptom:
  R1 pin bd and disable unprompted self-upgrade. A dependency that migrates the EVIDENCE STORE's schema
     without asking is the hazard; the skew was its first symptom. bd self-upgraded three times this arc
     (1.1.2 -> 1.2.1 -> 1.2.2) with no prompt.
  R2 workflow-doctor check asserting binary-version vs store-schema compatibility, failing LOUDLY and
     NAMED, in the shape of the existing DOCTOR_TOOL_COUNTS pinning.
  R3 fix the half-failure INDEPENDENTLY of the rollback. qa-gate.sh status returned
     {ok:true, status:not-entered, rc=0} against an unreachable store. That is a FALSE SUCCESS REPORT and
     it survives the repair: unavailable is not not-entered. This is the finding; the skew was only how we
     found it.
  R4 set the bd-mcp env key in the slot .mcp.json already declares ("env": {} on the bd server), so an
     agent granted bd-mcp does not silently lose its whole task surface.

Plus: .beads/issues.jsonl holds 354 issues dated 2026-08-11 against 397 live. CLAUDE.md calls that file
ground truth, so that claim is CURRENTLY FALSE — either reconcile the file or correct the doc. Tracked

title: Batch review shape: N tasks sharing one change set have no first-class representation
description:
From QA round 1 of Batch B, 2026-08-14. Evidence: the approval comments on 0in1/nq5f/46w9.

FOUR SEPARATE SYMPTOMS OF ONE MISSING CONCEPT.
- The Stop gate attributes a change set to ONE current-task id, so escalation basis, round count and
  impact-report path all key on whichever id the slot happens to hold.
- Spawn-time IMPLEMENTER records land on whichever id the slot holds. In Batch B that meant NONE of the
  three tasks carries an IMPLEMENTER record at all - independence held trivially rather than by evidence,
  and 46w9's own new model=/pin= instrumentation had no record to write into. The instrumentation task
  was defeated by the shape it shipped under.
- approve's finalization (truncate + baseline refresh) is per-task, so approving sibling 2 after sibling 1
  refuses impact_report_stale, and the obvious recovery - regenerate over the now-empty tracker - would
  bind an EMPTY set. QA had to restore the tracker manually between approvals and disclosed each restore.
- The gate template emitted <TASK_ID_NEEDED> five times rather than naming a task.

DECIDE THE CANONICAL SHAPE, then make finalization batch-aware: either an umbrella task/epic owning the
change set with children as review units (epic-gate.sh already models sibling overlap), or per-task
change-set partitions.

NOT fixed inside Batch B: growing the change set mid-review is the hash-move class 0in1 exists to fix.

DISCOVERED-FROM: Batch B QA round 1 (0in1, nq5f, 46w9).

title: mdnc's other half: a DELETED governing artifact still takes the doc-only fast path, because the enumeration is built from entries that exist
description:
SPLIT OUT OF claude-workflow-plugin-mdnc, which directed "KERNEL PATH RESOLUTION plus an
EXPLICIT DELETION ARM". The resolution half SHIPPED under mdnc and is measured across the full
spelling matrix on macOS and Linux. THIS HALF DID NOT, and it is filed rather than half-built
because building it is not small - see the cost below. mdnc's operator instruction 7 ("if item 2
turns out not to be small, stop and report rather than growing it") is the reason this is a task
and not a rushed second commit.

STATE TODAY, MEASURED, not asserted. doc-only-classifier.test.sh legs 6h.3/6h.3b pin the
CURRENT behaviour so that closing it later is a loud test change rather than a silent drift -
the same convention leg 6c used for the design artifact before D1 closed it:

    DELETING .claude/agents/qa.md        -> DOC-ONLY   (fast path, reviewed_by=none)
    DELETING .claude/rubrics/default.md  -> DOC-ONLY
    DELETING CLAUDE.md                   -> DOC-ONLY
    DELETING docs/specs/T-1.md           -> DOC-ONLY
  discriminators in the same run: a surviving declared sibling is still reviewable, and an
  ordinary README.md is DOC-ONLY for its own reason.
  cmd: bash .claude/scripts/tests/doc-only-classifier.test.sh   (section 6h.3)

WHY NO REDUCTION CAN FIX IT. The governing set comes from `workflow-manifest.sh governing`,
which SCANS THE POST-CHANGE TREE. After the deletion there is no directory entry, so no row is
emitted, so an exact-match lookup has nothing to match however correctly the path is reduced.
The declaration survives the deletion; its RESULTS do not.

WHAT A FIX NEEDS - the declaration's RULES, not its results. workflow-manifest.sh states the
rules today as call arguments inside generate_rows and runtime_contract_rows:
  scan_flat workflow ".claude/agents" '*.md'      (4 scan_flat calls)
  scan_tree workflow ".claude/skills"             (4 scan_tree calls, with prune sets)
  emit_row  workflow ".claude-plugin/plugin.json" (~12 named files)
  emit_row  runtime-contract "CLAUDE.md"
  scan_declared_dir design-artifact "docs/specs" '*.md'

DESIGN THAT AVOIDS A SECOND VOCABULARY (the s5qf header forbids minting one, correctly):
add a `governing-rules` subcommand that re-runs governing_rows IN A SUBSHELL with emit_row /
scan_flat / scan_tree / scan_declared_dir SHADOWED BY RECORDERS, so the rules come from the one
list rather than a copy and cannot drift from it. Then verify-before-stop.sh evaluates a
non-existent path against those rows (exact name; dir+glob at maxdepth 1; dir+prunes
recursively, minus *.log).

WHY THAT IS NOT SMALL, stated so the next person does not rediscover it:
  * it adds a second consumer of workflow-manifest.sh whose output shape must stay stable;
  * the rule evaluator is a SECOND implementation of what `find` does (maxdepth, prune, -name),
    so the two can disagree - a scan/rule mismatch is a new false-verdict surface;
  * packaging-parity.test.sh TEXTUALLY parses generate_rows' surface lines and cross-checks them
    against install.ps1, so anything that reshapes those lines has to move three artifacts
    together;
  * `generate`'s output is frozen per release under manifests/ and byte-compared by the
    reproducibility assert, so the change has to prove it did not move a single row.

A CHEAPER PARTIAL EXISTS AND IS DELIBERATELY NOT TAKEN ALONE: runtime_contract_rows could emit
CLAUDE.md unconditionally (it is declared BY NAME, and that function is never called by
generate_rows, has no class, no upgrade verdict, no uninstall row and no frozen table). One
line, closes 1 of the 3 cases the operator named as reachable in ordinary operation. Shipping
only that and calling it "the deletion arm" would be a false closure on a family already
declared closed once - which is the exact defect mdnc exists to repair - so it is offered here
as an OPERATOR DECISION, not taken silently.

RELATED: claude-workflow-plugin-mdnc (resolution half, shipped), s5qf (the declaration), bbh
(the removed path-shape inference), and the workflow-manifest.sh GOVERNING-ARTIFACT-SURFACE
header, whose "WHAT IT DOES NOT REACH" note has named this case since s5qf shipped.

title: doc-only-classifier 6e2 skips a section on every Linux runner, so CI's STRICT_SECTIONS=1 l1-unit job fails on the first push
description:
FOUND BY: the first-ever Linux container run of the L1 tier (claude-workflow-plugin-mdnc,
`make test-linux`). This is the finding the container target was built to surface BEFORE a
first push, so that a red CI run would not have to be attributed between "the a9hh rewiring"
and "first Linux exposure".

MECHANISM. doc-only-classifier.test.sh's 6e2 symlink-spelling legs are guarded by

    GROOT_PHYS=$(cd "$GROOT" && pwd -P)
    if [ "$GROOT_PHYS" != "$GROOT" ]; then ... 3 legs ... else
        printf '  note: 6e2 symlink-spelling legs SKIPPED - this platform spells the\n'

The guard is correct in intent — a leg that cannot fail is worse than an absent one — but its
condition is a property of `mktemp`'s ROOT, not of the code under test. On macOS `mktemp -d`
returns /var/folders/... whose physical spelling is /private/var/folders/..., so the two differ
and the legs run. On Linux `mktemp -d` returns /tmp/... which is already physical, so the arm
fires on EVERY Linux runner, including every ubuntu-latest GitHub runner.

CONSEQUENCE. The l1-unit CI job sets STRICT_SECTIONS=1. A PARTIAL spec is RED under that flag.
So the job fails, with:

  Total: 37  Passed: 34  Failed: 3  Skipped: 0  Partial: 1
  PARTIAL - doc-only-classifier.test.sh - 1 section-level skip(s), 143 assertion(s) ran
  SECTION SKIPS ARE NOT COVERAGE: ...

  cmd: bash .claude/tests/linux/run-linux-tier.sh --tiers l1   (STRICT_SECTIONS=1 by default)
  at : 0de5ceb

Also note the ASSERTION COUNT moves with it: 3291 on macOS, 3288 on Linux - exactly the three
legs inside the arm. The completeness line alone would not have shown this; the assertion total
is what makes it attributable.

THE FIX IS NOT "DELETE THE GUARD". The legs need a root with two genuinely different spellings.
Build one: mktemp a directory, create a SYMLINK to it beside it, and drive the pair. Then the
precondition holds on every platform and the guard becomes unreachable rather than
platform-dependent. Prove it by running the spec in the Linux container and showing Partial: 0.

RELATED: the l1-unit job's header carries a section-granular sweep of "arms that could fire in
this job", taken at 535c89a. This arm landed AFTER that sweep (s5qf / fkm.3), which is exactly
the staleness STRICT_SECTIONS exists to catch - it worked, it just had nowhere to report until
there was a way to run the tier on Linux.

title: hash_file mis-reads GNU sha256sum's escaped output: a path with a newline or backslash dies on Linux, works on macOS
description:
FOUND BY: the first-ever Linux container run of the L1 tier (claude-workflow-plugin-mdnc,
`make test-linux`, ubuntu:24.04/aarch64, coreutils 9.4). NOT found by any macOS run, and it
cannot be: the two hash tools disagree only here.

MECHANISM. workflow-manifest.sh's `hash_file` reads the digest as `${raw%% *}`:

    sha256sum)  raw=$(sha256sum "$f" 2>/dev/null) || raw="" ; out="${raw%% *}"
    shasum)     raw=$(shasum -a 256 "$f" 2>/dev/null) || raw="" ; out="${raw%% *}"

GNU coreutils ESCAPES a filename containing a newline or a backslash: it prefixes the whole
output line with a literal backslash and writes `\n` for the newline. So `raw` begins with `\`,
`out` is 65 characters, the `[ "${#out}" -ne 64 ]` guard fires, hash_file exits 1, and the
caller gets an empty string. BSD `shasum` does not escape, so macOS never sees it.

MEASURED. `design-artifact.test.sh` leg 9.2 ("precondition: the newline spelling opens the
OUTSIDE decoy, not the real artifact") is the reproducer that already exists in the tier:

    macOS   : expected=<sha> actual=<sha>            PASS
    ubuntu  : expected=2120550733018a2a... actual=   FAIL

  cmd: bash .claude/tests/linux/run-linux-tier.sh --tiers l1
  at : 0de5ceb + the mdnc change set

BLAST RADIUS, in order of severity:
  * `workflow-manifest.sh hash-file <path>` returns nothing and exits 1 for any path whose name
    carries a newline or a backslash. On Linux only.
  * `generate` calls hash_file per row via emit_row, so a repo with a backslash in a scanned
    filename would make manifest generation DIE on Linux and succeed on macOS. Frozen tables
    are cut from that output.
  * qa-gate.sh design-record binds the design artifact's digest through the same path. The
    product behaviour there is fail-CLOSED (no digest, no record), which is the safe direction —
    but the D1 machinery deliberately handles hostile artifact paths, and on Linux one whole
    class of them cannot be hashed at all.

THE FIX IS SMALL AND SHOULD BE MEASURED, NOT REASONED ABOUT: feed the file on STDIN
(`sha256sum < "$f"`), which makes the tool print `<hash>  -` with no filename to escape. That
is exactly what .claude/tests/linux/repo-bytes.sh already does, and why. Pair it with a leg
that hashes a file whose name contains a backslash AND one whose name ends in a newline, on
both platforms, and prove the leg reddens against the shipped `${raw%% *}` read.

DO NOT close this by asserting the escaping does not happen: it is a documented GNU coreutils
behaviour and it is reproducible with `touch 'a\b'; sha256sum 'a\b'`.

title: .beads/issues.jsonl is stale and fails SILENTLY WITH ZEROS, while CLAUDE.md calls it ground truth
description:
MEASURED by the round-baseline backfill, 2026-08-13.

The export is stamped 2026-08-11 14:38 and has not moved since. Measured against live bd:
  fkm.2 (D0):  jsonl returns 0 comments, live has 24
  fkm.3 (D1):  jsonl returns 0 comments, live has 58
  a9hh:        jsonl holds 62 of 68 - missing iteration=11, the final two COMPLETION records, and the
               FINAL APPROVAL at change_set_hash 33ddc1c7

So a baseline built from the jsonl reports a9hh as approved at the WRONG HASH, and reports D0 and D1 as
having no review history at all.

THE FAILURE MODE IS ZEROS, NOT AN ERROR. A consumer that queries a task added after the export gets a
well-formed empty answer and no indication anything is missing. That is this release's own defect family
- a measurement that did not happen looking identical to one that returned nothing - sitting in the file
CLAUDE.md names as ground truth:

  'For multi-session continuity, refer to: .beads/issues.jsonl for Beads ground truth.'

It IS reliable for pre-2026-08-11 data: the backfill verified it exact against live bd on 17 Phase P
tasks. So the fix is not distrust, it is freshness that announces itself.

NEEDS: either regenerate the export as part of the commit flow so it cannot lag, or have consumers read
live bd (bd comments <id> --json) and demote the jsonl in CLAUDE.md from 'ground truth' to what it is - a
snapshot with a date. If it stays, it must carry its own staleness loudly: a consumer asking for a task
newer than the export stamp should get an error, not an empty list. Pair with a leg that queries a
post-export task and asserts a loud failure, plus a control proving a pre-export task still answers.

DISCOVERED-FROM: the review-round baseline backfill.

comments.author: username
comments.text:
BLOCKED-BY j7kk (evidence-layer stabilization). DO NOT FIX THIS BY RUNNING bd export UNTIL QUARANTINE LANDS.

MEASURED 2026-08-15 by the L1 contamination census, at dolt HEAD 84rgg6ubp38nn09qpsl9eev6emsa4scg,
git c5d6706.

title: iteration= on review records is caller-supplied, so rounds collide and finding IDs are ambiguous across concurrent reviewers
description:
MEASURED by the backfill, 2026-08-13. qa-gate.sh interpolates a caller-supplied $iter into the
REVIEW-ARTIFACT grammar rather than deriving it.

OBSERVED COLLISIONS, all in shipped records:
- fkm.3 (D1) has TWO iteration=1 and TWO iteration=5 - and BOTH iteration=5 records emit a finding id
  R5-F1, from different reviewers, describing different defects.
- fkm.3's iteration=7 was filed BEFORE its iteration=6.
- a9hh has no iteration=10 at all.
- qzv's single artifact says iteration=7 because it continued 94d's session counter.

CONSEQUENCE. Round counts derived from iteration= are wrong in both directions, and a finding cited as
'R5-F1' is ambiguous where two lanes review the same hash. Dual-family review makes this normal, not
exceptional - and D4's PARALLEL IMPLEMENTERS make it strictly worse, because concurrent units will
produce concurrent reviews of sibling change sets.

FIX: derive iteration from a count of existing anchored REVIEW-ARTIFACT v1 records for that task rather
than accepting it, and add lane=<reviewer-id> and round=<derived> so finding ids cannot collide across
concurrent reviewers.

Note the counting discipline this also requires, measured: EVERY record grep must be ANCHORED AT COLUMN
0, because prose that quotes the record grammar inflates counts - 2ty reads as 3 blocks instead of 1 and
3 artifacts instead of 2; fkm.3 reads as 10 artifacts instead of 9; fkm.2 matches a spurious
'reviewer=top' quoted out of the model-roles file. 2ty is itself the fix for this over-count class.

DISCOVERED-FROM: the review-round baseline backfill.

title: The IMPLEMENTER and COMPLETION records carry no model, and reviewer_model restates config by spec while misreporting in practice
description:
OPERATOR DIRECTIVE: instrument BEFORE D4, because D4 spawns parallel implementers and the open question
'did the tier change cost rounds' cannot be answered afterwards from records that do not exist.

MEASURED by the backfill, 2026-08-13. Per-task model attribution is NOT RECOVERABLE from any existing
record:
- 'IMPLEMENTER: role=<r> task=<t> at <ts>' carries role and timestamp only.
- COMPLETION v1's declared field set is task_id, role, files_changed, tests_added, decisions, blockers,
  llm_observations, context_coverage. No model field.
- reviewer_model in REVIEW-ARTIFACT v1 IS NOT EVIDENCE. qa.md:397 instructs the reviewer to fill it
  from 'your own pinned model, from this file's model: frontmatter' - BY SPEC IT RESTATES CONFIG. And it
  does not even do that: qa.md's pin has been claude-fable-5 since 45c833d (2026-07-25), yet ~30 of ~40
  qa-claude records from 2026-08-04 self-report claude-opus-5[1m], matching the ROOT SESSION model in
  session-model-drift.json. fkm.1.11 flips mid-task (fable on iterations 1-2, opus[1m] from iteration 3)
  with no config change in between.

title: A role-class config change is INERT until the resolver runs, and nothing surfaces the gap: D0's tier flip never reached any agent file
description:
MEASURED by the round-baseline backfill, 2026-08-13, and verified independently by the orchestrator.

  git show HEAD:.claude/model-roles       -> implementer=sonnet-class   (set by acc4ce1, D0)
  git show HEAD:.claude/agents/devops.md  -> model: claude-opus-5
  git log -p --follow .claude/agents/devops.md | grep '^[+-]model:'
      -> last change f980626, 2026-07-25 (opus-4-8 -> opus-5). NO SONNET PIN WAS EVER WRITTEN.
  jq '.resolved_at, .roles.implementer' .claude/.qa-tracking/model-roles-resolved.json
      -> 2026-08-10T08:41:33Z, claude-opus-5   # the resolver last ran TWO DAYS BEFORE D0 shipped

CONSEQUENCE. D0 shipped a deliberate product decision - implementer opus-class -> sonnet-class - with a
recorded rider to track review rounds before and after and revert if they rose. The flip's entire effect
depends on model-select.sh cmd_apply rewriting agent frontmatter at SessionStart. That has not fired
since. So Phase D1 ran on claude-opus-5, the rider is UNTESTED rather than falsified, and THERE IS NO
'AFTER' SAMPLE AT ALL. Nobody noticed across an entire phase.

This is not the resolver malfunctioning - cmd_apply does what it says when it runs. The defect is that
NOTHING REPORTS THE GAP between configured and applied. D0 built missing_keys and SessionStart Warning
10 for keys that are ABSENT; there is no equivalent for keys that are PRESENT AND UNAPPLIED. A config
file can assert one world while every agent runs in another, silently, indefinitely.

THE FIX (operator directive, before D4): a resolver-drift check at SessionStart comparing
.claude/model-roles strategies against LIVE agent frontmatter, failing loudly on mismatch.
.claude/.qa-tracking/model-roles-resolved.json already holds one side of that comparison. Per
.claude/tests/README.md the check ships with a negative control and at least one leg observing the
shipped artifact running.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE RIDER: D4 spawns PARALLEL implementers. A silent divergence between the model
the config names and the model that runs makes every per-unit escalation claim in D0 unverifiable in
production, not just offline - which is a stronger statement than correction 13's disclaimer.

DISCOVERED-FROM: the review-round baseline backfill (operator directive, pre-D4 instrumentation).

title: Deleting an s5qf-declared governing artifact escapes the veto and takes the doc-only fast path
description:
Found by sol-codex (R1-F4) during Phase D1 review; qa-claude reproduced it and ruled it PRE-EXISTING
for every s5qf-declared path rather than introduced by D1. Filed per CONTRIBUTING as a new task.

MECHANISM. The governing declaration is generated by SCANNING FILES THAT EXIST in the post-change
tree. After a deletion the file is gone, so no governing row is emitted for it. The tracked deleted
path still ends in a documentation suffix, so the Stop classifier's exact-path governing lookup cannot
veto it, and is_doc_only_path matches. A change set consisting of the DELETION of a governing artifact
is therefore auto-approved with reviewed_by=none.

SCOPE, per qa-claude: this is NOT specific to docs/specs. It applies to every path s5qf declared -
.claude/agents/*.md, .claude/rubrics/*.md, CLAUDE.md, and now the design-artifact directory. Deleting
CLAUDE.md, or an agent prompt, takes the ungated exit today.

WHY THE EXISTING DISCLOSURE DOES NOT COVER IT. The shipped content-veto header (verify-before-stop.sh,
DOC-CONTENT-VETO region) argues that an unresolvable path yields no evidence and that 'deleting
documentation is a legitimate doc-only commit, and a deleted file ships no content, so
unresolvable => reviewable would deadlock it while buying no safety at all'. That reasoning is sound
for the CONTENT veto and does NOT transfer to the GOVERNING veto: the content veto asks what a file
IS, and a deleted file is nothing; the governing veto asks what the PROJECT DECLARES, and the project
still declares that path. Deleting a declared governing artifact IS the behaviour change, not the
absence of one.

NEEDS: a decision on whether the governing lookup should consult the DECLARATION (which survives
deletion) rather than the post-change filesystem scan. Note the declaration for named entries
(CLAUDE.md via runtime_contract_rows) is knowable without scanning; the design-artifact DIRECTORY form
is not, since artifacts are named per task - so a deletion under a declared directory may need the
tracker's own record of the deleted path. Pair with a leg that deletes a declared artifact and asserts
the Stop refuses, plus an anti-overreach control proving an ordinary doc deletion still fast-paths.

RELATED: claude-workflow-plugin-s5qf (shipped the declaration), claude-workflow-plugin-bbh (removed the
path-shape inference the content veto replaced).

WIDENED by qa-claude during Phase D1 review round 4, 2026-08-12. The declared-path veto is far weaker
than 'deletion escapes it'. It is defeated by A BARE DOT.

governing_artifact_origin (verify-before-stop.sh:1242) reduces an incoming path by LITERAL PREFIX
STRIP with no canonicalisation, then looks the result up as an exact key. So any non-canonical
spelling of a declared artifact misses the lookup and classifies DOC-ONLY. Measured with controls
holding:

  $ROOT/./docs/specs/T-1.md          -> DOC-ONLY
  docs/./specs/T-1.md                -> DOC-ONLY
  docs/specs/../specs/T-1.md         -> DOC-ONLY
  .claude/agents/../agents/qa.md     -> DOC-ONLY

Uniform across EVERY s5qf-declared path - agent prompts, rubrics, CLAUDE.md, and now the design
artifact directory. The canonical spelling is vetoed correctly; every equivalent spelling is not.

CONSEQUENCE FOR SCOPE, which is why this is recorded here rather than as a third task: it discounts
how much the two D1-round findings (find not descending a symlinked declared directory; find failing
open on an enumeration error) actually ADD to the reviewed_by=none exposure. qa-claude's words: 'the
veto they defeat is already defeatable by a dot.' Fixing the D1 halves without fixing this leaves the
front door open while sealing two windows.

NEEDS: canonicalise before the lookup, on both sides - the declaration and the incoming path - or
compare by resolved identity rather than by string. Note s5qf deliberately chose an EXACT-PATH match
over a path-shape inference, and that choice is still right; the defect is that an exact match over
un-normalised strings is not an exact match over paths. Pair with legs driving each non-canonical
spelling above, plus the anti-overreach control that an ordinary doc in a declared directory still
fast-paths.

QA DISCLOSED A CONTROL FAILURE IN FINDING THIS, worth recording: its first harness returned DOC-ONLY
for EVERY path and would have supported a much larger claim. The extracted library resolved its tool
path from BASH_SOURCE, so with the library outside the fixture's scripts dir the governing set was
empty and the veto never ran at all. It caught this because CLAUDE.md - a path it KNEW was declared -

SCOPE SPLIT, and the reason for it, recorded before the work is handed back.

The directive was "KERNEL PATH RESOLUTION plus an EXPLICIT DELETION ARM". The RESOLUTION half is
done and measured across the whole required matrix on both platforms. The DELETION half is NOT
done: it is filed as claude-workflow-plugin-e4ox with a costed design, per operator instruction 7
("if item 2 turns out not to be small, stop and report rather than growing it").

WHY THE TWO HALVES ARE NOT THE SAME SIZE, which was not obvious until the mechanism was read:

* RESOLUTION is one function's control flow. The shipped reduction chained its attempts with
  `elif`, so the FIRST attempt that produced a string won and the rest were never tried —
  and producing a string is not finding the artifact. The fix is "every reduction is a
  CANDIDATE and any hit wins", plus two candidates handed to `cd` / `cd -P` instead of to
  string surgery. Confined to governing_artifact_origin in verify-before-stop.sh.

* THE DELETION ARM needs the declaration's RULES rather than its RESULTS, because the
  enumeration is built by SCANNING THE POST-CHANGE TREE and a deleted file emits no row —
  no reduction, however correct, can match a row that does not exist. Exporting the rules
  means a new surface on workflow-manifest.sh, whose `generate` output is frozen per release
  under manifests/ and whose generate_rows lines are TEXTUALLY PARSED by
  packaging-parity.test.sh and hand-mirrored in install.ps1. e4ox carries the design (shadow
  the four emitters in a subshell and re-run governing_rows, so the rules come from the one
  list rather than a copy) and the four reasons it is not small.

A CHEAPER PARTIAL WAS AVAILABLE AND DELIBERATELY NOT TAKEN: runtime_contract_rows could emit
CLAUDE.md unconditionally — one line, no frozen table touched — closing 1 of the 3 cases the
operator named as reachable in ordinary operation. Shipping that and calling it "the deletion
arm" would be a false closure on a family already declared closed once, which is the precise
defect this task exists to repair. It is offered in e4ox as an operator decision instead.

THE RESIDUAL IS MEASURED, NOT DESCRIBED. doc-only-classifier.test.sh 6h.3/6h.3b/6h.3c/6h.3d
drive the deletion of an agent prompt, a rubric, CLAUDE.md and a design artifact, pin the
current DOC-ONLY verdict, and carry two discriminators (a surviving declared sibling is still
reviewable; an ordinary README.md is DOC-ONLY for its own reason) so the legs cannot pass
because the classifier died. Closing e4ox will be a loud test change — the same convention leg
6c used for the design artifact before D1 closed it.

ONE THING THE MATRIX FOUND THAT REASONING HAD MISSED, worth recording because it is the second
time in this arc a "resolve it properly" instinct was wrong in the same direction: with ONLY
the physical (`cd -P`) candidate, an artifact under a declared directory that is itself a
SYMLINK OUT OF THE TREE went back to DOC-ONLY for the dot spelling — the physical answer leaves
the root entirely, so containment refuses it. That is fkm.3's own R4-F3 shape reached from the
consumer side. The LOGICAL (`cd`) candidate is what answers it, and leg 6h.1 is the fixture.
Measured, not predicted: the first build of the fix shipped that hole and the probe caught it.

The work is strong and most of it is confirmed. I independently reproduced every number
reported: host L1 37/37, Partial 0, 3400 assertions, floor HELD, rc=0; container L1 37/37,
36 passed, 1 failed, Partial 1, 3397 assertions, bytes MATCH; make lint rc=0 with the new

attribution holds; a7mq and hzv8 both reproduce as Linux-ONLY (design-artifact passes on the

the bd amd64 digest is byte-identical to .github/workflows/test.yml and both node digests
match nodejs.org's own SHASUMS256.txt; the 7 fixture copies are byte-identical to the shipped
script; and L2 genuinely does not read those copies (it builds a synthetic tree under
COMPONENT_FIXTURE_PATH), so the disclosed staleness of the container L2 is immaterial to the
code under review.

=== MUST FIX (R1-F1, HIGH) ===
THE CHANGE IS NOT MONOTONE. The invariant stated in `decisions` ("can only turn DOC-ONLY into
reviewable and never the reverse") and in the GOV-PATH-RESOLUTION header ("Every candidate can
only ADD a hit") is FALSE, in the fail-open direction, at TWO sites.

You attacked the candidate you ADDED. Candidate 5 (logical `cd`) is sound: it can only add
hits, its over-reach is toward more review, and I could not falsify it — your argument for it
is correct and I am not asking you to change it. The defect is in the candidate you CHANGED
without recording that you changed it:

  verify-before-stop.sh:1478   `cd "$pdir" && pwd -P`  ->  `cd -P "$pdir" && $PWD`
  verify-before-stop.sh:1198   same substitution on PROJECT_DIR, for _GOV_ROOT_PHYS

Those are different functions. Old = physical-resolve(lexical-collapse(p)). New candidate 4 =
kernel-physical(p). They diverge exactly when a symlink precedes a `..` — the divergence your
own header documents. `cd -P` was added; the old composition was DROPPED. That is a
substitution, not an addition, and it deletes a reduction the shipped code had.

MEASURED, both platforms, against HEAD extracted with the test's own awk extractor.
34-spelling sweep, macOS bash 3.2.57: 9 verdicts moved DOC-ONLY->reviewable (your fix, correct)
and ONE moved the wrong way:

  $P/alias/.claude/x/../agents/qa.md    HEAD: reviewable    now: DOC-ONLY
  ($P/alias -> proj ; proj/.claude/x -> a directory outside the tree)

Reproduced identically on ubuntu:24.04 bash 5.2.21 aarch64, in your own container, with harness
controls asserted — my first container attempt returned all-reviewable on an empty mount and I
discarded it rather than report it.

SECOND SITE, same substitution, same direction, worse blast radius. With PROJECT_DIR spelled
`$R/.claude/x/../..` the lexical collapse is $R while `cd -P` lands two levels out, so
_GOV_ROOT_PHYS becomes a WRONG ROOT and every absolute governing path misses:

  $R/.claude/agents/qa.md    HEAD: reviewable    now: DOC-ONLY
  (control: with a canonical PROJECT_DIR the same path is still reviewable)

The header at :1183-1189 argues confidently for `-P` here on the grounds that "the kernel would
land in the parent of link's TARGET ... which is the case this function exists to get right".
For the ROOT computation that is backwards: you want the physical location of the directory the
project logically IS, which is what `pwd -P` after a logical `cd` gives you.

REMEDY, TESTED: never remove a reduction, only add. That is your own thesis — the `elif` bug was
removal by short-circuit, this is removal by substitution; apply the thesis one level up and the
residual disappears. I re-added the old composition as a sixth candidate (`cd -P` on the logical
answer, compared against _GOV_ROOT_PHYS) and re-ran the same sweep on both platforms: old->remedy
is strictly monotone (ZERO reviewable->DOC-ONLY), the alias case is closed, and zero ordinary-doc
controls moved. It costs one subshell on the already-slow miss path. Take that shape or another,
but the property has to hold at both sites.

BOUNDARY, so you do not have to guess at the scope: the change is monotone EXCEPT where the
logical parent resolves outside both root spellings while its physical resolution lands inside
_GOV_ROOT_PHYS. That is the whole gap; I enumerated the cases rather than sampling.

PAIR IT. No leg in the 109 new assertions can see this: section 6h reaches the project only by
its literal root or relatively, so an aliased route is unreachable from the matrix, and section
9's METAs compare shipped-vs-region-stripped, never shipped-vs-HEAD. Add a 6h leg driving the
alias route (a symlink to the project root, plus a `..` after an intermediate symlink) with its
ordinary-doc control, and a leg pinning _GOV_ROOT_PHYS for a `..`-bearing PROJECT_DIR.

WHY THIS IS HIGH rather than the MEDIUM its traffic would suggest. Reachability is narrow at both
sites and I am not claiming otherwise. The severity is what the falsified invariant costs: it is
the licence for the safety argument being directional rather than exhaustive, and this task exists
to repair a false closure on a family already declared closed TWICE. Shipping the repair with a
fresh false claim in the same function's header would be the third instance of the same failure in
the same family, which is the one outcome the operator directive singles out as worse than an open
bug.

=== ADVISORY, and I ask for F2/F3 in this round because the round is open ===

R1-F2 (MEDIUM) run-linux-tier.sh:228-239, :312 — the tier CAN report a false green, which is
exactly what you asked me to judge. When repo-bytes.sh fails to yield a digest on either side,
BYTES_STATUS goes UNCHECKED and control FALLS THROUGH: tiers run and a green run prints the
unqualified "VERDICT: every requested tier ran on Linux and passed" and exits 0. Measured through
your own DOCKER= seam, four cells: byte-check ok/pass -> 0; byte-check UNAVAILABLE/pass -> 0;
unavailable/fail -> 1; ok/fail -> 1. Worse, :312 gates the post-run recheck on BYTES_STATUS=MATCH,
so the same condition also disables the MOVED-UNDER-THE-RUN detector — the one that shipped because
it bit you for 13 bogus L2 failures. A byte MISMATCH correctly refuses at 2; only cannot-measure
falls through. Your own contract says exit 2 is "the bar was not measured", and README.md:99 says
the mount is "*verified* every run ... a checked claim rather than an asserted one". One branch
fixes it: carry UNCHECKED to exit 2 and put the degradation in the VERDICT line, not only in a
report row four lines above it.

To be clear about the rest of that answer, because most of it is a pass: NOT RUN can NOT be
mistaken for a pass. I drove five paths — both tiers green -> 0; l1 fails and l2 skipped -> exit 2
INCOMPLETE naming l2; --keep-going with both failing -> 1; bad tier name -> 2; image absent with
--no-build -> 2. The per-tier loop that forces 2 for any requested-but-unrun tier is the right
design and it works. The read-only mount plus a per-run two-sided digest is a genuinely stronger
claim than a copy, and it is sound when it runs; its two honest bounds are that it covers tracked
paths only (so .claude/tests/linux/* is outside its own verification until committed) and F2.

R1-F3 (MEDIUM) — the tier's own four checks (mount identity, mid-run drift, stale image,
exit discipline) ship with NO negative control and NO UNPAIRED declaration. Verified: nothing under
.claude/scripts/tests or .claude/tests/{component,e2e,mutation} references run-linux-tier.sh,
repo-bytes.sh or tests/linux; run-tests.sh discovers only $TESTS_DIR/*.sh at maxdepth 1, and
EXPECTED_SPECS=37 is unchanged, so the floor cannot notice. You DID declare the GOV-LITERAL-PREFIX
residual UNPAIRED with a reason in the same change, so the convention was known and applied to one
half only. This is not pedantry: F2 is precisely what a negative control would have caught, it took
me a ~40-line stub to find, and the ${DOCKER:-docker} seam that makes the driver testable already
exists by design. A tier whose thesis is "every failure mode is loud" should carry one leg that
watches a failure mode be loud.

R1-F4 (LOW) run-linux-tier.sh:201-208 — when DOCKERFILE_SHA is empty the staleness test
short-circuits and BUILD_NOTE still reads "reused (Dockerfile digest matches the image label)".
Nothing was compared. Say "staleness UNCHECKED (no sha256 tool)".

R1-F5 (LOW) — a7mq, hzv8, ogi8 and e4ox were all filed with ZERO dependency edges (bd_list_deps:
0 blockers, 0 dependents on each). e4ox, mdnc's own other half, has no discovered-from back to
mdnc. Add those edges, and hang blocks-edges from a7mq and hzv8 onto whatever task asserts CI
greenness — a9hh is closed, so today nothing stops the next push walking into findings this change
already paid to discover.

=== THE TWO SCOPE QUESTIONS ===

1. a7mq / hzv8 STAY FILED — do not pull them into Batch A. The directive bought a separation of two
unknowns; fixing the findings inside the change set that first produced them spends that separation
immediately, and the tier's first-run evidence (three real Linux defects, unfixed, on named bytes)
is the artifact that proves the tier works. You were told to report Linux breakage rather than patch
the tier green and you did; reversing that at review time punishes the compliance. Neither is
release-authorising — they red a CI job that is not green today regardless. But "filed" is only
worth something with edges on it, which is R1-F5: wire them before the push, do not fix them here.

2. THE HOST-L2 COMPOSITE DOES NOT NEED RE-RUNNING FOR ITS OWN SAKE, and the question resolves
itself. Your disclosure is correct and the weakness is real — three runs cannot rule out the
cross-spec interference a single run measures, and landing exactly on baseline is consistent with
correctness without establishing it. But the container L2 ran end to end in one process over the
final verify-before-stop.sh bytes (I verified both last edits touch only doc-only-classifier.test.sh
and the 7 fixture copies, and that L2 reads neither), and its 43-vs-42 delta is explained by the bd
version difference you measured rather than assumed. So a single-run end-to-end L2 covering the code
under review already exists. Since R1-F1 changes verify-before-stop.sh again, both L2 runs go stale
anyway: the fix round must produce a single-run host L2 over the corrected bytes, which closes the
question without asking for it twice.

=== WHAT IS PROVEN WHERE, for the approval that follows ===
  macOS / BSD / bash 3.2.57   — the full 6h matrix and section-9 METAs; host L1 37/37, 3400
                                assertions, Partial 0, floor HELD, rc=0; make lint rc=0.
  linux/arm64 / GNU / bash 5.2.21 — the same 6h matrix at identical counts; container L1 37/37,
                                36 passed, 1 failed (a7mq), Partial 1 (hzv8), 3397 assertions,
                                mount digest MATCH over 670 files / 1 link. Plus, from my own
                                probe, the kernel-vs-lexical divergence and R1-F1 itself.
  linux/amd64                 — UNEXERCISED. CWP_LINUX_PLATFORM exists and has never been run;
                                CI is amd64. Both findings so far are GNU-vs-BSD tooling and a
                                mktemp root shape, neither arch-sensitive, but that is an argument,
                                not a measurement, and it should stay labelled as one.
  OPEN RESIDUAL               — e4ox, the deletion arm, pinned by 6h.3b with two discriminators.

ON THE SCOPE SPLIT: I ENDORSE IT, without reservation. Declining the one-line CLAUDE.md partial was
right for exactly the reason you gave — shipping 1 of 3 named cases AS "the deletion arm" would be a
false closure on a family already declared closed once, which is the defect this task exists to
repair. 6h.3b pinning the current DOC-ONLY verdict with a surviving-sibling discriminator is the
correct way to carry an open residual, and it makes closing e4ox a loud test change.

title: The gate's own reconcile stage moves change_set_hash mid-review, so a completed review round counts as ZERO
description:
MEASURED on claude-workflow-plugin-fkm.3 (Phase D1), 2026-08-12.

SEQUENCE.
1. Orchestrator computes change_set_hash = 05fdd298... and builds a review packet against it.
2. sol-codex reviews and returns FOUR HIGH findings.
3. Meanwhile a Stop hook fires. Its detection stage runs reconcile_tracker (the P1/94d work), which
   adds git-visible paths the post-edit tracker had missed: tracker goes to 18 distinct paths.
4. change_set_hash is now 7b8a0107..., because it hashes the sorted PATH LIST.
5. The review artifact, correctly, records reviewed_hash=05fdd298 - the hash it was given.

MEASURED CONSEQUENCE:
  review-check.sh gate --change-set-hash 7b8a0107...  ->  {"rounds":0}
  review-check.sh gate --change-set-hash 05fdd298...  ->  {"rounds":1}
The gate believes NO reviewer has examined this change set. Four HIGH findings are invisible to it.

THE CONTENT NEVER MOVED. Verified: the diff of the three shipped scripts sol reviewed is
byte-identical before and after (cmp of the captured diff vs a fresh one). The tree hash excluding
.beads was stable at 89c1ab60 across the whole review. Only the tracker's PATH LIST grew.

WHY THIS IS WORSE THAN k0mc, NOT THE SAME BUG. k0mc is the over-claiming direction: content changes,
the path list does not, so an approval attests to bytes nobody read. This is the UNDER-claiming
direction: content is identical, the path list grows, and a real review with real findings does not
count. Both follow from hashing the path list, but this one has a specific and repeatable trigger -
THE GATE'S OWN HOUSEKEEPING INVALIDATES REVIEWS THAT ARE IN FLIGHT.

SECOND-ORDER, and this is the dangerous part: J21 suppresses escalation while 'a review cycle is OPEN
and no REVIEW-ARTIFACT record exists for this change set' (2ty). With rounds=0 that suppression fires
even though a reviewer HAS disagreed, at HIGH, four times. The gate reports 'no reviewer has disagreed
with anything' - a sentence that is false and that the gate cannot know is false.

NEEDS a decision, not just a patch. Candidates:
- Bind reviews to a CONTENT hash (v5 already builds one for design artifacts: workflow-manifest.sh
  hash-file over raw bytes, refusing before hashing). The design side is now stricter than the code
  side, which is backwards.
- Or: make rounds match on a set-RELATION rather than equality - a review of a subset still counts,
  and the gate says which paths were not covered.
- Or at minimum: when rounds=0 but a REVIEW-ARTIFACT exists for a DIFFERENT hash on the same task,
  say so loudly instead of reporting silence. Silence and 'reviewed, superseded' must not look alike.

Pair with a leg that reproduces the sequence above and a control proving the leg reds when the
relation is restored.

RELATED: claude-workflow-plugin-k0mc (approve rebinds a subset), claude-workflow-plugin-fkm.1.20
(freshness detects drift but not loss), claude-workflow-plugin-2ty (the suppression that misfires).
DISCOVERED-FROM: Phase D1 (fkm.3) review round 1.

THIS IS AN ACCOUNTING BUG, NOT A HASHING BUG. Content held constant; the path set moved LEGITIMATELY
(the Stop hook's own reconcile stage added git-visible paths the post-edit tracker had missed - that
is reconcile working). The defect is that ROUNDS AND FINDINGS ARE KEYED TO HASH IDENTITY. That is the
same error fkm.1.19 identified from a different angle: review-check.sh gate reads only the LATEST
review artifact.

THE FIX IS A REVIEW-THREAD IDENTITY THAT SURVIVES CHANGE-SET EVOLUTION - not a change to what is
hashed. A review of an earlier path set is still a review OF THIS TASK'S WORK; it may be superseded,
it is not void. The thread must carry forward and the gate must be able to say 'reviewed at an earlier
set, N paths added since' instead of silence.

WHY NON-NEGOTIABLE: the gate printed 'no reviewer has disagreed with anything' while FOUR HIGH findings
sat recorded on the task. That sentence is false, and the gate cannot know it is false. A gate that
reports confidently on evidence it cannot see is this release's own defect family, in the release's own
gate. D2 IS the review loop; building it on an accounting that can silently zero a review is
disqualifying.

Do NOT fix this by making change_set_hash content-based - see k0mc for that decision, which is separate
and later.

title: The repo's plan mirror is the uncorrected DIRECTIVE, not the plan: every specialist brief has cited sections that do not exist
description:
Found while verifying Phase D1 anchors, 2026-08-12.

MEASURED:
  /Users/edk0/.claude/plans/v5-0-0-design-stateless-wilkinson.md  827 lines, 56401 bytes
  docs/plans/v5-design-phase.md                                   217 lines, 35092 bytes
These are DIFFERENT DOCUMENTS, not two versions of one. Section structure:
  authoritative: Context / Decisions locked / CORRECTIONS TO THE DIRECTIVE / Setup / Phase P /
                 Phase D0 - role classes 3 to 5 / Phases D1-D6 / Phase D7 / Verification / Risks
  mirrored:      Read first / Cross-cutting principles / Accountability model / Phase P /
                 Phase D0 - Role expansion and model mapping / ... / Phase D7

The repo copy is the ORIGINAL DIRECTIVE. The PLAN - which exists because the directive is wrong in
FOURTEEN specific, enumerated ways - was never mirrored. The plan's own Setup section says
'cp <this directive> docs/plans/v5-design-phase.md', so this is the documented setup working as
written; the DEFECT is the consequence, not the copy.

CONSEQUENCE, MEASURED. Orchestrator briefs have said things like: read 'docs/plans/v5-design-phase.md
section Phase D0 - role classes 3 to 5 plus corrections 7, 11, 13, 14 in section Corrections to the
directive'. NEITHER of those sections exists in that file. The D0 specialist reported 'several plan
line numbers had drifted, I located those by content' - it was reading a different document. Work has
been correct only because the orchestrator carried the corrections inline in every brief, which is
fragile and does not survive a new session, a new orchestrator, or a compaction.

It also produced a false finding in the D1 verification: 'the plan contradicts itself, D1 bullet 1
says extend the PreToolUse block and correction 9 says do not path-scope it'. Those are the DIRECTIVE
and the PLAN respectively; the correction layer exists precisely to overrule the directive. A verifier
reading only the repo cannot see that.

NEEDS: mirror the authoritative plan into the repo so the corrections layer is readable by anyone the
work is delegated to, and keep the directive as the input it is - two files with unambiguous names,
indexed in docs/plans/README.md following the v4.1 entry format. Then fix every brief-facing reference.
Note docs/ is NOT scanned by workflow-manifest.sh, so neither file becomes an install row.

BLOCKS: D2-D7 briefing quality. Not D1's implementation, but D1 is the right moment to fix it.
