title: qa-gate approve: a bracketed suffix the gate TRUSTS is forgeable from the operator-typed approval summary
description:
Found by the D1 anchor-verification workflow, 2026-08-12, and independently confirmed by the orchestrator.

MECHANISM. cmd_approve builds a comment line that interpolates the operator-supplied $summary and
then appends $comment_suffix on the SAME line (qa-gate.sh:3542-3608). $summary comes from bare
positionals with no validation. The readers do NOT parse structure - they grep the whole comment text:
  verify-before-stop.sh:3776  printf '%s' "$MATCHED_APPROVAL_TEXT" | grep -qF '[review bypass:'
  verify-before-stop.sh:4217  printf '%s' "$text"                 | grep -qF '[review bypass:'

CONSEQUENCE, LIVE TODAY: 'qa-gate.sh approve <tid> "done [review bypass: x]"' satisfies the
review-discipline skip without any bypass having been authorised. The suffix space is self-asserted
by whoever types the approve command.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND ITSELF. The v5 D1 plan proposed routing the DESIGN BINDING into this same
bracketed-suffix space (' [design: <h>]'). That would make a value the gate must TRUST forgeable by
the same string. The verification workflow ruled against it on independent grounds too: all seven
existing suffix bodies are unvalidated human prose (:3571 contains parentheses, :3440 contains spaces),
so the space carries NO precedent for holding a machine-extracted value - and qa-gate.sh:3531-3541
constrains token ORDER, not COUNT, so a fourth machine token after change_set_hash IS available and is
the correct home.

NEEDS: validate or structurally separate the suffix space so a summary cannot forge one. Candidates -
reject '[' in $summary at the writer (reject, never sanitise, per the bjx class); or emit suffixes on
their own line; or have readers anchor on the suffix position rather than grep the whole text. Pair
with a leg that reds when a crafted summary satisfies a reader, plus a control proving an honest
summary still passes.

RELATED, same file, stale by two releases and to be fixed as a matched pair: qa-gate.sh:3539-3541
'Final shape' lists 2 of 6 possible suffixes; qa-gate.sh:2091-2094 (usage) lists 3 of 6.

DISCOVERED-FROM: the Phase D1 anchor verification (fkm.3).

title: A timed-out Codex MCP call leaves the process ALIVE with write access to the repo under review
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-11 during claude-workflow-plugin-a9hh.

WHAT HAPPENED. codex-review.sh / the codex MCP lane was driven as an IMPLEMENTER (sandbox
workspace-write). The harness aborted the call after 1800s of silence and reported failure.
The PROCESS WAS NOT KILLED: codex-code-mode-host pid 87945 ran a further 2h41m, cwd = this
repo, with write access to all three shipped runners. It launched its own full run-tests.sh
AFTER a replacement specialist had been spawned, and last wrote runner-completeness.test.sh
three minutes after that spawn. Its MCP call had already timed out, so nothing it produced
could ever reach a consumer. The orchestrator killed it manually (TERM, confirmed gone).

MEASURED CONSEQUENCES, all in the dangerous direction:
- The orchestrator described the tree to a specialist and was WRONG, because it read a file
  that was being written concurrently. It reported a label missing at line 514 that already
  existed at line 519.
- The specialist discarded one full spec run it had edited mid-flight and re-ran it hash-pinned.
- Two writers held the same files with no mechanism anywhere in the workflow noticing.

WHY IT MATTERS FOR v5. D4/D5 run PARALLEL WORKTREE BATCHES and the design-reviewer lane is
Sol-via-Codex. A lane that can outlive its own call while holding write access is a
correctness hazard for every measurement taken during it, and 'the tree was stable' is the
single most load-bearing precondition in this repo's evidence discipline.

ALSO MEASURED: the Codex lane is fine as a REVIEWER (four rounds at 326s, 493s, 496s, 613s)
and unusable as an IMPLEMENTER through this harness, because implementation work reproduces
races and runs silent past the idle timeout.

QA's note, recorded as HYPOTHESIS not finding: the host ran 2h41m past timeout_seconds=2400,
and codex-review.sh kills with a bare 'kill $SERVER_PID' with no escalation - the exact shape
this arc proved insufficient. But the argv is codex-code-mode-host, not the 'codex ... mcp-server'
that script spawns, so the link is unproven.

NEEDS: a per-server timeout in MCP settings (or CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_TOOL_IDLE_TIMEOUT) so review
turns are not aborted mid-flight; and an escalation on whatever kills the lane, so an aborted
call cannot leave a writer behind. Pair the check with a control that proves the process is
actually gone, not merely signalled.

comments.author: username
comments.text:
WIDENING, 2026-08-12: this is not one lane's bug, it is a missing PROCESS-OWNERSHIP PROTOCOL. Three
near-misses in a single session, each caught by an agent's care rather than by any mechanism:

1. THE ORIGINAL (this task). A timed-out Codex MCP call left codex-code-mode-host alive for 2h41m with
   write access to the repo under review, launching its own full test tier. Its output could never
   reach a consumer. It corrupted the orchestrator's reading of the tree - the orchestrator described
   a half-applied fix that was not, because it read a file mid-write - and forced a specialist to
   discard and re-run a measurement. Killed manually.

2. A REVIEWER CAUGHT ITSELF CONTENDING. qa-claude's pristine-HEAD baseline overlapped the
   orchestrator's confirming bar's component tier for ~19 minutes. It noticed, killed its own run,
   reaped the orphaned per-spec children, and DELIBERATELY LEFT A NUMBER UNVERIFIED rather than report
   one taken under contention.

3. A SPECIALIST NEARLY KILLED A REVIEWER'S RUN. The D1 specialist saw run-tests.sh processes it did
   not recognise and was about to kill them as its own stragglers. It checked timestamps first: the
   runs started 17:51:22 and 18:10:30 local, its own completion record was written 17:40 local, so
   they postdated its work - they were QA picking up qa-pending. It stopped. Its own words: it would
   have killed them 'on the strength of the word stragglers rather than a timestamp'.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY MISSING. Nothing on this machine can answer 'who owns this process?'. Every agent
that shares the host must either guess or interrogate ppid/start-time by hand. The failure modes are
asymmetric and both bad: kill someone else's work, or leave a runaway writer perturbing a tree under
review. Related and already filed: the specs/model-select.sh fixed /tmp/ms-*.err race, where two
concurrent component runs clobber each other's error capture and the only interlock in the tree is
the orchestrator's own pgrep guard - which guards ONE side.

WHY BEFORE D4. Phase D4 computes PARALLEL BATCHES and D5 runs them in worktrees. Concurrency stops
being incidental and becomes the design. Three near-misses under INCIDENTAL concurrency is the
signal.

CANDIDATE DIRECTION (a decision, not a design): a per-run token every long-running job stamps into
its argv or a lockfile, naming owner and start time, so ownership is a read rather than an inference;
plus a tier-level advisory lock so a second tier run refuses loudly instead of interleaving. Note the
repo already learned the per-run-token lesson once, in runner-completeness.test.sh, after machine-global
pgrep literals turned a control red whenever a second copy of its own tier ran.

comments.author: username
comments.text:
OPERATOR DIRECTIVE 2026-08-13: this is a D4 PREREQUISITE, not an incidental follow-up. D4 computes
parallel batches and D5 runs them in worktrees - concurrency stops being accidental and becomes the
design.

REQUIRED SHAPE, as directed:
- LEASES carrying OWNER IDENTITY and a HEARTBEAT. Ownership must be a READ, not an inference. Three
  near-misses this session were each caught by an agent reasoning about ppid and start-time by hand.
- STALE-LEASE RECLAIM, so a dead owner does not wedge the repo the way the timed-out Codex host did for
  2h41m.
- NO FIXED /tmp PATHS. specs/model-select.sh writes /tmp/ms-*.err today; two concurrent runs clobber
  each other. Per-run scratch under the runner's own directory.
- NO MEASUREMENT OF A TREE ANOTHER WRITER CAN TOUCH WITHOUT A LEASE OR AN EXPLICIT QUIESCE. THIS IS THE
  ONE THAT COST REAL WORK: a 97-minute L2 run was discarded because CONTENT_MOVED=YES, and the
  orchestrator could not tell whether the mover was a code edit or bd telemetry, because the guard
  hashed .beads/ and reported a bare boolean. A measurement that cannot name what moved is not a
  measurement.

The existing evidence is in the widening comment above: a runaway writer past its own abort, a reviewer
that killed its own run rather than report a contended number, and a specialist that nearly killed a
reviewer's tier and caught itself on a timestamp.

comments.author: username
comments.text:
SCOPE ADDITION — measured 2026-08-15/16, live, during the j7kk review. Routed here by QA's ruling: no
line of j7kk's diff touches TEST_LOG, so this is 9xl4's, not that batch's.

THE GATE ASSERTED A FAILURE IT COULD NOT SUBSTANTIATE. Verbatim from a Stop hook on the orchestrator's
turn:

    Verification failed (iteration 1 of 3).
    - Tests failing (exit 2) — see .claude/.qa-tracking/last-test-output.log
    --- last 50 lines of test output ---
    (no log)

Measured immediately after:

    ls -la .claude/.qa-tracking/last-test-output.log        -> No such file or directory
    ps aux | grep -E '[m]ake test|[r]un-tests.sh' | wc -l   -> 2      (QA's review drives)
    grep -n 'TEST_LOG=' .claude/scripts/verify-before-stop.sh
      40:TEST_LOG="$QA_TRACKING_DIR/last-test-output.log"

A FIXED PATH shared by every concurrent run — the operator's 'no fixed /tmp paths' clause, in the
tracking dir rather than /tmp. QA independently disclosed its four spec drives ran 23:06-23:13 concurrent
with that window and are a plausible contributor, and concluded the shared path is the root either way.

STATED AS AN INFERENCE, NOT AN OBSERVATION: two concurrent runs plus a fixed path plus a missing file is
circumstantial. It is NOT established that QA's run removed the file, nor that the missing log CAUSED the
exit-2.

TWO REASONS THIS MATTERS BEYOND ITS SIZE.

1. IT PROVES THE CHEAP HALF DOES NOT SUBSUME THE LEASE HALF. j7kk shipped skip-when-unchanged precisely to
   remove most contention. Here the orchestrator's tree HAD moved, so the skip CORRECTLY declined to fire
   — and the collision happened anyway. Skip-when-unchanged removes the redundant-run case; it does not
   resolve ownership of shared paths. That was the open question when the work was split, and it now has a
   measured answer.

2. THE SAME UNCERTAINTY IS HANDLED HONESTLY IN ONE ORGAN AND DISHONESTLY IN ANOTHER. j7kk's store canary
   faces exactly this ambiguity and HEDGES: 'either this spec wrote, or another process wrote
   concurrently'. QA ruled that hedge load-bearing and refused to let it be tightened to name a spec. The
   Stop hook, facing the same ambiguity, ASSERTS a failure and cites evidence that does not exist. When
   9xl4 lands, the failing-path tail read deserves the canary's treatment: say what is known, name what
   cannot be distinguished, never assert past the evidence.

NEEDS: per-run log paths (or a lease covering the tracking dir), and a tail read that says 'the log is
absent' rather than presenting an unevidenced red as a measured one.

comments.author: username
comments.text:
SECOND OCCURRENCE, 2026-08-16 — the TEST_LOG fixed-path collision is REPEATABLE, not circumstantial.

Same signature as the first, under the same conditions:

    Verification failed (iteration 2 of 3).
    - Tests failing (exit 2) — see .claude/.qa-tracking/last-test-output.log
    --- last 50 lines of test output ---
    (no log)

Measured at the moment of the report: the cited log ABSENT, and concurrent suite processes live (a QA
review round running make test against the same fixed path, TEST_LOG at verify-before-stop.sh:40).

WHY THE SECOND INSTANCE MATTERS. The first was filed with an explicit disclaimer that two concurrent runs
plus a fixed path plus a missing file was circumstantial, and that it was NOT established the concurrent
run removed the file. Two independent occurrences, both with a confirmed concurrent writer, both producing
an asserted failure with absent evidence, is a reproducible defect rather than a coincidence. The
disclaimer can be retired; the causal claim still should not be overstated beyond 'the shared path is the
root either way', which is where the first filing left it.

AND NOTE WHAT DID NOT SAVE US. j7kk shipped skip-when-unchanged specifically to cut contention, and it
works — it fired on an orchestrator turn earlier today and correctly reused a cached result. But on BOTH
occurrences of this defect the tree HAD moved, so the skip correctly declined, and the collision happened
anyway. That is now measured twice: the cheap structural half does not subsume the lease half.

The remedy remains as filed: per-run log paths (or a lease covering the tracking dir), plus a tail read
that says 'the log is absent' rather than presenting an unevidenced red as a measured one — the treatment
the store canary already gives the same class of ambiguity.

title: approve truncates the tracker, so a post-approval fix round rebinds a SUBSET: 4 of 21 paths, and reconcile cannot recover the rest
description:
MEASURED on claude-workflow-plugin-a9hh, 2026-08-11, after the round-9 approval.

SEQUENCE THAT PRODUCES IT.
1. QA approves. cmd_approve runs truncate_changed_files_tracker by design.
2. A reviewer finding arrives (sol-codex R8-F1) that the approval did not cover.
3. A fix round edits 4 files. post-edit.sh rebuilds the tracker with exactly those 4.
4. change_set_hash now covers 4 paths. git status shows 21 modified.
5. A second 'approve --expect-hash' would bind, and attest to, 4 of 21 files.

MEASURED STATE.
  tracker distinct paths : 4  (run-tests.sh, component/run.sh, runner-completeness.test.sh, CHANGELOG.md)
  tracker line count     : 20 (duplicates; append-only, no dedupe on read)
  git-modified paths     : 21
  change_set_hash        : 453ed3b6a6c4f4e406e9fe67c75d4cde4b853edb35ba97e0ebae3e0de40a1452 (the 4-path set)
  prior bound hash       : 668b8d19a2dbebe2cadd3c1a03f26f927ed600175171656f3a299910ee600535 (the 19-path set)
  cmd: wc -l < .claude/.qa-tracking/changed-files.txt ; git status --porcelain | wc -l ;
       bash .claude/scripts/impact-report.sh --hash-only claude-workflow-plugin-a9hh

WHY reconcile DOES NOT FIX IT. 'qa-gate.sh reconcile' ran and changed nothing. The other 17 paths
were already dirty when the new cycle opened, so gate_baseline_exclude_tracked treats them as
pre-existing dirt and subtracts them. That is correct for its original purpose (do not sweep an
operator's unrelated work into a review) and wrong here, because those 17 paths are the SAME task's
earlier rounds, already reviewed but not yet committed.

WHY IT MATTERS. This is the qzv/94d family on a seam neither covered. qzv bound approve to a hash so
an approval names the set it classified; 94d made the tracker cover what git sees. Neither anticipated
a SECOND approval in the same uncommitted working tree. The failure is silent and in the dangerous
direction: the approval record looks complete and binds a fraction. It is reachable on any task where
a reviewer finding lands after an approval and before the commit - which is exactly what a parallel
second-family review produces, and v5 makes that the normal case.

CANDIDATE DIRECTIONS (a decision, not a design).
- Do not truncate on approve; truncate on COMMIT, which is when the change set genuinely closes.
- Or: on cmd_enter, seed the tracker from the previous cycle's approved-hash file list when the task
  is still in_progress and uncommitted, so a re-review re-binds the union.
- Or: make approve REFUSE when the tracker's path set is a strict subset of the git-visible,
  non-denylisted set, naming the difference - fail closed, same shape as IMPACT-REPORT-REFUSAL.

TESTS IT NEEDS. A leg driving approve -> edit -> recompute and asserting the hash covers the union;
a negative control proving the leg fails against today's behaviour; and a leg pinning that an
operator's genuinely unrelated dirty file is still NOT swept in (the anti-overreach constraint that
made gate_baseline_exclude_tracked correct in the first place).

DISCOVERED-FROM: claude-workflow-plugin-a9hh review round 8/9.

comments.author: username
comments.text:
OPERATOR DIRECTIVE 2026-08-13: NOT a D2 blocker, but DECIDE THE MECHANISM NOW and land the migration
BEFORE D5.

WHY NOT D2: D1's design_hash is already CONTENT-based with refusal-before-hashing, so D2's design-side
binding is sound as built. The path-only hash bites at D5/D6, where coherence is INHERENTLY A CONTENT
ASSERTION - a rollup that claims N units cohere is claiming something about their bytes.

THE DECISION, taken now rather than at D5: UNIFY ON D1'S MECHANISM - a content hash that refuses before
hashing (absent, unreadable, empty each exit non-zero with a named error, never the empty-string
digest e3b0c442 that every shape check accepts). Design-side stronger than code-side is backwards; the
code side is the one that gates releases.

WHY BEFORE D5 SPECIFICALLY: there are TWO readers of the change-set hash today. D5 and D6 add more. A
migration with two readers is a contained change; with four it is a coordination problem. Land it while
it is cheap.

Note the two failure directions are now both observed and they are opposites: k0mc = content moves, hash
does not, so an approval attests to bytes nobody read (a9hh: five files rewritten between rounds, hash
identical). 0in1 = content holds, hash moves, so a real review counts as zero. A content hash closes the
first; 0in1's review-thread identity closes the second; neither substitutes for the other.

comments.author: username
comments.text:
EVIDENCE from rqer QA round 1, 2026-08-15 — a new instance, measured live.

QA verified rqer's AC-6 three-token scheme has no fixpoint, and observed on its OWN review cycle:
reviewed_hash f5fd255f (27 files) != post-artifact e5f7d831 (28 files), via impact-report.sh --hash-only
before and after. That part is sound.

BUT QA recorded a letter-vs-mechanism note that belongs here: because change_set_hash hashes PATH
MEMBERSHIP and is content-blind, a same-round RE-RECORD can equalize the two hashes. The artifact path
is already in the set the second time, so the pre-artifact and post-artifact sets are identical, and the
distinction AC-6 relies on collapses.

This does not break rqer — its three tokens are still non-self-referential and the first record on any
round behaves correctly. It is one more concrete case where path-list hashing cannot express a property
the system reasons about, which is this task's whole subject.

Worth carrying into the migration design: content hashing would make the re-record case behave the same
as the first record, with no special casing.

NOT A DEFECT IN THE MECHANISM. fkm.1.1 built these guards and they work — the guard is what surfaced this, and session-start.sh:691 already carries the exact operator message for the state. What is missing is the repair, which beads-ledger.sh deliberately does not perform automatically.

WHY P1 RATHER THAN HOUSEKEEPING. beads-ledger.sh's own header states the stake: "The ledger is not a nicety. It is the portable ground truth: a fresh clone recovers the issue database from it, and .beads/embeddeddolt/ is gitignored machine-local state. A silently stale ledger is silent data loss that only surfaces at the next clone." Eight P1/P2 issues currently exist only in machine-local state.

MEASURED COST ALREADY PAID, and this is the concrete part. CLAUDE.md:64 tells every agent ".beads/issues.jsonl for Beads ground truth" and AGENTS.md:46 calls it "the portable ground truth". Two consecutive QA rounds on fkm.1.11 grounded provenance work in that file:

  - round 10 corrected the attribution by DESCRIPTION search over the SAME stale file and quoted "returns exactly 1" as the uniqueness evidence. Over the live corpus that phrase matches 2 (QA R11-F1).
Worse, fkm.1.11's own completion contract cites iu5o and 71gw by id, and NEITHER appears in the ledger — so an auditor following CLAUDE.md:64 concludes two cited ids are fabricated. Both cannot be right at once.

HAZARD — READ BEFORE RUNNING THE REPAIR. .beads/issues.jsonl is measured denylisted=no AND self_written=no against workflow-denylist.sh, i.e. it IS a reviewable change-set member, deliberately (qa-gate.sh:530; docs/HOOKS.md:660 and :1094 both say so explicitly). Running reconcile --apply now would make it git-visible, the next `qa-gate.sh enter` / reconcile_tracker would fold it into the change set, and change_set_hash would MOVE — invalidating fkm.1.11's graded hash f090e911d8243dacb84b808452b86d5d1c45f3a92f22bf2744ae89526a3aed84, its persisted impact report, and the standing RUBRIC binding. DO THIS AFTER fkm.1.11 IS APPROVED, or accept a deliberate hash migration and a re-grade.

DELIVERABLES:
  (1) bash .claude/scripts/beads-ledger.sh reconcile --apply, then commit .beads/issues.jsonl — AFTER fkm.1.11's approval, per the hazard above.
  (2) Re-run `beads-ledger.sh check` and record the post-repair counts with the command and the commit (the 71gw convention).
  (3) DECIDE, and this is the durable half: the ledger can lag the database silently between session boundaries, yet CLAUDE.md:64 and AGENTS.md:46 present it as ground truth without qualification. Either qualify both lines (name it the COMMITTED LEDGER, note it can lag, point at `beads-ledger.sh check`), or close the gap so the two cannot diverge unnoticed. Prefer whichever keeps ONE place authoritative rather than adding a second reader.

THE HONEST CEILING: a staleness window is inherent to a committed export of a live database. This task should not pretend to eliminate it — it should make the window visible at the moment an agent reads the file, which is exactly when it currently is not.
close_reason: Repaired post-approval, as scoped. reconcile --apply: 343 -> 352 records, nothing discarded; beads-ledger.sh check now reports 'fresh: the ledger matches the database'. THE DEFERRAL WAS THE POINT: .beads/issues.jsonl measures denylisted=no self_written=no, so it was a REVIEWABLE MEMBER of fkm.1.11's change set. Reconciling mid-cycle would have dirtied it, the approve-time tracker rebuild would have grown the reviewed set, and change_set_hash would have moved out from under the graded RUBRIC binding, the persisted impact report and five review artifacts simultaneously. QA identified that ordering constraint and recorded it; the orchestrator had run reconcile --apply several times earlier in the session out of habit and would plausibly have run it again.

title: component/run.sh has NO PER-SPEC TIMEOUT: one hung spec blocks the entire L2 tier indefinitely — measured at 75 minutes and counting, with no upper bound
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-09. failure-hook-crash.sh hung for 1h15m (ps etime 01:15:06), stalling the tier at spec 15 of 44. Killed by hand. QA flagged this class as out-of-scope during ce5 and measured it at ELEVEN MINUTES then; this instance is nearly seven times longer, which establishes there is no bound at all rather than a long-but-finite worst case.

THE DEFECT: .claude/tests/component/run.sh runs each spec in a bash -u -c subshell and WAITS. Nothing caps that wait. A spec that blocks — on a real bd call, a network fetch, a process that never exits — blocks the whole tier forever. The runner emits no per-spec progress the caller can time out on either, so from outside it is indistinguishable from a slow-but-live run.

WHY IT IS P1 RATHER THAN AN ANNOYANCE, and this is the part that connects it to the rest of the arc: an L2 run that never finishes produces NO completeness line. Every discipline this release has built — read the completeness line, never the absence of FAIL; a measurement that did not happen must not look like one that passed — depends on the tier terminating. A hung tier is the one state where those rules give no answer at all. Tonight it cost a full bar: L1, lint and L3 completed and described the tree, L2 never did, and the run had to be discarded.

IT COMPOSES WITH TWO OPEN TASKS. mrd2: a hung runner holds the machine, so every other agent either waits or measures under contention. skka: because component fixtures ln -sf the live scripts, a hung tier is also an open window during which any specialist edit silently changes what the tier is executing — which is exactly what happened here, the round-7 specialist edited verify-before-stop.sh while this run sat stalled.

FIX DIRECTION: a per-spec wall-clock cap in run.sh that KILLS the spec and reports it as FAILED with a distinct reason, never as passed or skipped. The cap must be visible in the summary so a truncated tier cannot read as a complete one. Note the interaction with a9hh: a skip must not be a pass, and a timeout must not be a skip. Whatever ships needs a control that hangs a spec deliberately and asserts the tier still terminates with a red.

RELATED: a9hh (skip-is-not-a-pass + the completeness floor — same file family, same class), mrd2, skka, tak8.
close_reason: Shipped in bd377f5 on v5/design-phase. Ten review rounds across two model families (sol-codex, qa-claude), seventeen findings, all fixed and independently re-verified. Approved at change_set_hash 33ddc1c7 (the earlier 19-path set at 668b8d19). Measured at bd377f5: L1 36/36/0/0 Partial 0 with 2677 assertions and the completeness floor HELD; make lint rc=0; shellcheck on the L2 runner rc=0 separately; L3 451p/5s/0f; L2 44 specs 43 passed 1 failed Partial 1, 2928/2, sole red the PRE-EXISTING installer-v3-upgrade 8e-B proven at pristine 535c89a. Linux evidence is an ubuntu:24.04/bash 5.2.21/aarch64 container; GitHub-hosted x86_64 remains UNMEASURED and the rewired l1-unit job's first push is its first measurement.

comments.author: username
comments.text:
CAUSE DIAGNOSED, AND IT IS ENVIRONMENTAL — NOT THE HOOK, NOT THIS BATCH. Recording before anyone optimises the wrong thing.

THE SYMPTOM, three L2 runs on this change set: killed at failure-hook-crash.sh after 75 minutes; watchdog at 2700s with 30/44 (contended); watchdog at 3600s with 35/44 on an IDLE machine with the tree provably stable (content snapshot 9679d6c14e41f5ec both sides). Earlier runs in the same session completed 44/44.

WHAT I RULED OUT BY MEASUREMENT:
- A single hanging spec. The three runs died at THREE DIFFERENT specs — failure-hook-crash.sh, qa-gate.sh, rubric-loop.sh. General slowness, not one blocker.
- The hook growing. verify-before-stop.sh went 3478 -> 4529 lines (+30 percent) in this batch, which was my first suspicion. But a fingerprint-equivalent over 40 untracked files measures 34ms per call — three calls in 103ms. Not the bottleneck.

THE ACTUAL CAUSE: FIVE bd daemon PROCESSES, AGED 16 TO 20 DAYS (etime 16-05:36, 16-05:32, 20-11:13, 16-09:47, 20-04:55). With them live, a plain bd show takes 1279ms and bd list 462ms. L2 specs drive bd dozens of times each; at over a second per call the tier crawls, and which spec the watchdog happens to catch is arbitrary.

They PREDATE this entire session by more than two weeks. I noticed five of them at session start and left them alone because I could not establish they were mine and one might have been serving the live workspace. That caution cost three L2 runs.

WHY THIS DOES NOT WEAKEN THIS TASK: the missing per-spec timeout is still a real P1 and is what turned a slow environment into an UNBOUNDED one. A tier that degrades from 45 to 75+ minutes should report which spec is slow and keep going, or fail that spec and continue — not sit silently forever producing no completeness line. The environmental cause explains the SLOWNESS; the absent cap explains why slowness became a total loss of measurement.

IT ALSO ARGUES FOR A SECOND THING THE FIX SHOULD DO: report per-spec elapsed time. All three of my runs would have been diagnosable in seconds rather than hours if the runner printed how long each spec took.

RELATED, and now clearly connected: mrd2 (contention), tak8 (a busy-check that cannot come back clear), skka (measuring a moving tree). The daemons are a fourth member of that family — environment state nobody measured, silently degrading every measurement taken on top of it.

title: The orchestrator's own bar tree-stability assertion is CONTENT-BLIND: git status --porcelain md5 cannot see a content edit, so every 'TREE_MOVED=no' this session was weaker than reported
description:
SELF-REPORTED AND MEASURED BY THE ORCHESTRATOR, 2026-08-09, after the round-4 devops specialist disclosed that an in-flight L2 had executed its edits.

THE DEFECT. Every full-bar run this session wrapped the tiers in:
  T0=$(git status --porcelain | md5)
  ... run L1, lint, L3, L2 ...
  TREE_MOVED=$([ "$T0" = "$(git status --porcelain | md5)" ] && echo no || echo YES)
and the result was reported to QA, repeatedly, as 'tree asserted unmoved across the bar'.

MEASURED JUST NOW: appending a line to an ALREADY-MODIFIED tracked file leaves git status --porcelain BYTE-IDENTICAL (md5 c0abe7b37fea67d9552920d473379787 before and after). The porcelain format emits 'M <path>' — the path list and its status letters, never content. So the check proves only that the SET OF MODIFIED PATHS was stable. It is blind to exactly the mutation that was happening.

THIS IS xii, IN MY OWN INSTRUMENTATION. The whole session has been about a hash that binds a path list rather than content; I built a stability assertion with the identical hole and then quoted it as evidence in every QA brief.

IT IS NOT THEORETICAL — the composition is measured:
1. Component fixtures SYMLINK the real scripts: .claude/tests/component/lib/fixture.sh:501 does ln -sf "$s" for every .claude/scripts/*.sh. An L2 run therefore reads whatever the real script says AT THAT MOMENT.
2. The round-4 specialist edited verify-before-stop.sh while my round-3 bar's L2 was running, and disclosed it: 'their in-flight L2 executed my edits ... the run consumed a moving artifact'.
3. My bar reported TREE_MOVED=no for that same run.
So the round-3 L2 figures (44 specs / 43 passed / 2913 assertions / 2 failed, and component/specs/verify-before-stop.sh 198/0) may describe a MIXTURE of round-3 and round-4 bytes. I reported them to QA as describing round 3.

MITIGATING, stated so this is not overclaimed: the specialist measured that no component spec references the ledger functions, that normal-host behaviour was unchanged, and that no spec's source-grep pattern was touched. So the numbers are probably still true. PROBABLY IS THE PROBLEM — that is the same word this entire batch exists to eliminate.

THE FIX IS ALREADY IN THE TREE. This batch just built tree_fingerprint (verify-before-stop.sh), which hashes HEAD plus the diff plus untracked content and is exactly the right primitive. The bar should call it, or hash the content of the modified set directly. Do not invent a third canonicalisation.

SECOND, SEPARABLE ITEM: because fixtures symlink live scripts, ANY specialist edit during an L2 run corrupts that run — the contention class mrd2 records, with a mechanism sharper than 'two runners on one box'. A lock that the runner itself writes (tak8's durable fix) would cover both.

RELATED: xii (the parent defect), mrd2 (contention), tak8 (the busy-check that cannot come back clear), 71gw (every number carries the command that produced it).

title: CONVENTION: every number in a report or audit row carries the command that produced it, measured at the commit that ships it
description:
OPERATOR INSTRUCTION 2026-08-08, given as part of the Tier 1 batch: 'any number in a report or audit row carries the command that produced it, measured at the commit that ships it - the same fix applied to our own outputs.'

WHY, from tonight's evidence. Every one of the orchestrator's five errors this session was a PROXY REPORTED AS A MEASUREMENT, and each would have been caught by this convention:
- The sentinel guard count was quoted as 22, then 24. Measured three ways at 1233ea5 it is 12 line-initial, 24 anywhere-in-line, 20 indented; the census reported a fourth number, 25. FOUR COUNTS, NO STATED METHOD.
- L3 was reported green while naming bar-l3.log, which was the RED pre-sync run; the green one was bar-l3b.log. QA found the right file by mtime.
- A restore hash (2f9146a2) was passed into a QA brief unverified; QA found it matches neither current nor HEAD.
- Two grep outputs were labelled 'empty above = good' over output that was not empty.
- An L1 completeness line was read off a per-spec summary block rather than the run's final line.

AND IT IS NOT ONLY MINE. QA re-measured a ledger count of 117/342 and got 116/342, because the ledger moved between the two measurements - correctly, and it caught it. The LESSON already recorded says an absolute count against a live ledger goes stale the moment it is written. This convention is that lesson made mechanical.

WHAT IT REQUIRES: a number appearing in RELEASE_AUDIT rows, CHANGELOG entries, HANDOFF verification blocks, task closures and review artifacts carries (a) the command that produced it and (b) the commit it was measured at. A reader must be able to re-run it and compare.

WHAT IT IS NOT: not a demand that every number be re-measured on every read, and not a licence to bury numbers in prose to avoid the requirement. The point is falsifiability - a number a reader cannot reproduce is an assertion, not a measurement.

SHIPS WITH: the pairing requirement and the post-close-finding convention, in the fkm.1.11 batch. All three are closeout-convention changes and belong in the same landing.

comments.author: username
comments.text:
LANDED. Canonical home: `CONTRIBUTING.md` § "Every number carries the command that produced it and the commit it was measured at".

WHERE THE CLOSEOUT CONVENTION ACTUALLY LIVES — established, not assumed. There is no single closeout-convention file. Searched `closeout|close-out` across the repo's markdown: the hits are (a) per-release plan docs under `docs/plans/` (principle 11, "per-phase closeout", which is per-release and not durable), (b) `docs/AGENTLINT_REPORT.md` section headers, and (c) `AGENTS.md` § "Landing the Plane (Session Completion)", which is the SESSION-end protocol. The durable contributor-facing surface is `CONTRIBUTING.md`, with `.claude/tests/README.md` as the deep reference it already defers to for test conventions. So all three conventions in this batch landed in `CONTRIBUTING.md` (the four-part pairing standard canonical in `.claude/tests/README.md`, where the existing META-TEST convention and its one mechanical arm already live), with pointers from `AGENTS.md` Landing-the-Plane steps 1 and 2 — the two moments at which these mistakes are actually made.

DISCOVERABILITY WAS THE REAL RISK. `CLAUDE.md`'s conditional-loading table previously routed to `CONTRIBUTING.md` only for "extending the workflow with a new specialist", so a convention landed there would have been read by almost nobody. Three rows added to that table, keyed on the ACT rather than the area: adding a check of any kind; finding a defect in already-closed work; writing a number into a report/audit row/CHANGELOG/closure/review artifact.

THE CONVENTION APPLIED TO ITSELF, and this is the part worth reading. The draft example block quoted "12 line-initial / 24 anywhere" from this task's own description. I measured before shipping it and got 20 / 101 / 29 — because the filing's population and mine differed (flat `.claude/scripts/*.sh` versus a RECURSIVE walk that includes `.claude/scripts/tests/`). Neither is wrong; they answer different questions, and nothing in either write-up said which. So:
- the historical bullet no longer asserts those figures as measurements — it says plainly that no method was recorded and that re-deriving them is therefore impossible, which is the actual lesson;
- the worked example carries only figures I measured, with the exact command inline, and it uses the population discrepancy as the illustration.

Verified: the documented command reproduces its stated number verbatim.
    for f in $(git ls-tree -r --name-only 1233ea5 -- .claude/scripts | grep '\.sh$'); do git show "1233ea5:$f"; done | grep -c '^# .* BEGIN'
    -> 20   (at 1233ea5)

Also applied to the RELEASE_AUDIT append in the same batch: the new "Standing attestations" section states that the v4.1.0 scoped greps are unperturbed, and every one of the five was re-run after the append to confirm — 13 / 3 / 0 / 0 / 16.

NEGATIVE CONTROL: NONE, declared. This convention is prose and no shipped executable changes behaviour when it changes, so there is no execution leg (pairing standard, leg 4) and none is claimed. A check that grepped the wording would be a byte-comparison over markdown — the exact false pair the census named. What the control IS instead is stated in `.claude/tests/README.md` § "This convention is itself UNPAIRED": it binds at review rather than at runtime, and its reliability is a reviewer's. The honest gap: a mechanical arm would need a registry of number-bearing rows, which does not exist.

title: CI REPORTS GREEN OVER 276 UNEXECUTED ASSERTIONS: six L1 specs exit 0 having run nothing under BD_SHIM_ONLY=1, and run-tests.sh scores exit-0 as PASSED
description:
FOUND by the negative-control census v2 against a pinned worktree at 1233ea5; every number below INDEPENDENTLY RE-MEASURED by the orchestrator before filing.

THE MECHANISM, three facts that compose:

1. .github/workflows/test.yml:90 sets BD_SHIM_ONLY: '1' on the l1-unit job, and that job installs no bd (it verifies only jq and bash).

2. Six L1 specs carry this shape, verbatim from review-separation.test.sh:138-142:
     if ! command -v bd >/dev/null 2>&1; then
         if [ "${BD_SHIM_ONLY:-0}" = "1" ]; then
             echo "SKIPPED: ... (bd not available; CI env BD_SHIM_ONLY=1)"
             exit 0
   So in CI they print SKIPPED and exit 0 having executed ZERO assertions.

3. run-tests.sh:51 scores by exit status alone:
     if bash "$test_file"; then PASS=$((PASS + 1)); else FAIL=...
   An exit-0-with-nothing-run is counted PASSED. The completeness line reads
   Total: 34  Passed: 34  Failed: 0 whether the specs RAN or SKIPPED.

MEASURED BLAST RADIUS, assertions per affected spec:
  bd-github-link            16
  mcp-unestablished-results 51
  phase5-synthetic-tests    33
  qa-gate-choose            33
  qa-gate-grade-record      79
  review-separation         64
  TOTAL                    276  of 1973 L1 assertions = 14.0 percent

WHY THIS IS P1 AND NOT A CI-CONFIG NIT: this is the censused defect family, in the tier that gates every PR, at the one place where no human is watching. A measurement that did not happen is byte-indistinguishable from one that passed. Locally with bd installed these specs run and pass; the completeness line is identical in both worlds, so nothing anywhere reports the difference.

WORST INDIVIDUAL LOSS: review-separation.test.sh, 64 assertions, is the spec behind the claim that NOBODY SIGNS OFF ON THEIR OWN WORK - RELEASE_AUDIT row TM5, verdict PROVEN, whose evidence line cites this exact file including its section-6 META. In CI that META has never run. mcp-unestablished-results.test.sh is the negative control shipped THIS SESSION for rmz/fkm.1.18; its section 3 is the real-bd fidelity half.

FIX DIRECTION, and the choice matters:
(a) A skip must not be a pass. The runner needs a third outcome, and the tier needs a completeness FLOOR - an expected spec count or expected assertion total that fails when the executed set shrinks. Exactly one file in the tier has one today (evidence-before-fix.test.sh, EXPECTED_ASSERTIONS=29), and it guards only its own aborted run, not the file set.
(b) Or install bd in the l1-unit job and delete the skip arm. More honest, costs CI time, and removes the seam rather than instrumenting it.
Do NOT fix this by making the skip louder in the log. Nobody reads a green log.

RELATED: the same run-tests.sh has NO completeness floor at all - delete 20 of the 34 spec files and it prints Total: 14 Passed: 14 Failed: 0 and exits 0. It exits 2 only when the discovered list is EMPTY. Same class, filed here because the fix is the same floor.

OPERATOR DECISION 2026-08-08 - Option C, FLOOR FIRST, and it runs as its OWN BATCH at the start of the next session, before D0. Deliberately kept out of tonight's fkm.1.11 batch.

ORDER IS PART OF THE DECISION:
1. Make a SKIP a THIRD OUTCOME that is not a pass. Today run-tests.sh:51 scores by exit status alone - if bash $test_file; then PASS++ - so a spec that exits 0 having executed zero assertions is counted PASSED.
2. Add the TIER COMPLETENESS FLOOR - an expected spec/assertion total that fails when the executed set shrinks. This also closes the separate hole in the same file: delete 20 of 34 spec files and it prints Total: 14 Passed: 14 Failed: 0 and exits 0, because it exits 2 only when the discovered list is EMPTY.
3. THEN install bd in the l1-unit job and delete the skip arm.

THE FRAMING IS THE POINT, and it is the operator's: FRAME THE FLOOR AS THE NEGATIVE CONTROL FOR THE COMPLETENESS LINE. IT IS THE PAIRING CONVENTION'S FIRST APPLICATION. The completeness line is a claim - Total: 34 Passed: 34 Failed: 0 - and until now nothing could make that claim fail while it was false. The floor is exactly the control the new convention demands of every other check, applied to the instrument the whole tier is read through. Build it that way and say so in the code, because it is the worked example every future check will be measured against.

MEASURED BLAST RADIUS, re-verified at 1233ea5: 276 of 1973 L1 assertions - 14.0 percent - across bd-github-link 16, mcp-unestablished-results 51, phase5-synthetic-tests 33, qa-gate-choose 33, qa-gate-grade-record 79, review-separation 64.

THE COMPLETENESS FLOOR (run-tests.sh, sentinel-delimited COMPLETENESS-FLOOR block): EXPECTED_SPECS=36; an unfiltered run fails when the discovered set shrinks — closing the delete-20-specs hole — and a --filter matching NOTHING is now rc=2 instead of a green `Total: 0`. 3. THEN CI: l1-unit installs the real bd — pinned v1.1.2 (the exact version dev machines run), sha256-verified release tarball (a72d71ed…01c2), so a moved tag or tampered tarball fails loudly — plus npm ci for bd-mcp (without which mcp-unestablished-results whole-file-skips, and a skip is now red). THE PAIRED CONTROL (runner-completeness.test.sh, 40 assertions, four-part standard): drives the SHIPPED L1 runner over full/shrunken/skipping/silent/hanging fixtures; drives an UN-FLOORED MUTANT (sentinel excision, awk found-check + byte-comparison + bash -n) over the same shrunken set and watches it print the exact green line the floor falsifies (`Total: N-1  Passed: N-1  Failed: 0`, rc=0); restore controls on both runners; L2 legs prove skip-leaves-Passed and hang-terminates-red with no orphaned children (the hanging stub blocks via a CHILD process; after the kill, the child is asserted gone).

## QA round 1 — a9hh + iu5o, one change set, hash 5b47c019, 15 files

Verdict: **BLOCK** on R1-F1 (high). R1-F2 (medium) / R1-F3 (low) are below
`risk_threshold=high` and routed into the same round.

### Method note — the thing that mattered

Everyone in the loop measured the **old** CI shape to prove the defect.
Nobody measured the shape the change **ships into**. I rebuilt both. The
residual was in the second one.

### Review modules executed

- **CONFIG** — `.claude/review-config` is a shipped-defaults surface (both
  installers copy it verbatim). Independently parsed the shipped file through
  `read_cap` extracted from the shipped driver: 12 / 2400 / 10 / high / 1.
  Confirmed the new rationale prose cannot shadow the assignments — line 48
  (`# max_review_iterations=3"`) is one `#` from a real shadow, and C8's
  12-assertion would catch it if that `#` ever went away. `.github/workflows/test.yml`:
  `permissions: contents read / checks write` unchanged; action pinning
  (`@v4`) matches repo convention.
- **DEPS** — the bd install is pinned by version **and** sha256. Fetched the
  asset: digest matches exactly, Linux x86-64 ELF, top-level `bd` member so
  `tar -C /usr/local/bin bd` works, `bd version` rc=0 in and out of a `.beads`
  repo. The new `npm ci` on bd-mcp pulls 7 known advisories (3 high),
  transitively via `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` -> `express-rate-limit` ->
  `ip-address` — pre-existing and already shipped to every install; CI merely
  installs what users already run. Not a finding here; worth its own task.
- **SECRETS** — clean; nothing credential-shaped in the diff.
- **AI** — the caps govern the optional paid Sol lane. Spend bound checked at
  source: the driver performs one turn per invocation and exits (`exit 6` is a
  refusal boundary, not a scheduler), `malformed_retry` stays 1, so 12 turns
  requires 12 orchestrator-initiated rounds. Residual acceptable as stated.
- INJECTION / AUTH / MOBILE / DATA — not triggered by this diff.

### Measurements I ran (not read)

| What | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Unfixed @535c89a, old CI shape | `Total: 35 Passed: 35 Failed: 0`, rc=0, over **six** SKIPPED specs; 2147 of 2461 assertions executed |
| Whole-file loss, per spec | 20 / 53 / 33 / 30 / 90 / 60 = **286** exactly as filed |
| Fixed tree, old CI shape (**like-for-like**) | `Total: 36 Passed: 30 Failed: 5 Skipped: 1`, rc=1, floor HELD, each loss named with rc + elapsed |
| **Fixed tree, NEW CI shape** | `Total: 36 Passed: 36 Failed: 0 Skipped: 0` + `floor HELD (36/36 discovered and executed)`, rc=0 — **over 15 unexecuted assertions** (R1-F1) |
| Blocker 1 (spec lost at commit) | `COMPLETENESS FLOOR BREACH: discovered 35 ... expected exactly 36`, rc=1 — the fix protects its own landing |
| `runner-completeness.test.sh` alone | 40/40, rc=0 |
| Same, with one decoy `sleep 31337` | `FAIL: 5.6 ... expected gone, actual alive`, rc=1 (R1-F2) |
| L2 `codex-review` via shipped runner | 66/66 in 16s; C8 = 15 assertions, all four pairing parts |
| shellcheck + `bash -n`, all changed shell | rc=0 / all parse |
| Watchdog overhead, 36 instant stubs | ~1s total (not per-spec) — negligible |

The flip pair as filed was **not** like-for-like: the unfixed side was measured
with bd-mcp `node_modules` absent, the fixed side with them present. That is why
the record says Failed:6/Skipped:0 and I measured Failed:5/Skipped:1. Both are
correct for their environment; mine holds the environment fixed so the change is
the only variable.

### Judgments the brief asked for

- **Skip keyed on measured absence** — right call, and it cannot misclassify in
  the dangerous direction. It is fail-**closed**: an assertion-free spec goes red
  and forces its author to emit an assertion. All 36 current specs emit.
- **The L1/L2 split (u84b)** — sound. L2's exit-0-on-skip is inseparable from
  installing bd there; moving it as a side effect of the L1 round would have
  changed `l2-component`'s red/green without its own review. Honesty landed now
  (skips leave `Passed`, `COMPLETENESS:` caveat), policy deferred.
- **iu5o C1-C7 / C8 split** — correct. C1-C7 test cap *mechanics* with fixture
  configs; C8 alone pins shipped bytes. Coverage composes: C4 already brackets
  the timeout behaviourally (`write_config 2` -> exit 5), so C8's `read_cap` pin
  of 2400 is a parse pin on top of a proven-used mechanism, not a substitute.
- **The 12-paid-turn residual** — acceptable as stated, for the reason in AI above.
- **Blocker 2** — de-risked as far as is possible without a runner (digest, arch,
  extraction layout, `bd version` rc). The genuinely unmeasured part is bd 1.1.2's
  runtime under a fresh CI `$HOME` with no git identity. Declining to add a
  speculative `git config` step was the right call.

### Findings

- **R1-F1 (high)** — CI installs bd-mcp deps but not code-graph-mcp deps;
  `impact-report.test.sh` runs 24 of 39, section 4 (the **live** code-graph path:
  `server=code-graph`, exit-0-despite-per-file-error, non-git relativisation
  fallback) silently skipped under a green floor-HELD line. Same class, same job,
  new claim, named nowhere.
- **R1-F2 (medium)** — `runner-completeness.test.sh:246,:316` probe orphans with
  `pgrep -f` over machine-global literals; any concurrent tier run turns the
  trust anchor red. Prior art in the same tier (`impact-report.test.sh:314`)
  already scopes its pgrep per-run.
- **R1-F3 (low)** — `workflow-manifest.test.sh:751` still asserts "run-tests.sh
  has no SKIP verb ... reads exit code and nothing else". Both clauses now false.

### Follow-ups filed

- `claude-workflow-plugin-c6zu` — mutation-sweep scores every mutant KILLED
  (13.4-min tier oracle under a 60s timeout, rc=124 folded into "killed").
  Pre-existing, same defect family, out of this change set.

QA-GATE BLOCKED at 2026-08-10T14:01:17Z: QA re-review round 3 (R3) — BLOCK on 2 HIGH, both recorded in the qa-claude review artifact (REVIEW-ARTIFACT v1 iteration=3, reviewed_hash=8761ac66). The R2 fix round is otherwise correct and I independently reproduced its headline claims: L1 36/36, Assertions executed 2578, floor HELD, Partial 0, rc=0; runner-completeness 117 assertions; 0 SECTION_SKIP_RE hits across the whole tier (the zero-false-positive claim HOLDS as measured); 0 set -m job-control notices; R1-F2 and R1-F3 correctly fixed; the disclosed group-KILL asymmetry is accurately described and genuinely harmless.

R3-F1 (HIGH) — the survivor sweep fails and SIGKILLs specs for bd send-metrics, which bd spawns and detaches (ppid=1) but does NOT setsid, so it stays in the CALLER process group. Reproduced end-to-end through the SHIPPED runner, 4 of 25 iterations, on a fixture that backgrounds nothing and reaps everything it starts: "FAILED - returned with 1 live background process(es), killed", rc=1, tier RED. Survivor captured at sweep time: pid=84621 ppid=1 pgid=84316 bd send-metrics, where 84316 is the spec pid==pgid. Census over 25 minutes of live tier activity: 61 distinct bd send-metrics processes, 61/61 in the caller group, 0/61 setsid, max lifetime 3s against the sweep 2.0s grace. Observed live in your own in-flight bar run before I built any fixture (pid 55155, pgid 40023 = qa-gate-grade-record.test.sh). This falsifies the header sentence that justifies the sweep ("bd own daemon does this, measured: pgid=self, ppid=1" — true of bd daemon, false of bd send-metrics). CI l1-unit is MORE exposed than this box: real bd, no ~/.config/bd so metrics are not disabled, no BD_DISABLE_METRICS. Local L2 is exposed across 44 bd-heavy specs — I predict your in-flight L2 surfaces it. Excluding ppid==1 is NOT a viable fix: the R2-F2 escaped child is reparented to 1 too, so that predicate would delete the detection this round adds.

R3-F2 (HIGH) — both runners STDIN paragraphs state the opposite of what set -m does, and both are NEW text in this change set (git show HEAD of run-tests.sh has a 15-line header with no STDIN paragraph; the L2 one is a pure + block). Substring match ("metrics: OFF" inside "Anonymous usage metrics: OFF"), no ordering coupling (10.11 writes nothing into the shared probe HOME, measured), and the variable is stronger than the legs assert — it overrides an explicit config that says ON. Survivor line: safe for CI logs. ps escapes embedded newlines as \012 (I tried to forge a second survivor row through argv and could not), %s/%d/%n are inert because argv is a printf ARGUMENT not the format, cut -c1-160 bounds each line, and the two jobs that run the runners carry no repository secrets (only STRICT_SECTIONS / BD_SHIM_ONLY) while ps args= exposes argv only, never env.

description:
QA round-1 finding R1-F3 on claude-workflow-plugin-bbh, recorded in the qa-claude
review artifact on that task. NOT a defect in bbh — bbh discloses this residual
explicitly and specifically, in the DOC-CONTENT-VETO/classifier region header and
again in .claude/agents/qa.md. This task exists because the residual is about to
acquire NEW instances in v5 and nothing currently binds D0/D1 to act on it.

MEASURED against the SHIPPED post-bbh classifier (function extracted from
verify-before-stop.sh by awk and driven directly, PROJECT_DIR = this repo):

  DOC-ONLY   docs/specs/claude-workflow-plugin-abc.md
  DOC-ONLY   .claude/agents/designer.md
  DOC-ONLY   .claude/agents/design-reviewer.md
  DOC-ONLY   .claude/agents/qa.md
  DOC-ONLY   CLAUDE.md
  DOC-ONLY   .claude/rubrics/default.md

WHY bbh DOES NOT CLOSE IT. bbh removed the two arms that inferred content type
from path SHAPE (`*/docs/*|docs/*` and `LICENSE.*`) and added an affirmative
content veto (exec bit, or a `#!` first line). After it, `docs/` confers nothing
— but `*.md` still does, and a prompt, a rubric or a design spec carries neither
the exec bit nor a shebang. So the veto cannot see them, correctly and by
construction.

WHY IT MATTERS FOR v5 SPECIFICALLY.
  * D1 (claude-workflow-plugin-fkm.3) stores the design artifact at
    docs/specs/<task-id>.md when Linear is absent. That document GOVERNS
    implementation — it is the thing the design-reviewer reviews and the thing
    the implementer builds from. As a `.md` it is doc-only, so a Stop whose
    change set is exactly that artifact is F1-eligible and auto-approves with
    reviewed_by=none.
  * D0 adds .claude/agents/designer.md and .claude/agents/design-reviewer.md,
    both behaviour-bearing markdown, both doc-only.

THE LIVE ILLUSTRATION, from bbh's own change set: .claude/agents/qa.md is a
member of it and is itself DOC-ONLY. Had that edit landed alone, F1 would have
auto-approved a change to the QA agent's own prompt with reviewed_by=none.

WHAT A FIX MUST NOT BE. Not another shape inference — that is the mistake bbh
removed, and the operator's binding direction on bbh was "remove the path-shape
inference rather than widen the pattern list". A `docs/specs/` arm would be the
same error in a new place.

CANDIDATE DIRECTION (a decision, not a design). An explicit, project-scoped
DECLARATION of behaviour-bearing documentation paths — a list a project states
about itself, the way workflow-denylist.sh is stated — consulted by
is_doc_only_path as a second veto. That is not inference: it is a fact about a
project's layout, which is exactly what the bbh region header says no path or
content check can recover. Seed it for this repo with CLAUDE.md,
.claude/agents/*.md, .claude/rubrics/*.md and docs/specs/*.md.

AVAILABILITY COST, which must be measured before fixing, as it was for bbh: every
declared path loses the fast path when it changes alone. For this repo that is
the agent prompts and the rubrics — files that genuinely do change alone and
often. Measure it before choosing the default.

TESTS IT NEEDS.
  * Unit legs on is_doc_only_path for each declared path, plus a control that an
    ORDINARY doc in the same directory still fast-paths (the anti-overreach
    constraint bbh's 2c/9B legs already encode).
  * A leg proving the declaration is consulted, and a META on whichever region
    introduces it.
  * A leg pinning that an EMPTY or ABSENT declaration changes nothing, so
    installs that never declare are unaffected.

BLOCKS: D0/D1 should not ship a new artifact class into the residual without a
decision recorded here — either the fix, or an explicit accept-and-say-why.

## DESIGN DECISION — the manifest's enumeration is the oracle, no path arms

Implements the operator's binding direction (comment of 2026-08-08) literally: **no path glob was added anywhere.** `is_doc_only_path` gains a second veto that asks one question with a factual answer — *is this path part of the surface the project itself declares it ships?* — and gets it from `workflow-manifest.sh`, the enumeration install.sh copies from and every frozen table under `manifests/` is cut from.

### What was added

- `workflow-manifest.sh governing <root>` — new subcommand, sorted TSV `<path><TAB><origin>`. Every `generate_rows` path (origin = its manifest class) **plus** `runtime_contract_rows` (origin = `runtime-contract`), which names `CLAUDE.md` and nothing else. No hashes: `MANIFEST_EMIT_HASH=0` drops the digest column, so the query needs no sha256 tool and the hashed `generate` statement is byte-untouched.
- `verify-before-stop.sh` GOVERNING-ARTIFACT-VETO region — memoised (once per Stop), exact-string membership, fail-OPEN + `log_sync_error` when the query cannot run.

### Scope: the WHOLE declared surface, not a "governing" subset

A subset would have to be **minted here**, and a minted list is a new place for the next artifact to be missing — the objection that removed the `docs/` arm rather than narrowing it. The manifest header already states the property that makes the whole surface correct: workflow-class files are *"plugin-owned product ... an operator edit to one of them is a local fork, not a setting."* So `docs/HOOKS.md` and `docs/CODEX_SETUP.md` are in, deliberately. It also generalises with **no list edited anywhere**: creating `.claude/agents/designer.md` disqualifies it on the next Stop (pinned by leg 6f, measured before/after).

### On the orchestrator's two claims

1. **"Availability cost is ZERO" — NOT reproduced. It is 1, not 0.** The 7 doc-only commits reproduce exactly; the "0 of them governing" does not. `ea6ae385 "update documentation for mandatory delegation"` changed `docs/HOOKS.md` alone, which the manifest classifies as workflow-class plugin product. The orchestrator's grep approximation filed it under "purely ordinary docs". Cost is **1 in 142 non-merge commits**. The structural half is confirmed and stronger than stated: **60** commits touch a veto-reachable governing artifact, **59** carried a reviewable path anyway.
2. **Manifest coverage — confirmed exactly**, at the cited lines: `:306` agents, `:335` rubrics, `:290-291` CLAUDE.md excluded, `:294-301` docs/ never scanned. Adding either to `generate_rows` was NOT done; the negative control asserts `generate` still emits no `CLAUDE.md` row and its output is unchanged.

### docs/specs/ — deferred to D1 (fkm.3), agreed

Closing it here needs either a `docs/specs/` arm (forbidden) or a `scan_flat docs` (enumerates an operator's own docs and widens the uninstall walk). D1 owns the writer and can disqualify it from the design RECORD that names the file, or a marker written INTO it — affirmative evidence, strictly better than a path arm. **Pinned by leg 6c so D1 closing it is a loud test change, not silent drift.** Building a reader now for a marker nothing writes would be vacuous by this file's own standard.

### Residuals, disclosed in the region header

- a **deletion** of a declared path (not in the enumeration; same asymmetry the content veto documents — and a correct deletion also moves `plugin.json` or a frozen table, neither doc-named)
- `docs/specs/<task-id>.md` (above)
- anything doc-named that nothing declares

title: INVERTED ASSERTION passing green: phase5-synthetic-tests.sh:411 asserts its own opposite and will go RED when the defect it names is fixed
description:
FOUND by the negative-control census (iexi), INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED by the orchestrator 2026-08-07 in an UNCONTAMINATED file (phase5-synthetic-tests.sh is not in the modified set).

THE DEFECT, three measured facts:
1. assert_match at :52-60 increments PASS when grep -qE MATCHES. Match means pass.
2. The call at :411-412 is: assert_match with the name skill: intent-router does NOT contain Step 4 legacy text, pattern Mandatory roles|Mandatory delegation flow.
3. grep -c over .claude/skills/workflow-engine/SKILL.md for those two headings returns 2. Both alternation branches are LIVE HEADINGS in the target.
4. grep -c assert_not_match over the file returns 0. The negating helper DOES NOT EXIST. There is no typo-of-a-real-helper explanation available.

SO: the check passes PRECISELY BECAUSE the text it declares absent is present.

WHY THIS IS WORSE THAN VACUOUS, and why it is P1. A vacuous check is green over everything and merely tells you nothing. This one is INVERTED - wrong in both directions at once. It is green over exactly the input it exists to catch, AND it will turn RED on the day someone actually removes the legacy text, i.e. on the day the codebase becomes correct. Whoever does that cleanup will be handed a failing test telling them they broke something, for having fixed it. The severity rule the repo uses says announcing success over the input it exists to catch is critical; this does that AND the noise direction simultaneously.

WHERE IT SITS: inside the test suite. This is an instance of the claimed-but-unverified family living in the instrument that is supposed to detect it.

FIX: decide what the check was FOR. If the intent is that the legacy Step 4 text is gone, the repo needs an assert_not_match helper (it has none) and the assertion inverted - but note that would go RED TODAY, because the text is present, so the underlying question of whether that text SHOULD be there must be answered first and is NOT a rename. If the intent is that the skill carries those headings, the check name is simply wrong and the fix is the name. DO NOT pick whichever makes the suite green - that choice is the whole finding.

REQUIRED: whatever ships must carry a negative control proving the corrected assertion fails on the state it rejects. And sweep for siblings: any other assert_match in the repo whose NAME contains a negation is suspect by construction.

    within an open cycle, rewrite a listed file        -> hash identical (filing's measurement, reproduced)
    add a path                                          -> hash moves
    after approval, re-edit a SUBSET of the approved set -> hash moves      -> BLOCKS
    after approval, re-edit EXACTLY the approved set     -> hash identical  -> RELEASES
    after approval, single-file approved set, re-edit it -> hash identical  -> RELEASES

So the corrected bullet says the block is caused by working on a DIFFERENT SET OF FILES, and explicitly notes that re-editing a path the approval already covered moves no hash by itself. That is true in every one of the five rows above; "true only for newly tracked paths" is not.

title: Negative-control census: inventory every check for a paired META-TEST, treat unpaired as presumed vacuous, and make pairing a closeout requirement
description: THE FAMILY-LEVEL FIX for the 26 recorded instances of a check that claimed more than it verified. Every fix this arc has been instance-shaped; this one targets the generator. DO IT BEFORE D2/D4/D5/D6 mint new checks, not after. MEASURED BASELINE 2026-08-07: 22 distinct sentinel-wrapped guards in .claude/scripts/*.sh; META appears in 30 of 33 L1 spec files and 33 of 44 L2 spec files. THOSE FILE COUNTS ARE A PROXY AND MUST NOT BE THE ANSWER — a file mentioning META says nothing about whether each individual check in it has a negative control, and counting mentions to prove coverage is the exact error class being fixed. DELIVERABLES: (1) a per-check inventory across L1, L2 and L3, each check either paired with a specific named negative control or listed as UNPAIRED, (2) a recorded coverage number stated as measured with its denominator defined, (3) unpaired checks triaged by whether the underlying guard is load-bearing, (4) the pairing requirement added to the closeout convention so a new check cannot ship without a negative control, (5) the convention that a finding discovered after a task closes opens a NEW task and is never left as a comment on a closed one. THE HONEST CEILING must be stated: a census run by the same process that produced the gap is itself subject to the gap, so say what the census cannot see.

comments.author: username
comments.text:
CENSUS RAN AND ITS HEADLINE NUMBER IS CONTAMINATED - read before writing anything up.

CONTAMINATION: I ran the census as a parallel workflow while a specialist was editing the tree. Seven files moved under it mid-run (qa.md, qa-gate.sh, verify-before-stop.sh, specs/verify-before-stop.sh, docs/HOOKS.md, docs/WORKFLOW.md, plus a NEW file doc-only-classifier.test.sh created after its inventory phase). Recorded as the seventh instance on mrd2. My error, not the census.

DO NOT PUBLISH 33 PERCENT. The census reported 121 of 367 checks PAIRED = 33.0 percent, and to its credit stated in the same breath that it read only 64.2 percent of the suite (28,372 of 44,159 lines; 56 of 77 files) and that the unread third is NOT a random sample - it is the densest mutant/control vocabulary in the repo and, on the two files sampled, materially BETTER paired. A 33 percent quoted as a suite figure would be exactly the overclaim this task exists to eliminate.

THE CENSUS AUDITED ITSELF AND FOUND THREE DEFECTS IN ITS OWN ARITHMETIC - keep this, it is the most valuable part: (a) the L1 header tally does not reconcile with its own rows, and two of the five UNKNOWN rows are not checks at all, (b) it REFUTED its own loudest finding - F1-APPROVE-REFUSAL was reported as the single worst gap with no control at any tier, and is in fact a six-leg triad at specs/verify-before-stop.sh:1941-1999 with two restore-control legs, missed only because it sits in one of the 16 L2 specs nobody opened, (c) the L2 detail array truncates at bd-compat so 91/82/25 is repeated, not audited. Its own words on (b) are the thesis of this task: an absence-of-coverage claim derived from a partial population is itself an unmeasured claim announcing a result.

CORRECTION TO ITS SELF-DIAGNOSIS: it concluded it had a POPULATION-LOGIC defect because doc-only-classifier.test.sh was invisible from inside its report. Wrong cause. That file did not exist at inventory time - the specialist created it mid-run. It reasoned from an absence to a cause without checking whether the tree moved.

VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY BY THE ORCHESTRATOR, both in uncontaminated files, both now filed: q249 (phase5-synthetic-tests.sh:411 inverted assertion, P1) and the relay-deferral chain (P2, census overstatement corrected in the filing).

WHAT THIS TASK NOW REQUIRES: re-run the census against a PINNED TREE - git worktree at a commit, never the live tree - covering the full 77 files, and report the number with its denominator. The methodology, the four-part PAIRED standard including the execution leg as discriminator, and the self-audit are sound and should be reused verbatim.

comments.author: username
comments.text:
OPERATOR DECISION 2026-08-08 - STOP THE FAN-OUT CENSUS. Two runs, both partial; no third.

THE REASONING, which changes what this task IS: THE PAIRING INVENTORY IS A STANDING INVARIANT AND MUST COVER L2/L3 ANYWAY. So route that coverage through ORDINARY WORK WITH QA REVIEW - one tier at a time, gated - rather than a third fan-out. A census is a snapshot; an invariant is maintained. Building the invariant covers the population as a side effect and keeps covering it.

BANK THE BIMODAL FINDING. In the population actually covered, the pairing split is almost perfectly predicted by ONE variable: is the artifact under test an EXECUTABLE or a DOCUMENT. Every PAIRED row drives a shipped script, a shipped JS module, or a function extracted verbatim from one. Every FALSE-PAIR row compares bytes in markdown, JSON, or a script's COMMENT TEXT. Not one document check reaches the execution leg; not one executable check fails it. The tier is not uniformly weak, it is bimodal - which makes the fix targetable.

RECORD PARTIAL CENSUS COVERAGE IN THE AUDIT, with the pairing number NAMED AS THE FORWARD MECHANISM. Do not publish a tier-wide coverage percentage. v1 read 64 percent of a smaller population and was contaminated by a concurrent writer (my error, mrd2). v2 ran against a pinned worktree and delivered 2 of 6 chunks - L2's 44 specs and 25,316 lines and L3's 22 files were NEVER censused, a larger population than the tier that was. v2's own words: a total whose rows were never delivered is a claim nothing checks, which is the defect being censused.

COST CONTEXT for the record: the two runs consumed roughly 3.5M subagent tokens between them.

comments.author: username
comments.text:
DELIVERABLES (4) AND (5) LANDED. The census itself is untouched, per the 2026-08-08 operator decision to stop the fan-out.

(4) THE PAIRING REQUIREMENT — canonical in `.claude/tests/README.md` § "The pairing requirement — a new check ships with its negative control", directly under the existing META-TEST convention (where the one mechanical arm already lives). Pointer + closeout framing in `CONTRIBUTING.md` § "Failure-injection convention (META-TESTs)"; a new `CLAUDE.md` conditional-loading row keyed on the ACT ("if you are adding a new CHECK of any kind") so it is reachable without knowing where it lives.

The consequence is written as the actionable form — if the thing under test is prose, either drive the executable whose behaviour it describes, or declare UNPAIRED and say what the control is.

Both earned warnings are recorded as rules with their mechanism: do not count text to prove a claim about code; do not verify a removal by grepping for the removed pattern (the region header documenting a deleted arm contains the pattern, so it survives as prose in the file that removed it).

THE HONEST CEILING IS STATED, as this task requires. No tier-wide coverage percentage is published. The section says both runs were partial, names the contamination (a concurrent writer, seven files) and the truncation (2 of 6 chunks; L2's 44 specs and L3's 22 files never censused), and states that the pairing inventory is a standing invariant maintained one tier at a time through reviewed work rather than a snapshot.

(5) THE POST-CLOSE-FINDING CONVENTION — `CONTRIBUTING.md` § "A finding discovered after a task closes opens a NEW task", with the mechanical reason (a comment on a closed task never surfaces in a ready-work query; `bd ready`/`bd list` exclude closed by default), the wrong-vs-right command pair, `bd dep add --type discovered-from` for provenance, the instruction to put the EVIDENCE in the new task rather than in a comment on the closed one, and reopening named as the other legitimate option. NEGATIVE CONTROL FOR THESE TWO: NONE, and it is declared in the artifact rather than only here — `.claude/tests/README.md` § "This convention is itself UNPAIRED, and that is the declaration it asks for". Both conventions are prose with no shipped executable whose behaviour they change, so leg 4 is unavailable and is not claimed; a check over the wording would be the false pair this task exists to eliminate. What the control is instead: (a) they bind at review, not at runtime, with a reviewer's reliability, said plainly; (b) their worked examples carry the execution legs the prose cannot, and those are pinned — `.claude/scripts/tests/gate-claim-honesty.test.sh` ships FIVE guards in this same batch, each with a mutation that provably lands, a named specific misbehaviour, a restore control, and a leg that runs the shipped artifact; (c) the one mechanical arm that does exist is narrow and is named as such — `specs/_invariants.unit.spec.ts:1639-1678` runs `it.each(listInvariants())` and fails when a registered invariant has no `it("META-TEST: …")`, with a `META_EXEMPT` escape at :1634. STILL OPEN on this task: deliverables (1) the per-check inventory, (2) the coverage number with its denominator, and (3) the triage of unpaired checks. Per the operator decision those route through ordinary tier-at-a-time reviewed work rather than a third fan-out; the requirement they will be measured against now exists.

title: Sol review packets are bounded by size, not raw timeout: mechanize cap-completeness and a measured packet budget
description:
SUPERSEDES THE ORIGINAL TITLE/BODY, per operator directive 2026-08-13 ("the task body is stale; it predates the measurements — rewrite it to what was actually measured this arc, then fix it"). The original framing (timeout_seconds=300 cannot complete a real review; the Sol lane has never produced an artifact) is FALSIFIED — both premises were already corrected in the comment thread below before this rewrite, and are folded in here rather than left as a multi-comment trail.

CURRENT MEASURED STATE (2026-08-13), superseding everything above it:
- timeout_seconds=2400 and max_review_iterations=12 already ship as product defaults (iu5o, 2026-08-10) and are pinned by an L2 leg (codex-review.sh spec, section C8) against the shipped file's bytes.
- Sol has produced EIGHT artifacts across a9hh and fkm.3 — the lane works.
- PACKET SIZE, not timeout_seconds, is the actual lever: an ~88KB packet completed in 326s/493s/496s/613s/635s across five separate rounds; an ~144KB packet EXHAUSTED the full 2400s budget with NO artifact and NO diagnosis. These two points are NOT linear (a 1.6x size increase cost the whole budget, not 1.6x the time) — this task does not extrapolate a curve from them, it sets a budget at the last CONFIRMED-GOOD measurement.
- D2's packet (review artifact + grilling record + impact report + lessons) is expected to exceed the 144KB failure point on its own, which is why this needed to land before D2, not after its first review turn silently burns 40 minutes.

FIXED IN THIS PASS:
1. **Packet budget, checked before any Sol call.** `.claude/review-config` gained `max_request_bytes=100000` (~88KB, the confirmed-good ceiling, no headroom claimed above it — the true breakpoint before 144KB is unmeasured). `codex-review.sh` now measures the request file's byte size immediately after request validation and refuses with the NEW exit code 7 (no server spawn, no wall-clock spend at all) before doing any of the expensive FIFO/server work. Component spec `codex-review.sh` section C9 drives this end-to-end (real refusal, real byte counts in the message) with a META that strips the guard and shows the same oversized-per-cap request now reaches a real (stubbed) Sol call.

PREMISE FALSIFIED BY MEASUREMENT, 2026-08-09. THE 300s TIMEOUT WAS NEVER THE BLOCKER.

This task says review-config timeout_seconds=300 cannot complete a real review payload and that the Sol lane has never produced an artifact on one. Measured today on a real payload — a 1008-line scoped diff of verify-before-stop.sh, 63957-byte request:

  SOL_RC=0   elapsed=66s   verdict=findings   stopped_by=stop_condition   1 HIGH finding
  reviewer_identity=sol-codex   reviewer_model=gpt-5.6-sol

66 SECONDS. Well inside the ORIGINAL 300s budget. Sol produced a schema-valid artifact carrying a genuine HIGH that six Claude review rounds had not found.

WHAT ACTUALLY BLOCKED IT, measured first: max_review_iterations=3. The first attempt returned rc=6 at ZERO seconds — 'iteration 7 exceeds max_review_iterations=3'. The budget was never reached because the turn never started.

WHY THAT MATTERS MORE THAN THE TIMEOUT: the iteration counter does not distinguish CODEX turns from CLAUDE ones. This change set had consumed six CLAUDE review rounds, so it was permanently ineligible for a Codex turn regardless of budget. A task that needs several rounds — exactly the task where a second model family is most valuable — is exactly the task the cap excludes. That inverts the intent.

CORRECTED SCOPE FOR THIS TASK: (a) max_review_iterations must count Codex turns only, or be per-lane; (b) the timeout claim needs re-measurement rather than assumption — 300s was sufficient for 1008 lines at 66s, so the real question is where the payload/time curve actually breaks, not whether 300 is 'too small'; (c) the operator raised the budget to 2400s and the cap to 12 in this session, which unblocked it — that config change is in the working tree and needs committing.

METHOD NOTE for whoever re-measures: the payload was SCOPED to one file rather than the whole 7886-line change set. That scoping is what a real reviewer would receive and is probably why it fit comfortably. An unscoped whole-change-set payload has still never been measured.
