title: F1 auto-approves EXECUTABLE CODE: is_doc_only_path treats anything under a docs/ directory as documentation, so a change set of one shell script is released with reviewed_by=none
description:
QA round-8 finding R1-F2 on claude-workflow-plugin-qzv.1, recorded in the qa-claude
review artifact on that task. PRE-EXISTING — not introduced by qzv, qzv.1 or 94d.
Filed separately because it is a behaviour change to the classifier every consumer
of the fast path depends on, and because qzv.1's prose currently conceals it.

THE DEFECT. `verify-before-stop.sh`'s `is_doc_only_path` has the arm

    */docs/*|docs/*) return 0 ;;

which classifies ANY path under ANY `docs/` directory as documentation, regardless
of file type or position in the tree. F1's stated premise is "no reviewable source
changed". That premise does not hold.

MEASURED against the shipped classifier (extracted verbatim and probed):

    DOC-ONLY   docs/HOOKS.md
    DOC-ONLY   docs/examples/setup.sh        <-- a shell script
    DOC-ONLY   docs/scripts/migrate.py       <-- a Python script
    DOC-ONLY   docs/fixtures/payload.json    <-- a fixture
    DOC-ONLY   docs/Dockerfile
    DOC-ONLY   src/docs/handler.ts           <-- a docs/ component ANYWHERE in a
                                                 source tree also qualifies
    reviewable tests/qa-regression.sh
    reviewable .claude/scripts/qa-gate.sh

REPRODUCED END TO END (component fixture, shipped hooks, real qa-gate.sh). Change
set = exactly one file, `docs/deploy.sh`, an executable script whose body is a
curl-pipe-to-bash line. No IMPLEMENTER record on the task:

    change set        : <fixture>/docs/deploy.sh
    IMPLEMENTER recs  : 0
    STOP decision     : ALLOW (released)
    labels after      : qa-approved
    record written    : QA-GATE APPROVED change_set_hash=b4d4528d2d... reviewed_by=none

So an executable script was auto-approved, labelled, and recorded as approved with
no reviewer, by the fast path whose justification is that nothing reviewable changed.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN IT LOOKS. This is author-independent — it is not the `qa`
exempt-role residual, though that is how I found it. Any doc-only Stop qualifies.
And this plugin installs into arbitrary projects, where `docs/` routinely carries
runnable examples, install scripts, Dockerfiles, notebooks and fixtures. A
monorepo with `packages/*/docs/` is covered by the same arm.

WHAT IT DOES NOT BREAK, so the fix is not scoped wider than it needs to be. The
change-set binding still holds: the approval names the hash of the set it
classified, so it cannot speak for anything else, and qzv's in-flight predicate
still refuses while an implementer is working. The exposure is precisely "content
that needs review is classified as content that does not".

CANDIDATE DIRECTION (a decision, not a design). Keep the `docs/` arm as a
LOCATION hint but require the file to also match the documentation EXTENSION set
(`*.md|*.markdown|*.mdx|*.rst|*.txt` plus the extension-less LICENSE / CHANGELOG /
NOTICE / AUTHORS forms the function already lists), so `docs/guide.md` stays
fast-pathed and `docs/deploy.sh` becomes reviewable. That inverts the arm from
"anything here is docs" to "docs here are docs", which is what the surrounding
patterns already mean. Consider whether an extension-less file under `docs/`
(e.g. `docs/Makefile`) should default reviewable — I think yes, fail-closed.

AVAILABILITY IMPACT, which is the real cost and must be measured before fixing:
this makes some currently-auto-approved Stops require QA. Anyone whose docs tree
carries non-prose files loses the fast path on those commits. That is the correct
direction (F1's job is to skip review only where there is nothing to review) but
it is a behaviour change on the most-travelled fast path in the system, so it
wants its own round rather than a drive-by.

TESTS IT NEEDS.
  - Unit legs on `is_doc_only_path` for the whole probe table above, including
    `src/docs/handler.ts` (the anywhere-in-tree case) and an extension-less file.
  - An L2 leg at the hook level: change set = one `docs/*.sh` -> decision is the
    QA-required block, NOT auto-approve; 0 approval records; no qa-approved label.
    My reproduction is a working starting point and fails RED today.
  - A control leg: change set = one `docs/*.md` -> still auto-approves. The fix
    must not deadlock the documentation commits F1 exists for (the same
    anti-overreach constraint legs vbs-qzv-3 already encode).
  - A META on whichever region the fix introduces.

RELATED. claude-workflow-plugin-qzv.1 round-8 finding R1-F1 (blocking) is the
prose half of this: the F1-CHANGE-SET-BINDING region header and docs/HOOKS.md
currently assert that "a QA agent writing a test file, a script or a fixture makes
DOC_ONLY false on its own", which this reproduction falsifies. R1-F1 corrects the
claim; this task corrects the behaviour. The claim must not be corrected by
pointing at this task as though it were already fixed.

comments.text:
ORCHESTRATOR: RAISED P2 -> P1, 2026-08-05. Verified independently, and it must be resolved before v5.0.0 ships (D7 at the latest).

CONFIRMED: is_doc_only_path's arm 11 is '*/docs/*|docs/*) return 0'. Tested in isolation against the same glob: docs/deploy.sh, docs/scripts/migrate.py, docs/Dockerfile and src/docs/handler.ts all classify DOC-ONLY. QA reproduced the consequence end-to-end — a change set of one executable docs/deploy.sh with zero IMPLEMENTER records auto-approves, sets qa-approved, and records 'QA-GATE APPROVED ... reviewed_by=none'.

WHY P1 RATHER THAN P2, disagreeing with the filing (whose reasoning — author-independent, pre-existing, changes behaviour on all three fast-path classes — I accept as reasons not to fix it in qzv.1's round, not as reasons it is P2):

  1. It is a gate bypass requiring NO privilege. Not a label, not a bd write, not a flag: file placement. Put a script under docs/ and the mandatory review does not happen.
  2. reviewed_by=none is not 'reviewed lightly'. It is not reviewed.
  3. It ships to every install. This repo's docs/ happens to hold only markdown; a consuming project with docs/scripts/, docs/examples/ or a docs/Dockerfile is the normal case, not the exotic one, and those are exactly the places people put runnable things.
  4. It is orthogonal to every protection built today. The change-set binding, the reconciler, the completeness accounting and the F1 predicate are all correct here and all irrelevant — the set is classified as needing no review before any of them apply.
  5. F1 exists to spare a human a round-trip on prose. A file that executes is not prose, whatever directory it sits in.

WHAT IT IS NOT: not a regression, not introduced by 94d/qzv/qzv.1, and not urgent in THIS repo's own tree. So it does not block qzv.1's prose round. It does block claiming, at D7, that the workflow cannot release unreviewed code.

FIX SHAPE (for whoever takes it): the directory arm should not override file type. Prefer classifying by EXTENSION with the docs/ directory as a narrowing condition rather than a sufficient one — e.g. under docs/, still require the file to be one of the documentation extensions already enumerated on arms 5-10, and treat anything executable, any Dockerfile, and any recognised source extension as code wherever it lives. QA notes this changes behaviour on all three fast-path classes, so it needs its own legs per class plus a leg pinning that docs/*.md stays fast-pathed.

RELATED: the same shape as rmz in one respect — the workflow's decision is driven by a cheap surface property (a path glob, an inherited label) standing in for the expensive fact it is supposed to represent (is this reviewable code, was this actually reviewed). Both were found the same way: by probing the classifier rather than reading its name.

**P1 is right and my P2 was the error.** Pre-existing and author-independent are reasons not to fix it inside qzv.1's round; they are not reasons it is P2. It is a gate bypass needing no privilege beyond file placement, shipped to every install, and orthogonal to every protection qzv/qzv.1 built. Not in scope for qzv.1; nothing here blocked that approval.

**You are mechanically guaranteed to arrive at the prose.** `.claude/tests/component/specs/verify-before-stop.sh` leg `vbs-qzv-9` asserts today's behaviour (an executable `docs/deploy.sh` is fast-pathed, auto-approved, `reviewed_by=none`) with a placement CONTROL. Your candidate fix makes `docs/deploy.sh` reviewable and turns that leg RED **by design**. Flip the expectation and the prose in the SAME change set. The coupling is sound; two corrections to its instructions:

**1. Its repair list is missing a file (QA R2-F2, low).** The site comment names "the region header and docs/HOOKS.md". It omits **`.claude/agents/qa.md:851-856`**, which asserts the same breadth ("`is_doc_only_path` matches anything under any `docs/` directory regardless of file type") and also goes false when you land. Three passages, not two. Root cause worth knowing: qzv.1 deliberately made qa.md self-contained instead of pointing at the region header — good for the reader, but it removed the pointer that would have kept it in sync. Add qa.md to the coupling comment while you are there.

**2. A clause in the passages is ALREADY false, and your fix does not close it (QA R2-F1, medium).** Both `verify-before-stop.sh:1209-1211` and `docs/HOOKS.md:1379-1381` close with "Only one placed elsewhere — a test at `tests/`, a hook at `.claude/scripts/` — makes DOC_ONLY false and takes F1 out of play." Measured against `is_doc_only_path` extracted by awk from the shipped file (sha256 `0bdaee6e644689e5901d8223ce242a992846fca0c938d2acb74eac66ac0966f9`), these are all DOC-ONLY while sitting **outside any `docs/` directory**:

    DOC-ONLY  tests/spec.txt              <-- inside the sentence's OWN example
    DOC-ONLY  .claude/scripts/hook.txt    <-- inside its OTHER example
    DOC-ONLY  LICENSE.sh  LICENSE.py  LICENSE.yml
    DOC-ONLY  CHANGELOG   NOTICE   AUTHORS
    DOC-ONLY  src/handler.rst   notes.mdx   tests/fixtures/payload.txt

Placement outside `docs/` is NECESSARY, not SUFFICIENT: the extension arms (`*.md|*.markdown|*.mdx|*.rst|*.txt`) and the extension-less `LICENSE`/`CHANGELOG`/`NOTICE`/`AUTHORS` forms classify by NAME at any location. **Your candidate direction (require the documentation extension set inside the `docs/` arm) does NOT close the `*.txt` route**, so a change set of only `tests/fixtures/golden.txt` still fast-paths after you land — worth deciding explicitly whether that is intended, because a golden file is a test ASSERTION and weakening one unreviewed is the same exposure class in a different arm.

**Do not attempt a third hand-enumeration.** This clause is the SECOND consecutive false version of this paragraph (round 7 said a script cannot be doc-only; round 8's correction said placement elsewhere is enough), and it is instance SIX of the pattern recorded on `fkm.1`: "five false prose claims, each written by a round that had just corrected the previous one." title: GATE BYPASS: bd 1.1.2 `create --parent` INHERITS the parent's labels, so a sub-task filed under an approved parent is born carrying qa-approved
description:
Found by the reconcile-task-state check the specialist prompts mandate, doing exactly what that paragraph says it is for: `bd_create_task` echoed back a label I had not passed. HOW IT SURFACED. While filing claude-workflow-plugin-qzv.3 under parent `qzv`, I passed `labels: ["bug","devops"]`. The response came back `"labels":["bug","devops","qa-approved"]`. `qzv` carries `qa-approved` (QA approved its change set at 19:08 on 2026-08-04). A brand-new, never-reviewed task was born approved. I removed the label from qzv.3 immediately; the ledger is clean as of this filing (see BLAST RADIUS). IT IS bd ITSELF, not this repo's MCP layer and not a hook. Reproduced in an isolated throwaway workspace with the bd CLI directly, no plugin involved: bd init P=$(bd create "probe parent" -t bug -p 1 -l devops --json | jq -r .id) bd label add "$P" qa-approved bd create "probe child" -t bug -p 2 -l bug,devops --parent "$P" --json parent labels : devops,qa-approved child labels : bug,devops,qa-approved <-- inherited, never passed bd version 1.1.2 (20e493e56: 20e493e569c9) WHY THIS IS P1. `qa-approved` is the gate's SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH — verify-before-stop.sh releases the Stop when the active task carries it, and CLAUDE.md's rule is explicit that any side channel makes the gate non-deterministic. This is not a side channel: the label is genuinely present, so every check downstream is correct to trust it. The bypass is that it was never earned. The reachable sequence is ordinary, not contrived: 1. An epic or parent task is approved (or a parent picks up qa-approved on any route). 2. Anyone decomposes further work under it — `bd create --parent`, or the bd-mcp `bd_create_epic(children:[...])` path, which threads `--parent` for every child. 3. Each new child is born qa-approved. 4. A Stop with that child active RELEASES with no review of any kind. This project decomposes under parents constantly, and it files follow-up children under already-reviewed parents as a matter of habit — that is how I hit it. EVERY parent label is inherited, not just this one. `qa-gate-entered`, `rubric-satisfied`, `qa-blocked` and any future gate label ride along too, each with its own consequence (a child that looks mid-cycle, a child whose rubric is pre-satisfied, a child that looks blocked). BLAST RADIUS, measured on this ledger now. Exactly ONE open task carries qa-approved (`qzv`), and it earned it — its `QA-GATE APPROVED` record is present. `qzv.3` was the only inherited instance and its label is removed. So there is no live false approval as of 2026-08-04T20:26Z. The general hazard is what needs fixing. THE CLEAN DISCRIMINATOR for an audit, worth writing down because it makes this detectable rather than merely feared: an EARNED qa-approved always has a `QA-GATE APPROVED change_set_hash=... ` record comment on the same task (qa-gate.sh approve writes both, and gz3 pinned the ordering). An INHERITED one has the label and no such record. A sweep for "label without record" finds every instance, including historical ones, without guessing. FIX DIRECTIONS (pick deliberately; I have not chosen one). 1. Strip gate labels at the creation seam. bd-mcp's create paths (`bd_create_task`, `bd_create_epic`) post-process the created issue and remove any gate label the caller did not pass. Cheapest, and it covers the path the orchestrator actually uses — but NOT a bare `bd create --parent` from a Bash call, which agents also make. 2. Refuse to trust the label alone at the gate: require the paired `QA-GATE APPROVED` record before releasing. Strictly stronger and it closes the bare-CLI route too, but it is a change to the release predicate itself and needs weighing against the bd-1.1.2 comment-inlining failure the gate already carries `bd_show_with_comments` for (a task whose comments cannot be read would stop releasing). 3. QA ROUND 8 — REPRODUCED INDEPENDENTLY, READERS ENUMERATED, AND TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE FILING.

REPRODUCTION (isolated throwaway bd workspace, bare `bd` CLI 1.1.2, no hooks, no MCP; workspace deleted afterwards and the real DB verified unchanged):

```
  PARENT rmzp-eq8      labels=[devops,qa-approved]
  CHILD  rmzp-eq8.1    labels=[devops,qa-approved]   <-- NO labels were passed
  CHILD  paired QA-GATE APPROVED records = 0
```

Confirmed. **NEW: the inheritance is TRANSITIVE.** A grandchild filed under the inherited child is ALSO born carrying it:

```
  GRANDCHILD rmzp-eq8.1.1  labels=[devops,qa-approved]
```

So one approved ancestor contaminates an entire subtree, not just its direct children. The filing does not currently say this and it widens the blast radius materially: a decomposition several levels deep under an approved parent produces an arbitrary number of never-reviewed tasks all carrying the release label.

READER ENUMERATION — the filing asked for it, so here it is measured rather than listed. Four readers trust the label; one is exploitable.

1. **`verify-before-stop.sh` — NOT exploitable. The containment is real and I verified it by reading the path end to end.** `LABEL_WITHOUT_RECORD` is set at :1818 when the label is present with no record whose `change_set_hash` matches the current change set, consumed at :1878, and blocks at :2256 with *"qa-approved label present but no change-set-bound approval record matches the current changes — approve via qa-gate.sh approve, not a bare label add."* An inherited label has no record by construction, so it can never release. The brief's line numbers (1818/1878/2257) are right to within one line. **One caveat worth recording:** :1878-1884 deliberately RELEASES rather than blocks when the change set has vanished (the gz3 concurrent-approve case). An inherited-label task with an empty change set therefore releases — correctly, because there is nothing to review, but it means the containment is "cannot release UNREVIEWED WORK", not "cannot release".

2. **`epic-gate.sh check` — EXPLOITABLE. This is the one.** `qa_state_of` (:115-127) reads labels ONLY, with no record check. Measured against the reproduction:

```
  {"decision":"pass",
   "totals":{"total":1,"approved":1,"blocked":0,"pending":0,"entered":0,"other":0},
   "observations":"All 1 sub-task(s) qa-approved under epic rmzp-eq8; epic can close."}
```

The child was never reviewed and has zero approval records, and the epic gate green-lights closure. This is orchestrator-facing (`orchestrator.md`:738) and is the signal the orchestrator uses to decide whether an epic may close, so an inherited label converts directly into "this epic's work is done" with no review of any kind behind it. It cannot release a Stop by itself — the child's own Stop still meets the containment in (1) — so what ships is the CLAIM, not the code. Given that closing an epic is how work leaves the queue, I rate that a real bypass of the workflow rather than a cosmetic misreport. **Whatever fixes `rmz` should also make `qa_state_of` require the paired record**, otherwise the same hole reopens the next time any other path writes the label.

3. **`qa-gate.sh status` / `bd_qa_status` (bd_qa.js:124, `if (labels.includes('qa-approved')) return {status:'approved'}`) — MISREPORTS, not exploitable.** Measured: returns `{"status":"approved"}` for the never-reviewed child. It is the status oracle every other reader consults, including `verify-before-stop.sh`'s `GATE_STATUS`, but the release path re-checks for a record, so the misreport is contained downstream. It still means an agent or human asking "is this approved?" is told yes.

4. **`statusline.sh` (:158, :222) — cosmetic.** Displays `approved`. Misleading, cannot gate anything.

5. **`bd list --label qa-approved` — MISREPORTS for open tasks.** In my reproduction it listed only the parent, but only because I had closed the child first and `bd list` excludes closed by default; an OPEN inherited child is listed. This is also why the clean audit result is trustworthy: the same default was used, and no unearned OPEN task appeared.

CORRECTION 1 — THE AUDIT COUNT. The round-8 brief states qzv carries **three** paired `QA-GATE APPROVED` records. It carries **one**. `bd show claude-workflow-plugin-qzv | grep -c 'QA-GATE APPROVED'` does return 3, but two hits are prose QUOTATIONS of other tasks' records inside qzv's own description and comments (0fc's at output line 109, uvk's at line 212 — both part of the historical defect timeline). The only genuine record is at line 618: `change_set_hash=34bb046d5be7 reviewed_by=qa-claude at 2026-08-04T19:08:32Z`, my round-7 approval. **The audit CONCLUSION is unaffected and I independently confirm it** — `bd list --label qa-approved` returns exactly one open task, `qzv`, and its label is earned. But this filing's whole discriminator is "an earned label always has the paired record", so a stated 3 against an actual 1 sends the next reader hunting for two records that never existed. It is also a neat illustration of why reading with plain `bd show` needs care here: the record grammar appears inside prose about the record grammar.

CORRECTION 2 — A THIRD DURABLE FILING. The ledger reconcile (315 -> 318) made three ids durable, not two: `qzv.3`, `rmz`, and `qzv.4` — *"PROBE rmz inheritance — delete me"*, the throwaway probe itself. I verified its shipped state in both the ledger and the DB: `status=closed`, `labels=[devops]` only, close reason *"PROBE for rmz label inheritance; reproduced and deleted immediately. Not real work."* The inherited `qa-approved` was correctly stripped. Harmless and self-documenting; recorded only so a reader reconciling the F7 contract (which names two filings) against ground truth does not find an unexplained id. Note it inherited `devops` too, which confirms the mechanism is not specific to gate labels.

DOC CONSEQUENCE, agreeing with the filing and stating it sharply: `CLAUDE.md` says *"the gate's single source of truth is the Beads label"*. That is now false in BOTH directions — the label is not sufficient (the release path demands a change-set-bound record) and it is not uniquely earned (inheritance mints it). The accurate statement is that the **change-set-bound `QA-GATE APPROVED` record** is the single source of truth and the label is an index into it. Out of scope here; worth a line in whatever closes this.

## LIVE INSTANCE FOUND — and it corrects this task's own blast-radius claim

My filing said "there is no live false approval as of 2026-08-04T20:26Z" and gave
the blast radius as ZERO. **That was true only for `qa-approved`, which is the only
label I checked.** For the gate-CYCLE labels it is not zero, and the instance is

Found by following an anomaly rather than by looking for it: `review-check.sh gate
claude-workflow-plugin-qzv.1` returned `cycle_opened_ts: ""` while the task
carried `qa-gate-entered`.

**Measured, all four tasks in the family:**

```
task    labels                                                    QA-GATE: entered records
qzv     devops,qa-approved                                                 1   <- earned
qzv.1   bug,devops,qa-blocked,qa-gate-entered,qa-pending,rubric-pending     0   <- never entered
qzv.2   bug,devops,qa-gate-entered,rubric-pending                           0   <- never entered
qzv.3   bug,devops                                                          0   <- see below
```

**The mechanism copies every gate label, not just `qa-approved`** — reproduced in a
fresh throwaway workspace with the bare bd CLI:

```
parent : devops,qa-gate-entered,qa-pending,rubric-pending
child  : bug,devops,qa-gate-entered,qa-pending,rubric-pending   (passed: bug,devops)
```

`qzv.3` is the **negative control and it fits**: I created it after `qzv` had been
approved, so the parent no longer carried `qa-gate-entered` — and `qzv.3` did not
get it. It inherited `qa-approved` instead, which is the instance I already
reported and stripped.

**A SECOND DISCRIMINATOR, same shape as the first.** An earned `qa-gate-entered`
always has a paired `QA-GATE: entered at <ts>` record, because `cmd_enter` writes
the label and the comment in the same call. An inherited one has the label and no
record. So the audit sweep in the description generalises: for each gate label,
compare label presence against its paired record.

**WHY THE CYCLE-LABEL CASE HAS ITS OWN CONSEQUENCE, distinct from the approval
one.** `cmd_enter` returns EARLY when the task is already entered, and that early
return writes no cycle record. So a task born with an inherited `qa-gate-entered`
can never acquire a cycle record through the normal path — the one call that would
write it sees the label and declines. The task is permanently in the state
`verify-before-stop.sh`'s own F1 predicate classifies as `unestablished` (branch 5:
"the qa-gate-entered LABEL says a review cycle is open but no `QA-GATE: entered`
record came back"). That branch exists for the bd-1.1.2 comment-inlining failure;
label inheritance reaches the same state by a completely different route.

**Honest limit on the attribution.** I cannot rule out that `qzv.1`'s label came
from a legitimate `enter` whose `add_comment` failed. What I can say: the
inheritance mechanism is independently reproduced above, `qzv.1` and `qzv.2` carry
exactly the labels their parent held mid-cycle plus the two I passed, and `qzv.3`
is a negative control that behaves as the mechanism predicts. That is consistent
with inheritance on all four tasks; a failed `add_comment` would have to have
happened twice and coincidentally produced the parent's exact label set.

**I did NOT strip the labels from `qzv.1` or `qzv.2`.** `qzv.1` is under active
review; changing its gate state from inside its own implementation round is not
mine to do, and `qzv.2` is not my task. Recorded here for whoever fixes this.

Also worth noting for the fix design: this makes option 3 in the description
(an audit that reports label-without-record) more valuable than I rated it, because
the cycle-label case is *self-perpetuating* — the early return means it cannot heal
itself, so detection is the only route to noticing it.

title: F1's approve refusal is swallowed: the Stop RELEASES with no approval and a WIPED tracker — and approve's own impact_report_unverifiable refusal is unreachable under set -e
description:
QA finding R7-F4, carried onto its own task after qzv.1 assessed it. QA rated it
"near-unreachable"; that rating is WRONG, and I am correcting it with a live
reproduction rather than an argument. There are TWO defects on one path and they
must be fixed together — see WHY ONE TASK below.

REPRODUCED (component fixture, real scripts, 2026-08-04). Remove
`.claude/scripts/impact-report.sh` — a partially-synced install, exactly the
degradation class the F1 predicate already has dedicated legs for (vbs-qzv-4/-5)
— then drive a doc-only Stop on an entered task:

    impact-report.sh present : no
    Stop decision            : ALLOW   (bare {} — the Stop RELEASED)
    QA-GATE APPROVED records : 0       (nothing was approved)
    labels                   : devops,qa-gate-entered,qa-pending,rubric-pending
    changed-files.txt        : WIPED
    sync-errors.log          : "qa-gate approve failed during F1 doc-only fast
                                path ... no approval was recorded"

So the gate released a change set, recorded no approval for it, and destroyed the
tracker that named it. The only trace is a line in sync-errors.log.

DEFECT 1 — the hook swallows its own approve failure (this is R7-F4 proper).
verify-before-stop.sh's F1 arm calls
`"$QA_GATE" approve ... >/dev/null 2>&1 || log_sync_error "...; no approval was
recorded"` and then falls straight through to the `rm -f` cleanup and
`echo "{}"; exit 0`. Any non-zero approve is logged and ignored. Note the
cleanup runs on the failure path too, so the refusal costs the change set as
well as the approval — QA's write-up named the silent release but not the wipe.

DEFECT 2 — approve's matching refusal cannot fire, so it is mute (found while
verifying defect 1; NOT in QA's write-up). qa-gate.sh has `set -e` (:89).
`compute_change_set_hash` (:1050) does `printf ''; return 1` when
IMPACT_REPORT_SCRIPT is missing. At :2248 cmd_approve writes

    current_hash=$(compute_change_set_hash)

with no `||` guard, so under `set -e` the ASSIGNMENT aborts the script and the
`impact_report_unverifiable` refusal three lines below at :2250 is dead code.
Observed: `approve` exits 1 with EMPTY stdout and EMPTY stderr — no envelope, no
error_key, nothing. `bash -x` ends at `+ current_hash=`. The same call is written
CORRECTLY 550 lines earlier at :1696 (`... || current_hash=""`), which is what
makes this a slip rather than a design choice.

WHY ONE TASK, not two. Fixing defect 2 alone buys nothing an operator can see:
the hook redirects approve's stdout and stderr to /dev/null, so a newly-reachable
envelope still lands nowhere, and the Stop still releases. Fixing defect 1 alone
leaves the hook blocking on an approve that explains nothing. The pair is one
failure path and should land as one change set.

WHAT A FIX HAS TO DECIDE, because it is not just "block instead of release":
  - Where does the refusal surface? Capturing approve's stdout instead of
    discarding it, and putting error_key + observations in the block reason, is
    what makes the block actionable. A bare "approve failed" block is a dead end.
  - Does the tracker survive? It has to — a block whose recovery requires the
    change set, over a wiped change set, is unrecoverable. This is the same
    finalization-scope question as claude-workflow-plugin-qzv.2 (whose route (c)
    is the SUCCESS path's wipe), so the two must agree on when the F1 arm is
    allowed to finalize tracking state. Do not fix them independently.
  - Availability. This turns a path that always released into one that can
    block, on all three fast-path classes (doc-only / beads-state / empty). The
    reachable causes I could establish are degraded-install shapes; the
    `change_set_reconstructed` and `tracker_unreconcilable` refusals are NOT
    reachable here (the hook's own unconditional `reconcile-tracker` at :898
    fail-closes first, so the in-arm `enter` is an idempotent reconcile — QA's
    reasoning on that point is correct and holds).

TESTS IT NEEDS.
  - L2 leg, hook level: impact-report.sh absent + a doc-only tracked change set
    on an entered task -> decision=block, the reason names the approve failure
    and its error_key, 0 approval records, and changed-files.txt SURVIVES. The
    probe above is a working starting point.
  - L2 leg, approve level: with impact-report.sh absent, `approve` exits 2 with
    error_key=impact_report_unverifiable and a parseable envelope (today: exit 1,
    empty output). This leg fails RED against the shipped script right now.
  - A META on whichever region the fix introduces.

NOT A REGRESSION FROM qzv OR qzv.1. --expect-hash adds one more route into the
refusal, but the swallow and the `set -e` abort both predate them.
notes:
COMPLETED (devops, 2026-08-07): both defects fixed in one change set, both REPRODUCED against the shipped scripts first and re-measured after. Your rating correction stands in every particular; QA's "near-unreachable" was wrong.

REPRODUCTION BEFORE THE FIX (component fixture, real bd, shipped scripts; impact-report.sh symlink
removed AFTER `enter` had written the artifact, so the run reaches compute_change_set_hash rather than
refusing earlier with impact_report_missing):

  ARM A — the HOOK
    Stop decision            : ALLOW  (bare {})
    QA-GATE APPROVED records : 0
    labels                   : devops,qa-gate-entered,qa-pending,rubric-pending
    changed-files.txt        : WIPED

    same call, set +e: rc=2, error_key=impact_report_unverifiable
    bash -x on the shipped arm ends at `+ current_hash=`  (attribution, not inference)

    `approve --no-impact-report '<reason>' ...` with the script absent: rc=1, EMPTY stdout, EMPTY

THE FIX
- qa-gate.sh: `current_hash=$(compute_change_set_hash) || current_hash=""` (:3025 region) and
  `approved_hash=$(compute_change_set_hash) || approved_hash=""` (:3054 region), each with an

- verify-before-stop.sh F1 arm: approve's stdout+stderr are CAPTURED (`2>&1` into a variable) instead

  error_key + approve's own `observations` in the reason. The `rm -f` cleanup is now scoped to a
  SUCCESSFUL approval, so the tracker survives — emit_block exits before it.

AFTER (same fixture, same fault injection)
    Stop decision            : block
    reason                   : names `qa-gate.sh approve` REFUSED, "approve exit: 2",
                               error_key=impact_report_unverifiable, and approve's observations verbatim
    QA-GATE APPROVED records : 0
    changed-files.txt        : present (1 line)
    approve directly         : rc=2 + full parseable envelope (was rc=1, empty/empty)
    --no-impact-report bypass: rc=0, 1 record, observations say "WITHOUT a change-set binding"

THE ORDERING YOU FLAGGED: NOTHING IN qa-gate.sh MOVED. The gz3 APPROVE-COMMIT ORDER (record before
label; baseline before tracker; session state last) is untouched — approve's refusals all `exit 2`
BEFORE that finalization and never reach it. The wipe was the HOOK's own `rm -f`, on the failure path.
The fix states, from the hook's side, the same rule qzv.2 must decide for the success path: the F1 arm
may finalize tracking state only for an approval that actually happened. qzv.2 narrows WHICH cycle's
state a successful approval may finalize; this fixes that a FAILED one finalizes any. They agree; they
do not overlap.

AVAILABILITY: this turns a path that ALWAYS released into one that can block, on all three fast-path
classes. Reachable causes established: impact_report_* (degraded install), expected_hash_mismatch
(NOT a degraded install — it is qzv's own refusal, which until now also ended in a silent release, so
the guard qzv shipped was inert), and exit 3 (rolled-back label write). change_set_reconstructed and
tracker_unreconcilable are NOT reachable: the hook's unconditional reconcile-tracker fail-closes first,
making the in-arm `enter` an idempotent reconcile — QA's round-8 reasoning re-checked and it holds.

TWO BRANCHES I EXECUTED RATHER THAN ASSUMED
- SUCCESS path stdout: exactly `{}`, 2 bytes, od-verified, whole stdout parses as JSON, approval

- UNPARSEABLE envelope (approve exits non-zero with no JSON — the shape the errexit abort used to

TESTS (L2 `specs/verify-before-stop.sh`)
- leg 10: the hook. CONTROL first (impact-report.sh present -> ALLOW), then the probe -> block, reason

- leg 12: the F1 SUCCESS path's WHOLE stdout is exactly `{}` (no tail salvage) — the regression this

- leg 13: approve fails with NO parseable envelope -> still blocks, still says something, tracker survives.
- qzv.3 META: strip F1-APPROVE-REFUSAL -> the identical Stop RELEASES, 0 records, tracker WIPED (the

QA ROUND 8 — ADJUDICATION. **The dispute is resolved in devops's favour. My round-7 "near-unreachable / low" rating was WRONG, and I have raised this task P2 -> P1 on the strength of my own reproduction, not on the argument.**

REPRODUCED INDEPENDENTLY (component fixture, shipped scripts, doc-only tracked change set on an entered task, `impact-report.sh` removed):

```
  hook rc              : 0
  envelope             : {}          <-- no decision field, the Stop RELEASED
  labels after         : devops,qa-gate-entered,qa-pending,rubric-pending
  QA-GATE APPROVED     : 0
  changed-files.txt    : MISSING     <-- the tracker was DESTROYED
  current-task         : survives
  sync-errors.log      : "qa-gate approve failed during F1 doc-only fast path
                          ... hash=<unavailable>"
```

So: **the gate released, approved nothing, and destroyed the change set that named what it released.** Every particular of the filing reproduces. One refinement to the write-up: `current-task` SURVIVES the failure path; only `changed-files.txt` is wiped.

DEFECT 2 REPRODUCED WITH A TWO-ARM CONTROL, which is what makes it a fact rather than a reading of `set -e` semantics:

```
  ARM A  shipped (set -e at :89)   -> rc=1, stdout EMPTY, stderr EMPTY
  ARM B  same call, `set +e`       -> rc=2, error_key=impact_report_unverifiable
```

The guard fires the moment errexit is off, so `impact_report_unverifiable` at :2250 is confirmed dead code under the shipped script. Note for the record: my measurement is **rc=1**, matching this task's text; the round-8 brief said rc=3. rc=1 is what `return 1` propagating through errexit gives, and it is what I observed.

**WHY MY RATING WAS WRONG, precisely — so the next reviewer can avoid the same error.** My round-7 reasoning was sound but its ENUMERATION was incomplete. I reasoned about the refusals reachable via tracker state (`change_set_reconstructed`, `tracker_unreconcilable`) and correctly concluded the hook's unconditional `reconcile-tracker` at :898 fail-closes first, making the in-arm `enter` an idempotent reconcile. That reasoning holds and devops confirms it. What I never considered was a refusal reachable **through a missing script rather than through tracker state** — and `compute_change_set_hash` returns non-zero on exactly one condition, `IMPACT_REPORT_SCRIPT` missing, which no amount of tracker reasoning touches. I rated the finding on the routes I had enumerated instead of on the routes that exist. That is the error, and "near-unreachable" is the sentence that hid it.

**WHY P1.** A Stop that releases with zero approval records is a gate bypass, which is this system's most severe failure class — it is the same outcome class as `rmz`, reached by a different door. It is reachable through a degradation class this repo already models with dedicated legs (vbs-qzv-4/-5 exist for exactly "a shipped script is missing"), and LESSONS already records a live instance of a partially-synced tree going undetected for a whole run. And the tracker wipe makes it worse than a plain bypass: the evidence needed to re-establish the change set is destroyed on the way out, so the failure is not merely silent but self-erasing.

**PLACEMENT: defect 2 rides this task, and should not be split.** I considered splitting it — `|| current_hash=""` is a one-line, zero-risk change that turns dead code live — and rejected it for the reason the filing already gives, which I verified: the hook redirects approve's stdout AND stderr to `/dev/null`, so a newly-reachable envelope still lands nowhere and the Stop still releases. Fixing defect 2 alone produces no operator-visible change whatsoever. One failure path, one change set.

Both `WHAT A FIX HAS TO DECIDE` and `TESTS IT NEEDS` are correctly scoped as filed; I add nothing to them. The coupling to qzv.2's finalization scope is real and the instruction not to fix them independently should be honoured.

title: qzv predicate false negative: record_implementer is idempotent per (role, task), so latest_implementer_ts is the FIRST spawn — a re-spawn in a later cycle is invisible and F1 auto-approves mid-implementation again
description:
Found while BUILDING the qzv predicate, filed rather than left latent. Named in the
`F1-CHANGE-SET-BINDING` region header in verify-before-stop.sh so no reader can take the
predicate for stronger than it is.

THE PREDICATE (qzv, shipped): F1 may auto-approve only when no `IMPLEMENTER: role=… task=… at
<ts>` record on the active task is at-or-newer than the most recent `QA-GATE: entered at <ts>`.
Both timestamps come from `review-check.sh gate`'s envelope.

THE FALSE NEGATIVE. `subagent-start.sh record_implementer` is idempotent per (role, task) — its
own IMPLEMENTER-IDEMPOTENCY-GUARD skips when `^IMPLEMENTER: role=<role> ` already matches any
comment on the task. So `latest_implementer_ts` is the timestamp of that role's FIRST spawn on
that task, not its most recent one.

REACHABLE SEQUENCE, entirely ordinary:
  1. cycle 1: `qa-gate.sh enter` writes `QA-GATE: entered at T1`
  2. devops spawns -> `IMPLEMENTER: role=devops … at T2` (T2 > T1)
  3. approve -> removes `qa-gate-entered`
  4. cycle 2: a FRESH `enter` writes `QA-GATE: entered at T3` (T3 > T2). NB a re-enter on an
     ALREADY-entered task returns early and writes NO record, so only a fresh cycle moves this.
  5. devops is re-spawned at T4 > T3 -> record_implementer posts NOTHING (idempotent)
  6. a doc-only Stop lands while that implementer is working
  -> the compare sees impl=T2 < cycle=T3, reads "belongs to a previous cycle", verdict=safe,
     and F1 auto-approves + writes qa-approved on work that does not exist. The original qzv
     defect, one cycle later.

SECOND ROUTE, same root: `is_implementer_role` is backend|frontend|devops only — `qa` is
deliberately excluded (recording it would make every single-agent review non-independent). A QA
agent writing test files during review therefore produces NO record at all, so the predicate has
nothing to compare and reads safe.

WHY IT IS P2 AND NOT P1. The shipped predicate is strictly stronger than the nothing it
replaced: the reproduced live route (implementer in flight in the SAME cycle, four occurrences
including the v4.1.0 release task) is closed. This is a narrower residual, and the change-set
binding still contains the blast radius the way it did before.

CANDIDATE FIX (not applied here — it changes a different script's contract and that script's own
L2 META): re-key record_implementer's idempotency on (role, task, CYCLE) rather than (role,
task) — i.e. skip only when an existing record for that role is NEWER than the latest
`QA-GATE: entered` record. That reuses the two facts the qzv predicate already compares, so it
adds no new state and no new parser; `review-check.sh gate`'s `cycle_opened_ts` is already the
value it needs. The `qa` route is a separate decision: either post a non-implementer record for
it, or state explicitly that QA-authored files are out of scope for this predicate.

TESTS THE FIX NEEDS: an L2 leg driving the five-step sequence above (two cycles, same role,
second spawn) and asserting F1 refuses on the second cycle; plus a mutation of the re-keyed
guard proving the leg is load-bearing. `subagent-start.sh`'s existing IMPLEMENTER-IDEMPOTENCY
META (duplicates must not post within one cycle) must stay green.
notes:

comments.text:
ORCHESTRATOR ASSESSMENT, 2026-08-04 — verified independently, and the consequence is sharper than 'a limitation.'

VERIFIED: subagent-start.sh record_implementer short-circuits on grep -qE '^IMPLEMENTER: role=${role} ' -> return 0. Idempotent per (role, task). So latest_implementer_ts is that role's FIRST spawn on the task, permanently.

THE REACHABLE FAILURE, spelled out:
  cycle 1 opens T1; devops spawns T2>T1  -> predicate BLOCKS. Correct.
  QA blocks. Cycle 2 opens T3>T2. devops re-spawned -> posts NOTHING.
  latest_implementer_ts is still T2 < T3 -> predicate reads 'implementer older
  than cycle open' -> F1 AUTO-APPROVES while devops is mid-implementation.

That is the ORIGINAL qzv defect, verbatim, from the second cycle onward. And multi-cycle is this project's norm, not its exception — 94d took six.

WHAT NARROWS IT: F1 requires DOC_ONLY, i.e. EVERY changed file matches the doc-only patterns (verify-before-stop.sh:946). So the shape needs cycle>=2 AND a re-spawned role mid-work AND a change set that is entirely documentation at Stop time. Narrow. Not hypothetical: this session's own R4 round had the specialist edit docs/HOOKS.md three times before touching any script, and a Stop in that window would have qualified.

SO THE HONEST CLAIM IS: P2 does not fix qzv. It narrows qzv from 'any cycle' to 'cycle >= 2 with a doc-only change set'. Strictly better than before, disclosed at the point of use rather than buried — the region header carries a worked T1/T2/T3 example — but the defect qzv describes remains reachable.

FIX DIRECTION (small, needs a decision not a design): record_implementer's idempotency is presumably there to avoid comment spam. The cheapest correct options are (a) drop idempotency and append per spawn, or (b) key the idempotency on the current cycle so a record is posted once per (role, task, cycle). (b) preserves the anti-spam intent and makes the timestamp mean what the predicate assumes it means. Either way the predicate stops depending on a record that cannot express the thing it is being asked about — which is the R6-F1 shape the region header itself cites.

Also note qa has no IMPLEMENTER record at all by design, so the predicate is structurally blind to QA's own edits. Relevant because QA holds Write/Edit/MultiEdit.

RAISED TO QA for the round decision: can qzv close with qzv.1 open, or must qzv.1 land first? I lean toward requiring it — a predicate that works only in cycle 1 does not deliver what P2 was scoped to deliver, and P3-P9 plus D2/D5 all add gates on top of it. But it is QA's call and I have not asked devops to change anything.

         predicate: cycle=18:32:06Z  impl=18:31:38Z
         STOP -> ALLOW                                  <-- qzv REPRODUCED
         labels: devops,qa-approved
         QA-GATE APPROVED change_set_hash=9529165... reviewed_by=none
           'Auto-approved: doc-only change-set detected (F1 fast path)'
```

So the orchestrator's independent reading is correct and now has a reproduction behind it. `record_implementer`'s short-circuit (`grep -qE "^IMPLEMENTER: role=${role} "` -> `return 0`) matches ANY comment on the task, so `latest_implementer_ts` is that role's FIRST spawn permanently, and from cycle 2 onward F1 reads "previous cycle" and auto-approves mid-implementation. That is the ORIGINAL qzv defect verbatim.

WHAT P2 DID FIX, IN EVERY CYCLE — worth stating precisely, because it is not nothing and it changes what remains:
- **Effect (2), the close, is gone unconditionally.** In the cycle-2 reproduction above the task stayed `status=in_progress`. Both `bd update --status closed` sites are removed (0 executable occurrences; the 5 surviving textual hits are all comments).
- **Effect (4), an approval bound to the wrong change set, is closed** by `--expect-hash` plus the pre-existing change-set binding.

WHAT REMAINS FROM CYCLE 2 ONWARD: effect (1), `qa-approved` on work that does not exist, and effect (3), the tracker/current-task wipe — which my run also triggered, confirming qzv.2 route (a) is strictly downstream of this task. Fix this and qzv.2 narrows to route (c) alone, exactly as qzv.2 is filed.

WHY THIS BLOCKS qzv's CLOSURE RATHER THAN P2's APPROVAL. This is P2's own newly-installed semantics applied to P2: an approval binds a CHANGE SET, closing claims the TASK's work is done. The change set is complete, correct and honestly disclosed, so it is approved. qzv's titular defect — "F1 ... writes qa-approved to the TASK" — is still reachable in this project's normal multi-cycle mode, so the task is not done. P2 removed the auto-close precisely so this distinction could be expressed; this is its first use.

ALSO REQUIRED WHEN THIS LANDS — carry R7-F1 (medium, recorded in the round-7 `qa-claude` review artifact on qzv): all four specialist prompts assert "The mechanism is fixed (`claude-workflow-plugin-qzv`)" — `backend.md:319`, `frontend.md:297`, `devops.md:245`, `qa.md:841`. My reproduction falsifies it. It is deliberately NOT blocking P2, because the sentence becomes TRUE the moment this task lands, and bouncing a change set to edit prose that is about to be re-edited buys nothing. But it must not ship un-corrected if this task slips: the paragraph's whole job is to sustain the reconcile habit that caught the only detected occurrence of this defect out of four, and telling every specialist at spawn that the mechanism is fixed is the one claim that could stop them doing the check while it is still needed. Correct it in the same landing (and give those four sentences their missing terminating period — R7-F6).

THE `qa` ROUTE IS A SEPARATE DECISION, and I am the interested party so I will state it plainly rather than quietly: `is_implementer_role` is `backend|frontend|devops` only, so QA authoring test files during review produces no record and the predicate is structurally blind to it — while QA holds Write/Edit/MultiEdit. Re-keying on (role, task, cycle) does not touch this. Either post a non-implementer record for the qa role, or state in the region header that QA-authored files are out of scope for the predicate. Do not leave it implicit; a reader of the header currently cannot tell that the gate's own agent is exempt from the gate's in-flight check.

Candidate fix as filed still looks right: skip only when an existing record for that role is NEWER than the latest `QA-GATE: entered`. `review-check.sh gate` already returns `cycle_opened_ts`, so it adds no state and no parser. The L2 leg it needs is the five-step sequence above; my reproduction script is a working starting point for it, and `subagent-start.sh`'s existing IMPLEMENTER-IDEMPOTENCY META (no duplicates within one cycle) must stay green.

title: The impact-report freshness check detects DRIFT but cannot detect LOSS — recorded_hash == current_hash passes for a shrunken tracker
description:
Raised by QA in review iteration 5 on 94d, 2026-08-04, from a live vacuous pass.

cmd_approve refuses when the persisted impact report is missing or stale, comparing the recorded change-set hash against a recompute. That comparison is sound for DRIFT (the change set moved after the report was written) and structurally blind to LOSS (the change set shrank before the report was written).

MEASURED LIVE: after session-start.sh:273 destroyed the tracker and reconcile rebuilt a 10-path subset of a 26-path change set, enter generated an impact report over those same 10 files, and approve's freshness enforcement PASSED — because recorded_hash and current_hash both faithfully described the shrunken set. Six of the eight files the implementer's own F7 contract declared were absent from what an approval would have bound. The enforcement did not fail; it succeeded vacuously.

The general rule this instance proves: two numbers derived from the same truncated source cannot detect the truncation. Any completeness check must compare the change set against an INDEPENDENT witness of what the session did — git-visible dirt, the F7 contract's declared file list, the review artifact's files_verified — not against a second read of itself.

Cheapest independent witness already on disk: the F7 completion contract declares files_changed. Cross-checking the bound change set against that list would have caught this instance immediately (6 of 8 missing). P7 is already adding completion-record validation at approve; this check belongs with it rather than as a separate mechanism.

Blocks nothing today but must be resolved before P2 binds approvals to the hash: a binding is only as strong as the completeness of the set it binds.

title: bd_list_comments MCP tool returns ok:true with 0 comments on tasks that have dozens — every agent using the default path is blind to the durable record
description:
REPRODUCED BY THE ORCHESTRATOR, 2026-08-04, on claude-workflow-plugin-94d.

  mcp__bd__bd_list_comments(task_id=claude-workflow-plugin-94d)
    -> {"ok":true,"headline":"bd_list_comments claude-workflow-plugin-94d: 0 comment(s)","data":{"comments":[]}}

  bd show claude-workflow-plugin-94d --json | jq .comment_count  -> 76
  bd show claude-workflow-plugin-94d (plain, COMMENTS section)   -> 81 entries

The failure is not the wrong number. It is ok:true. No error, no degradation flag, no empty-vs-unavailable distinction — a well-formed success response asserting zero comments on a task carrying 76, including every F7 completion contract, every review artifact record, every RUBRIC verdict, and every finding raised across four review rounds.

ROOT CAUSE, from the tool own description: 'Replaces shell: bd show <id> --json | jq .comments'. bd 1.1.2 STOPPED INLINING .comments in --json output. That is the exact breaking change the predecessor task (claude-workflow-plugin-vfh / fkm.1.1) was opened to absorb — its title is literally 'bd show --json no longer inlines .comments'. Four contracts were migrated across scripts, specs, prompts and installers; the MCP tool was not. bd show --json still reports comment_count correctly, so the count is available even though the bodies are not.

WHY THIS IS P1. The Beads comment stream IS this project institutional memory: F7 contracts, coupling assessments, review artifacts, grader verdicts, J21 decisions, orchestrator findings records. An agent that calls the MCP tool — the DEFAULT path, and the one agent prompts steer toward — receives ok:true and an empty array, and proceeds with no history at all. It cannot tell 'this task has no comments' from 'I cannot read this task comments'.

HOW IT WAS FOUND, and the near-miss that matters: a devops specialist noticed the discrepancy while starting the R4-F1 round and said so — 'I would have started this round without your round-6 plan had I trusted the MCP tool.' It read the CLI because the orchestrator brief happened to say 'plain bd show, not --json'. Nothing mechanical caught it. Every agent brief in this session has carried that instruction as folklore rather than as a fix.

FIX: reimplement over a bd 1.1.2 read path that actually returns bodies (bd comment list / the CLI plain output / whatever 1.1.2 exposes), and — non-negotiable — make 'cannot read comments' an ERROR, never ok:true with an empty array. An empty array must mean the task genuinely has none. Add an integration assertion that a task with a known comment count returns that count through the MCP surface, so the two paths cannot silently diverge again.

FAMILY: this is the same defect as fkm.1.11 (Stop gate reports 'technical checks passed' while running only L1), fkm.1.14 (codex-review.sh deletes its own error_key on a paid failure), fkm.1.17 (impact-report nested JSON returns plausible values for wrong paths), and dpe (reconcile subtracts silently). All are 'the measurement that did not happen looks exactly like the measurement that passed.' This is the most consequential of the five, because it blinds agents to the record every other guarantee is written into. Nine instances of the family are now recorded this session; six of them are read paths that return a confident wrong answer.

Recommend fixing this and fkm.1.11/.14/.17 as ONE design pass with a single rule — no read or check may report success it did not establish — rather than four separate patches.
notes:
COMPLETED: an empty comment list now means empty, and an unreadable one is an error.

THE CORRECTION TO THE FILING'S ROOT CAUSE, measured rather than inferred.
The TRANSPORT was already fixed. fdfd6ce (fkm.1.1, 2026-08-03) added
--include-comments to runBdShowJson and wired includeComments:true into all four
readers, one day BEFORE the 2026-08-04 reproduction. Driving the on-disk
bd_list_comments handler against the real ledger returns 88 comments on
claude-workflow-plugin-94d today. The reproduction was almost certainly against
an MCP server process started before that commit (stdio servers do not reload).

THAT DOES NOT MAKE THE FINDING WRONG — IT MAKES IT SHARPER, and it is exactly the
sentence the filing leads with: "the failure is not the wrong number, it is
ok:true". A transport fix with nothing checking it is why a stale server could
answer zero and nothing caught it. So the fix is the CHECK, not the flag.

WHAT SHIPPED. resolveComments() in exec-bd.js cross-checks the returned bodies
against bd's own comment_count — a witness that is present even on the plain show
that carries no bodies — and returns one of three states:
  verified     count agrees with the bodies (INCLUDING the genuine-zero case)
  unverified   bodies present, no count to check them against (older bd)
  unavailable  count > 0 and the bodies are missing or truncated; or nothing
Applied at all four readers, because four spellings of `task.comments || []` is
four chances to regress:
  bd_list_comments  REFUSES on unavailable (returning bodies IS its contract)
  bd_doc_read       REFUSES for list_only and named docs; a `main` read comes
                    from .notes and stays available, so a specialist can still
                    load the SPEC under a degraded transport
  bd_doc_write      REFUSES for named docs — a blind read computes nextVersion=1
                    over an existing chain and FORKS it, which is worse than
                    blindness
  bd_show_task      degrades by SAYING "comments: UNAVAILABLE (comment_count=N)"
                    rather than printing a 0 it did not establish; it does not
                    fail, because comments are one field of its payload rather
                    than its whole contract

MEASURED ACROSS THE WHOLE LEDGER (342 issues, bd 1.1.2, hydrated), and the third
row is why the obvious implementation would have been wrong:
  comment_count present            342/342
  comment_count == comments.length 342/342
  `comments` KEY ABSENT            117/342 — exactly the 117 with count 0
bd omits the comments key entirely on a zero-comment task EVEN WHEN HYDRATING, so
"key absent => unavailable" would have failed 34% of this ledger. The count is
the witness; key presence is not.

TESTS: .claude/scripts/tests/mcp-unestablished-results.test.sh. Section 1 is the
full discriminator table as a pure-function test (runs in CI, which has no bd),
including the assertion the finding actually demands: a genuine empty and an
unavailable source produce DIFFERENT answers. Section 3 drives a real bd through
a PATH shim that strips --include-comments, reproducing the pre-migration
transport: the shipped tools refuse, and a mutant that restores
`task.comments || []` returns ok:true with 0 comments on a task carrying three —
the historical bug, reproduced on demand.
close_reason: Fixed with rmz under change set 4cd9cca9. ROOT CAUSE IN THE FILING WAS WRONG and is corrected on the task: fdfd6ce (2026-08-03) had already migrated the comments transport, one day BEFORE this was filed on 08-04; the on-disk handler returns 88 comments on the task the filing reproduces 0 on. The ok:true/0 came from a running MCP server serving pre-fdfd6ce code (server PID 5843 started 08-07, confirmed by QA). Filed as b1an. THE FIX IS THE CHECK, NOT THE FLAG — which is the filing's own lead sentence: the failure is ok:true, not the number. A transport fix with nothing checking it is precisely how a stale server answers zero and nothing catches it. Shipped: three states (verified / unverified / unavailable), stronger than the two demanded, with comment_count as the witness rather than key presence. Measured across the whole ledger: comment_count present 342/342, equals comments.length 342/342, key-absence implies count-0 with zero exceptions — so a key-presence test would have false-errored on roughly a third of the ledger. Residual filed as the bd comments --json decider task.

ROOT CAUSE IN THIS FILING IS WRONG - corrected 2026-08-08 by the specialist, verified independently by the orchestrator.

THE FILING SAYS: bd 1.1.2 stopped inlining .comments, four contracts were migrated, and the MCP tool was not. That is a clean story and it is false.

WHAT ACTUALLY PRODUCED THE ok:true/0 RESPONSE: a running MCP server process started before fdfd6ce, serving stale code. Unprovable now - the process is gone - and the specialist said so rather than asserting it. Filed as its own task because the hazard is general.

WHY THE FIX IS STILL RIGHT, AND WHY IT IS BETTER FOR THIS: the filing's own lead sentence was always the real finding - THE FAILURE IS NOT THE WRONG NUMBER, IT IS ok:true. A transport fix with nothing checking it is precisely how a stale server could answer zero and nothing caught it. So the deliverable is the CHECK, not the flag. The shipped fix distinguishes three states (verified / unverified / unavailable) rather than the two this task demanded, and uses comment_count as the witness rather than key presence - measured across all 342 issues in the ledger, the comments key is absent on exactly the 117 that genuinely have zero, so a key-presence test would have false-errored on a third of the ledger.

title: reconcile_tracker's baseline subtraction goes stale on commit: a path dirty at baseline capture, then COMMITTED, then re-modified in the same cycle escapes the change set silently
description:
Found while VERIFYING that a `lessons.sh add` append would be hash-neutral before making it (round on `dmi`, change set `01296db9…`). The append turned out to be hash-neutral — and the reason it is hash-neutral is the defect.

## The shape

`reconcile_tracker` subtracts the gate baseline with `comm -23` over RAW PORCELAIN LINES (`qa-gate.sh:541-551`), and the baseline is a snapshot of `git status --porcelain` text taken when the gate baseline was last written. A porcelain line is not content-addressed, so the subtraction cannot distinguish:

- "this path is dirty for the same reason it was dirty at baseline capture" (correctly excluded as pre-existing dirt), from
- "this path was dirty at capture, has since been COMMITTED, and is now dirty again for a NEW reason" (incorrectly excluded).

The second case is under-coverage — the direction 94d exists to close. The edit is git-visible, appears in `git diff`, and is absent from `changed-files.txt`, from `canonical_changed_files`, and therefore from `change_set_hash`. No log line, no warning: `reconcile_tracker` reports `added=0` and `ok:true`. A reviewer diffing the tracker's paths cannot see it, which is the same "unreviewable BY CONSTRUCTION" property `post-edit.sh`'s containment region names for out-of-project paths.

## Measured, on the live tree, one variable

```
gate-baseline: head=bb8fce7e83467929b77cee19048cb97f089844f2
               captured_at=2026-08-03T04:38:22Z
               body contains: " M LESSONS.md"
current HEAD:  454c441a7811c256971fd60d47ae29286cdf0458
git log bb8fce7..HEAD -- LESSONS.md
               -> fdfd6ce  fix(bd): migrate to bd 1.1.2 and remove the ledger auto-repair
```

So the baselined dirt was committed by `fdfd6ce`. Then `lessons.sh add` re-dirtied the path:

```
git status --porcelain -- LESSONS.md      ->  " M LESSONS.md"   (byte-identical to the baseline line)
git diff --numstat -- LESSONS.md          ->  1  0  LESSONS.md
grep -c LESSONS changed-files.txt         ->  0
qa-gate.sh reconcile-tracker              ->  ok:true, "already covers every reviewable git-visible path", added=0
impact-report.sh --hash-only              ->  01296db9…  (UNMOVED, 26 paths)
```

Alternatives ruled out — `workflow_denylisted` says keep and `workflow_self_written` says reviewable for the absolute spelling, so no lib rule claims it.

The isolating experiment, same `comm -23`, one line changed:

```
survivors WITH  the stale baseline entry -> LESSONS.md absent  (0)
survivors WITHOUT it                     -> LESSONS.md present (1)
```

The stale baseline line is the sole cause.

## Why it is reachable rather than theoretical

It needs a commit to land BETWEEN the baseline capture and the end of the cycle, for a path that was dirty at capture. This cycle has seven J21 CONTINUEs, spans two days, and has commits landing mid-cycle (`fdfd6ce`, `bb8fce7`, `454c441`). That is the normal shape of a long gate cycle, not an exotic one. The longer a cycle runs, the more baselined paths get committed, and every one of them becomes a hole for the rest of the cycle.

## Not fixed here, and why

Hash-bound. Any fix changes what `reconcile_tracker` appends, which moves `change_set_hash` off `01296db9…` — the hash the graded packet, the r3 review artifact and the rubric verdict are all bound to. It must land after 94d's approval, as its own single hash-migration landing (the `docs/HOOKS.md` "Denylist changes are a hash migration" rule applies verbatim: growing or shrinking the tracker's input IS the migration).

## Candidate fixes, in preference order

1. **Invalidate the baseline against its own recorded head.** The baseline already stores `head=<sha>`. On reconcile, for each baseline entry, check whether the path changed between the recorded head and the current HEAD (`git diff --name-only <head>..HEAD -- <path>`); if it did, the entry is stale and must NOT subtract. Cheap (one call over the survivor set, which is small), uses a field the baseline already carries, and fails in the safe direction (a false "stale" verdict over-tracks).
2. **Content-address the baseline** (path + blob sha at capture). Strictly better discrimination, but it changes the baseline file format, which is a second migration on top of the first.
3. **Refuse and re-baseline when `head` has moved.** Simplest and loudest, but forces a re-baseline on every mid-cycle commit, which is friction on exactly the long cycles that need the gate most.

Whichever lands, add an L2 assertion that drives the three-step sequence — dirty at baseline, commit, re-modify — and asserts the path IS reconciled in. That sequence has no coverage today; `specs/gate-baseline-v2.sh` and `specs/qa-gate-baseline.sh` both exercise baseline subtraction with a STATIC head.

## Disclosure for the current cycle

The one-line `LESSONS.md` append made by the `dmi` round is itself uncertified by this hole: it is in `git diff` and not in the change set. That is disclosed rather than hidden, and reverting it is a one-command undo (`git checkout -- LESSONS.md`) if the reviewer prefers the diff to match the graded measurement exactly. Reverting does not close the hole, and it does not restore certification either — it only removes the demonstration.

## QA scope correction — this is wider than the description states, in two ways, and the second one invalidates candidate fix 1

Verified independently during QA round 6 on 94d. The mechanism as described is
correct and I reproduced it. Two corrections to the scope.

### 1. The staleness is total, not partial — 154 of 154

The description says the shape "needs a commit to land BETWEEN the baseline
capture and the end of the cycle, for a path that was dirty at capture" and calls
that "the normal shape of a long gate cycle, not an exotic one". True, but
unquantified. Measured:

```
gate-baseline body entries                        154
  (file is 159 lines; 5 are header, before the `--`)
recorded head                                     bb8fce7
paths committed in bb8fce7..HEAD                  154
baseline entries whose path was committed         154   (100%)
baseline entries still un-stale                     0
```

The whole baseline is stale. Every path it holds was committed by `fdfd6ce` or
`454c441`. This is the audit the `dmi` contract left as its secondary residual
("I did not audit the other 158 baseline entries against `bb8fce7..HEAD`"); it
costs one `git diff --name-only`.

### 2. NO COMMIT IS REQUIRED — the unnamed third case

The mechanism paragraph contrasts two cases: "dirty for the same reason it was
dirty at capture" (correctly excluded) versus "was dirty at capture, has since
been COMMITTED, and is now dirty again" (incorrectly excluded). There is a third:

**dirty at capture, NOT committed, and modified AGAIN during the cycle.**

The porcelain line is unchanged, so it is subtracted, and the new work is
invisible — with no commit anywhere in the story. Reproduced in an isolated repo,
one variable:

```
git init; commit v1
append v2            (pre-existing dirt)
baseline snapshot -> " M tracked.txt"
append v3            (a Bash write during the cycle)
current  snapshot -> " M tracked.txt"      byte-identical
comm -23 survivors -> 0
git diff --numstat -> 2  0  tracked.txt    the work is real and uncovered
```

So the blind spot is **every path with a baseline entry**, not just the committed
subset. On this tree those are the same 154 paths, but the reachability argument
is much weaker than the description implies: it needs no commit, only that the
path was already dirty when the baseline was taken — which is true of every file
under active work in a cycle that has been reconciled once.

### Consequence: candidate fix 1 is insufficient

Candidate 1 (the stated preference) is "invalidate the baseline against its own
recorded head" — for each entry, check whether the path changed between the
recorded head and current HEAD. **That cannot see case 3 at all**, because
nothing was committed. Landing dpe per its own preference order would close the
committed variant, leave the no-commit variant open, and look closed.

Only candidate 2 (content-address the baseline: path + blob sha at capture)
closes both. That is a baseline format change, so it is the more expensive
option — but it is the one that matches the defect. Candidate 3 (refuse and
re-baseline when `head` has moved) also fails on case 3.

Suggested reordering: 2 as the fix, 1 as a strict subset not worth landing alone.

### The L2 assertion needs a second leg

The description asks for an assertion driving the three-step sequence (dirty at
baseline, commit, re-modify). Add a second leg for the two-step sequence (dirty
at baseline, re-modify, no commit), or the no-commit variant stays uncovered by
the regression test as well as by the fix.

### Where this bites in shipped docs — filed against 94d as R4-F1 (HIGH)

`docs/HOOKS.md`'s `prevent-orchestrator-edits.sh` row asserts that the Bash write
vector "is not invisible — `qa-gate.sh reconcile-tracker` puts a Bash-written
file into the change set from `git status`, so the edit still reaches QA". This
defect makes that false for all 154 baselined paths, and the reverted
`lessons.sh` append is a live demonstration inside the cycle that shipped the
sentence. That disclosure gap is hash-neutral and is blocking 94d's approval;
this task stays hash-bound and deferred as designed.

### Not disqualifying for 94d's change set

Recorded so the two are not conflated. Live under-coverage on 94d's change set is
**zero** — all 60 dirty paths are self-written, denylisted, or already tracked, so
nothing survives the reconciler's filters only to be wrongly subtracted
(confirmed by re-implementing the filter order and by the live reconciler:
`added=0`, `denylisted=21`, hash unmoved). 94d strictly improves on the pre-94d
state, where there was no reconciler at all.

title: codex-review.sh discards the failure diagnosis on a PAID failure — error_key is computed then deleted by the cleanup trap
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-04, review iteration 2 on claude-workflow-plugin-94d. THIS FAILURE COST REAL MONEY, unlike the ARG_MAX one.

WHAT HAPPENED. With fkm.1.12 fixed, the 1610381-byte request WAS delivered to Sol (gpt-5.6-sol) — the ARG_MAX defect is genuinely closed and the frame reached the model. Sol answered, its output failed review-check.sh validate-artifact, the driver spent its one permitted corrective turn (malformed_retry=1), that also failed validation, and it exited 5 with:

    [codex-review] Sol did not produce a valid artifact after 1 corrective turn(s); no artifact

TWO PAID TURNS, NO ARTIFACT, AND NO DIAGNOSIS.

THE DEFECT. validate_candidate() DOES capture the reason:
    :286  printf '%s' "$text" > "$WORK/candidate.json"
    :288  out=$(... review-check.sh validate-artifact "$WORK/candidate.json")
    :293  printf '%s' "$out" | jq -r '.error_key // "invalid_json"' > "$WORK/error_key"
and :366 reads it back to build the corrective prompt. But WORK=$(mktemp -d) at :212 with 'trap cleanup EXIT' at :223, so on the failure path $WORK — candidate.json AND error_key — is deleted before the operator can read either. The final stderr line names neither the error_key nor the model's actual output.

CONSEQUENCE. A paid review that fails validation is UNDIAGNOSABLE after the fact. You cannot tell whether Sol emitted prose around the JSON, missed a required key, hit a length limit, or ignored the schema entirely — so you cannot fix the prompt, and the only available action is to pay again and hope. That is the worst possible property for the one code path in this repo that spends the operator's money.

SAME SHAPE AS ITS TWO SIBLINGS. fkm.1.12 (empty frame written, guard could not fire, silent full-timeout wait) and fkm.1.13 (leaked servers) are both 'the failure leaves no usable trace'. This is the third instance in one script: the evidence exists, is computed correctly, and is then thrown away.

FIX DIRECTION (cheap, no spend to test):
  1. Echo the error_key in the exit-5 log line — it is already in a variable at :366.
  2. Preserve the candidate on failure: copy $WORK/candidate.json and $WORK/error_key to .claude/.qa-tracking/review-failure-<task-id>-r<n>.{json,key} before cleanup, or honour a CODEX_REVIEW_KEEP_WORK env seam. Prefer the .qa-tracking copy — it is denylist-covered (workflow_self_written), so it will not enter a change set.
  3. Consider raising malformed_retry above 1 ONLY after (1) and (2) land; retrying blind is what makes this expensive.

TESTABLE WITHOUT SPEND: point the driver at the existing stub server, have the stub emit deliberately invalid artifact text, and assert the exit-5 path names the error_key and leaves the preserved candidate on disk. The stub already exists (tests/component/.../stub-codex-mcp.js) and the whole path is upstream of any billing.

STRONG SUSPECT for the underlying validation failure, flagged by QA before the spend and now the leading hypothesis: the request is 77.4% impact-report JSON (1245795 of 1610381 bytes) and only 10.1% actual diff, with 779 node references pointing at fixture duplicates verified byte-identical. A reviewer handed 1.25MB of machine JSON may well lose the strict-output-format instruction. That makes QA's suggested trim (qa.md 6p.1 / impact-report verbosity) a correctness measure, not merely a cost measure. UNPROVEN — and unprovable until (1) and (2) land, which is exactly the point.

BLOCKS: the plan's D7 LIVE-2 cost-gated Codex arc. It would fail here identically, after paying, with no way to learn why.
