comments.text: SCOPE ADDITION (QA round 2 on claude-workflow-plugin-rqer, 2026-08-15): a SECOND mechanism in the same diagnostics-loss family, distinct from the trap-deletes-evidence-files arm this task already names. codex-review.sh's teardown step ('We have our answer; tear the server down now', line ~475 at 9488c69+rqer) runs `exec 3>&- 2>/dev/null || true` — a command-less exec applies ALL its redirections to the shell PERMANENTLY, so the 2>/dev/null leg reassigns the script's OWN fd 2 to /dev/null for the rest of execution. Every fail_no_artifact message emitted after that line — the rqer round-2 DIR-SHAPE-GUARD and POST-MOVE-GUARD refusals, the mkdir/assemble/move failures, and the cap-truncation log — is unobservable to ANY external caller regardless of how stderr is redirected from outside. Exit codes and side effects are correct (verified); only the diagnostic text is lost. EVIDENCE (measured, QA round-2 probe, isolated fixture + stub server): shipped driver with a directory pre-placed at the derived path exits 5 with EMPTY stderr; an otherwise-identical copy with only that line's 2>/dev/null removed (exec 3>&- || true) exits 5 AND emits the full '[codex-review] the derived artifact path ... already exists as a directory ...' refusal. The one-token fix must ALSO review cleanup()'s identical line (~259) and should land together with this task's trap-evidence fix — un-muting stderr alone still leaves the trap-deleted candidate.json/error_key gap. Cross-refs: component/specs/codex-review.sh C10's 'NOT asserted here: RD_ERR's content' comment; rqer fix-round completion record decisions (R1-F1 residual).

title: codex-review.sh cannot marshal a review request larger than ARG_MAX — paid Sol lane silently unusable on large change sets
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-04 attempting the first paid Sol relay of the v5 arc, on task claude-workflow-plugin-94d (P1).

ROOT CAUSE, quantified. codex-review.sh:296-297 builds the JSON-RPC tools/call frame by passing the ENTIRE review request through argv:

    CALL=$(jq -nc --arg p "$ENVELOPE" --arg cwd "$PROJECT_DIR" \
        '{jsonrpc:"2.0",id:2,method:"tools/call",params:{name:"codex",arguments:{prompt:$p,...}}}')

getconf ARG_MAX on this host = 1048576. QA assembled request = 1568552 bytes (1.5x the limit). jq therefore dies with 'Argument list too long' and $CALL is EMPTY.

WHY THE FAILURE MODE IS WORSE THAN THE BUG. The next line is:
    send_frame "$CALL" || fail_no_artifact "could not write codex tool call (server gone)"
send_frame SUCCEEDS writing an empty frame, so the guard does not fire. Control reaches wait_id 2, which then waits for a reply to a request that was NEVER SENT until the full timeout_seconds budget expires, and only then reports exit 5 / no artifact. With timeout raised to 2700s for the size, that is 45 minutes of dead wait presenting as a legitimate paid review in progress. The Codex mcp-server is spawned and idle on stdin the whole time.

COST: zero on this occasion — no prompt was ever delivered, so no tokens were billed. That is luck, not design: an operator who did not inspect the process tree would have read 'RUNNING' and waited 45 minutes for exit 5, then degraded to the Claude lane per the driver contract, never learning the lane has a size ceiling.

FIX DIRECTION: pass the envelope by FILE, not argv — jq --rawfile p "$REQ_FILE" (or --slurpfile) instead of --arg p "$ENVELOPE". Then add a hard precondition: if the envelope exceeds ARG_MAX (or simply always), refuse to reach send_frame with an empty CALL. A guard asserting CALL is non-empty and valid JSON before send_frame converts a 45-minute silent hang into an immediate named error.

TEST: an L2 leg driving codex-review.sh with a >ARG_MAX request and asserting it fails FAST with a named error rather than hanging to timeout. That leg needs no Codex server and no spend — the failure is upstream of the transport.

CONSEQUENCE FOR v5: the paid Sol lane is currently unusable for any change set whose assembled request exceeds ~1MB, which includes P1 itself and will include most of D1-D6. The plan's LIVE-2 cost-gated Codex arc at D7 depends on this working. Until fixed, either the request must be kept under 1MB or the lane degrades to Claude — and the degradation is currently silent and slow rather than loud and immediate.
notes:
COMPLETED (P1 / fkm.1.12) — ARG_MAX marshalling fix + frame guard + L2 legs. Ready for QA.
The F7 completion contract is the comment on this task and is authoritative. Summary only, below.

WHAT SHIPPED (2 authored files + 7 mechanical fixture copies)

• codex-review.sh: the tools/call envelope now reaches jq BY FILE
  (--rawfile p "$WORK/envelope.txt") instead of through argv. $ENVELOPE is
  CONSTRUCTED by the driver (section 5 heredoc + $REQUEST_RAW), not the request
  verbatim, so it is staged to $WORK — which already exists before the frame
  build and is rm -rf'd by the pre-existing EXIT trap. The stage write is checked
  so a partial write cannot ship a truncated review prompt.
• codex-review.sh: FRAME-GUARD BEGIN/END (fkm.1.12) sentinel block immediately
  before send_frame. Asserts jq's rc == 0 AND $CALL non-empty AND $CALL parses as
  JSON; on failure, fail_no_artifact with a named, actionable error carrying the
  envelope byte count, jq's rc, and "nothing was sent" (the first fact an
  operator needs on a PAID lane). Exit 5, reasoned in-file: the request is
  schema-valid so not 4, the invocation is well-formed so not 1, the iteration is
  in-cap so not 6, and the exit-5 caller move in orchestrator.md 5c Step D
  (degrade to the Claude lane, do not retry the paid call) is exactly correct for
  a deterministic marshalling failure.
• NO up-front size precondition, deliberately — that would reinstate the ~1MB
  ceiling the fix removes. Recorded as a DO-NOT in the driver comment.
• specs/codex-review.sh: C6 (oversize envelope is marshalled AND delivered,
  self-calibrating so it cannot go vacuous on a roomier host), C7 (unbuildable
  frame fails fast with the named error and sends NOTHING), and META (fkm.1.12)
  which awk-excises the sentinel block and proves every C7 assertion inverts —
  the production hang, reproducible on demand, in 3.3s instead of 45 minutes.
  26 new assertions; 25 -> 51 total; 8s -> 14s.
• make sync-fixtures run after the last canonical edit: 7 dirs synced, zero
  drift, all 7 copies byte-identical to canonical.

MEASURED, BEFORE AND AFTER (offline stub, zero spend)
  UNFIXED: exit 5 after the FULL timeout budget; stderr misreports a wall-clock
           timeout; stub log shows only initialize — no tools/call ever arrived.
  FIXED:   exit 0 in 1116ms, 1,101,445-char prompt delivered intact.
  GUARD:   631ms named failure WITH the guard vs 6352ms full-budget hang WITHOUT.

NOT DONE, ON PURPOSE
• fkm.1.13 (leaked codex mcp-server) untouched — and measured separable: after a
  guard-triggered exit there are 0 stub processes and no $WORK dir left, because
  the guard routes through the existing EXIT trap. No reap added.
• qa-gate.sh / verify-before-stop.sh / review-check.sh untouched; the
  reviewer-lane-degradation structural assertion re-verified green (8/8).
• installer-v3-upgrade 8e leg B untouched.

FOR QA
• This fix lands INSIDE the 94d change set under review, so it grows that change
  set and moves its hash. Operator-accepted.
• The 7 fixture copies are NOT in changed-files.txt (written by sync-fixtures,
  not Write/Edit, so post-edit.sh never fired). git status surfaces all 9 —
  94d's own reconcile_tracker should pick them up, which makes this a live
  exercise of the reconciler 94d just shipped. Flagged, not hand-edited.
• Pre-existing weakness flagged NOT fixed (scope): the C3 META is tautological
  (it SETS stopped_by then asserts it is not the other value) and reads a path
  C4 deletes and C5 overwrites. Belongs to 1vq.1, worth its own task.
• I ran only bash -n, make lint, the targeted codex-review spec, the
  lane-degradation spec, and one L1 file. make test-component / test-e2e-unit /
  test are the operator's measurement, per the explicit division of labour.
close_reason: Fixed and CONFIRMED IN PRODUCTION. The envelope is now staged to $WORK/envelope.txt and read with jq --rawfile instead of passed through argv, plus a FRAME-GUARD block asserting $CALL is non-empty and re-parses as JSON before send_frame. Measured: broken build 6352ms with a misreported timeout vs guarded build 631ms with a named marshalling error — the exit code is identical either way, which is why the defect survived, and latency plus stderr are now assertions. QA independently verified against the REAL 1610442-byte round-2 envelope: old --arg form rc=126 with an empty frame; shipped --rawfile form rc=0 with an 1855156-byte frame and a lossless 1609732-codepoint round-trip. Confirmed end-to-end by the second paid relay attempt, which DELIVERED the 1.6MB request to gpt-5.6-sol — something the pre-fix driver could not do at all. Unadvertised bonus found by QA: --arg previously exposed the entire change-set diff in the process argument list (ps auxww); the fix removes that. Ships with C6/C7 + META in specs/codex-review.sh, where C6 self-calibrates off getconf ARG_MAX so it cannot go vacuous on a roomier host. NOTE: that relay still produced no artifact — Sol's output failed schema validation twice — but for an unrelated reason tracked as fkm.1.14, which is now the remaining blocker on ever getting a paid Sol artifact for this arc.

The request is schema-valid (a 1,100,214-byte request passes review-check.sh validate-request — measured; review-check.sh has no size cap and reads via printf|jq, never argv), so 4 is wrong; the invocation is well-formed, so 1 is wrong; the iteration is in-cap, so 6 is wrong; no artifact is written and the correct caller move is orchestrator.md 5c Step D's exit-5 branch (degrade to the Claude lane, do not retry the paid call) — which is exactly right here, since a retry would fail identically and deterministically.",

Linux is the real motivation — it caps a SINGLE argument at MAX_ARG_STRLEN (~128KB), far below its larger ARG_MAX, so sizing off getconf ARG_MAX clears the effective limit on both platforms.",

### llm_observations

**The fix lands inside the change set currently under review for 94d.** It grows that change set and moves its hash. Operator-accepted and expected; recording it here so QA does not read the hash movement as tampering. Nine files: 2 authored + 7 mechanical fixture copies.

**The 7 fixture copies are NOT in `changed-files.txt`.** They were written by `make sync-fixtures` (a Bash command), not by Write/Edit, so `post-edit.sh` never fired on them. The tracker holds only the 2 canonical paths (lines 83-95, duplicated once per Edit call). `git status` surfaces all 9, so 94d's own `reconcile_tracker` should pick the 7 up at gate time — which incidentally makes this a live end-to-end exercise of the reconciler 94d just shipped. Flagging rather than hand-editing the tracker.

**No scratch leaked into the change set.** Every probe went to the session scratchpad via Bash heredocs, so `post-edit.sh` never recorded a `/tmp`, `/private/tmp` or `/var/folders` path. Verified: `grep -nE '^/private/tmp|^/tmp|/var/folders' changed-files.txt` → no matches.

**The leaked-server issue (fkm.1.13) is genuinely separable — measured, not assumed.** The brief asked me to justify a trap-based reap if I considered it inseparable from part 2. It is not: the guard's exit path runs `fail_no_artifact` → `exit 5` → the pre-existing `trap cleanup EXIT`, which kills + waits the server and `rm -rf`s `$WORK`. Measured after a guard-triggered exit: **0** `stub-codex-mcp.js` processes remaining and **no** `codex-review.XXXXXX.*` work dir left on disk. So the guard adds no new leak and needs nothing from fkm.1.13. Nothing added.

**Pre-existing weakness I did NOT fix, flagged for the record.** The C3 `META (plan-mandated)` is tautological independent of my change. It does `jq '.stopped_by="verdict"' "$CAPHIT_ARTIFACT"` and then asserts the field is not `cap:max_findings` — it SETS the field and then asserts it is not the other value, so it can only fail if jq's assignment itself breaks. It never re-runs C3's assertion against the mutated artifact. Compounding it, `$CAPHIT_ARTIFACT` is a path that C4 deletes and C5 overwrites, so by the time the META runs it is reading C5's approve artifact, not C3's cap-hit artifact. That belongs to the 1vq.1 change set, not fkm.1.12, and silently strengthening someone else's plan-mandated META inside a change set under review would be scope creep. Worth its own task.

**Residual portability doubts, named.** (a) The C7 mutation `sed` is keyed to the literal `--rawfile p "$ENVELOPE_FILE"`; a rename silently no-ops the sed — but the "mutation applied" assertion then FAILS loudly, which I verified is the failure direction. Same for the awk excision keyed to `^# FRAME-GUARD BEGIN \(`. Both fail loud, never silent. (b) `getconf ARG_MAX` above 8MB makes C6 print an explicit skip rather than generate a huge payload; I verified the skip branch prints and that no C6-only variable is referenced past its closing `fi` (line 294), so the skip path is `set -u` safe. (c) The 1.5MB blocking `printf` into the FIFO does not deadlock — the server drains stdin and writes its reply to a FILE, not back through a pipe — confirmed by C6 running green end-to-end with a 1,082,789-char prompt delivered.

**One thing I could not test and am shipping on:** whether the REAL codex-cli 0.145.0 server accepts a >1MB prompt (a model-context or server-side line-length limit would be a separate ceiling, above the transport). That needs paid spend and is out of scope. The stub enforces the real verified inputSchema, so the frame SHAPE is proven; only the real server's size tolerance is unknown. If it refuses, the failure is now a fast named one rather than a 45-minute phantom, which is the point.

**Cost of the new legs: +5-6s** on the codex-review spec (8s → 14s; 25 → 51 assertions). ~3.3s of that is the META deliberately paying for the hang it proves, on a 3s budget rather than the production 2700s.

title: Stop gate reports 'technical checks passed' while running only L1 — L2/L3/manifest are invisible to it
description:
Observed live 2026-08-03 during P1 (94d). The Stop hook auto-detects a runner (verify-before-stop.sh:1173-1178) and on this repo resolves runner=make, which executes Makefile:40 'test:' -> run-tests.sh, i.e. **L1 ONLY**. Makefile:176 'test-ci' is the target that chains test + test-component + test-e2e-unit + manifest-validate.

The block reason at verify-before-stop.sh:2077 then reads: 'QA approval required (iteration N, runner=make, technical checks passed).'

MEASURED CONSEQUENCE: with four L2 specs failing (qa-gate-baseline 19/4, verify-before-stop 77/1, verify-review-discipline 18/6, worktree-approval-resolution unknown — 28 assertion failures total) INCLUDING a probable regression of the F1 doc-only release path, the Stop gate emitted 'technical checks passed' on every attempt. L2, L3 and manifest-validate are structurally invisible to the gate.

THE DEFECT IS THE CLAIM, NOT THE SCOPE. Running a 10+ minute L2 on every Stop is untenable and should not be the fix. 'technical checks passed' overclaims what was executed; it means 'the detected runner default test target passed'. Two candidate fixes, not exclusive:
  (a) honest phrasing that names the tier actually run, e.g. 'L1 passed (runner=make; L2/L3/manifest NOT run this loop)';
  (b) a cheap staleness signal — e.g. record the last full test-ci result and its tree hash, and say so when the current tree has moved past it.

This is the v4.1 closure finding in a new place: a gate that reports confidently on unverified evidence is worse than no gate, because it is trusted. The orchestrator read 'technical checks passed' repeatedly during this session and treated it as broader coverage than it was.

Related: the escalation branch at :2073 additionally suppresses the suite entirely ('Test suite NOT re-run this loop per the escalation contract'), so a SPURIOUS 2ty escalation both mislabels state and disables checking. See the 2ty task for the three live escalations recorded today.

MEASURED GROUND TRUTH (orchestrator, 2026-08-03) — replaces inference with the actual detect-stack.sh output on this repo:

  runner   = make
  test_cmd = cd "<repo>" && make test      -> Makefile:40 -> run-tests.sh  == L1 ONLY
  lint_cmd = cd "<repo>" && make lint      -> shellcheck
  type_cmd = (empty)                        -> nothing runs
  manifest = Makefile   overrides: test=false lint=false type=false

So the gate executes L1 + lint. It does NOT execute test-component (L2), test-e2e-unit (L3), or manifest-validate. Makefile:176 test-ci is the only target that chains all four.

Precision for the fix: honest phrasing should name BOTH tiers actually run, e.g. 'L1 + lint passed (runner=make; L2/L3/manifest NOT run)'. An earlier draft of this finding risked implying no checks run at all — they do, and the overclaim is one of SCOPE, not of existence.

Two adjacent facts worth keeping, both measured while establishing the above:
  1. type_cmd is empty on this repo, so the gate's type-check stage is a no-op here. Whether that is correct (no TS at the L1 boundary) or a gap (the e2e tier IS TypeScript and _lib.unit.spec.ts:136 carries a known tsc error) was not investigated.
  2. macOS ships no 'timeout' binary — verify-before-stop.sh:450-455 already handles this correctly by falling back timeout -> gtimeout -> bare 'bash -c'. Noted because two of my own probes silently returned rc=127 before I noticed, which is the same class of error this finding is about: a command that did not run looking identical to one that passed.

FIXED with BOTH (a) and (b). Justification for taking both, since the filing left the choice open.

(a) ALONE IS INSUFFICIENT, AND (b) ALONE IS DISHONEST. Honest phrasing tells the reader what the gate did not run; it does nothing about the fact that nobody knows whether the wider tier is green — which is the tax the operator has been paying by hand every round. A staleness signal without honest phrasing leaves the overclaiming sentence in place next to it. They close different halves of one defect, so both shipped.

(a) THE CLAIM. `checks_scope_claim()` / `checks_scope_note()` in a `CHECK-SCOPE` sentinel region. The flat literal `technical checks passed` is gone from every branch. The header now reads `QA approval required (iteration N, runner=make; tests + lint passed — and nothing else ran).` and the note names the LITERAL commands executed, marks every skipped stage with WHY it was skipped, and states that a wider tier the project defines is not run here and not covered. Both block-reason paths call it — the QA-required path and the FAILED_CHECKS path, which had its own smaller overclaim: "the FULL test suite + FULL type-check" standing next to a bare `Detected runner:` line, on a repo where `type_cmd` resolves EMPTY. That sentence now says what it means (a statement about scoping, not coverage) and is followed by the same note.

(b) THE LEDGER. `.claude/.qa-tracking/verification-ledger` — one line per record: timestamp, command, exit code, tree fingerprint, HEAD. `make test-ci` writes its own result, so no agent types the exit code; the Stop readout reports it with explicit provenance ("this gate did not run it and does not vouch for it") and says whether the tree has moved since. `make test-ci` also stopped failing fast: it was a prerequisite chain, so a RED run aborted before recording and the ledger would have kept showing the last GREEN result — a stale green is this task's defect at one remove. It now runs all four tiers and returns the worst rc, which also matches CI (independent jobs).

THREE THINGS I MEASURED THAT THE FILING DID NOT HAVE, all found by building it:

1. `make -n test-ci` MINTED A FALSE GREEN on the first attempt. make does NOT skip a recipe line containing `$(MAKE)` — it runs it. The sub-makes printed instead of running, rc stayed 0, and the recorder wrote `make test-ci exited 0` over a suite that had not executed. I wrote that record into this repo's ledger and deleted it. Guarded now on MAKEFLAGS' FIRST WORD (measured: `n` for `make -n`, empty for `make --no-print-directory`) — matching the first word only is what stops a long option containing the letter n from silently disabling the record on a real run.

2. THE FINGERPRINT MUST NOT BE PORCELAIN-DERIVED. `git status --porcelain` prints the same ` M path` line however many times a file is rewritten, so a porcelain-based staleness signal would carry the identical blind spot to `change_set_hash` — this batch's other defect. It is HEAD + `git diff HEAD` + `git hash-object` over untracked files, so it moves on tracked content, on untracked appearance, and on untracked content.

3. RECORDING MOVED THE TREE IT HAD JUST RECORDED. The ledger write is itself an untracked file, so the first version reported MOVED immediately after writing UNCHANGED. It does NOT reproduce in this repo — `.gitignore:12` hides `.claude/.qa-tracking/` here — and it DOES reproduce in an installed target, because install.sh writes that ignore rule only when the target had no `.gitignore` at all. Fixed with the SHARED `workflow_self_written` rule rather than a local pattern, which required moving the region below the denylist sourcing.

NEGATIVE CONTROL: `.claude/scripts/tests/gate-claim-honesty.test.sh`, 79 assertions, sections 3/3M (the claim), 4/4M (the fingerprint), 5/5M (the dry-run guard), plus 1/2/2M for ko82 in the same file. Every guard has a mutation with an explicit landed-leg, a named specific misbehaviour, a restore control, and a leg that RUNS the shipped artifact.

RUN AGAINST THE UNFIXED STATE AND OBSERVED TO FAIL, which is the point:
    fixed tree   (this change set) : 79 passed / 0 failed, rc=0
    unfixed tree (1233ea5)         : 32 passed / 47 failed, rc=1
Command: `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR=<sandbox of 1233ea5 blobs> bash .claude/scripts/tests/gate-claim-honesty.test.sh`.

AND THE SPEC CAUGHT A VACUOUS ASSERTION IN ITSELF. Check 5.4 originally asserted that the dry run's OUTPUT contained the guarded branch's echo. `make -n` PRINTS the recipe, so that string was present whichever branch ran — the assertion passed identically on the guarded and unguarded Makefile. Its own 5M leg is what exposed it. It now observes a marker FILE, which only the executing branch creates. Recorded in the spec's comments because it is a live instance of the pairing convention's leg-4 point: an assertion over printed text is an assertion about the source, not about behaviour.

NOT DONE, deliberately: no L2/L3 run (operator instruction); the ledger is a self-report and the readout says so rather than the gate pretending to have verified it.

R1-F1 (HIGH) — THE LEDGER READOUT ASSERTS A PROVENANCE THE MECHANISM DOES NOT ESTABLISH.
verify-before-stop.sh:317-318 prints, unconditionally: "this gate did not run it and does not vouch for it — the command recorded its own result, re-run it to check". record_verification (:268) takes <label> and <exit-code> as ARGUMENTS and writes them verbatim; the ledger line carries five fields and no provenance field, so nothing distinguishes a make-written record from a hand-typed one. The only record in this repo s ledger was typed by hand tonight, so the first real record falsifies the sentence that describes it. The empty-ledger branch (:298-303) is sharper still: it claims "the command writes its own result, so the record cannot claim a run that did not happen" and then prints, two lines below, the exact command that does precisely that.

This is NOT the documented forged-record residual (qa-gate.sh:1441-1445, :3383-3389, :3516-3525). That boundary describes what an ADVERSARY can do. This is a false statement produced by HONEST use of the advertised interface: someone who ran the tiers as four separate commands has no other way to record them, and the gate then vouches for their record s provenance in words the mechanism cannot support. The task s own criterion is that the gate stop claiming more than it delivers; the half added to satisfy that criterion does not satisfy it.

Fix is text-only and small. R1-F1 (high) STANDS, and the orchestrator now concurs. But its scope needs stating precisely, because the orchestrator's own message contains the mechanism the finding is about.

Their point 2 credits the output for disclaiming its vouching, quoting the whole parenthesis approvingly:

  "(this gate did not run it and does not vouch for it - the command recorded
   its own result, re-run it to check)"

Split into its four clauses (verify-before-stop.sh:317-318):

  "this gate did not run it"                    TRUE
  "and does not vouch for it"                   TRUE
  "the command recorded its own result"         NOT ESTABLISHED - false of the

  "re-run it to check"                          TRUE, and the right remedy

Three true clauses and one false one, and the false one is the clause that supplies the READER'S REASON TO BELIEVE THE RECORD. It rode along inside a parenthesis being praised for its honesty. That is exactly the structure ko82 exists to correct - "it sat third in a list of four whose other three are accurate, so its true neighbours lent it credibility" - reproduced live, in the reading of an experienced reviewer, one file over. I am recording this not as a point against the orchestrator but as the strongest available evidence that the clause needs to go: if it survives a careful reading by someone who already knows the finding, it will survive every other reading.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE FIX. The orchestrator frames option 1 as correcting "the rationale text". That is necessary but NOT sufficient. The false claim exists in three places and the rationale is the least important of them:

  2. verify-before-stop.sh:300-301  "the command writes its own result, so the
     record cannot claim a run that did not happen" - SHIPPED, and printed
     directly above the manual recipe that falsifies it.
  3. The bd rationale / KEY DECISIONS: "written by make test-ci itself, never
     by an agent."

- **The correction to QA's own r8 judgement is real.** `text`/`eol` reproduces
  the full tracked-half false UNCHANGED: `git status` ` M`, `update-index
  --refresh` rc=1, flagged diff 0 bytes, fingerprint frozen across an eol-only

  family was too weak to produce a false UNCHANGED was WRONG. Non-vacuity

## QA's judgement on the two questions put to it

1. **`--attr-source`: named-and-declined is CORRECT.** The version argument
   alone would only mandate a *guard*, not a decline — so it is not by itself
   sufficient. What settles it is the second, version-independent reason: aiming
   `--attr-source` at the empty tree un-filters every file whose filter is doing
   its job, so a repo that deliberately strips notebook output would start
   reporting MOVED on every re-execution — a false positive on exactly the
   changes it has declared uninteresting, plus a re-baseline of every recorded

   residual. Separately, taking `--no-filters` while declining `--attr-source`
   is not inconsistent: `--no-filters` predates the script's existing floor

2. **The ledger-continuity residual is ACCEPTABLE as stated**, and QA measured

   filter-using installs that have filtered *untracked* files, self-correcting
   at the next `record_verification`, and in the fail-safe direction (MOVED
   means re-verify).

NOTE ON VERSIONS: the two earlier "qa-plan v1" comments exist because the running
bd-mcp server predates this change set's hydration fix and reads zero comments
(so each write numbered itself v1). This v2, posted via the CLI, is canonical.
Content below is the full iteration-2 record, identical in substance to the
second v1 comment.

## Delta scope: reviewed hash 5fd3327d... -> 59400c98...; tracker 73 -> 74 (+.claude/agents/qa.md). Content deltas in exactly 11 files, everything else byte-stable (verified by diff-of-diffs against the saved iteration-1 diff).

## All four iteration-1 findings RESOLVED and re-verified live
- R1-F1 HIGH: classify() (3 conservative signals) + refresh REFUSAL (exit 3) + manual reconcile (import-then-export). Repros re-run: fresh-clone truncation REFUSED (ledger byte-identical, missing ids named); two-sided divergence REFUSED; comment-richer-only case REFUSED; strict-subset control auto-repaired (no overtrigger). reconcile additive in all probes incl. field-conflict (bd import preserves newer DB state). session-start Warning 3c + doctor exit-3 FAIL branch verified (import-direction remedies, never export). AGENTS.md reconcile->pull->reconcile. Spec sections 6 (6.1-6.19) + 7 (7.1-7.8) pin refusal, data survival, comment-only case, db-ahead control, fresh-clone regression.
- R1-F2 MEDIUM: chain applied at qa.md:549/638, BEADS.md (also fixed its array-shape/.text accessor), TROUBLESHOOTING.md. BEADS.md shape live-verified on 1.1.2.

- R1-F4 LOW: two-branch bdcompat_sha256 + non-vacuity shape guard (^[0-9a-f]{64}$) before the determinism pin.

## Verification battery (iteration 2)
L1 32/32. L3 451/5 skipped. lint 0. Targeted L2 over the delta surface: 11 specs / 558 assertions / 0 fail (bd-compat, beads-ledger, epic-gate, installer-beads-upgrade, installer-target-functional, qa-gate-baseline, qa-gate, session-lifecycle, subagent-start, tech-debt, verify-before-stop). Fixture copies 175/175 byte-identical to new canonical. Hash coherence: tracker == impact report == review request == 59400c98...

## Residuals BELOW threshold (follow-ups, not blockers)
1. classify() failure modes fall through to db-ahead: jq-less PATH reproduced DESTROYING a ledger-ahead ledger, masked as "refreshed (2 -> 2 records)". Reachability: install.sh hard-exits without jq. Recommend fail-toward-refusal (cannot-classify => refuse), honoring the script's own "conservative by construction".
2. session-end.sh still direction-blind `export`: mid-session pull outside the protocol + normal session end destroys pulled ledger-only records. Recommend export -> refresh (refusal already composes with sync-errors log + Warning 3c).
3. docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md:356/598 advise `bd daemon restart`/`bd daemon status` — REMOVED in 1.1.2 (verified: unknown command). Same removed-command class as bd sync, in a file this change set edited.
4. OPERATIONAL: a bd-mcp server started before this upgrade reads zero comments for the whole session (writes fine) — bd_doc_read/bd_list_comments/bd_show_task observations degrade silently until restart. No doc mentions restarting MCP servers after upgrading MCP code. One line in TROUBLESHOOTING/MCP_SERVERS closes it. (This session's server exhibits it; it explains the duplicate qa-plan v1s and spawn-1's "comments: 0" observation.)
5. Carried pre-existing: bd-mcp integration #7 fixture rot (predates G2.n6d); TROUBLESHOOTING marker-file advice; bd delete vs divergence ambiguity note.

comments.text: RESOLVED R2-F1 at 2026-08-02T14:09:42Z: fix=install.sh:518-580 upgrade_beads_if_old — safeguard now writes via `bd sync --flush-only || bd export -o` (0.47.1 sync preserves comments 3/3; export drops them 3->0, re-measured) and VERIFIES: ledger_comment_count() compares before/after, restores the .pre-upgrade.bak and refuses on any regression test=.claude/tests/component/specs/installer-beads-upgrade.sh::6.3 all 3 comments survive; ::6.8-6.13 a comment-dropping exporter REFUSES and the ledger is restored with all 3; ::6.14-6.15 META proves the modelled 0.47 exporter really shreds while preserving record count — The safeguard was writing the pre-upgrade ledger with bd 0.47.1 bd export, which drops every comment (974->0 per LESSONS.md; re-measured here as 3 comments in the DB -> a ledger with no comments key, exit 0), then bootstrapping 1.1.2 from it — destroying every approval record, rubric verdict, IMPLEMENTER identity and REVIEW-ARTIFACT. Fixed by choosing the version-appropriate WRITER (0.47 sync --flush-only preserves comments) and by verifying rather than trusting it: comment counts are compared before and after, and a drop restores the backup and refuses the upgrade. The old spec was vacuous here because its fake bd modelled no comments at all; it now seeds three gate records and asserts they survive end to end.

comments.text: RESOLVED R2-F2 at 2026-08-02T14:10:02Z: fix=beads-ledger.sh classify() rewritten: db-ahead now requires POSITIVE per-record evidence (canonically identical | DB updated_at strictly newer | DB has more comments — the last leg is required because bd comments add does NOT bump updated_at, measured). Adds a jq/tooling gate and a parse-integrity gate; new indeterminate verdict refuses on exit 3. cmd_check/cmd_refresh only write on db-ahead. session-end.sh switched from export to refresh. test=.claude/tests/component/specs/beads-ledger.sh::8.1-8.4 label-only / dependency-only / equal-count-different-comment-text / arbitrary-field all refuse with the ledger byte-identical; ::8.5-8.6 same-second updated_at; ::8.7-8.9 unparseable line refuses instead of being skipped; ::8.10-8.12 jq-less PATH refuses (QA live repro); ::8.13-8.14 CONTROL — a local comment-add is still proven db-ahead and IS exported — classify() enumerated three ledger-ahead signals and fell through to db-ahead, so every unmodeled difference resolved to the destructive direction and line 357 overwrote it. The default is now inverted: only positive proof that the database is the newer side authorises a write, and cannot-classify (missing jq, unparseable lines, a difference with no evidence either way) refuses on the same exit code as ledger-ahead. The comment-count leg is load-bearing rather than incidental — bd comments add does not bump updated_at, so a timestamp-only rule would have refused the commonest legitimate case and made the mechanism useless; that path is pinned as a control so the refusals cannot be satisfied by refusing everything.

QA-GATE BLOCKED at 2026-08-02T14:32:41Z: QA iteration 3: BLOCK on R3-F1 (HIGH, recorded in the qa-claude REVIEW-ARTIFACT r3, reviewed_hash f3f4c3db...).

R3-F1 — classify() rule ordering lets db-newer-timestamp authorise an export that destroys pulled comments. Reproduced live: shared record, ledger copy has 2 comments at updated_at T0 (comments do not bump updated_at), DB copy has 1 comment but a later local edit (T1 > T0). Rule 2 proves it db-ahead before the comment comparison is consulted; session-start refresh then rewrites the ledger and the pulled TEAMMATE comment is gone (reported ok:true, refreshed 1 -> 1 records; check says plain stale). This is the second-machine-after-git-pull state the script header lists as protected.

FIX SHAPE (small): in the classify() awk (beads-ledger.sh:281-286), the ledger-more-comments comparison must GUARD, not rescue: a shared record with ledger_comments > db_comments classifies ledger-ahead (or at minimum is never proven db-ahead) BEFORE the timestamp rule. Comments are append-only and updated_at does not track them, so ledger-more-comments always means the DB lacks comment content regardless of timestamps.

SPEC (extend section 8, which currently holds timestamps EQUAL in 8.1-8.6 — the spec blind spot mirrors the code): (a) pulled-comment + later-local-edit refuses with the ledger byte-identical; (b) CONTROL: later local edit at EQUAL comment counts is still proven db-ahead and exports (so the fix cannot be satisfied by widening refusal to every newer-timestamp record).

Also while in the file: R3-F2 (LOW, recorded): record_meta header claims jq -S canonicalisation; code uses plain tojson. Add -S or fix the comment.

Everything else in this round is VERIFIED GOOD: R2-F1 (writer chain + verify/restore/refuse; spec 6.x non-vacuous, META 6.14/6.15 mutually guarded), R2-F2 controls bite (8.13/8.14), jq-less subprocess precondition holds (8.10-8.12), R2-F3 parity Section 8 + mutation META (652 assertions), session-end refresh switch, TROUBLESHOOTING/MCP_SERVERS fixes. comments.text: RESOLVED R3-F1 at 2026-08-02T15:40:33Z: fix=beads-ledger.sh classify() awk — the comment-asymmetry test is now a GUARD evaluated BEFORE the timestamp rule: `($2+0) > ($5+0) { print $1; next }` precedes `($6 > $3) { next }`, so a shared record whose ledger side holds more comments can never be proven db-ahead by a later local edit. Indeterminate message reworded to "no proof the database loses nothing" (it previously claimed "same timestamp and no extra comments", which was false for exactly this state). test=.claude/tests/component/specs/beads-ledger.sh::9.1-9.8 the destructive state (ledger richer in comments AND database updated_at newer, both preconditions asserted) refuses on check and refresh, ledger byte-identical, the colleague QA-GATE APPROVED record survives; ::9.9-9.12 CONTROL — equal comment counts plus a newer local edit is still db-ahead and DOES export — The db-ahead legs prove the database record is NEWER; for append-only sub-records that is not the same claim as "loses nothing", and bd comments add does not bump the parent updated_at. So a teammate comment arriving via git pull plus any later local edit short-circuited on the timestamp rule and the automatic session-start refresh destroyed it, reporting ok:true / refreshed (1 -> 1 records) — an identical record count, so nothing looked lost. Reproduced end to end before the fix and re-run after. Fix is the ordering change only, as scoped. Non-vacuity proven directly: the same state run against a copy with the guard demoted below the timestamp rule exits 0 and destroys the record, while the shipped version exits 3 and preserves it, so 9.5/9.7 fail on the pre-fix ordering. Section 8 could not have caught this because every case there holds updated_at equal.

QA-GATE BLOCKED at 2026-08-02T15:58:54Z: QA round 4: BLOCK on R4-F1 (HIGH, recorded in the qa-claude r4 artifact) — the R3-F1 family has one more member, and it is the one I scoped past in round 3.

R4-F1 — comment-count evidence is blind to comment-SET divergence under concurrent writers. Verified live against the SHIPPED guard, two variants: (A) equal counts, disjoint sets (ledger: teammate comment TA; DB: local comment LB) + any later local edit -> rule 3 proves db-ahead -> refresh destroys TA. (B) DB has MORE comments, disjoint (ledger: TA; DB: LB+LC), NO local edit -> rule 4 proves db-ahead -> refresh destroys TA. Variant B needs nothing but both machines commenting on the same task — the review workflow itself.

FIX PROPERTY (not prescribing the implementation this time — round 3 taught me count-guards are my blind spot too): no db-ahead proof may rest on comment COUNTS. The comment dimension is safe only when the ledger record comment set is a SUBSET of the DB record comment set, on canonical comment identity (full comment objects, not text alone). Local appends (ledger set strictly inside db set) must remain provable db-ahead — keep a 9.9-style control for that.

PINS REQUIRED: variant A refuses, ledger byte-identical; variant B refuses likewise; CONTROL: db = ledger comments + locally-appended extras still exports; plus a demote/mutation META in the same style as the R3-F1 one so the subset guard is demonstrated load-bearing.

Everything else in round 4 is VERIFIED GOOD: the R3-F1 ordering fix (guard before timestamp, confirmed against my original repro — comment survives), pins 9.1-9.12 all pass with both preconditions asserted, the demote-mutation non-vacuity demonstration, R3-F2 comment correction (accepted — refusal is the fallback either way), both lessons applied, L1 32/32, L3 451/5, lint 0, beads-ledger spec 91/0, fixture copies synced. Resolve via qa-gate.sh resolve-finding R4-F1 with --fix/--test; QA re-verifies with the exact producer/consumer kit (BASE0/PULLED1 snapshots, recipe in the artifact evidence).

comments.text: RESOLVED R4-F1 at 2026-08-02T21:53:00Z: fix=ELIMINATED, not patched. beads-ledger.sh: cmd_refresh (the automatic write) DELETED — invoking it is now a usage error. reconcile and export are dry-run by default and require --apply (worktree-sweep.sh convention); export dry-run additionally names what it would discard. session-start.sh and session-end.sh call `check` only and write nothing; both surface the divergence and name `reconcile --apply`. workflow-doctor beads_ledger check retained with remedies updated. AGENTS.md Landing-the-Plane, BEADS.md and TROUBLESHOOTING.md updated to --apply. test=.claude/tests/component/specs/beads-ledger.sh::10.1-10.12 QA variants A and B rebuilt as detector regressions — preconditions asserted (equal counts/disjoint sets; DB more comments/disjoint), detector reports non-zero, and 10.9 asserts the detect-and-warn path performed NO WRITE with the teammate record surviving both hooks; ::11.1-11.7 NEGATIVE CONTROL — no hook contains a ledger-writing invocation, cmd_refresh is gone, plus a demote/mutation META that plants a `reconcile --apply` in SessionStart and proves the probe flips; ::3.3, 4.2, 4.8 hooks leave the ledger byte-identical; ::6.11a-c dry-run default pinned — The finding is the fifth member of one family: every member was an evidence rule whose claim was weaker than the safety property it authorised — newer-record is not loses-nothing, more-comments is not superset, count is not set. Four rounds of strengthening individual rules left the shape intact, so the mechanism is removed rather than guarded again. classify() survives as the DETECTOR; nothing writes the ledger without an explicit operator --apply, and the negative control fails if any automatic path reacquires the ability. Direction hints can still be imperfect in variants A and B, and that is now harmless and stated plainly in the spec — which is the point of removing the write rather than trusting the classifier. Precedent verified before citing: gl6 closed the same way after six rounds and thirteen findings ("Resolved by SCOPE REDUCTION" — a 103-line automated sweep declined in favour of automate-the-read / hand-do-the-write).

  installer-beads-upgrade.sh (L2, 43 assertions) — fresh + ALREADY-INSTALLED paths,

    export would drop comments, and 6.14/6.15 METAs proving the modelled 0.47

  packaging-parity.test.sh Section 8 (L1, 19 assertions) — install.sh <-> install.ps1

     was weaker than the safety property it authorised (newer-record != loses-nothing;

     worktree-sweep.sh's convention. export's dry run names what it would DISCARD.

     restores the backup and refuses the upgrade.

  1. installer-v3-upgrade 8e leg B — 2 assertions, adjudicated, D7 manifest freeze.

--- llm_observations ---
Five defects, one mechanism, four review rounds, every member found by someone
else. After round 2 I had already written "the default was the bug" in my own
report and then shipped two more members of the same family. A family that keeps
producing members despite each fix being individually correct is evidence about
the DESIGN, not the rules — that signal was available to me two rounds before the
operator gave the removal instruction, and recognising it faster is the single
biggest improvement available to me on work of this shape.

Two of my own guards were initially wrong in the LAX direction, which is the
expensive direction for a guard: the negative-control probe matched remediation
TEXT as if it were an invocation, and a jq-less precondition was satisfied by
bash's command hash table rather than the PATH under test. Both were caught only
because the demote/mutation META is now house standard; neither would have been
caught by the assertion passing.

mistaken for oversight):

    sentence that was corrected in qa.md this round. Same wording, same defect;
    only qa.md was in scope.

    over agent prompts and docs for bd-invocation patterns would have caught both
    and is the durable fix.

    to the ledger, and deliberately untouched.

surfaces were files THIS change set had already edited. Editing a file for one
reason does not mean its prose was re-read for another.

--- context_coverage ---
READ, to ground the work: bd 1.1.2's own --help surface for show/init/export/
import/bootstrap/dep/sql/hooks/upgrade, and every subcommand it lists diffed
programmatically against every bd subcommand the repo invokes (that diff is how
`bd sync`'s removal was found rather than guessed); LESSONS.md:92 (the 974->0
export entry, my own, from the previous task); worktree-sweep.sh's ARG_APPLY /
--report-only precedence, as the dry-run convention to match; gl6's full
close_reason via `bd show --include-comments`, to confirm the SCOPE REDUCTION
parallel actually held before citing it; WORKFLOW_DENYLIST_REGEX with an empirical
match test on both a .qa-tracking path and a scratchpad path; bd-compat.sh's
130-line pin inventory; _fixture-script-sync.unit.spec.ts's header (which is what
corrected my earlier wrong belief that the e2e fixture copies were frozen
snapshots); review-check.sh cmd_gate and the artifact grammar; the doctor's check
registry and exit-code arms.

MEASURED rather than assumed, because assuming is what produced most of the
defects: comment and dependent inlining on BOTH bd versions; --no-daemon's cobra
arg-eating mechanism; `bd sql` refused in embedded mode (which closed off the
cheap staleness predicate); `bd init` now running `git init` and scaffolding
CLAUDE.md/.claude/settings.json; the `--deps blocks:` INVERSION and its
type-specificity (discovered-from and parent-child land correctly); 0.47.1's
`bd export` dropping every comment while `sync --flush-only` preserves them;
`bd comments add` NOT bumping updated_at (which is why a timestamp-only rule
would have refused the commonest legitimate case); export byte-determinism; and
every R1-R4 reproduction run against the UNFIXED state before being fixed.

DELIBERATELY NOT READ, with reasons:
  - install.ps1 was never EXECUTED. pwsh is not installed on this machine and the
    file has never been run by anyone, anywhere (v4.1 closure). Its PowerShell
    semantics — $LASTEXITCODE after a throwing native call, Push-Location around a
    failing bd, Invoke-Expression on a piped irm — are verified by mirroring bash
    logic and by machine-checked text parity, nothing more. I am not claiming
    Windows is tested.
  - The bd-mcp `npm test` integration suite: its #7 is pre-existing red, fails
    identically on the pre-change tree, and is wired into no CI lane. Classified
    not-mine by QA and the orchestrator; not re-derived.
  - The LIVE e2e tier (L3 fixtures needing API keys) was never run. Everything I
    know about runFixture/beadsCapture under 1.1.2 comes from the unit tier plus
    targeted probes, not from an end-to-end replay.
  - installer-v3-upgrade 8e leg B's internals, beyond diagnosing the coupling —
    adjudicated out.

LARGEST REMAINING UNKNOWN I SHIP ON: with the automatic write removed, the ledger
now goes stale whenever an operator ignores the warning. Detection is loud (a
per-session SessionStart warning, a sync-errors.log line, and a named doctor FAIL)
and the Landing-the-Plane protocol writes it on the release path, so the failure
mode is recoverable staleness rather than loss — which is the right trade after
five destructive defects. But nobody has yet observed how often that warning gets
ignored in practice, and its failure mode is quieter than a red test. If the
ledger turns out to drift in real use, the answer is a commit-time or CI check,
NOT a restored automatic write: spec 11 will fail if anyone tries the latter.

## D1 implementation complete — awaiting the final measured tier run

**Rulings 1, 2 and 4 accepted as briefed. Ruling 3 accepted with one refinement (the HOST of the hash), disclosed below.**

### Ruling 3 refinement — host the hash on `workflow-manifest.sh hash-file`, not `impact-report.sh --hash-file`

The ruling ("`--hash-file` MUST refuse before hashing") is implemented in full. What changed is *where*. Measured at `acc4ce1`:

* `workflow-manifest.sh hash_file()` already implements the exact contract the ruling demands — three backends, 64-lowercase-hex validation, **hard fail with no sentinel** — and its own header names the same hazard ("a plausible-but-wrong hash"). `impact-report.sh`'s `sha256_stdin` implements the inverse (the `sha256-unavailable` constant).
* The plan's `sed -e 's/\r$//' -e 's/[[:space:]]*$//'` **erases Markdown hard line breaks**. Measured: `line one␣␣\nline two` and `line one\nline two` both hash to `e9024f1a…`; raw bytes give `87f1d7bd…` vs `e9024f1a…`. The artifact is Markdown, so the normalisation hides the edits the hash exists to detect.
* Raw bytes also mean `shasum -a 256 <file>` reproduces a recorded binding by hand. The spec asserts that equality.
* **One map claim I could NOT reproduce**: "routing through sed appends a final newline, so files with and without a trailing newline collide." On this platform (BSD sed) they do NOT collide — `printf 'a'` → `ca978112…`, `printf 'a\n'` → `87428fc5…`, both equal to their raw digests. The `s/\r$//` redundancy claim DOES hold (both spellings byte-identical).

### Ruling 3, the vacuity it was about, reproduced and now a negative control

`sed … /nonexistent/x.md 2>/dev/null | shasum -a 256` → `e3b0c442…` at **rc=0** — the same constant `impact-report.test.sh:363` pins as the empty change set. Both legs are in the new spec as CONTROLS (1.6/1.6b, 1.7/1.7b), so if they ever stop reproducing, the refusals have become decoration and it will show.

### The record and the binding

* `qa-gate.sh design-record` writes `DESIGN-ARTIFACT v1 task=… designer=… design_hash=… units=… at <ts>: <summary>` — split from D2's review verdict because D2's independence check needs a durable statement of WHO the designer was.
* `approve` gains `design_hash=<h>` as a **fourth machine token**, after `worktree=`, immediately before ` at `. Four-arm ladder: bind only when a live re-hash agrees with the recorded one; otherwise no token and the reason named.
* Suffix forgery reproduced from source: `$summary` is unvalidated positionals (`cmd_approve`'s `*)` arm) interpolated on the same line, and both readers use `grep -qF '[review bypass:'` over the whole comment. Decisive for ruling 1. Not fixed here (`yrij`).

### Two defects I found in my OWN code by driving it, not reading it

1. **`$ids | index(.)` returns 0 forever.** A jq function argument is evaluated against that function's INPUT, so `index(.)` searched `$ids` for `$ids`. The undeclared-dependency check validated a unit depending on `"U9"` as clean.
2. **`$ready | index(.id)` ABORTS jq** ("Cannot index array with string"), and a trailing `|| cyclic=""` turned the abort into "no cycle". Reachable only once something becomes ready — so a pure two-unit cycle was caught while every graph with a root silently passed, including the valid one.

Both fixed; the acyclicity check now reports a failed computation instead of swallowing it. Recorded in `LESSONS.md`.

### Three things I deliberately did NOT do

* **The `spec` bd_doc pointer** (plan D1). Named bd docs are append-only, so every stale pointer with its stale hash stays visible forever, and eleven read-sites in nine files currently promise that doc "carries the goal, acceptance criteria, constraints and out-of-scope notes". Nothing in D1 reads a pointer. Under the plan's own rule that a field no reader parses is decoration, it belongs with **D5**, where spec injection at spawn gives it a reader.
* **`bd update --design`.** Zero shipped readers; `subagent-start.sh`'s injection is `head -8` + a NOTES-anchored awk window + `jq '.labels'`, so a DESIGN section is structurally dropped. Not written, not claimed.
* **`docs/AGENTS.md`'s "Adding a New Agent" recipe** — the plan assigns that file to D7 and D0 already refreshed the roster. It is genuinely stale (it prescribes keyword routing, which CLAUDE.md forbids), but pulling it forward would be undeclared scope.

### Reddening mutations — ten, each run, each red

| mutation | reds |
|---|---|
| delete `hash-file`'s three refusals | 5 (incl. the empty-file constant reaching a caller) |
| neuter the sentinel-count check | 4 |
| make an unparseable block read as zero units | 1 |
| neuter `artifact_outside_spec_dir` | 1 |
| neuter `designer_touched_source` | 3 |
| delete the `design-artifact` governing row | 4 (manifest) + 1 (doc-only) |
| widen the row to scan all of `docs/` | 10 |
| restore `Bash`/`Edit` to `designer.md` | 2 |
| add a second DESIGN-UNITS extraction to `qa-gate.sh` | 1 |

The first mutation run reddened **zero** in five of nine mutants — the mutant tree was built from `git ls-files` and the new spec is untracked, so nothing ran. Investigated rather than believed.

### One self-inflicted hazard caught before it shipped

A comment I wrote in `review-check.sh` cited `codex-review.sh` by name — `reviewer-lane-degradation.sh` asserts **zero** case-insensitive `codex|reviewer[._]lane` matches in the three gate scripts, comments included. Rewritten to name the helper without the token; count is back to 0/0/0.

description:
# Phase D2 — design review loop, DS1-DS8 rubric, the design-verdict record, amendments, gate enforcement

MEASUREMENT BASIS. Everything below was resolved by command at HEAD 9488c69 (branch
v5/design-phase, tree clean) on 2026-08-14. Where a claim was NOT established by a command
it is marked UNVERIFIED. The plan section for D2 is `docs/plans/v5-design-phase-plan.md`
lines 574-626 (`grep -n "^### D2\|^### D3"` -> 574 / 627; file is 846 lines, not 827).
READ SECTION 2 BEFORE THE PLAN. The plan's D2 section was written before D1 shipped and
four commits have landed on the files it cites; most of its anchors and three of its
design decisions are wrong against the tree.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 1. WHAT D2 BUILDS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

### 1.1 `.claude/agents/design-reviewer.md` — the prompt body

The file exists and is registered (`jq -r '.agents[]' .claude-plugin/plugin.json` lists it;
`wc -l` -> 82). Its frontmatter is final: `tools: Read, Grep, Glob, LS` (byte-identical to
`grader.md`), `model: claude-fable-5`, `effort: max`. **D2 replaces the body only.**

The placeholder body is more current than the plan and self-describes the contract. It
names this task (`claude-workflow-plugin-fkm.4`), the verdict shape
`{verdict, criterion_results, required_fixes, iteration, rubric_version, reviewer_identity}`,
the rubric path, the loop shape, and the packet. It also states three constraints that
already bind: nobody reviews their own work; a model-family collapse is a warning not a
block; the agent is read-only and is a documented exemption in
`.claude/scripts/tests/agent-mcp-tools-parity.test.sh`. Do not restate those from the plan
— read the file.

`required_fixes` is the correct field name. `qa-gate.sh`'s existing grade recorder keys on
that literal: `qa-gate.sh:4392` is `for key in verdict criterion_results required_fixes
iteration rubric_version; do`. `grep -rn "required_changes" .claude/scripts .claude/agents`
returns zero.

The spawn is ROOT-ORCHESTRATED. Subagents cannot spawn subagents; the design-reviewer spawn
must follow the relay pattern at `orchestrator.md:389` (`#### 5a. Rubric-grader relay`), not
be invoked from inside `designer.md`. Regression-guarded by
`no-nested-spawn-instructions.test.sh`.

### 1.2 `.claude/rubrics/design.md` — DS1..DS8

`ls .claude/rubrics/` -> `backend.md bugfix.md default.md devops.md frontend.md`. No
`design.md`. `grep -rn "DS1" .claude/agents .claude/rubrics .claude/scripts` -> one hit,
`design-reviewer.md:48`.

Shipped rubric frontmatter grammar (`head -12 .claude/rubrics/default.md`, `head -8
.claude/rubrics/backend.md`) is `version:` / `name:` / optional `extends:`. `applies_to:`
exists only in `bugfix.md:4` and is read by NO script — the only consumer is an assertion,
`qa-gate-grade-record.test.sh:709`. Criterion id style is `C1..C8`
(`grep -n "^### C" .claude/rubrics/default.md`), so `DS<n>` is consistent and collides with
nothing.

Rubric SELECTION is prompt-level, not script-level: `qa.md:533-545` is a `cat` plus a shell
`case` on the domain label. `grep -rn "rubrics/" .claude/scripts/*.sh` (excluding tests)
returns only comments. D2 therefore has to add the design rubric to a PROMPT selector (the
design-reviewer's own, most likely), not to a script.

Manifest coverage is automatic: `workflow-manifest.sh:376` is
`scan_flat operator ".claude/rubrics" '*.md'`, so a new `design.md` is picked up without a
new row — but it changes the manifest's hash set.

Criteria per the plan (unchanged, and the plan is not stale here): acceptance criteria
observable and falsifiable; decomposition complete and disjoint; every unit declares
files/interfaces/verification; >=2 approaches with technical rejection reasons;
`out_of_scope` non-empty; global constraints copied verbatim; **DS7 reuse-before-building**;
**DS8 contradicts no `LESSONS.md` entry and no existing record grammar**.

DS1 MUST BE WRITTEN AGAINST THE SHIPPED SCHEMA, NOT THE PLAN'S. `review-check.sh:740-742`
enforces `acceptance[]` entries as OBJECTS with non-empty `id` and `text`

### 1.3 The design-verdict subcommand and its `DESIGN-REVIEW v1` grammar

`grep -rn "<new-cap-key>" .claude/agents .claude/scripts --include='*.md' --include='*.sh'`
shows a hardcoded numeric default anywhere except that file plus the documented fallback in
the `grep -E '^…=' … || echo N` idiom already used at `orchestrator.md:398` / `qa.md:698`.

**4.9** No new exit code is introduced in `qa-gate.sh`, `review-check.sh` or
`verify-before-stop.sh` unless a written rationale amends `qa-gate.sh:143-149`. FAILS IF:
`grep -c "exit 5\|exit 6\|exit 7"` becomes non-zero on any of the three AND
`qa-gate.sh:143-149` still reads "A new code would make every existing caller's `case` on the
exit status silently incomplete for no gain."

**4.10** `subagent-start.sh`'s implementer set is unchanged, or if changed, the change is
paired with a leg proving `designer_touched_source` still fires. FAILS IF:
`sed -n '106p' .claude/scripts/subagent-start.sh` no longer reads
`        backend|frontend|devops) return 0 ;;` and no test asserts the edit ban still
engages for a designer-only task.

**4.11** `make test` is green and `EXPECTED_SPECS` at
`.claude/scripts/tests/run-tests.sh:200` matches the spec count the run reports. FAILS IF:
run-tests.sh reports a spec-count mismatch. Do NOT verify the bump against
`ls *.test.sh | wc -l` — lines 193-199 document that it is off by exactly one by
construction.

**4.12** Every ordering-rationale comment D2 invalidates is amended in the same change. In
particular the comment inside `cmd_approve` that enumerates FOUR refusals must reflect the
real count. FAILS IF: the enumeration count in that comment does not equal the number of
post-argparse refusal families reachable in `cmd_approve` (`qa-gate.sh:2731`-`:4072`).

**4.13** `docs/HOOKS.md` gains rows for the new subcommand AND for D1's `design-record`
(currently `grep -c "design-record" docs/HOOKS.md` -> 0). FAILS IF: either count is still 0.

**4.14** Nothing D2 adds re-introduces the Sol-first separation breach:
`grep -cEi 'codex|reviewer[._]lane'` remains 0 in `qa-gate.sh`, `verify-before-stop.sh` and
`review-check.sh`. FAILS IF: any of the three returns non-zero
(`.claude/tests/component/specs/reviewer-lane-degradation.sh` enforces this with a live META).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 5. THE PAIRING — required for EVERY new check (`.claude/tests/README.md:532-572`)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

A pair is PAIRED only when all four parts are present. At closeout every check D2 adds is
either paired below or listed as UNPAIRED with a reason.

1. **Non-vacuity** — a mutation of the shipped artifact (or the state it reads) WITH an
   explicit leg proving the mutation landed where it was aimed: `END { if (!found) exit 7 }`
   on an `awk` strip, a byte-comparison of mutant against shipped, a `bash -n` on the result.
2. **Specific misbehaviour** — an assertion that the mutant fails IN THE WAY THE GUARD
   PREVENTS, naming the check that would fail. Not "the mutant is different".
3. **Restore control** — the shipped artifact, same inputs, same call shape, behaving
   correctly.
4. **Execution** — **at least one leg observes the shipped artifact RUNNING.** This is the
   leg that gets skipped, and README `:557-569` records that the census split perfectly on
   executable-vs-document: not one document check reached leg 4, not one executable check
   failed it.

Per-check plan:

**P1 — design-satisfied refusal at approve.** Mutate: strip the refusal arm from the shipped
`qa-gate.sh` into a throwaway copy, `END{if(!found) exit 7}` on the strip plus `bash -n`.
Misbehaviour: the mutant's `approve` writes the `QA-GATE APPROVED` comment on a task with no
design verdict — name that assertion. Control: shipped `qa-gate.sh`, same task, refuses and
leaves `bd show` comment-free. Execution: both legs invoke `bash qa-gate.sh approve`.

**P2 — design_hash staleness (ladder arm 2 -> refusal).** Mutate the ARTIFACT, not the
script: append one byte to `docs/specs/<tid>.md` after recording, and prove the hash moved by
comparing `workflow-manifest.sh hash-file` before/after. Misbehaviour: without the refusal,
approve binds a `design_hash=` token naming bytes that no longer exist. Control: unmodified
artifact -> approve proceeds. Execution: both legs run `qa-gate.sh approve`. NOTE: raw-byte
hashing means a CRLF-only edit is a valid non-vacuous mutation here — use it as a second
non-vacuity leg, and do NOT write a test asserting CRLF is ignored (2.14).

**P3 — reviewer/designer independence at record time.** Mutate the INPUT: a verdict whose
`reviewer_identity` equals the `designer=` on the task's `DESIGN-ARTIFACT` record.
Non-vacuity: assert the two strings are equal before the call. Misbehaviour: the record is
written, so a self-review satisfies the gate. Control: a distinct identity records ok.
Execution: both legs invoke the shipped subcommand. Do NOT build this on `cmd_gate`'s
role-token membership test — 2.2e shows it returns `independent:true` vacuously for
non-role identities.

**P4 — `cap_terminated` predicate (criterion 4.7).** Mutate: replace `stopped_by=verdict`
with `stopped_by=cap:max_review_iterations` in the artifact record line. Non-vacuity: assert
`.artifact.cap_terminated` flipped `false` -> `true` in the gate envelope (use
`jq 'if has("cap_terminated") then … else "?" end'`, NOT `// "?"` — `review-count.test.sh:545`
records that `//` falls through on a literal `false` and silently misreports every non-cap
case). Misbehaviour: without the predicate, the capped review satisfies design-satisfied,
i.e. the transcript above (`ok:true`, `RC=0`) is accepted as a pass. Control: the two
non-cap conclusions (`verdict`, `stop_condition`) satisfy. Execution: both legs run
`review-check.sh gate` and the design predicate. A second META leg — strip the classification
at `review-check.sh:1218-1221` and assert the mutant reports `cap_terminated=false` for a
cap-terminated input — mirrors `review-count.test.sh:582-600`.

**P5 — DESIGN-SCALAR-CLASS writer-side rejection.** Mutate the INPUT: a `reviewer` value
containing a character outside the declared class, and an `iteration` that is not `^[0-9]+$`.
Non-vacuity: assert the offending byte is present in the argument. Misbehaviour: the record
is written with the injected byte, so a downstream anchored `capture(...)` mis-parses — name
which reader. Control: in-class values record ok. Execution: both legs invoke the
subcommand. The rejection must REJECT, never sanitise (the bjx class).

**P6 — amendment / duplicate-artifact refusal.** Mutate: a second design block, or a second
record at the same `iteration`. Non-vacuity: count the `DESIGN-UNITS BEGIN` sentinels before
and after. Misbehaviour: name which reader silently concatenates or `tail -1`s. Control: the
legitimate `iteration=n+1` amendment records with `[amends: <prev-hash>]`. Execution: both
legs run the subcommand.

**P7 — anything asserted about PROMPT text** (`design-reviewer.md`, `design.md`,
`orchestrator.md`) is a DOCUMENT check and will fail leg 4 on its own. Per README `:571-575`,
either find the executable whose behaviour the prose describes and drive that, or list the
check UNPAIRED with the reason. Do not ship a three-leg triad over markdown byte-equality and
call it paired.

**P8 — the second reader in `verify-before-stop.sh`**, IF open question 6.4 resolves in
favour of building it. Mutate: hand-write the approval label without the design record.
Misbehaviour: Stop releases. Control: the shipped hook re-arms. Execution: run the Stop hook
with `stop_hook_active` handling intact. Note the four existing gate call sites (2.7) — the
release predicate is the one in `mark_escalation_if_capped()` (`verify-before-stop.sh:4147`),
not the one in `emit_block()` or `review_rounds_probe()`.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 6. OPEN QUESTIONS — each answerable by measurement
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

**6.1 What identity space does the design independence check compare?**
Measure: take the `designer=<id>` values `cmd_design_record` actually writes on a real task
and the `reviewer_identity` values the design-reviewer prompt actually returns, and check
whether they are drawn from the same vocabulary. If they are not, a membership test is
unbuildable and the check must be string equality on a normalised identity. The shipped
`cmd_gate` computation is NOT a candidate (2.2e, measured `independent:true` vacuously for
`sol-codex`).

**6.2 Does the design refusal need a new exit code, or does `error_key` carry it?**
Measure: enumerate every caller that switches on `qa-gate.sh approve`'s exit status and check
whether any distinguishes the design class from the existing exit-2 / exit-4 classes on the
number alone rather than on `error_key`. If none does, reuse 2 and 4 per `qa-gate.sh:143-149`.
Also check whether a new code would be swallowed by a `*)` catch-all in any existing `case`.

**6.3 Where does the design refusal sit relative to COMPLETION-CONTRACT-REFUSAL?**
Measure: for each candidate position, whether the task is still untouched at the refusal
point. The first task-state write in `cmd_approve` is `add_comment` at `qa-gate.sh:3788`, so
both `:3425` (immediately after REVIEW-SEPARATION END) and `:3717` (the existing
DESIGN-BINDING-TOKEN block) satisfy "leaves the task untouched". The discriminator is the
COMPLETION-CONTRACT block's own prose claim to the last refusal slot, plus whether the design
refusal needs the ladder's computed `recorded_design_hash` / `live_design_hash` locals (which
exist only at `:3717`). Measure that dependency before choosing.

**6.4 Should the second reader exist in `verify-before-stop.sh` at all?**
Measure: the two constraints point opposite ways — `qa.md:466` bans a THIRD reader of "these
records" (the review artifact corpus), and `qa.md:480` bans wiring THE RUBRIC LOOP into the
Stop hook. Determine, from the shipped code, which of the two the design loop is
structurally: does the design verdict gate RELEASE (like the review artifact) or does it gate
APPROVAL (like the rubric)? Answer by checking whether a design verdict recorded AFTER
approval needs to re-arm the gate. If it does not, the second reader is unnecessary and
`qa.md:480` governs.

**6.5 What is the design-loop cap, and where does the key live?**
Measure: the shipped cap idiom is a prompt-level `grep -E '^iteration_cap='` with a numeric
fallback in the same expression (`orchestrator.md:398`, `qa.md:698`). Determine whether a
second key in `.claude/rubric-config` (which today has exactly one, at line 15) or a second
config file produces fewer readers of a hardcoded default. Count the readers each way.

**6.6 Who creates `docs/specs/`?**
Measure: `ls -d docs/specs` fails today and `grep -c "docs/specs" install.sh install.ps1` is
0/0, so the first `design-record` invocation refuses `design_spec_dir_missing`. Determine
whether `workflow-manifest.sh`'s `generate_rows` path can emit it as an install row (it is
declared in `runtime_contract_rows` but that function is reached only via `governing_rows`),
or whether `design-record` should create it, or whether D2 ships it as a tracked directory.

**6.7 Does `design-artifact.test.sh` pass at HEAD?** UNVERIFIED — I did not execute it
(shared tree; the spec creates Beads tasks). It exists (111,996 bytes) and carries the
control D2 must not break at `:505` (`3.10 CONTROL: the identical source path records once an
implementer has SPAWNED`) and `:507` (`3.10b`). Measure with a clean `make test` before
touching `subagent-start.sh` or the implementer-record pattern.

**6.8 Which prompt selects the design rubric?**
Measure: `qa.md:533-545` is the only rubric selector in the tree and it is a `cat` + `case`
in prose. Determine whether the design-reviewer reads `design.md` directly (one reader) or
whether the selector must grow a design arm (two readers, one of them in QA's loop which does
not run design reviews). Count readers each way before writing either.

**6.9 What happens to the plan document?**
The corrections block near the top of `docs/plans/v5-design-phase-plan.md` does not cover any
of section 2's findings — I checked, and no correction addresses the D2 line numbers or the
`design-record` name collision. Decide whether D2 appends corrections 15+ or whether the D2
section is rewritten in place. Note the plan uses THREE competing names for the approve-time
check across its own text (`design-gate`, `design-conform`, DESIGN-SEPARATION); pick one and
say so.

## 3. NEW CONSTRAINTS

### 3a. The store canary (j7kk, `run-tests.sh`)

Three sentinel regions: **ARM `605-667`** (`PROTECTED_STORE="$PROJECT_DIR/.beads"` at `:601`, `PROJECT_DIR` at `:164`), **SAMPLE `806-858`**, **VERDICT `923-954`** with a dedicated FAIL arm `elif [ "$STORE_WRITES" -gt 0 ]` at `:944`. The predicate is **store state** (`dolt hashof('HEAD')` before/after each spec), never a test marker, and the failure text says *"either this spec wrote, or another process wrote concurrently"*. Spec discovery is `find "$TESTS_DIR" -maxdepth 1 -type f -name '*.sh'` at `:322`.

**The isolation census D2 would rely on is measurably wrong in a releasing direction.** The shipped prose at `model-roles.test.sh:125-126` reads: *"CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR, BEADS_DIR, BEADS_DB and --db are all INERT as store redirects on bd 1.2.2."* Measured at HEAD, `bd 1.2.2`, cwd = repo root, baseline `bd list --json | jq length` = **188**:

| configuration | `bd list --json \| jq length` | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR=<tmp>` | 188 | INERT — prose correct |
| `BEADS_DIR=<existing empty dir>` | 188 | INERT — falls back to **production** |
| `BEADS_DIR=<nonexistent>` | 188 | INERT — falls back to **production** |
| `BEADS_DIR=<provisioned store>` | **0** | **REDIRECTS** — prose wrong |
| `BEADS_DB=<any path>` | **0** | **REDIRECTS** — prose wrong |
| `bd --db <nonexistent>.db` | **0** | **REDIRECTS**, and **provisions** a full tree: `find` shows `…/.beads/embeddeddolt/beads/.dolt` |
| `bd -C <dir with no store>` | rc=1 | fail-closed, no fallback |

So `BEADS_DIR` is a **fail-open redirect**: it isolates only when the target is an initialised store. A D2 spec that points it at a fixture whose `bd init` did not run writes to production. Only mechanisms A (`cd` into an initialised fixture) and B (`bd -C`) measured fail-closed.

**UNVERIFIED:** every row above is a **read**. I was barred from `bd create/update/comment`, so whether a bd *write* resolves identically is not established. The circumstantial case is strong (a read provisioned a complete embedded-Dolt tree at the redirect target) but it is inference.

**A concurrent writer is live right now.** The baseline is 188 where a prior session measured 187, and the canary hash moved from `lmqf03d45r1095vumlqslou3mujftle1` to `18daua56uaf7200nmubbttu2urh8369l`. The canary is a *reachability* guard, not an authorship guard — a green D2 spec can go red for someone else's write.

### 3b. skip-when-unchanged (j7kk, `verify-before-stop.sh`)

The skipped region is **one top-level block, `3797`–`3956`**: `if [ "$QA_ESCALATED" = "true" ]` (`3797`) / `elif [ "$VERIFY_SKIP_UNCHANGED" = "true" ]` (`3816`) / `else` (`3832`) / `fi` (`3956`). Three sibling top-level blocks follow: `3797-3956`, `4239-4367`, and the gate block opening at **`4397`** (`if command -v bd … && [ -d "$PROJECT_DIR/.beads" ]`), which reads `GATE_STATUS` at `4399` and runs REVIEW-DISCIPLINE at `4421-4506`.

- A design gate at the **REVIEW-DISCIPLINE site (4421+)** evaluates on every Stop, including a skipped one. No release-surface hole.
- A design check wired in as a `FAILED_CHECKS` contributor **inside 3797-3956** is skipped *and replayed stale*: the skip branch reads `last_failed_checks_file_for` (`3823-3826`) and re-emits the previous Stop's verdict verbatim.

The skip precondition `verified_state_unchanged()` (`:2419`) is file-based only: `tree_fingerprint()` (`:611`) minus `WORKFLOW_SELF_WRITTEN_REGEX` (`workflow-denylist.sh:265` = `(^|/)\.claude/\.qa-tracking/|(^|/)\.beads/interactions\.jsonl$`, exactly two alternatives). **A design verdict recorded only as a Beads comment or label moves neither instrument → the skip fires.** A verdict recorded as a file under `docs/specs/` or `docs/reviews/` moves the fingerprint.

Also: `qa-gate.sh status` now returns `{"ok":false,…,"status":"unavailable"}` and `exit 3` (`:2814-2815`). The existing read is `jq -r '.status // "error"'`, so `unavailable` fails closed. A D2 design gate reading gate status must preserve that.

### 3c. `docs/reviews/` and a second helper-set precedent

`REVIEW_ARTIFACT_SUBDIR="docs/reviews"` at `:4920`; `review_artifact_path_for()` `:4925`, `review_dir_is_review_subdir()` `:4939`, `review_path_is_contained()` `:4959`, `finding_id_in_latest_artifact()` `:4980`. `git ls-files docs/reviews/` → 4 tracked files (`…-rqer-r1/r2.json`, `…-j7kk-r1/r2.json`). The header at `:4890-4892` states it is *"deliberately the SAME shape as a design artifact"*. D2 now has **two** parallel helper sets to copy from, not one — and a third copy is the third instance of the same pattern.

### 3d. The completeness floor (j7kk/a9hh, `run-tests.sh`)

`COMPLETENESS-FLOOR-BEGIN/END` sentinels; `EXPECTED_SPECS=39` at `:200`; the floor compare at `:1066` calls `finish 1` on any mismatch; a `SKIP IS NOT A PASS` arm fails the tier if any spec executed zero assertions; a `PARTIAL` annotation names specs that skipped a section. Negative control is the new `runner-completeness.test.sh` (124KB). **Any D2 spec must execute at least one assertion in every section or the tier goes red**, and adding a spec requires bumping `EXPECTED_SPECS` in the same change.

### 3e. The wipe exemption

`wipe_review_artifacts()` at `:1076-1091`, sole call site `:4060`, every glob prefixed `$QA_TRACKING_DIR/`. Its header at `:1067-1075` is load-bearing prose: *"the canonical review-artifact copy now lives OUTSIDE this directory, at `$REVIEW_ARTIFACT_SUBDIR` (docs/reviews/) … Nothing below globs that directory, and it must not start … The scratch-file wipe below is scoped to `$QA_TRACKING_DIR` alone, by construction, not by omission."* D2 must not extend the wipe to any `docs/` path.

### 3f. The exit-code namespace

`grep -c "exit 5\|exit 6\|exit 7"` → **0** in all three of `qa-gate.sh`, `review-check.sh`, `verify-before-stop.sh`. Literal exits at HEAD (line-anchored): qa-gate `{1:85, 2:23, 3:4, 4:3}`; review-check `{0:4, 1:15, 2:4, 4:31}` plus `exit "$code"` at `:879`. So 5/6/7 are literally unused and AC 4.9 is unchanged.

**But exit 3 is now overloaded.** j7kk's STATUS-UNAVAILABLE region (`2807-2817`) emits `exit 3` for "the store could not be read", while the contract table at `133-145` still documents 3 only as *"atomic operation rolled back"*. The per-subcommand help at `:20-24` documents the new meaning; the contract table does not. If D2 amends the contract (AC 4.9 makes that the price of any new code), the amendment has to fix this too.

**UNVERIFIED:** whether 5/6/7 are *reachable*-free. `set -e` is at `qa-gate.sh:155`, so the observable status is not bounded by the literal `exit` statements. I did not enumerate every unguarded command in 6348 lines.

### 3g. The firstline grammars, and where a new token may go

Five writers at HEAD:

| grammar | line | shape |
|---|---|---|
| QA-GATE APPROVED | `qa-gate.sh:3951` | `${hash_field}reviewed_by=$reviewed_by ${worktree_field}${design_field}${review_file_hash_field}at $ts: $summary$comment_suffix` |
| REVIEW-ARTIFACT v1 | `qa-gate.sh:5204` | `… findings=[$findings_token] artifact_hash=$artifact_hash at $ts: $summary` |
| COMPLETION v1 | `qa-gate.sh:5475` | `task= role= model= pin= fields= payload_sha= at $ts: …` |
| DESIGN-ARTIFACT v1 | `qa-gate.sh:6107` | `task= designer= design_hash= units= at $ts: $summary$record_suffix` |
| IMPLEMENTER | `subagent-start.sh:451` | `role= task= model= pin= at $ts` (no summary tail) |

The five optional machine fields on the approval record are initialised empty at `3809/3818/3835/3836` and set at `3811/3829/3901/3944` — **each carries its own trailing space**.

**The placement rule rqer established, in both grammars it touched:** the new token goes **last among the machine tokens, immediately before ` at <ts>`**. `git show 9488c69:… | grep -n 'comment_text="REVIEW-ARTIFACT'` → `4840` (no `artifact_hash`); HEAD `:5204` inserts it after `findings=[…]`. Same for the approval record: `artifact_hash=` after `design_hash=`. The trust boundary is the colon — anything after `$summary` is unvalidated positional text and can never be a gate input.

**Two hazards for a D2 token:**
- **Positional anchoring.** `qa-gate.sh:6147` reads `capture("^DESIGN-ARTIFACT v1 task=[A-Za-z0-9._+-]+ designer=[A-Za-z0-9._+-]+ design_hash=(?<h>[A-Za-z0-9-]+) ")` — slots 1/2/3 are pinned. Same at `:1743` and `:1766` for COMPLETION's `role=`. A token inserted *before* those breaks the reader silently.
- **Substring capture.** REVIEW-ARTIFACT's readers are unanchored greps with `head -1`: `review-check.sh:1196` (`model=`), `:1202` (`pin=`), `:1203` (`reviewed_hash=`), `:1211` (`artifact_hash=`). A D2 token named `design_model=` or similar, placed before the existing one, would be captured instead.

### 3h. A 7-way mirror obligation the audit does not mention

`git diff 9488c69..HEAD --name-only | grep 'scripts/qa-gate.sh'` returns **8** paths: the shipped script plus seven real (non-symlink) byte-identical copies under `.claude/tests/e2e/fixtures/*/. claude/scripts/`. All eight hash to `f8fb55d93e61403e7f3c69e66a2a7107` at HEAD. The sync command is `make sync-fixtures` (Makefile `:411-430`), and `.claude/tests/e2e/specs/_fixture-script-sync.unit.spec.ts:159` enforces presence. Note the fixture copies are excluded from the change set by `WORKFLOW_DENYLIST_REGEX` (`workflow-denylist.sh:186`), so they will not show up in a change-set hash — but the e2e spec will fail without them.

## 4. WHAT IS UNCHANGED — trust these parts of the 1035-line scope

Each of the following was re-measured at HEAD and resolves exactly as the audit states.

- **`subagent-start.sh` in full.** Byte-identical across 9488c69 / HEAD / worktree. `is_specialist()` `90-95` with `backend|frontend|devops|qa` at `:92`; `is_implementer_role()` `104-109` with **`:106` = `        backend|frontend|devops) return 0 ;;`**; gate at `:493`/`:495`; record at `:517`/`:518`. **AC 4.10's `sed -n '106p'` FAILS-IF is runnable verbatim.** Sections 2.2(a) and 2.2(b) are exact.
