The sentence naming D2 as its consumer is still at `:1226-1227`. **AC 4.7 is unchanged.**
- **review-check.sh's entire design-validation surface** (`378, 533, 553-556, 587, 588, 592, 614, 726, 730-748, 833`) — unmoved. Section 3.1 and DS1's object-shape constraint are exact.

All verbatim. **2.8 and OQ 6.4's two competing constraints are unchanged.**

- **`.claude/rubrics/`** — still five files (backend, bugfix, default, devops, frontend), **no `design.md`**. AC 4.2 unchanged.
- **`docs/specs/`** — `ls -d docs/specs` → "No such file or directory"; `grep -c "docs/specs" install.sh install.ps1` → 0, 0. **2.15 and OQ 6.6 unchanged.**

## 5. OPEN QUESTIONS — each answerable by measurement

**Q1. Does a bd WRITE resolve the store the same way a read does?** Every row in §3a is measured on reads; I was barred from writes. Measure in a throwaway fixture: for each of `bd -C <uninitialised>`, `BEADS_DIR=<uninitialised>`, `--db <nonexistent>`, run a `bd create`, then check whether the repo-root store's `dolt sql -q "SELECT hashof('HEAD')"` advanced. This is the load-bearing question for every D2 spec's isolation.

**Q2. Third ladder or promoted arm 4?** Measure whether the design refusal actually needs `recorded_design_hash` / `live_design_hash` — locals scoped to `3837-3906` — and read `docs/reviews/claude-workflow-plugin-rqer-r{1,2}.json` for the reasoning QA accepted when rqer chose to add a sibling ladder at `3908` instead of converting one. That is the precedent D2 will be measured against.

**Q3. Does a sixth machine token on the approval record break any reader?** Measure by running the two positionally-anchored jq captures (`qa-gate.sh:6147`, `:1743`/`:1766`) and the four unanchored `head -1` greps (`review-check.sh:1196/1202/1203/1211`) against a synthetic record carrying the proposed D2 token, appended after `${review_file_hash_field}`.

AC 4.11 names 39. Measure with `git log -1 --format=%H -- .claude/scripts/tests/run-tests.sh` and a clean, uncontended `make test` at D2 start.

**Q5. Do the three stale grammar sites belong to D2 or a new task?** `qa-gate.sh:2170-2171`, `:2245-2247`, `:3753-3754` all omit `artifact_hash=` that the writers at `:3951` and `:5204` emit. Measure against AC 4.12's wording ("every ordering-rationale comment **D2 invalidates**") — D2 does not invalidate these; rqer already did. CONTRIBUTING.md's post-closure rule says new task.

**Q6. Does `design-artifact.test.sh` pass at HEAD, and does its shim leak?** Its `bin/bd` is a **pass-through** (`exec ${REAL_BD} "$@"`, `:117-123`); its entire isolation is the single `cd "$FIXTURE" && bd init` at `:125` plus `export CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR="$FIXTURE"` at `:126` — which §3a measures as inert. ACCEPTANCE RUN — D2 IS APPROVED BUT NOT SHIPPABLE. Uninterrupted component tier, completed 2026-08-17T19:14:48Z,
tree at 43 paths on base 238d26b.

  Specs:      Total 46   Passed 42   Failed 4   Partial 1
  Assertions: Passed 3124   Failed 10

FAILURES:
  denylist-shared.sh        rc=1, 411s    NEW
  rubric-binding.sh         rc=1, 1156s   NEW
  upgrade-gate-compat.sh    rc=1, 271s    NEW
  installer-v3-upgrade.sh   rc=1, 210s    known 8e B carry, pre-existing

NONE of the three new ones were in QA's round-3 verification set. That set was the five specs identified as
broken plus two negative controls — correctly scoped to the finding it was checking, and blind to these.

THE TEN FAILING ASSERTIONS SPLIT INTO TWO CLASSES:

CLASS 1 — approve refuses where the spec expects a release. Same shape as R2-F1:
    denylist-C1: a matching approval record RELEASES (pre-migration control)
    denylist-D5: the pre-landing approval RELEASES (control)
    upgrade-gate 4: the full v4 path RELEASES on the upgraded tree
    upgrade-gate 5: precondition - the tree is dirty with exactly the pre-upgrade file

CLASS 2 — GRAMMAR ANCHORS. This class was never enumerated:
    upgrade-gate 4: the NEW record is in the v4 grammar (hash, reviewed_by, worktree, then the timestamp)
    upgrade-gate 4: ...whose change_set_hash is the hash of the reviewed change set
    rubric-bind-C1: precondition - the change set is byte-identical to the graded one

WHY THE DENOMINATOR DID NOT CATCH THIS, AND IT IS NOT CARELESSNESS. The denominator enumerated every
APPROVE CALL SITE. Class 2 is a different population: assertions that anchor the ORDER of tokens in the
approval record. D2 inserts design_hash= / design_verdict_hash= between worktree= and 'at', so any
assertion pinning 'hash, reviewed_by, worktree, then the timestamp' breaks WHETHER OR NOT the spec calls
approve itself. QA found exactly one instance (wtres-1.2) and the fix round routed it correctly; nobody
generalised from that one to the class.

So this is the THIRD consecutive completeness failure on this migration, and the first one WITH an
enumerated denominator in hand. The denominator was right about its own population and the population was
wrong. The correct enumeration is the UNION: every approve call site, plus every assertion that anchors
the approval-record grammar or the change-set hash.

That is the lesson worth more than the fix: an enumerated denominator is only as good as the question that
chose what to enumerate.

NEXT: establish base-vs-current for each of the three (238d26b vs worktree) before assuming causation —
installer-v3-upgrade is proof that a red here can predate the change set.

## What population this enumerates, and why (STEP ZERO discipline applied to the deliverable itself)

The acceptance run's diagnosis was right that the v2 denominator answered the wrong question — but
its own two-class split conflates two DIFFERENT failure mechanisms under "Class 2 — grammar anchors".
Verified against the actual code (reconcile_tracker, write_gate_baseline, cmd_approve's token
composition) rather than accepted at face value:

- **Population 2A — grammar/token-order anchors.** An `assert_match` (or equivalent `grep -qE`) that
  pins the LITERAL SEQUENCE of tokens in a `QA-GATE APPROVED ...` comment. D2 disturbs these because
  `cmd_approve` now composes `...worktree=<tok> ${design_field}${review_file_hash_field}${design_verdict_field}at <ts>...`
  — two new tokens inserted between worktree= and the timestamp whenever a design record exists.
- **Population 2B — change-set-hash byte-identity anchors.** An assertion (or a Stop-hook release
  check) that depends on a SPEC-LOCAL restoration of `changed-files.txt` being byte-set-identical to
  whatever was ACTUALLY bound at approve time. D2 disturbs these NOT through token order but through
  `seed_design_verdict` (folded into `seed_review_records`) writing a NEW real, tracked file —
  `docs/specs/<tid>.md` — that a restoration written before fkm.4 never learned to include. This is
  the SAME class rqer already fixed once, for `docs/reviews/<tid>-r1.json`; fkm.4 adds a second
  instance of the same file type.

`rubric-bind-C1` (cited in the acceptance run under "Class 2") is a 2B case, not a grammar anchor —
its regex-free `assert_eq "same"/"differs"` never touches token order. Filing it as "grammar" would
have sent the fix in the wrong direction (a `--no-design` bypass does nothing for 2B: the design doc
gets written by `seed_review_records` regardless of what flag the LATER approve call uses).

The union is: population 1 (every `qa-gate.sh approve` / `cmd_approve` / `bd_qa_approve` call site,
carried forward from v2) UNION population 2A UNION population 2B.

## Population 1 — re-verified, not re-derived

No changes to the v2 enumeration's A/B/D/E/F/G rows (shipped scripts, L1 specs, fixtures, MCP
surface, docs recipes) — none of this round's findings touch those. The C rows (L2 specs) are
corrected below only where this round's investigation added information.

LESSONS DEBT OWED TO P8 — text preserved here because the file write itself was uncertified.

During the 94d fix rounds a specialist appended this lesson to LESSONS.md via lessons.sh. Verifying the write was hash-neutral revealed WHY it was: claude-workflow-plugin-dpe. reconcile_tracker subtracts the gate baseline over raw porcelain lines, so a path dirty at baseline capture, then COMMITTED, then re-modified, is subtracted as pre-existing dirt. LESSONS.md was exactly that shape (baseline head=bb8fce7 carried ' M LESSONS.md'; fdfd6ce committed it; the append re-dirtied it) so the append produced added=0 and never entered the tracker. The orchestrator reverted it with git checkout --: committing a file change that no approval binds, inside the very task whose purpose is to eliminate exactly that, would be self-defeating.

THE LESSON, to be added under P8 once the write can be certified:

Comment and doc accuracy is not achievable by care; it needs a mechanical check. Evidence from ONE task (claude-workflow-plugin-94d): five false prose claims were found across successive rounds, and each was written by a round that had just corrected the previous one.
  1-3. R1-F2 / R1-F3 / the false .beads/*.jsonl sentence — corrected in the fix round.
  4. fkm.1.16 — that same round asserted the -n guard was load-bearing because set -e would abort on command-not-found; bash exempts if-condition commands from errexit. Measured false.
  5. R5-F1 / dmi — the round whose STATED THEME was comment accuracy wrote a fresh false claim (an in-repo symlink pointing out is DROPPED; measurement says TRACKED) and it reached docs/HOOKS.md, the operator-facing guide.
  And a sixth was nearly shipped IN the fix for the fifth: the first draft of the correction cited :309/:311/:313 when the author own insertion had already moved them to 339/358/359. Caught only by re-measuring.

The structural answer applied in dmi, and the one worth generalising: anchor prose on SENTINELS and IDENTIFIER NAMES, never on line numbers, and assert the anchor. This repo already has the rule for tests; the same reasoning applies to every comment that cites a location. Three residuals in this same change set are the stale-line-number class (bd-compat.sh:66 cites 121 for a call now at 391; two dated historical docs).

Related: claude-workflow-plugin-fee records that qa.md:196 carries two sentences this change set falsified — the same class again, in an agent prompt.

comments.text:
OBSERVED TWICE on claude-workflow-plugin-z9m (C0b), 2026-07-28/29.

The J21 escalation cap fired twice on a task where the code was healthy both times:

INSTANCE 1: a concurrency false-failure (see claude-workflow-plugin-1nz) — the gate
reported workflow-doctor.test.sh failing; standalone it was 94/94 and the full suite
29/29. Escalated on a spurious signal.

INSTANCE 2 (this one): the gate escalated with 'technical checks passed' and skipped
re-running them per the escalation contract. Nothing was failing. The independent
review simply had not returned yet, and each orchestrator Stop while waiting incremented
the counter.

MECHANISM: the iteration counter increments per Stop attempt, and an orchestrator
waiting on a long-running independent review necessarily Stops repeatedly. So the cost
of a THOROUGH review is charged to the same budget as defect rounds. C0b's reviews were
genuinely thorough — round 2 alone ran five mutants of the shipped installer plus a
full E2E preserve/destroy matrix — and that thoroughness is exactly what the escalation
penalised.

WHY IT MATTERS: the auto-defer rule means that if no J21 choice is recorded by the next
Stop, the gate sets qa-deferred. On this task that would have deferred the release's P0
fix while its review was still running and about to pass. The failure mode is silent and
favours haste.

SUGGESTED DIRECTIONS (not chosen; needs a design pass):
  a) Do not increment when the Stop is a pure wait — i.e. when technical checks passed
     AND the change set hash is unchanged since the previous iteration AND a review is
     in flight. That triple is cheap to evaluate and precisely characterises 'nothing
     happened since last time'.
  b) Count REVIEW ROUNDS (block records / review artifacts) rather than Stop attempts.
     Closer to J21's stated intent — 'this task has needed N attempts' — and immune to
     orchestrator polling frequency.
  c) Leave the counter and make the escalation text distinguish 'iterated N times with
     failures' from 'stopped N times, nothing failing', so the operator's J21 choice is
     informed. Cheapest, and it fixes the misleading signal without touching semantics.

Prefer (b) if the design allows: it measures the thing J21 is named for. (a) is a good
interim. Recorded as an observation with two data points rather than a proposal — the
evidence-before-fix pass should confirm the increment site before anything changes.

LIVE EVIDENCE, 2026-08-05, from qzv.1's own gate — measured, not inferred.

The gate escalated at 'iteration 3 of 3' on a task that has had exactly ONE review verdict.

  iteration-count.claude-workflow-plugin-qzv.1  = 3
  QA-GATE BLOCKED records on the task           = 1
  REVIEW-ARTIFACT records                       = 2  (QA wrote one corrupted then one clean; see its own disclosure)
  QA-GATE: entered records                      = 6

So the counter charged 3 for 1 round of review, across 6 gate entries. That is exactly the defect this task describes: the counter tracks Stop-hook passes and gate transitions, not review rounds.

The Stop that triggered the escalation says so in its own words: 'Test suite NOT re-run this loop per the escalation contract.' Under P4's fix — bump only when this Stop will actually run the suite, and escalate on max(ITER, ROUNDS) where ROUNDS counts REVIEW-ARTIFACT firstlines matching the reviewed_hash — this Stop would not have bumped, ROUNDS would be 1, and no escalation would have fired.

WHY IT COSTS SOMETHING RATHER THAN BEING COSMETIC: a spurious escalation forces a J21 decision, and the default when none is recorded by the next Stop is DEFER — which sets qa-deferred and allows the next Stop to release. So a counter that over-charges pushes a task toward automatic release-without-approval on a timer, for no reason connected to review quality. In this instance the correct choice was 'continue' and the block was real, so nothing bad happened; the point is that the mechanism steered toward defer on evidence that had nothing to do with the finding.

Also note the interaction with the 6 enters: cmd_enter calls wipe_iteration_state, so the counter is reset by each fresh cycle — meaning the 3 it reached was accumulated within a single cycle's Stops. The over-charge is per-cycle, not cumulative across the task's life.

THIRD INSTANCE, 2026-08-05, and a DISTINCT SHAPE — the escalation fired WHILE THE REVIEW WAS IN PROGRESS.

Same task (8zi), same counter, but the timing is new and worse than the two already recorded:
  - instance 1 (qzv.1): counter reached 3 with ONE completed review round.
  - instance 2 (8zi):   counter reached 3 with ZERO reviews, all three bumps caused by infrastructure (three 529s + a watchdog stall).
  - instance 3 (8zi, this one): counter reached 3 AGAIN, while the QA agent was actively mid-review and had not yet reported a verdict.

THE NEW CONSEQUENCE. The J21 default when no choice is recorded by the next Stop is DEFER, which sets qa-deferred and allows the following Stop to release. Instances 1 and 2 could release work that had been reviewed once, or never. Instance 3 can release work whose review IS RUNNING — the reviewer is still reading, has written no artifact, and the gate is already steering toward allowing the Stop. The race is: whichever finishes first, the counter or the reviewer, decides whether the review's verdict matters.

That is the strongest argument yet for P4's fix, and it sharpens the fix's requirement. It is not enough to bump only when the Stop runs the suite. The escalation predicate should also not fire while a review is demonstrably in progress — and there IS a signal for that: qa-gate-entered is set with a cycle record written and no REVIEW-ARTIFACT yet for the current reviewed_hash. That state means 'a reviewer has claimed this cycle and not yet reported', and escalating in it is never useful.

Concretely, for whoever implements P4: escalate on max(ITER, ROUNDS) as planned, but ALSO suppress escalation entirely when a cycle is open with zero artifacts against the current hash. In that state there is nothing to escalate about — no reviewer has disagreed with anything, because no reviewer has spoken.

Recorded choose continue for the third time on this task. Three spurious escalations in one session, on two tasks, none caused by a finding.

PRIORITY RAISED P3 -> P1 and the 1nz EDGE RECUT, 2026-08-06, orchestrator.

PRIORITY. Filed 2026-07-29 as P3 on the theory that a miscounted iteration is bookkeeping. Three live instances in one session say otherwise, and all three are recorded above with measurements. The decisive one: the J21 default when no choice is recorded by the next Stop is DEFER, which sets qa-deferred and allows the following Stop to RELEASE. So an over-counting counter steers work toward release-without-approval on a timer, driven by nothing connected to review quality. Instance 3 fired while the reviewer was actively mid-review. That is a release-path defect wearing bookkeeping's clothes, which is the same misclassification QA made on qzv.3 (rated low on the routes enumerated rather than the routes that exist) and corrected.

THE 1nz EDGE. The plan's correction 4 states it and I confirm it from the code: 1nz does not really block 2ty. The edge encodes 'lock the iteration counter against concurrent writers first', but the fix is not to make the counter safe to share — it is to STOP THE COUNTER BEING AUTHORITATIVE. Escalating on max(ITER, ROUNDS), where ROUNDS counts REVIEW-ARTIFACT records against the current reviewed_hash, means a mis-shared counter can no longer force an escalation on its own. Build the lock first and you build something 2ty then deletes. Recorded here because the mechanical edge removal may not have taken.

WHAT THE THREE INSTANCES ADD TO THE PLANNED FIX, beyond 'bump only when the Stop runs the suite':
  1. SUPPRESS escalation entirely while a cycle is open with ZERO artifacts against the current hash. That state means a reviewer has claimed the cycle and not yet spoken; escalating there is never useful because nobody has disagreed with anything.
  2. ROUNDS must anchor on the firstline grammar ^REVIEW-ARTIFACT v1, never a substring. QA handed us the regression case: before any artifact existed on 8zi, grep -c 'REVIEW-ARTIFACT' returned 1, and the hit was prose inside QA's own note reading 'zero REVIEW-ARTIFACT firstlines'. A leg seeding a task whose only mention is prose must measure 0. The same shape applies to ^RUBRIC [0-9]+ iteration and QA-GATE BLOCKED.
  3. The counter is reset by cmd_enter's wipe_iteration_state, so the over-count accumulates WITHIN a cycle, not across a task's life. Any fix must be correct per-cycle.

ORCHESTRATOR CORRECTION, 2026-08-06 — PART OF MY OWN EVIDENCE ON THIS TASK WAS FALSE. Caught by the P4 implementer, verified by me against HEAD before this change.

WHAT I WROTE, twice, in the comments above: that the escalating Stop 'says so in its own words: Test suite NOT re-run this loop per the escalation contract — the counter charged for a Stop that ran nothing.'

THAT READOUT WAS LYING, and not about my instances specifically — about every cap-hit Stop. Verified against HEAD (22d053e):
  - verify-before-stop.sh:2439, the QA-required escalated path, printed 'Test suite NOT re-run this loop per the escalation contract' UNCONDITIONALLY.
  - The sibling escalation path ten lines earlier correctly branched on [ "$SUITE_REUSED" = "true" ].
  - mark_escalation_if_capped sets QA_ESCALATED=true at :1666, and is called at :1675 and :2383 — i.e. WITHIN the same Stop that just ran the suite.
So on the Stop that HITS the cap, the suite ran, the escalation was marked, and the message then announced that the suite had not run. False on exactly the Stop an operator is most likely to read it.

WHAT SURVIVES AND WHAT DOES NOT:
  - The defect is REAL and the three instances stand. Every one was established by direct measurement — the iteration-count.<tid> file contents, and anchored counts of REVIEW-ARTIFACT / QA-GATE BLOCKED firstlines. None of those depended on the readout.
  - What does NOT survive is the corroboration. I offered the hook's own sentence as independent confirmation that the counter charged for a Stop that ran nothing. It was not independent and it was not confirmation; it was a hardcoded string. On the cap-hit Stop the suite HAD run.

WHY I AM RECORDING THIS RATHER THAN QUIETLY DROPPING IT: I used a readout as evidence without checking whether the readout was true. That is the exact error this session has catalogued eighteen times in other people's code and my own — something claimed a thing that nothing checked. Nineteenth instance, mine, on the task whose whole subject is a mechanism reporting something it did not establish. Anyone auditing 2ty later would otherwise find a citation that does not hold and have no way to tell which parts of the case were measured.

FIXED IN P4: the wording now branches on SUITE_REUSED, so the sentence is only printed when the suite genuinely was reused.

METHOD NOTE, for the next agent tempted to quote a tool's own output: a message emitted by the thing under investigation is a claim by that thing, not an observation about it. If it is worth citing, verify the branch that produces it.

R1-F1 (HIGH) — verify-before-stop.sh:1758-1763, emitted at :2045 and :2813.
The suppression paragraph is built in the ESCALATION-BASIS region, which runs BEFORE the suite and therefore cannot consult FAILED_CHECKS. Both emission sites print it verbatim. Reproduced three times on the shipped tree (L2 fixture, real gate, real bd):

I recorded a correction on 8zi with an explicit mechanical rule:

  'When a task id appears in a close reason or commit message, it must be CAPTURED FROM THE CREATE'S OWN OUTPUT, never written in advance. bd create echoes the allocated id; use that value. Writing an id you expect to be allocated is a PREDICTION, and this session has recorded fifteen cases of predictions being reported as measurements.'

I then wrote '8gx' in advance, in the same command that created the task, exactly as before.

WHY I AM RECORDING RATHER THAN QUIETLY FIXING IT. Twenty-first instance of the family, and the most instructive one available, because it isolates the variable: I had identified the pattern, written the rule, and stated the mechanism. None of that prevented the recurrence. The failing step is not knowing the rule; it is that composing a close reason and running a create are a single motion, and the id is needed in the sentence before it exists. The specialist put this better than I have, about itself, on this very task: 'the failure is not sloppiness about facts, it is writing the sentence at the moment the intention is fresh instead of at the moment the evidence is.'

THE STRUCTURAL ANSWER, which is what I should have taken the first time: do not write the sentence and create the record in one motion. Create first, capture the id, then compose. That is the same discipline the P4 specialist used when it wrote QA's reproductions as test legs BEFORE fixing — so the claim and the evidence are produced at the same moment rather than the claim first.

After the @devops subagent finished, the working tree showed 14 modified paths but
.claude/.qa-tracking/changed-files.txt held only 9 (excluding .beads/issues.jsonl,
which verify-before-stop classifies separately as beads-state). Four files were
modified on disk and absent from the tracker:

  .claude/tests/component/specs/installer-manifest-parity.sh
  .claude/tests/component/specs/installer-mcp-config.sh
  .claude/tests/component/specs/installer-v3-upgrade.sh
  .claude/tests/component/specs/upgrade-gate-compat.sh

WHY THIS IS A GATE-INTEGRITY BUG, NOT AN ANNOYANCE: change_set_hash is computed over
the denylist-filtered CHANGED-FILES.TXT list, not over git status. So an approval bound
to that hash certifies a SMALLER set than the diff actually being shipped. The four
missing files were not incidental — they carry the decision to export
CWP_SKIP_MCP_DEPS=1 / CWP_SKIP_VERIFY=1 into four installer specs, i.e. exactly the kind
of change a reviewer must see, because it narrows what those specs exercise.

The failure is silent in both directions: nothing warns that the tracker under-covers,
and a reviewer who takes the impact report as the file list (which the QA prompt
explicitly instructs) reviews only what was tracked. The gate would then have recorded
a correctly-formed, change-set-bound approval over an incomplete change set.

CORRECTION APPLIED THIS CYCLE (manual, and the fact that it had to be manual is part of
the report): appended the four absolute paths to changed-files.txt and regenerated the
impact report. Hash moved a835e8c6 (9 files) -> 1dad1479 (13 files) and review proceeded
against the full set.

RELATION TO EXISTING LESSONS: LESSONS.md:35 already records that helper-REWRITTEN files
never land in changed-files.txt. This is the same failure with a different cause — these
were ordinary Edit calls from a subagent, not helper rewrites. C0a's subagent edits DID
land (17 files tracked), so it is not simply 'subagent edits are never tracked'. The
discriminating question for whoever picks this up: what distinguishes the tracked edits
from the untracked ones in the same session? Candidates worth checking first — whether
the PostToolUse hook fires for every subagent tool call or drops some under
concurrency/nesting; whether post-edit.sh's append raced (it has no flock on macOS, per
LESSONS, and C0b ran long); and whether an Edit that follows a Read of a file already
open in another agent's context takes a different path.

SUGGESTED MITIGATION regardless of root cause: have qa-gate.sh enter (or approve) diff
the tracker against  M .beads/issues.jsonl
 M .claude/mcp/bd-mcp/README.md

 M .claude/scripts/tests/installer-flags.test.sh

Third confirmed recurrence, measured during the C0c independent QA review (`claude-workflow-plugin-20e`), plus a **second, opposite** failure mode not yet captured here.

**Under-coverage.** At review time `changed-files.txt` held **10** paths; `git status --porcelain` held **19**. Absent from the tracker:

```
.beads/issues.jsonl
.claude/tests/e2e/fixtures/go-cli-refactor/.claude/scripts/session-start.sh
.claude/tests/e2e/fixtures/monorepo-frontend-only/.claude/scripts/session-start.sh
.claude/tests/e2e/fixtures/multi-domain-signup/.claude/scripts/session-start.sh
.claude/tests/e2e/fixtures/node-react-auth/.claude/scripts/session-start.sh
.claude/tests/e2e/fixtures/python-django-bug/.claude/scripts/session-start.sh
.claude/tests/e2e/fixtures/qa-block-recovery/.claude/scripts/session-start.sh
.claude/tests/e2e/fixtures/rubric-revision-loop/.claude/scripts/session-start.sh
LESSONS.md
```

The seven fixture copies are written by `make sync-fixtures` (a Bash-tool `cp`, not a Write/Edit call), and `LESSONS.md` by `lessons.sh add` — so the pattern is specifically **script-mediated writes**, not subagent edits. Each of those seven files carries the same 448-line diff as the canonical script, so the mechanical impact report certified 10 of the 19 genuinely-changed paths and the `change_set_hash` bound the smaller set.

**Over-coverage (new, opposite direction).** The post-edit recorder also captured `/tmp/enc-diff.sh` — a QA scratch file **outside the repo**, created with the Write tool. That single entry shifted `change_set_hash` from `a950fa6b…` to `cb000516…`, which made `qa-gate.sh approve` refuse the (correct) impact report as stale. So the recorder has no out-of-repo filter, and any agent that writes a temp file with Write/Edit silently invalidates the gate's hash.

Mitigation used this cycle: I reviewed all nine uncovered paths from `git status` instead (the seven fixture copies verified byte-identical to canonical by `sha256`, the `LESSONS.md` diff read), removed the `/tmp` line, and regenerated the report.

Suggested acceptance additions: (1) record script-mediated writes, or reconcile `changed-files.txt` against `git status --porcelain` at `qa-gate.sh enter`; (2) drop paths outside `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` at record time.

## Coupling assessment: does P1 discharge `claude-workflow-plugin-fkm.1.2`?

**Verdict: PARTIAL. P1 discharges the consequence for UNCOMMITTED work and leaves two residuals. fkm.1.2 stays filed. Not fixed here, per instruction.**

Measured, not reasoned. I reproduced the finding's exact sequence in two legs that differ in ONE variable — whether the cycle's work was committed before the session boundary — and read the impact report's own `files` count and `change_set_hash`.

### Leg 1 — work UNCOMMITTED (the observed 2026-08-03 03:20 incident): DISCHARGED

```
after enter (pre-boundary):   tracker=1 path   report files=1   hash=06381ae28bc3
session-start.sh runs:        tracker exists? NO        (the rm -f still happens)
hash right now:               e3b0c44298fc              <-- the empty-set hash, the finding's symptom
after re-enter:               tracker=1 path   report files=1   hash=06381ae28bc3
```

The reconcile at `enter` repopulates from `git status` before `generate_impact_report`, and the
report binds a hash **byte-identical to the pre-boundary one**. The hollow binding the finding
describes does not occur. Its recovery is no longer luck (the incident recovered only because a
stale grading packet happened to contain the 79-path list) — it is mechanical.

### Leg 2 — work COMMITTED before the boundary: NOT discharged

```
pre-boundary report:  files=1  hash=3bf9c86373f0
work committed:       git status --porcelain is now EMPTY
session-start.sh:     tracker exists? NO
post-boundary report: files=0  hash=e3b0c44298fc      <-- still the empty-set hash over 0 files
approve --no-review:  status=approved                  <-- and approve does NOT refuse
bound record hash:    e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855
```

`git status` is the reconciler's only source, and committed work is invisible to it. So the
approval binds the empty set over zero files and the gate accepts it, exactly as the finding
describes. (`--no-review` was used only to isolate the impact gate from the independent-review
gate; it is not part of the claim.)

### The two residuals, stated separately

1. **Half (a) is untouched and is wrong independently of recoverability.** `session-start.sh:273`
   still `rm -f`s `changed-files.txt` while a cycle is in flight — visible in BOTH legs above
   ("tracker exists? NO"). P1 makes the damage *usually* repairable; it does not stop the
   destruction. Destroying an in-flight cycle's state and then reconstructing an approximation of
   it from a different source is not the same as not destroying it, and leg 2 is the case where
   the reconstruction is empty.

2. **Half (b) survives in a narrowed form.** The finding asks approve to refuse or warn "when the
   change set is empty while git shows un-baselined dirt". After P1 that exact conjunction is
   structurally unreachable at `enter`/Stop/`approve` — the reconcile fills the tracker from that
   very dirt. What remains is the case with no un-baselined dirt to reconcile: an empty change set
   because the work is in HEAD. Nothing in the gate distinguishes "legitimately nothing changed"
   from "the tracker was destroyed and the evidence was committed", because both present as an
   empty tracker plus a clean tree. Closing it needs a signal the gate does not currently have —
   the obvious candidate being for `session-start` to preserve or archive the tracker mid-cycle
   (half (a)) rather than for `approve` to guess.

### Recommendation

Keep fkm.1.2 open, with its priority unchanged. Its scope narrows to: (a) `session-start` must not
destroy an in-flight cycle's tracker — now the primary fix, since P1 has absorbed the recoverable
part of the consequence and left the unrecoverable part exposed; and (b) the residual empty-set
binding for committed work, which is downstream of (a).

Reproduction script for both legs: `probe-fkm112.sh`, session scratchpad (throwaway; a denylisted
path, so it never entered any change set). It is ~90 lines and reconstructs the fixture from the
canonical scripts, so it is cheap to re-derive if wanted.

<!-- BD-MCP-META: {"kind":"completion-contract-addendum","source":"devops-agent","contract":"F7","phase":"P1","seq":1,"status":"in-progress"} -->
## F7 ADDENDUM 1 — L2 full-suite findings (written incrementally; two stalls cost the attestation twice)

State: **5 L2 specs failed the full suite; 1 fixed and confirmed, 4 open.** Root cause identified
for 4 of 5. Two coordinator hypotheses tested — **both refuted, with evidence.** No production
defect found so far; one production question closed by code reading, one still open.

### The single root cause behind 4 of the 5 specs

A component fixture that (a) is a git repo and (b) has git-visible dirt that is **not in a gate
baseline** now has that dirt correctly folded into the change set by `reconcile-tracker`. Three
ways a spec gets into that state: no `.gitignore` for the harness's own instrumentation, no gate
baseline ever captured, or a baseline the spec *deliberately deletes* mid-cycle.

Every failing assertion is downstream of that, in one of three shapes:
- a hash that moved between `enter` and `approve` (`qa-gate-baseline` A, `denylist-shared` C4, `approve-idempotency` E1)
- a change set that is no longer doc-only (`verify-review-discipline` D4, `verify-before-stop` F1)
- a delta that is no longer a subset of an approved set (`worktree-approval-resolution`)

**This is the reconciler reporting the truth about those trees, not misbehaving.** The evidence:
in every case the block reason is `LABEL_WITHOUT_RECORD` or plain `QA approval required` — my
reconcile's own block text ("the change-set tracker could not be reconciled against git") appears
**nowhere**. `reconcile_tracker` returned 0 every time.

### Hypothesis 1 — "F1 vs fail-closed reconcile is a design conflict, not shippable": REFUTED

There is no conflict. No reconcile block fired anywhere. I measured F1 in a real-shaped session
(committed clean tree, `session-start` baseline, doc-only edit through the Write tool), three legs
with the baseline as the only variable:

```
LEG A  doc-only edit, baseline present            -> ALLOW, F1 record written
                                                     (reviewed_by=none, worktree token intact)
LEG B  + ONE non-doc file dirtied, un-baselined   -> block   (correct: the set is mixed)
LEG C  that same non-doc dirt BASELINED           -> ALLOW again
```

F1 is alive in production. What changed is that F1 can no longer be reached by *mis-classifying* an
under-covering change set as doc-only: previously a modified `.gitignore` that the tracker missed
was invisible, so F1 auto-approved a set that contained it. That is the coverage 94d exists to add,
and it is strictly stricter, never looser.

### Hypothesis 2 — "`qa-gate-baseline` is staleness from my `write_gate_baseline` fix": REFUTED

Not staleness, and not my empty-snapshot fix. The spec deliberately does `rm -f "$BASELINE"`
between `enter` and `approve` to isolate what *approve* writes. That makes **all** tree dirt
un-baselined, so the reconcile folds it in and approve refuses. Captured envelope:

```
error_key: impact_report_stale
  recorded: e3b0c44298fc…  (the EMPTY SET — the spec never seeds the tracker,
                            so enter's report bound nothing)
  current:  d790f4bb0aa7…  (the reconcile folded in the now-un-baselined dirt)
```

The baseline file is absent afterwards only because approve never reached the refresh. The
assertions still pin the correct contract; the spec needs its impact report regenerated after it
perturbs baseline state. That is the fix, and it is a spec change *required by a deliberate
behaviour change* — recorded here as such.

### Hypothesis 3 (coordinator's second) — "`.beads/issues.jsonl` folds in after bd work, so F1 is dead in production": REFUTED

Measured twice, including a probe mirroring the failing spec's construction exactly (git init, `add
-A`, commit, then the stub replacement):

```
baseline (arrival):      T .claude/scripts/detect-stack.sh
bd create + comments add + label add
git status AFTER:        T .claude/scripts/detect-stack.sh
                        ?? .claude/.qa-tracking/
reconcile:              added=0
tracker:                docs/notes.md          <- unchanged, still doc-only
grep -c issues.jsonl tracker: 0
```

`.beads/issues.jsonl` never appears in `git status` and never reaches the tracker. Two independent
reasons: bd 1.1.2 rewrites `interactions.jsonl` on every call but `issues.jsonl` **only on an
explicit export** (measured earlier, and the reason I excluded only `interactions.jsonl`), and
`bd init` adds `.beads/` to `.git/info/exclude` (its own `.beads/.gitignore` names that
fork-protection mechanism).

**Production question 2, answered by code reading:** `session-start.sh` captures the baseline in the
MIDDLE of its bd work — after `bd doctor --quiet`, before `bd prime` / `bd blocked` / `bd list`. So
bd calls do land after the capture. That would be a production hole **if** those calls dirtied a
non-denylisted tracked file; they do not, because they are reads and because `issues.jsonl` only
moves on export. So no hole from that path. The residual risk is narrower and worth stating: an
explicit `bd export` / `beads-ledger.sh` run mid-cycle *would* dirty `issues.jsonl` after the
baseline and fold it into the change set. That is correct behaviour (the ledger is a committed
deliverable) but it does mean such a cycle stops being doc-only. Not a defect; a documented
consequence.

### Confirmed fixed

- **`verify-before-stop` 77/1 -> 78/0.** `baseline_incidental_dirt "$FIXTURE"` before the F1 case.
  Coordinator-verified.

### New shared helper

`baseline_incidental_dirt <root>` in `.claude/tests/component/lib/fixture.sh` — a pure addition,
opt-in, no other spec affected. It runs `qa-gate.sh baseline-capture --by session-start
--exclude-tracked`, i.e. "this fixture's arrival dirt was already here", which is the state
`session-start.sh` produces on every real session. `--exclude-tracked` is load-bearing: the spec's
SUBJECT (whatever the tracker names) is never baselined and stays gated.

### Still open, with the next measurement named

- **`verify-review-discipline` 18/6.** The helper is in place at the right point and my
  reconstruction of D4 does NOT reproduce the failure (reconcile adds 0, set stays doc-only). So the
  cause is state left by the EARLIER D-section cases, not the fixture's arrival state. Next
  measurement: truncate a copy of the spec after D4 and dump the tracker, `git status` and the Stop
  reason at that exact point — the technique that identified `qa-gate-baseline`'s cause in one run.
  Note D4's three failures are ONE cause (the two empty-haystack assertions are downstream of the
  block).
- **`worktree-approval-resolution` 50/15** — numbers obtained (the coordinator's two runs outran
  their budget; a targeted run completed). Signature is uniform: `current change-set hash is … but
  no QA-GATE APPROVED record … carries a matching change_set_hash`, i.e. the primary checkout's
  un-baselined dirt breaks `wtres_delta_is_subset`. Same class, needs the helper in the primary
  checkout before each bridge Stop.
- **`qa-gate-baseline` 19/4** — cause established above; fix is to regenerate the impact report
  after the deliberate `rm -f "$BASELINE"`.
- `installer-v3-upgrade` — untouched known carry (8e leg B), resolves at the D7 manifest freeze.

### Unchanged commitments

The reconcile has NOT been weakened and will not be to make a test pass. Nothing in this addendum
changes `reconcile_tracker`'s contract. If a genuine production conflict emerges I will state the
trade-off and stop rather than absorb it.

## F7 ADDENDUM 2 — PRODUCTION DEFECT I INTRODUCED. F1 *is* dead once bd has been touched.

**The coordinator was right about the consequence and wrong about the mechanism. I was wrong to
close the question on the mechanism alone.** Recording before I touch code.

### What I measured at the real D4 point

```
git status:   M .beads/interactions.jsonl
              T .claude/scripts/detect-stack.sh
             ?? .claude/.qa-tracking/
baseline:     T .claude/scripts/detect-stack.sh
             ?? .claude/.qa-tracking/
tracker:     docs/notes.md          <- reconcile added 0. The tracker is PRISTINE.
block:       "1 file(s) changed ... Files changed: docs/notes.md"
current-task: set   gate status: not-entered   qa-gate.sh: executable
tracker AFTER the Stop: docs/notes.md   <- F1 never ran (it deletes the tracker)
```

Every precondition F1 needs is satisfied, the change set it reports is a single doc file, and it
still blocked. So `FASTPATH_CLASS` was not `doc-only` — while `CHANGE_COUNT` said 1 and named only
`docs/notes.md`.

### The mechanism

Those two numbers come from **different sources**, and after my change they disagree:

- `CHANGE_COUNT` / `Files changed:` / the J18 payload / **`change_set_hash`** read the TRACKER.
- `FASTPATH_CLASS` / `DOC_ONLY` / `CODE_CHANGES_DETECTED` read `reviewable_changes()` — which I
  turned into a **UNION** of the tracker and the baseline-relative git walk.

`comm -23` leaves ` M .beads/interactions.jsonl` (dirty from bd work, not in the baseline). The git
half emits it, `is_tracked_change` keeps it (`.beads/*.jsonl` is deliberately NOT denylisted), so
`ALL_CHANGED_FILES = {docs/notes.md, .beads/interactions.jsonl}` -> `DOC_ONLY=false` -> no fast
path -> block. Meanwhile `reconcile_tracker` **correctly excluded** that same path from the tracker
under my own "paths the workflow itself rewrites" rule.

**So I built the exact defect the shared denylist exists to prevent: the hash and the gate disagree
about what "the changes" are.** The tracker excludes `interactions.jsonl`; the detector includes it.
One rule, applied in one of the two places that must agree.

### Why this is production, not fixtures

`bd` rewrites `.beads/interactions.jsonl` on **every** invocation, including the gate's own
`add_comment` and `label add`. So in any repo where that file is not already baselined, the first bd
write of a cycle puts it in `ALL_CHANGED_FILES` and **no change set is ever doc-only again** — every
documentation-only Stop demands a full QA round. This live repo survives only because
`interactions.jsonl` happens to be in `gate-baseline` already; that is the accident of ordering the
coordinator named, and it is real.

My earlier refutation measured the TRACKER (correct: `issues.jsonl` never lands there) and stopped.
The union was the half I did not check. That was the error.

### The fix I am about to make — not a weakening of the reconcile

Make the two halves agree by sharing the ONE rule, exactly as the denylist consolidation did:

1. `workflow-denylist.sh` gains `WORKFLOW_SELF_WRITTEN_REGEX` + `workflow_self_written <path>` — a
   SEPARATE predicate, not folded into `WORKFLOW_DENYLIST_REGEX`. Members unchanged:
   `.claude/.qa-tracking/**` and `.beads/interactions.jsonl`.
2. `reconcile_tracker` consults it instead of its inline `case` (removing the duplicate).
3. `reviewable_changes()`'s git half consults it too.

Deliberately NOT folded into the denylist regex: that would drop these paths from the change set
entirely and flip a beads-only change set from `beads-state` fast-path (releases WITH a gate record)
to `empty` (releases with none) — a classification change llh.3 made deliberately in the other
direction. This keeps denylist semantics untouched and only stops the detector contradicting the
hash. The reconciler's contract is unchanged; nothing becomes less visible than it is today, and
`change_set_hash` covers exactly what it covered an hour ago.

### Consequence for the four open specs

`verify-review-discipline`'s six failures are all downstream of this, so the fix is code, not
fixture — I was about to paper over a production hole in a spec, which is what the instruction to
establish the mechanism first prevented. `worktree-approval-resolution` and `qa-gate-baseline` are
still the fixture/staleness classes from addendum 1 and are unaffected by this.

## F7 ADDENDUM 4 — the last spec: both hypotheses ruled OUT by measurement, then one fix

### Rule-out 1: `reconcile_tracker` resolves the prefix CORRECTLY inside a linked worktree

Not a reconciler bug. Real `git worktree add`, `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` = the worktree:

```
PROJECT_DIR (W)      = /var/folders/.../wtpfx-wt.../wt-feature
show-toplevel from W = /private/var/folders/.../wtpfx-wt.../wt-feature
canon(W)             = /private/var/folders/.../wtpfx-wt.../wt-feature
porcelain in W:      ?? src/wonly.ts
reconcile:           +1 path
tracker:             /var/folders/.../wt-feature/src/wonly.ts     <- EXISTS on disk
```

`canon($PROJECT_DIR)` equals `canon(--show-toplevel)` in a linked worktree, so the prefix is
`$PROJECT_DIR` — the worktree's OWN root, in the unresolved spelling post-edit would have used, not
the primary's. The `pwd -P` comparison is doing exactly the job it was written for. This was the one
candidate that would have been unfixable in a spec.

### Rule-out 2: the fail-closed Stop block does NOT pre-empt section 9c

`reconcile-tracker` needs `git` and `workflow-denylist.sh`; it never invokes `impact-report.sh`. With
`impact-report.sh` deliberately deleted it still returns **rc 0, ok:true**. So 9c's causation probe
("removing it blocks, restoring it releases") still observes the thing it was written to observe, and
no META control is unsound for that reason.

### The fix: one insertion point, in the spec's own pre-Stop helper

All five failures are in later sections that keep writing instrumentation into the PRIMARY's
`.claude/scripts/` after my single arrival-state capture — section 8's stripped hook, section 9's
`qa-gate-notoken.sh`, section 9c's removal and restoration of `impact-report.sh`. Each is real,
git-visible, un-baselined dirt that `reconcile-tracker` correctly folds into the primary's change
set; the delta then stops being a subset of what the worktree's approval covered,
`wtres_delta_is_subset` returns 1, and every RELEASE assertion collapses.

`restage()` is the shared helper every section calls before driving a Stop, and it touches only the
primary's tracker and current-task — so `baseline_incidental_dirt "$PRIM"` at its END covers all five
at once. Placed AFTER the tracker is seeded so `--exclude-tracked` protects that case's SUBJECT: the
paths just staged are never baselined and stay gated. The WORKTREE's baseline is untouched, so 5.1
("new dirt in the worktree AFTER approve BLOCKS") and 5.4 ("a worktree with NO gate-baseline cannot
prove absence of drift") still measure what they always did. Grepped first: no assertion anywhere in
that spec reads the primary's baseline provenance or asserts its absence.

The reverted `.gitignore` attempt is left in the file as a comment with its measurement (15 -> 37
failures, because `wtres-0.4` needs the hook surface COMMITTED for `git worktree add` to materialise
it), so the next person does not repeat it.

## F7 revision — llm_observations and context_coverage (the two mandatory free-form fields)

### llm_observations

**The rule ran ~20 times live this session and dropped nothing.** Every Edit I made
after the region landed went through it with `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` = the real repo.
`.claude/.qa-tracking/sync-errors.log` is still **0 bytes, mtime 2026-08-02** — zero
false drops on a real workload, which is the measurement I would have wanted from
whoever shipped rule 2. It is not proof of no false positives; it is one clean
sample of the only kind of session this hook sees.

**Two of my own edge probes came back wrong and BOTH were probe artifacts, not
bugs.** `root=/` reported "skipped" and a nonexistent-root path reported "skipped".
In both legs I had varied `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` while still reading the tracker under
the *original* root — the hook had written to the tracker under the NEW root, which
is where it belongs. Re-measured correctly: the nonexistent-root path is tracked with
rc=0 and no containment log (the logical root is still usable), and the `/` branch
returns "inside" when the two functions are extracted and unit-driven. I am recording
this because the first result looked exactly like a real bug in new code, and the
difference was entirely in my instrumentation.

**Residual 1 — a stale line citation my change caused, in a file I may not touch.**
`.claude/tests/component/specs/bd-compat.sh:66` cites `post-edit.sh:121` for the
`bd comments add` call site; that call is now at **:391**. bd-compat.sh is NOT in the
change set, so correcting it would move the graded hash. Left deliberately, recorded
here for the next hash-moving window. It is a locator in a call-site inventory, not a
behavioural claim.

**Residual 2 — the agent prompts now over-warn, in the safe direction.** `qa.md` 3a
and the three specialist prompts (including the devops prompt I ran under) tell agents
that "a probe you Write to an absolute path ... enters `changed-files.txt`, the
change-set hash, and the Stop gate". After fkm.1.15 that is false for out-of-repo
paths — the probe is dropped and logged instead. The guidance is still worth
following (an in-repo scratch file DOES enter the change set, and the log line is
noise nobody needs), so the staleness is conservative rather than dangerous. The
prompts are not in the change set; correcting them would move the hash. Recommend a
follow-up that rewrites those paragraphs to say "the mechanism now drops it and logs
it; write to the scratchpad so there is nothing to log".

**Residual 3 — `docs/plans/v3-upgrade.md` and `docs/RELEASE_AUDIT.md` also carry
`post-edit.sh:<line>` citations that my insertion invalidated.** Both are dated
historical records (RELEASE_AUDIT explicitly says "read 2026-06-13"), neither is in
the change set, and I judged a dated observation to be a different kind of artefact
from a live claim. Not fixed, disclosed.

**New mutable surface for the next mutation sweep.** The containment region adds
comparison operators the sweep will mutate: the `-n`/`-z` root guards, `[ "$r" = "/" ]`,
the `"$r"|"$r"/*` case, and `${out%/*}` in the normaliser. Section 13 was written to
kill the ones with a behavioural consequence — the separator boundary (13b sibling
leg), the normalisation (13b `..` leg), the log (13d) — but I have NOT run a sweep
against the new region, so I cannot claim mutation coverage of it.

**One thing I deliberately did not do, and it is the same call rule 2 made.** I did
not add containment to `reconcile_tracker`, because it cannot produce an out-of-project
path — `git status --porcelain` is repo-scoped by construction. If a future change ever
teaches the reconciler to walk a second checkout, that reasoning expires and the rule
needs a second applier plus the structural guard in `denylist-source.test.sh` that rule
2 has. The code says so at the decision site.

**A suspicion I could not close.** `verify-before-stop.sh`'s `wtres_no_drift_in`
(QA R1-F4, out of scope here) is a fourth walk over tree state; I did not check whether
it can be handed an out-of-repo path now that the writer filters them. It reads a
worktree's own git view, so I expect not, but I did not verify and it is not in my scope.

### context_coverage

**Read, to ground this change.** The grader's full iteration-1 verdict (all 16
criterion justifications and three `required_fixes`, recovered from the grader
subagent's own transcript — the short `RUBRIC 2 iteration 1` record on the task carries
only the verdict and the failed criteria); QA's round-4 `qa-plan` (doc v1 at
2026-08-04T04:24, the R3-F1/R3-F2 text verbatim); the 2026-07-29 15:52 bug report's

`.claude/scripts/post-edit.sh` complete; `workflow-denylist.sh` complete;
`.claude/tests/component/specs/post-edit.sh` complete; `specs/denylist-shared.sh`
helpers (:150-260) and sections A, B4-B5, D, E in full;
`.claude/scripts/tests/denylist-source.test.sh` complete; `docs/HOOKS.md` PostToolUse
+ shared-denylist + second-rule sections (:320-660); `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` PostToolUse
(:125-175); `impact-report.sh`'s out-of-project handling (:495-505, which is where the
`ok:false` claim in my code comment comes from); `verify-before-stop.sh:447-453` for the
sibling guard shape; `gate-baseline-v2.sh:505-565`; the contemporaneous fkm.1.12 record
at 2026-08-03T23:50:47Z and the RESOLVED R2-F4 / R2-F2 records at 02:47, which is how I
established the causal order rather than relaying the grader's; and the installed Claude
Code binary's NotebookEdit schema and hook-payload construction.

**Deliberately NOT read, with reasons.** The e2e TypeScript harness and its specs — the
fixture copies of both changed scripts are denylisted, drift is 0 by sha256, and the
instruction was not to run `test-e2e-unit`; the mutation harness under
`.claude/tests/mutation/` — no sweep this round (see the residual above); `qa-gate.sh`'s

resolution is reachable in production at all. Every leg that exercises it here is
macOS-shaped (`/var/folders` vs `/private/var/folders`); on a Linux CI runner the

unchanged. Then `impact_of` on both new symbols: `_pe_norm` and `_pe_within` are

Measured false for every path carrying a gate-baseline entry — **154 of 154**.
`comm -23` runs over raw porcelain lines, which are not content-addressed, so a
Bash write to an already-baselined path leaves `" M path"` byte-identical and is
subtracted as pre-existing dirt. Reproduced in an isolated git repo: baseline
`" M tracked.txt"`, one further append, current `" M tracked.txt"`, `comm -23`
survivors **0**, `git diff --numstat` 2 added lines. **No commit is required** —
strictly wider than `dpe`, which frames the hole as needing a mid-cycle commit.

Already falsified by an event inside this cycle: the `lessons.sh` append is a
Bash-mediated write that produced `added=0` and never entered the change set,
which is why the orchestrator reverted it. And the failure is silent —
reconcile-tracker returns `ok:true`, "already covers every reviewable git-visible
path", `added=0`.

**Why HIGH when I held R5-F1 at medium in the same file.** R5-F1's error direction
was over-tracking, the region's own fail-closed side. This one runs the other way:
it asserts coverage that does not exist, in the under-coverage direction 94d
exists to close, about the gate's own integrity, and it is the stated justification
for not re-scoping `prevent-orchestrator-edits.sh` after the `5535a6d` revert. An
operator accepting the Bash write vector as a residual is relying on this sentence.

The authoritative section does not rescue it. "The tracker reconcile" opens with
"the reason the change-set hash can be trusted" and names this exact class (Bash
redirect, `cp`, `mv`, `sed -i`, generator scripts) as what it repairs. Its "Known
limits, named rather than latent" bullet names the enabling mechanism — "the
baseline subtracts at line granularity" — but scopes it to the collapsed `?? dir/`
case, and its commit bullet states the opposite direction. Neither tells a reader
that a Bash write to an actively-worked path silently misses the change set.

**Fix is hash-neutral** — `docs/HOOKS.md` is already path 26 of 26, exactly as the
R5-F1 correction was. This blocks on the disclosure; `dpe` stays deferred.

### The `dmi` correction: verified, not accepted

**The two-mechanism distinction is REAL.** This was the orchestrator's explicit ask.
Direct dirname measurement on a scratch tree: `dirlink/g.ts` resolves to the OUT
tree (outside the root), `filelink.ts` resolves to the root itself. Then the
behavioural confirmation, one variable — mutant **M1**, guard
`if ! _pe_within "$_PE_CANDIDATE"` -> `if true`, retry body byte-identical,
apply confirmed by diff and `bash -n`:

| shape | canonical | M1 (retry forced to run) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| in-project control | TRACKED | TRACKED |
| plain outside control | dropped | dropped |
| in-repo DIR symlink out | TRACKED | **dropped** |
| in-repo FILE symlink out | TRACKED | **TRACKED** |
| outside symlink -> IN | TRACKED | TRACKED |

That is the asymmetry, measured: the directory shape would have been dropped had
the retry run; the file shape would have been kept regardless. Both controls hold.

**13e's two in-repo legs are not vacuous.** I built and ran **E2** myself (leaf
resolution via `readlink` plus dirname resolution, both before the lexical test —
the deleted comment implemented): both in-repo legs go red, controls hold. The
specialist's anti-vacuity argument reproduces.

**Other claims in the region, all verified true:** no executable line calls
`readlink`/`realpath`/`stat` or tests `-L`/`-h` (1 comment-line hit for the first
pair, 2 for the second, **0 executable**); `pwd -P` in exactly two places, both
`cd <DIR> && pwd -P` (`:346`, `:375`); no line numbers anywhere in the new prose
(header 251-299, spec 403-430 and 493-519); `+20` assertions exactly (13e 7,
13N 13); the old false sentence survives only as an explicit quotation inside the
correction plus synced fixture copies.

**The `_PE_RESOLVED` hoist is inert.** `impact_of` -> 0 callers, file-local,
present at identical lines 363/376 in canonical and all 7 fixture copies.

### Impact pass (section 3a)

Report read first, then refreshed — it was content-stale (generated 07:14:52Z,
before the `dmi` edits at 07:35-08:07). Regenerated 09:29:26Z: 26 files,
`server: code-graph`, **0 per-file errors**, hash bound.

**Honest correction to last round's alarm:** `post-edit.sh` is **48 nodes, unchanged
from round 5's 48**. Round 5 saw 27 -> 48 and I called item 7's staleness
"material, not cosmetic". This round it was not — `dmi` added comments, one
hoisted initialisation and spec sections, no new symbols. The refresh was
procedurally right and substantively a no-op. `specs/post-edit.sh` is 96 nodes.
`file_dependents` empty everywhere, consistent with round 5.

**My own instrumentation error, again.** My first read showed `nodes=0` for both
files because I selected `.impact.nodes`; they live at `.impact.data.nodes`. Last
round I made the sibling mistake (`.ok` vs `.impact.ok`) and flagged it as a
legibility signal. That is now four instances across two agents on one artifact.

### Findings below threshold — recorded, not blocking

- **R4-F2 (medium)** — `dpe` understates its own scope twice: 154/154 stale
  (unquantified) and the no-commit variant unnamed. The second matters because
  `dpe`'s **preferred** fix (candidate 1, invalidate entries against the recorded
  head) cannot see the no-commit variant at all; only candidate 2
  (content-address the baseline) closes both. Landing it per its own preference
  order would leave half the hole open and look closed. Measurement posted to `dpe`.
- **R4-F3 (medium)** — the `dmi` F7 `decisions` entry claims "That distinction is
  now asserted (13N's last two legs)". Those legs assert only that neither in-repo
  shape *reaches* the retry, which is symmetric and says nothing about how they
  would differ if it ran. E2 is symmetric too. The counterfactual is prose-only —
  and **TRUE**, per M1 above, so this is not a sixth false claim; it is an
  overstated coverage claim in the field the grader reads as evidence.
- **R4-F4 (low)** — the `cmp -s` "MUTANT DID NOT APPLY" guard the specialist
  recommends for all future mutation probes exists nowhere in the tree; with
  `LESSONS.md` reverted its only home is a bd comment. The `fkm.1` LESSONS-debt
  comment preserves the false-prose and line-number lessons but not this one.
- **R4-F5 (low)** — 13N's `awk` strip patterns are unanchored while the paired
  assertion is anchored; a future prose line containing the sentinel substring
  would start the strip early and the assertions could not detect it.

### Two procedural judgements, stated rather than buried

**I authored an r4 artifact past `max_review_iterations=3`.** Round 5 read the cap
as binding on the Claude lane and declined r4; that was harmless then because no
finding reached threshold. It is not harmless now: a HIGH held only in prose would
leave `review-check.sh gate` reporting `open_findings: 0`, and a later `approve`
would pass the mechanical check with a HIGH open. `.claude/review-config`'s own
header says the caps "only shape the optional Codex turn; the Claude review path
and the qa-gate release credential are unaffected", which resolves the ambiguity
`qa.md` 6p.2 creates in favour of recording. Recording is also the fail-closed
direction. Gate now reads `open_finding_ids: ["R4-F1"]`, `rc=4`.

**The lane probe said `codex`; I ran the Claude lane anyway.** The Codex lane
degraded on this task at review iteration 2 (`codex-review.sh` exit 5, recorded)
and rounds 3-5 all ran Claude. Deferring an already-measured blocking HIGH to a
paid relay round-trip would delay the block for no added independence — I am
`qa-claude` against `implementers: ["devops"]`, so separation holds either way.

### Bar

Not re-run per instruction. Orchestrator's serial measurement on the settled tree:
L1 32/32 · lint rc=0 · L2 43 specs 42/1, **2380** assertions pass / 2 fail (the
`installer-v3-upgrade 8e B` carry) · L3 15/15 files 451 pass / 5 skipped / 0
failed · fixture drift 0/175.

Independently re-verified: fixture drift 0 across all 7 `post-edit.sh` copies
(sha256 `50e532a4…` identical to canonical); `sync-errors.log` **0 bytes**, mtime
Aug 2; hash `01296db9…` unmoved after every step including a live
`reconcile-tracker` and an impact-report regeneration; `LESSONS.md` still clean
(0 numstat entries); git dirty count still 60; tracker 179 lines with **0** probe
paths.

Probe hygiene: every probe tree under `mktemp -d` (`/var/folders/…`), never the
session scratchpad — rule 1's `^(/private)?/tmp/claude-[^/]+/` branch would have
swallowed those paths and turned every "dropped" into the denylist's answer
instead of containment's. Probe scripts by heredoc only, never the Write tool.
All probe trees removed.

### No packet refresh this round

I am **not** returning `needs-grading`. The R4-F1 correction changes
`docs/HOOKS.md` content, so packet items 1, 3 and 4 would need regenerating again
immediately after. Refresh for rubric iteration 2 once R4-F1 is resolved or
overruled. Item 7 is already current and bound.

### R4-F1 reproduced independently before the rewrite

Isolated `mktemp -d` repo, the real scripts symlinked in, driven through
`qa-gate.sh baseline-capture` and `qa-gate.sh reconcile-tracker`:

- `tracked.txt` dirty at capture (` M tracked.txt`), then **two** Bash-redirect
  appends, **no commit** (HEAD identical before/after). `git diff --numstat`: 3
  added lines. Reconciler: `ok:true`, `added=1`, and `tracked.txt` **absent** from
  `changed-files.txt`. `sync-errors.log` never created.
- `later.txt` clean at capture, one Bash write: reconciled in. So the `added=1`
  covers the OTHER file — the readout looks like a successful reconcile while one
  of the two Bash-written paths was dropped. That is the shape of the danger.

Live-tree exposure, read-only: the gate baseline holds **154** entries (142 ` M`,
12 `??`) captured at `head=bb8fce7`; **29** of them are byte-identical to a current
porcelain line, i.e. 29 of the 60 dirty paths are invisible to a further Bash write
right now — **including 14 of the 26 change-set paths**, among them `docs/HOOKS.md`,
`specs/post-edit.sh` and `lib/fixture.sh`. I made every edit this round with
Write/Edit for that reason (post-edit.sh records those unconditionally); a Bash-side
edit to those three would not have reached the change set. No tree-specific counts
went into the shipped prose — they decay — but they are the measurement behind it.

### Fail-first, three observations

1. **`assert_mutant_applied`** — driven in isolation with a `sed 's/a\\|b/c/'`
   mutation (the recorded BSD-sed shape: no error, matches nothing): `FAIL:
   MUTANT DID NOT APPLY: byte-identical to its source`, returns 1. Also red for a
   missing file, green for a real substitution.
2. **In situ** — with 13R's awk anchor changed to a name that matches nothing, the
   spec reports **exactly one** failure (the guard) and the 12 dependent legs are
   skipped: 102 pass instead of 115. Before the guard existed that same state was a
   silent green.
3. **13R and 7.6 both watched red.** 13R with a byte-different but
   behaviourally-inert mutant: both structural legs red, and the DIRECTORY-symlink
   leg red (reports `tracked`) while the FILE-symlink leg stays green — the
   asymmetry, from the failing side. 7.6/7.7 run against the no-subtraction mutant:
   4 legs red (`added=0`, tracker absence, hash blind, and 7.7's "still absent").
   Both temporary edits were reverted from a byte-copy and re-run green.

### Bar

- `bash -n` on all 5 edited shell files: ok
- `make lint`: **rc=0**
- `make sync-fixtures` after each canonical edit (2 runs). Fixture drift **0**:
  all 7 copies of `qa-gate.sh` / `post-edit.sh` / `verify-before-stop.sh`
  sha256-identical to canonical
- L2 targeted: `gate-baseline-v2` **114 pass / 0 fail** (was 89) ·
  `specs/post-edit` **115 pass / 0 fail** (was 98) — +42 assertions
- L1, the suites that read the edited files: `denylist-source` 59 ·
  `impact-report` 39 · `review-separation` 60 · `installer-flags` 94 ·
  `packaging-parity` 652 · `platform-audit` 29 · `workflow-manifest` 131 — all 0 fail
- `sync-errors.log` still **0 bytes**, mtime Aug 2. Tracker carries **0** probe paths
- NOT run, per instruction: `make test-component`, `make test-e2e-unit`. Also not
  `workflow-doctor` (its `beads_ledger` leg is a known pre-existing stale)

### llm_observations

**The guard I landed cannot catch the failure I hit while landing it, and that is
worth writing down.** `assert_mutant_applied` answers "did the file change", not
"did the intended edit land". My fail-first run 3 above passed the guard (bytes
differed) while the mutation was behaviourally inert — the structural legs caught
that. So the guard is necessary and not sufficient, and the per-mutant textual
sanity checks it sits next to are not redundant. The lib header says exactly that
rather than implying the guard is the whole answer.

**A vacuity trap I nearly shipped.** 7.6's "the block reason never names it" leg
would have passed under 7R's mutant for the wrong reason: the mutant inflates the
tracker past the reason's 15-path cap, so the path is missing because the list was
truncated. Same failure family as the whole arc — a measurement that did not happen
looking exactly like one that passed. Fixed with a companion assertion that the
list is not truncated.

**A comment I wrote and had to retract inside five minutes.** My first version of
the `strip_reconcile_regions` note claimed the reconcile sentinels are only ever
named *inside* the regions they delimit, so anchoring was unnecessary. I checked
before shipping it: `qa-gate.sh:2294` names `TRACKER-RECONCILE` in prose outside
any region. The unanchored patterns survive only because that line carries neither
`BEGIN` nor `END`. I anchored both patterns instead of arguing for the exception.

**`bd_list_comments` (MCP) reports 0 comments on 94d while `bd comments <id>
--json` (CLI) returns 71.** `bd show --json` agrees with the CLI (`comment_count:
71`) but no longer inlines bodies. So the MCP surface silently answers "no
comments" where the truth is "71" — I would have started this round without QA's
round-6 plan had I trusted it. That is `fkm.1.17`'s family exactly (a plausible
value instead of an error) and it is a different tool from the impact report, so
the count there is five instances across three agents, not four.

**Adjacent smell, not fixed.** The residual's blast radius is a function of how old
the baseline is: this one is from 2026-08-03T04:38Z with 154 entries against a
26-path change set, and 2 commits have landed since. `approve` refreshes it in

## R5 ARTIFACT CORRECTION — R5-F1's live-state claim, and two consequences

Posting this against my own record within minutes of writing it, because the tree moved under the review and the artifact's evidence text is now partly stale. The findings stand; one of their framings does not.

### 1. R5-F1: the mechanism is unchanged, the live instance has been REPAIRED

`review-artifact-...-r5.json` describes the tracker as holding 10 of 26 paths and the change-set hash as `0b5a546e…`. That was true from **15:00:01 to 16:08:01** local — the whole span of this review. It is no longer true: `changed-files.txt` was restored to the 26-path set at **16:08:01** (mtime), and `impact-report.sh --hash-only` now returns `01296db9…` again. The restore was not mine; the orchestrator was working the same tree.

Consequences for the record:

- The artifact's `reviewed_hash` is `01296db9…`, because `--hash-only` was evaluated after the restore. That binding is **correct** — the 26-path set is the content I actually reviewed.
- The `evidence` prose inside R5-F1 that says "the change set an approval would bind is `0b5a546e…` / 10 paths" should be read as **past tense**, describing a 68-minute window, not the state now.
- What does **not** change: the mechanism, which I reproduced independently of the live tree in an isolated repo with the real scripts (`added=1`, `ok:true`, `denylisted=0`, the baselined path silently absent). Nor the arithmetic: 154 baseline entries, 29 byte-identical porcelain lines, 14 of the 26 change-set paths among them. Nor the fact that a session boundary mid-cycle triggers it with no guard (`session-start.sh:273` vs the guard already present at `:348`).

R5-F1 therefore remains open as a **defect**, not as a live emergency. Restoring the tracker by hand is exactly the "recovery was luck, not design" that `fkm.1.2` records; it does not close the hole that made it necessary.

### 2. The impact report is now STALE, and approve correctly refuses

    recorded (impact-report-…-94d.json): 0b5a546e…  (10 files, generated 11:02:48Z)
    current  (--hash-only):              01296db9…  (26 paths)

So `approve` would refuse with the stale-report error even setting my findings aside. This is the gate working as designed — no action needed beyond letting the next `enter` regenerate it, but do not mistake a later green `enter` for evidence that nothing happened here.

### 3. R5-F4 is now largely moot — and that itself is worth a look

`review-check.sh gate` now reports `open_finding_ids: [R5-F1, R5-F2]`; **R4-F1 has dropped out of the open set** without any `resolve-finding` record, because the predicate reads only the LATEST artifact and my R5 artifact does not re-raise it. In this instance that is the right outcome — I verified the R4-F1 fix at all seven sites and it is genuinely correct. But note the general shape: **a later review artifact silently retires every earlier finding it omits, with no evidence trail.** That is a weaker discipline than `resolve-finding --fix … --test …` implies, and P2's binding leans on this predicate. Worth a task; I am not raising it as a blocking finding on 94d.

### 4. R5-F3 downgraded in urgency

`impact-report---hash.json` is no longer load-bearing now that the tracker is restored, so it is safe to delete. Keep it if you want the audit trail of the 26-path list; it is the artifact that made the byte-faithful recovery proof possible.

At 15:46:39Z the implementer was still in read-only exploration. workflow-doctor.sh
did not exist. The only dirty paths were docs and .beads, so F1 classified the change
set correctly — and then wrote its label to the TASK.

THE DEFECT, stated precisely: F1's verdict is a statement about a CHANGE SET ('no
reviewable source changed'). Its label is a statement about a TASK ('this task's work
is approved'). Those are not the same proposition. Any doc-only Stop that happens while
a task is open — mid-implementation, during exploration, during a docs commit in an
adjacent session — converts the first into the second.

WHY THE BLAST RADIUS IS SMALL TODAY, AND WHY THAT IS LUCK: the change-set-bound release
predicate (llh.18 / v4) means the NEXT Stop recomputes a different hash, finds no bound
record, and re-arms. So the damage is a misleading 'bd show' and a closed task, not an
unreviewed release. The gate held for the wrong reason — it held because the approval
went stale, not because it was never granted.

CONTRIBUTING: F1 auto-approves only WITH an active task. That coupling is what puts the
label on a task at all. Compare claude-workflow-plugin-prm/dkp: the SAME coupling in the
other direction hard-blocks task-less plan-mode sessions. One mechanism, two opposite
failures — approves what it should not, blocks what it should not.

CANDIDATE FIXES (not yet chosen — needs the evidence-before-fix pass):
  a) F1 records its verdict WITHOUT the qa-approved label when the task carries an
     IMPLEMENTER record and no completion contract. Narrowest.
  b) F1 scopes its label to the change set it actually judged — i.e. it may only
     approve a task whose recorded change set is the doc-only one.
  c) F1 refuses to auto-approve any task in status=in_progress with an IMPLEMENTER
     record, and says so in the block reason.
Prefer (b) if it can be made to hold: it makes the label mean what the verdict means.

NOT FIXED IN v4.1 — filed rather than folded in, because it is not this release's
subject and the change-set binding contains it. Whoever takes it: the reproduction is
free, just enter a gate on a task and touch only a .md file.

comments.author: username
comments.text:
SECOND CONSEQUENCE, observed 2026-07-28 immediately after the first.

The spurious F1 approve does not only mislabel the task — it also CLEARS THE
current-task POINTER, because `qa-gate.sh approve` truncates changed-files.txt and
clears current-task as part of its normal post-approval cleanup.

Observed: after the implementer removed the qa-approved label and reopened 0fc, the
next Stop hook reported 'No active Beads task detected' over a 15-file change set,
and `current-task.sh get` returned empty. The orchestrator had explicitly set that
pointer before delegating.

So one doc-only Stop mid-implementation produces THREE effects, none of them intended:
  1. qa-approved stamped on a task whose work does not exist
  2. the task closed
  3. the active-task pointer cleared, so the NEXT Stop cannot even identify the task
     it should be gating and falls through to the task-less hard block

Effect 3 is what makes this user-visible rather than merely untidy: recovery requires
re-running current-task.sh set, which is not mentioned in any block reason. A reader
who hits this sees 'No active Beads task detected' and has no way to know a fast path
silently unset it.

This strengthens the case for candidate fix (b) — scope F1's label AND its cleanup to
the change set it actually judged. A verdict about a doc-only change set has no business
clearing the implementation tracker for an unrelated in-flight task.

comments.author: username
comments.text:
FOURTH consequence, and the most serious: it fired on the RELEASE task (uvk), 2026-07-30.

At 12:32:11Z — 22 seconds after the C5 implementer was spawned and before it had written
anything — F1 recorded 'QA-GATE APPROVED change_set_hash=9942b2bd reviewed_by=none' and
CLOSED uvk. That hash was C4's leftover doc-only change set. C5's actual work (version
bump to 4.1.0, CHANGELOG, the v4.1.0 RELEASE_AUDIT ledger, README, HANDOFF, the new
frozen manifest) hashes to 914ceeff. **The release's version bump was recorded as
approved under a review bypass, for a change set that did not contain it.**

CONTAINMENT HELD, and the reason is worth stating because it validates the v4 design:
the change-set binding meant the Stop hook would emit LABEL_WITHOUT_RECORD and re-block
rather than release on the stale label. And plugin.json is reviewable source under F1's
own classifier (verify-before-stop.sh:134-136), so a second auto-approval over C5's set
was impossible. Nothing could ship unreviewed. The damage was to the RECORD.

So: v3 would have released on this; v4 did not. That is exactly the containment this
task's original filing predicted, now demonstrated on the highest-stakes task in the
repo.

NEW DETAIL — how it was caught, which is a process finding in its own right: the
implementer noticed only because bd_update_task ECHOED BACK 'status=closed,
labels=[devops,qa-approved]' when it had passed neither. It was setting notes. Had it
written notes without reading the response, this release would have been tagged with a
bypassed approval on its version bump and nobody would have looked. Its suggestion —
that specialists re-read task state at completion as a matter of course — is cheap and
would have caught all four instances.

The full consequence set is now: (1) qa-approved stamped on work that does not exist;
(2) the task closed; (3) current-task cleared, so the next Stop cannot identify what it
is gating; (4) an approval bound to the WRONG change set, surviving into the release
record until someone reads a hash.

Candidate fix (b) from the original filing — scope F1's label to the change set it
actually judged — would have prevented all four. Still not fixed in v4.1: folding a gate
change into the release commit that ships the gate, unreviewed, is the wrong trade.
