# Default rubric (v1)

Applies to every task graded under the rubric-grader QA loop (spec Phase A). Each criterion below is a pass/fail assertion the grader evaluates from the grading packet: `bd show` for the task, the SPEC doc, the diff of the files listed in `.qa-tracking/changed-files.txt`, the F7 completion contract returned by the specialist, and `LESSONS.md`. One-line justification per criterion. No numeric score theater — pass or fail.

The criteria are intentionally short and checkable. Where the criterion needs context (boundary-mock fidelity, F7 fields), the "Evidence that satisfies it" line names the artefact the grader looks at.

## Criteria

### C1. Behavior matches the task description and SPEC.

The shipped diff implements the behavior the task description asks for, and matches the goal + acceptance criteria stated in the attached SPEC doc (read via `bd_doc_read(task_id, name="spec")`). Out-of-scope behavior the SPEC explicitly excludes is NOT in the diff.

Evidence that satisfies it: a 1-2 sentence walk-through that maps every user-visible behavior in the SPEC to a code path in the diff (or to a deliberate, documented deferral in the F7 `decisions` array). A diff that adds plausibly-related behavior the SPEC does not name fails this criterion — that is scope creep.

### C2. Tests added exercise user behavior rather than implementation.

Where the diff introduces new behavior, the diff also introduces tests that assert against the user-visible contract (return shape, side effects, error envelope, accessibility role, status code) rather than against the implementation's private structure (function-name mocking, line-coverage gymnastics, internal control-flow assertions).

Evidence that satisfies it: at least one test in the diff that would still pass if the implementation were rewritten while keeping the user contract identical. A test that asserts only against private symbols, internal call counts, or framework boilerplate fails this criterion.

### C3. The F7 completion contract carries all six fields with substantive `llm_observations`.

The specialist's structured completion payload includes `task_id`, `files_changed`, `tests_added`, `decisions`, `blockers`, and `llm_observations`. `llm_observations` is non-trivial narrative — what surprised the specialist, what was unclear, what they noticed and did not act on. A boilerplate one-liner like "no observations" fails this criterion (principle 9: `llm_observations` is mandatory and substantive).

Evidence that satisfies it: each of the six fields is present and the `llm_observations` paragraph is the kind of thing a human engineer would say at a stand-up.

### C4. No unrelated scope in the diff.

Every file the specialist touched serves the task. Drive-by refactors, formatting churn on untouched lines, and "while I'm here" cleanups that exceed the task brief fail this criterion — they should be filed as paired follow-up Beads tasks instead.

Evidence that satisfies it: the diff's file list maps cleanly to the SPEC's deliverables; any incidental change is either trivial (one-line typo fix) or explicitly justified in the `decisions` array.

### C5. J26 modules relevant to the diff are addressed.

Where the diff touches a domain covered by the J26 security taxonomy (SECRETS, INJECTION, AUTH, CONFIG, DEPS, AI, MOBILE, DATA — see `docs/AGENTS.md`), the diff demonstrates that the relevant modules were considered. Untouched J26 domains are out of scope.

Evidence that satisfies it: the `decisions` array (or the SPEC) names which J26 modules apply, and the diff shows defences in those modules (input validation at the trust boundary, parameterised queries, narrow CORS, audited logging, etc.). A diff that touches user input handling without naming INJECTION fails this criterion.

### C6. Docs updated where behavior changed.

When the diff changes user-visible behavior, the documentation that describes that behavior is updated in the same change. This includes `CHANGELOG.md`, README sections, `docs/*.md`, command help text, and SPEC docs the diff renders out of date.

Evidence that satisfies it: a docs-only file in `files_changed` paired with each behavioral change, or a deliberate `decisions` entry stating why a doc deferral is correct (e.g. an internal refactor that ships without user-visible change). A behavioral change that ships with no doc update and no deferral note fails this criterion.

### C7. Boundary-mock fidelity (LESSONS.md lesson 2).

When the diff introduces or modifies mocks of boundaries the project does not control (third-party HTTP APIs, external SDKs, system calls, message-bus payloads), every such mock derives its shape from a fixture extracted from the real downstream producer's spec (OpenAPI, proto file, SDK source, vendor docs). The fixture's source is cited in a comment, the `decisions` array, or `llm_observations`.

**Automatic needs_revision:** circular pass-through assertions are an immediate fail. A mock that feeds `body.error` so a test can assert `body.error` proves nothing — it tests the test's own setup, not the production behavior. Cite `LESSONS.md` lesson 2 in the justification.

Evidence that satisfies it: every new boundary mock points at a fixture file (`.fixtures/`, `__fixtures__/`, `testdata/`) carrying a snapshot of the producer's payload, and the fixture has a comment naming the source (URL, commit, SDK version). Tests assert against the producer's contract, not against the mock's own input.

# DevOps rubric (v1)

Applied additionally when the task carries the `devops` label. Default criteria still apply; these add domain-specific checks pulled from `.claude/agents/devops.md`. The leverage is default + bugfix — these are the few devops-specific failure modes that recur.

## Criteria

### D1. Scripts are idempotent and re-runnable.

Install, uninstall, hook, and CI scripts in the diff produce the same end state when run twice in a row. A second run of `install.sh` does not double-write hooks, clobber prior settings, or fail because a directory already exists. A migration script that exits non-zero on its second run fails this criterion.

Evidence that satisfies it: every new script uses `mkdir -p`, conditional inserts, and idempotent label operations (`bd label add` returns success if already present); the `decisions` array documents any deliberately non-idempotent step (e.g. a one-shot data migration) and pairs it with a guard (lock file, completion sentinel) so a re-run is detected.

### D2. Graceful degradation on missing optional tools.

When the diff depends on an optional tool (gitleaks, shellcheck, a particular bd version, a specific CI runner image), the missing-tool path is handled: log a structured warning, fall back to a safe default, exit zero where the workflow allows. A hook that exits non-zero because `gitleaks` is not installed fails this criterion — that is not a developer-machine-portable failure mode.

Evidence that satisfies it: every new tool dependency is probed (`command -v tool >/dev/null`); the fallback path is documented in the script comments and tested at L1; the `decisions` array names the dependency and its installation hint.

### D3. No new permission prompts; autonomy preserved.

The diff does not add `permissions.deny` rules to `settings.json`, narrow specialist tool lists below the broad allow set, or introduce any user-facing approval step the plugin previously ran without. Principle 3 of the v3 plan is "full autonomy, no permission prompts" — every deny rule becomes a future approval prompt and breaks the workflow.

Evidence that satisfies it: a diff of `.claude/settings.json` shows only `permissions.allow` expansions, never `deny`; specialist tool frontmatter is unchanged or expanded; the `decisions` array calls out any new tool the broadened allow set covers.

### D4. Secrets and PII stay out of source, logs, and history.

Hardcoded API keys, tokens, passwords, private keys, committer emails, and PII are absent from the diff. Logs that the diff adds redact sensitive fields before writing. A commit that introduces an `.env` file with values, a personal email address in a script header, or unredacted PII in a log line fails this criterion (extends C5 / SECRETS + DATA).

Evidence that satisfies it: secrets read from a secret manager or environment variable at runtime; PII fields in new log lines are redacted (`***@`, `user_id=***`); a `gitleaks`-equivalent pass on the diff is clean, and the `decisions` array names the secrets the diff touches.

title: Bug: LABEL_WITHOUT_RECORD block prints a remediation that cannot work — `enter` does not clear qa-approved, `approve` no-ops
description:
Discovered while implementing claude-workflow-plugin-3mg.1 (shared denylist / hash migration).

## Symptom
When `verify-before-stop.sh` blocks with LABEL_WITHOUT_RECORD ("qa-approved label present but no change-set-bound approval record matches the current changes"), the block reason prints this remediation:

```
  bash .claude/scripts/qa-gate.sh enter <id>
  bash .claude/scripts/impact-report.sh <id>
  bash .claude/scripts/qa-gate.sh approve <id> '<summary>'
```

That sequence does NOT recover. The gate stays blocked and the agent is deadlocked on a correct-looking recipe.

## Root cause
`qa-gate.sh cmd_enter` never removes the `qa-approved` label (verified: the only `remove_label "$tid" "qa-approved"` calls in qa-gate.sh are approve's own rollback arms, lines ~1071 and ~1092). `cmd_approve` then hits its idempotency guard at qa-gate.sh:865:

```
    if [ "$had_approved" = "1" ]; then
        emit_json 1 "approve" "$tid" "approved" "qa-approved already set; idempotent no-op"
        return 0
    fi
```

so no new `QA-GATE APPROVED change_set_hash=<h>` record is written, the recomputed hash still fails to match, and the Stop hook re-blocks.

## Evidence (reproduced deterministically)
Reproduced in an L2 component fixture and PINNED as a regression test in `.claude/tests/component/specs/denylist-shared.sh` section C:

- `denylist-C4: bare enter+approve is an idempotent no-op (KNOWN GAP)` — approve's JSON observation literally reads `qa-approved already set; idempotent no-op`.
- `denylist-C4: ...so the gate is STILL blocked after it (KNOWN GAP)` — decision stays `block`.
- `denylist-C5: a fresh cycle (drop label -> enter -> approve) recovers` — ALLOW only after `bd label remove <id> qa-approved`.

## Why it matters more now
This predates 3mg.1 (it is llh.18's approve-idempotency guard meeting llh.18's change-set hash binding), and until now it only fired on the rare post-approval-edit case. A denylist landing re-hashes every recomputed change set, so it puts EVERY in-flight review cycle on this path at once.

## Options (needs a decision, do not fix blind)
1. Make `cmd_enter` remove `qa-approved` — semantically right (entering a new cycle means the task is no longer approved), but it is a gate-semantics change with blast radius: `bd_qa_approve`'s documented idempotency, existing L1/L2 specs that enter an already-approved task, and the e2e cassettes.
2. Make `cmd_approve`'s idempotency guard hash-aware: no-op only when a matching change-set-bound record already exists; otherwise write a fresh record.
3. Leave the semantics and fix only the block reason to print the `bd label remove` step.

Option 2 is the narrowest behavioural fix (it makes the guard mean what it claims to mean) but needs its own SPEC + QA cycle.

## Interim mitigation shipped in 3mg.1
The working recipe is documented in CHANGELOG (Phase V4 pt1 upgrade note) and `docs/HOOKS.md` ("Denylist changes are a hash migration"), including the required `bd label remove <task-id> qa-approved` first step.
acceptance_criteria:
- A LABEL_WITHOUT_RECORD block can be recovered by following EXACTLY the remediation the block reason prints (no undocumented `bd label remove` step).
- `denylist-shared.sh` section C is updated: the C4 "KNOWN GAP" assertions are replaced by an assertion that the printed remediation recovers, and C5 keeps proving the explicit-label-removal path still works.
- Whichever option is chosen, the existing idempotency contract is either preserved or its change is documented in CHANGELOG + `docs/HOOKS.md` + the `bd_qa_approve` MCP tool description.

# gz3 pre-fix reproduction harness (evidence artifact, NOT shipped)

This is the exact harness used to reproduce both gz3 defects against **pristine
pre-fix code** before anything was changed. It asserts the DEFECTIVE behaviour on
purpose, so it cannot live in `.claude/tests/component/specs/` (it would fail
against the fixed tree — that is the point).

## How to re-run it

```bash
cd /Users/edk0/Desktop/projects/claude-workflow-plugin
git worktree add --detach /tmp/gz3-prefix <pre-fix-sha>     # ee75125 was HEAD at the time
# paste the script below to:
#   /tmp/gz3-prefix/.claude/tests/component/specs/zz-gz3-prefix-repro.sh
cd /tmp/gz3-prefix && bash .claude/tests/component/run.sh --filter zz-gz3-prefix-repro
```

Expected against the PRE-FIX tree: `pass=28 fail=0` (every assertion asserts the
defect).

Expected against the FIXED tree (source the four `lib/*.sh` from the fixed
checkout and `. ` this file): `pass=15 fail=13` — the 13 failures are the four
windows flipping to correct behaviour:

| assertion | pre-fix | fixed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R1-3 printed approve is a no-op | idempotent no-op | writes a fresh bound record |
| R1-3 record count stays 1 | 1 | 2 |
| R1-4 gate still blocked after the recipe | block | ALLOW |
| R1-5 only `bd label remove` recovers | 2 records | 3 (already recovered) |
| R2-2 straddling Stop blocks | block, `current change-set hash is e3b0c44…` | ALLOW (`{}`) |
| R3-0 record count at the label-add drive point | 0 | 1 (record precedes label) |
| R3-1 mid-approve Stop blocks | block (forged-label text) | ALLOW |
| R4-0 current-task at the rubric-pending drive point | cleared | present |
| R4-1 mid-approve Stop blocks | block (`No active Beads task`) | ALLOW |

Teardown: remove the `node_modules` symlink first if you made one, then
`git worktree remove --force /tmp/gz3-prefix`.

## Source

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# zz-gz3-prefix-repro.sh — PRE-FIX REPRODUCTION HARNESS for gz3 (v4.1 U1).
#
# R1  DEADLOCK — following the block's own printed remediation EXACTLY is a
#     no-op loop; only the undocumented `bd label remove` recovers.
# R2  RACE / window W3 — a Stop whose two change-set reads straddle approve's
#     tracking-state finalization blocks with the EMPTY-SET hash as "current".
# R3  RACE / window W1 — approve adds qa-approved BEFORE writing the record, so
#     a Stop landing in between sees the forged-label block for a legitimate
#     in-flight approval.
# R4  RACE / window W2 — approve clears current-task BEFORE truncating the
#     tracker, so a Stop landing in between blocks with "No active Beads task".
#
# W1/W2 drive points are the fixture's own `bd` wrapper: it runs the real bd
# call, then fires the Stop hook synchronously, then returns. One process tree,
# no sleeps, no concurrency — the interleaving is exact and deterministic.

set -u

quiet_stack() {
    local root="$1"
    rm -f "$root/.claude/scripts/detect-stack.sh"
    printf '#!/bin/bash\nprintf %s\n' "'{\"runner\":\"npm\",\"test_cmd\":\"\",\"lint_cmd\":\"\",\"type_cmd\":\"\"}'" \
        > "$root/.claude/scripts/detect-stack.sh"
    chmod +x "$root/.claude/scripts/detect-stack.sh"
}

gate_fixture() {
    mk_fixture
    bd_required_or_skip
    (cd "$COMPONENT_FIXTURE_PATH" && git init -q 2>/dev/null \
        && git config user.email t@t.t && git config user.name t \
        && git add -A && git commit -qm baseline 2>/dev/null) || true
    quiet_stack "$COMPONENT_FIXTURE_PATH"
}

seed_tracker() {
    local root="$1"; shift
    : > "$root/.claude/.qa-tracking/changed-files.txt"
    local l
    for l in "$@"; do printf '%s\n' "$l" >> "$root/.claude/.qa-tracking/changed-files.txt"; done
}

qg() { local root="$1"; shift; ( cd "$root" && CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR="$root" bash "$root/.claude/scripts/qa-gate.sh" "$@" ); }
ct() { local root="$1"; shift; ( cd "$root" && CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR="$root" bash "$root/.claude/scripts/current-task.sh" "$@" ); }
ir() { local root="$1"; shift; ( cd "$root" && CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR="$root" bash "$root/.claude/scripts/impact-report.sh" "$@" ); }
bdq() { local root="$1"; shift; ( cd "$root" && bd "$@" ); }

stop_json() {
    local root="$1" hook="${2:-$1/.claude/scripts/verify-before-stop.sh}"
    ( cd "$root" && printf '%s' '{"stop_reason":"end_turn","stop_hook_active":false}' \
        | CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR="$root" bash "$hook" 2>/dev/null | tail -1 )
}
stop_decision() { printf '%s' "$(stop_json "$@")" | jq -r '.decision // "ALLOW"' 2>/dev/null; }
json_field() { printf '%s' "$1" | jq -r "$2 // empty" 2>/dev/null || echo ""; }

approval_records() {
    bdq "$1" show "$2" --json 2>/dev/null \
        | jq -r '(if type=="array" then .[0].comments else .comments end) // [] | .[].text' 2>/dev/null \
        | grep '^QA-GATE APPROVED ' || true
}
record_count() { approval_records "$1" "$2" | grep -c . | tr -d '[:space:]'; }
new_task() { bdq "$1" create "$2" -t task -p 1 -l devops,qa-pending --json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.id // empty'; }

armed_cycle() {
    local root="$1" tid="$2"; shift 2
    seed_tracker "$root" "$@"
    qg "$root" enter "$tid" >/dev/null 2>&1
    ct "$root" set "$tid" >/dev/null 2>&1
    seed_review_records "$tid" "qa-claude" "backend" "$root" >/dev/null 2>&1
    ir "$root" "$tid" >/dev/null 2>&1
}

real_bd_of() {
    local p
    p=$(sed -n 's/^exec \(.*\) --no-daemon.*/\1/p' "$1/bin/bd" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '"' | head -1)
    [ -z "$p" ] && p=$(command -v bd)
    printf '%s' "$p"
}

drive_point_bd() {
    local root="$1" a1="$2" a2="$3" a4="$4"
    local real; real=$(real_bd_of "$root")
    rm -f "$root/.claude/.qa-tracking/.drive-fired"
    cat > "$root/bin/bd" <<EOF
#!/bin/bash
if [ "\$1" = "$a1" ] && [ "\$2" = "$a2" ] && [ "\$4" = "$a4" ] && [ ! -f "$root/.claude/.qa-tracking/.drive-fired" ]; then
    : > "$root/.claude/.qa-tracking/.drive-fired"
    $real --no-daemon "\$@"; rc=\$?
    $real --no-daemon show "\$3" --json 2>/dev/null \\
        | jq -r '(if type=="array" then .[0].comments else .comments end) // [] | .[].text' 2>/dev/null \\
        | grep -c '^QA-GATE APPROVED ' > "$root/.claude/.qa-tracking/.drive-records" 2>/dev/null
    [ -f "$root/.claude/.qa-tracking/current-task" ] && cp "$root/.claude/.qa-tracking/current-task" "$root/.claude/.qa-tracking/.drive-current-task" 2>/dev/null
    wc -l < "$root/.claude/.qa-tracking/changed-files.txt" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' ' > "$root/.claude/.qa-tracking/.drive-tracker-lines"
    ( cd "$root" && printf '%s' '{"stop_reason":"end_turn","stop_hook_active":false}' \\
        | CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR="$root" bash "$root/.claude/scripts/verify-before-stop.sh" 2>/dev/null \\
        | tail -1 > "$root/.claude/.qa-tracking/.drive-stop.json" )
    exit \$rc
fi
exec $real --no-daemon "\$@"
EOF
    chmod +x "$root/bin/bd"
}
restore_bd() {
    local root="$1" real; real=$(real_bd_of "$root")
    printf '#!/bin/bash\nexec %s --no-daemon "$@"\n' "$real" > "$root/bin/bd"
    chmod +x "$root/bin/bd"
}
drive_stop_json() { tail -1 "$1/.claude/.qa-tracking/.drive-stop.json" 2>/dev/null || echo ""; }

evidence() { printf '  EVIDENCE: %s\n' "$1"; }

# ===========================================================================
# R1 — THE DEADLOCK (original gz3 defect).
# ===========================================================================
gate_fixture
F1="$COMPONENT_FIXTURE_PATH"
TID1=$(new_task "$F1" "prefix-repro: deadlock")
armed_cycle "$F1" "$TID1" "src/a.ts"
qg "$F1" approve "$TID1" "reviewed a.ts" >/dev/null 2>&1
assert_eq "R1-0: pre-fix baseline — the first approve wrote one bound record" \
    "1" "$(record_count "$F1" "$TID1")"

seed_tracker "$F1" "src/a.ts" "src/b.ts"
ct "$F1" set "$TID1" >/dev/null 2>&1
R1_JSON=$(stop_json "$F1")
R1_REASON=$(json_field "$R1_JSON" '.reason')
assert_eq "R1-1: the post-approval edit BLOCKS" "block" "$(json_field "$R1_JSON" '.decision')"
assert_contains "R1-1: ...on the LABEL_WITHOUT_RECORD branch" \
    "no change-set-bound approval record matches" "$R1_REASON"

R1_REMEDY="$F1/.claude/.qa-tracking/printed-remediation.txt"
printf '%s\n' "$R1_REASON" | grep -E '^[[:space:]]*bash \.claude/scripts/' \
    | sed 's/^[[:space:]]*//' > "$R1_REMEDY"
assert_eq "R1-2: the block prints a 3-command remediation" \
    "3" "$(grep -c . "$R1_REMEDY" | tr -d '[:space:]')"
assert_eq "R1-2: ...and never mentions 'bd label remove'" \
    "0" "$(grep -c 'bd label remove' "$R1_REMEDY" | tr -d '[:space:]')"
R1_APPROVE=""
while IFS= read -r cmd; do
    [ -z "$cmd" ] && continue
    cmd=${cmd//\'<approval summary>\'/\'re-reviewed after the post-approval edit\'}
    LINE=$( cd "$F1" && CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR="$F1" eval "$cmd" 2>&1 | tail -1 )
    case "$cmd" in *"qa-gate.sh approve"*) R1_APPROVE="$LINE" ;; esac
done < "$R1_REMEDY"
evidence "pre-fix approve after the printed recipe: $R1_APPROVE"
assert_contains "R1-3: REPRODUCED — the printed approve is an idempotent no-op" \
    "idempotent no-op" "$R1_APPROVE"
assert_eq "R1-3: ...writing NO fresh record (still 1)" "1" "$(record_count "$F1" "$TID1")"
seed_tracker "$F1" "src/a.ts" "src/b.ts"
ct "$F1" set "$TID1" >/dev/null 2>&1
assert_eq "R1-4: REPRODUCED — the gate is STILL blocked after following the recipe (deadlock)" \
    "block" "$(stop_decision "$F1")"

bdq "$F1" label remove "$TID1" qa-approved >/dev/null 2>&1
while IFS= read -r cmd; do
    [ -z "$cmd" ] && continue
    cmd=${cmd//\'<approval summary>\'/\'re-reviewed after dropping the label\'}
    ( cd "$F1" && CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR="$F1" eval "$cmd" >/dev/null 2>&1 )
done < "$R1_REMEDY"
assert_eq "R1-5: ...only the UNDOCUMENTED 'bd label remove' first writes a fresh record" \
    "2" "$(record_count "$F1" "$TID1")"
seed_tracker "$F1" "src/a.ts" "src/b.ts"
ct "$F1" set "$TID1" >/dev/null 2>&1
assert_eq "R1-5: ...and only then does the gate release" "ALLOW" "$(stop_decision "$F1")"

# ===========================================================================
# R2 — THE RACE, window W3 (drive point: detect-stack.sh, between the hook's
#      two change-set reads).
# ===========================================================================
gate_fixture
F2="$COMPONENT_FIXTURE_PATH"
EMPTY_PROJECT=$(mktemp -d -t gz3-empty.XXXXXX)
__COMPONENT_FIXTURES_TO_CLEAN+=("$EMPTY_PROJECT")
EMPTY_SET_HASH=$(CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR="$EMPTY_PROJECT" bash "$F2/.claude/scripts/impact-report.sh" --hash-only 2>/dev/null || echo "")
assert_eq "R2-0: the canonical empty-set hash is computable" \
    "yes" "$([ -n "$EMPTY_SET_HASH" ] && echo yes || echo no)"
evidence "empty-set hash = $EMPTY_SET_HASH"

TID2=$(new_task "$F2" "prefix-repro: approve races the Stop hook")
printf 'export const f = 1;\n' > "$F2/src-f.ts"
armed_cycle "$F2" "$TID2" "src-f.ts"
ARMED_HASH=$(ir "$F2" --hash-only 2>/dev/null || echo "")
cat > "$F2/.claude/scripts/detect-stack.sh" <<EOF
#!/bin/bash
if [ ! -f "$F2/.claude/.qa-tracking/.race-fired" ]; then
    : > "$F2/.claude/.qa-tracking/.race-fired"
    cd "$F2" || exit 0
    CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR="$F2" bash "$F2/.claude/scripts/qa-gate.sh" approve "$TID2" \
        'reviewed mid-Stop (the racing approve)' > "$F2/.claude/.qa-tracking/.race-approve.json" 2>&1
fi
printf '%s' '{"runner":"npm","test_cmd":"","lint_cmd":"","type_cmd":""}'
EOF
chmod +x "$F2/.claude/scripts/detect-stack.sh"
R2_JSON=$(stop_json "$F2")
R2_APPROVE=$(tail -1 "$F2/.claude/.qa-tracking/.race-approve.json" 2>/dev/null || echo "")
assert_json_field "R2-1: the racing approve landed mid-Stop" "$R2_APPROVE" '.status' "approved"
assert_eq "R2-1: ...it truncated the tracker under the running hook" \
    "empty" "$([ -s "$F2/.claude/.qa-tracking/changed-files.txt" ] && echo populated || echo empty)"
evidence "pre-fix raced Stop reason: $(json_field "$R2_JSON" '.reason' | head -3 | tr '\n' ' ')"
assert_eq "R2-2: REPRODUCED — the straddling Stop BLOCKS (transient false block)" \
    "block" "$(json_field "$R2_JSON" '.decision')"
assert_contains "R2-2: ...on the LABEL_WITHOUT_RECORD branch" \
    "no change-set-bound approval record matches" "$(json_field "$R2_JSON" '.reason')"
assert_contains "R2-2: ...naming the EMPTY-SET hash as 'current' (the live fingerprint)" \
    "current change-set hash is $EMPTY_SET_HASH" "$(json_field "$R2_JSON" '.reason')"
assert_eq "R2-3: ...while the record it just wrote binds the REVIEWED set, not the empty one" \
    "$ARMED_HASH" "$(approval_records "$F2" "$TID2" | sed -nE 's/.*change_set_hash=([A-Za-z0-9-]+).*/\1/p' | tail -1)"
assert_eq "R2-4: ...and the very next Stop allows, proving the block was noise" \
    "ALLOW" "$(stop_decision "$F2")"

# ===========================================================================
# R3 — THE RACE, window W1 (drive point: `bd label add <tid> qa-approved`).
# ===========================================================================
gate_fixture
F3="$COMPONENT_FIXTURE_PATH"
TID3=$(new_task "$F3" "prefix-repro: label lands before the record")
armed_cycle "$F3" "$TID3" "src/c.ts"
drive_point_bd "$F3" label add qa-approved
R3_APPROVE=$(qg "$F3" approve "$TID3" "approve interrupted at the label add" 2>&1 | tail -1)
restore_bd "$F3"
R3_STOP=$(drive_stop_json "$F3")
assert_json_field "R3-0: the interrupted approve still completed" "$R3_APPROVE" '.status' "approved"
assert_eq "R3-0: the drive point fired while NO record existed yet" \
    "0" "$(tr -d '[:space:]' < "$F3/.claude/.qa-tracking/.drive-records" 2>/dev/null || echo missing)"
assert_eq "R3-0: ...with the tracker still populated (approve had not finalized)" \
    "1" "$(tr -d '[:space:]' < "$F3/.claude/.qa-tracking/.drive-tracker-lines" 2>/dev/null || echo missing)"
evidence "pre-fix W1 Stop reason: $(json_field "$R3_STOP" '.reason' | head -2 | tr '\n' ' ')"
assert_eq "R3-1: REPRODUCED — a Stop between label and record BLOCKS" \
    "block" "$(json_field "$R3_STOP" '.decision')"
assert_contains "R3-1: ...with the forged-label message, for a legitimate in-flight approval" \
    "no change-set-bound approval record matches" "$(json_field "$R3_STOP" '.reason')"

# ===========================================================================
# R4 — THE RACE, window W2 (drive point: `bd label remove <tid>
#      rubric-pending`, which approve runs after clear_current_task).
# ===========================================================================
gate_fixture
F4="$COMPONENT_FIXTURE_PATH"
TID4=$(new_task "$F4" "prefix-repro: current-task cleared before truncate")
armed_cycle "$F4" "$TID4" "src/d.ts"
drive_point_bd "$F4" label remove rubric-pending
R4_APPROVE=$(qg "$F4" approve "$TID4" "approve interrupted after clear_current_task" 2>&1 | tail -1)
restore_bd "$F4"
R4_STOP=$(drive_stop_json "$F4")
assert_json_field "R4-0: the interrupted approve still completed" "$R4_APPROVE" '.status' "approved"
assert_eq "R4-0: the drive point fired with current-task ALREADY cleared" \
    "cleared" "$([ -f "$F4/.claude/.qa-tracking/.drive-current-task" ] && echo present || echo cleared)"
assert_eq "R4-0: ...and the tracker still populated (truncation not yet reached)" \
    "1" "$(tr -d '[:space:]' < "$F4/.claude/.qa-tracking/.drive-tracker-lines" 2>/dev/null || echo missing)"
evidence "pre-fix W2 Stop reason: $(json_field "$R4_STOP" '.reason' | head -2 | tr '\n' ' ')"
assert_eq "R4-1: REPRODUCED — a Stop in that window BLOCKS" \
    "block" "$(json_field "$R4_STOP" '.decision')"
assert_contains "R4-1: ...with 'No active Beads task', for work that was just approved" \
    "No active Beads task" "$(json_field "$R4_STOP" '.reason')"

[ "$FAIL" -eq 0 ]
```

## gz3 IMPLEMENTED (devops, v4.1 U1) — evidence-before-fix record

Note on prior state: a devops session on 2026-07-27 12:54-14:02Z left ~8 files edited and uncommitted with no report (progress comments #730-732). That work was read, independently verified, corrected in four places (below), and extended. Nothing was discarded.

### STEP 1-3 — REPRODUCTIONS (pristine pre-fix code, not mutants)

A throwaway `git worktree add --detach /tmp/gz3-prefix ee75125` gave the pre-fix scripts, and a 28-assertion harness drove **four** windows there deterministically — drive points, no sleeps, one process tree. Harness source + re-run instructions are attached as doc `repro-harness` (v1). Result pre-fix: `pass=28 fail=0` (every assertion asserts the defect).

**D1 / DEADLOCK (the original gz3).** armed cycle -> approve -> post-approval edit -> Stop blocks LABEL_WITHOUT_RECORD -> the 3 commands were EXTRACTED FROM THE BLOCK TEXT and run verbatim. Evidence, verbatim from the run:
`{"ok":true,"subcommand":"approve",...,"status":"approved","observations":"qa-approved already set; idempotent no-op"}`
Record count stayed 1; the next Stop still returned `block`. Adding the undocumented `bd label remove <tid> qa-approved` first, then the same 3 commands: record count 2, Stop `ALLOW`. So the printed recipe provably could not recover and the undocumented step provably was the recovery.

**D2 / RACE, three windows.** `approve` runs in the QA subagent while the Stop hook runs in the parent session; every intermediate state of `cmd_approve` is observable.

- **W3 (the live occurrence, comment #619).** Drive point: `detect-stack.sh`, which the hook invokes BETWEEN its two change-set reads. A stub that runs a full `approve` from there makes the hook's second read land after the truncation. Pre-fix result: `block`, reason `current change-set hash is e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855` — byte-identical to the `e3b0c44…` in comment #619, and that hash is the sha256 of the EMPTY list (computed from `impact-report.sh --hash-only` against an empty project, not hardcoded). The record written by the racing approve bound the real reviewed hash. The very next Stop returned ALLOW, confirming the block was transient noise.
- **W1 (label before record).** Drive point: the fixture's `bd` wrapper intercepts `bd label add <tid> qa-approved`, runs the real call, then fires the Stop hook. Pre-fix: 0 approval records existed at that instant, tracker still populated -> `block` with the forged-label text, for a legitimate in-flight approval.
- **W2 (current-task cleared before truncate).** Drive point: `bd label remove <tid> rubric-pending`, which `cmd_approve` runs after `clear_current_task` and before the baseline refresh. Pre-fix: current-task already cleared, tracker still populated -> `block`, reason `QA approval required ... No active Beads task detected`.

CORRECTION to comment #619's inference: it reads "after approve truncated changed-files.txt but before the gate-baseline refresh". At the pre-fix HEAD the baseline refresh already PRECEDED the truncation (qa-gate.sh:1250 vs :1264), so that exact interleaving was not reachable. The real mechanism is the two-read straddle (W3) — same fingerprint, same conclusion, and W2 explains the "No active Beads task" variant. Baseline-before-tracker was therefore NOT changed by this fix; it is a pre-existing invariant that the new Stop-side re-read now DEPENDS on, and is pinned as such.

### STEP 4-5 — FIX, and the same drive points re-run

Running the identical pre-fix harness against the FIXED tree: `pass=15 fail=13`. All 13 failures are the four windows flipping (per-assertion table in the `repro-harness` doc). That is the falsification leg: every pre-fix assertion now fails, in the intended direction, and nothing else moved.

1. **Hash-aware idempotency** (task option 2). `.claude/scripts/qa-gate.sh:1039` — CORRECTED LOCATION for the task body's stale `qa-gate.sh:865` reference (the guard is `if [ "$had_approved" = "1" ]`). It now no-ops only when a record already binds the change set this approve WOULD bind; otherwise it proceeds and re-verifies every precondition (impact freshness, independent review, rubric) before writing a FRESH bound record. Reference hash comes from `set_idempotency_reference`: the live `--hash-only` recompute when the tracker is populated, the PERSISTED `impact-report-<tid>.json` when it is empty (LESSONS.md:42 — approve truncates the tracker, so the persisted record is the only surviving witness; this is what keeps a plain double-approve a no-op instead of a staleness refusal).
2. **Approve-commit order.** Record BEFORE label (closes W1); session-state clearing AFTER the truncation (closes W2); baseline-before-tracker unchanged and now pinned; tracking-state finalization still AFTER every rollback-capable step.
3. **Stop-side vanished-change-set release** (closes W3 — no approve-side ordering can, since both reads belong to the Stop process). Before emitting LABEL_WITHOUT_RECORD the hook re-derives `reviewable_changes()` from fresh state and releases only when BOTH halves (tracker and baseline-relative git status) are empty.
4. **Message + docs.** The printed remediation is now exactly correct and says explicitly not to remove the label first; `docs/HOOKS.md` gained "Approve idempotency is hash-aware" + "The vanished-change-set release" and its denylist recovery recipe lost the `bd label remove` step; the `bd_qa_approve` MCP description carries the new contract.

### ROLLBACK-ARM ANALYSIS (record-before-label)

- `add_label qa-approved` fails -> exit 3, no labels changed. The record is already on the task and comments are append-only, so the envelope says so and states the record is INERT without the label (release needs label AND record). Asserted functionally in E1.
- Step-3 / step-4 arms unchanged: they still remove `qa-approved` (and restore `qa-gate-entered`) on failure. New consequence: a rolled-back approve leaves a matching record with no label. That is inert by construction, and a later re-approve takes the `had_approved=0` path and writes a fresh record.
- The record is still written AFTER every refusal (impact freshness, review separation, rubric), so no path writes a record for an approval that was refused.
- The window that replaces W1 (record present, label not yet) yields the ordinary "QA review required" block instead of the alarming forged-label one — two bd calls wide, fail-closed, and unavoidable without a lock.

### FOUR CORRECTIONS to the prior session's work

1. `IDEM_REF_SOURCE` was set inside a function called as `h=$(f)` — a subshell, so the value died and the envelope rendered `... via )`. Caught by a new assertion, not by inspection. Function reshaped to `set_idempotency_reference` returning both values by global.
2. `APPROVE-COMMIT ORDER` comment implied all three ordering rules were changes. Rule 2 (baseline before tracker) was already the order at HEAD; rewritten to name W1/W2/W3 and which mechanism closes each.
3. "three live occurrences" appeared in a shipped script comment, HOOKS.md and the spec header. Only ONE occurrence is recorded in Beads. All three now cite the recorded occurrence plus the deterministic reproduction. HOOKS.md also said "Two ordering rules" above three bullets.
4. An `assert_contains` was passed a whole hook file as its haystack, which made `grep -q` close the pipe and print `printf: write error: Broken pipe` mid-run. Replaced with a file-based grep.

### KNOWN RESIDUAL (found by probing, reproduced, pinned as section H)

Tracker empty AND real un-baselined dirt (work written by a helper, never seen by post-edit.sh — LESSONS.md/bi3.2): the Stop blocks on the git half while the persisted report still witnesses the PREVIOUS approval, so a bare `approve` no-ops (exit 0) and the block stands. Verified: block -> bare approve no-ops -> still block -> full printed recipe (its step 2 re-persists the report) -> ALLOW. The gz3 acceptance criterion holds (the printed remediation recovers); the residual only bites when a step of it is skipped. QA AUDIT CORRECTION (rubric i1 revision, item 2) — I got a load-bearing fact wrong in review iteration 1. Owning it here, plainly, because the correction matters more than the record looking clean.

## What I claimed vs what the artifact says

Iteration 1's artifact (R1-F3), the packet header, and my `qa-plan` doc all stated that per-file `impact_of` **"returned 0 nodes for every file"**, attributed to bash cross-file linkage being invisible to tree-sitter. That is **false**. The impact report actually contains substantial graph data:

| file | nodes | callers (depth 5) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `.claude/scripts/qa-gate.sh` | 1275 | **925** |
| `.claude/scripts/verify-before-stop.sh` | 383 | 5 |
| `.claude/tests/component/lib/shim.sh` | 26 | 6 |
| `.claude/mcp/bd-mcp/src/tools/bd_qa.js` | 37 | 2 |
| the three component specs | 142 / 64 / 93 | 0 each |
| `CHANGELOG.md`, `docs/HOOKS.md` | — | not in the index (markdown) |
| 6 × `/tmp` probe paths | — | skipped, outside the analyzed project |

Nine project entries, not 14 (now 15 entries with CHANGELOG.md added). The grader's numbers were right on every point.

## Root cause

Each per-file entry stores the **raw MCP response envelope** `{ok, headline, data, llm_observations}`, so the payload lives at `.impact.data.nodes`. Reading `.impact.nodes` returns `null`; `length` of `null` is `0`. The misread produces a confident zero for every file **with no error surfaced** — the artifact was summarized through a path that could only ever yield zero, and the resulting claim was self-consistent enough to survive into three separate documents. I reproduced the error before correcting it: my own first `jq` this spawn made exactly the same mistake, which is how I found the envelope.

## Does the regression assessment still hold? Yes — and the corrected data supports it better than the false premise did

This is my judgment, recorded as mine rather than inherited from the grader's "not in question."

I decomposed qa-gate.sh's 925 callers instead of taking the count at face value:
- **670 (72%)** are inside the seven byte-identical e2e fixture **copies** of the very scripts under review. Not independent risk: all 14 copies are cmp-verified identical and the L3 drift guard (175/175) exists to pin exactly that.
- **155 (17%)** are in other test files. **100 (11%)** are in production files.
- By node kind: **648 (70%) are `variable`** — name-only edges, which the code-graph tool documents as deliberately high-recall. A `variable` named `org` in `bd-github-link.sh`, or a JS `<module>` in an e2e fixture's `server/index.js`, is not a caller of a bash function.
- Of the **26 depth-1 production function-kind** edges, 15 are MCP tool registrars (`register*Tools`) and 9 are local helpers in unrelated scripts (`frame_grep`, `_hs_frame`, `read_override`, `_model_roles_value`, `current_pin`, `plugin_json_version`, `detect_v2_install`, `manifest_root_rows`). **Exactly two are genuine**, both in `verify-before-stop.sh` (`:233 get_recorded_repo`, `:455 read_iteration`).
- Corroborated textually: `verify-before-stop.sh` references `qa-gate.sh` **45** times; `review-check.sh` once; `session-start.sh` 4; `install.sh` 3; `subagent-start.sh` 3; `statusline.sh` 1.

So the genuine coupling the graph identifies is `verify-before-stop.sh` and secondarily `review-check.sh` — precisely the surface this review exercised hardest. `verify-before-stop.sh` is itself in the change set and is driven end-to-end by the new spec's 93 assertions including the section-F approve/Stop straddles that are the whole point of W3; `review-check.sh gate` I ran live against the real comment stream.

**One check the corrected reading newly prompted, which I then ran.** The W2 fix moves `clear_current_task` to AFTER the tracker truncation, and ten scripts read `.qa-tracking/current-task`. Direction of the move: it leaves the file populated **longer**, which is strictly the safer direction — a reader either sees the still-active task (correct, approve in flight) or sees it cleared with nothing left to review. The old order *was* the W2 bug. `statusline.sh:117` reads the file directly rather than via the helper, so worst case it renders the approved state a fraction of a second differently; cosmetic, no gate consequence. The ordering is now test-pinned by the spec's section F.

**Honest caveat.** That convergence was fortunate, not designed. The false premise did not change what I checked, but it removed a cross-check I believed I had. Had the graph pointed at a subsystem outside my manual net, the misread would have concealed it. That is the real cost of the error, and it is why I am recording the root cause rather than just the corrected numbers.

## Corrected everywhere

`review-artifact-...-r2.json` (R2-F3 supersedes R1-F3), the packet header, and `qa-plan` v3. R1-F2 (stale CHANGELOG recipe) is **resolved** by the implementer's fix — recorded in prose rather than via `qa-gate.sh resolve-finding`, because that verb requires a `--test` reference and no test asserts CHANGELOG body text; citing one would be fabricated evidence.

# SPEC — 3mg.1 V4 pt1: verify PR#2 + shared denylist + gate-baseline v2 + I8 fix (epic 3mg)

Source: `docs/plans/v4-trimodel.md` Phase V4. PR #2 (impact-report path relativisation) is ALREADY MERGED into this branch (commit 64008eb, local, unpushed). The worktree= approval token + bounded Stop-side resolution + the 3 transcript-scenario fixtures are 3mg.2 — NOT this task. Canonical model (decided): per-worktree tracking, per-worktree hash, per-worktree baseline; hash inputs stay byte-literal (no git normalization). This task lands the shared infrastructure; 3mg.2 lands the cross-checkout resolution on top.

## Deliverable 0 — VERIFY PR#2 (reconcile the stale L1 test) — DO THIS FIRST
The merge surfaced a latent gap: PR #2 changed `impact-report.sh` (foreign/non-git paths now return an explicit `skipped:` record instead of an error; relative-path handling changed via `relativize_for_impact`), but `.claude/scripts/tests/impact-report.test.sh` Section 4 still asserts the PRE-PR#2 contract. CI missed it because Section 4 is the "real code-graph present" live section, which SKIPS in CI (no code-graph server) — it only fails locally where code-graph runs. Two failing assertions:
- "rejected entry carries impact.error.message" — expects pattern `project-relative`; new behavior returns `skipped: path is outside the analyzed project …`.
- "relative entry resolved (impact.ok=true)" — expects true; new behavior returns false (relative-vs-absolute handling changed).
FIX: read PR #2's actual `relativize_for_impact` behavior in impact-report.sh and reconcile Section 4 to the NEW contract — a foreign/non-git path is a `skip` (assert the skip record shape PR #2 emits, e.g. impact.ok=false with the skip message / a `skipped` marker), and correct the relative-entry expectation to what the relativisation actually produces (read the code; if PR #2 intends changed-files entries to be absolute and a bare-relative entry is now a skip, assert that). This is legitimately "verify PR #2" — the same defect exists on main; note it. Confirm the L2 `impact-report-paths.sh` (PR #2's spec) stays green. Do NOT weaken the test to pass — assert the CORRECT new behavior.

## Deliverable 1 — shared denylist lib `.claude/scripts/workflow-denylist.sh` (NEW)
Three drifted copies of the denylist regex exist: `impact-report.sh:~116`, `post-edit.sh`, `verify-before-stop.sh` (only verify-before-stop's includes `(^|/)\.claude/worktrees/` + the e2e-fixture-churn alternation). Consolidate into ONE source:
- NEW `.claude/scripts/workflow-denylist.sh` — **FLAT under scripts/, NOT lib/** (the fixture-sync glob `make sync-fixtures` and the vitest drift guard's `listCanonicalHookScripts` enumerate flat `.claude/scripts/*.sh` only; a nested lib/ would silently not sync into the 7 fixtures and break their sourced hooks). Define exactly: `WORKFLOW_DENYLIST_REGEX='<consolidated>'` + `workflow_denylisted() { [[ "$1" =~ $WORKFLOW_DENYLIST_REGEX ]]; }` (0=drop/1=keep). No side effects; bash 3.2.
- Consolidated regex = the current base ∪ `(^|/)\.claude/worktrees/` ∪ the e2e-fixture-churn alternation (both currently Stop-only) ∪ NEW memory patterns `(^|/)MEMORY\.md$` and `(^|/)\.claude/memory/`. Deliberately NOT denylisted: `CLAUDE.md` (behavior-bearing; session-start injects it), `LESSONS.md`/`HANDOFF.md` (audit deliverables; the *.md doc-only fast path already handles them when alone). `qa-block-*.md` lives under $HOME → out of repo, no pattern needed.
- Rewire all three consumers to `source` it **BASH_SOURCE-relative** (NOT PROJECT_DIR-relative — 3mg.2's cross-worktree resolution runs the primary's script with CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR=<worktree>). Keep each consumer's local var name (`DENYLIST_REGEX="$WORKFLOW_DENYLIST_REGEX"`) so diffs stay minimal. Missing-lib behavior: impact-report.sh → hash fails (upstream already treats empty hash as fail-closed); post-edit.sh → skip filtering + track anyway (over-track = fail-closed for the gate; still emit `{}`); verify-before-stop.sh → block (unverifiable class).
- EFFECT (all desirable, name them in the commit/CHANGELOG): post-edit stops tracking harness-worktree paths (they polluted the hash while invisible to Stop); the hash and the gate's view finally agree; memory files exit the reviewable set BEFORE F1 doc-only classification (a memory-only change set → `empty` fast path, never `doc-only`).
- **HASH MIGRATION (fail-closed, documented):** changing the denylist changes recomputed hashes → in-flight pre-3mg.1 approvals hit LABEL_WITHOUT_RECORD and re-block until a fresh `qa-gate enter` + re-approve. Ship ALL denylist additions in ONE landing = ONE migration. Document in CHANGELOG + HOOKS.md.

## Deliverable 2 — gate-baseline v2
Replace `approved-baseline` with a versioned per-checkout `.qa-tracking/gate-baseline`:
```
# gate-baseline v1
head=<sha|none> / captured_at=<ts> / captured_by=session-start|qa-gate-enter|qa-gate-approve
--
<LC_ALL=C-sorted `git status --porcelain` lines>
```
- Writers: session-start.sh (full snapshot, only when no active task — in-flight cycles stay gated), qa-gate.sh enter (write-if-missing, minus already-tracked changed-files entries so session work is never baselined), approve (full refresh as today). 
- **FIX the latent `-d "$PROJECT_DIR/.git"` bug** (verify-before-stop.sh:541,626; qa-gate.sh write_approved_baseline): a linked worktree's `.git` is a FILE, so `-d` silently disables baseline/fallback there. Use `git -C "$PROJECT_DIR" rev-parse --git-dir >/dev/null 2>&1` presence, not `-d .git`.
- Consumer: verify-before-stop.sh's git-status fallback (~line 626) reads lines-after-`--` of gate-baseline via `comm -23`; legacy `approved-baseline` read as fallback for ONE release, deleted on first v2 write. **No hash-side subtraction** (verified: changed-files.txt is fed only by post-edit from actual tool edits — pre-existing dirt cannot enter it; an edited already-dirty file correctly gates). This fixes transcript scenario 1 (pre-existing dirty primary): session-start baseline → the git-fallback subtracts pre-existing dirt so the gate evaluates only the session's delta.

## Deliverable 3 — I8 cross-repo guard fix
`detect_cross_repo` (verify-before-stop.sh:247) currently compares `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` strings, so a same-repo LINKED WORKTREE (different toplevel, same repo) trips the I8 block. Fix: compare canonical `git -C <dir> rev-parse --git-common-dir` (resolved, e.g. via `cd … && pwd -P`) of the recorded vs current root — same repo via a linked worktree → no block; genuinely different repo → still blocks (failure-cross-repo.sh spec stays green). Recorded path deleted/unresolvable → mismatch (fail closed). `current-task.sh`'s cwd-based fingerprint WRITE semantics are deliberately unchanged (keep I8's cwd basis for genuine cross-repo detection).

## Tests
- L1 `denylist-source.test.sh` (NEW): all three consumers source `workflow-denylist.sh`; no residual literal `DENYLIST_REGEX='(^…'` definitions in them. META: a fixture copy re-declaring a literal regex must fail the check.
- L2 `denylist-shared.sh` (NEW): a canary pattern added once to the lib filters in post-edit tracking, `--hash-only`, AND Stop detection (three consumers, one edit — **the spec must `cp` over the fixture's symlink before sed**, or it mutates the real script); memory-only set (`MEMORY.md` + `.claude/memory/x.md`) → F1 `empty` fast path (NOT doc-only); mixed memory+`src/a.ts` → Stop lists only `src/a.ts`; hash excludes memory lines; hash-migration: an approval recorded, then a pattern added matching a tracked path → LABEL_WITHOUT_RECORD block (fail closed), `enter`+re-approve recovers. META: the canary is the sensitivity proof.
- L2 `gate-baseline-v2.sh` (NEW; may supersede an existing qa-gate-baseline spec — rewrite the enter case since enter no longer just deletes): **transcript scenario 1** — repo with 3 pre-dirty files; session-start baseline written; VBS allows; new dirt post-baseline blocks naming only the new path (both fail on pre-fix code). **META (spec-mandated): truncate the baseline file to empty → the pre-existing-dirt-exclusion assertion must fail (gate blocks on all 3).** Also: enter write-if-missing + tracker subtraction; approve full-refresh; legacy approved-baseline fallback read; the `-d .git`→rev-parse fix (a linked-worktree `.git`-file case where baseline now works).
- Extend `failure-cross-repo.sh`: I8 still blocks true cross-repo; a same-repo linked worktree no longer trips I8 (common-dir compare). Keep its existing META.
- Reconciled `impact-report.test.sh` (deliverable 0) green; PR#2's `impact-report-paths.sh` still green.

## Constraints
bash 3.2 + jq; denylist lib FLAT + sourced BASH_SOURCE-relative; gate paths fail CLOSED (block/refuse on unverifiable), SessionStart fail-open (exit 0); no hash-side baseline subtraction; ONE denylist landing = ONE hash migration (documented); do NOT implement the worktree= token / Stop-side resolution / scenario-2/3 fixtures (3mg.2); TEXT-anchored METAs; no version bump; re-sync the touched canonical scripts (impact-report.sh if you touch it — you shouldn't for deliverable 0 which is test-only; post-edit.sh, verify-before-stop.sh, session-start.sh, qa-gate.sh, and the NEW workflow-denylist.sh) into the 7 fixtures via `make sync-fixtures` (it exists now, from PR#2).

Full L1 (`make test`) GREEN — impact-report.test.sh reconciled + green locally (code-graph present); L2 (`bash .claude/tests/component/run.sh`) GREEN incl. the new denylist + gate-baseline specs + the scenario-1 META; `make lint`; `make sync-fixtures` + `make test-e2e-unit` drift guard green (workflow-denylist.sh synced into all 7 fixtures); the hash-migration behavior documented. - CWD outside the repo → explicit skip (not an error).

- Section 4's fixture is a `mktemp -d` (NOT a git repo), so the non-git fallback branch runs, which can only anchor the literal `$PROJECT_DIR/` prefix ⇒ a bare-relative entry is deterministically a skip there.

+#
+# `enter` arms a review cycle mid-session: files the session ALREADY edited

+# the session's own work "pre-existing" and hand it a free pass. Tracked
+# entries are absolute (post-edit records `tool_input.file_path` verbatim)
+# while porcelain paths are repo-relative, so we match on both spellings.
+gate_baseline_exclude_tracked() {
+    local status_out="$1"
+    local tracking="$QA_TRACKING_DIR/changed-files.txt"
+    [ -s "$tracking" ] || { printf '%s' "$status_out"; return 0; }
+
+    local tmp_tracked
+    tmp_tracked=$(mktemp -t gate-baseline-tracked.XXXXXX 2>/dev/null) || {
+        printf '%s' "$status_out"; return 0
+    }
+    local t
+    while IFS= read -r t; do
+        [ -z "$t" ] && continue
+        printf '%s\n' "$t"
+        case "$t" in
+            "$PROJECT_DIR"/*) printf '%s\n' "${t#"$PROJECT_DIR"/}" ;;
+        esac
+    done < "$tracking" | LC_ALL=C sort -u > "$tmp_tracked"
+
+    local line p kept=""
+    while IFS= read -r line; do
+        [ -z "$line" ] && continue
+        p="${line#???}"
+        # Rename/copy entries are "R  old -> new"; the destination is the
+        # path a tracker entry would name.
+        case "$p" in *" -> "*) p="${p##* -> }" ;; esac
+        if grep -qxF "$p" "$tmp_tracked" 2>/dev/null; then
+            continue
+        fi
+        kept="$kept$line
+"
+    done <<< "$status_out"
+    rm -f "$tmp_tracked" 2>/dev/null || true
+    # Trim the single trailing newline the accumulator adds.
+    printf '%s' "${kept%$'\n'}"

+### Changed (Phase V4 pt1 — one denylist, gate-baseline v2, I8 repo identity, epic 3mg, 2026-07-26)
+
+> **UPGRADE NOTE — one-time hash migration.** The change-set denylist changed,
+> so the Stop hook recomputes a DIFFERENT `change_set_hash` for any change set
+> containing a newly-filtered path. An approval recorded before this landing no
+> longer matches that hash: the gate emits `LABEL_WITHOUT_RECORD` and re-blocks
+> until the cycle is re-approved. That is the correct fail-closed direction — a
+> stale approval must not release — and every denylist addition in this release
+> ships in ONE landing, so an in-flight cycle pays the migration exactly once.
+> Recovery for a cycle caught mid-flight (see `docs/HOOKS.md`, "Denylist changes
+> are a hash migration"):
+>
+> ```bash
+> bd label remove <task-id> qa-approved     # retire the stale approval
+> bash .claude/scripts/qa-gate.sh enter <task-id>
+> bash .claude/scripts/impact-report.sh <task-id>
+> bash .claude/scripts/qa-gate.sh approve <task-id> '<summary>'
+> ```
+>
+> The `bd label remove` step is required: `enter` does not clear `qa-approved`,
+> and `approve` short-circuits as an idempotent no-op while that label is
+> present. (Pinned by `denylist-shared.sh` section C.)
+
+- **ONE denylist, three consumers.** New `.claude/scripts/workflow-denylist.sh`
+  defines `WORKFLOW_DENYLIST_REGEX` + `workflow_denylisted()`; `post-edit.sh`
+  (what gets TRACKED), `impact-report.sh` (what enters the change set and its
+  HASH) and `verify-before-stop.sh` (what needs REVIEW) all source it,
+  BASH_SOURCE-relative. The three copies had drifted: only the Stop hook's knew
+  about `.claude/worktrees/` and the e2e fixture churn, so post-edit tracked
+  worktree paths INTO the hash that the gate could not see — the hash and the
+  gate disagreed about what "the changes" were. Desirable effects, all now
+  guaranteed to move together: harness-worktree paths leave the tracked set,
+  the hash and the gate's view agree, and a change-set of only build/workflow
+  churn is `empty` rather than half-visible.
+- **Memory files are no longer reviewable work.** `MEMORY.md` and
+  `.claude/memory/` join the denylist, so they exit the change set BEFORE F1
+  doc-only classification: a memory-only change set now takes the `empty` fast
+  path (release, no gate record) instead of being auto-approved as `doc-only`
+  with a `[review bypass: F1 doc-only ...]` record about agent recall state.
+  `CLAUDE.md` (behaviour-bearing — session-start injects it), `LESSONS.md` and
+  `HANDOFF.md` (audit deliverables) are deliberately NOT denylisted.
+- **Missing-lib behaviour is fail-closed per consumer**: `impact-report.sh`
+  exits 3 (no hash, which upstream already treats as refuse-to-release),
+  `verify-before-stop.sh` BLOCKS with a remediation reason (after the
+  `stop_hook_active` circuit breaker, never before it), and `post-edit.sh`
+  tracks the path unfiltered — over-tracking is the fail-closed side for a hook
+  whose output feeds the gate.
+- **gate-baseline v2.** `.claude/.qa-tracking/approved-baseline` (a bare line
+  list, one writer) is superseded by `.claude/.qa-tracking/gate-baseline`, a
+  versioned file with a provenance header (`head=`, `captured_at=`,
+  `captured_by=`) over the `LC_ALL=C`-sorted `git status --porcelain` snapshot.
+  Three writers now: `session-start.sh` on arrival (only when no review cycle is
+  active — baselining an in-flight cycle would release its work unreviewed),
+  `qa-gate.sh enter` (write-if-missing, minus paths already in
+  `changed-files.txt` so the session's own edits are never baselined), and
+  `qa-gate.sh approve` (full refresh, as before). New subcommand
+  `qa-gate.sh baseline-capture [--by <who>] [--if-missing] [--exclude-tracked]`
+  so session-start has one implementation to call. The legacy file is read as a
+  fallback for one release and deleted on the first v2 write. Closes the
+  "session opened in an already-dirty repo blocks on dirt the session never
+  made" case; there is deliberately NO hash-side subtraction (the baseline is
+  subtracted only in the git fallback, so editing an already-dirty file still
+  gates).
+- **`-d "$PROJECT_DIR/.git"` replaced by `git rev-parse --git-dir`** in
+  `verify-before-stop.sh` and `qa-gate.sh`. In a LINKED WORKTREE `.git` is a
+  FILE, so the old predicate answered "not a git repo" and silently disabled
+  both the baseline writer and the Stop gate's git-status fallback — with an
+  empty `changed-files.txt` the gate then had no detector at all and FAILED
+  OPEN, in exactly the `isolation: "worktree"` topology the plugin tells agents
+  to use.
+- **I8 cross-repo guard compares REPOSITORY identity, not checkout identity.**
+  `detect_cross_repo` used `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`, which is
+  per-checkout, so a Stop fired from a linked worktree of the SAME repo the task
+  was claimed in tripped the cross-repo block. It now compares the
+  symlink-resolved `git rev-parse --git-common-dir`, which every worktree of a
+  repo shares and which differs across repos. A genuinely different repo still
+  blocks; a recorded repo path that no longer resolves is still a mismatch
+  (fail closed).

+  source the lib, none carries a literal regex; 3 METAs) and new L2
+  `denylist-shared.sh` (canary sensitivity across all three consumers, memory
+  patterns, hash migration) + `gate-baseline-v2.sh` (transcript scenario 1 with
+  the spec-mandated truncate-the-baseline META, the three writers, the legacy
+  fallback, the linked-worktree case). `failure-cross-repo.sh` gains the
+  worktree cases; `qa-gate-baseline.sh` is retargeted at the v2 file; four
+  existing METAs that copied a hook to a fixture ROOT now copy it into

+  lib and blocks for the wrong reason — a silent false pass).

+  longer contain the server's absolute-path validation error.

#!/bin/bash
# workflow-denylist.sh — THE definition of "paths the workflow never treats
# as reviewable work" (claude-workflow-plugin-3mg.1, v4 Phase V4).
#
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS
# --------------------
# Three scripts each need the same answer to "is this path reviewable?":
#
#   post-edit.sh           what gets TRACKED into changed-files.txt
#   impact-report.sh       what enters the canonical change set + its HASH
#   verify-before-stop.sh  what the Stop gate treats as needing REVIEW
#
# They each carried their own copy of the regex and the copies DRIFTED:
# only verify-before-stop's knew about `.claude/worktrees/` and the e2e
# fixture-churn alternation. The consequence was not cosmetic — post-edit
# tracked harness-worktree paths that the Stop gate could not see, so those
# paths entered the change-set hash while being invisible to the gate's own
# view of the change set. The hash and the gate disagreed about what "the
# changes" even were.
#
# One definition, three consumers. A change here changes all three at once,
# which is the point — see the HASH MIGRATION note below for the cost.
#
# CONTRACT
# --------
#   WORKFLOW_DENYLIST_REGEX   ERE, for `[[ "$p" =~ $WORKFLOW_DENYLIST_REGEX ]]`
#   workflow_denylisted <path>
#       exit 0  -> DROP the path (build artifact / workflow-internal churn)
#       exit 1  -> KEEP the path (reviewable work)
#
# Sourcing convention (all three consumers): resolve this file relative to
# ${BASH_SOURCE[0]} of the CONSUMER, never relative to $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR.
# A hook script may legitimately run with CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR pointing at a
# DIFFERENT checkout than the one the script itself lives in (the primary's
# gate evaluating a worktree); the lib must always be the sibling of the
# script that sources it.
#
# No side effects: this file defines one variable and one function and does
# nothing else. bash 3.2 compatible (no associative arrays, no ${x^^}).
#
# WHAT IS DELIBERATELY *NOT* DENYLISTED
# -------------------------------------
#   CLAUDE.md   behaviour-bearing (session-start injects it) — reviewable.
#   LESSONS.md  audit deliverable — reviewable.
#   HANDOFF.md  audit deliverable — reviewable.
#   .beads/*.jsonl, .claude/.qa-tracking/*
#               NOT denylisted: they stay in the change set / audit trail.
#               verify-before-stop.sh classifies them separately via
#               is_beads_or_gate_path (a change set consisting solely of
#               them is fast-path eligible). Denylisting them would erase
#               them from the hash too, which is not the intent.
# The *.md doc-only fast path (F1) already handles the three .md files above
# when they change alone.
#
# HASH MIGRATION (fail-closed, one landing = one migration)
# ---------------------------------------------------------
# change_set_hash is a sha256 over the DENYLIST-FILTERED changed-files list.
# Editing this regex therefore changes the recomputed hash for any change set
# containing a newly-(un)matched path. An approval recorded before the edit no
# longer matches the hash the Stop hook recomputes after it, so the gate emits
# LABEL_WITHOUT_RECORD and re-blocks until a fresh `qa-gate.sh enter` +
# re-approve. That is the correct fail-closed direction (a stale approval must
# not release), but it is USER-VISIBLE friction: ship denylist additions in ONE
# landing so in-flight cycles pay the migration exactly once. See CHANGELOG
# and docs/HOOKS.md ("Denylist changes are a hash migration").

# Consolidated regex. Alternation order is cosmetic (ERE alternation is
# unordered for a boolean match); grouped by intent for readability.
#
#   1. build / dependency output directories
#   2. .claude/worktrees/       parallel-agent scratch checkouts. Never a
#                               deliverable; the worktree's own gate reviews
#                               its work in situ.
#   3. e2e fixture churn        .claude/tests/e2e/fixtures/<f>/.claude/{scripts,beads}
#                               and <f>/.beads — rewritten mechanically by the
#                               harness's run-start sync and by the live run's
#                               own bd writes. ANTI-OVERREACH: scoped to those
#                               subtrees only, so a real edit to a fixture's
#                               fixture.yaml / src/ is still reviewable.
#   4. memory files             MEMORY.md (the auto-memory index) and
#                               .claude/memory/. Agent-written recall state,
#                               not deliverables; they must leave the
#                               reviewable set BEFORE F1 doc-only
#                               classification so a memory-only change set is
#                               `empty` (nothing to review) rather than
#                               `doc-only` (auto-approved WITH a gate record).
#   5. lock / map / minified / compiled artifacts
WORKFLOW_DENYLIST_REGEX='(^|/)(node_modules|dist|build|coverage|\.git|\.next|\.nuxt|target|__pycache__)/|(^|/)\.claude/worktrees/|(^|/)\.claude/tests/e2e/fixtures/[^/]+/(\.claude/(scripts|beads)|\.beads)/|(^|/)MEMORY\.md$|(^|/)\.claude/memory/|\.(lock|lockb|map|pyc)$|\.min\.(js|css)$|(^|/)(pnpm-lock\.yaml|package-lock\.json|yarn\.lock|bun\.lockb|Cargo\.lock|poetry\.lock|go\.sum)$'

# workflow_denylisted <path> — 0 = drop it, 1 = keep it.
workflow_denylisted() {
    [ -n "${1:-}" ] || return 1
    [[ "$1" =~ $WORKFLOW_DENYLIST_REGEX ]]
}

#!/bin/bash
# denylist-source.test.sh — claude-workflow-plugin-3mg.1 (v4 Phase V4).
#
# ONE definition of "which paths the workflow treats as reviewable", three
# consumers. This L1 spec is the structural guard on that invariant: it reads
# the shipped scripts as TEXT and refuses a tree in which any consumer has
# grown its own copy of the regex again.
#
# WHY A STRUCTURAL TEST AND NOT ONLY A BEHAVIOURAL ONE
# ----------------------------------------------------
# The three copies that 3mg.1 consolidated did not diverge in one dramatic
# commit; they drifted, one alternative at a time, over three separate fixes.
# Only verify-before-stop.sh's copy ever learned about `.claude/worktrees/`
# and the e2e fixture churn, so post-edit.sh tracked worktree paths INTO the
# change-set hash that the Stop gate could not see — the hash and the gate
# disagreed about what "the changes" were. A behavioural spec catches a
# divergence only for the pattern it happens to probe (that is L2's
# denylist-shared.sh, which drives a canary through all three consumers).
# THIS spec catches the re-introduction itself, for every pattern at once,
# the moment someone pastes a literal regex back into a consumer.
#
# ASSERTIONS
#   1. .claude/scripts/workflow-denylist.sh exists, is FLAT under scripts/
#      (the fixture-sync glob and the vitest drift guard enumerate flat
#      `.claude/scripts/*.sh` only — a nested lib/ would silently not sync
#      into the 7 e2e fixtures and break their sourced hooks), defines
#      WORKFLOW_DENYLIST_REGEX + workflow_denylisted, and parses.
#   2. Each of the three consumers SOURCES it, resolved BASH_SOURCE-relative
#      (never $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR-relative: 3mg.2 runs the primary checkout's
#      hook with CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR pointing at a worktree).
#   3. No consumer carries a literal `DENYLIST_REGEX='(^...` definition of
#      its own. Assigning FROM the shared variable is the sanctioned form.
#
# META-TEST: a fixture copy of a consumer that re-declares a literal regex
# must FAIL check 3, and one with its source line deleted must FAIL check 2.
# Without those, both checks could be vacuously green.
#
# Exit codes:
#   0  all assertions pass and the META-TESTs flag the broken fixtures
#   1  one or more assertions failed

set -u

PASS=0
FAIL=0
FAILED_TESTS=()

PROJECT_DIR="${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/../../.." && pwd)}"
SCRIPTS_DIR="$PROJECT_DIR/.claude/scripts"
LIB="$SCRIPTS_DIR/workflow-denylist.sh"

# The three consumers, by design: what gets TRACKED, what enters the change
# set + its HASH, what the Stop gate treats as needing REVIEW.
CONSUMERS="impact-report.sh post-edit.sh verify-before-stop.sh"

assert_eq() {
    local name="$1" expected="$2" actual="$3"
    if [ "$expected" = "$actual" ]; then
        PASS=$((PASS + 1))
        printf '  PASS: %s\n' "$name"
    else
        FAIL=$((FAIL + 1))
        FAILED_TESTS+=("$name")
        printf '  FAIL: %s\n    expected: %s\n    actual:   %s\n' \
            "$name" "$expected" "$actual"
    fi
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The two checkers. Both take a FILE so the META-TESTs can run them against
# deliberately broken fixture copies — the assertion and its sensitivity
# proof then exercise byte-identical logic.

# check_sources_lib <file> — 0 when the file sources workflow-denylist.sh
# BASH_SOURCE-relative; 1 when it sources it some other way (e.g. anchored on
# $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR); 2 when it does not source it at all; 3 no such file.
#
# Anchoring matters as much as sourcing: a $PROJECT_DIR-relative load reads
# the lib out of whatever checkout the hook was POINTED at rather than the
# one it was INSTALLED in, so a worktree missing the lib would silently
# degrade the primary's gate.
check_sources_lib() {
    local f="$1"
    [ -f "$f" ] || return 3
    grep -qE '(^|[[:space:]])(\.|source)[[:space:]]+"[^"]*/workflow-denylist\.sh"' "$f" || return 2
    grep -qF 'BASH_SOURCE' "$f" || return 1
    # The dir variable feeding the source must be derived from BASH_SOURCE,
    # not from PROJECT_DIR. One line, both tokens.
    grep -qE 'dirname "\$\{BASH_SOURCE\[0\]' "$f" || return 1

# denylist-regex definition, 1 when it does.
#

# single-quoted ERE starting with the `(^|/)` path anchor every copy of this
# regex has always opened with. `DENYLIST_REGEX="$WORKFLOW_DENYLIST_REGEX"`
# (double-quoted, a reference) is the sanctioned form and is NOT matched.
# The lib's own canonical definition is not a consumer and is never passed
# to this checker.
check_no_literal_regex() {
    local f="$1"
    [ -f "$f" ] || return 2
    if grep -qE "^[[:space:]]*[A-Za-z0-9_]*DENYLIST_REGEX='\(\^" "$f"; then
        return 1

# The L1 spec denylist-source.test.sh guards the STRUCTURE (all three source
# `.claude/scripts/workflow-denylist.sh`, none carries a literal copy). This
# spec guards the BEHAVIOUR: a single edit to the lib must move all three
# consumers at once, and the two patterns 3mg.1 added must actually change
# what the gate sees.
#
# WHY IT MATTERS (the defect that motivated the consolidation)
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Before 3mg.1 only verify-before-stop's copy knew about `.claude/worktrees/`
# and the e2e fixture churn. post-edit therefore TRACKED worktree paths that
# the Stop gate could not SEE: they entered the change-set hash the approval
# is bound to while being invisible to the gate's own view of the change set.
# The hash and the gate disagreed about what "the changes" were, and the only
# symptom was an occasional un-releasable approval nobody could explain.
#
# SECTIONS
#   A. CANARY (the sensitivity proof). One pattern added to the lib, three
#      consumers observed. Each leg is asserted BEFORE the edit (control) and
#      AFTER (effect), then the lib is restored and the control re-asserted —
#      so a green run cannot come from fixture drift.
#   B. MEMORY PATTERNS (shipped behaviour). MEMORY.md and .claude/memory/
#      leave the reviewable set BEFORE F1 doc-only classification, so a
#      memory-only change set releases with NO gate record instead of being
#      auto-approved as `doc-only`. CLAUDE.md is the anti-overreach control:
#      it is behaviour-bearing and must still gate.
#   C. HASH MIGRATION. Changing the denylist re-hashes recomputed change sets,
#      so an approval recorded before the change no longer matches and the
#      gate re-blocks (LABEL_WITHOUT_RECORD). That is the correct fail-closed
#      direction; this section pins BOTH the block and the recovery path that
#      actually works. See the C4 note — the remediation the block reason
#      prints is incomplete, and this spec pins that gap rather than papering
#      over it.
#
# THE SYMLINK HAZARD (read before editing this file)
# --------------------------------------------------
# mk_fixture SYMLINKS the plugin's real scripts into the fixture. An in-place
# `sed -i` against `$FIXTURE/.claude/scripts/workflow-denylist.sh` can rewrite
# THE REAL PLUGIN FILE through the link. Every mutation here goes through
# mutate_denylist_lib, which `rm`s the symlink and `cp`s a private copy FIRST,
# and A5 asserts afterwards that the real plugin lib is still canary-free.

set -u

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Helpers shared by all three sections.

# mutate_denylist_lib <fixture> <extra-alternative>
#   Replace the fixture's workflow-denylist.sh SYMLINK with a private copy
#   whose WORKFLOW_DENYLIST_REGEX gains <extra-alternative> as a leading
#   alternation branch. Prints the real (plugin) path it copied from so the
#   caller can restore the symlink.
mutate_denylist_lib() {
    local root="$1" alt="$2"
    local lib="$root/.claude/scripts/workflow-denylist.sh"
    local real
    real=$(readlink "$lib" 2>/dev/null || printf '%s' "$lib")
    rm -f "$lib"                 # break the link BEFORE writing anything
    cp "$real" "$lib"
    chmod +x "$lib"
    # -i.bak is the spelling both BSD and GNU sed accept.
    sed -i.bak "s#^WORKFLOW_DENYLIST_REGEX='#WORKFLOW_DENYLIST_REGEX='${alt}|#" "$lib"
    rm -f "$lib.bak"
    printf '%s' "$real"
}

restore_denylist_lib() {
    local root="$1" real="$2"
    local lib="$root/.claude/scripts/workflow-denylist.sh"
    rm -f "$lib"
    ln -sf "$real" "$lib"
}

# hash_of <fixture> <line>...  — the canonical change-set hash impact-report.sh
# computes for a tracker containing exactly <line>... This is the same
# `--hash-only` entry point qa-gate.sh approve and the Stop gate use, so the
# assertions below measure the shipping hash, not a re-implementation.
hash_of() {
    local root="$1"; shift
    local tracker="$root/.claude/.qa-tracking/changed-files.txt"
    : > "$tracker"
    local l
    for l in "$@"; do printf '%s\n' "$l" >> "$tracker"; done
    CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR="$root" bash "$root/.claude/scripts/impact-report.sh" --hash-only 2>/dev/null || echo ""
}

# track_path <fixture> <path> — drive post-edit.sh exactly as the PostToolUse
# hook does and report whether the path landed in changed-files.txt.
track_path() {
    local root="$1" p="$2"
    local tracker="$root/.claude/.qa-tracking/changed-files.txt"
    : > "$tracker"
    printf '{"tool_input":{"file_path":"%s"}}' "$p" \
        | CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR="$root" bash "$root/.claude/scripts/post-edit.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1
    if grep -qxF "$p" "$tracker" 2>/dev/null; then printf 'tracked'; else printf 'skipped'; fi
}

# stop_decision <fixture> — the Stop hook's verdict, "ALLOW" when it releases.
stop_decision() {
    local root="$1"
    printf '%s' '{"stop_reason":"end_turn","stop_hook_active":false}' \
        | CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR="$root" bash "$root/.claude/scripts/verify-before-stop.sh" 2>/dev/null \
        | tail -1 | jq -r '.decision // "ALLOW"' 2>/dev/null
}

stop_reason() {
    local root="$1"
    printf '%s' '{"stop_reason":"end_turn","stop_hook_active":false}' \
        | CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR="$root" bash "$root/.claude/scripts/verify-before-stop.sh" 2>/dev/null \
        | tail -1 | jq -r '.reason // empty' 2>/dev/null
}

# seed_tracker <fixture> <line>... — set changed-files.txt to exactly these.
seed_tracker() {
    local root="$1"; shift
    local tracker="$root/.claude/.qa-tracking/changed-files.txt"
    : > "$tracker"
    local l
    for l in "$@"; do printf '%s\n' "$l" >> "$tracker"; done
}

# fast_stack_stub <fixture> — a detect-stack.sh that reports no test/lint/type
# commands, so the technical-check pass is a no-op and the specs below measure
# the GATE decision rather than a toolchain run.
fast_stack_stub() {
    local root="$1"
    rm -f "$root/.claude/scripts/detect-stack.sh"
    printf '#!/bin/bash\nprintf %s\n' "'{\"runner\":\"npm\",\"test_cmd\":\"\",\"lint_cmd\":\"\",\"type_cmd\":\"\"}'" \
        > "$root/.claude/scripts/detect-stack.sh"
    chmod +x "$root/.claude/scripts/detect-stack.sh"
}

seed_tracker "$FC" "src/a.ts" "$MIGRATE_PATH"
bash "$CT_C" set "$TID_MIG"

# approval keeps releasing. A second Stop must not re-block.
seed_tracker "$FC" "src/a.ts" "$MIGRATE_PATH"
bash "$CT_C" set "$TID_MIG"
assert_eq "denylist-C6: the recovered approval keeps releasing (one landing, one migration)" \
    "ALLOW" "$(stop_decision "$FC")"

restore_denylist_lib "$FC" "$DL_REAL_C"
