title: 0.2 Make the QA-gate escalation cap binding
description: Live transcript showed ESCALATION: Iteration 7 (>= 3) still looping with full-suite re-runs. Add escalated state: qa-escalated label + J21 comment at first cap hit, skip-suite while escalated, auto-defer (qa-deferred) on next choiceless Stop, deferred=allow in verify-before-stop, SessionStart surfaces deferred, runner-vs-assertion failure classification. Spec 0.2.
notes:
IN PROGRESS: spec 0.2 implementation landed locally — escalation cap binding now in place. Awaiting QA review.

KEY DELIVERABLES:
- qa-gate.sh gains `choose <approve|continue|tech-debt|defer> <task-id> <note>` subcommand recording a J21 decision (comment + label/counter side effects) — keeps the audit trail thin.
- qa-gate.sh enter clears qa-deferred/qa-escalated + wipes per-iteration cache on every enter so a deferred task naturally resumes normal gating.
- wipe_iteration_state wipes new escalation cache files (last-test-rc, last-failed-checks, last-runner, escalation-posted).
- verify-before-stop.sh: new state machine.
  * Reads qa-deferred → allow Stop (single audited escape valve, principle 6).
  * Reads qa-escalated; at ITER > MAX_ITERATIONS + 1 → auto-defer (qa-deferred label + audit comment + allow).
  * While qa-escalated set, skip suite re-run; reuse cached FAILED_CHECKS + runner.
  * At first cap hit (ITER reaches MAX_ITERATIONS), set qa-escalated + post J21 ESCALATED comment exactly once (idempotent via marker file).
  * Failure classification: classify_test_failure() distinguishes runner (exit 126/127, "command not found", "Cannot find module", testcontainers TypeError, etc.) from assertion. Runner path leads with "Test suite failed to run (environment/runner issue — fix the environment before changing code)".
- session-start.sh: surfaces qa-deferred tasks ABOVE qa-pending with a banner naming the auto-defer flow.

DOCS:
- docs/WORKFLOW.md label table gained qa-escalated, qa-deferred, qa-gate-entered, qa-blocked (full lifecycle).
- docs/HOOKS.md got a new "Escalation State Machine (spec 0.2)" subsection plus updated qa-gate.sh entry mentioning the `choose` subcommand.

TESTS (all green):
- L1: .claude/scripts/tests/qa-gate-choose.test.sh — 30 assertions covering usage errors, all four choose branches, and re-enter clearing qa-deferred/qa-escalated.
- L2: .claude/tests/component/specs/escalation-binding.sh — 42 assertions:
  * Iterations 1-3 invoke the test shim (count climbs to 3) and iter 3 sets qa-escalated + posts one comment.
  * Iter 4 blocks with escalation wording WITHOUT re-running the suite (shim count stays at 3).
  * Iter 5 auto-defers (qa-deferred set, {} envelope, qa-pending preserved).
  * Subsequent Stop with qa-deferred allows immediately.
  * Re-enter clears qa-deferred/qa-escalated and the next Stop re-runs the suite (count to 4).
  * Runner-vs-assertion classification: exit 127 lands on "Test suite failed to run"; exit 1 with assertion output lands on "Tests failing".
  * Counter reset on active-task change: TID2/TID3 hold independent counter files.
  * ACCEPTANCE invariants: suite NOT re-run after cap (npm=3 across iters 4+5) AND qa-deferred recorded by iter 5.
  * META-TEST: mutating bump_iteration to always return 1 makes the cap-assertion fail (qa-escalated never set, npm count exceeds 3).

VERIFICATION:
- make lint  -> clean (shellcheck 0.11.x).
- make test  -> Total: 3 Passed: 3 Failed: 0 (L1).
- make test-all  -> Specs: 17 / Passed: 17 / Failed: 0; Assertions: 295/0.
- L2 escalation-binding.sh standalone summary: Assertions: Passed: 42 Failed: 0.

KEY DECISIONS:
- Auto-defer threshold: ITER > MAX_ITERATIONS + 1 (i.e., ITER >= MAX+2). Iter 3 = cap-hit (block + escalate). Iter 4 = one more escalated Stop (block, no suite re-run). Iter 5 = auto-defer. Matches the prompt's L2 walkthrough exactly.
- The `choose` subcommand is single-shot: approve delegates to cmd_approve, continue resets state, tech-debt calls tech-debt.sh add --bd-task, defer sets qa-deferred. Comments + labels are the record (principle 7).
- Per-task escalation cache files live alongside iteration-count.<task>. Naming: last-test-rc.<task>, last-failed-checks.<task>, last-runner.<task>, escalation-posted.<task> (idempotency marker). All wiped by wipe_iteration_state.
- classify_test_failure() is conservative: only patterns that are unambiguous runner-infra signals classify as runner; everything else stays "assertion" so we never mis-direct an assertion failure to "fix the environment".

FILES CHANGED:
- .claude/scripts/qa-gate.sh
- .claude/scripts/verify-before-stop.sh
- .claude/scripts/session-start.sh
- docs/WORKFLOW.md
- docs/HOOKS.md

FILES CREATED:
- .claude/scripts/tests/qa-gate-choose.test.sh
- .claude/tests/component/specs/escalation-binding.sh

NEW SUBCOMMANDS:
- qa-gate.sh choose <approve|continue|tech-debt|defer> <task-id> <note> [tech-debt: severity file:line effort]

LLM OBSERVATIONS:
- Spec text was internally inconsistent about auto-defer timing: high-level spec said "one more Stop" (iter 4), but the prompt's L2 walkthrough explicitly assigned iter 4 to "blocks with J21 wording" and iter 5 to "auto-defers". Followed the prompt's explicit walkthrough since it is the testable acceptance — iter 4 provides a warning shot, iter 5 acts.
- The escalation comment is idempotent via a marker file (escalation-posted.<task>) rather than a label check, because the label may be removed by `choose continue` and re-set on a future regression — the marker is part of wipe_iteration_state and therefore also clears at the same transitions, but it lives in the filesystem rather than Beads so we don't double up.
- Considered using the existing `qa-blocked` label to mark cap-hit but the spec wants the lifecycle preserved (qa-blocked is the human-pushed "QA found issues" state, distinct from the auto-set qa-escalated). Kept them separate so the audit reads cleanly.
- The `cmd_choose` uses `case` rather than dispatching to four sub-functions to keep audit-comment writing centralised — every choose path emits the same "QA-GATE CHOICE <choice>" prefix so a grep on `bd show` will surface all four.

NEXT STEP: QA review. Did NOT approve the gate; did NOT commit.

Enumeration mechanism (authoritative):
- API: GET https://api.anthropic.com/v1/models with header 'X-Api-Key: $ANTHROPIC_API_KEY' and 'anthropic-version: 2023-06-01'.
- Source: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/models-list
- Pagination: cursor-based via after_id/before_id, limit max 1000. 'Has_more' flag + last_id usable for follow-up.
- Response shape per model: { id (e.g. 'claude-opus-4-6'), display_name, created_at (RFC3339, descending — 'more recently released models are listed first'), type:'model', max_input_tokens (context window in tokens), max_tokens, capabilities.{effort:{low,medium,high,xhigh,max,supported},thinking:{...},...} }.
- No CLI listing (verified: 'claude --help' offers --model but no list subcommand).
- No publicly documented 'claude-opus-latest' style alias on the API response (only model-id versions).

Aliases in agent frontmatter and model: settings:
- Source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/model-config
- Subagent .md 'model:' frontmatter accepts: 'sonnet','opus','haiku','fable','inherit', or a full model ID (e.g. 'claude-opus-4-8'). Source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents (Supported frontmatter fields table).
- settings.json top-level 'model:' field accepts the same — plus 'default','best','opusplan' and the '[1m]' suffix for 1M context window variants (sonnet[1m], opus[1m], claude-opus-4-8[1m]).
- 'best' alias = Fable 5 where org has access, else latest Opus.

Implementation choice:
- Enumerate via curl GET /v1/models when ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is set; cache 1h; rank via .claude/model-ranking (family order, version DESC, unknown-newer = same prefix higher version); prefer the '[1m]' variant where the listing distinguishes context window via max_input_tokens (we'll filter family-prefix matches and pick max max_input_tokens, suffixed with [1m] when supported).
- Fail-open paths: no ANTHROPIC_API_KEY -> warn + keep pin; curl failure / timeout -> warn + keep pin; ranking empty -> warn + keep pin.

title: L3-live golden-cassette drift — structurally unfixable with current normalizer; 4 paths forward documented
description:
L3-live golden-cassette drift is structurally unfixable with the current normalizer in lib/goldenCompare.ts.

STATE AS OF 2026-05-11 ~22:00 UTC:
- 6 goldens committed (commit 7167ebd) — refreshed against Claude Opus 4.7.
- CI run 25689568757 on main: L1, L2, L3-vitest-unit, manifest-validate, shellcheck all GREEN. L3-live FAILED on all 6 fixtures with "golden cassette drift". L4 daily drift skipped (cron only).
- All 6 specs failed matchesGolden on tool sequence, subagent invocation count, hook firing sequence, or label transition list.
- ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is set in repo secrets (so L3-live runs for real on every PR).

WHAT WAS TRIED (over 2 days, ~$200+ in API spend):
1. Initial captures landed during Phase C of G8 (one capture per fixture, ~$30-60 total).
2. After CI infrastructure was fixed (musl/glibc native binary in workflow), L3-live actually ran for the first time on CI — and showed drift between the local captures and CI runs (run 25677101212).
3. Local refresh attempt with RECORD_GOLDEN=1 didn't write goldens because matchesGolden's contract is write-if-missing.
4. Deleted all goldens + ran live (~83 min, ~$30-60). 3 fixtures (qa-block-recovery, go-cli-refactor, monorepo-frontend-only) wrote cleanly via matchesGolden's path. 3 fixtures (node-react-auth, python-django-bug, multi-domain-signup) failed earlier assertions BEFORE matchesGolden:
   - node-react-auth: beadsTasksCreated==0 (orchestrator didn't create a bd task)
   - python-django-bug: AskUserQuestion permission denial
   - multi-domain-signup: beadsTaskCount==2 vs >=3 (orchestrator didn't decompose into 3 children)
5. Those 3 were promoted from same-run replays via lib/promoteReplay.ts.
6. After commit + push (7167ebd), CI L3-live STILL failed on all 6 fixtures.

ROOT CAUSE DIAGNOSIS:
Model behavior is non-deterministic enough that even fresh same-day goldens drift against subsequent runs. The matchesGolden normalizer in lib/goldenCompare.ts compares:
- tool call sequences (Bash/Read/Edit ordering)
- subagent invocation count
- hook firing sequence
- file write set
- Beads label transitions

Real-Claude variability shifts:
- Bash↔Read ordering swaps regularly (the model decides whether to peek-then-do or do-then-verify)
- Subagent count varies (orchestrator sometimes invokes devops for shim setup, sometimes not)
- Beads tasks created varies (depends on whether orchestrator decomposes into siblings or one task)
- Permission denials surface inconsistently (AskUserQuestion sometimes triggered)

The normalizer is too STRICT for the actual variability of the model.

WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY FIX IT (any of these — pick one):

A) MORE TOLERANT NORMALIZER (probably 1-2 days of work):
   - Compare structural SETS rather than ordered sequences for tools (allow Bash/Read order to swap freely).
   - Compare subagent COUNTS within tolerance (±1 invocation OK).
   - Make hook firing sequence position-agnostic.
   - Add a "looseness" score per fixture; allow some drift threshold.

B) SEMANTIC MATCHING (probably 3-5 days):
   - Stop matching tool sequences. Match outcomes: "did backend get invoked AT ALL", "did QA approve at the end", "were any auth-related files written", etc.
   - This is what the spec-level assertions already do (subagentInvoked, hookFired, etc.). matchesGolden becomes a "did the trace look broadly similar" check rather than a structural-snapshot.

C) DROP matchesGolden ENTIRELY (probably 1 hour):
   - Remove the assertion from all 6 specs.
   - Keep all the OTHER spec-level assertions (subagentInvoked, hookFired, noPermissionDenials, etc.) — those are what actually test plugin behavior.
   - L3-live becomes a "did the plugin route end-to-end correctly" test, not a "did the output look exactly like last time" test.
   - Lose: regression detection against past behavior shifts.
   - Gain: stable CI, no $30-60 re-record cost per drift event.

D) ADVISORY-ONLY L3-LIVE (5 min):
   - Set `continue-on-error: true` on the L3-live job in .github/workflows/test.yml.
   - L3-live still runs, still surfaces failures in the job summary, but doesn't block PR merging.
   - Keep matchesGolden as a "for visibility" signal.
   - This is the cheapest stopgap while deciding between A/B/C.

E) MOVE matchesGolden TO L4 ONLY (~30 min):
   - L3-live on PR keeps the spec-level assertions but drops matchesGolden.
   - L4 daily drift watch keeps matchesGolden as the canary signal.
   - Drift is documented, doesn't block PRs.

RECOMMENDED PATH: D (5 min) as immediate unblock, then C or E as the longer-term resolution. Avoid A/B until we know whether we actually use matchesGolden for anything in practice.

FILES IMPLICATED:
- .claude/tests/e2e/lib/goldenCompare.ts (the normalizer)
- .claude/tests/e2e/specs/*.spec.ts (6 specs, all call matchesGolden)
- .claude/tests/e2e/cassettes/golden/*.jsonl (6 captures committed)
- .github/workflows/test.yml (L3-live job config)
- /tmp/g8-rerecord-final.log (full vitest output from the last refresh attempt)

DON'T DO:
- Another fresh RECORD_GOLDEN run. Same drift wall, ~$30-60 wasted.
- Loosen the matchesGolden normalizer ad-hoc without a clear theory of which dimensions are noise vs signal.

title: Bug: .claude-plugin/plugin.json schema invalid for SDK plugin loader; hooks/commands/agents/skills fields all rejected

title: runFixture must set allowDangerouslySkipPermissions: true alongside permissionMode: bypassPermissions
description: QA review of G8 Phase A (claude-workflow-plugin-0wk.1) found that lib/runFixture.ts line 585 sets permissionMode: 'bypassPermissions' but does NOT pass allowDangerouslySkipPermissions: true in queryOpts. Per the @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk 0.2.138 d.ts (lines 1499 and 1512) and the public docs at code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/typescript, the SDK contract is 'allowDangerouslySkipPermissions is required when using permissionMode: bypassPermissions'. In the installed 0.2.138 sdk.mjs the flag is read with default false and forwarded to the underlying claude-code executable; whether the CLI hard-rejects bypassPermissions without the flag depends on the binary version. This must be fixed BEFORE the Phase A live capture is attempted, otherwise the live happy-path spec may fail with a permission-mode contract error rather than executing the orchestrator -> backend + frontend -> QA flow. Fix: in runFixture.ts queryOpts (line 578-589), add allowDangerouslySkipPermissions: opts.permissionMode === 'bypassPermissions' || (opts.permissionMode ?? 'bypassPermissions') === 'bypassPermissions' ? true : undefined  (or equivalent). Add a unit test asserting the flag is passed through. Verified in QA review of claude-workflow-plugin-0wk.1.

title: Bug: bd-github-link.sh hook regex misses canonical 'bd update <tid> --status closed' form
description:
The hook-mode regex on line 357-359 of bd-github-link.sh fails to detect the most natural close-task command. The regex is: 'bd[[:space:]]+update[[:space:]]+([A-Za-z0-9._-]+)[[:space:]]+(.+--status[[:space:]]+closed)'. The '.+' requires at least one character between the task id and '--status', so commands like 'bd update <tid> --status closed' (where there's only a single space) DON'T match. Verified by exhaustive shape testing:
- 'bd update foo --status closed': MISS
- 'bd update foo --status closed --notes bar': matches but BASH_REMATCH[1] captures 'foo --status closed' (incl. spaces), and the id-shape regex on line 365 then rejects it
- 'bd update --status closed foo' (alt order): MISS for same reason
- 'bd close foo': OK
- 'bd update foo -n notes --status closed': OK

The plugin's OWN verify-before-stop.sh uses the canonical form 'bd update "$CURRENT_TASK" --status closed' (lines 435, 742). When the orchestrator/QA agent later runs the same form via the Bash tool, the PostToolUse hook will silently fail to fire the gh-link comment.

SUGGESTED FIX: change '.+' to '.*' in both lines 357 and 358, AND fix the BASH_REMATCH[1] capture-group ambiguity (the alt-order regex captures the rest as group 1 and the tid as group 2, but the code reads BASH_REMATCH[1] unconditionally). Cleanest fix: a single regex with a named capture group, or a 4-way explicit if/elif checking each shape and assigning TASK_TO_CLOSE explicitly. SEVERITY: HIGH — breaks the I3 round-trip in the most common close path.
notes: FIXED: replaced the brittle three-alt regex (lines 357-359) with extract_tid_from_tail() — a token-walking helper that tolerates flag-before-id, --status closed (space) AND --status=closed (equals), multi-id (first wins), surrounding quotes, and shell redirections. The earlier regex's '.+' between tid and --status closed rejected the canonical single-space form used by verify-before-stop.sh:435 and :742. Verified by 10 assertions in .claude/scripts/tests/bd-github-link.test.sh Section 1 covering every shape the plugin emits plus negative cases (--status open, unrelated commands).
close_reason: Closed

title: Bug: bd-github-link.sh idempotency grep cannot find existing comment due to bold markdown mismatch
description: post_link_comment() in bd-github-link.sh writes a comment body of 'bd-link: tracked as **`<tid>`** (...)' (line 221, includes `**` bold markers) but the idempotency grep (line 234) looks for 'bd-link: tracked as `<tid>`' (NO bold markers). Because grep -F is fixed-string and the literal contains `**` between 'as ' and '`<tid>`', the grep never matches. Result: duplicate comments WILL be posted on every close — idempotency is broken. Reproduce: post a comment via the script, then run it again with the same task. Both runs will call gh comment. SUGGESTED FIX: change the grep pattern on line 234 to 'bd-link: tracked as **`<tid>`**' (match the actual body shape) OR change the body shape on line 221 to NOT use bold markers. Either keeps idempotency. SEVERITY: HIGH — duplicates pollute issue threads.
notes: FIXED: removed the bold markdown markers around the backtick-wrapped tid in gh_link_comment_body() (line 221, was 'tracked as **`tid`**', now 'tracked as `tid`'). The grep -F idempotency pattern in post_link_comment() (line 240, unchanged) now byte-aligns with the body. Added a comment block above gh_link_comment_body explaining the byte-alignment requirement so future edits can't drift again. Verified by 2 assertions in .claude/scripts/tests/bd-github-link.test.sh Section 3, including a stateful gh stub that proves '3 close fires => exactly 1 post'.
close_reason: Closed

title: Bug: bd-github-link.sh pr-create regex misses URL form references
description: The regex in bd-github-link.sh (--manual pr-create mode line 320-322 and hook mode line 416) only matches `Closes #N` or `Closes owner/repo#N` — it does NOT match URL form like `Closes https://github.com/x/y/issues/3`. The Phase 6b acceptance criteria explicitly require all three formats: '#42', 'owner/repo#7', 'https://github.com/x/y/issues/3'. The normalize_ref helper does support URLs (line 119-123) but the outer regex never feeds a URL into BASH_REMATCH. find_gh_link works correctly because it captures everything after gh-link: and feeds the whole thing to normalize_ref. Test: bash .claude/scripts/bd-github-link.sh --manual pr-create body.md where body.md has 'Resolves https://github.com/x/y/issues/3' — no gh-link is appended. SUGGESTED FIX: extend the regex to: ([Cc]loses|[Ff]ixes|[Rr]esolves)[[:space:]]+(https?://github\.com/[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+/[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+/(issues|pull)/[0-9]+|[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+/[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+#[0-9]+|#[0-9]+) on lines 320, 321, 322, and 416. SEVERITY: HIGH — explicitly part of Phase 6b's acceptance criteria.
notes: FIXED: extended pr-create regex on lines 320 (manual mode) and 416 (hook mode) to accept all four ref forms — '#N', 'owner/repo#N', 'https://.../issues/N', 'https://.../pull/N'. Used a single-alternation regex so BASH_REMATCH[2] always carries the ref regardless of form. BASH_REMATCH[3] holds the (issues|pull) sub-capture for URL forms (Bash ERE has no non-capturing groups; we just ignore it). Verified by 5 assertions in .claude/scripts/tests/bd-github-link.test.sh Section 2.
close_reason: Closed

QA-GATE BLOCKED at 2026-05-08T16:10:22Z: Phase 4 review found multiple defects contradicting the implementation report.

CRITICAL (must-fix):

1. bd update --status completed is invalid in Beads 0.47.1 (verify-before-stop.sh:258, :545). Valid value is closed. The || true swallows the error, so tasks never auto-close after QA approval. Self-hosting evidence: this very task is still in_progress with qa-gate-entered+qa-pending despite enter having succeeded.

2. epic-gate.sh files_changed_of second jq invocation is missing -R flag (epic-gate.sh:130). Result: always returns []. The shared-files subcommand reports my_files=[] even when notes contain a valid {"files_changed":[...]} block. The entire B2 file-intersection feature is non-functional. Reproduction: bash .claude/scripts/epic-gate.sh shared-files <id> on any task that has a JSON contract in notes.

3. rc=$? after if ! run_with_timeout always reports 0 under set -e (verify-before-stop.sh:303-308, 314-319, 326-331). The timeout-vs-fail distinction is silently broken. Failed test runs report 'Tests failing (exit 0)' regardless of actual exit code. Reproduction: synthesize an override .claude/test-cmd that exits 7; the block reason says exit 0.

4. get_current_task fallback to bd list --status in_progress | jq .[0].id (verify-before-stop.sh:91-92, post-edit.sh:32-33, intent-router.sh:23-24). When the helper file is empty (which happens when qa-gate.sh enter's best-effort write_current_task silently fails — exactly the case for THIS task), the fallback picks an arbitrary in_progress task. Defeats F3's single-source-of-truth promise and reintroduces the brittle 'first in_progress' anti-pattern Phase 1 was supposed to remove.

MATERIAL FEATURE GAPS:

5. Iteration counter leaks across tasks. Counter file is at a fixed path, not keyed by task_id; only approve clears it. If a user abandons task A at iter=3 and starts task B without approving A, B begins at iter=4. Implementation report explicitly claims 'Verify it doesn't leak across tasks (different task_id should reset)' — that test would fail. Reproduction: set iteration-count=3 with task A as current-task, switch current-task to B, fire vbs — counter becomes 4 not 1.

6. J21 decision-gate options only surface on FAILED_CHECKS path (verify-before-stop.sh:375-388). The QA-required path (technical checks passed but no QA approval yet) never includes the options, even at iter>=3. The plan calls for 'decision gate at the end: present options' — currently the more common case (clean tech-checks waiting on QA) never sees the options.

LESSER CONCERNS (recommended follow-ups):

7. intent-router.sh:53-62 only computes CURRENT_TASK inside if command -v bd && [ -d .beads ]. When bd is unavailable, the helper-file value is silently dropped, contradicting the F3 docstring. Move the F3 read out of the bd-conditional block.

8. prevent-orchestrator-edits.sh case '*orchestrator*' is over-broad — 'data-orchestrator-pipeline' or any other subagent name containing the substring would be blocked. Tighten the match to exact identifiers.

9. compute_intent_payload diff_summary contains literal newlines in jq pretty-printed output. The OUTER block-reason envelope handles this via jq -Rs, but when the LLM extracts the inner JSON code-block as text and parses it, control characters U+0000-U+001F in strings are technically invalid per RFC 8259. Use jq -c (compact) for the inner payload.

WHAT WORKS:

- Marker bypass remains closed.
- qa-gate.sh enter/status/approve/block flow + atomicity + rollback.
- F3 helper file when bd is initialized AND helper file is non-empty.
- detect-stack.sh polyglot detection across npm/pytest/go/cargo/maven/gradle/phpunit/rake/swift/dotnet/make + .claude/{test,lint,type}-cmd overrides.
- F1 doc-only fast path WITH a current-task auto-approves correctly.
- F1 doc-only WITHOUT a current-task and no other in_progress task falls through with QA-required block (but breaks when there's any other in_progress task — see Issue 4).
- All hook outputs produce valid JSON (post-edit, vbs, intent-router, prevent-orchestrator-edits, qa-gate).
- prevent-orchestrator-edits.sh correctly probes 7 candidate subagent paths and doesn't false-positive when data is missing.
- tech-debt.sh add appends rows cleanly, sanitizes pipe characters, creates header on first run, --bd-task spawns linked task.
- Approval call (this exact qa-gate.sh approve invocation) succeeds even after multiple Stop fires; F4 wipes iteration state cleanly.
- hooks.json and settings.json hooks blocks are identical and well-formed; PreToolUse anchored matcher correct.
- Iterative loop counter increments on Stop fires AND escalation block fires at iter>=3 (when on FAILED_CHECKS path).
- Epic gate check decision transitions (defer / pass / block) are correct.

DECISION: Block. Issues 1-4 are functional defects directly contradicting Phase 4 spec items. Issue 9 is a critical regression that silently breaks the most-frequent code path — every task approved via the gate stays in_progress because the bd update line uses an invalid status value. Issue 3 entirely defeats B2's purpose. Issue 7 hides timeout vs failure distinction in all checks. Issue 4 lets verify-before-stop pick arbitrary tasks when the helper file is empty — and the plugin's own Phase 4 task is currently in that state, so this is reproducible right now.

The implementation report's 'synthetic tests run, all pass' claim is incomplete; tests 4 ('iteration counter increments... ESCALATION + J21 options surface at iter 3') and 11 ('qa-gate.sh enter writes current-task') would have caught issues 9, 6, and 4 if they exercised the actual production code paths.

pinning: "the IDENTICAL reader lives in verify-before-stop.sh ... keep them in sync".
U1's copy (now ~:2023 awk `|| true`, ~:2027 cat `|| true`, consumer ~:2146) still
carries the pre-i8cx `|| true` on both arms. So as of ed45abe+wave-1 the header
asserts a synchronisation that does not hold.

WHY IT WAS NOT FIXED IN WAVE 1
U1 analysed the direction and it is FAIL-CLOSED, unlike its five release-path sites:
every failure mode SHRINKS the baseline, so the git half over-reports, so the hook
blocks MORE, never less. The empty-set release requires BOTH halves empty, which a
shrunken baseline cannot produce. It therefore carries no release hazard, and the
four-tier acceptance had just certified the current bytes when it was found.

READY SHAPE (U1's, mirroring U3's landed twin)
  - `|| return 1` per arm with an explicit `return 0` tail — the explicit tail
    matters because `[ -n ] && printf` leaves the function's rc as the test's,
    which is the trap that makes a guarded reader silently rc-1 on the empty path.
  - consumer split into a guarded read + a guarded sort feeding the existing sentinel.
  - one new spec section with three cases:
      unreadable baseline      -> sentinel (refusal)
      readable baseline        -> still subtracts, unchanged
      ABSENT baseline          -> unchanged rc-0-empty
    The third is the one that matters: absent-baseline is the pre-0wk.2 common path,
    and an over-eager refusal would break it first. That case is the negative control.

PRIORITY: P2. Fail-closed, no release hazard, but it leaves a stated invariant
false, which is the defect family this release exists to close - a claim nothing
checks. Either land the fix or correct the header; do not leave both.

title: Deferred R8-F3 half: batching output is not re-validated against file-conflict and dependency-order invariants
description:
DEFERRED HALF of D4b review finding R8-F3 (docs/reviews/claude-workflow-plugin-xsu1-r8.json).

WHAT IS BEING FIXED IN D4b (in scope, round 8):
  - validate r/unresolved against unit_task_map (the predicate currently never
    receives it)
  - validate batch members' task_id against unit_task_map

WHAT IS DEFERRED HERE:
Independent re-validation of the batching OUTPUT against the invariants it is
supposed to establish:
  - no two units in a batch declare the same file (file-conflict invariant)
  - no dependent is scheduled before its prerequisite (dependency-order invariant)

WHY IT IS NOT A ROUND-8 PATCH
Re-deriving those invariants at the gate is a SECOND IMPLEMENTATION of the
batching algorithm sitting next to the first. Done casually it is worse than
nothing: two implementations that agree prove only that they share a bug, and the
guard becomes a place where a subtle divergence produces spurious refusals. It
needs a design decision about what independent means here - ideally a checker
derived from the DECLARATIONS (unit files, unit deps) rather than from the
scheduler's own intermediate state, so the two do not share a common ancestor.

REPRODUCTION (reviewer, round 8, literal probes against the current predicates):
  {ok:true,batches:[[{unit_id:"U1",task_id:"forged"},{unit_id:"U2",task_id:"forged"}]]}
    passes the :2099 gate against R = U1,U2 - correct unit-id multiset, forged
    task ids, no file-conflict or dependency-order check performed.
  {r:[],unresolved:["U1","U2"],blocked:[],ud_r:{}}
    passes the :2004 gate against ids U1,U2 - every real bound unit reclassified
    as unresolved.
Both require a targeted rc-0 jq malfunction to reach, i.e. a selectively lying
toolchain rather than normal operation. That is why it is a residual rather than
a release blocker, and it is stated here rather than left implicit.

RELATED: claude-workflow-plugin-uopo (fail-open jq, ~250 sites) and
claude-workflow-plugin-i8cx (no pipefail, 338 pipelines) are the two channels
through which such a lie reaches these gates. Closing either shrinks this task's
reachable surface; closing both may make it moot. Sequence after them and
re-assess whether it is still worth building.

title: reconcile-tracker never subtracts vanished paths, so a deleted file stays in the change set and the approval binds a path that does not exist
description:
OBSERVED CONCRETELY on claude-workflow-plugin-xsu1, and reproducible from that state.

A stray file <repo>/~/.config/bd/config.yaml was created inside the repo by an agent's unexpanded-tilde path (filed separately as claude-workflow-plugin-bag7). I deleted it. The tracker still lists it:

  $ ls -d './~'
  (absent)
  $ grep -n '/~/' .claude/.qa-tracking/changed-files.txt
  44:/Users/edk0/Desktop/projects/claude-workflow-plugin/~/.config/bd/config.yaml
  $ bash .claude/scripts/qa-gate.sh reconcile-tracker
  {"ok":true,...,"observations":"tracker reconcile: changed-files.txt already covers every reviewable git-visible path (denylisted=7); subtracted=0 (added=0)"}
  $ grep -c '/~/' .claude/.qa-tracking/changed-files.txt
  1

So reconcile ADDS git-visible paths the Write/Edit hooks missed, and SUBTRACTS the gate baseline, but has no notion of a tracked path whose file no longer exists. Every subsequent Stop-hook change-set listing continues to name it, and the impact report and change_set_hash both cover it.

WHY IT MATTERS, precisely — and why P2 not P1: the change set naming a created-then-deleted file is arguably TRUE (it was part of the work), and the impact report tolerates the absent path rather than erroring. The tracker is also truncated on approve, so the state self-clears at the end of a cycle. What is wrong is narrower: an operator or reviewer reading the change set sees a path they cannot open, with nothing distinguishing 'deleted during this work' from 'tracker stale'. That is a small instance of this project's own recurring class — a record whose meaning cannot be checked against the thing it describes.

DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED BY HAND. I did not edit changed-files.txt to remove the line, because the tracker is gate state and hand-editing it is the side-channel this project's whole evidence layer is built to distrust (cf. the comment-text-fallback and marker-file bypasses CLAUDE.md forbids). A stale entry that is visible is better than a tracker an orchestrator has been reaching into.

SUGGESTED DIRECTION (not prescriptive): reconcile could mark, rather than remove, an entry whose path no longer exists — e.g. keep it in the set but emit it in the listing as deleted, so the reader sees 'D <path>' instead of an unopenable path. That preserves the audit fact (it changed) while making the current state legible, and avoids the harder question of whether removing entries could ever be used to shrink a change set an approval binds.

PAIRING NOTE: whichever way it goes, the negative control must prove that a path deleted mid-cycle is still ACCOUNTED FOR — the risk in 'reconcile now subtracts' is that it becomes a way for a change set to quietly shrink, which is the opposite failure and a worse one.

title: plan-batches ships file-set intersection only; the impact_of half of the parallel-safety test is deferred and must be named as degradation
description:
SCOPE DECISION by the orchestrator, recorded so it is not mistaken for an omission.

docs/plans/v5-design-phase.md:158 (the PARENT design doc, which is NOT stale — unlike the implementation plan) specifies the full parallel-safety test verbatim:

  'Two units may run concurrently when their declared file sets do not intersect AND THEIR impact_of SETS DO NOT INTERSECT; reuse epic-gate.sh shared-files and the code-graph server for the computation. Degradation to file-set-only intersection must be NAMED IN THE BATCH READOUT, never silent — dxz makes graph availability genuinely unreliable, and an invisible fallback would quietly widen every batch.'

DECISION: D4b ships the FILE-SET half only. The impact_of half is deferred to this task. The condition attached to that deferral is not optional: D4b's output MUST name the degradation (reason token e.g. code_graph_absent / impact_intersection_not_computed) whenever the impact_of intersection was not performed — which, while this task is open, is ALWAYS. A plan that silently omits the graph half is the 'invisible fallback that quietly widens every batch' the design doc explicitly forbids.

WHY DEFERRED: two units can share no declared files and still collide through a call-graph edge, so this genuinely matters. But it adds a second, independently-degradable data source (the code-graph server, whose flakiness is claude-workflow-plugin-dxz's own subject) to a slice that already carries a new batching algorithm with no shipped precedent in this tree. The gsfd arc is the evidence for splitting: one batch that grew to five members took seven fix rounds and six review rounds.

WHEN PICKED UP: reuse impact-report.sh's existing degradation vocabulary (:43-50 — server:'code-graph'|'absent', per-item {ok:false,error:{message}}, artifact always exists on exit 0) rather than minting a second one, and reuse the same checked-rc-AND-shape discipline D4a established at qa-gate.sh:8391-8426. The intersection primitive itself (epic-gate.sh:308-311) is reusable for impact sets, but note it is EXACT STRING EQUALITY with no normalization — impact_of returns symbol/file identifiers whose canonical spelling must be established before intersecting, the same trap condition 13 of the D4b brief identifies for declared paths.

title: Nothing prevents two tasks from binding the same design unit — the rebind gate is per-task only
description:
Found by the D4b scope-audit workflow.

VERIFIED: the design_binding_exists refusal is keyed per TASK, not per unit. Both branches read latest_design_unit_binding "$tid" (qa-gate.sh:7963-7972 and :7986-7995) and the flock path is keyed on the task id (:7925). Nothing scans other tasks for an existing binding to the same unit_id.

CONSEQUENCE: tasks T1 and T2 can both bind unit U1. Each binding is individually legal — neither is a repeat write on its own task, so --rebind is never required and no refusal fires. A unit-keyed consumer (plan-batches emits one entry per unit) then produces a plan in which U1 appears once while TWO implementers are spawned against U1's identical declared file set. That is precisely the concurrent-writers-on-one-file outcome the batching exists to prevent, arriving through the mapping rather than through the intersection.

BOUNDED: this requires an orchestrator error (opening two tasks for one unit, or re-opening a unit's task without retiring the first). It is not reachable from a single well-formed decomposition. Filed at P2 for that reason — but note that at HEAD nothing writes bindings AT ALL (claude-workflow-plugin-6im2), so the invariant has never been exercised in practice and there is no evidence about how easy the mistake is.

SUGGESTED: a unit-keyed check at bind time (refuse unit_bound_to_multiple_tasks unless --rebind, symmetric with the existing per-task gate), or a plan-batches-side detection that degrades with that reason. The bind-time check is better — it refuses at the point the mistake is made rather than at the point it becomes dangerous. Whichever lands, note the existing lock is per-task-id, so a unit-keyed check needs a unit-keyed lock or it has the same race the per-task gate had before claude-workflow-plugin-fkm.6 R2-F2.

title: reviewer-lane invariant costs 0.09s but only runs inside the ~50-minute L1 tier — violation cadence far exceeds guard cadence
description:
A direct instance of this repo's own recorded icn4 lesson: GUARD CADENCE MUST BE AT LEAST VIOLATION CADENCE — a seconds-cheap grep bundled into a reserved expensive tier inherits that tier's cadence.

MEASURED:
  $ /usr/bin/time -p bash .claude/scripts/tests/reviewer-lane-structural.test.sh
  real 0.09
  $ grep -rln 'reviewer-lane-structural' Makefile .claude/hooks/ .claude/settings.json .github/workflows/ .claude/scripts/*.sh
  .claude/scripts/model-select.sh        # <- the only hit, and it is not an invocation site

So the invariant executes in 90 MILLISECONDS and its only cadence is inside the L1 tier, which takes roughly 50 minutes. It has no Makefile target of its own, no hook, no CI step, no pre-commit path.

OBSERVED VIOLATION RATE: three times in a single session, across THREE DIFFERENT specialist agents, each of which had an explicit written warning in its delegation brief that these three files must contain zero matches for codex|reviewer[[:space:]_.-]*lane:
  1. claude-workflow-plugin-gsfd fix round 2 — attribution comments in qa-gate.sh + verify-before-stop.sh
  2. claude-workflow-plugin-gsfd fix round 3 — the same trap again, 3 comments
  3. claude-workflow-plugin-fkm.6 (D4a) fix round 1 — 10 comments (9 in qa-gate.sh, 1 in review-check.sh), all of the shape '(R1-Fn, <reviewer> review round 1)'

Every occurrence cost a full ~50-minute L1 run to surface a defect a 90ms check would have caught at write time. A warning ignored three times by three independent agents is a design signal, not a discipline problem: the natural thing to write when documenting why a line changed is to credit the review that found it, and the guard's whole purpose is that those three gate scripts must not reason about reviewer identity.

WHY THE GUARD ITSELF IS CORRECT AND MUST NOT BE RELAXED: reviewer-lane-degradation.sh asserts these three scripts carry zero codex/reviewer-lane references because a gate that reasons about which reviewer lane produced a verdict is a gate that can be steered by lane selection. That property is worth keeping. This task is about CADENCE, not about the assertion.

SUGGESTED SHAPES (not prescriptive):
  - a cheap Makefile target (e.g. folded into 'make lint', which already runs in seconds and is already run by the Stop gate on every iteration), or
  - a PostToolUse hook on Write/Edit against those three paths, or
  - both: cheap-and-immediate plus the existing L1 leg retained as the durable proof.

PAIRING NOTE: whatever lands must keep a leg that proves the check still FAILS on a violation (the existing spec already has the METAs). Adding a second invocation site must not become a second, drifting copy of the pattern — the pattern lives in the spec today (LANE_GUARD_PATTERN='codex|reviewer[[:space:]_.-]*lane'); a new call site should invoke the spec, not re-spell the regex. Two copies of a grammar that must agree is a defect class this repo has hit repeatedly.

title: 15.9 dolt-flusher positive control can intermittently false-red, costing every task a wasted gate iteration
description:
Filed by the orchestrator on behalf of QA. NOTE ON PROVENANCE: the QA-GATE APPROVED record for claude-workflow-plugin-gsfd states 'Follow-up task filed' for R7-F1, but no such task existed — QA terminated on a spend limit immediately after approving and before the write landed. Verified absent by searching open tasks for 15.9/flusher/dolt/probe/false-red/retry/telemetry/send-metrics; nothing matched. Recording that here because an approval record asserting a filing that did not happen is the same defect family this whole batch is about.

FINDING (QA round 7, R7-F1, MEDIUM — recorded in docs/reviews/claude-workflow-plugin-gsfd-r7.json):
Assertion 15.9 in .claude/scripts/tests/runner-completeness.test.sh:2635 is the POSITIVE control for the dolt telemetry disarm ('the installed dolt spawns its flusher against a fresh store with no local config'). poll_for_dolt_flusher's observation windows are bounded and sampling-based, so the control can intermittently read not-seen when a flusher did spawn — a false RED.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THIS BATCH: runner-completeness.test.sh is in the L1 tier that the Stop gate runs for EVERY task in this repo. When 15.9 false-reds, an unrelated task pays a wasted gate iteration against its own J21 budget.

WHY QA ACCEPTED IT RATHER THAN BLOCKING (all three hold, and the acceptance is only valid while they do):
  1. The direction is FAIL-CLOSED — a false red never certifies anything false; it only costs an iteration.
  2. claude-workflow-plugin-gsfd strictly IMPROVED this probe: store-scoped pid attribution (cwd via /proc or lsof, plus newly-observed-since-snapshot) replaced the previous host-wide 'any dolt send-metrics anywhere' guess, which could false-green as well as false-red.
  3. Genuinely closing the windows needs event-based observation rather than sampling, which the operator-directed design collapse explicitly put out of scope.

SUGGESTED FIX (QA's, and it is the right shape):
A bounded retry of the POSITIVE probe only — retry on not-seen, multiplicatively shrinking the false-red rate.
DO NOT retry the 15.10 NEGATIVE control. Retrying a negative control weakens it: repeated sampling until 'not-seen' is what converts a real spawn into a pass. 15.10 must keep exactly one observation window. This asymmetry is the whole point and must survive into whatever implementation lands.

Pair per .claude/tests/README.md. A leg proving the retry does NOT apply to 15.10 is worth more here than one proving it applies to 15.9.

title: L2 vbs-tmo-a (timeout-disclosure gate-block) is CI-blind: Linux ships timeout, so the absent-binaries leg always skips there
description:
The L2 `vbs-tmo-a` leg (`.claude/tests/component/specs/verify-before-stop.sh`, "vbs-tmo" section, added for claude-workflow-plugin-gsfd's round-7 disclosure fix) proves that a host with neither `timeout` nor `gtimeout` on PATH gets an honest `TIMEOUT NOT ENFORCED:` disclosure in the Stop hook's operator-facing gate summary, through the REAL end-to-end dispatch (detect-stack -> npm -> run_with_timeout -> checks_scope_note -> the hook's JSON `.reason`).

The leg is CONDITIONAL on the ambient host: it runs for real only when `command -v timeout` and `command -v gtimeout` both already fail on the machine running the suite, and prints an honest, named `SKIPPED: vbs-tmo-a (...)` marker otherwise -- matching this tier's own established idiom for an environment the harness cannot force (see `failure-cross-repo.sh` section 5, `gate-baseline-v2.sh` section 6, and `.claude/tests/README.md`'s "reports skips honestly ... but still exits 0 on skips").

Linux CI runners ship `timeout` as part of coreutils, so on every CI run the precondition `command -v timeout || command -v gtimeout` succeeds and `vbs-tmo-a` takes the SKIPPED branch, unconditionally. THE END-TO-END GATE-BLOCK PATH FOR THIS DISCLOSURE HAS NEVER BEEN EXERCISED IN CI, AND CANNOT BE, ON THE CURRENT RUNNER IMAGE. It is only ever exercised when `make test-component` is run by hand on a macOS-like host lacking GNU coreutils (verified true of the box the round-7 fix was authored and described against).

What IS covered everywhere, including CI: `run-with-timeout.test.sh` section 2 (2a) forces the absent-binaries condition directly via a curated PATH restricted to a scratch directory plus the small set of coreutils `run_with_timeout` itself needs, so the FUNCTION-LEVEL behaviour (the log marker, the TIMEOUT_NOT_ENFORCED flag, the passed-through exit code) is proven on every host, CI included. The gap is specifically the INTEGRATION wiring: does that flag's effect genuinely reach the real Stop hook's JSON `.reason` through the actual detect-stack/npm/run_with_timeout dispatch, end to end, for a real not-yet-approved task -- that question is answered only on whatever host happens to already lack both binaries.

WHY THIS WAS NOT CLOSED IN THE ROUND THAT FOUND IT (recorded so whoever picks this up does not have to rediscover the reasoning): forcing "neither binary resolves" for the FULL Stop hook -- which shells out to `jq`/`git`/`bd`/`sed`/`awk` and to five sibling scripts (`qa-gate.sh`, `detect-stack.sh`, `current-task.sh`, `workflow-denylist.sh`, `tree-lease.sh`) -- would need a curated PATH covering every tool ALL of those touch, not just the one binary `run_with_timeout` itself calls. Building that blind -- the L2 tier is explicitly the operator's own call to run (`make test-component`), kept separate from L1, so the specialist who found this gap could not execute it to verify a curated-PATH reconstruction actually worked -- was judged a worse trade than an honest, named skip: a fragile reconstruction that silently broke (a missing tool the curator forgot about) would look identical to a passing leg, which is a worse failure mode than a skip that says plainly what it did not check.

COUNTERPART, not a duplicate: claude-workflow-plugin-v4jn tracks a DIFFERENT, still-open gap in the same area -- nothing anywhere proves `run_with_timeout` returns 124 for a GENUINE (non-backgrounding-trick) hang past its deadline. That gap needs the OPPOSITE PATH setup from this one: a WORKING `timeout` shim present (so a cap exists to race a hang against), where this gap's leg needs both binaries ABSENT (so the unbounded branch is reached at all). Closing one does not close the other, and a future fix attempt should not assume it does.

POSSIBLE SHAPES for closing this (not prescribed -- for whoever picks it up): (a) a curated PATH allowlist for the full hook's dependency surface, built and verified incrementally with `make test-component` available, rather than blind; (b) a container/CI job stage that deliberately hides `timeout`/`gtimeout` from PATH for just this one spec invocation; (c) accepting the L1-only guarantee as sufficient and downgrading this from a gap to a documented, permanent limitation -- a legitimate outcome, but one that should be a decision, not a default.
acceptance_criteria:
- Either: `vbs-tmo-a` (or a replacement assertion) genuinely exercises the end-to-end gate-block path on the CI runner image, verified by observing it FAIL when the disclosure fix is reverted (paired negative control per `.claude/tests/README.md`'s pairing requirement) and PASS against the shipped code, on CI, not just locally; or:
- A documented, reviewed decision that the L1 function-level coverage is the accepted permanent ceiling for CI, with the `vbs-tmo-a` SKIPPED marker's wording updated to point at that decision instead of implying future closure.
- Whichever shape is chosen, `claude-workflow-plugin-v4jn` is not accidentally folded into or closed by this work -- it is a separate property (124-on-genuine-hang vs. disclosure-on-unbounded-run).

title: run_with_timeout has zero test coverage for a genuine (non-backgrounding-trick) deadline firing 124
description:
Discovered while cleaning up claude-workflow-plugin-gsfd's heartbeat/lease removal (round 6 DESIGN COLLAPSE): `run_with_timeout` in `.claude/scripts/verify-before-stop.sh` was reverted to the original, pre-fix-arc `timeout(1)`/`gtimeout(1)`-based dispatch (no in-process poll loop, no group-based kill check, no heartbeat). `.claude/scripts/tests/run-with-timeout.test.sh` sections 2-4 (R4-F1/R4-F2 coverage) tested the now-deleted in-process rewrite specifically — those sections were removed in gsfd because their targeted literals (`kill -0 -- "-$child_pid"`, in-loop `lease_heartbeat` calls) no longer exist in the shipped function, so their mutants could not land (DIFF count 0, not 2 — the same "mutant guards absent code" defect class this batch is about).

That removal leaves a real gap: NOTHING anywhere in the L1/L2 suite proves that `run_with_timeout` actually returns 124 when a command genuinely runs past its deadline via an ordinary (non-backgrounding-trick) hang — e.g. `run_with_timeout 2 log "sleep 10"`. The remaining sections (0: extraction validity, 1: exit-code passthrough + log capture for quick commands) never drive a command slow enough to hit the cap. `classify_test_failure` and the three FAILED_CHECKS branches in verify-before-stop.sh depend entirely on 124 actually being returned by a genuine hang — this is the single most safety-critical property of the function and it is currently unverified.

Complication discovered while scoping this: the current dev box (macOS, this checkout) has NEITHER `timeout` NOR `gtimeout` on PATH (`brew --prefix coreutils` resolves a theoretical prefix but the formula is not actually installed/linked) — so `run_with_timeout` silently takes its unbounded `else` branch on this machine today, and any new test would need to either (a) skip cleanly when neither binary is present rather than false-passing or hanging, or (b) run only under `make test-linux` where GNU coreutils' `timeout` ships in the base image. Designing that skip behavior correctly is itself non-trivial and was deliberately left out of gsfd's scope per the operator's "delete substantially more than you add" instruction for that batch.

Suggested shape for the fix: one small section (plus META) added back to run-with-timeout.test.sh: assert `run_with_timeout 2 log "sleep 10; exit 0"` returns 124 within a bounded wait, with a restore/mutant pair that flips the `command -v timeout` / `command -v gtimeout` detection (e.g. shadow both on PATH within a subshell) to prove the assertion is sensitive to the dispatch actually being invoked, not just to bash's own SIGTERM default. Gate the whole section on `command -v timeout || command -v gtimeout` being available, with an honest `SKIPPED:` marker (matching the tier's four recognized skip-marker shapes) when neither is present, so it fails closed on Linux CI (`make test-linux`, which provisions GNU coreutils) rather than silently never running anywhere.

comments.author: username
comments.text:
Adjacent disclosure fix just landed on gsfd (`run_with_timeout` now records, both in the log and in `checks_scope_note`'s gate summary, when neither `timeout` nor `gtimeout` was on PATH for a given dispatch — see `.claude/scripts/tests/run-with-timeout.test.sh` sections 2a/2b and `.claude/tests/component/specs/verify-before-stop.sh` section `vbs-tmo`). Recording here, as requested, why that work does NOT narrow this gap, and why the gap is platform-dependent in a stronger sense than the existing description states:

A host lacking BOTH binaries (measured again just now on this checkout: `command -v timeout` -> ABSENT, `command -v gtimeout` -> ABSENT) cannot reach the genuine-hang-returns-124 code path AT ALL, by construction — `run_with_timeout`'s `else` branch is unconditional and never invokes anything that could return 124; there is no cap-enforcement call in that branch for a hang to race against. This is different from (and structurally simpler than) what the new disclosure sections needed: those wanted the ABSENT case specifically (a restricted PATH with only `bash`, proving `command -v timeout`/`gtimeout` both fail), which this dev box already satisfies natively. Proving 124-on-genuine-hang needs the OPPOSITE setup — a PATH shim that makes at least one of `timeout`/`gtimeout` resolve to something that actually enforces a bound (a real GNU/BSD `timeout`, not the inert pass-through stub the new restore-control leg uses, which deliberately does not enforce anything and says so in its own comment) — so any fix here still needs its own skip-when-neither-present handling, exactly as this task's suggested shape already says, and still cannot be exercised on today's dev box without installing (or shimming in) a working timeout implementation first.

Not closing this — the suggested shape in the description still stands as the path forward.

title: gate-baseline path subtraction survives the commit that lands its dirt — new dirt on a baselined path is invisible to the change set
description:
# The gap, measured during fkm.5's QA review (2026-08-18, HEAD d8f75ab)

`gate-baseline` (v2, `.claude/.qa-tracking/gate-baseline`) subtracts pre-existing dirt from `reconcile_tracker` **by path only**. It records `head=<sha>` at capture (`qa-gate.sh:342` writes it) but **no reader ever consults it** — verified: `grep -n 'head=' qa-gate.sh verify-before-stop.sh` shows only the two writers and cosmetic uses.

## Measured consequence (fkm.5 / Phase D3 cycle)

1. fkm.4's approve captured the baseline 2026-08-17T16:37:37Z at `head=238d26b`, listing the 7 e2e fixture `qa-gate.sh` copies as then-dirty (D2's `make sync-fixtures` output, approved-not-yet-committed).
2. `d8f75ab` then **committed** that dirt. The baseline entries now describe dirt that no longer exists.
3. D3's implementer ran `make sync-fixtures` again (Bash `cp`, so post-edit.sh never tracks it — the reconcile is the ONLY mechanism that would catch it), re-dirtying the same 7 paths with **new** content.
4. Both reconciles that ran this cycle (05:44 rebuild, 07:33 at QA's enter) subtracted the 7 paths as "already-baselined". Result: fkm.5's bound change set held 16 paths while the completion record honestly declared 23. Command: `sort -u .claude/.qa-tracking/changed-files.txt | wc -l` = 16 vs `jq '.files_changed|length' completion-...-devops.json` = 23, measured at d8f75ab.

Containment this time was luck-shaped: the 7 escaped files were byte-identical (`cmp -s`) to the reviewed canonical `qa-gate.sh`, so no unreviewed content shipped. A future cycle where the baselined-then-committed path takes non-derived edits would certify a change set missing real work — exactly the shape 94d.1 exists to refuse, arriving through a different door.

## Fix directions (pick one at design time)

- Invalidate (or re-capture) baseline entries whose recorded dirt has been committed: cheapest is comparing the stored `head=` to current HEAD and dropping entries that are clean in `git status` at read time... except the path is dirty AGAIN, which is indistinguishable at path level — so this needs content: store `git hash-object` of each baselined path at capture, subtract only when the current dirty content still matches.
- Or: refresh the baseline at COMMIT time, not only at approve time (a post-commit touchpoint does not exist today).

Per the pairing requirement, whatever ships needs a negative control reproducing exactly this sequence: capture baseline with path P dirty, commit P, re-dirty P differently, assert reconcile APPENDS P.

title: session-start's TRACKER-PRESERVE predicate baselines a tree that already carries in-flight edits when no cycle is open
description:
Found by the D2 post-acceptance fix round, 2026-08-17, traced through the code rather than guessed — and
deliberately NOT worked around by hand-editing gate state.

OBSERVED at reconciliation: .claude/.qa-tracking/changed-files.txt and current-task were both ABSENT, and
gate-baseline had been freshly captured at session start (2026-08-17T15:12:22Z) already treating that
round's three edited files as PRE-EXISTING DIRT.

MECHANISM. session-start.sh's TRACKER-PRESERVE predicate (94d.1) keys purely on whether current-task names
a task. The sequence that produces the fault:

  1. a QA approve completes and CLEARS current-task (by design)
  2. a follow-up fix round edits files but never re-enters the gate (nothing required it to)
  3. a session boundary fires session-start.sh
  4. the predicate reads 'no cycle in flight', so it captures a NEW baseline
  5. that baseline now contains the fix round's own edits, classified as arrival dirt

The window is exactly: after an approve clears the slot, before the next enter, across a session boundary.
That is not exotic — it is the ordinary shape of a post-approval fix round, which is how it happened here.

EXPECTED BLAST RADIUS, stated as the reporter stated it — a well-evidenced hypothesis traced through the
code, NOT an empirically reproduced live approve: the next approve should hit change_set_reconstructed
rather than silently mis-binding. That is the fail-closed direction and is why this is P2 rather than P1.
The reporter deliberately did not trigger a live enter/approve to confirm, to avoid mutating shared gate
state further without being asked. Confirming it is the first task here.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE ONE CASE: the predicate answers 'is a cycle in flight?' with 'does a slot name a
task?', and those differ precisely when work continues after an approval. This arc has now seen the same
mismatch twice — j7kk's finding that a design verdict recorded only in bd moves neither skip instrument is
the same shape: a state question answered by the wrong proxy.

NEEDS: a predicate that distinguishes 'no work in flight' from 'work in flight with no open gate cycle'.
Candidates worth measuring rather than reasoning about: consult the tracker's own contents, or the tree
fingerprint against the last recorded verified state, before deciding to re-baseline.

comments.text:
SCOPE WIDENED by QA's D2 round-4 review, 2026-08-17. The original filing described ONE failure shape.
Two more were established from code, and both are worse than the one filed.

FILED SHAPE (the benign one): the next approve hits change_set_reconstructed — loud, fail-closed.

SHAPE 2 — ENTER-FIRST LAUNDERS THE REBUILD. The obvious operator recovery is to run 'enter' before
'approve'. Doing so makes the tracker non-empty, which sets REBUILT_FROM_EMPTY=0, which means the refusal
NEVER FIRES and a subset binds SILENTLY. So the documented recovery path converts a loud refusal into a
quiet mis-bind. That is strictly worse than the defect it is meant to recover from.

SHAPE 3 — THE REFUSAL IS NOT EVEN REACHABLE AT THE MOMENT OF THE FAULT. The refusal requires
RECONCILE_ADDED > 0. At the exact state the fix round observed, a bare approve would have bound an EMPTY
SET, silently. The refusal only armed once QA's own review artifact folded into the change set — i.e. the
loud path depended on a later, incidental write rather than on the fault itself.

SO THE FILED FRAMING WAS THE OPTIMISTIC READING. The fault is not 'a stale baseline produces a loud
refusal'; it is 'a stale baseline produces a silent empty bind, and the documented recovery produces a
silent subset bind, with the loud refusal reachable only by accident'.

HOW QA HANDLED IT rather than routing around: it rejected BOTH documented exits — --accept-reconstructed
binds a proven subset over real work, and enter-first launders as above — and instead reconstructed
changed-files.txt from evidence: mtime triage of all 46 paths against the round-3 approve timestamp,
yielding 5 deltas (3 spec files from the devops F7, fixture.sh byte-compared against a captured r3 diff
probe to confirm comment-only, and LESSONS.md's single fkm.4-sourced entry). 'enter' then kept them
('nothing to add'), and the completion cross-check passed 3/3. Provenance is in the approval record and
qa-plan v4.

REMEDIATION MUST COVER ALL THREE SHAPES. A fix that only makes the refusal fire more reliably leaves
shapes 2 and 3 intact.

title: qa-gate.sh choose approve cannot pass bypass flags through to cmd_approve
description:
Found by D2 Part B, 2026-08-17, worked around via fixture seeding rather than papered over.

cmd_approve accepts audited bypass flags (--no-review, --no-impact-report, --no-completion, and now
--no-design). 'qa-gate.sh choose approve' — the J21 decision-gate path — has no mechanism to forward any of

shape of defect this arc keeps finding — two routes to one outcome that do not carry the same information —
and it becomes more likely to bite as the number of audited bypasses grows. D2 just added a fourth.

Pre-existing, not introduced by D2. Part B routed around it by seeding fixtures instead, which is correct
for a test but is not available to an operator.

NEEDS: forward the bypass flags through choose to cmd_approve, parsed in the same loop, with the same
audited-reason requirement. Pair it.

title: make lint's shellcheck scope excludes .claude/tests/component/, so it can pass without looking at the file under change
description:
Found by the icn4 fix round, 2026-08-16, and disclosed unprompted: 'make lint passed purely because it
never looked at the file I edited.'

The Makefile's shellcheck invocation covers .claude/scripts/*.sh, .claude/scripts/tests/*.sh, install.sh,
uninstall.sh and (since mdnc) .claude/tests/linux/*.sh. It does NOT cover .claude/tests/component/ — where
run.sh and 45 component specs live.

CONSEQUENCE, demonstrated this round: a specialist edited .claude/tests/component/run.sh, ran make lint,
and got rc=0 from a command that never opened the file. It ran shellcheck directly as a substitute (clean),
which is the right instinct and is also not a guarantee anyone else will have it. A gate that is green
because it did not look is the defect family this whole arc is about.

NOT A TRIVIAL WIDENING, and the specialist said so rather than just doing it: it has not been established
whether the 45 component specs would newly redden shellcheck if the scope were widened. So the work is:
(1) measure what widening would catch — run shellcheck over .claude/tests/component/ and count;
(2) decide per-finding whether to fix or to add a scoped disable with a reason;
(3) widen the Makefile only once (1) and (2) are done, so the widening lands green rather than red.

Do NOT widen first and fix after — a red lint gate trains people to ignore it, which costs more than the
gap does.

RELATED: the same shape as the correction-10 exposure (a guard that exists but does not run over the thing
it guards), and as icn4's own item 1 (a guard at the wrong cadence). Third instance of 'the check is fine,
its coverage is not'.

comments.author: username
comments.text:
Reproduced under real concurrent load during claude-workflow-plugin-icn4's `make test` run (another independently-invoked `make test` was running concurrently against this same checkout throughout, confirmed via `ps` — distinct PID tree, offset elapsed time).

`bash .claude/scripts/tests/run-tests.sh --filter runner-completeness` (isolated re-run, still under residual contention): 253/253 assertions PASSED, then classified FAILED with:

```
--- runner-completeness.test.sh: FAILED — returned with 1 live background process(es), killed (253 assertion(s) in 221s) ---
    survivor: 257     1 21968 /opt/homebrew/bin/dolt send-metrics
```

The survivor is named: `dolt send-metrics`, ppid=1. This is the same telemetry-flusher shape `BD_DISABLE_METRICS=1` exists to prevent at the OUTER runner's own bd calls (a9hh R3-F1) — but `runner-completeness.test.sh` spawns NESTED bd-calling fixtures/mutants of both runners as part of its own testing, and at least one of those nested invocations apparently doesn't inherit or re-apply the disarm in every code path being driven, letting a real flusher through under load. This is a concrete lead for "reproduce under real load ... only then hypothesize": the leak is very likely one specific nested fixture invocation (not the outer spec itself, which is otherwise clean at 253/253) missing the `BD_DISABLE_METRICS=1` export somewhere in its own bd-calling setup. Not investigated further — out of scope for icn4, reported here per CONTRIBUTING's "a finding discovered after a task closes" convention (this task is still open, so a comment suffices).

comments.author: username
comments.text:
ROOT CAUSE ESTABLISHED, 2026-08-16 — and it explains every property that made this leak resist three
negative reproductions.

THERE ARE TWO TELEMETRY FLUSHERS. THE DISARM COVERS ONE.

  run-tests.sh:144-161  TELEMETRY-DISARM-BEGIN (a9hh R3-F1)  -> export BD_DISABLE_METRICS=1
                        Its own comment: 'bd spawns a telemetry flusher (bd send-metrics) from ANY bd
                        command when metrics are enabled, detached to ppid=1 WITHOUT setsid — it stays in
                        the spec's process group, and when the metrics endpoint is slow it outlives the
                        survivor sweep's grace, so the sweep kills the SPEC for a process it never
                        started with &, cannot wait for, and cannot see.'

That describes THIS leak exactly — but for bd's flusher. icn4 identified the actual leaked process as
'dolt send-metrics'. bd EMBEDS dolt; the embedded engine spawns ITS OWN flusher, a different binary with a
different control. BD_DISABLE_METRICS=1 cannot stop it.

MEASURED JUST NOW:
  dolt config --help | grep -i metrics   -> 'metrics.disabled - boolean flag disables sending metrics
                                            when true.'
  ps aux | grep -c '[d]olt send-metrics' -> 1        (a live specimen, right now)
  grep -rnE 'DOLT_DISABLE|metrics\.disabled|dolt config.*metrics' .claude/ Makefile
                                         -> no matches       (nothing disables dolt telemetry anywhere)

WHY IT NEVER REPRODUCED IN ISOLATION. Three separate negative reproductions are now explained rather than
mysterious: the spawn needs a bd call that reaches the embedded dolt engine AND a slow enough metrics
endpoint to outlive the sweep's grace. Neither is reliable on a quiet machine; both are likely under load.
The 2-day-old orphaned $WORK dir is the same story — a run that never reached its cleanup trap because the
sweep killed it for dolt's child.

THE FIX MUST PREVENT THE SPAWN, NOT EXEMPT IT. The existing disarm's comment already rejected the
alternative and the reasoning still applies verbatim: 'An argv-pattern exemption in the sweep was REJECTED:
argv is forgeable (exec -a "bd send-metrics" would hide exactly the leak the sweep exists to catch), and
excluding ppid==1 would delete the R2-F2 detection outright.' So: disarm dolt's flusher at the source,
beside bd's, inside the same sentinel region.

ONE CAUTION, AND IT IS THE REASON I AM NOT JUST DOING IT: 'dolt config --global --add metrics.disabled true'
mutates the USER'S GLOBAL dolt configuration, outside this repo, affecting every dolt use on the machine.
That is not a change a test runner should make unilaterally. Establish first whether dolt honours a
repo-local config or an environment variable, and prefer that. If only the global config works, it needs an
explicit operator decision, not a silent write — and the honest fallback is to document the leak rather
than reach outside the repo to suppress it.

Pair whatever lands, per the four-part standard: the existing disarm has a negative control and this one
needs the same.

DISCOVERED-FROM: the icn4 fix round's root-cause lead, confirmed here by command.

comments.author: username
comments.text:
**Root cause fixed and driven-verified, under claude-workflow-plugin-gsfd.**

`disarm_dolt_telemetry()` added beside `BD_DISABLE_METRICS=1` in BOTH runners' TELEMETRY-DISARM regions (`.claude/scripts/tests/run-tests.sh`, `.claude/tests/component/run.sh`): idempotently calls `dolt config --local --add metrics.disabled true` against `$PROJECT_DIR/.beads/embeddeddolt/beads` at startup, guarded by the same existence/PATH checks the STORE-CANARY already uses (no-op on a store-less checkout or a host with no `dolt`).

**Verified by driving it, not by reading `dolt config --help`** (per the task's own instruction):

```
dolt sql -r csv -q "SELECT hashof('HEAD')" against .beads/embeddeddolt/beads, ps -axo pid,ppid,args
polled every 50ms for 5s after each call, filtered to genuine `dolt send-metrics` argv:
  no local config set:                4/4 trials spawned the flusher (ppid=1, in-group)
  metrics.disabled=true set --local:  0/4 trials spawned anything
```

`dolt config --local` writes to `.beads/embeddeddolt/beads/.dolt/config.json`, confirmed via `git check-ignore -v` to be excluded by `.beads/.gitignore:11` (`embeddeddolt/`) — never touches the user's global dolt config (`~/.dolt/config_global.json`, confirmed empty on both sides of the experiment), never enters a change-set hash. Idempotent: `--add` on an already-true key overwrites cleanly across 4 repeated applications (never grows a multivar).

Automated, paired coverage added: `runner-completeness.test.sh` section 15 (10 assertions) — wiring proof against a real embedded-Dolt fixture store for both runners, a META-TEST that excises the (shared) TELEMETRY-DISARM region and proves the fixture's config is left unset, and a direct spawn-detection probe against the *installed* dolt (mirrors section 10.11/10.12's split for `BD_DISABLE_METRICS`). Section 15 is green on the latest full run of the file.

This directly resolves 7tfe's titled defect: the leaked background descendant (`dolt send-metrics`, ppid=1) can no longer spawn from a repo-scoped checkout with this disarm applied, so it can no longer be the survivor the L1 sweep kills the spec for.

Recommend closing once QA confirms independently — labeling `qa-pending` rather than closing it myself, since this fix landed as a side effect of gsfd's own scope rather than as dedicated work on this task id.

Files: `.claude/scripts/tests/run-tests.sh`, `.claude/tests/component/run.sh`, `.claude/scripts/tests/runner-completeness.test.sh` (section 15).

title: Correction 10's guard is narrower than every description of it, and its own header depends on the fact it omits
description:
Established 2026-08-16 during v9dx, by reading the guard and every citation of it — not inferred.

THE GUARD: .claude/tests/component/specs/reviewer-lane-degradation.sh asserts the three gate-critical
scripts match zero of

    grep -cEi 'codex|reviewer[._]lane'

THE NUANCE NOBODY WROTE DOWN: the second branch requires a LITERAL '.' or '_' immediately between the two
words. So the space-separated phrase 'reviewer lane', and the hyphenated spec filename
reviewer-lane-degradation.sh, are NEVER matches. In practice the ONLY unconditional tripwire is the bare
substring 'codex'.

WHERE IT IS NOT STATED — all checked verbatim:
  reviewer-lane-degradation.sh lines 1-17 (header) and 29-37 (the structural loop) — silent
  model-select.sh:1339                                                              — silent
  docs/plans/v5-design-phase.md:225 and v5-design-phase-plan.md:88 (correction 10)   — silent

AND THE HEADER DEPENDS ON THE FACT IT OMITS: its own prose uses 'reviewer lane' (space-separated) twice, at
lines 3 and 10. Those lines are inside a file the guard does not scan, so they are harmless — but they
demonstrate that the author was writing the phrase freely while the guard's description implies the phrase
is forbidden.

TWO OPPOSITE FAILURE MODES, both live:
  OVER-AVOIDANCE  a reader believing the description contorts prose to dodge a pattern that was never a
                  match.
  FALSE SECURITY  a reader believing the description assumes 'reviewer lane' in a gate script would be
                  caught. It would not. Lane logic could be introduced, described in prose using the
                  natural spelling, and pass.

The second is the one that matters: the guard is the mechanical enforcement of correction 10, whose whole
point is that lane knowledge must not reach the gate scripts.

NEEDS a decision, not just a comment:
  (a) document the actual semantics at the guard, at model-select.sh:1339, and in correction 10; or
  (b) WIDEN the pattern to match the phrase in any spelling and fix whatever it then catches — which is
      what most readers already believe is happening.
(b) is the honest reading of the invariant's intent. (a) is cheaper and truthful. Do not do neither.

DISCOVERED-FROM: v9dx, whose fix was needed only because the bare 'codex' branch caught a comment naming a
test file.
close_reason: Closed by icn4 item 2, shipped 238d26b. Resolved via option (b) — WIDENED the pattern rather than documenting the narrow one, which was the honest reading of correction 10's intent. codex|reviewer[._]lane -> codex|reviewer[[:space:]_.-]*lane. QA proved the strict superset three ways (formally by class containment, over a 26-string adversarial corpus including must-NOT-match cases like 'reviewer's lane' and 'reviewer plane', and repo-wide via git grep -iE <old> | grep -cvEi <new> = 0) and could not construct a disproving string. The one site the widening newly caught — qa-gate.sh:4881, carrying the space form and evading the guard at base, exactly as this task predicted — was reworded rather than exempted. Live citations updated at model-select.sh:1339 and docs/CODEX_SETUP.md. RESIDUAL, deliberately left and tracked in icn4's closure: correction 10 in docs/plans/v5-design-phase*.md still describes the retired narrow pattern. Not edited because that file declares itself a byte-for-byte mirror of an out-of-repo original with 'WHERE THEY DISAGREE, THIS FILE WINS' — editing only the in-repo copy would make the stale copy authoritative under that pair's own rule. The fix belongs in ~/.claude/plans/v5-0-0-design-stateless-wilkinson.md, which is the operator's to make, and it matters at D7 when the release audit cites correction 10.

title: L2's slowest spec runs at 1.12x headroom against its own cap: verify-before-stop.sh took 802s against 900s
description:
Measured during mdnc round 1, 2026-08-14, on a machine the specialist could NOT establish as idle - 42
samples over 7 minutes never exceeded 76% CPU idle and load rose 3.49 -> 6.05.

  .claude/tests/component/specs/verify-before-stop.sh : 802s
  SPEC_TIMEOUT_S (L2)                                 : 900s
  headroom                                            : 1.12x

The mwrb cap was sized at 3.9x against a worst-observed 228s. That margin is gone for this spec, and the
sizing rationale in the runner still cites the old number.

WHY IT IS NOT COSMETIC. A spec that times out is reported as FAILED-with-a-distinct-reason, which is
correct and loud - but it is loud in a way that looks like a code failure to a reader scanning a CI log,
and this spec is the one that exercises the Stop gate itself. Under CI contention, or once D4 runs
PARALLEL BATCHES on one host, 1.12x is not margin.

Note the interaction with claude-workflow-plugin-9xl4: D4 makes concurrency the design rather than an
accident, and every concurrent tier run competes for the same CPU. A cap sized on an idle single-run
measurement is the wrong cap for that world.

NEEDS: re-measure the slowest specs under representative contention rather than idle, then either raise
the cap with the new measurement recorded beside it, or split the spec. Per CONTRIBUTING every number
carries the command that produced it and the commit it was measured at.

Found by qa-claude during the Phase D1 final verdict, 2026-08-13, when the completeness cross-check
fired at approve and it answered the alarm rather than letting it pass as noise.

MECHANISM. make sync-fixtures propagates canonical scripts into the seven e2e fixtures with cp. The
change-set tracker is built by post-edit.sh from tool_input.file_path, and cp is not an edit tool, so
the copies never enter changed-files.txt. They ARE in git status and they ARE declared in the
specialist's completion contract, so approve's completeness cross-check reports N absent declared
paths on every task that touches a synced script.

MEASURED on fkm.3: 7 absent declared paths, all cp-propagated fixture copies of qa-gate.sh, all
byte-identical to the canonical file (verified individually by QA rather than assumed). Nothing
unreviewed - but the alarm is indistinguishable from the alarm that would fire if a declared path had
genuinely gone missing.

WHY IT MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING COSMETIC. The completeness cross-check exists to catch a truncated
change set. It now cries wolf on a schedule - every commit that edits qa-gate.sh, review-check.sh,
verify-before-stop.sh, workflow-manifest.sh, model-select.sh, statusline.sh, session-start.sh or
session-end.sh. A check that fires benignly on a routine action trains its reader to dismiss it, which
is how the real instance gets waved through. This session already ran the fixture sync five times
across three phases.

It is also a COMMIT obligation the gate structurally cannot see: bbh recorded the same shape for the
same file set, and the fixture .claude/scripts/ paths are denylisted, so no approval can ever bind
them.

CANDIDATE DIRECTIONS (a decision, not a design): have sync-fixtures append the paths it wrote to the
tracker directly, the way reconcile does; or teach the cross-check that denylisted mirror paths of a
tracked canonical file are expected-absent and say so in the envelope rather than counting them; or
have the completion contract declare the canonical file only, with the mirrors implied. The first
keeps the tracker honest; the second keeps the tracker minimal and moves the knowledge into the
checker. Prefer whichever makes a GENUINE absence still loud.

Pair with a leg that runs sync-fixtures then asserts the cross-check is quiet, plus a control proving
it still fires when a genuinely declared path is missing.
