comments.text:
ORCHESTRATOR CORRECTION, 2026-08-06 — MY PREMISE ON THE IMPACT-REPORT ITEM WAS WRONG, and the truth is worse for D4.

I filed it as 'code-graph does not model shell invocation'. FALSE. The P6 specialist drove the real server against a three-file shell fixture and measured:
  - parser-loader.js maps .sh -> bash; queries.js defines bash defs, calls AND source imports. Shell IS modelled.
  - symbol_callers(helper_fn) correctly resolved caller-source.sh:3.
  - BUT edges=7, resolved_edges=1, and impact_of(file=...) returned file_dependents: [] for all three files — including lib.sh, which caller-source.sh literally sources.
  - code_context('bash') showed 1 usage; code_context('lib.sh') showed 0/0.

THE MECHANISM: 'bash "$SCRIPT_DIR/other.sh"' records an edge against the INTERPRETER WORD 'bash', not the target script. And '"$SCRIPT_DIR/other.sh" --flag' records NO edge at all, because the command name is not a bare (word) node.

So the artifact is not empty because nothing was modelled. It is empty because every cross-script edge either binds to the wrong symbol or is dropped — while the server reports healthy and the report looks well-formed.

WHY THIS IS WORSE THAN AN ABSENT SERVER, AND WHY IT ESCALATES BEYOND A NOTE: D4 (plan-batches) computes parallel batches from impact_of intersections. Vacuous intersections mean nearly every pair looks independent, so BATCHES WIDEN SILENTLY — the exact failure D4's PLAN-BATCHES-NO-DESIGN-GUARD was written to prevent, arriving through a channel that guard cannot see. The existing degradation vocabulary (server:'absent', impact:null) cannot express it either, because the server IS present and IS healthy.

WHAT WOULD MAKE IT VISIBLE, per the specialist: a third state or a quality signal — resolved_edges/edges as a ratio, or the observation '0 dependents across 100% of files', which is a fact no real codebase produces. Either makes 'answered vacuously' distinguishable from 'answered'.

FAMILY: this is the sharpest instance yet of the shape this whole phase has been chasing — a check that reports success it did not establish. Twenty-second recorded. And note it was found the same way as most of the others: by driving the real thing against a fixture instead of reading its description.

SCOPE: still not fixed here. But it should be resolved BEFORE D4 rather than after, because D4's correctness depends on it and D4's own guard cannot detect it.

title: make sync-fixtures writes by shell, so the 21 e2e fixture copies never reach changed-files.txt — an approval binds 8 paths while 29 moved
description:
Raised by QA during P4's review, 2026-08-06, and confirmed by the orchestrator against the live tree.

MEASURED on 2ty's change set: git shows 21 modified fixture script copies; changed-files.txt holds 0 of them. The approval hash therefore binds 8 paths while 29 files moved.

MECHANISM, and it is the 94d defect exactly: post-edit.sh only sees Write/Edit/MultiEdit tool payloads. 'make sync-fixtures' copies files with shell 'cp', so no PostToolUse hook fires and the copies never enter the tracker. reconcile_tracker would normally fold git-visible paths in, but the fixture copies are DENYLISTED (workflow-denylist.sh rule 3, e2e fixture churn), so they are deliberately excluded from the change set.

SO THE TWO MECHANISMS COMPOSE INTO A GAP NEITHER INTENDED:
  - the denylist excludes fixture churn because it is mechanical noise — correct in itself;
  - the approval hash binds only the tracker — correct in itself;
  - therefore the SHIPPED fixture copies are never bound by any approval, and no reviewer's record attests to their contents.

WHY IT IS NOT ACADEMIC: the fixture copies are what the e2e tier actually executes. A drift between canonical and fixture is caught by the L3 drift guard (7 assertions, and it did fire this session), so the copies cannot silently diverge — that guard is the only thing standing between a bad sync and an unreviewed test substrate. QA's exact framing: 'my cmp check is the only evidence the shipped mirrors match reviewed content.'

NOT INTRODUCED BY sync-fixtures OR BY P4. It is a pre-existing consequence of 94d's design that only became visible when the orchestrator ran the sync itself and QA went looking for what the approval covered.

CANDIDATE DIRECTIONS, none obviously right:
  (a) leave it, and rely on the L3 drift guard as the binding — cheapest, and arguably correct since the guard proves byte-identity to reviewed content;
  (b) have sync-fixtures append the copies to changed-files.txt, which fights the denylist's purpose and would put 21 mechanical paths into every review;
  (c) record a separate 'fixtures synced from <canonical-hash>' attestation at approve time — binds the relationship rather than the bytes.
(c) is the smallest honest statement: the copies are not independently reviewed, they are derived, and what should be bound is the derivation.

Decide before D7, because the release audit will otherwise imply the approval covered the shipped tree.

comments.text:
<!-- BD-MCP-META: {"kind":"qa-note","source":"qa-agent","from_task":"claude-workflow-plugin-bbh","finding":"R1-F1"} -->
## Diagnostic correction from QA (bbh review, 2026-08-08): the mechanism is the DENYLIST, not the shell write

This task's title and description attribute the miss to the write mechanism —
"`make sync-fixtures` writes by shell, so the 21 e2e fixture copies never reach
`changed-files.txt`". That is true but it is not the binding cause, and the
difference changes what a fix has to do.

**MEASURED** — I sourced `.claude/scripts/workflow-denylist.sh` and tested
`WORKFLOW_DENYLIST_REGEX` against real fixture paths in both spellings:

```
DENYLISTED   .claude/tests/e2e/fixtures/node-react-auth/.claude/scripts/verify-before-stop.sh
DENYLISTED   .claude/tests/e2e/fixtures/go-cli-refactor/.claude/scripts/qa-gate.sh
DENYLISTED   /Users/edk0/.../fixtures/qa-block-recovery/.claude/scripts/verify-before-stop.sh
trackable    .claude/scripts/verify-before-stop.sh
```

The matching alternative is
`(^|/)\.claude/tests/e2e/fixtures/[^/]+/(\.claude/(scripts|beads)|\.beads)/`.

**What follows.** Fixture `.claude/scripts/` paths are excluded from the change
set by an explicit denylist rule, so:

* Converting `sync-fixtures` to Write/Edit tool calls would **not** fix this.
  `post-edit.sh` filters through the same denylist, so the paths would still be
  dropped.
* `94d`'s `reconcile_tracker` would not pick them up either — it subtracts
  denylisted paths from the git-visible remainder before appending.
* So **no mechanism currently in the system can put a synced fixture copy into a
  bound change set.** The 8-vs-29 gap is not a leak; it is the denylist doing
  what it was written to do.

**Which makes this a framing question rather than a plumbing bug.** The fixture
copies are mechanical mirrors whose correctness is asserted byte-for-byte by the
`_fixture-script-sync` DRIFT GUARD, and the guard is a *stronger* witness than a
QA read of 21 identical diffs would be. So the honest options are:

1. **Accept and say so.** The sync is a COMMIT obligation, not a CHANGE-SET
   obligation. Document that an approval deliberately does not bind fixture
   mirrors, and point at the drift guard as the thing that does. This also means
   running `make sync-fixtures` never moves `change_set_hash` and therefore never
   invalidates a review already performed — which is useful, not merely benign.
2. **Remove the denylist rule** for `fixtures/*/.claude/scripts/` and accept 21
   mirror paths in every change set that touches a canonical script, plus the
   review noise that comes with it.

Option 1 looks right to me, but it is a decision this task should record rather
than leave implied — right now the title asserts a cause that a fix acting on it
would not close.

title: bd dep remove reports a confident success for an edge that does not exist, leaving the real edge intact
description:
REPRODUCED 2026-08-06 by the orchestrator while recutting the 1nz -> 2ty edge for Phase P4.

The edge was '1nz blocks 2ty' (i.e. 2ty depends on 1nz). I ran the arguments in the wrong order:

  $ bd dep remove claude-workflow-plugin-1nz claude-workflow-plugin-2ty
  ✓ Removed dependency: claude-workflow-plugin-1nz ... no longer depends on claude-workflow-plugin-2ty

Exit 0, a check mark, and a sentence naming both tasks. Then:

  $ bd dep list claude-workflow-plugin-2ty
  claude-workflow-plugin-1nz: ... [P2] (open) via blocks     <- STILL THERE

The reverse-direction edge never existed, so nothing was removed. The success message describes a state change that did not occur, and it is indistinguishable from the message the correct invocation prints. Running it the right way round (bd dep remove 2ty 1nz) then removed the real edge, verified by dep list returning 'no dependencies'.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND ONE TYPO: dependency edges gate 'bd ready', which is how agents and humans pick up work. An agent that removes a blocker in the wrong argument order sees success, reports the task unblocked, and the task stays blocked — or worse, believes it recut an edge that still governs sequencing. There is no signal to check against except re-reading dep list, which is exactly the discipline that a confident success message discourages.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOUR: removing a nonexistent edge should be a no-op that SAYS SO, e.g. 'no such dependency: A does not depend on B' with a non-zero exit or at minimum a distinguishable message. Idempotent no-ops are fine; silently reporting them as changes is not.

FAMILY: eighteenth instance recorded this session of 'something claimed a thing that nothing checked'. Siblings in the same tool: fkm.1.18 (bd_list_comments returns ok:true with 0 of 76 comments), rmz (create --parent silently mints inherited gate labels), and bd label remove exiting 0 for both an absent label and a nonexistent task — the last of which is what l1r.3 forced remove_label to stop trusting. Four instances in bd's own CLI surface, all the same shape: exit status and output that do not distinguish 'did the thing' from 'did nothing'.

Not a plugin defect. Worth an upstream report, and worth a note wherever the plugin's docs tell an agent to manipulate dependencies — verify with dep list, do not trust the success line.

title: P3 residuals (R1-F1..F5 from 8zi's approval): canary names no task, gz3 recipe mechanism stale, third approve-drops surface, token pin count, dangling cross-ref
description:
Five findings from QA's r1 approval of 8zi, 2026-08-05. None at/above high; the change set was approved and committed with these open. All are one-liners or prose.

Landing them separately is the correct order, not deferral.

Land alongside yj2 if that is taken soon, since R1-F1 is about yj2's own coupling.

title: approve's rollback cannot un-write the approval record, so a rollback under unprovable label removals exits 3 while leaving a releasable {qa-approved, bound record} pair
description:
Surfaced by 8zi's l1r.3-6c leg. PRE-EXISTING and NOT made worse by 8zi — filed because 8zi is the first thing to make it observable, and it is now asserted rather than latent.

## The state

`cmd_approve` writes the `QA-GATE APPROVED ... change_set_hash=<h>` comment BEFORE adding `qa-approved` (the gz3 ordering rule: the {record, label} pair must never be half-visible to a concurrent Stop). Comments are append-only, so no failure after that point can un-write the record.

`set_terminal_label` therefore rolls back LABELS only. When the rollback runs on a bd whose removals cannot be proven, it cannot remove the `qa-approved` it just added either. Result, measured under the l1r.3 shim (`bd label remove` exits 0 and does nothing):

    exit code 3, ok=false
    observations: "...failed to remove qa-gate-entered after qa-approved was set;
                   rolled back — WARNING the restore itself did not complete..."
    on the task:  qa-approved STILL SET, and a change-set-bound approval record present

Both halves of the Stop hook's release predicate (llh.18) are then satisfied, so a Stop could release work whose approval reported exit 3.

## Why this is pre-existing, stated precisely

Before 8zi, the same bd produced the OPPOSITE report and the same release: the unverified `remove_label` returned success, approve exited 0, and the envelope claimed `removed qa-gate-entered=1` for a removal that never happened. So the release outcome is unchanged; what changed is that the gate now says loudly that it could not prove the transition, and `l1r.3-6c` asserts every part of that (exit 3, ok=false, names the label, admits the incomplete restore, and never emits the false counter).

The reachability precondition is narrow: bd must be accepting writes (the record and the label add both land) while label REMOVALS do not stick. l1r.3's own reproduction — a stale-JSONL auto-import replaying a pre-removal label set — is exactly that shape.

## Options, none obviously right

1. Append a compensating `QA-GATE APPROVAL VOIDED <hash>` record and teach `verify-before-stop.sh` to treat a voided hash as unbound. Correct, but it adds a fourth record type and a new reader to the release predicate.
2. Add the label BEFORE the record. Reintroduces the gz3 half-visible window in the other direction (a label with no record = LABEL_WITHOUT_RECORD blocks), which is arguably the safer failure — worth measuring rather than asserting.
3. Accept and document. The envelope already says it; the residual is that nothing downstream reads the envelope.

Do not pick one without reproducing a release off this state first — option 2 in particular trades one narrow window for another and the trade needs measuring.

title: assert_json_field cannot assert a false boolean — jq's // maps false to empty, so every '.ok' false assertion silently mis-measures
description:
Found in 8zi while asserting the exit-3 rollback envelope.

## The defect

`.claude/tests/component/lib/assert.sh`, `assert_json_field`, extracts with:

    actual=$(printf '%s' "$json" | jq -r "$path // empty" 2>/dev/null || echo "")

jq's `//` is the ALTERNATIVE operator: it yields the right-hand side when the left is `false` OR `null`. So a genuinely-present `false` is indistinguishable from an absent field. Verified directly:

    $ echo '{"ok":false}' | jq -r '.ok // empty'      ->  (prints nothing)
    $ echo '{"ok":false}' | jq -r '.ok'               ->  false
    $ echo '{"ok":true}'  | jq -r '.ok // empty'      ->  true

## Consequence

`assert_json_field "<name>" "$OUT" '.ok' "false"` can NEVER pass, however correct the envelope. It fails with `actual:` empty, which reads exactly like a malformed or truncated envelope — and that is how it was initially triaged during 8zi ("`.ok` is absent from the exit-3 envelope, an envelope-shape bug"). It was not. Measured on the shipped script:

    jq 'has("ok")' -> true
    jq '.ok'       -> false
    jq 'keys'      -> ["observations","ok","status","subcommand","task_id"]

The cost is a wrong diagnosis pointed at production code. That is worse than a missing assertion, because the "fix" it invites is a change to the envelope writer.

## Why it went unnoticed

Every existing `assert_json_field '.ok'` call site in the tier asserts `"true"`, which the `//` form handles correctly. The refusal legs that need falsity already use a substring form (`assert_contains '"ok":false'`) — so the helper's blind spot never had a caller until now. Same pattern in the L1 tier is worth a check.

## Suggested fix

Distinguish absent from false. E.g. extract with `jq -r 'if has("<key>") then <path> else "" end'`, or keep `// empty` only as the null-coalescing path and add an `assert_json_field_raw` that uses a bare `<path>`. Then audit for call sites that were silently relying on `false` -> empty.

## Interim (shipped in 8zi)

The two new legs use `assert_contains '"ok":false'`, matching the existing refusal legs, with an inline comment naming the jq constraint so nobody "fixes" the envelope instead of the helper.

title: Component harness: mk_bd_shim chains into a previously-replaced fixture wrapper, so one spec section's selective bd failure poisons every later fixture
description:
Found while writing the 8zi/l1r.3/jue legs in .claude/tests/component/specs/qa-gate.sh. DIRECTLY OBSERVED, not inferred.

## Mechanism

- `mk_fixture` PREPENDS `<root>/bin` to PATH for every fixture it builds.
- `mk_bd_shim` builds each wrapper from `command -v bd`.

So once any spec section REPLACES its own fixture's `bin/bd` with a selective shim, every fixture created afterwards **in the same spec shell** is generated as `exec <that-other-fixture>/bin/bd "$@"` and silently inherits the other section's failure injection.

## Reproduction (observed)

Fixture A's wrapper replaced with a shim that fails `label remove <tid> qa-pending`. A fixture B created afterwards:

    B bin/bd: exec /var/.../component-fixture.XXXXXX.1RQ8h2tLSh/bin/bd "$@"
    bd label remove <tid-in-B> qa-pending  -> rc=1
    labels after            -> [qa-pending]   (survived)

## Live instance in the tree

In `specs/qa-gate.sh` the poisoner is the pre-existing "approve Step-3 rollback guard" section, whose shim fails exactly `label remove ... qa-pending`. It has been poisoning `FIXTURE_BIND` (llh.18 binding section) and `FIXTURE_TU` (tracker-unreconcilable section) for as long as both have existed. It stayed LATENT because neither of those sections removes `qa-pending`.

It stopped being latent the moment a section whose subject IS a label sweep arrived: the 8zi legs failed with approve exiting 3, which is indistinguishable from the defect under test — the removal genuinely did not happen and the new verified `remove_label` correctly refused to claim it did. 18 assertion failures, all traceable here.

## Why this matters beyond one spec

The failure mode is a spec measuring a *deliberately broken* bd while believing it has a working one. That produces either a false red (what happened here) or, worse, a false green if the injected failure happens to satisfy the assertion.

## Interim containment (already shipped in 8zi)

`specs/qa-gate.sh` now defines `depoison_bd <root>`, which walks the `exec <path> "$@"` chain to the binary at the end of it and rewrites the wrapper as a single hop. Each of the three new fixtures calls it, and two assertions PIN the hazard rather than merely working around it:

    8zi-0: the inherited bd wrapper IS poisoned by an earlier section  -> "poisoned"
    8zi-0: ...and this section's wrapper now execs a real bd           -> "clean"

The first of those is a canary: if the harness is ever fixed, it flips and tells whoever fixed it that the local workaround can be removed.

## Suggested fix

Make `mk_bd_shim` resolve the chain itself (same walk as `depoison_bd`) so `command -v bd` resolving to another fixture's wrapper cannot propagate an injection. Cheap, and it removes the trap for every future spec.

NOT done inside 8zi deliberately: it is a shared-harness change affecting all L2 specs, and 8zi could not validate it — the specialist was instructed not to run whole suites, and a change with that blast radius needs a full-tier run, not a targeted one.

title: 94d.1's rebuild-from-empty notice fires on the BENIGN post-commit path, writing to sync-errors.log — the 'flag users learn to ignore' risk realised in under a day
description:
OBSERVED 2026-08-05 by the orchestrator while running the P3 bar. Not a defect in the fix — a consequence to decide about deliberately rather than discover in six weeks.

sync-errors.log right now holds 6 entries, all from this session, all the same shape:
  2026-08-04T15:30:20Z [qa-gate] reconcile_tracker: changed-files.txt was absent-or-empty while a gate cycle was in flight (claude-workflow-plugin-qzv)
  ... 15:31:42 (qzv), 19:44:58 + 19:45:50 (qzv.1), 09:52:41 + 09:53:42 (8zi)

Every one is 94d.1's SUBTRACTION-ACCOUNTING announcing a rebuild from an empty tracker while a cycle was in flight. The mechanism is correct and is exactly what we built: reconcile cannot distinguish 'legitimately empty' from 'destroyed', so it states its assumption and writes a durable line.

THE PROBLEM IS THAT THE BENIGN CASE IS THE COMMON CASE. All six fired because 'enter' ran right after a commit, when the tracker is legitimately empty — the prior approve truncated it and nothing has been edited yet. Zero of the six indicate anything wrong. SessionStart surfaces sync-errors.log as a warning, so the next session reports a Beads sync error that is not one.

WHY IT IS NOT COSMETIC: the v5 plan's risk table already names this mode for another flag — 'a flag users learn to ignore is worth revisiting if it persists'. Under 24 hours from shipping 94d.1 we have six false positives. And this log is the ONLY durable record of the case 94d.1 exists to catch — a tracker destroyed mid-cycle. We are burying our own new signal under routine output.

FIX DIRECTION, cheapest first:
  (a) suppress when no IMPLEMENTER record is newer than the last approval — an empty tracker is expected there;
  (b) suppress when git shows no relevant uncommitted delta — nothing COULD have been lost, so the notice is vacuous by construction;
  (c) keep the observation in RECONCILE_OBS (in-band, per-call) and write the DURABLE line only when work could actually have been lost.
(b) is strongest and nearly free: on a clean tree both the added and subtracted sets are empty. Five of the six entries were on trees with no relevant delta.

DO NOT weaken the destroyed-tracker case. 94d.1's loudness is right; only its scope needs narrowing. Any change needs a leg plus a leg proving genuine mid-cycle destruction still writes the durable line — gate-baseline-v2 7S.2 asserts that today and must stay green.

title: F1 approve still truncates the tracker and clears current-task — a legitimate doc-only auto-approve destroys an unrelated in-flight change set and the next Stop cannot name the task
description:
The residual qzv's own filing predicted, re-assessed AFTER the P2 fix landed so the number is
what remains rather than what was there.

THE MECHANISM, unchanged. F1's fast path calls `qa-gate.sh approve`, and every approve ends with
the tracking-state finalization: `write_gate_baseline` -> `truncate_changed_files_tracker` ->
`clear_current_task` -> `wipe_iteration_state`. So an F1 auto-approve wipes changed-files.txt and
the active-task pointer, for whatever cycle they happened to belong to.

DO NOT REORDER THAT PAIRING. The gz3 APPROVE-COMMIT ORDER note in qa-gate.sh is explicit and
tested: baseline BEFORE tracker (an empty tracker must always imply a refreshed baseline, or the
Stop-side VANISHED-CHANGE-SET re-read that closes race W3 can observe a half-finalized pair), and
session state LAST (clearing current-task before the truncation is race W2, "No active Beads task
detected" for work just approved). Both are pinned by approve-idempotency.sh sections E and F. A
fix here must not move those lines.

WHAT P2 CLOSED. The predicate now refuses to auto-approve while an IMPLEMENTER record on the
active task is at-or-newer than the cycle open, so the LIVE reproduction — the exact route
observed four times, including on the v4.1.0 release task — can no longer reach approve, and
therefore can no longer reach the wipe. That is the majority of the occurrences.

WHAT REMAINS, three routes, all reachable:
  (a) claude-workflow-plugin-qzv.1 — record_implementer's per-(role, task) idempotency means a
      role re-spawned in a LATER cycle posts no record, so the predicate reads safe and F1
      approves + wipes while that implementer works. Fixing qzv.1 closes this one.
  (b) The `qa` role has no IMPLEMENTER record by design, so a QA agent writing files during
      review is invisible to the predicate. Also covered by qzv.1's second route.
  (c) INDEPENDENT OF qzv.1, and the one that survives it: a change set that is GENUINELY
      doc-only and legitimately auto-approved still clears current-task. The orchestrator sets
      that pointer before delegating; F1 unsets it, and the NEXT Stop over a real change set
      falls through to the task-less hard block. Recovery is `current-task.sh set <id>`, which
      no block reason mentions — that is what makes it user-visible rather than merely untidy
      (qzv's "second consequence", observed live). Route (c) is not a mis-approval: the approval
      is correct, the CLEANUP's blast radius is wrong.

SO THE HONEST ASSESSMENT: P2 removes the mis-approval that made the wipe common, and does not
touch the wipe. Route (c) is what is left after qzv.1, and it is a scope bug, not a correctness
bug — a verdict about change set A has no business finalizing the tracking state of cycle B.

`--expect-hash` does NOT help here and it would be wrong to claim it does: on these routes the
classified set IS the bound set. The defect is what the cleanup destroys, not what the approval
binds.

CANDIDATE FIXES (pick one, deliberately; each has a cost):
  1. F1 does not call the finalization at all — approve grows a flag (mirroring
     --no-impact-report / --no-review / --accept-reconstructed) that skips the tracking-state
     finalization, and F1 passes it. Cheapest and most surgical; the cost is a fifth audited
     flag on approve and a path where the baseline is NOT refreshed, which has to be checked
     against the W3 reasoning before it ships.
  2. Scope the wipe to the change set the approval bound: truncate only the tracker entries the
     bound hash covered. The tracker has no per-cycle structure today, so this is new state.
  3. Leave the wipe and make the recovery discoverable: name `current-task.sh set <id>` in the
     task-less block reason. Does not fix the loss, makes it survivable — the weakest option,
     and worth doing anyway regardless of which of 1/2 is chosen.

TESTS A FIX NEEDS: an L2 leg where cycle B has a live tracker and current-task, an F1 doc-only
Stop auto-approves, and both survive; plus the existing approve-idempotency E/F sections staying
green (they are what pin the ordering the fix must not disturb).

comments.author: username
comments.text:
CROSS-REFERENCE from claude-workflow-plugin-qzv.3 (devops, 2026-08-07). Not a fix to this task; a note so the finalization-scope question is not re-decided from scratch.

qzv.3's filing said the two must agree on when the F1 arm may finalize tracking state, and "do not fix them independently". What qzv.3 landed, and the rule it commits to:

**THE F1 ARM MAY FINALIZE TRACKING STATE ONLY FOR AN APPROVAL THAT ACTUALLY HAPPENED.** The arm's `rm -f` cleanup (changed-files.txt, edit-count, the iteration counters, the auto-defer counter) is now inside the success branch; a refused `approve` emits a block and `emit_block` exits before the cleanup runs. Reproduced both ways: with `impact-report.sh` removed, the pre-fix arm released with 0 approval records and a WIPED tracker; the fixed arm blocks and `changed-files.txt` survives with its one line.

WHAT THIS DOES **NOT** TOUCH, i.e. what is still entirely yours:
- Route (c), the one that survives qzv.1. A GENUINELY doc-only change set that is legitimately auto-approved still clears `current-task` and still truncates the tracker for whatever cycle they belonged to. That is the SUCCESS path. Nothing in qzv.3 narrows it.
- Nothing in `qa-gate.sh` moved. In particular the gz3 `APPROVE-COMMIT ORDER` (record before label; baseline before tracker; session state last) is byte-for-byte unchanged — approve's refusals all `exit 2` **before** that finalization and never reach it, so the wipe qzv.3 removed was the HOOK's own `rm -f`, not approve's. `approve-idempotency.sh` sections E and F are unaffected.

SO THE TWO DECOMPOSE CLEANLY: qzv.3 fixed that a FAILED approval finalizes anything at all; qzv.2 still has to decide WHICH cycle's state a SUCCESSFUL one may finalize. Your candidate 1 (a fifth audited `approve` flag that skips the tracking-state finalization) is unaffected by qzv.3 and would compose with it — the flag would only ever be passed on the success path, which is the only path that still reaches the finalization. Candidate 3 (naming `current-task.sh set <id>` in the task-less block reason) is likewise untouched and still worth doing.

One datum for whoever takes this: qzv.3's reproduction confirmed QA's round-8 refinement to the original filing — on the FAILURE path `current-task` always survived; only `changed-files.txt` was destroyed. The success path is where both go.

title: TRACKER-PRESERVE guard probes the sibling HELPER, not the state file — a degraded install still destroys the tracker silently
description:
R6-F1 (medium), found and reproduced by QA in review iteration 6, 2026-08-04. Approved-with-residual; QA's recommendation is to land this ALONGSIDE P2 (qzv), not after.

session-start.sh:285-288 establishes SS_ACTIVE_TASK behind [ -f "$SS_SCRIPT_DIR/current-task.sh" ] — it probes the sibling HELPER SCRIPT rather than the state file the helper writes.

REPRODUCED: state file says a cycle is in flight, helper moved aside -> SS_ACTIVE_TASK empty -> tracker DESTROYED, silently, with a valid envelope.

WHY IT IS A REAL PATH, NOT A HYPOTHETICAL: qa-gate.sh:137-158 write_current_task EXPLICITLY supports the helper-absent case via a direct write, and reconcile_tracker reads the same fact directly at :798. So two other consumers already treat the state file as the source of truth and tolerate the helper's absence; only this guard does not.

THE IRONY, WHICH IS THE POINT: the region header rejects the label-based predicate precisely because it would make a local-file decision depend on an external dependency (bd + jq + a round-trip). The shipped predicate then keeps a dependency of the same class — on a sibling script — for a fact the gate already writes and reads directly. QA's framing: 'your own preserve-when-the-read-fails rule, applied to the read that shipped.'

FIX (one line, two acceptable forms):
  (a) read $QA_TRACKING_DIR/current-task directly, as reconcile_tracker does at :798; or
  (b) keep the probe but PRESERVE when the probe is impossible rather than defaulting to delete.
(b) is the more general rule and matches the fail-closed direction already adopted everywhere else in this fix.

Extend session-lifecycle.sh section 8 with a leg for the helper-absent + cycle-in-flight state. The existing 8M META stays as-is.

FAMILY: same shape as 94d.1's parent — a guard whose evidence is weaker than the property it protects. Eleventh instance recorded this session.

title: review-check.sh gate reads only the LATEST review artifact, so findings retire by omission with no evidence trail — P2's binding predicate leans on this
description:
Raised by QA as R5-F4 + suggested follow-up, 2026-08-04, verified against 94d's own review history.

review-check.sh cmd_gate computes the open-finding set from the LATEST REVIEW-ARTIFACT only. Consequence: recording round N+1 silently retires every finding from round N. R4-F1 (the HIGH false-prose finding) was never formally resolved via resolve-finding — it retired by omission the moment R5 was recorded.

In this instance the outcome was correct: QA had independently verified the R4-F1 fix at all seven prose sites before recording R5. But the mechanism does not distinguish 'the reviewer verified the fix' from 'the reviewer forgot'. It is right by reviewer diligence, not by construction, and the flags imply otherwise.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND HYGIENE: P2 (qzv) binds F1 auto-approval to a predicate over these same records, and D2/D5 add design-gate readers on top. A predicate whose open-set can be emptied by writing a newer artifact is a weak foundation for a binding gate.

Fix direction (not yet designed): either require an explicit resolve-finding record per finding before it leaves the open set, or have cmd_gate union open findings across artifacts for the same reviewed_hash and only retire on an explicit resolution. Prefer whichever reuses the existing record grammar — no new id-space (see the arbitrate/finding_id_in_latest_artifact coupling at qa-gate.sh:2539).

FAMILY NOTE: adjacent to the session's recurring shape but distinct. Here nothing reports a false success; rather, an absence is indistinguishable from a resolution. Same root: a state that means two different things with no way to tell which.

comments.author: username
comments.text:
<!-- BD-MCP-META: {"kind":"qa-note","source":"qa-agent","task":"claude-workflow-plugin-qbhw","round":3} -->
## New live instance, and a refinement to the proposed fix direction

Second confirmed instance, from QA round 3 of `claude-workflow-plugin-qbhw` (2026-08-06). Recording it because it is a *stronger* instance than the 94d one and because it breaks one of the two fix directions this task proposes.

**The instance.** I was mid-way through composing a superseding artifact that carried `R1-F1` and `R1-F4` forward alongside two new findings when the session died. The findings existed only in my context. Nothing was recorded; nothing was lost either, because the supersede never landed and the two HIGHs stayed open. It failed safe — but only by luck of *where* the crash landed. Had it hit one step later, the carry-forward would have dropped and both HIGHs would have retired by omission with the gate reporting clean.

**Why this instance is stronger than 94d's.** That one was "right by reviewer diligence" — the reviewer had verified the fix and simply never recorded the resolution. This one is not a diligence failure at all: an infrastructure failure landed precisely on the non-atomic step. The description says the mechanism "does not distinguish 'the reviewer verified the fix' from 'the reviewer forgot'". It also does not distinguish either from *'the reviewer was killed between computing the finding set and writing it'*, and that third case is not addressable by asking reviewers to be careful.

**The refinement — the `reviewed_hash` union would NOT have covered this.** The proposed direction is "union open findings across artifacts for the same `reviewed_hash` and only retire on an explicit resolution." In my round the specialist landed repair commits *while I was reviewing*, so the change set moved 19 → 21 files and the hash moved `1800e3b4…` → `d7311b4b…`. The prior artifacts (`r1`, `r1b`) are bound to the OLD hash; my superseding `r2b` is bound to the NEW one. A union keyed on equal `reviewed_hash` would have found no prior artifact to union with, and the carry-forward would have been exactly as silent as it is today.

That is not an edge case — it is the *normal* shape of a fix round, where the whole point is that the change set moves between reviews.

**So the first proposed direction is the sound one:** require an explicit `resolve-finding` (or `arbitrate … overrule`) record per finding id before it leaves the open set, independent of which artifact is latest and independent of hash. Retirement should be an *act*, not a side effect of writing something newer. If the hash-union is kept at all, it should be a convenience on top of that, not the mechanism.

**Cheap interim mitigation, if the full fix is not scheduled soon:** have `review-record` compare the incoming artifact's finding ids against the currently-open set and *report* (not refuse) any id being dropped without a resolution — e.g. `WARNING: this artifact omits R1-F1, R1-F4, which are open and unresolved; they will retire`. That is the same report-don't-refuse shape `completion_files_crosscheck` uses, it needs no new record grammar, and it converts a silent retirement into a visible one. It would have caught both instances.

**What I did this round, for the record:** carried both HIGHs forward verbatim into `r2b` with their round-1 evidence plus this round's verification, then closed each with an explicit `resolve-finding` citing fix and test refs — so they left the open set by resolution rather than by omission. The gate then correctly reported one remaining open finding (`R2-F1`).

QA CORRECTION FROM P7's APPROVAL, 2026-08-07 — THE PROPOSED FIX WOULD NOT HAVE WORKED, and the reason generalises.

This task proposed that cmd_gate union open findings across artifacts sharing the same reviewed_hash, retiring only on explicit resolution. QA established from its own live case that the union COVERS NOTHING:

  a fix round MOVES the change set BY DESIGN — P7 went 19 -> 21 files, hash 1800e3b4 -> d7311b4b.

So the prior artifact binds the OLD hash and a same-hash union finds no priors to union with. The mechanism is inert exactly when it is needed: after a fix, which is the only time findings could retire by omission.

CHEAP INTERIM QA PROPOSES, and it matches the shape this phase settled on elsewhere: have review-record REPORT the finding ids being dropped without a resolution — the same report-don't-refuse structure completion_files_crosscheck uses (P7/fkm.1.20). It does not block anyone; it makes an omission visible at the moment it happens rather than discoverable later by comparing artifacts.

A different reviewer, or the same one interrupted, would have dropped them silently; QA was in fact killed mid-supersede by a connection error during this very round, and the findings survived only because the partial write never landed.

title: The rubric relay does not persist the grader's structured verdict — the RUBRIC record carries no required_fixes and no grader-verdict-<id>-i<n>.json is written
description:
Found by QA round 5 on 94d, recorded as R5-F2 (medium). A relay/audit defect, not a defect in 94d's change set. Below risk_threshold=high, so it did not block the round.

OBSERVED. For rubric iteration 1 on claude-workflow-plugin-94d:

  - The recorded verdict comment is a BARE ONE-LINER:
      "RUBRIC 2 iteration 1: needs_revision change_set_hash=01296db9... — failed: C1, C4"
    No criterion-by-criterion justifications, no required_fixes JSON block.
  - There is NO .claude/.qa-tracking/grader-verdict-claude-workflow-plugin-94d-i1.json,
    although 12 such files exist for other tasks (p5n, gl6-i1/i2, bjx, m7e, gz3-i1/i2,
    x15, ehv, gzc, pnf, 56r, 36z).

WHY IT MATTERS.
  1. qa.md section 6c/6d instructs QA to extract required_fixes from the latest RUBRIC comment's JSON block and route them through qa-gate.sh block. On this task QA could not: there is no JSON block to parse.
  2. The specialist's own context_coverage records the workaround it had to use — it recovered the full verdict "from the grader subagent's own transcript", noting that "the short RUBRIC 2 iteration 1 record on the task carries only the verdict and the failed criteria".
  3. Consequence for iteration 2: the grader has no durable view of what iteration 1 actually said, so it cannot see whether its own prior reasoning was addressed or contradicted.
  4. Consequence for audit: QA round 5 verified the three required fixes against the ORCHESTRATOR'S DESCRIPTION of them, not against a durable record of the verdict. The fixes are independently verified as discharged; what is unverifiable is whether they were the right three.

WHERE TO LOOK. qa-gate.sh grade-record is documented (qa.md 6c) as recording "the structured JSON pasted below the summary by the helper". Determine whether (a) grade-record dropped the JSON body, (b) the orchestrator invoked it with only a summary, or (c) the grader returned a verdict the helper could not parse into a persisted artifact — and make the failure loud rather than silent. A verdict recorded without its required_fixes should be refused or should warn, in the same spirit as approve refusing a stale impact report.

RELATED. claude-workflow-plugin-fkm.1.3 (the grading packet has no generator and decays silently) is the sibling defect on the input side of the same relay; this one is on the output side.

title: post-edit.sh:249-250 and docs/HOOKS.md:680-681 document a containment limit that measurement contradicts (in-repo symlink pointing out is KEPT, not dropped)
description:
Found by QA round 5 on 94d (rubric iteration 2 packet refresh), recorded as R5-F1 (medium). Below risk_threshold=high, so it did not block the round.

THE CLAIM. The fkm.1.15 CONTAINMENT-FILTER region closes with a two-clause disclosure, present verbatim in two places:

  post-edit.sh:249-252
    LIMIT, stated rather than discovered later: a symlink INSIDE the repo whose
    target is outside resolves to the target and is DROPPED; a symlink outside
    pointing in is KEPT.

  docs/HOOKS.md:680-681 — the same sentence, in shipped operator docs.

THE MEASUREMENT. The first clause is false. QA drove the canonical hook with CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR on a scratch tree over two shapes:

  - in-repo DIRECTORY symlink -> outside:  $ROOT/dirlink -> $OUT ; file_path=$ROOT/dirlink/g.ts   => TRACKED
  - in-repo FILE symlink -> outside:       $ROOT/filelink.ts -> $OUT/real.ts                      => TRACKED

Both are tracked, with no containment log line. The second clause ("a symlink outside pointing in is KEPT") IS correct and QA confirmed it separately.

THE MECHANISM, from the code. `_pe_norm` (post-edit.sh:264) is purely lexical and `_pe_within` (:281) matches the root prefix lexically, so a path spelled through an in-repo symlink is judged INSIDE on the first comparison. The physical resolution at :311 only runs when both root spellings miss, which this shape never does. There is no readlink, realpath, or -L anywhere in the region (verified by grep over :178-320), so nothing can resolve the symlink target on the keep path.

WHY IT IS MEDIUM AND NOT HIGH. The actual behaviour over-tracks, which the region itself repeatedly names as the fail-closed side for the gate. There is no gate-integrity consequence and no behavioural regression: an over-tracked path costs a review look, an under-tracked one is an edit the Stop gate never sees.

WHY IT STILL MATTERS.
  1. It is the FOURTH false-comment instance on 94d (after R1-F2, R1-F3, and R3-F2/fkm.1.16), and the first written from scratch by the round whose own stated theme is comment accuracy. fkm.1.16's close reason already argues that "a round that corrected three false comments and wrote a fourth is evidence comment accuracy needs a mechanical check, not more care"; that argument was made about pre-existing prose the change falsified. This is the stronger version of it.
  2. It sits in the one place a reader is invited to trust as the honest boundary statement of a new rule.
  3. It is the first of the four to reach shipped operator documentation.

FIX. Correct both sites to state what the code does: a path spelled through an in-repo symlink whose target is outside is KEPT (the comparison is lexical and never resolves the target), and only the reverse case reaches the :311 physical retry. Both files are already in 94d's change set, so correcting them is HASH-NEUTRAL — this can land inside the current change set without moving 01296db9....

Consider also whether the stated limit should become the implemented one. QA has no opinion; the safe direction is the one already implemented.
notes:

The F7 completion contract and the root-cause record are the two comments on this

path is the region's own fail-closed side, so the limit was corrected to match the

comments.text:
<!-- BD-MCP-META: {"kind":"root-cause","source":"devops-agent","finding":"R5-F1","verdict":"confirmed"} -->
## Root cause, reproduced independently before touching anything

R5-F1 is confirmed. I did not take QA's measurement on relay — I drove the
CANONICAL `.claude/scripts/post-edit.sh` myself over a fresh scratch tree with
`CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` pointed at it. Probe tree under `mktemp -d`
(`/var/folders/…`) and NOT the session scratchpad, deliberately: rule 1's
`^(/private)?/tmp/claude-[^/]+/` branch would have swallowed every scratchpad
path and every "dropped" would have been the denylist rather than containment.
Probe scripts written by bash heredoc, never the Write tool, so nothing here
entered `changed-files.txt`.

```
root        = /var/folders/…/r5f1.…/root      (CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR)
root pwd -P = /private/var/folders/…/r5f1.…/root

A control in-project        $ROOT/src/a.ts          -> TRACKED (silent)
B control plain outside     $OUT/x.ts               -> dropped (logged)
C in-repo DIR symlink out   $ROOT/dirlink/g.ts      -> TRACKED (silent)
D in-repo FILE symlink out  $ROOT/filelink.ts       -> TRACKED (silent)
E outside symlink -> IN     $OUT/inlink/x.ts        -> TRACKED (silent)
```

Rule 1 = keep and rule 2 = reviewable for all five paths, checked against the
lib directly, so C/D/E being TRACKED is containment's answer and not another
rule's absence. Controls A and B prove the region is live in the same run.

**So the comment's first clause is false: C and D are KEPT, not dropped.**
The second clause ("a symlink outside pointing in is KEPT") is correct — E.

### The mechanism, and it is two different mechanisms, not one

`_pe_norm` (:264) is purely lexical and `_pe_within` (:281) compares against the
root PREFIX lexically, so a path spelled through an in-repo symlink is judged
INSIDE on the first comparison and the `:311` retry never runs. There is no
`readlink`, no `realpath`, no `-L`, no `stat` anywhere in `post-edit.sh` (grep,
whole file). `pwd -P` appears exactly twice, at :299 and :311.

But C and D are kept for measurably different reasons, which is the part the
false claim was reasoning past:

```
C dirname -> pwd -P : /private/var/folders/…/r5f1.…/out    (OUTSIDE the root)
D dirname -> pwd -P : /private/var/folders/…/r5f1.…/root   (the root itself)
```

- C (directory symlink) would have been DROPPED had the retry run. It is kept
  purely because the lexical test already said "inside".
- D (file symlink) would have been KEPT even if the retry had run, because
  `:311` resolves the DIRNAME's ancestry and `:313` reattaches
  `$(basename …)` unresolved. A leaf symlink's own target is never consulted
  anywhere in the region.

### The direction is safe; the behaviour stays

Both are over-tracking, which the region's own header names as the fail-closed
side ("an untracked edit is an edit the Stop gate never sees"). No gate-integrity
consequence. I am correcting the two documentation sites and NOT changing the
behaviour to match the old comment.

### Checked in passing, no defect: the `&&` list at :313

`[ -n "$_PE_DIR" ] && _PE_RESOLVED=…` returns 1 when `cd` failed, and the hook
runs under `set -e`, so I checked whether a path whose dirname does not exist
aborts the hook mid-envelope. It does not — `/no-such-dir-r5f1/f.ts` gives
`rc=0`, stdout `{}`, stderr empty. The failing command is the one BEFORE the
final `&&`, which errexit exempts. No change needed; recording it so the next
reader does not have to re-derive it.

### llm_observations

**Two of my mutants silently failed to apply, and the suite reported green.** E6
and E7 first ran with BSD-sed-incompatible patterns (`\|` alternation is a GNU
extension); the mutant file came out byte-identical to the original and the spec
reported 97/0, which reads exactly like "the assertion is fine". I caught it only
because the harness prints the diff. I then added a hard guard — `cmp -s` the
mutant against the backup and abort with "MUTANT DID NOT APPLY" rather than run
the suite. This is the deployment-checklist item about infra assertions in its
purest form: a check that never executed, a grep that matched a comment, and a
job that silently skipped all look identical to green. Any future mutation probe
in this repo should carry the same guard.

**The 13N token-count assertion was red on its first run, and it was right.** I
copied 12M/13M's `grep -c '<SENTINEL>'` idiom, and it failed because my own
corrected header names `SECOND-CHANCE` in prose three times outside the region.
Worth noting for whoever adds the next strip-META: that idiom is only sound while
no prose mentions the sentinel, which is an invisible precondition of both
existing copies.

**The self-inflicted near-miss is the most instructive thing here.** My first
draft of the corrected comment cited `:309`/`:311`/`:313`. My own insertion had
already moved them to 339/358/359. Had I not re-measured, this round would have
replaced a false claim about symlinks with a false claim about line numbers, in
the same paragraph, while arguing that comment accuracy needs mechanical
enforcement. My edit also staled nothing pre-existing — I checked all five
surviving citations in the region (`:194-197`, `:453`, `:143-150`, `:89-92`,
`impact-report.sh:502`) and each still resolves to what it names.

**A latent errexit question, checked and clean.**
`[ -n "$_PE_DIR" ] && _PE_RESOLVED=…` returns 1 when the `cd` failed, and the
hook runs `set -e`. A path whose dirname does not exist (`/no-such-dir/f.ts`)
gives rc=0, stdout `{}`, empty stderr — the failing command precedes the final
`&&`, which errexit exempts. No change needed; recorded so the next reader does
not re-derive it.

**Adjacent smell not fixed, out of scope.** The gate baseline is 159 lines while
the change set is 26 paths, because it snapshots every dirty path including the
21 denylisted fixture copies. That is not wrong, but it means the baseline's
staleness surface (see `dpe`) is much larger than the change set's.

**Probe hygiene.** Every probe tree lived under `mktemp -d` (`/var/folders/…`),
never the session scratchpad — rule 1's `^(/private)?/tmp/claude-[^/]+/` branch
would have swallowed every scratchpad path and turned every "dropped" into the
denylist's answer instead of containment's. Probe scripts were written by bash
heredoc, never the Write tool, so none reached `changed-files.txt`; the tracker
was checked for `r5f1|pe-symout|pe-canonical|scratchpad` and is clean, and all
probe trees were removed.

### context_coverage

**Read to ground this change.** QA's round-5 `qa-plan` in full (comment 62 of 64
on 94d) plus the `dmi` task description, which is where the measurement and the
mechanism came from; `post-edit.sh:1-405` entire, not just the region, because the
claim under repair is about what the whole file does or does not call;
`docs/HOOKS.md:610-712`, the containment section and the two adjacent rules'
subsections; `specs/post-edit.sh` sections 11 through 13M and the
mutation-survivor block, to match the house idiom for keeps, drops, controls and
strip-METAs; `.claude/tests/component/lib/fixture.sh` `mk_fixture`/`plugin_root`,
to establish that the fixture SYMLINKS the canonical scripts (which is why a
mutant must be applied in place) and that `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` is exported to the
fixture root; `qa-gate.sh` `reconcile_tracker` `:496-605` and
`gate_baseline_entries` `:362-371`, to prove the LESSONS.md append was
hash-neutral before making it; `workflow-denylist.sh`'s regex line;
`LESSONS.md`'s existing entries, specifically the `20e` comment-accuracy lesson
and the `llh.20` line-number-anchor lesson, so the new entry escalates rather
than duplicates. Also ran `git grep` for the false sentence across the whole tree
to confirm there was no third independent copy — only the two named sites and the
seven fixture copies, which `sync-fixtures` refreshes.

**Deliberately NOT read.** The e2e harness under `.claude/tests/e2e/` beyond the
fixture script copies, and `verify-before-stop.sh`'s detection stage: the change
is confined to one hook's containment comment plus one L2 spec, `impact_of` on
`_pe_norm`/`_pe_within` (QA's, re-checked against the graph) shows no fan-out past
the hook's own execution path, and `make test-e2e-unit` was forbidden this round —
so reading the harness would have produced an opinion I could not measure. Also
did not read the other 40 L2 specs; I ran the three L1 suites that name
`post-edit.sh` instead, on the theory that a comment-and-spec change can only
break a test that greps the file, and those are the tests that do.

**Largest remaining unknown.** Whether 13e's third leg passes on a non-darwin
runner. The reasoning is solid — the region has no platform conditional and
`cd <symlink> && pwd -P` is POSIX — but the measurement is darwin-only, and I
have written that limitation into the spec comment rather than into a claim of
platform independence. Secondary unknown: whether `dpe`'s stale-baseline hole has
already silently dropped an edit earlier in this two-day cycle. I did not audit
the other 158 baseline entries against `bb8fce7..HEAD`; that audit belongs on
`dpe`, and doing it here would have moved nothing but my confidence.

## Correction to this task's F7 contract — `decisions[1]` overstated its coverage (QA finding R4-F3 on 94d)

The entry reads:

> "Named the two DIFFERENT mechanisms rather than one. […] That distinction is now
> **asserted (13N's last two legs)**, not just written."

**That was wrong, and QA is right about why.** 13N's last two legs assert that the
in-repo DIRECTORY symlink and the in-repo FILE symlink are both still TRACKED when
the `SECOND-CHANCE` region is excised. That is a statement about **non-reachability**
and it is symmetric: it says the retry is not the cause of either verdict, and
nothing at all about how the two would differ if the retry DID run. The asymmetry —
the whole content of the "two different mechanisms" claim — was reasoning in a
comment, not an assertion. Describing it as asserted put an unearned coverage claim
in the field the rubric grader reads as evidence.

The claim itself is TRUE. QA verified it with mutant M1 (guard forced true, retry
body byte-identical) and measured the DIR symlink flipping TRACKED -> dropped while
the FILE symlink stayed TRACKED, both controls holding.

**Resolved by adding the assertion rather than by softening the sentence** —
`specs/post-edit.sh` **13R**, 13 legs, using exactly QA's mutant shape:

- the guard `if ! _pe_within "$_PE_CANDIDATE"; then` is forced to `if true; then`
  by a text-anchored `awk` substitution, so the retry runs for every path;
- the `SECOND-CHANCE` region is asserted **byte-identical** to the shipped copy, so
  the one variable is the guard and not the body;
- three controls hold (in-project path tracked, plainly-outside path dropped,
  out-of-repo-symlink-pointing-in tracked);
- **the asymmetry**: `dirlink/g.ts` -> dropped (and the drop is LOGGED, so it went
  through containment's arm), `filelink.ts` -> still TRACKED;
- and the shipped hook keeps BOTH, so the divergence is the forced retry rather than
  anything about the two shapes on the real code path.

Observed red before green: with the mutation replaced by a byte-different but
behaviourally-inert edit, the two structural legs and both asymmetry legs go red
(the DIR symlink reports `tracked`) while the FILE-symlink leg stays green — which
is the discriminating result. Spec now 115 pass / 0 fail (was 98).

The prose was corrected in the same pass, in both places that carried it:
`post-edit.sh`'s region header and `docs/HOOKS.md`'s symlink table note now say
what 13N pins (non-reachability, symmetric) and what 13R pins (the counterfactual),
and name R4-F3 as the reason the distinction is spelled out.

Change-set hash unmoved: `01296db9f6e5af2e8254e55ae02b6664163544830357f007a20bb477f05f9ca9`, 26 paths.

title: 94d shipped only half its acceptance list: out-of-repo paths are still recorded (acceptance item 2 never landed)
description:
R3-F1, found by QA at review round 4 of P1 (claude-workflow-plugin-94d) and MEASURED, not inferred.

The 2026-07-29 bug report that opened 94d documents TWO failure modes and closes with TWO numbered acceptance items:
  (1) fold git-visible changed paths INTO the tracker  -> SHIPPED as reconcile_tracker
  (2) drop paths OUTSIDE CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR at record time -> NEVER SHIPPED

Item 2 appears in no F7 completion contract, no decisions entry, no resolve-finding record, and in NONE of QA four review rounds until round 4. A grep of the entire task record finds '/tmp/enc-diff.sh' and 'over-coverage' only inside the original report itself.

MEASURED STILL LIVE (3 legs): a path under /tmp, a path in a different git repo, and a mktemp -d path under /var/folders/ are ALL recorded into changed-files.txt by post-edit.sh.

WHY IT WAS NOT BLOCKED AT ROUND 4: pre-existing rather than regressed; fail-closed (over-coverage, never under); visible rather than silent; and conditional on an agent choosing an out-of-repo target rather than firing deterministically the way R2-F5 did. QA judged that blocking on something it had failed to raise in three prior rounds, after the specialist discharged everything it DID raise, would be moving the goalposts. Correct call.

THE ARGUMENT THAT MATTERS, from QA: the specialist own reasoning against a call-site fix for R2-F5 — that it makes correctness depend on every future writer picking the right TOOL — applies verbatim to the current mitigation for this half, which is a paragraph in qa.md 3a telling every agent to pick the right DIRECTORY. Same defect shape, same objection.

FIX DIRECTION: a containment check against CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR at record time in post-edit.sh, beside the two existing filters. QA notes this narrow fix does NOT carry the objection recorded against widening the /tmp denylist, because a containment check keeps the component suite own fixture paths — they are written INSIDE the mktemp root the suite points CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR at.

SEQUENCING: land AFTER the grader verdict on 94d. Fixing it now moves the change-set hash and costs that verdict its binding.

WHAT THIS IS EVIDENCE FOR, and why it belongs in Phase P rather than being quietly fixed: 94d had NO spec doc and an EMPTY task description, so C1 had to be graded against two bug-report comments. Half an acceptance list went unshipped and unnoticed across four adversarial review rounds by two reviewers plus a paid lane attempt. This is the v5.0.0 thesis as a measured fact about the plugin own work: nothing verified that the implementation matched the intent, because the intent was never written anywhere a check could read it. Cite this task in the D1 design-artifact rationale.
close_reason: Landed inside 94d's change set, hash-neutral (01296db9… unmoved). post-edit.sh CONTAINMENT-FILTER region drops out-of-project paths at record time and logs each drop; pinned by specs/post-edit.sh section 13 (23 assertions incl. a 13M strip-META, watched failing first at 9/69) and specs/denylist-shared.sh D4, which asserts rule 1 still keeps /tmp scratch while the hook drops it. Acceptance item (2) of the 2026-07-29 report is discharged; docs and the falsified prose updated in the same set. Full record in the comment.

title: grade-record does not persist required_fixes into the durable record; qa.md 6c claims it does
description:
R6-F4, confirmed by two independent reviewers during fkm.1.1. qa-gate.sh grade-record writes 'RUBRIC <v> iteration <n>: <verdict> ... failed: C6' and drops the required_fixes array entirely. The iteration-3 verdict for fkm.1.1 survives in Beads as the string 'failed: C6' and nothing else.

Consequence: QA had to reconstruct all eight required_fixes from the orchestrator's J21 comment to verify their discharge. A verdict that names what must change, whose list of what must change is not stored, cannot be mechanically checked against the fix.

Also fix .claude/agents/qa.md section 6c, which states the helper pastes the structured JSON below the summary. It does not. Same defect class as the F7 completion contract having no mechanical path into the durable record.

title: The grading packet has no generator and decays silently against the tree
description:
Observed live during fkm.1.1. .claude/.qa-tracking/grading-packet-<task>.md is hand-assembled; nothing regenerates it. It went stale across 17 files spanning two remediation waves, carrying 8 live copies of a pre-R4-F1 claim that existed 0 times in the tree.

Cost: two full grader iterations were spent on text that was already fixed, and the loop's 3-iteration cap was nearly exhausted on a stale artifact. Caught only because someone diffed the packet against the tree.

qa-gate.sh enter already computes item 3 (the git diff) and item 7 (the change set + caller data). Emitting them into the packet retires the class. A working generator was written during r5 review and left in the session scratchpad rather than installed (correctly — it was out of scope then).

title: Phase D3 — grilling record precondition and vendored-doc integrity
description:
# Phase D3 — grilling record precondition and vendored-doc integrity

SCOPE RE-AUDITED against the tree at d8f75ab, 2026-08-18, per CONTRIBUTING's convention that a phase's
scope is re-audited before it starts. The plan's D3 section was written 2026-08-12, before D1 shipped;
D1, D2, mdnc, rqer, j7kk and icn4 have all landed since. Anchors below are MEASURED, not quoted from
the plan.

## What D3 builds

### 1. The grilling record

    qa-gate.sh grilling-record <tid> --rounds <n> --questions <n> --approaches <n> --unresolved <n> '<summary>'

    GRILLING v1 rounds=<n> questions=<n> approaches=<n> unresolved=<n> vendor_hash=<h> at <ts>: <summary>

Same validation-ladder shape as the existing recorders. approaches >= 2 (the vendored method's own bar)
else insufficient_approaches. WRITTEN BY THE ORCHESTRATOR AT ROOT — it ran the dialogue; no subagent
can.

Writer-side character classes are mandatory, reject-never-sanitise, per the bjx class. Note 46w9 needed
a WIDER class for model ids because real ones carry brackets; pick each class from real values and test
it against them.

### 2. vendor_hash and the integrity half

    vendor_hash = workflow-manifest.sh hash-file .claude/vendor/superpowers/brainstorming/SKILL.md

MEASURED live at this commit: a4b64ceabc10fc9239c257019f44481ae8e9ccaa620252438d4d6de1dac5f249
The instrument is at workflow-manifest.sh:909 (hash-file subcommand), already shipped.

The point: the record names WHICH METHOD TEXT WAS IN FORCE, so later drift cannot retroactively validate
a dialogue that never followed it.

.claude/vendor/superpowers/MANIFEST.md gains the recorded hash — MEASURED: it carries NO hash line today
(grep for sha/hash returns only unrelated prose in its conflict table). vendored-skills.test.sh asserts
the recorded hash equals the live one, with a META perturbing a copy.

MEASURED: vendored-skills.test.sh exists, currently PASSES 94 assertions, and enforces its own
EXPECTED_ASSERTIONS floor at :654 with the message 'Update EXPECTED_ASSERTIONS deliberately, or find the
dropped assertion.' Bump it deliberately in the same change — that floor is the same shape as the L1
completeness floor and exists for the same reason.

### 3. The precondition

design-record refuses grilling_record_missing when no GRILLING v1 record exists on the task OR ITS PARENT
EPIC, inside # GRILLING-PRECONDITION BEGIN/END.

MEASURED: design-record is D1's, cmd_design_record at qa-gate.sh:6091, writing DESIGN-ARTIFACT v1. That
is the correct host for the precondition — you should not be able to record a design artifact without
having grilled first. Do NOT put it on D2's design-review-record (a different subcommand, a different
record, written by a different actor at a different time).

Its existing refusal ladder to match in shape: artifact_path_not_derived, artifact_outside_spec_dir,
designer_touched_source.

THIS IS THE PRE-DELEGATION PATH AND IT IS A SCRIPT, so the check is mechanical — NOT at Stop. The v4.1
closure already states the reason.

Carve-out --no-grilling '<reason>' for the F1 doc-only class and the single-line-typo path. NOTE THE
LESSON D2 PAID FOR: when you add an audited bypass, every existing call site that must pass it has to be
found by ENUMERATION, not by searching until you find one. D2's R1-F1 was exactly this — the F1
fast-path approve lacked --no-design and every doc-only Stop blocked. Enumerate the readers, not just
the callers: writer call sites, plus assertions anchoring the grammar, plus restorations reproducing the
state the record binds (see LESSONS.md, and fkm.4's 'denominator' task doc for the worked example).

## Measured facts that shape the work

- Exit codes 5, 6 and 7 are ALL FREE in qa-gate.sh (0 occurrences each). Exit 3 is overloaded — the
  contract table documents 'atomic operation rolled back' while j7kk's store-unavailable path also
  emits it. If you amend the table, fix that too (filed separately).
- The store canary fails any L1 spec during which the production Beads store advances. Isolate with a
  mechanism that measured FAIL-CLOSED: cd into an initialised fixture, or bd -C. BEADS_DIR is
  FAIL-OPEN — it isolates only when the target is already a store and silently falls back to production
  otherwise. Verify by driving.
- EXPECTED_SPECS for the L1 tier is 42. Adding a spec means bumping it in the same change.
- make lint does not cover .claude/tests/component/; run shellcheck directly if you touch it.

## Related open work
- e2j — vendored-skills.test.sh's positive sentinel against the vendored file. D3's integrity half is
  adjacent; read it and say whether D3 closes it, partly closes it, or is orthogonal.

## Acceptance
Four-part pairing on every new check. Red-before-fix, reported with what each leg printed. Every number
carries its command and the commit it was measured at.

GRILLING v1 record via grilling-record with approaches>=2 enforced, live vendor_hash recompute binding the brainstorming method text, MANIFEST.md hash row asserted by vendored-skills section 13 (94->100 assertions, verified RED pre-D3), and the design-record precondition refusing grilling_record_missing on task-or-parent-epic with an audited --no-grilling carve-out. Cross-file counts match the implementer's claim exactly. Reader population enumerated repo-wide (`grep -rn GRILLING`): no reader missed; the modified DESIGN-ARTIFACT grammar only gains a free-text suffix after the summary, past every machine token.
- Forgery probes (isolated fixture): prose quotation containing `GRILLING v1 ` mid-comment → still `grilling_record_missing` (anchoring sound). Prefix-only forged comment with no counters/vendor_hash → satisfies the precondition (reader validates 12 chars; see R1-F1).

## Rulings on the two flagged judgment calls
1. **Existence-only: CORRECT.** A grilling precedes the artifact, so there is no design_hash to bind at grilling time; amendment-aware re-grilling would put the human dialogue inside every D2 revision round (reviewer loop deadlocks on human availability) plus new re-grill/waive machinery. D2's reviewer already polices artifact-level drift per amendment. Residual (old grilling + much-later design) is disclosed in grilling_record_exists's header and mitigated by vendor_hash + timestamps for human audit. Alternative cost: disproportionate for a phase-start ceremony gate.
2. **Forgery framing: VERIFIED with one refinement.** True at the transport layer — every record is an unauthenticated bd comment; bd has no per-agent identity (all comments author as the same user), so no sibling is defended either, and "nothing to compare against" for `who=` is sound. Refinement: GRILLING v1 is the laxest READER in the family (prefix-only, measured), where siblings re-derive content (design-satisfied re-hashes the artifact; approve binds change_set_hash). Not blocking; cheap tightening suggested (R1-F1).

## e2j: ORTHOGONAL, confirmed, with a refinement posted to e2j
Section 13 is hash-identity; a gutted-but-hash-updated file passes it cleanly — e2j's criteria (sentinel against $VENDORED_SKILL, non-vacuity floor) remain unmet and open. Refinement: e2j's uncoordinated-deletion repro steps are now stale (they trip 13.2 post-D3); comment left on e2j.

# Default rubric (v2)

Applies to every task graded under the rubric-grader QA loop (spec Phase A). Each criterion below is a pass/fail assertion the grader evaluates from the grading packet: `bd show` for the task, the SPEC doc, the diff of the files listed in `.qa-tracking/changed-files.txt`, the F7 completion contract returned by the specialist, and `LESSONS.md`. One-line justification per criterion. No numeric score theater — pass or fail.

The criteria are intentionally short and checkable. Where the criterion needs context (boundary-mock fidelity, F7 fields), the "Evidence that satisfies it" line names the artefact the grader looks at.

## Criteria

### C1. Behavior matches the task description and SPEC.

The shipped diff implements the behavior the task description asks for, and matches the goal + acceptance criteria stated in the attached SPEC doc (read via `bd_doc_read(task_id, name="spec")`). Out-of-scope behavior the SPEC explicitly excludes is NOT in the diff.

Evidence that satisfies it: a 1-2 sentence walk-through that maps every user-visible behavior in the SPEC to a code path in the diff (or to a deliberate, documented deferral in the F7 `decisions` array). A diff that adds plausibly-related behavior the SPEC does not name fails this criterion — that is scope creep.

### C2. Tests added exercise user behavior rather than implementation.

Where the diff introduces new behavior, the diff also introduces tests that assert against the user-visible contract (return shape, side effects, error envelope, accessibility role, status code) rather than against the implementation's private structure (function-name mocking, line-coverage gymnastics, internal control-flow assertions).

Evidence that satisfies it: at least one test in the diff that would still pass if the implementation were rewritten while keeping the user contract identical. A test that asserts only against private symbols, internal call counts, or framework boilerplate fails this criterion.

### C3. The F7 completion contract carries all seven fields with substantive `llm_observations`.

The specialist's structured completion payload includes `task_id`, `files_changed`, `tests_added`, `decisions`, `blockers`, `llm_observations`, and `context_coverage`. `llm_observations` is non-trivial narrative — what surprised the specialist, what was unclear, what they noticed and did not act on. A boilerplate one-liner like "no observations" fails this criterion (principle 9: `llm_observations` is mandatory and substantive).

Evidence that satisfies it: each of the seven fields is present and the `llm_observations` paragraph is the kind of thing a human engineer would say at a stand-up. C3 scores presence-of-seven plus the quality of `llm_observations`; the quality of `context_coverage` is C8's job, so a payload can pass C3 on presence and still fail C8 on substance.

### C4. No unrelated scope in the diff.

Every file the specialist touched serves the task. Drive-by refactors, formatting churn on untouched lines, and "while I'm here" cleanups that exceed the task brief fail this criterion — they should be filed as paired follow-up Beads tasks instead.

Evidence that satisfies it: the diff's file list maps cleanly to the SPEC's deliverables; any incidental change is either trivial (one-line typo fix) or explicitly justified in the `decisions` array.

### C5. J26 modules relevant to the diff are addressed.

Where the diff touches a domain covered by the J26 security taxonomy (SECRETS, INJECTION, AUTH, CONFIG, DEPS, AI, MOBILE, DATA — see `docs/AGENTS.md`), the diff demonstrates that the relevant modules were considered. Untouched J26 domains are out of scope.

Evidence that satisfies it: the `decisions` array (or the SPEC) names which J26 modules apply, and the diff shows defences in those modules (input validation at the trust boundary, parameterised queries, narrow CORS, audited logging, etc.). A diff that touches user input handling without naming INJECTION fails this criterion.

### C6. Docs updated where behavior changed.

When the diff changes user-visible behavior, the documentation that describes that behavior is updated in the same change. This includes `CHANGELOG.md`, README sections, `docs/*.md`, command help text, and SPEC docs the diff renders out of date.

Evidence that satisfies it: a docs-only file in `files_changed` paired with each behavioral change, or a deliberate `decisions` entry stating why a doc deferral is correct (e.g. an internal refactor that ships without user-visible change). A behavioral change that ships with no doc update and no deferral note fails this criterion.

### C7. Boundary-mock fidelity (LESSONS.md lesson 2).

When the diff introduces or modifies mocks of boundaries the project does not control (third-party HTTP APIs, external SDKs, system calls, message-bus payloads), every such mock derives its shape from a fixture extracted from the real downstream producer's spec (OpenAPI, proto file, SDK source, vendor docs). The fixture's source is cited in a comment, the `decisions` array, or `llm_observations`.

**Automatic needs_revision:** circular pass-through assertions are an immediate fail. A mock that feeds `body.error` so a test can assert `body.error` proves nothing — it tests the test's own setup, not the production behavior. Cite `LESSONS.md` lesson 2 in the justification.

Evidence that satisfies it: every new boundary mock points at a fixture file (`.fixtures/`, `__fixtures__/`, `testdata/`) carrying a snapshot of the producer's payload, and the fixture has a comment naming the source (URL, commit, SDK version). Tests assert against the producer's contract, not against the mock's own input.

### C8. `context_coverage` names what was read, what was skipped, and the largest unknown.

The F7 payload's seventh field records three things, in order: the sources the specialist actually read to ground the change; the sources they deliberately did NOT read, and why; and the largest remaining unknown the work ships on. It fails on the same three-way taxonomy C3 applies to `llm_observations` — **empty**, **boilerplate** ("read the relevant files", "full context gathered"), or **detached from the work**: sources named that the diff plainly does not depend on, or the file carrying the diff's central change missing from the list. A coverage note with no deliberate omission in it is boilerplate by construction, because there is always one.

This is not a new principle. It is the evidence-before-fix discipline (`docs/AGENTS.md`) applied *before* the change rather than after — that protocol arms only on bug-typed tasks, and the ordinary feature work that produced the motivating 14-PR speculative-fix chain never gets typed as a bug at all.

Evidence that satisfies it: named files or artefacts (paths, doc names, task ids, log lines) in the "read" part; at least one explicit omission carrying its reason; and an unknown concrete enough that a reviewer could act on it. Grade it against the diff, not against its own confidence — the sources named should be the ones the change actually depends on.

# DevOps rubric (v1)

Applied additionally when the task carries the `devops` label. Default criteria still apply; these add domain-specific checks pulled from `.claude/agents/devops.md`. The leverage is default + bugfix — these are the few devops-specific failure modes that recur.

## Criteria

### D1. Scripts are idempotent and re-runnable.

Install, uninstall, hook, and CI scripts in the diff produce the same end state when run twice in a row. A second run of `install.sh` does not double-write hooks, clobber prior settings, or fail because a directory already exists. A migration script that exits non-zero on its second run fails this criterion.

Evidence that satisfies it: every new script uses `mkdir -p`, conditional inserts, and idempotent label operations (`bd label add` returns success if already present); the `decisions` array documents any deliberately non-idempotent step (e.g. a one-shot data migration) and pairs it with a guard (lock file, completion sentinel) so a re-run is detected.

### D2. Graceful degradation on missing optional tools.

When the diff depends on an optional tool (gitleaks, shellcheck, a particular bd version, a specific CI runner image), the missing-tool path is handled: log a structured warning, fall back to a safe default, exit zero where the workflow allows. A hook that exits non-zero because `gitleaks` is not installed fails this criterion — that is not a developer-machine-portable failure mode.

Evidence that satisfies it: every new tool dependency is probed (`command -v tool >/dev/null`); the fallback path is documented in the script comments and tested at L1; the `decisions` array names the dependency and its installation hint.

### D3. No new permission prompts; autonomy preserved.

The diff does not add `permissions.deny` rules to `settings.json`, narrow specialist tool lists below the broad allow set, or introduce any user-facing approval step the plugin previously ran without. Principle 3 of the v3 plan is "full autonomy, no permission prompts" — every deny rule becomes a future approval prompt and breaks the workflow.

Evidence that satisfies it: a diff of `.claude/settings.json` shows only `permissions.allow` expansions, never `deny`; specialist tool frontmatter is unchanged or expanded; the `decisions` array calls out any new tool the broadened allow set covers.

### D4. Secrets and PII stay out of source, logs, and history.

Hardcoded API keys, tokens, passwords, private keys, committer emails, and PII are absent from the diff. Logs that the diff adds redact sensitive fields before writing. A commit that introduces an `.env` file with values, a personal email address in a script header, or unredacted PII in a log line fails this criterion (extends C5 / SECRETS + DATA).

Evidence that satisfies it: secrets read from a secret manager or environment variable at runtime; PII fields in new log lines are redacted (`***@`, `user_id=***`); a `gitleaks`-equivalent pass on the diff is clean, and the `decisions` array names the secrets the diff touches.
