### 5. LESSONS.md — the WHOLE ledger, verbatim

# Lessons ledger

Production lessons learned the hard way. Each entry is a single-sentence
takeaway, traceable to the Beads task(s) that produced it, tagged for
retrieval, with the date it was first recorded.

## Entry grammar

One line per lesson, three HTML comments in a fixed order:

    - <text> <!-- sources: id1, id2 --> <!-- tags: gate, testing --> <!-- recorded: YYYY-MM-DD -->

**Line order is load-bearing.** `.claude/agents/grader.md` and
`.claude/rubrics/default.md` cite lessons by ordinal position ("lesson 1",
"lesson 2"), and `.claude/agents/orchestrator.md` cites "entry 1". Never sort,
group or re-section this file: doing so repoints those citations at different
lessons *silently* — nothing errors, and the citation still reads plausibly.
Scoping happens through tags, which leave line order untouched.

A field value containing `-->` would close its comment early and relocate
every later field on read-back, so `lessons.sh` rejects such input rather than
cleaning it. The arrow `->` is fine; `-->` is not.

## Tag vocabulary (closed)

Every entry carries at least one tag. Tags are a coarse retrieval filter, not
a taxonomy — an entry carries every tag a reader might plausibly filter on,
and when in doubt the tag goes on.

| Tag | Covers |
| --- | --- |
| `gate` | the QA gate and its machinery: approval binding, labels, hooks, Stop-time checks, the change-set tracker |
| `testing` | test design: oracles, fixtures, META-tests, what an assertion actually proves |
| `packaging` | install / uninstall / upgrade, the manifest, releases, vendored and generated artifacts |
| `agents` | agent prompts, spawning and delegation, model selection and ranking, subagent runtime behaviour |
| `evidence` | how you know a thing is true: measurement versus claim, silent-success failure modes, root cause |
| `process` | workflow and planning rules, the tracker, cost, and where a decision has to be written down |

The vocabulary is enforced by `TAG_VOCABULARY` in `.claude/scripts/lessons.sh`;
extending it means editing that list and this table together, and a test
asserts the two agree.

## Adding an entry

    bash .claude/scripts/lessons.sh add --stdin \
        --source <task-id> --tag <tag> [--tag <tag>]... <<'LESSON'
    <one sentence, framed as the rule for next time, not the story of this time>
    LESSON

**Use `--stdin` with a quoted heredoc.** Neither inline quote style is safe
for this corpus: single quotes protect the backticks lessons routinely contain
but end at the first apostrophe, and double quotes protect apostrophes but run
backticks as command substitution. Several entries below lost their
possessives to the single-quoted form — "the gate's own" became "the gate
own". **Do not repair them by re-adding a corrected version**: dedup matches on
normalized text, so a corrected re-add appends a duplicate instead of
replacing the damaged entry. Never hand-edit; the only legitimate hand-edit is
pruning entries that are no longer relevant.

## Reading

    lessons.sh list                            # the whole file, verbatim
    lessons.sh list --tag gate --tag testing   # OR-combined
    lessons.sh list --since 2026-07-01 --limit 10
    lessons.sh list --untagged                 # must always be empty

The orchestrator reads a recent slice during planning, the QA agent proposes
additions at epic close, and the grader (Phase A) receives the WHOLE ledger in
its packet — lessons are criteria-by-reference there, so filtering the
grader's copy would narrow the criteria it can apply. That is why `list` with
no flags prints the file verbatim, and why the grading-packet step in
`qa.md` must never pass a filter.

Treat this as the institutional memory the plugin runs against, not a static
reference doc.

## Lessons

- Parallel agents in the same working tree contaminate each other's branches; concurrent specialists require worktree isolation. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-e0d.7 --> <!-- tags: agents, process --> <!-- recorded: 2026-06-11 -->

A mock that feeds `body.error` so the test can assert `body.error` is circular and proves nothing. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-e0d.7 --> <!-- tags: testing --> <!-- recorded: 2026-06-11 -->
- New agent files must be registered in .claude-plugin/plugin.json agents[] in the same commit that creates them; an unregistered agent is silently invisible to the SDK — no error surfaces. Guard: agents-manifest-parity test. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-l1r.5 --> <!-- tags: agents, packaging --> <!-- recorded: 2026-06-11 -->

Any agent-spawning step must live at the root conversation level; design multi-agent handoffs as root-orchestrated relays, never nested spawns. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-l1r.5 --> <!-- tags: agents --> <!-- recorded: 2026-06-11 -->

When a workflow REQUIRES a tool call, make it mechanical (compute it where calls are reliable — e.g. orchestrator at root — and pass results down), don't prompt for it. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-n6d --> <!-- tags: agents --> <!-- recorded: 2026-06-12 -->

- A count offered as evidence must name the population it was counted over: a grep against a committed export is not a query against the live database, and the export can lag it silently, so an exactly-N that establishes a negative is only as wide as the corpus behind it. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-fkm.1.11 --> <!-- tags: evidence --> <!-- recorded: 2026-08-10 -->
- A review control set's sensitivity to a defect is measurable, not assumable: revert the fix into a copy, run the suite, and count the reds — a suite that stays green over the revert was never reviewing that defect. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-fkm.1.11 --> <!-- tags: testing --> <!-- recorded: 2026-08-10 -->
- When a fix pins one mechanism by which repository configuration decides what a producer emits, enumerate the whole family before claiming the class is closed — clean/smudge filters, eol and encoding normalisation, and textconv/external diff are three separate doors into the same room. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-fkm.1.11 --> <!-- tags: evidence --> <!-- recorded: 2026-08-10 -->
- When a fix removes a class of blindness from an instrument, re-measure in the environment the fix ships INTO, not only the one that exhibited the bug: the residual hides exactly at the edge of what the instrument can newly see, which is where the fix will naturally stop. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-a9hh --> <!-- tags: evidence, testing --> <!-- recorded: 2026-08-11 -->
- An orphaned-process assertion must probe a token unique to its own run; a machine-global literal like `pgrep -f 'sleep 31337'` turns the control red whenever a second copy of its own tier runs on the same host. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-a9hh --> <!-- tags: testing --> <!-- recorded: 2026-08-11 -->
- A runner or hook that will execute on a different OS or shell major version than the dev box must be measured on that platform before it ships; a container run costs minutes and is the only evidence covering the platform CI actually uses. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-a9hh --> <!-- tags: testing --> <!-- recorded: 2026-08-11 -->
- A docker bind mount whose source path does not exist is created as an empty directory rather than failing, so a control run can silently measure nothing; pipe scripts in with `bash -s` and make every control prove it executed before its result is believed. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-a9hh --> <!-- tags: evidence --> <!-- recorded: 2026-08-11 -->
- Any observation placed inside a trap can mask a trap-timing defect: in a9hh a file write in the EXIT trap hid a mid-tier scratch-dir deletion, and the guard both reviewers reached for made it worse. Prefer empty trap-space to a guarded trap, and treat every in-trap probe as a possible probe effect. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-a9hh --> <!-- tags: evidence, testing --> <!-- recorded: 2026-08-11 -->
- A count of assertion CALL SITES is not the count that executed, and reports slide between them silently: a9hh's control has 232 assert_* call sites and executes 216. Report what ran, and say which number you counted. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-a9hh --> <!-- tags: evidence --> <!-- recorded: 2026-08-11 -->
- Label a probe variant by its body verbatim, never by a component list: "guard + write + rm" cannot distinguish guard-then-write from write-then-guard, and in a9hh those two byte-identical statements differ 28/40 BAD versus 0/40 — a whole round was spent reconciling an ambiguous label against an unambiguous table. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-a9hh --> <!-- tags: evidence, testing --> <!-- recorded: 2026-08-11 -->
- A reddening mutation only binds the bytes it was run against: re-verify the negative control after any later edit to the spec, because a control validated against pre-edit bytes proves nothing about what ships. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-a9hh --> <!-- tags: testing --> <!-- recorded: 2026-08-11 -->
- When a report attributes a cause, check the cause's timestamps against the effect's before repeating it — an explanation that predates its own mechanism is a guess wearing evidence. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-a9hh --> <!-- tags: evidence --> <!-- recorded: 2026-08-11 -->
- A busy-guard that samples once at start does not exclude a writer that arrives a minute later; a measurement taken for a gate decision must assert exclusivity for its whole duration, not at its first instant. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-a9hh --> <!-- tags: evidence, gate --> <!-- recorded: 2026-08-11 -->
- A restore check built on a content hash cannot see a file's mode, so a mutation sweep that rewrites and restores a file must compare mode alongside sha256 or it will silently strip the executable bit. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-s5qf --> <!-- tags: evidence, testing --> <!-- recorded: 2026-08-11 -->
- A NEW GUARD IS VACUOUS UNTIL ITS REDDENING MUTATION IS RUN, and two shapes of vacuity look identical to a green suite. The first: the guard duplicates a failure the code already had, so the assertion passes against a build with the guard deleted. D1 added `[ -f ]` / `[ -r ]` refusals to a file hasher whose existing 64-hex length check ALREADY exited non-zero on a missing path — the "refuses a missing file" legs passed with the guards removed, and only asserting the guard's OWN diagnostic string made them sensitive. The second: the guard aborts and its abort is swallowed. Two `index(.)` calls in a jq validator were wrong in the way jq is famously wrong — a function argument is evaluated against that function's INPUT, so `$ids | index(.)` searches $ids for $ids and returns 0 forever, while `$ready | index(.id)` raises "Cannot index array with string" — and a trailing `|| result=""` turned the abort into "no cycle found". The dependency-cycle check was reachable only on a graph where NOTHING is ready at step one, so a pure two-unit cycle was caught while every graph with a root silently passed. Both were found by writing a wrong artifact and driving it, not by reading the code. Run the mutation, count the reds, and investigate a mutant that reds NOTHING before believing it: the first mutation run here reddened zero assertions in five of nine mutants because the mutant tree was built from `git ls-files` and the new spec was untracked. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-fkm.3 --> <!-- tags: gate, testing --> <!-- recorded: 2026-08-12 -->
- Two containment checks for one directory, in one control flow, using two notions of containment: `design_path_is_foreign` reduced a path LEXICALLY while `cmd_design_record`, 130 lines later, resolved it PHYSICALLY. Either half read as correct on its own. Together they were a hole: `$PROJECT_DIR/docs/specs/../../src/pwn.sh` was "inside the design directory" for the check that enforces the designer edit ban and "outside" for the one that refuses `--file`, so a designer could modify source and still record the design. The symlink case was the same defect from the other side — `-f` follows a leaf, and only `dirname` was resolved, so the record bound bytes from outside the repository. When two call sites ask the SAME question, they must call the SAME function; a second implementation of a predicate is a second answer waiting for an input that separates them. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-fkm.3 --> <!-- tags: gate, testing --> <!-- recorded: 2026-08-12 -->
- A pairing requirement satisfied on the SAFE half of a pair manufactures confidence. The design-artifact spec drove a `../` traversal at `--file` — the entry point that was already resolved physically — and correctly refused, so the green run read as "traversal is handled". The check that actually enforces the ban reads the change-set tracker, and no leg ever put a hostile spelling into it, which is why two HIGH findings shipped green under 121 passing assertions. For any check with more than one entry point, drive the hostile input at EVERY entrance, in every spelling that defeats the reduction being replaced: `..`, a leaf symlink, a relative path, and the root spelled through a symlink. And run the mutation: my own "nothing was recorded" legs passed under the fully un-fixed build, because a DIFFERENT guard (an artifact task_id mismatch) refused first — the fixture had to be corrected before those legs measured containment at all. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-fkm.3 --> <!-- tags: evidence, testing --> <!-- recorded: 2026-08-12 -->
- `cd <dir>` in bash is LOGICAL mode: it collapses `..` LEXICALLY and only falls back to physical resolution when the reduced path fails to chdir, so `pwd -P` afterwards cannot undo a `..` the `cd` already ate — it reports where the `cd` landed. A containment check built as `( cd "$(dirname "$p")" && pwd -P )` therefore answers for the SPELLING whenever a `..` follows a directory symlink and the lexical reduction happens to exist, which is the common case for a path spelled through the directory being guarded. The fix is one flag, `cd -P`; the reason it shipped is that the comment beside it credited `pwd -P` with the resolution, so no reader had a reason to look for the flag. When a comment names the mechanism, assert in a test that the code and the comment agree — a prose leg over the region's comment lines reddens on the next edit that quietly drops the flag. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-fkm.3 --> <!-- tags: evidence, gate --> <!-- recorded: 2026-08-12 -->
- An enumeration whose EXIT STATUS is discarded is a check that fails open, and `while read ... done < <(find ... 2>/dev/null)` discards it twice over: process substitution loses the status and the redirect loses the diagnostic. A directory that is searchable but not listable then produces zero rows at rc 0, which a consumer cannot distinguish from "nothing is declared" — and the consumer here documented that exact distinction in its own comments, captured the query's rc carefully, and was defeated by the inner layer returning 0. Read the enumeration from a file whose status can be checked, and quote the tool's own diagnostic in the refusal. The same call also needs `-H` when the enumerated directory may itself be a symlink: `find` does not descend a final symlink operand without it, on BSD and GNU alike, while the `[ -d ]` guard above it does follow — so the guard passes and the scan comes back silently empty. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-fkm.3 --> <!-- tags: gate, testing --> <!-- recorded: 2026-08-12 -->
- A PATHNAME ROUND-TRIPPED THROUGH A COMMAND SUBSTITUTION IS A DEFECT CLASS, NOT A BUG. `$( )` strips EVERY trailing newline and cannot tell a newline that terminates a command's output from a newline that is the last byte of a filename, so `p=$(dirname "$x")` and `n=$(basename "$x")` silently answer for a DIFFERENT path than the kernel opens. One containment predicate carried eleven of them — two `dirname`, four `basename`, one `readlink`, and five CALLER captures of the answer the predicate printed — and four consecutive review rounds each fixed the spelling that was reported and were each followed by another. Three things generalise. First, the caller's capture is part of the class: making the walk byte-preserving while the caller still writes `x=$(predicate "$p")` moves the truncation one frame out and can INVERT the answer, so a predicate that decides containment should return an EXIT STATUS and compare both sides as `$PWD` inside one subshell rather than print a path. Second, prefer deleting the input to filtering it: the artifact path was derivable from the task id all along, so making `--file` an assertion that may only restate the derived value retired five findings at once, where a character-class filter would have retired none of them and broken a project living under `/My Drive`. Third, `${p%/*}` is not `dirname` — dirname strips trailing slashes FIRST, and forgetting that flips the verdict on a bare directory entry — and where a command's output genuinely cannot be read byte-preservingly (`readlink` has no portable `-z`), the reconstruction can still be PROVEN with `[ "$orig" -ef "$recon" ]`, bash's device+inode comparison, which is false exactly when the round-trip lost a byte. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-fkm.3 --> <!-- tags: evidence, gate --> <!-- recorded: 2026-08-12 -->
- ANDing a new necessary condition onto a predicate silently un-loads every existing leg whose case the new condition also refuses: in D1, adding a leaf-name arm left seven legs that had been proving the directory walk was physical green against a build with no directory arm at all. When you narrow a predicate, re-derive which arm makes each existing leg pass and re-drive the orphaned claims under an input only the old arm can refuse. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-fkm.3 --> <!-- tags: evidence, testing --> <!-- recorded: 2026-08-13 -->
- A bash string operation is not a path operation. $(dirname), $(basename) and command substitution generally strip trailing newlines that belong to the pathname, and `cd` without -P collapses `..` lexically before the kernel ever sees it; D1 produced findings from five separate spellings of that one mismatch before the fix became "stop handing the function a path it must parse". <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-fkm.3 --> <!-- tags: testing --> <!-- recorded: 2026-08-13 -->
- Two model families reviewing the same bytes produce DISJOINT finding sets, measured across six paired rounds on a9hh and fkm.3: sol-codex 4+5+1+3 HIGH, qa-claude 2+3+2+1 HIGH, with near-zero overlap and every convergence reached from a different fixture. The strongest single case: qa-claude censused design_foreign_paths as clean — correctly, for the newline round-trip class it was auditing — and sol-codex found a live bug in the same function by asking a different question, which entity are we classifying. Two sound audits, one bug between them. Allocate the second family by FAILURE-MODE SILENCE, not surface novelty. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-fkm.3 --> <!-- tags: evidence, process --> <!-- recorded: 2026-08-13 -->
- STOPPING RULE for review rounds: when the marginal finding moves from mechanism to prose or test-vacuity, the round budget is spent. Observed on fkm.3 — rounds 1 through 5 found mechanism defects, rounds 6 through 8 found a false sentence, a leg passing for a new reason, and a redundant-by-construction line. That transition is the signal to close, not the count of rounds or the count of findings. Make it a rule rather than a judgement call, because the orchestrator's judgement at that exact point proposed a filter that would have replaced a true disclaimer with a false closure claim. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-fkm.3 --> <!-- tags: process --> <!-- recorded: 2026-08-13 -->
- "ADDING a candidate can only add a hit" is true of ADDING and false of CHANGING one, and the difference is invisible in a diff that shows both a `+` and a `-` line. mdnc's fix replaced `cd "$d" && pwd -P` with `cd -P "$d"` at two sites, reading `-P` as a correction; they are different functions of the same input — they diverge exactly when a symlink precedes a `..` — so the swap DELETED a reduction and the deletion failed OPEN, putting a declared governing artifact back on the reviewed_by=none fast path in the very change that existed to take it off. The safety argument in the header said "can only ADD a hit" and was quoting the rule for the wrong operation. Two consequences worth carrying: state the invariant as NEVER REMOVE A REDUCTION, ONLY ADD ONE, so a substitution has to justify itself as a deletion; and when a header claims monotonicity, check which of its lines were added and which were REPLACED, because the replaced ones are where the claim is doing no work. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-mdnc --> <!-- tags: evidence, testing --> <!-- recorded: 2026-08-13 -->
- A MONOTONICITY CLAIM IS A CLAIM ABOUT THE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN TWO ARTIFACTS, so no leg that runs only one of them can test it — and 109 new assertions over the new bytes were all compatible with the fail-open they were written to prevent. The 6h-style legs drove the shipped classifier; the section-9 METAs compared the shipped bytes against a region-stripped copy of THEMSELVES; neither ever loaded the version being replaced. The fix is a differential leg with a FROZEN, sha256-pinned copy of the old artifact checked in beside the test, plus a `git show HEAD:` arm that is live exactly while the change is uncommitted, which is when a reviewer reads it. Pin the baseline's digest: without it, "refresh the baseline to match what we ship" is a one-line change that deletes the invariant and leaves every assertion green. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-mdnc --> <!-- tags: testing --> <!-- recorded: 2026-08-13 -->
- An approval's change-set hash binds the tracked-file LIST the reconciler could see, not every byte the session moved: shell-written files ride outside it via the denylist and the path-granular baseline, so the approve envelope's completeness cross-check line is the only signal that a change set is SHORT — read it and record the ruling for each named path. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-mdnc --> <!-- tags: gate --> <!-- recorded: 2026-08-13 -->
- A gate baseline captured at session start over a tree already dirty with in-flight batch work silently reclassifies that work as arrival dirt, so a reviewer must reconcile the tracker against the implementers' declared file unions before binding any hash. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-0in1 --> <!-- tags: gate --> <!-- recorded: 2026-08-14 -->
- Sibling tasks sharing one change set need the tracker restored from the attested union between approvals, because approve truncates per-task and the next sibling would otherwise bind an empty or reconstructed set. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-nq5f --> <!-- tags: gate --> <!-- recorded: 2026-08-14 -->
- A checked `mv` cannot close the pre-existing-directory arm — `mv file dir` succeeds INTO the directory with rc=0 — so a writer that must land bytes at an exact path needs a -d/-e refusal or a [ -f ] post-check, never an exit-status check alone. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-rqer --> <!-- tags: evidence --> <!-- recorded: 2026-08-15 -->
- When fixture script copies are in a change set, run the fixture-sync drift guard (test-e2e-unit) before handing off: a sync finished by patch instead of copy leaves the guard red on exactly the file whose canonical copy changed after the sync. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-rqer --> <!-- tags: testing --> <!-- recorded: 2026-08-15 -->
- A phase's scope is re-audited against the tree before that phase starts, because the plan was written before its predecessor shipped: D2's plan section named a subcommand D1 had already taken, described acceptance entries as strings the shipped validator requires to be objects, specified a refusal the shipped derivation makes impossible, and told the phase to add a binding block that already existed warn-only. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-fkm.4 --> <!-- tags: process --> <!-- recorded: 2026-08-15 -->
- The convention that every number carries the command that produced it extends to inferences: state what was observed, then verify before relaying the conclusion — an inference relayed in the voice of an observation is indistinguishable from a measurement to everyone downstream, and three of five orchestrator corrections in the v5 arc were conclusions reported as observations. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-1gw --> <!-- tags: evidence --> <!-- recorded: 2026-08-15 -->
- A structural invariant must be guarded at least as often as it can be violated: a seconds-cheap grep leg bundled into a reserved expensive tier inherits that tier's cadence, and the measured cost was a two-commit exposure that four green verification passes could not see. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-j7kk --> <!-- tags: process, testing --> <!-- recorded: 2026-08-16 -->
- A "side-effect-free" claim about a script must be probed from a foreign cwd with its env fallbacks unset — unconditional `mkdir -p` on a `${ENV:-$(pwd)}`-derived path is invisible from the repo root, where the directory already exists. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-icn4 --> <!-- tags: testing --> <!-- recorded: 2026-08-16 -->
- A size-capped request that embeds a mechanically-generated artifact must be budgeted against the artifact's measured size, not the diff's — this repo's impact-report embed alone (~1.08MB) exceeds max_request_bytes=100000 tenfold, so no paid Sol turn can fit under the current request schema regardless of how small the change set is. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-icn4 --> <!-- tags: agents, process --> <!-- recorded: 2026-08-16 -->
- A full-suite run is only as quiet as every live bd client on the machine: one concurrent session's comment auto-commit is enough for the store canary to redden an otherwise 100%-green tier, so schedule tier runs in windows with no live bd writers and read the canary's named commit before treating the red as a defect. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-icn4 --> <!-- tags: process, testing --> <!-- recorded: 2026-08-16 -->
- A migration's completeness claim needs an enumerated denominator — every call site listed and classified with a reason — because an existential search stops at its first satisfying hit: two consecutive rounds shipped falsified completeness claims from exactly that search shape while five whole spec-local seed helpers stayed unmigrated. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-fkm.4 --> <!-- tags: evidence, process --> <!-- recorded: 2026-08-17 -->
- A record-format migration's denominator must enumerate the READERS of the format, not the callers of the writer: the union is every writer call site PLUS every assertion anchoring the output grammar PLUS every restoration reproducing the state the output binds — the third population is where two enumerated denominators in a row were still short. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-fkm.4 --> <!-- tags: evidence, testing --> <!-- recorded: 2026-08-17 -->

+# _grilling_comment_on <tid> — 0 when <tid> ITSELF (never a relative) carries a
+# comment matching the FULL GRILLING v1 machine prefix; 1 otherwise, including
+# on any read failure.
+#
+# QA R1-F1 (claude-workflow-plugin-fkm.5, reviewed_hash 1a0c9f53): the first
+# version of this check was `startswith("GRILLING v1 ")` alone, MEASURED to
+# accept a hand-posted comment reading exactly
+# `GRILLING v1 totally informal, no counters, no vendor_hash` — design-record
+# recorded over it. That is a lower forgery bar than every sibling reader:
+# latest_design_artifact_hash captures a real `design_hash=` value,
+# `approve` binds `change_set_hash=`, completion binds `payload_sha=` — each
+# requires the forger to approximate a SHAPED field, not just twelve literal
+# prefix characters. The anchored `test(...)` below requires the reader to
+# see the SAME grammar the one real writer (cmd_grilling_record) always
+# produces — four `[0-9]+` counters and a 64-hex `vendor_hash=`, in order,
+# immediately before ` at ` — which is backward-compatible with every record
+# the shipped writer has ever produced (it cannot emit anything else) and
+# closes the forgery gap to the same bar the siblings already hold. This is
+# also what makes the ERROR TEXT on `rounds_not_integer` et al. true: those
+# messages say "the precondition reader parses [each counter] as [0-9]+" —
+# before this fix that was false of THIS reader (which parsed nothing), and
+# is genuinely true of it now.
+#
+# Still anchored at the START only (`^`, no trailing `$`) and never a
+# substring test — the same reasoning latest_design_artifact_hash documents
+# at length: agents quote record grammars in prose constantly (this very
+# file's --help text is a standing example), and a quotation must not
+# satisfy a precondition a real dialogue is supposed to gate. The free-text
+# `<summary>` after `at <ts>: ` is deliberately UNconstrained here, same as
+# every sibling reader leaves its own trailing prose unparsed.
+_grilling_comment_on() {
+    local tid="${1:-}" raw

+        (if type == "array" then .[0].comments else .comments end) // []
+# GRILLING-READER-GRAMMAR BEGIN (R1-F1)

+            "^GRILLING v1 rounds=[0-9]+ questions=[0-9]+ approaches=[0-9]+ unresolved=[0-9]+ vendor_hash=[0-9a-f]{64} at "

#      SAME instrument actually running (not a re-derivation of sha256 by a
#      second tool), so this file's own execution leg is the shipped script.
#
#   3. The GRILLING-PRECONDITION inside `cmd_design_record` (D3's third
#      deliverable): refuses `grilling_record_missing` with no `GRILLING v1`
#      record on the task itself OR on its parent epic; succeeds once one
#      exists on either; `--no-grilling '<reason>'` is the audited bypass,
#      recording `[grilling bypass: <reason>]`.
#
#   4. A METatest proving the precondition block is load-bearing: strip
#      `# GRILLING-PRECONDITION BEGIN/END` from a copy of qa-gate.sh and show
#      the SAME task state that the shipped script refuses instead records
#      cleanly on the mutant — mirroring the pairing plan's own P1 shape for
#      the sibling DESIGN-SATISFIED-REFUSAL METatest in design-review-record
#      .test.sh.
#
# Exit codes: 0 all assertions passed | 1 one or more failed | 2 harness error.

set -u

PASS=0
FAIL=0
FAILED_TESTS=()
KEEP_FIXTURE="${KEEP_FIXTURE:-0}"
[ "${1:-}" = "--keep" ] && KEEP_FIXTURE=1

assert_eq() {
    local name="$1" expected="$2" actual="$3"
    if [ "$expected" = "$actual" ]; then
        PASS=$((PASS + 1))
        printf '  PASS: %s\n' "$name"
    else
        FAIL=$((FAIL + 1))
        FAILED_TESTS+=("$name")
        printf '  FAIL: %s\n    expected: %s\n    actual:   %s\n' "$name" "$expected" "$actual"
    fi
}

assert_contains() {
    local name="$1" needle="$2" haystack="$3"
    if printf '%s' "$haystack" | grep -qF -- "$needle"; then
        PASS=$((PASS + 1))
        printf '  PASS: %s\n' "$name"
    else
        FAIL=$((FAIL + 1))
        FAILED_TESTS+=("$name")
        printf '  FAIL: %s\n    needle:   %s\n    haystack: %s\n' "$name" "$needle" "$haystack"
    fi
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Fixture. Same shape as design-review-record.test.sh: the real scripts, a
# real bd, a throwaway project root and HOME. `cd "$FIXTURE"` (no subshell)
# is the FAIL-CLOSED store-isolation mechanism this tier requires — BEADS_DIR
# alone is fail-open (falls back to the production store when the target is
# not already an initialised one), so every bd call below runs with this
# process's cwd inside the fixture, never via an env-var redirect alone.
# ALSO copies .claude/vendor/ (unlike its siblings before D3): this file's
# subject hashes the vendored brainstorming SKILL.md, so without it every
# grilling-record call would refuse vendor_hash_unavailable.

PLUGIN_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/../../.." && pwd)"
FIXTURE=$(mktemp -d -t grilling-record.XXXXXX)
TEST_HOME=$(mktemp -d -t grilling-record-home.XXXXXX)

# shellcheck disable=SC2329  # invoked via trap.
cleanup() {
    if [ "$KEEP_FIXTURE" = "1" ]; then
        printf '\nFixture kept at: %s\nTest HOME: %s\n' "$FIXTURE" "$TEST_HOME"
    else
        chmod -R u+rwX "$FIXTURE" 2>/dev/null || true
        rm -rf "$FIXTURE" "$TEST_HOME"
    fi
}
trap cleanup EXIT

mkdir -p "$FIXTURE/.claude/scripts" "$FIXTURE/.claude/.qa-tracking" \
    "$FIXTURE/.beads" "$FIXTURE/bin" "$FIXTURE/docs/specs" \
    "$FIXTURE/.claude/vendor/superpowers/brainstorming" \
    "$TEST_HOME/.claude/projects"

cp "$PLUGIN_DIR/.claude/scripts/"*.sh "$FIXTURE/.claude/scripts/"
chmod +x "$FIXTURE/.claude/scripts/"*.sh
cp "$PLUGIN_DIR/.claude/vendor/superpowers/brainstorming/SKILL.md" \
    "$FIXTURE/.claude/vendor/superpowers/brainstorming/SKILL.md"

if ! command -v bd >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "bd CLI not on PATH — grilling-record tests require Beads."
    exit 2
fi
if ! command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "jq not on PATH — grilling-record tests require jq."
    exit 2
fi

REAL_BD=$(command -v bd)
cat > "$FIXTURE/bin/bd" <<EOF
#!/bin/bash
exec ${REAL_BD} "\$@"
EOF
chmod +x "$FIXTURE/bin/bd"
export PATH="$FIXTURE/bin:$PATH"

cd "$FIXTURE" && bd init >/dev/null 2>&1
export CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR="$FIXTURE"
export HOME="$TEST_HOME"

QG="$FIXTURE/.claude/scripts/qa-gate.sh"
WM="$FIXTURE/.claude/scripts/workflow-manifest.sh"
VENDORED_SKILL="$FIXTURE/.claude/vendor/superpowers/brainstorming/SKILL.md"

json_field() { printf '%s' "$2" | jq -r "$1" 2>/dev/null || printf ''; }

bd_show_with_comments() {
    bd show "$1" --json --include-comments 2>/dev/null \
        || bd show "$1" --json 2>/dev/null \
        || true
}

comments_of() {
    bd_show_with_comments "$1" \
        | jq -r '(if type=="array" then .[0].comments else .comments end) // [] | .[].text' \
        2>/dev/null || echo ""
}

# count_grilling <tid> — counts comments matching the FULL tightened
# grammar `_grilling_comment_on` requires (QA R1-F1), not a bare
# `^GRILLING v1 ` prefix — the two diverged the first time this file used
# count_grilling to check a FORGED, prefix-only comment (5.1b), where a
# bare-prefix count silently reported 1 for text the shipped precondition
# reader does not treat as a record at all. Every REAL grilling-record call
# always produces the full grammar, so this tightening changes nothing for
# this file's other four call sites (2.1b, D3b, 6.2c, 6.5c) — verified by
# re-running the full suite after the change.
count_grilling() {
    comments_of "$1" | grep -cE '^GRILLING v1 rounds=[0-9]+ questions=[0-9]+ approaches=[0-9]+ unresolved=[0-9]+ vendor_hash=[0-9a-f]{64} at ' 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' \n'
}

latest_grilling_line() {
    comments_of "$1" | grep -E '^GRILLING v1 ' | tail -1
}

# write_artifact <path> <task-id> — a minimal, schema-valid design artifact,
# byte-identical in shape to the sibling design-record specs so this file
# never guesses a second schema.
write_artifact() {
    local path="$1" tid="$2"
    cat > "$path" <<ARTIFACT
# Design — $tid

## Problem
Test subject.

## Approaches considered
1. Approach A — rejected: does not match the existing pattern.
2. Approach B — chosen: matches it.

## Chosen approach
Approach B.

## Units
See the machine block.

## Global constraints
None.

## Out of scope
Everything else.

## Verification plan
make test

## Revision log
- v1 initial.

<!-- DESIGN-UNITS BEGIN -->
\`\`\`json
{
  "contract_version": "1",
  "task_id": "$tid",
  "designer_identity": "designer",
  "units": [
    {
      "unit_id": "U1",
      "role": "devops",
      "goal": "test unit",
      "acceptance": [ { "id": "AC1", "text": "test fixture: nothing asserted" } ],
      "files": [ ".claude/scripts/qa-gate.sh" ],
      "verification": "make test",
      "depends_on": []
    }
  ]
}
\`\`\`
<!-- DESIGN-UNITS END -->
ARTIFACT
}

LIVE_VENDOR_HASH=$(bash "$WM" hash-file "$VENDORED_SKILL" 2>/dev/null)

# ===========================================================================
printf '\n=== Section 1: grilling-record — argument validation ladder ===\n'
# ===========================================================================

TID1=$(bd create "D3 grilling shape subject" -t task -p 1 --json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.id')
if [ -z "$TID1" ] || [ "$TID1" = "null" ]; then
    echo "harness error: could not create a Beads task"
    exit 2
fi

# 2>/dev/null (not 2>&1): a missing task id ALSO triggers usage()'s
# multi-line help text on stderr, ahead of the one-line JSON error on
# stdout — merging the two makes the combined blob unparseable as JSON.
OUT=$(bash "$QG" grilling-record 2>/dev/null); RC=$?
assert_eq "1.1 no task id: exit 1" "1" "$RC"
assert_eq "1.1b ...error_key=missing_task_id" "missing_task_id" "$(json_field '.error_key' "$OUT")"

OUT=$(bash "$QG" grilling-record "$TID1" --questions 3 --approaches 2 --unresolved 0 "s" 2>&1)
assert_eq "1.2 missing --rounds: missing_rounds" "missing_rounds" "$(json_field '.error_key' "$OUT")"

OUT=$(bash "$QG" grilling-record "$TID1" --rounds 2 --approaches 2 --unresolved 0 "s" 2>&1)
assert_eq "1.3 missing --questions: missing_questions" "missing_questions" "$(json_field '.error_key' "$OUT")"

OUT=$(bash "$QG" grilling-record "$TID1" --rounds 2 --questions 3 --unresolved 0 "s" 2>&1)
assert_eq "1.4 missing --approaches: missing_approaches" "missing_approaches" "$(json_field '.error_key' "$OUT")"

OUT=$(bash "$QG" grilling-record "$TID1" --rounds 2 --questions 3 --approaches 2 "s" 2>&1)
assert_eq "1.5 missing --unresolved: missing_unresolved" "missing_unresolved" "$(json_field '.error_key' "$OUT")"

# Each counter individually must be a non-negative integer — table-driven so
# every field's OWN reader-facing error_key is asserted, not just the first.
OUT=$(bash "$QG" grilling-record "$TID1" --rounds -1 --questions 3 --approaches 2 --unresolved 0 "s" 2>&1)
assert_eq "1.6 --rounds=-1: rounds_not_integer" "rounds_not_integer" "$(json_field '.error_key' "$OUT")"

OUT=$(bash "$QG" grilling-record "$TID1" --rounds 2 --questions abc --approaches 2 --unresolved 0 "s" 2>&1)
assert_eq "1.7 --questions=abc: questions_not_integer" "questions_not_integer" "$(json_field '.error_key' "$OUT")"

OUT=$(bash "$QG" grilling-record "$TID1" --rounds 2 --questions 3 --approaches 1.5 --unresolved 0 "s" 2>&1)
assert_eq "1.8 --approaches=1.5: approaches_not_integer" "approaches_not_integer" "$(json_field '.error_key' "$OUT")"

OUT=$(bash "$QG" grilling-record "$TID1" --rounds 2 --questions 3 --approaches 2 --unresolved -3 "s" 2>&1)
assert_eq "1.9 --unresolved=-3: unresolved_not_integer" "unresolved_not_integer" "$(json_field '.error_key' "$OUT")"

# THE VENDORED METHOD'S OWN BAR — 0 and 1 approaches are both below it;
# both must refuse the SAME way, and 2 must not.
OUT=$(bash "$QG" grilling-record "$TID1" --rounds 2 --questions 3 --approaches 0 --unresolved 0 "s" 2>&1)
assert_eq "1.10 --approaches=0: insufficient_approaches" "insufficient_approaches" "$(json_field '.error_key' "$OUT")"
assert_contains "1.10b ...names the vendored method's own bar" \
    "Propose 2-3 different approaches" "$OUT"

OUT=$(bash "$QG" grilling-record "$TID1" --rounds 2 --questions 3 --approaches 1 --unresolved 0 "s" 2>&1)
assert_eq "1.11 --approaches=1: ALSO insufficient_approaches" "insufficient_approaches" "$(json_field '.error_key' "$OUT")"

OUT=$(bash "$QG" grilling-record "$TID1" --rounds 2 --questions 3 --approaches 2 --unresolved 0 "s" 2>&1)
assert_eq "1.12 --approaches=2 (the exact bar): NOT insufficient_approaches" "recorded" "$(json_field '.status' "$OUT")"

# Unknown flag: same "free-text summary accumulator" shape design-record's
# own parser has — an unrecognised flag becomes part of the summary rather
# than a hard error, so this asserts the ACTUAL shipped behaviour rather
# than a stricter one nobody built.
TID1B=$(bd create "D3 grilling unknown-flag subject" -t task -p 1 --json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.id')
OUT=$(bash "$QG" grilling-record "$TID1B" --rounds 2 --questions 3 --approaches 2 --unresolved 0 --bogus 2>&1)
assert_eq "1.13 an unrecognised flag is folded into the free-text summary, not refused" \
    "recorded" "$(json_field '.status' "$OUT")"
assert_contains "1.13b ...and the literal text appears in the record" \
    "--bogus" "$(latest_grilling_line "$TID1B")"

# ===========================================================================
printf '\n=== Section 2: the GRILLING v1 record grammar and vendor_hash ===\n'
# ===========================================================================

TID2=$(bd create "D3 grilling record grammar subject" -t task -p 1 --json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.id')
OUT=$(bash "$QG" grilling-record "$TID2" --rounds 4 --questions 9 --approaches 3 --unresolved 2 \
    "explored a shared-helper design and a per-call-site one" 2>&1)
assert_eq "2.1 a fully-valid call records" "recorded" "$(json_field '.status' "$OUT")"

REC=$(latest_grilling_line "$TID2")
assert_eq "2.1b exactly one GRILLING v1 record exists" "1" "$(count_grilling "$TID2")"
assert_contains "2.2 the record carries rounds=4" "rounds=4 " "$REC"
assert_contains "2.3 ...questions=9" "questions=9 " "$REC"
assert_contains "2.4 ...approaches=3" "approaches=3 " "$REC"
assert_contains "2.5 ...unresolved=2" "unresolved=2 " "$REC"
assert_contains "2.6 ...the free-text summary" \
    "explored a shared-helper design and a per-call-site one" "$REC"

# THE EXECUTION LEG: vendor_hash is asserted against the SHIPPED instrument
# actually RUNNING (workflow-manifest.sh hash-file), never a re-derivation
# of sha256 by a second tool.
[ -n "$LIVE_VENDOR_HASH" ] && [ "${#LIVE_VENDOR_HASH}" -eq 64 ] || {
    echo "harness error: could not hash the fixture's vendored SKILL.md"
    exit 2
}
assert_contains "2.7 the record's vendor_hash equals workflow-manifest.sh hash-file's live recompute" \
    "vendor_hash=$LIVE_VENDOR_HASH " "$REC"

# A default (no summary text) still records, with the documented fallback.
TID2B=$(bd create "D3 grilling no-summary subject" -t task -p 1 --json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.id')
OUT=$(bash "$QG" grilling-record "$TID2B" --rounds 1 --questions 1 --approaches 2 --unresolved 0 2>&1)
assert_eq "2.8 no trailing summary text still records" "recorded" "$(json_field '.status' "$OUT")"
assert_contains "2.8b ...with the documented fallback text" \
    "grilling recorded" "$(latest_grilling_line "$TID2B")"

# rounds=0/questions=0/unresolved=0 are all LEGAL non-negative integers —
# only approaches has a floor above zero.
TID2C=$(bd create "D3 grilling zero-counters subject" -t task -p 1 --json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.id')
OUT=$(bash "$QG" grilling-record "$TID2C" --rounds 0 --questions 0 --approaches 2 --unresolved 0 "s" 2>&1)
assert_eq "2.9 rounds=0/questions=0/unresolved=0 are legal (only approaches has a floor)" \
    "recorded" "$(json_field '.status' "$OUT")"

# ===========================================================================
printf '\n=== Section 3: the GRILLING-PRECONDITION inside design-record ===\n'
# ===========================================================================

# D1: a fresh task with NO grilling record at all -> refused.
TID3=$(bd create "D3 precondition subject" -t task -p 1 --json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.id')
ART3="$FIXTURE/docs/specs/$TID3.md"
write_artifact "$ART3" "$TID3"
printf '%s\n' "$ART3" > "$FIXTURE/.claude/.qa-tracking/changed-files.txt"
bash "$QG" enter "$TID3" >/dev/null 2>&1

OUT=$(bash "$QG" design-record "$TID3" 2>&1); RC=$?
assert_eq "D1 no grilling record at all: design-record exit 1" "1" "$RC"
assert_eq "D1b ...error_key=grilling_record_missing" "grilling_record_missing" "$(json_field '.error_key' "$OUT")"
assert_contains "D1c ...names the remediation" "qa-gate.sh grilling-record $TID3" "$OUT"
assert_contains "D1d ...and the bypass" "--no-grilling" "$OUT"
DR_COUNT=$(comments_of "$TID3" | grep -cE '^DESIGN-ARTIFACT v1 ' 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' \n')
assert_eq "D1e the refusal wrote NOTHING — no DESIGN-ARTIFACT record exists" "0" "$DR_COUNT"

# D2: grill the SAME task directly -> design-record now succeeds.
bash "$QG" grilling-record "$TID3" --rounds 2 --questions 4 --approaches 2 --unresolved 1 \
    "grilled directly on the task" >/dev/null 2>&1
OUT=$(bash "$QG" design-record "$TID3" 2>&1)
assert_eq "D2 grilling recorded ON THE TASK: design-record succeeds" "recorded" "$(json_field '.status' "$OUT")"

# D3: parent-epic path. A CHILD task with NO grilling of its own, whose
# PARENT EPIC has been grilled, still succeeds. --no-inherit-labels is not
# load-bearing for this assertion (nothing here checks labels) but is kept
# for the same reason CLAUDE.md documents it everywhere else: a bare
# --parent copies the epic's labels onto the child, which is never what a
# fresh test task wants.
EPIC=$(bd create "D3 grilling epic" -t epic -p 1 --json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.id')
CHILD=$(bd create "D3 grilling child (ungrilled itself)" -t task -p 1 --parent "$EPIC" --no-inherit-labels --json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.id')
if [ -z "$EPIC" ] || [ "$EPIC" = "null" ] || [ -z "$CHILD" ] || [ "$CHILD" = "null" ]; then
    echo "harness error: could not create the epic/child pair"
    exit 2
fi
ART_CHILD="$FIXTURE/docs/specs/$CHILD.md"
write_artifact "$ART_CHILD" "$CHILD"
printf '%s\n' "$ART_CHILD" > "$FIXTURE/.claude/.qa-tracking/changed-files.txt"
bash "$QG" enter "$CHILD" >/dev/null 2>&1

OUT=$(bash "$QG" design-record "$CHILD" 2>&1)
assert_eq "D3 pre-check: child refuses too — grilling is on neither task nor epic yet" \
    "grilling_record_missing" "$(json_field '.error_key' "$OUT")"

bash "$QG" grilling-record "$EPIC" --rounds 3 --questions 6 --approaches 2 --unresolved 0 \
    "grilled at the epic level" >/dev/null 2>&1
CHILD_OWN_COUNT=$(count_grilling "$CHILD")
assert_eq "D3b the CHILD ITSELF still carries zero GRILLING records (the epic's is not copied down)" \
    "0" "$CHILD_OWN_COUNT"

OUT=$(bash "$QG" design-record "$CHILD" 2>&1)
assert_eq "D3c grilling recorded on the PARENT EPIC ONLY: the child's design-record still succeeds" \
    "recorded" "$(json_field '.status' "$OUT")"

# D4: --no-grilling bypass, on a fresh ungrilled task.
TID4=$(bd create "D3 no-grilling bypass subject" -t task -p 1 --json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.id')
ART4="$FIXTURE/docs/specs/$TID4.md"
write_artifact "$ART4" "$TID4"
printf '%s\n' "$ART4" > "$FIXTURE/.claude/.qa-tracking/changed-files.txt"
bash "$QG" enter "$TID4" >/dev/null 2>&1

OUT=$(bash "$QG" design-record "$TID4" --no-grilling 2>&1)
assert_eq "D4 --no-grilling with NO reason: missing_grilling_bypass_reason" \
    "missing_grilling_bypass_reason" "$(json_field '.error_key' "$OUT")"

OUT=$(bash "$QG" design-record "$TID4" --no-grilling "F1 doc-only class: no dialogue was needed" 2>&1)
assert_eq "D4b --no-grilling WITH a reason: succeeds despite no GRILLING v1 record anywhere" \
    "recorded" "$(json_field '.status' "$OUT")"
D4_RECORD=$(comments_of "$TID4" | grep -E '^DESIGN-ARTIFACT v1 ' | tail -1)
assert_contains "D4c the record carries the audited [grilling bypass: <reason>] marker" \
    "[grilling bypass: F1 doc-only class: no dialogue was needed]" "$D4_RECORD"

# ===========================================================================
printf '\n=== Section 4: META — the GRILLING-PRECONDITION block is load-bearing ===\n'
# ===========================================================================

# Strip the sentinel-delimited block from a COPY of qa-gate.sh and replay
# D1's exact scenario (a design artifact, `enter`, then design-record, with
# NO grilling record anywhere). Under the stripped copy the record SUCCEEDS
# — i.e. D1's "refused" assertion would fail — so D1 is testing the block
# itself, not an incidental side effect. Mirrors design-review-record.test
# .sh's own P1-shaped METatest for DESIGN-SATISFIED-REFUSAL.
QG_NOGUARD="$FIXTURE/.claude/scripts/qa-gate-noguard.sh"
STRIP_RC=0
awk '
    /# GRILLING-PRECONDITION BEGIN/ { skipping=1; found=1; next }
    /# GRILLING-PRECONDITION END/   { skipping=0; next }
    skipping { next }
    { print }
    END { if (!found) exit 7 }
' "$QG" > "$QG_NOGUARD" || STRIP_RC=$?
chmod +x "$QG_NOGUARD"
assert_eq "META-1a: GRILLING-PRECONDITION sentinels are present in the shipped qa-gate.sh (the strip found them)" \
    "0" "$STRIP_RC"

PARSE_RC=0
bash -n "$QG_NOGUARD" 2>/dev/null || PARSE_RC=$?
assert_eq "META-1b: the stripped copy still parses (the block is cleanly strippable)" "0" "$PARSE_RC"

BYTE_DIFF=$(cmp -s "$QG" "$QG_NOGUARD" && echo same || echo differ)
assert_eq "META-1c: the mutant's bytes actually differ from the shipped script" "differ" "$BYTE_DIFF"

TID_META=$(bd create "D3 GRILLING-PRECONDITION META subject" -t task -p 1 --json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.id')
ART_META="$FIXTURE/docs/specs/$TID_META.md"
write_artifact "$ART_META" "$TID_META"
printf '%s\n' "$ART_META" > "$FIXTURE/.claude/.qa-tracking/changed-files.txt"
bash "$QG" enter "$TID_META" >/dev/null 2>&1

MUT_OUT=$(bash "$QG_NOGUARD" design-record "$TID_META" 2>&1)
assert_eq "META-1d MISBEHAVIOUR: WITHOUT the block, design-record records a task NOBODY grilled" \
    "recorded" "$(json_field '.status' "$MUT_OUT")"
MUT_DR_COUNT=$(comments_of "$TID_META" | grep -cE '^DESIGN-ARTIFACT v1 ' 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' \n')
assert_eq "META-1e ...and the DESIGN-ARTIFACT record it wrote is real, not a dry run" "1" "$MUT_DR_COUNT"

# CONTROL: the SAME task state, the SHIPPED (guarded) script, refuses. Uses
# a fresh design-record call on the SAME task — design-record's own
# duplicate-artifact machinery is orthogonal to this assertion, so re-derive
# a clean second subject instead of fighting it.
TID_CTRL=$(bd create "D3 GRILLING-PRECONDITION control subject" -t task -p 1 --json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.id')
ART_CTRL="$FIXTURE/docs/specs/$TID_CTRL.md"
write_artifact "$ART_CTRL" "$TID_CTRL"
printf '%s\n' "$ART_CTRL" > "$FIXTURE/.claude/.qa-tracking/changed-files.txt"
bash "$QG" enter "$TID_CTRL" >/dev/null 2>&1

CTRL_OUT=$(bash "$QG" design-record "$TID_CTRL" 2>&1)
assert_eq "META-1f CONTROL: the SHIPPED script refuses the SAME ungrilled state the mutant just recorded" \
    "grilling_record_missing" "$(json_field '.error_key' "$CTRL_OUT")"
rm -f "$QG_NOGUARD"

# ===========================================================================
printf '\n=== Section 5: QA R1-F1 — the reader matches the FULL writer grammar, not a bare prefix ===\n'
# ===========================================================================
#
# QA finding (claude-workflow-plugin-fkm.5, reviewed_hash 1a0c9f53): the
# first shipped version of _grilling_comment_on was `startswith("GRILLING
# v1 ")` alone, MEASURED (in an isolated fixture) to accept a hand-posted
# comment carrying none of the real fields. This section pins the fix and
# proves the tightened reader is what closes it, not an incidental side
# effect.

TID5=$(bd create "R1-F1 forged-comment subject" -t task -p 1 --json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.id')
ART5="$FIXTURE/docs/specs/$TID5.md"
write_artifact "$ART5" "$TID5"
printf '%s\n' "$ART5" > "$FIXTURE/.claude/.qa-tracking/changed-files.txt"
bash "$QG" enter "$TID5" >/dev/null 2>&1

FORGED_TEXT="GRILLING v1 totally informal, no counters, no vendor_hash"
bd comments add "$TID5" "$FORGED_TEXT" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
    || bd comment add "$TID5" "$FORGED_TEXT" >/dev/null 2>&1
FORGED_LANDED=$(comments_of "$TID5" | grep -cF "$FORGED_TEXT" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' \n')
assert_eq "5.1 precondition: the forged comment actually landed on the task" "1" "$FORGED_LANDED"
assert_eq "5.1b precondition: it does NOT match the tightened grammar (no real counters/vendor_hash)" \
    "0" "$(count_grilling "$TID5")"

OUT=$(bash "$QG" design-record "$TID5" 2>&1)
assert_eq "5.2 the SHIPPED (tightened) script REFUSES design-record over the forged comment" \
    "grilling_record_missing" "$(json_field '.error_key' "$OUT")"

# --- META: reverting the reader to the pre-fix bare-prefix shape must
# accept the SAME forged comment, proving the tightened grammar (not
# something else) is what closes R1-F1.
QG_WEAKREADER="$FIXTURE/.claude/scripts/qa-gate-weakreader.sh"
WEAK_RC=0
awk '

<!-- BD-MCP-META: {"kind":"qa-ruling","source":"qa-agent","round":2} -->
QA RULINGS (requested by the orchestrator; both are decisions on the record, not defects). Measured at HEAD d8f75ab + the post-fix-round tree, 2026-08-18.

**Ruling 1 — existence-only grilling semantics: CORRECT AS SHIPPED.** The sharpened question was: when an amendment moves `design_hash`, a grilling that preceded the earlier design still counts — does that let a record attest to a design nobody grilled? No, because the grilling record never attests to a DESIGN at all: it attests to a DIALOGUE that preceded designing. A grilling cannot examine an artifact — it happens before one exists, so there is no `design_hash` for it to bind, which is why the record binds the only byte-addressable thing in its picture (`vendor_hash`, the method text in force). What re-validates an AMENDED artifact is D2's own amendment discipline: every amendment requires a fresh DESIGN-REVIEW verdict, and the design reviewer's packet includes the grilling record verbatim (design-reviewer.md, packet item 2) — so "does the dialogue still ground this design" is re-judged on every amendment round, at the only layer capable of judging it (it is not hash-decidable). Making the PRECONDITION amendment-aware instead would demand a fresh human dialogue per revision round: it either deadlocks the D2 reviewer loop on human availability or degrades into rubber-stamp re-grills that devalue every record. Cost of the alternative: re-grill machinery + a waive path + a human round-trip per amendment, to mechanically approximate a judgment the reviewer already makes with better information. Residual accepted and disclosed (grilling_record_exists's own header): a task grilled long ago can bind a design recorded much later; timestamps + vendor_hash leave that auditable by a human.

**Ruling 2 — forgery, post-tightening: AT PARITY on every constructible axis; intrinsically below siblings on exactly one, and that one is unfixable by a `who=` field.** Measured on the final tree (isolated fixture): a prefix-only forged comment (`GRILLING v1 totally informal, no counters, no vendor_hash`) is now REFUSED — pre-fix it recorded, which is R1-F1, so the implementer's original "shared property" framing was too generous about the reader until this round; a FULL-grammar forgery (fabricated counters, any 64-hex `vendor_hash`) still records. That is the same bar every sibling holds: COMPLETION's `payload_sha` and DESIGN-ARTIFACT's `design_hash` are hashes a forger computes over content they control. On `who=`: NO record in this system carries an authenticated identity — bd has no per-agent identity, every comment is authored by the same OS user, and COMPLETION's `role=`/`model=` are caller-supplied strings. A `who=` on GRILLING would be a string the forger also types, compared against nothing; the implementer's "nothing to compare against" is verified correct and adding the field would be theater. On hash binding: `vendor_hash` binds the METHOD text, not the dialogue, because the dialogue has no bytes — it happened in conversation, not in a file. That is the one axis where GRILLING is genuinely the weakest record in the set, and it is intrinsic to recording an unrecorded human conversation, not a construction defect. The alternative — demand a transcript artifact and hash it — changes the feature's cost and shape (volume, privacy, format) and is a later-phase design question if the residual ever bites. Fine as shipped.

title: manifests/v4.1.0.sha256 is stale at HEAD (LESSONS.md row) — moving the v4.1.0 tag would ship a manifest that misclassifies its own file
description:
Found during QA review of docs/v4.1-closure.md (claude-workflow-plugin-q7n).

## Evidence

`manifests/v4.1.0.sha256` was frozen at the release commit `57fb888`. `b04870b`
(the C7 CI fix, task `016`) then appended the 71st lesson to `LESSONS.md`, which
is a manifest-covered row (class `operator`, emitted at
`.claude/scripts/workflow-manifest.sh:341`).

Reproduced both ways:

```
# At the release commit — clean:
git worktree add --detach $T 57fb888
(cd $T && bash .claude/scripts/workflow-manifest.sh generate .) > /tmp/m_rel
cmp /tmp/m_rel $T/manifests/v4.1.0.sha256      # -> silent, exit 0

# At HEAD (418678a) — one row differs:
bash .claude/scripts/workflow-manifest.sh generate . > /tmp/m1
cmp /tmp/m1 manifests/v4.1.0.sha256
# 130c130
# < LESSONS.md  operator  275a844199f02828cfa6de4bf52570abf3ac4a4a0afe5f71b8ee59036848e397
# > LESSONS.md  operator  296ba96ff16f4160d1d73089396b2fc1b178389b1d53576a66a8d013167fff89

git show 57fb888:LESSONS.md | shasum -a 256   # 296ba96f...  (= the frozen row)
git show HEAD:LESSONS.md    | shasum -a 256   # 275a8441...  (= the regenerated row)
```

## Why it matters (and why it is NOT purely cosmetic)

Two consequences, of different weight:

1. `HANDOFF.md:385-391` asserts as a release verify-condition that
   `workflow-manifest.sh generate . | cmp manifests/v4.1.0.sha256` is silent
   with exit 0. That assert FAILS at HEAD. Anyone running HANDOFF's checklist
   today gets a red on a load-bearing determinism assert and has no way to know
   it is a stale-table artifact rather than a broken generator.

2. **The sharp one.** `docs/v4.1-closure.md` §1 recommends MOVING the `v4.1.0`
   tag off `57fb888` (whose tree fails CI) to the current head. If the tag
   moves, the release named `v4.1.0` ships a `LESSONS.md` (275a8441) whose hash
   is NOT the one its own `manifests/v4.1.0.sha256` records (296ba96f).

   Classification order is `.claude/scripts/workflow-manifest.sh:490-503`:
   `skip-current` (target == source) -> `replace-stock` (target == old table)
   -> else `preserve-custom` for class `operator`, which writes a `.new`
   sidecar. On a later upgrade FROM that v4.1.0, a stock target's LESSONS.md
   matches neither the new source nor the frozen `oldhash`, so it lands on
   `preserve-custom` and the operator gets a spurious `LESSONS.md.new` on a
   file they never touched.

   That is the same defect class `016`/`b04870b` just fixed ("stock 4.1 targets
   were being classified against v3.5's hashes and getting spurious `.new`
   sidecars"), reintroduced one release later by the very commit that fixed it.

## Candidate fixes (evidence-before-fix pass not yet run; do not patch on this alone)

a) Regenerate `manifests/v4.1.0.sha256` at whatever commit the tag ends up on,
   as a REQUIRED step of the tag-move decision. Narrowest, and it is the step
   the closure doc's §1 currently omits.
b) Leave the tag at `57fb888`, where the table is already correct, and treat the
   HEAD-relative cmp failure as expected drift — but then HANDOFF's assert needs
   to say "run this at the tag", not "run this".
c) Add an L1/L2 guard that fails when a manifest-covered path is modified after
   its frozen table was generated, so this cannot recur silently. This is the
   generalisable one; it is also the one that would have caught it here.

Prefer (a) + (c): (a) unblocks the tag decision, (c) stops the next release
making the same move.

## Note on scope

The closure document's own claim ("regenerate-and-`cmp` byte-identical under
three locales") was TRUE when measured at `57fb888` — the three-locale
reproduction is recorded in the ledger. It is the HEAD-relative restatement
that is false. The doc-side fix is tracked on `claude-workflow-plugin-q7n`;
THIS task is the repo-side defect.

title: installer-v3-upgrade 8e leg B: outcome assertions don't adapt to the no-frozen-table branch (comment claims they do)
description:
Found during QA of claude-workflow-plugin-016 (QA finding R1-F1, medium). NOT a blocker for v4.1.0 — the suite is green today and the release process is atomic.

## The claim

`.claude/tests/component/specs/installer-v3-upgrade.sh` leg B carries this comment:

> A future release that bumps plugin.json before freezing its own table is the
> same event again, and it must not fail here

That protection is only half-implemented.

## What actually happens

`UPG44_EXPECT_TABLE` (line ~1276) adapts the expected table NAME to whichever
branch the source lands in. But leg B's five OUTCOME assertions hardcode the
has-table (correct-classification) outcome:

  - "replaced (stock)       2"
  - "replaced (customized)  0"
  - "preserved (yours)      1"
  - no spurious `.claude/model-roles.new`
  - the not-left-stale `cmp`

In the no-table branch the installer legitimately produces leg C's NOISY
outcome (both source-edited files are absent from `v3.5.0.sha256`, so
`oldhash = "-"` -> replace-custom / preserve-custom). Leg B therefore
contradicts leg C and goes red.

## Reproduction (QA ran this)

In a throwaway clone at HEAD with the 016 spec applied:

    # bump the declared version, do NOT freeze the matching table
    sed -i '' 's/"version": "4.1.0"/"version": "4.2.0"/' .claude-plugin/plugin.json
    bash .claude/tests/component/run.sh --filter installer-v3-upgrade

Result: **249 pass / 5 fail**, all five in leg B, exactly the list above.
Leg B's two NAMING assertions PASSED (the derivation correctly resolved
`v3.5.0.sha256`), which is what isolates the defect to the outcome half.

## Severity bound

`git log --diff-filter=A -- manifests/v4.1.0.sha256` and the plugin.json bump
are the SAME commit (57fb888), so bump+freeze is atomic and this is a
transient working-tree state during release prep, not a committed-state risk.
That is why it is medium, not high, and why 016 was approved.

## Suggested fix

Guard leg B's outcome block with the same `if` that computes
`UPG44_EXPECT_TABLE`. Leg C already asserts the else-branch outcome, so the
guard needs no new assertions — leg B just has to assert the outcome matching
the branch it actually landed in. Then either the comment's claim becomes
true, or the comment should be narrowed to say only the NAME adapts.

Also worth folding in QA finding R1-F2 (low): leg B predicts the table from
`UPG44_MF_VERSION` (the target's install-manifest header) while install.sh
selects using `V3_DETECTED_VERSION` (the target's plugin.json) — two different
inputs assumed to agree.
acceptance_criteria: Bumping .claude-plugin/plugin.json to a version with no frozen table in manifests/ leaves the installer-v3-upgrade spec GREEN (leg C already covers the noisy outcome), OR leg B's comment is narrowed to claim only what it delivers. Whichever is chosen, the mutation must be watched to fail before the fix lands.

title: qa-gate.sh approve does not clear qa-blocked — a block -> fix -> approve cycle ends with both labels set
description:
Found during QA of claude-workflow-plugin-uvk (v4.1.0 release closeout), 2026-07-30.

## Symptom

`qa-gate.sh approve` is documented and implemented as
"Atomic: -qa-gate-entered, -qa-pending, +qa-approved, comment."
It does NOT remove `qa-blocked`. So the normal QA round-trip —

    qa-gate.sh block <id> '<findings>'     # +qa-blocked
    (specialist fixes)
    qa-gate.sh approve <id> '<summary>'    # +qa-approved

— terminates with the task carrying BOTH `qa-approved` and `qa-blocked`.
Reproduced live on `uvk`: after approving at `c01fccd8` the labels read
`['devops', 'qa-approved', 'qa-blocked']`.

## Blast radius — small but real

- `verify-before-stop.sh` does NOT read `qa-blocked` for the active task's
  release decision (only at :2014, for a SIBLING epic note), so release is
  NOT affected. This is a record defect, not a gate defect.
- `qa-gate.sh status` has correct precedence (approved > blocked), so it
  reports `approved`. Verified.
- The damage is to triage and to the audit trail: `bd list --label qa-blocked`
  surfaces approved work as blocked, and a reader of the task sees two
  contradictory gate labels with no indication which is current.

## Why it matters here specifically

This repo's whole thesis is that the gate's labels are the single source of
truth. A label that says `qa-blocked` on an approved release task is the same
class of wrong-record problem as `qzv` (an unearned `qa-approved`), just in the
opposite direction and with no release consequence.

## Suggested fix

Add `qa-blocked` to the labels `cmd_approve` removes, alongside
`qa-gate-entered` and `qa-pending`, and include it in the existing rollback set
so the operation stays atomic. Update the header comment at `qa-gate.sh:16` and
the `block` subcommand note at :30 (which currently says only that `block`
"Keeps qa-gate-entered").

Consider the same for `cmd_choose`'s approve path, which delegates to
`cmd_approve` and would inherit the fix.

## Test

An L2 spec asserting label state after a full block -> approve round-trip:
after `approve`, `qa-blocked` must be ABSENT and `qa-approved` PRESENT. A META
should confirm the assertion is non-vacuous by checking `qa-blocked` IS present
between the block and the approve.

## Interim

The stale label was removed by hand on `uvk` with a comment recording why; that
is record hygiene, not a gate bypass, since `qa-blocked` is not part of the
release predicate.

comments.text:
FRESH REPRODUCTION, 2026-07-30, on `claude-workflow-plugin-q7n` (the v4.1.0 closure-document review).

Clean instance of the full cycle, so it is worth pinning as the canonical repro:

1. `qa-gate.sh block q7n '<11 findings>'` -> labels `devops, qa-blocked, qa-gate-entered, rubric-pending`
2. Author fixed all eleven; gate re-entered at the same change-set hash.
3. `qa-gate.sh approve q7n '<summary>'` -> **labels `devops, qa-approved, qa-blocked`**

`approve`'s own observations confirm what it did and did not touch:

```
qa-approved set; removed qa-gate-entered=1 qa-pending=0; ...
rubric-pending cleared as cycle ends
```

`qa-gate-entered`, `qa-pending` and `rubric-pending` are all cleared. `qa-blocked` is not, so the task ends carrying two contradictory verdicts.

WHAT IS AND IS NOT BROKEN. The gate itself is correct: `qa-gate.sh status` returns `approved`, because the documented precedence is `approved > blocked > entered > not-entered`. So this is not a release-correctness bug and it did not affect the outcome here. The damage is to the READABLE record — `bd show` presents a task that is simultaneously approved and blocked, and anyone triaging by label (`bd list --label qa-blocked`) picks up tasks that were approved hours ago.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN IT LOOKS. This is the same family as `hbr` and `qzv`: a signal that reports something other than what it means. A `qa-blocked` label that survives approval trains readers to ignore `qa-blocked`, which is the label that is supposed to stop work. `q7n` is a particularly clean demonstration because the block was CORRECT and the fixes were CORRECT — nothing went wrong in the review, and the record still ends up self-contradictory.

SUGGESTED SHAPE (not chosen; needs the evidence-before-fix pass). `cmd_approve` already removes `qa-gate-entered` and `qa-pending` atomically with rollback. Adding `qa-blocked` to that same removal set looks like a one-line change in the existing atomic block rather than new machinery — but confirm against the rollback path, since the current removal list is what the rollback restores on partial failure. Whatever the fix, the regression test should assert the full post-approve label set, not just the presence of `qa-approved`; asserting presence is exactly what let this survive.

But it is a different claim, and the two were bundled into one sentence that reads as though a test would catch a regression. Nothing would.

If we want it enforced, one assertion in specs/qa-gate.sh pinning the two literals is the whole fix, and it belongs in this landing since the sweep rewrites the emitting code.

This is the same shape as the fourteen prose defects already recorded on fkm.1: a claim about what depends on something, where nothing checks. It is the first instance found in the PLAN rather than in the code or the docs.

I flagged cmd_enter's early-return arm as a trap (it writes no cycle record, and rmz means a task can be born holding qa-gate-entered — qzv.2 is live in that state with zero cycle records). Clearing it is therefore right, and the reasoning names the two real provenances rather than asserting a general rule.

That is the correct treatment of the trap and it composes three separately-filed findings (rmz inheritance, jue's stale label, the silent early return) into one coherent state model.

It had been poisoning the llh.18 and tracker-unreconcilable fixtures for as long as both existed, latently, because neither of those removes `qa-pending`.

So `8zi-1`'s exit 3 was **correct behaviour on a deliberately broken bd**: the removal genuinely did not happen and the read-back refused to claim it did. Reproduced standalone outside the spec, the same approve gives rc=0 and a final set of exactly `devops,qa-approved`.

**Resolution: the fixture, never the check.** `depoison_bd <root>` walks the `exec <path> "$@"` chain to the binary at the end and rewrites the wrapper as one hop; each of the three new fixtures calls it. Two assertions pin the hazard rather than hiding it — `8zi-0: the inherited bd wrapper IS poisoned by an earlier section` -> `poisoned`, then -> `clean`. The first is a canary: when the harness is fixed it flips and tells whoever fixed it the workaround can go. Filed as **`yj2`**.

One further failure was mine and unrelated: `depoison_bd` originally used `local root="$1" p="$root/bin/bd"`, and bash expands every word of a `local` before binding any of them, so under the runner's `bash -u` it aborted the spec with `root: unbound variable`. Split one-per-line, with the reason in a comment.

### Q2 — `.ok` IS present on the exit-3 rollback envelope

Measured directly on the shipped script, reading with plain `jq` rather than through the helper:

```
EXIT_CODE=3
{"ok":false,"subcommand":"approve","task_id":"...","status":"error","observations":"approve rolled back: failed to remove qa-pending after qa-approved was set; rolled back — pre-call label set restored exactly (devops,qa-blocked,qa-gate-entered,qa-pending,rubric-pending) ..."}

jq '.ok'         -> false
jq 'has("ok")'   -> true
jq 'keys'        -> ["observations","ok","status","subcommand","task_id"]
```

The field was never missing and the envelope was never malformed. **The apparent absence was the assertion helper**: `assert_json_field` extracts with `jq -r "$path // empty"`, and jq's `//` yields the right-hand side when the left is `false` OR `null` — so a present `false` is indistinguishable from an absent field. `echo '{"ok":false}' | jq -r '.ok // empty'` prints nothing; `jq -r '.ok'` prints `false`.

That is worth flagging as a diagnosis hazard, not just a test bug: the symptom pointed at production code, and the "fix" it invites is a change to the envelope writer. Every existing `assert_json_field '.ok'` call site asserts `"true"`, which the `//` form handles, so the blind spot had no caller until now. The two new legs use `assert_contains '"ok":false'` — the form the refusal legs in the same file already use — with the constraint named inline. Filed as **`m3c`**.

The same run confirmed byte-identical restoration: snapshot and post-rollback label strings are identical strings.

### Q3 — why `specs/approve-idempotency.sh` gained 82 lines

Because my change made 7 of its assertions fail, and all 7 are about the interaction between two independent closures of the same deadlock. Not scope creep — required, and I would rather you scrutinise it than not see it.

**The interaction.** The jue/gz3 deadlock (a Stop blocks with LABEL_WITHOUT_RECORD, prints `enter` -> `impact-report` -> `approve`, approve short-circuits, re-blocks forever) now has two closures in the tree: gz3's hash-aware idempotency guard, and jue's enter-side clear. The printed remediation runs `enter` first, so after the jue fix `qa-approved` is already gone when approve runs: `had_approved=0`, the idempotency block is not entered at all, and a mutant of that guard can express nothing.

Four changes, each preserving coverage rather than deleting it:

1. **E2 anchor re-pointed** (2 failures). E2 is a source-order test; its `L_LABEL` anchor was the literal `if ! add_label "$tid" "qa-approved"; then`, which no longer exists. The **invariant is untouched** — record still before label, label steps still before the tracking-state finalization — only the statement's spelling changed. New anchor is the `set_terminal_label` call, without the trailing `"${sweep_clear[@]}"` because `line_of` greps a BRE and `[...]` would be a bracket expression.
2. **Section G META driven WITHOUT `enter`** (3 failures). Driving the label-only-guard mutant through `enter` would assert nothing — a green leg measuring an unreachable branch, the exact failure mode this spec exists to prevent. The flow is now the plain re-run (edit, regenerate the report, approve again), where `qa-approved` is still set and the guard is the only thing between the operator and the deadlock. One variable, and it is the guard. Added a precondition asserting `qa-approved` is still set, so reachability is proven rather than assumed. The header names what this no longer covers (the enter-mediated path under a label-only guard) and where it is covered instead (jue-4a/4b/jue-META).
3. **A3 and H3 re-pointed** (2 failures). Both drive the printed remediation and asserted the approve envelope names a `stale-label re-bind`. It no longer does, correctly. Each now captures the remediation's **enter** line and asserts *it* reports the clear, plus `assert_not_contains` on the stale-label note — two assertions where there was one, both non-vacuous, encoding which closure does the work on that path. Everything those sections exist to prove (approve succeeds, is not a no-op, re-verifies the report and the review, writes a fresh bound record, and A4's "the printed remediation RELEASES the gate") was already passing and still passes.
4. **The `stale-label re-bind` literal re-asserted in section G**, where it is now the only reachable path, so the gz3 diagnostic did not lose its only assertion.

Result: `approve-idempotency` went from 125 pass / 7 fail to **137 pass / 0 fail** — a net gain of 12 assertions.

### The envelope-token measurement (owed from the brief)

The brief said "specs and operators grep them" and asked me to verify. **Nothing greps them.** A full-tree search for `removed qa-gate-entered=` and `removed qa-pending=`, and for the shorter `qa-gate-entered=` / `qa-pending=` forms, finds no consumer at all: not a spec, not a doc, not an agent prompt, not a hook. The only occurrences are the emitting line in `qa-gate.sh`, its synced fixture copies, and historical artifacts (grading-packet diffs, mutation-run mutant dumps, one captured e2e transcript, the code-graph index). One prose paraphrase exists in an `effort-ab` fixture note using different wording.

So the claim is **false for specs**. Operator-facing output stability is a real reason to keep the tokens and it costs nothing, so they are preserved verbatim — and there are now 8 assertions pinning both literals, because until this round a regression would have been silent. `$sweep_obs` carries the full cleared set, which the two counters cannot.

### Residuals I am shipping on

- **`5xy` (filed).** `approve` writes the append-only `QA-GATE APPROVED` record before adding the label (gz3), so a rollback can only undo labels. Under a bd whose removals cannot be proven, the rollback cannot remove the `qa-approved` it just added: exit 3, `ok=false`, a loud envelope — and both halves of the Stop's release predicate still satisfied. **Pre-existing and unchanged**: before this round the same bd made approve exit 0 and falsely report `removed qa-gate-entered=1`. What changed is that the gate now says it could not prove the transition, and `l1r.3-6c` asserts every part of that.
- **`cmd_enter`'s early-return arm still writes no cycle record.** Not fixed here — out of P3 scope and a much wider blast radius — but the arm's behaviour was decided (it clears `qa-approved`) and the file header now states that a `qa-gate-entered` label is *not* evidence that `enter` ever ran. `jue-4b` seeds that exact `rmz` inheritance shape.
- **`removed_entered` / `removed_pending` semantics shifted slightly**: derived from what the sweep actually removed, not from a `has_label` taken at the top of `cmd_approve`. Strictly sharper (it reports the transition performed, not a presence check taken several refusals and a record write earlier), but it is a change.
- `had_entered` / `had_pending` captures deleted as dead — the sweep does its own presence check and a second copy would be a stale second source of truth.

Recorded from the orchestrator: the gate escalated twice at the iteration cap during this round, both times on infrastructure — three server-side 529s plus one watchdog stall — with **zero review artifacts and zero blocks on `8zi`**. `choose continue` recorded both times; the second filed as a stronger `2ty` instance. ### Context coverage

**Read:** `8zi`, `jue`, `l1r.3` and `2j6`'s close reason via plain `bd show`; `docs/plans/v5-design-phase.md` Phase P and the whole correction layer; `y4a.13` to get the real five-label shape rather than invent one; `qa-gate.sh` in full for `cmd_enter`, `cmd_approve`, `cmd_block`, the label helpers, `emit_json` and the dispatch tail; the bjx `rubric-satisfied` logic and the `[rubric mismatch: ...]` override path before touching anything near them; all four `qa-blocked`/`qa-approved` label readers (`cmd_status`, `verify-before-stop.sh`, `epic-gate.sh:qa_state_of`, `statusline.sh` x2) to establish blast radius; `lib/fixture.sh` (`mk_fixture`, `seed_review_records`, `assert_mutant_applied`, `bd_show_with_comments`), `lib/shim.sh:mk_bd_shim`, `lib/assert.sh`, `run.sh`; the `TRACKER-RECONCILE` 7M and `WORKTREE-TOKEN` METAs for the sentinel-strip conventions; `approve-idempotency.sh` sections A/E/G/H.

ORCHESTRATOR CORRECTION, 2026-08-05 — I reported a COMPOSITE measurement three times and QA caught it.

I stated L3 as '444 passed / 5 skipped / 0 failed'. No such run exists. The 444 is the pass count from the PRE-sync run, which also had 7 FAILED (the fixture drift guard). The 0 is the failure count from AFTER the sync. I combined the two.

Verified both ends just now:
  pre-sync:  Tests  7 failed | 444 passed | 5 skipped (456)
  post-sync: Tests  451 passed | 5 skipped (456)   <- the truth, and QA's number

QA's diagnosis was exact: '444 looks like the pre-sync pass count paired with the post-sync failure count.'

WHY THIS IS WORSE THAN A WRONG NUMBER, and why it belongs on the record rather than just being fixed: a composite reads as a single observation. '444/5/0' has the shape of one measurement and the authority of one, while describing no run that was ever executed. Every consumer downstream — QA, the commit message, a future reader reconciling assertion counts — would treat it as a fact about a tree state. It is the same family as the fifteen prose defects already recorded on fkm.1, with one extra turn of the screw: the individual components were each true of SOME run, which is exactly what makes it survive a casual check.

The mechanical rule, for me and for anyone reading this later: report a tier's numbers from ONE run, quoting its own completeness line verbatim. Never assemble pass/skip/fail from separate invocations, even when the tree did not change between them — and especially not when it did, as here (make sync-fixtures ran between the two).

Related and already recorded: QA's R1-F4 corrected the specialist's '8 assertions pin the envelope tokens' to FOUR, because one of the eight is a NEGATIVE assertion (grep -c expecting 0) that a rename satisfies vacuously. I relayed the 8 without measuring it. Same lesson from the other direction: a count of assertions is not a count of what is pinned.
