Seventeenth instance of the family on fkm.1, and the second today where the defect and its own instance shipped together (the first being R4-F1's fix introducing new false prose).

Writing an id you expect to be allocated is a prediction, and this session has recorded fifteen cases of predictions being reported as measurements.

## QA round 1 of 2 — C1b worktree-sweep.sh

Reviewer: qa-claude (implementer role recorded on this task: devops). Change set
`5eaae437ba784c9439a6fb82705239f8a3a9b865565a01cc502738441fa57027`, 8 tracker
files, impact report FRESH (`server: code-graph`). File list taken from `git diff`
per the brief (31 git paths = 8 tracked + 21 `make sync-fixtures` copies + bd
state + the AgentLint report).

### FIRST ACTION (3a)
Read `.claude/.qa-tracking/impact-report-claude-workflow-plugin-8xv.json` before
reading the diff. All 8 seeds report 0 callers / 0 file-level dependents — the
sweeper is a new leaf, and the two edited hook scripts are platform entry points
with no in-repo callers. No high-fan-in caller set to chase, so the regression
surface is the hook wiring, which section 8 of the L2 spec covers end to end.

### Budget abort-checks — re-verified INDEPENDENTLY (both load-bearing)
1. **L2 under `BD_SHIM_ONLY=1`, real `bd` stripped from PATH.** Asserted
   `command -v bd` ABSENT and `which -a bd` empty FIRST, then ran the spec:
   **55 PASS / 0 FAIL / 0 SKIP**, zero `SKIPPED` lines in the output. (The task
   notes' "43/43" was an earlier snapshot; the spec has since grown to 55.) The
   required METAs therefore do run on the machine that guards the branch.
2. **Un-pushed META fails when the SHIPPED script is mutated.** Copied the plugin
   tree to a sandbox, control 55/55, applied the section-4 awk mutation to the
   shipped `worktree-sweep.sh` (mutation shown to land: diff printed, sha
   `2ff22e70e0ce56ab` -> `2356bef1e9e16a82`), re-ran: **exactly the claimed 9
   assertions fail — 1.3, 1.4, 1.7, 4.1, 4.5, 4.6, 5.3, 7.1, 7.4.** Restored ->
   55/55. Note 7.1/7.4 failing is the strong form: with the gate gone `--apply`
   removes 2 worktrees instead of 1, so the META proves a prevented DELETION,
   not just a changed reason string.

### Sensitivity spot-checks (asked for 2; ran 4 + 4 structural)
| mutation | claimed | measured |
|---|---|---|
| strip CONTAINMENT | 6 fail | **6** (1.3, 1.4, 1.10, 4.6, 7.1, 7.4) |
| strip AGE | 8 fail | **8** (1.3, 1.4, 1.9, 2.6, 2.7, 4.6, 7.1, 7.4) |
| strip UN-PUSHED | 9 fail | **9** |
| strip SessionEnd leg | 4 fail | **4** (8.2, 8.5, 8.6, 8.8) |
| control after each restore | 55/0 | **55/0** (three times) |
| inject `rm -rf $SWEEP_CANON` | A3+A4 | **A3+A4** |
| inject `worktree remove --force` | A6 | **A6** |
| inject a 2nd `ARG_APPLY=1` backdoor | A9 | **A9** |

### Safety path — verified BY CONSTRUCTION in my own fixtures, not by reading
- **`git worktree add` resolves symlinks** — reproduced independently. So the
  obvious symlink fixture would test nothing, confirming the implementer's probe.
- **B3 is NOT vacuous.** Rebuilt the repointed-`gitdir` shape from scratch:
  after the repoint, `git worktree list` reports
  `<repo>/.claude/worktrees/lnk` (string-LOOKS contained) whose `pwd -P`
  resolution is `<tmp>/outside/aliased` (physically outside). A string-prefix
  sweeper accepts it; `canon` + boundary-char rejects it. The hazard is real and
  the fixture exercises it.
- **Sibling-extends-root** reproduced in my own fixture (`.claude/worktrees-sibling`,
  the analogue of the live `<repo>-impactfix`) -> `not-contained`. Both live
  worktrees on this host were untouched throughout (verified after every probe).
- **Age direction.** Mapped `find -maxdepth 0 -mtime +N` empirically across 8 ages:
  1s / 1h / **23h59m** -> NO match at `+0`; 24h01m -> matches `+0` only; 7d01m ->
  matches `+2` but not `+7`. Truncation rounds toward **KEEPING**; the BSD man
  page's "rounded up" wording does not describe the implementation. GNU documents
  the same truncation. `--age-days 0` cannot reach a worktree created this session.
- **Naming off the safety path.** Own fixture: branch `wt-qa-closed-1`, no evidence
  file -> `no-task-id`. The token matches the shape regex, bd does not know it, so
  it resolves to NO id. Also `task-unknown` (evidence id bd does not know) and
  `detached-head` both fail toward KEEP.
- **`--report-only` beats `--apply` in BOTH flag orders** (post-parse precedence).
- **Never `--force`.** git refuses a dirty tree *and* a locked tree -> REMOVE-FAILED,
  rc=1, directory survives. Belt-and-braces on top of gate 3.
- **`--apply` re-classifies** rather than acting on a stale dry-run listing.
- **Blast radius is bounded**: `git worktree remove` does not delete branches —
  after `--apply` removed 3 worktrees in my fixture, all 3 branches survived, so
  committed work is never lost.
- **Structural**: zero `rm` anywhere in the file; `ARG_APPLY` raised in exactly one
  place; `session-end.sh` passes `--report-only` and no slash command invokes it.
- **No injection surface**: evidence-file content and branch tokens are
  shape-checked and only ever reach quoted arguments (`bd show "$id"`). An
  injection-shaped evidence id yields `no-task-id` and creates no marker file.
- **Robustness**: all bad operands rc=2 (incl. `--age-days --json`, `-1`, `1.5`);
  a 20-digit `--age-days` overflows into `require_uint` and fails CLOSED (rc=2);
  empty-array / no-worktree paths clean under bash 3.2 `set -u`; stdout carries
  the report and stderr is empty.

### Numbers — every claim re-run and confirmed
L1 **30/30** (worktree-sweep.test.sh 34 assertions) · L2 **41/41 specs, 1983/0
assertions** · e2e **15 files, 444 passed / 5 skipped / 0 failed**, drift guard
`_fixture-script-sync` **182 tests** · `make lint` **rc=0** (shellcheck also clean
on the new L2 spec, which is outside the lint glob) · packaging-parity **623/0** ·
workflow-manifest **131/0** · platform-audit **29/0** (was 23) · fixture sync
**168 (fixture,script) pairs byte-identical, 0 drift, 0 extra**, sha
`2ff22e70e0ce56ab` in all 8 copies, mode 0755 · line count **350**.
Packaging is complete without an explicit list: `install.sh:1664` glob-copies
`.claude/scripts/*.sh` and `workflow-manifest.sh` scans the same surface —
`worktree-sweep.sh` appears in `generate` as class `workflow` with the right sha.

### The three judged calls
1. **Pin-not-fix the `EVENT_DIFF:PostToolUse` defect — RIGHT, and the allowance is
   tight.** The defect is real: `git log -S` shows `bd-github-link` has NEVER been
   referenced in `settings.json`, so the Beads<->GitHub auto-link has never fired
   in this repo's own sessions. Fixing it is a behaviour change on the hook path
   (it would run on every Bash call) and needs a product decision, not a devops
   call inside a hard-budget task; `eo8` records both options with reproduction.
   I then attacked the allowance with five drift shapes: a second divergence in a
   different event (Stop timeout) -> 1 fail; a third PostToolUse matcher -> 1 fail;
   the `^Bash$` entry REMOVED -> 2 fails; an event deleted from BOTH files -> 4
   fails (count pin + set pin fire); the entry REORDERED to first -> 1 fail.
   Control 29/29 before and after. **No second divergence can hide behind it.**
2. **Gate-6/gate-3 coupling — ACCEPTABLE.** Reproduced both branches: with
   `.qa-tracking/` NOT gitignored the evidence file makes the tree read
   `?? .claude/` so gate 3 fires first (`dirty`) — the dependence fails toward
   KEEP. And the obvious tightening is self-defeating (see R1-F1). Consequence
   worth knowing: `install.sh` only writes its `.gitignore` when the target has
   none, so in most real installs the sweeper will be largely inert. That is the
   safe direction and the header already documents it.
3. **Age = top-dir mtime — AGREE, and I REJECT the proposed alternative.**
   `max(top-dir, admin-dir)` is not a 6-line improvement, it is unsound: `git
   status --porcelain` bumps the admin dir mtime, and `classify()` runs gate 3
   before gate 5, so the sweeper's own call would make every worktree read
   modified-now — and SessionEnd re-runs it every session. It would silently
   reduce the feature to a permanent no-op. If age ever needs to be load-bearing,
   use the tip commit's committer date.

### Other judgements
- **350 lines**: nothing is unnecessary surface. The 40-line header is the safety
  contract for a tool that deletes things, and every helper is on the gate path.
  Being exactly at the ceiling is a maintenance constraint for the next edit, not
  a defect.
- **Untested `timeout 8` leg — ACCEPT.** Neither binary exists here; the real
  backstop is the platform's 15s SessionEnd timeout in `settings.json`, and the
  failure mode is an absent warning (fail-safe). Noted in R1-F6 that a stub-`timeout`
  PATH test IS feasible using the `nojq-bin` pattern already in the same file.
- **`--json` without `jq`**: A16 asserts the precondition on its hand-built PATH
  before A17 asserts exit 2. Correct, and necessary — `/usr/bin/jq` exists here.
- No new file in `.qa-tracking/` breaks anything: every reader there uses explicit
  names (the only glob is `review-artifact-*.json`) and the denylist covers the dir.

### Findings — NONE at or above `high`, and none on the destructive path
R1-F1 medium (ignored files deleted with a swept worktree — documentation fix,
the code is correct), R1-F2/F3/F4 low, R1-F5/F6 info. Full text in the recorded
`REVIEW-ARTIFACT v1` comment.

### What I could NOT verify
- GNU `find` age semantics on Linux/CI (no GNU find on this host). Verified on
  BSD/macOS empirically; GNU documents the same truncation.
- The `timeout`/`gtimeout` legs of `session-end.sh` (neither binary present).
- Behaviour under a real Claude Code SessionEnd/SessionStart event (only the
  scripts were driven directly, as the L2 spec does).
- Sol's independent view: `codex-detect.sh` reports `reviewer_lane: codex`, but
  the orchestrator's brief directed the `claude` lane for this round, so the
  artifact is `qa-claude`. If round 2 happens, that is where Sol belongs.

title: code-graph-mcp.sh flakes in full L2 runs — 39/40 once, 40/40 on re-run, 29/29 isolated
description:
Observed during QA of wg6, unrelated to that change set (neither wg6 nor lv4 touches `.claude/mcp/code-graph-mcp/`).

EVIDENCE
  full L2 run 1  -> Specs: Total 40, Passed 39, Failed 1 (code-graph-mcp.sh)
                    Assertions: Passed 1927, Failed 1
  isolated re-run (`run.sh --filter code-graph-mcp`) -> 29/29, 0 failed
  full L2 run 2  -> Specs: Total 40, Passed 40, Failed 0
                    Assertions: Passed 1928, Failed 0

The failing assertion's text was lost — the run-1 capture was truncated by the reviewer's
own `tail -60`. Re-running the full suite is what produced the green, so the specific leg
is not yet known. Reproducing will require a full run with complete output retained.

HOST CONTEXT: two stale `node ./.claude/mcp/code-graph-mcp/bin/code-graph-mcp.js`
processes were alive at review time, started Sunday ~11PM and Monday ~12AM (days old,
predating the review session), both at ~0.0% CPU. Left running deliberately rather than
perturb the host mid-review, so their contribution is UNCONFIRMED — it is a hypothesis,
not a diagnosis.

WHY IT MATTERS: the spec boots real node MCP servers and asserts a lazy index build
(`code-graph-mcp-2: pre-build health reports status=uninitialized` then `healthy`). Boot
or build timing under 40-spec load is the obvious suspect class. It is fixture-isolated
(`$SAMPLE/.claude/.code-graph/index.db` under `mk_fixture`), so cross-run index state is
NOT the explanation.

COST: a flaky spec turns a full L2 run red for reasons unrelated to whatever diff is under
review, which is exactly the "guard that fails for unrelated reasons gets muted" failure
mode `lv4` documents for the doctor's non-mutation assertion.

SUGGESTED FIRST STEP: run the full suite N times retaining complete output, capture the
failing assertion text, then decide between a boot-readiness wait, a retry, or an explicit
precondition assertion. Do not "fix" it by loosening the assertion.
notes:
COMPLETED (P6, spec-side only): .claude/tests/component/specs/code-graph-mcp.sh — round 3 split into two server processes with a bounded readiness barrier between them.

ROOT CAUSE, measured (not inferred). The MCP SDK does not serialise requests: server/stdio.js `processReadBuffer` drains every complete frame in ONE stdin chunk in a single synchronous `while(true)` loop, and shared/protocol.js `_onrequest` dispatches each as `Promise.resolve().then(() => handler(...))` and returns. So two tools/call frames arriving in the SAME chunk are both queued as microtasks before either handler runs a line; code_search suspends on ensureIndex()'s `await preloadParsers(...)` having indexed nothing, and code_index_health's microtask runs immediately behind it, finds existsSync(index.db) false, and answers `uninitialized` — its response overtaking search's on the wire.

CORRECTION TO THE FILED DIAGNOSIS. The variable is NOT the 50 ms sleep racing the build duration. Measured against this repo's own server with controlled write timing:
  frames 50 ms apart, 2-file project   -> healthy
  frames 50 ms apart, 151-file project -> healthy, despite a ~1.9 s build (health frame written t=156 ms, answered t=2007 ms, 2 ms BEHIND search — it sat unread the whole build)
  all frames in ONE write, 2-file      -> uninitialized
  all frames in ONE write, 151-file    -> uninitialized
The trigger is whether the two frames land in the same stdin read — decided by bash's buffering of `printf` into the pipe and the scheduler, which machine load moves. That is the both-directions nondeterminism. It also means raising the sleep would have fixed nothing while appearing to work.

FIX = the SPLIT (round 3a builds, round 3b observes). One tools/call per process leaves nothing to chunk with and nothing to overtake. Every round in the spec now issues at most one tools/call; round 1 issues none.

EVIDENCE THE FIX FLIPS THE ARTIFACT. Under batch delivery — the condition that broke the old shape 100% of the time on both fixture sizes — the split shape returns: round 2 uninitialized, 3a ok/1 match, barrier found after 0 probes, 3b healthy (drift 0), section 4 unhealthy/corrupt_index. Both a 2-file and a 152-file fixture.

BARRIER. wait_for_index(): 20 x 0.25 s = 5 s ceiling. It is the readiness CONTRACT between the split halves, not the race fix. Timeout is a FAIL naming "the lazy build did not persist an index within 5s", never a skip or retry. In the healthy case it returns on probe 0 (bash waits for the whole pipeline, so node has exited and persisted by the time mcp_call returns); the loop keeps that from being an unstated assumption. Also applied to Section 5's stubbed-server index so its failure names the same mechanism.

SECTION 4 — CONFIRMED, WITH A CORRECTION. It does NOT "become deterministic for free": its round 5 issues exactly ONE tools/call, so it never had an interleaving window; the dxz race needs two in-flight requests. What changed is that its precondition (index.db present) is now positively established by the barrier instead of implied by round 3's timing, so a build regression surfaces at the barrier with the right message rather than at Section 4 as "index DB missing".

NOT TOUCHED, deliberately: server.js (orchestrator.md and qa.md both document empty/missing health as the expected pre-build state — serialising would change a documented contract to paper over a test bug); mcp_call (reused unchanged); the sleep values; impact-report.sh's degradation vocabulary (`server:"absent"`, `impact:null`), which D4 should reuse rather than mint a second one.

VERIFICATION STATUS: run.sh --filter code-graph-mcp x10 is the operator's to run per the house rules. bash -n OK and shellcheck rc=0 with zero findings, identical to the pristine baseline.

Reviewed under the claude lane because the codex relay returned rc=5 on a 300s budget (nq5f, P1) — the documented degradation in qa.md 6p.2, not a deviation.

New datum from QA of claude-workflow-plugin-016 (2026-07-30). **The failure is nondeterministic in BOTH directions** — this task's current framing ("29/29 isolated") no longer holds.

Two runs this session, same host, no concurrency (`ps` checked before each):

1. **Isolated run at BYTE-PRISTINE HEAD** (`252f720`), in a fresh `git clone --local` containing none of the 016 change, `run.sh --filter code-graph-mcp`:
   **28 passed / 1 failed** — `code-graph-mcp-2: post-build health reports status=healthy` (got `uninitialized`).
   So it CAN fail in isolation, which contradicts the 29/29-isolated observation recorded here.

2. **Full 41-spec L2 run in the live repo**, same session:
   **41/41 specs, 2002/0 assertions** — code-graph-mcp PASSED.
   So it can also PASS under full-suite load, which contradicts the "fails in full run" observation.

Confound ruled out: the clone DOES carry `.claude/mcp/code-graph-mcp/node_modules`, and the server booted fine — in the failing run `pre-build health reports status=uninitialized`, `code_search returns ok=true after lazy build` and `code_search found flagshipSymbol (count=1)` all PASSED. Only the post-build health assertion failed.

**Concrete lead** (from the 016 implementer, which I confirmed by reading the source): the lazy build demonstrably works — `code_search` returns a match — yet `code_index_health` reports `uninitialized`, which it only does when `existsSync(dbPath)` is false at `.claude/mcp/code-graph-mcp/src/tools/code_index_health.js:66-79`. `indexPath()` (`src/lib/resolve.js:32`) resolves `opts.cwd || CODE_GRAPH_CWD || CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR || process.cwd()`, and `db.js:117` uses `opts.dbPath || indexPath(opts)`. So the suspect class is the indexer and the health tool resolving the DB path from different roots (or the write not being flushed/visible at the moment health reads), not boot timing under load.

That reframes the suggested first step: rather than N full runs hunting a load-dependent flake, instrument the two paths and log the resolved `dbPath` from the indexer's write and from `code_index_health`'s read in the same round-trip. If they differ, that is the bug outright.

Not caused by 016 (change set is one test file, `.claude/tests/component/specs/installer-v3-upgrade.sh`); proven by the pristine-HEAD reproduction above.

title: Live-repo assertions + concurrent agent runs = false test failures (workflow-doctor non-mutation check vs a parallel installer experiment)
notes:
COMPLETED (P5, devops): Section 5a of workflow-doctor.test.sh narrowed, then
controlled. One file: .claude/scripts/tests/workflow-doctor.test.sh.

1. snapshot_live() no longer reads .qa-tracking at all. The five gate artifacts
   are gone from the live snapshot; a comment at the removal site names 5b as
   the owner and says why restoring one would be wrong.
2. A double-snapshot control guards the residue (agent model: pins + the
   .session-start mtime): two samples, no doctor run between. If the world moved
   with nothing running, 5a prints a bare `note:` and skips.
3. No skip verb was added. run-tests.sh reads exit codes only; the note moves
   neither counter, matching the idiom META-TESTs 3/4/5 already use.
4. META-TEST 7 is the control-of-the-control, three legs: an undisturbed fixture
   must HOLD (a control that fires on nothing would disable 5a permanently and
   invisibly); a .session-start perturbed between the samples must MOVE it; and
   the skip branch is then EXECUTED for real, asserting it prints a note and
   leaves PASS/FAIL untouched — plus a leg pinning the premise that this file's
   exit is a function of FAIL alone.
5. `diff` added to the required-tools check. The control reports "moved" on any
   non-zero diff exit, so an absent diff would have skipped 5a silently forever.

CONSEQUENCE TO EXPECT: this spec's assertion total is NOT a constant. The held
path contributes 3 (non-vacuity, pins, marker); the skipped path contributes 0.

NO LOCK, deliberately — candidate fix (c) on this filing. A lock cannot stop a
non-test writer and the Stop hook fires every turn regardless.

IN PROGRESS: none. NOT RUN BY ME: the spec end-to-end (house rule: orchestrator
measures). Targeted run to request:
  bash .claude/scripts/tests/workflow-doctor.test.sh

KEY DECISIONS
- gate-baseline is the one genuine coverage loss and is named in the code
  comment rather than papered over. It is not carried into 5b because that would
  be vacuous: session-start.sh captures the baseline only when current-task is
  EMPTY and 5b's fixture seeds current-task.
- The control's SECOND sample is reused as the measurement's BEFORE, so there is
  no gap between "the world was quiet" and "the measurement began".
- The control is honestly weak against a single write landing inside the doctor
  run; that limit is written into the code. The NARROWING is what makes 5a

comments.text:
OBSERVED TWICE IN ONE RELEASE, in opposite directions.

INSTANCE 1 (C0a review, round 1): QA's first sandbox experiment was contaminated by a
concurrent verify-before-stop.sh running the full L1 suite, which wrote
last-test-output.log mid-experiment. QA noticed, discarded the result, and re-ran
against an isolated copied target. Cost: one wasted experiment.

INSTANCE 2 (C0b, 2026-07-28): the Stop gate ESCALATED to J21 (iteration 3 of 3) naming
workflow-doctor.test.sh as failing. Re-run standalone with no concurrent agents:
94/94 PASS. Full L1 suite re-run: 29/29 specs, 0 failures. The implementer had
independently reported 29/29 minutes earlier. Cost: a spurious escalation on the
release's P0 task, which under the auto-defer rule would have set qa-deferred on the
NEXT Stop if no J21 choice had been recorded.

MECHANISM: workflow-doctor.test.sh Section 5c contains a deliberate NON-MUTATION
assertion — it snapshots live-repo state (.claude/.qa-tracking/approved content, the
session-start stamp mtime), runs the doctor, and asserts both are unchanged. That
assertion is correct and load-bearing: it is what proves the doctor's sandbox design
holds (see claude-workflow-plugin-0fc, where the absolute non-mutation claim was
falsified and had to be narrowed). But it measures GLOBAL state, so ANY concurrent
process touching .qa-tracking — a parallel installer experiment, another agent's Stop
hook, a second test run — makes it fail for a reason unrelated to the doctor.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND THE NUISANCE: the failure is indistinguishable from a real
regression in the gate's output. The Stop hook reported 'Tests failing (exit 2)' and
named the spec; nothing indicated the cause was external. An orchestrator that trusted
the signal would have sent a correct implementation back for a fourth round, or
accepted a defer on a P0.

CANDIDATE FIXES (not chosen; needs the evidence-before-fix pass):
  a) Have the non-mutation assertion detect concurrency and SKIP-with-log rather than
     FAIL — e.g. take the snapshot twice with no doctor run in between and skip if the
     control itself moved. This is the discriminating control the assertion currently
     lacks, and it is the same shape as the 'reduced regex must actually differ' leg in
     denylist-shared section D.
  b) Point the assertion at a copied target rather than the live repo. Weaker: it stops
     proving the property for the repo an operator actually runs it in.
  c) Advisory lock in run-tests.sh so two suite runs cannot overlap. Does not help
     against a non-test writer such as an installer experiment.
Prefer (a): it keeps the property under test and makes the interference visible instead
of fatal.

RELATED: claude-workflow-plugin-94d (tracker under-coverage) is the other gate-signal
integrity bug found this release. Both share a shape worth naming — the gate reports
with full confidence on evidence it did not verify was clean.

comments.author: username
comments.text:
FOURTH instance, 2026-07-30, and the clearest demonstration yet that this is systemic rather than incidental.

The Stop gate failed with:
  FAIL: non-mutation: the live repo's agent model pins + gate state are byte-identical
        after a doctor run
        expected: backend.md<TAB>claude-opus-5 / devops.md<TAB>claude-opus-5 ...

Cause: the C3 implementer agent was ACTIVELY EDITING those exact files at that moment —
it adds an EBF-CORE region to backend.md, frontend.md, devops.md and qa.md, and a
wire-in paragraph to orchestrator.md. The assertion snapshots live-repo state, runs the
doctor, snapshots again, and compares. Any concurrent writer to the snapshotted files
makes it fail for a reason unrelated to the doctor.

WHY THIS ONE MATTERS MORE THAN THE PREVIOUS THREE: earlier instances were a test run
racing another test run, which is at least avoidable by serialising suites. This is the
STOP HOOK's own mandatory verification racing the IMPLEMENTER it exists to gate. The
orchestrator does not control when the Stop hook runs — it fires on every turn — and an
implementer agent legitimately holds those files for many minutes. So the collision is
not a scheduling mistake anyone made; it is built into running a global-state assertion
inside a gate that fires while work is in flight.

Note this is NOT lv4 recurring. lv4 was the same spec's session-marker leg comparing AGE
instead of mtime; that is fixed and CI went green on b38714b. This is a different
assertion in the same spec (Section 5, agent model pins + gate state) failing for a
different reason. Two independent time/concurrency sensitivities in one spec is itself
the finding: the spec's whole Section 5 measures things the rest of the world is free to
change.

STRENGTHENS candidate fix (a) from the original filing: have the assertion take the
snapshot twice with no doctor run in between and SKIP-with-log if the control itself
moved. That converts 'something else touched the repo' from a fatal, misattributed
failure into a visible, correctly-attributed skip. It is the same discriminating-control
shape denylist-shared section D uses, and it is the only option that survives a gate
firing concurrently with an implementer.

Deliberately NOT fixed now: C3 (kfe) is mid-flight and an unrelated test edit would
enter its change set. Re-running cleanly after C3 lands is the correct next step, and
the earlier instances all passed on a clean re-run.

comments.author: username
comments.text:
FIFTH instance, 2026-07-30, and it settles the diagnosis: the assertion cannot hold during a review cycle BY CONSTRUCTION, not by bad luck.

Same assertion as instance four:
  FAIL: non-mutation: the live repo's agent model pins + GATE STATE are byte-identical
        after a doctor run

The C5 implementer is editing docs/RELEASE_AUDIT.md — nowhere near an agent prompt. What
moved is the second half: GATE STATE. During this window the gate legitimately churned
four times — the orchestrator removed an unearned qa-approved label, QA recorded a block,
current-task was restored after F1 cleared it, and a review artifact was written into
.qa-tracking/. Every one of those is the workflow working correctly.

So the failure mode is now fully characterised across five instances:
  1-2. a test run racing another test run (avoidable by serialising)
  3.   a killed runner (lv4, since fixed)
  4.   the Stop hook racing an implementer editing agent prompts
  5.   the Stop hook racing THE GATE'S OWN STATE MACHINE

Instance 5 is qualitatively worse than 4. An implementer editing prompts is at least
schedulable. But the Stop hook fires on every turn, and the gate mutates .qa-tracking on
every enter/block/approve/resolve — so this assertion is guaranteed to fail whenever a
review cycle is in flight, which is precisely when the Stop hook is most active. The
assertion and the gate are structurally incompatible.

THIS MAKES CANDIDATE FIX (a) THE ONLY VIABLE ONE. Sandboxing (b) is out — the whole point
is proving the doctor does not touch the LIVE repo. Serialising (c) cannot work against a
hook that fires on every turn. The double-snapshot control is the only design that
survives: take the snapshot twice with no doctor run between, and SKIP-with-log if the
control itself moved. That converts 'the world changed underneath me' from a fatal,
misattributed failure into a correctly-attributed skip.

Narrower alternative worth considering alongside it: split the assertion. Agent model
pins are genuinely static and worth asserting strictly; gate state under .qa-tracking is
mutable by design and probably should not be in a non-mutation snapshot at all. The
doctor's actual risk is that model-select.sh apply rewrites frontmatter — THAT is the
property worth guarding. Bundling volatile gate state into the same assertion is what
makes it unreliable.

Not fixed now: C5 is the release task and is mid-review. A test change would enter the
release's own change set.

comments.text:
LIVE INSTANCE, 2026-08-04, on qzv's own Stop hook. The Stop payload was INTERNALLY INCONSISTENT: changed_files[] (from the tracker) listed 7 paths while diff_summary (from git) showed 12, including four .claude/agents/*.md files.

NOT an ordering bug — I checked. reconcile-tracker runs at verify-before-stop.sh:898 and compute_intent_payload is called at :2282, so reconcile genuinely precedes the payload. The cause is a RACE: the Stop hook fired while a resumed subagent was still editing. Reconcile ran when 7 paths were dirty, the subagent then wrote the four prompt files, and the payload's git half saw them while its tracker half did not. Roughly 1400 lines of script execution separate the two reads.

Running qa-gate.sh reconcile-tracker afterwards folded all four in correctly: '+4 git-visible path(s) that no Write/Edit hook recorded (denylisted=0); subtracted=0 (added=4)'. So the mechanism is sound; the window is the problem.

WHY IT MATTERS FOR P5's SCOPE: this is not the .qa-tracking-vs-doctor contention P5 was opened for, but the same class — two reads of related state separated by enough execution for another writer to act. The consequence here is specific and bad: the file list handed to QA under-reported by 36%, and a reviewer working from changed_files[] alone would never have seen the four specialist prompts. The 94d.1 accounting did not catch it either, because nothing was subtracted — the paths simply did not exist yet at reconcile time.

Worth considering in P5: whether the payload should be computed from a single snapshot taken at reconcile time, or whether the two halves disagreeing should itself be a reported condition rather than something a reader has to notice by comparing two fields. The second is cheaper and matches the fkm.1.20 rule — a check that cannot detect divergence between its own inputs is not a check.

Process note, mine not the code's: I ended a turn while a specialist was still editing, which is what fired the Stop mid-implementation. Legitimate scenario the gate must survive, but I should not have invited it.

P5 / devops — ROOT CAUSE, with citations, before the patch.

X did Y because W:
`snapshot_live()` in `.claude/scripts/tests/workflow-doctor.test.sh` Section 5a
folds FIVE `.qa-tracking` artifacts into a byte-identical-before/after
assertion. Those five are rewritten in normal operation, by design and often —
so the assertion measures other agents' correct behaviour and reports it as a
doctor regression.

Evidence (read, not inferred):
- `post-edit.sh` — `TRACKING_FILE="$QA_TRACKING_DIR/changed-files.txt"` is
  appended on every Write/Edit, and `EDIT_COUNT=$((EDIT_COUNT + 1)); echo
  "$EDIT_COUNT" > "$EDIT_COUNT_FILE"` runs on every Write/Edit by ANY agent
  (guarded only on `bd` present + `.beads/` present — both true in this repo).
- `qa-gate.sh` approve — `if ! write_gate_baseline "qa-gate-approve"` with no
  `--if-missing`: an UNCONDITIONAL rewrite of `gate-baseline` on every approve.
- `session-start.sh` — `rm -f "$QA_TRACKING_DIR/approved"` is unconditional;
  `current-task` is written by the gate on enter/block/restore.
- Observed live during this task: `.claude/.qa-tracking/current-task` mtime
  moved to 14:53 while two other specialists were editing.

This is the LESSONS.md rule stated at the ledger's own line: "a non-mutation
assertion must compare a quantity that moves only when the property is
violated" (sourced to lv4, which was the AGE-vs-mtime leg of this same spec).
Section 5a violates it in a second, independent way — which is the finding
instance 5 already reached: "the assertion and the gate are structurally
incompatible."

Coverage check before removal (this is why removing is not a loss):
5b seeds approved / changed-files.txt / edit-count / current-task into a COPIED
target via `seed_gate_state` and asserts all four survive; META-TEST 3 runs
`session-start.sh` directly against an identically-seeded copy and asserts the
same four are destroyed. Both directions, over input the spec controls.

ONE GENUINE, NARROW LOSS, recorded rather than glossed: `gate-baseline` is in
`snapshot_live` but NOT in `seed_gate_state`/`gate_state_fingerprint`. It is not
carried into 5b because doing so would be vacuous: `session-start.sh` calls
`qa-gate.sh baseline-capture` only inside `if [ -z "$SS_ACTIVE_TASK" ]`, and
5b's fixture deliberately seeds `current-task`, so nothing in that path can move
it. In the live half it was equally inert whenever a cycle was in flight — i.e.
during every review — and volatile the rest of the time. Trade taken knowingly.

Fix shape: (a) from the original filing, as strengthened by instances 4 and 5.
Narrow the snapshot to the low-volatility residue, then guard the residue with a
double-snapshot control that notes-and-skips. No lock: a lock cannot help
against a non-test writer, and the Stop hook fires on every turn regardless.

ORCHESTRATOR ERROR, 2026-08-06 — I REPORTED A CORPSE AS A RUNNING SUITE, THREE TIMES, AND THE LEDGER HAD ALREADY WARNED ME.

I told QA to poll /tmp/p568.log for the full L2 result and said 'L2 still running' across three turns. Verified after QA challenged it:
  - wrapper process: DEAD (pgrep finds nothing)
  - log mtime frozen at 15:48:20, last line '=== L2 FULL ==='
  - 110 orphaned component-fixture.* temp dirs left behind
The run was killed at roughly 70 minutes and produced no result.

WHY IT WAS INVISIBLE, which is the part worth keeping: I piped 'make test-component' through a sed range filter that emits only on completion. So a killed run and a running run produce a BYTE-IDENTICAL log — absence of output was indistinguishable from work in progress, and I read it as the latter every time.

LESSONS.md ALREADY CONTAINS THIS LESSON, VERBATIM, from z9m on 2026-07-29: 'A no-failures signal is not a the-run-finished signal: assert the suite completeness line (Total: N specs), because a killed runner reports zero failures from the specs it did reach.' QA checked the PID and mtime instead of reading the quiet log as green, and said the ledger predicted the finding. It did. I wrote the brief that sent QA to that log, so had it trusted me it would have reported an L2 result that never existed.

TWENTY-FOURTH INSTANCE of the family, and the second where I committed an error the record already warned against — the first being writing a task id before the create returned, twice, the second time after recording the rule myself. Same shape: knowing the rule is not the intervention.

THE MECHANICAL FIX, and it is mine to apply going forward: never pipe a long suite through a filter that suppresses progress. Let it stream, or tee it. A run I cannot distinguish from a dead one is a run I cannot report on. QA's own suggested follow-up says the same thing from the other side — have long background runs emit per-spec progress so a killed run is distinguishable without inspecting the PID.

WHAT REPLACED IT: QA identified the 13 of 44 specs touching the changed surface and ran those plus code-graph-mcp — 14 specs, 1495 assertions, 2 failures, both installer-v3-upgrade 8e leg B, matching the baseline exactly. It stated plainly that this is scoped-by-construction rather than complete coverage, and that the unrun 30 rest on its grep-based blast-radius judgement rather than on a measurement. That is the honest framing and I am not restating it as a full-tier pass.

SIXTH INSTANCE, 2026-08-07 — AND IT IS A SPEC P5 DID NOT COVER.

The Stop hook's L1 run reported review-separation.test.sh FAILING. My own L1 minutes earlier reported 32/32. Re-ran the spec alone: PASSED: 60 assertion(s), zero failures.

Concurrent writer identified by pgrep at the moment of the red: QA driving 'bash .claude/tests/component/run.sh --filter installer-v3-upgrade' (PIDs 82016/82018/82098) while the Stop hook ran the full L1 tier.

WHY THIS MATTERS AFTER P5 SHIPPED: P5 narrowed workflow-doctor.test.sh's snapshot_live() because it was the known instance. It is not the only one. review-separation.test.sh drives the real qa-gate.sh against live bd records, so a concurrent spec run that also writes bd records perturbs it the same way. The narrowing fixed the instance; the CLASS is still open for any spec that exercises live shared state.

THE COST IS EXACTLY WHAT THIS TASK PREDICTED: a red that is not a regression teaches everyone to re-run rather than believe, and the re-run habit is what lets a real regression through. In this session that cost is measurable — I have now twice had to distinguish a genuine failure from contention by hand, and QA had to do the same on P4.

WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY CLOSE THE CLASS, rather than the next instance: the component runner and the L1 runner should not both be able to hold the live repo at once. Either a lock at the runner level (rejected for P5 on the grounds that a lock cannot stop a NON-test writer — still true, but two test runners are exactly the case a lock CAN stop), or the specs that touch live bd records get fixture-local bd workspaces the way the component tier already gives fixture-local .beads. The second is the durable fix and is larger than a Phase P item.

Recorded here rather than as a new task because it is this task's own class, freshly evidenced against a different spec — and because 1nz's title says 'concurrent agent runs', which is precisely what produced it.

title: qa-gate.sh approve does not clear a prior cycle qa-blocked label
description:
Found during athena-hk4 r2 (ENG-2574). Same script family and same defect class as claude-workflow-plugin-jue (enter not clearing qa-approved) and athena-m7l.

SYMPTOM: cmd_approve clears qa-gate-entered, qa-pending and rubric-pending, but NOT a qa-blocked label left by a previous cycle. A task that was blocked and then re-approved ends up carrying BOTH qa-approved and qa-blocked simultaneously — a contradictory state that any label-based reader (a watcher, a dashboard, a human skimming) can resolve either way. QA had to remove it by hand to leave the trail coherent.

Observed live: athena-hk4 showed 'LABELS: backend, devops, frontend, qa-approved, qa-blocked' immediately after approve; a monitor polling labels reported APPROVED off a state that also said BLOCKED.

FIX: cmd_approve should clear qa-blocked as part of the same atomic label transition it already performs. Pair with claude-workflow-plugin-jue — together they are 'the label transitions are not exhaustive across cycles', and the cheapest durable fix is one function that sets the terminal label and clears every other cycle label unconditionally.

BROADER PATTERN (worth fixing at the root): label presence is being used as a verdict signal, so any stale label is a false verdict. Consider having approve/block write the bound change_set_hash to a machine-readable file that readers poll for a CHANGE, rather than asking them to interpret a set of flags.
close_reason: Duplicate of claude-workflow-plugin-8zi — same defect (approve does not clear a prior-cycle qa-blocked). Merged into 8zi, which carries the fix in v5 Phase P3. Closed in v5 Phase P0.

title: qa-gate.sh: enter does not clear a prior cycle qa-approved, so re-review cannot record a fresh approval
description:
Surfaced on athena-g55 (ENG-2574, 4-repo change) where a QA-approved change set legitimately needed a second review cycle after a rebase.

TWO SYMPTOMS, ONE ROOT CAUSE — cmd_enter clears rubric-satisfied but NOT qa-approved:

1. cmd_approve short-circuits as an idempotent no-op on the second cycle, so NO new hash-bound record is written. The previous cycle's change_set_hash silently remains the last approval on record while verify-before-stop.sh keeps the gate armed — an unresolvable deadlock without manual 'bd label remove qa-approved'. QA had to do exactly that surgery to complete cycle 2.

2. Any watcher polling for the qa-approved LABEL reads the stale label as a verdict on the new commits. The orchestrator hit this: a monitor keyed on the label fired immediately and reported a prior-cycle approval as approval of a later commit. Caught only by reading the approval record and comparing hashes.

SUGGESTED FIX (either is sufficient, first is cleaner):
- cmd_enter clears qa-approved alongside rubric-satisfied; or
- cmd_approve refuses to no-op when the current change-set hash differs from the last approval record's hash.

Also worth considering: have cmd_approve write the bound hash into a machine-readable file so watchers can poll a value that must change, rather than a flag that is merely present.
close_reason: Fixed in the 8zi landing: cmd_enter clears a prior-cycle qa-approved in BOTH the fresh arm and the early-return arm. The early-return argument is structural — {qa-gate-entered, qa-approved} is unreachable through the gate's own transitions since the sweep includes qa-gate-entered and no add_label qa-approved survives outside set_terminal_label — so a task in that state got the label from rmz inheritance or a partial transition. QA verified. qzv.2 is a live instance of that shape.

title: review-check.sh gate has no hash-freshness predicate: a stale REVIEW-ARTIFACT satisfies the gate for bytes it never reviewed
description:
Demonstrated with numbers during gl6 (v4.1 U1). After a round that REMOVED the 103-line function all five of Sol iteration-3 findings targeted, the gate still reported green on that artifact:

  current change_set_hash : f147c9eb42c8d7184459621c7c9fe3443ab84dfec909e798dc98c60b4cf7f71e
  artifact reviewed_hash  : 56758d90e77afea6bf5b94ee9aadae4d140278f2df6178489b8794eca3b12536
  review-check.sh gate    : {"ok":true, "open_findings":0}

cmd_gate parses reviewed_hash into its emit payload but has no predicate comparing it to the current change set — the conditions are existence, well-formedness, independence, and resolved/overruled findings. So an approval can cite an independent review of bytes that no longer exist. QA caught this by judgment, not mechanism: it declined to reuse the stale artifact and re-assembled a fresh request. The Stop-side approval record IS hash-bound (that is what change_set_hash exists for), so this is not a release-forgery hole — the gap is that the REVIEW half of the release credential has no freshness binding while the APPROVAL half does.

Decide whether reviewed_hash != current change_set_hash should warn or refuse. Refuse is the direction consistent with the rest of the gate (fail closed), but note it would force a fresh paid review on any post-review edit however trivial — so a warn-plus-record, or refuse-unless-explicitly-overridden, may be the better shape. Worth pairing with the U1 experience: this cycle ran five review rounds, and a refuse rule would have made each fix round require a new Sol run at 300s and 8-of-9 degradation odds (xo8).

Related: yp8 (rubric criteria have no resolution verb — QA judges that correct by design since the rubric loop is deliberately not a gate).

comments.author: username
comments.text:
DESIGN TENSION observed live on gl6 (v4.1 U1), worth folding into whatever fix j9u gets.

The two mechanisms interact badly at the boundary:
- review-check.sh gate has NO hash-freshness predicate, so a stale artifact satisfies it (demonstrated: gate ok=true with reviewed_hash=56758d90 against current d4d1a40f — green on a review of a 103-line function that no longer exists).
- .claude/review-config caps max_review_iterations=3, so codex-review.sh REFUSES a fresh review past that (exit 6, "iteration 4 exceeds max_review_iterations=3").

So on a task that legitimately ran more review rounds than the cap allows, the system simultaneously (a) will not produce a fresh independent review and (b) accepts the stale one as satisfying the gate. Neither half is wrong alone — the cap is bounded diligence, the gate is deliberately not hash-bound so trivial post-review edits do not force a paid re-review — but together they mean "the review of record can be arbitrarily stale precisely when the change has churned the most."

If j9u adds a freshness predicate, it must not deadlock against the cap: a refuse-on-stale rule plus a cap-refused fresh review equals an unapprovable task. Candidate shapes: (1) freshness WARNS and the warning is recorded in the approval record, so staleness is auditable rather than blocking; (2) refuse-on-stale, but the cap-refused case is an explicit documented exception requiring the Claude lane to author at the current hash (which is what happened here by orchestrator judgment, not by mechanism); (3) reset the iteration counter on a material scope change, since gl6 iteration 4 was reviewing a materially SMALLER artifact than iteration 3 — arguably a new review subject rather than a fourth pass at the same one.

Evidence: gl6 ran six rounds; Sol reviewed at iteration 3 (5 HIGH, all against code later deleted); the fix rounds then reduced the doc from 103 executable lines of automation to a hand-edit procedure; iteration 4 was refused by the cap.

comments.author: username
comments.text:
<!-- BD-MCP-META: {"kind":"design-view","source":"qa-agent","observed_on":"claude-workflow-plugin-gl6"} -->
## QA view: the two mechanisms are not symmetric, and that asymmetry is the way out of the deadlock

I have now watched both fire on gl6, so here is a view. The tension is real and stated
correctly: the gate accepts an arbitrarily stale review **precisely when the change has
churned most**, while the cap refuses to produce a fresh one. A naive refuse-on-stale
predicate would deadlock against the cap and make the task unapprovable.

### The observation that breaks the symmetry

**Staleness and iteration count measure different things, and only one of them is about
cost.**

- The **cap** exists to bound *spend*. Its unit is "paid reviewer turns on this task".
- **Freshness** is about *evidential validity*. Its unit is "does the review describe the
  bytes being approved".

On gl6 these came apart completely. Sol's r3 findings were all against a 103-line function
that no longer exists. Iteration 4 was not a fourth pass at the same subject — it was a
**first** pass at a materially different one. Charging it against a budget for "more review
of the same thing" is a unit error, and it is the unit error that produces the deadlock.

That is why of the three candidate shapes listed, **resetting the counter on a material
scope change is the one I would pursue** — not as a convenience, but because it corrects
the unit rather than trading one failure for another. The other two shapes both leave the
unit error in place and then argue about which failure to prefer.

### But "material scope change" must be defined mechanically, or it becomes a bypass

This is where I would put the design effort, because a soft definition here is an
unbounded-spend hole wearing a correctness costume. A change set can churn indefinitely,
and if every churn resets the counter, the cap is gone. Constraints I would want:

1. **Reset must be bounded too.** A cap on resets (e.g. at most one counter reset per
   task, or a hard ceiling of N total paid turns regardless of resets) so the worst case
   is bounded spend rather than unbounded.
2. **Mechanically detectable, not asserted.** Something derivable from artifacts already
   on disk — e.g. the reviewed construct is gone, or the diff's overlap with the reviewed
   diff falls below a threshold. On gl6 the signal was unusually clean: every finding
   location in the r3 artifact pointed into a function that no longer exists. "All finding
   locations in the last artifact are absent from the current bytes" is a candidate
   predicate that is cheap to compute and hard to game accidentally.
3. **Recorded, not silent.** A reset should write its own record with the evidence, so a
   reader sees "counter reset at iteration 4 because the reviewed construct was removed"
   rather than an unexplained fourth paid turn.

### What I would NOT do

**Do not make the gate refuse on stale.** Refusing is the fail-closed instinct and it is
wrong here, for a reason gl6 demonstrates: the resulting deadlock has no legitimate exit,
so every real occurrence would be resolved by an override, and a predicate whose normal
resolution is an override is worse than no predicate — it trains people to bypass the gate
and it buries the actual evidentiary weakness under a procedural one.

**Warn instead, and put the warning where the decision is made.** The gate should surface
`reviewed_hash != current change_set_hash` in its JSON envelope and in the approve path's
observations, the way `approve` already warns on `rubric-pending`. That is enough: it makes
the weakness visible to the reviewer who is about to approve, without creating a state the
system cannot leave. On gl6 I reached the right answer by judgment — re-assembling the
request instead of reusing r3 — but judgment is not a predicate, and a warning is the
cheapest way to make the next reviewer's judgment informed rather than lucky.

### The residual this leaves, stated plainly

Even with a warning, gl6's outcome stands: the final bytes were approved on a **free-lane**
independent review, and the only paid review of this task described code that has been
deleted. That is a legitimate outcome — the Claude lane is a first-class reviewer and the
artifact is honest about which lane produced it (see the lane-provenance comment on gl6) —
but it is materially weaker evidence than the task's history suggests at a glance. Whatever
shape this lands on should make that visible at approve time, because the failure mode
worth preventing is not "an unapprovable task", it is **a reviewer who believes a paid
second opinion covered bytes it never saw.**

title: Gate gap: at-threshold RUBRIC criteria have no resolution verb — resolve-finding is artifact-keyed only, so a failed rubric criterion cannot be gate-recorded
description:
Found by gl6 (v4.1 U1) while trying to record the C6 resolution. `qa-gate.sh resolve-finding <tid> C6 …` fails with finding_id_not_found: the verb only accepts ids from the latest REVIEW-ARTIFACT comment (there, R3-F1..R3-F5). Rubric criteria live in a separate RUBRIC comment, and the only resolution verbs that exist (resolve-finding, arbitrate) are both artifact-keyed.

The implementer correctly REFUSED the available workaround — reusing an R3 id would have filed C6 content under a Sol finding and corrupted the audit trail — and recorded a RUBRIC-FIX-headed comment instead.

Two possible readings, and the fix depends which is intended: (a) at-threshold rubric criteria SHOULD require gate-recorded resolutions, in which case resolve-finding needs to accept rubric criterion ids (or a sibling verb resolve-criterion must exist); or (b) failed criteria are closed by the next grading round alone, in which case nothing is broken and only the orchestrator instruction was wrong — but then the durable trail for a rubric fix is a free-text comment with no schema, which is weaker than every other gate record in this system.

Evidence: gl6 rubric i1 failed C6; the fix landed and is verified; the trail is a RUBRIC-FIX comment rather than a RESOLVED record. Related: the same cycle found resolve-finding rejects summaries containing triple-quote delimiters on shell quoting (separate usability nit).

comments.author: username
comments.text:
<!-- BD-MCP-META: {"kind":"design-view","source":"qa-agent","observed_on":"claude-workflow-plugin-gl6"} -->
## QA view: artifact-keyed `resolve-finding` is correct by design; the gap is documentation, not mechanism

Asked for a view on which reading is intended. Mine, with the reasoning:

**`resolve-finding` should stay artifact-keyed.** The two loops are deliberately
asymmetric in the spec, and the asymmetry is load-bearing:

- The **review artifact** loop IS mechanically gated. `review-check.sh gate` is called
  by both `qa-gate.sh approve` and `verify-before-stop.sh`, and an unresolved finding
  at/above `risk_threshold` refuses with `unresolved_findings`. Resolutions therefore
  need machine-readable records with mandatory `--fix`/`--test` refs — hence
  `resolve-finding`.
- The **rubric** loop is explicitly NOT a gate. qa.md §6 says the rubric is "a QA
  INPUT, not a parallel gate", and carries a standing instruction to future editors:
  "do not wire the rubric label into `verify-before-stop.sh`". Its state lives in
  `RUBRIC` comments plus the `rubric-satisfied` / `rubric-pending` labels, and §6f
  requires QA's approve comment to cite the verdict. The verification that a
  `needs_revision` criterion was addressed is **the re-grade**, not a resolution record.

So there is no missing subcommand. Adding `resolve-criterion` (or letting
`resolve-finding` accept rubric ids) would create a second machine-checkable gate over
rubric state, which is exactly what principle 6 ("one approval source of truth") and the
qa.md editor note forbid.

**The implementer's handling on gl6 was right on both counts.** It refused to reuse an
`R3-F*` id to make the command green — that would have filed rubric criterion C6's
content under a Sol finding and corrupted the audit trail — and used a `RUBRIC-FIX`
headed comment instead. `finding_id_not_found` was the gate behaving correctly: C6 is
not a finding in the latest artifact, so there is nothing for it to key on.

**What IS missing is a sentence.** Nothing in qa.md or orchestrator.md tells an
implementer what to do with a `needs_revision` criterion, so the natural move is to reach
for the nearest-looking verb and get a confusing `finding_id_not_found`. Suggested
narrowing of this task, in preference order:

1. Add to qa.md §6d (the `needs_revision` path): rubric criteria are resolved by
   **re-grading**, not by `resolve-finding`; record the work in a `RUBRIC-FIX` comment
   and let the next grader pass be the verification. State explicitly that reusing an
   artifact finding id for a rubric criterion is forbidden because it corrupts the
   review record.
2. Optionally improve the error text: when the id looks like a rubric criterion
   (`^C[0-9]+$`) rather than an artifact finding (`^R[0-9]+-F[0-9]+$`), say so —
   "`C6` looks like a rubric criterion; rubric criteria are not gate-recorded, see
   qa.md §6d" instead of the bare `finding_id_not_found`.
3. Close as working-as-intended once (1) lands.

### Adjacent gap found while checking this — worth its own task, not this one

`review-check.sh gate` has **no hash-freshness predicate**. On gl6 right now:

```
current change_set_hash : f147c9eb42c8d7184459621c7c9fe3443ab84dfec909e798dc98c60b4cf7f71e
artifact reviewed_hash  : 56758d90e77afea6bf5b94ee9aadae4d140278f2df6178489b8794eca3b12536
gate                    : {"ok":true, "open_findings":0}
```

The gate is green on an artifact whose five findings were all against a shell function
that **no longer exists in the doc** — the implementer removed it this round. Nothing is
wrong with the resolutions; the problem is that "independent review exists and has no
open findings" is satisfied by a review of bytes that are gone. QA is handling it by
judgment this round (re-assembling the request and asking for a fresh Sol iteration
rather than reusing the artifact), but judgment is not a predicate. Whether the gate
should warn on, or refuse, an artifact whose `reviewed_hash` differs from the current
change set is a real design question and deserves its own task rather than being folded
in here — noting it so the connection is not lost.

title: F1 doc-only fast path has an off-repo blast-radius blind spot: docs carrying copy-pasteable commands that write outside the repo auto-approve unreviewed
description:
Systemic gap surfaced by gl6 (v4.1 U1). The F1 doc-only fast path in verify-before-stop.sh auto-approves any change set whose paths are all doc-only (is_doc_only_path matches *.md), on the reasoning that "no reviewable source changed". But a markdown file can carry copy-pasteable shell commands whose blast radius is entirely OUTSIDE the repo — gl6 added a recipe that rewrites the operator global ~/.codex/config.toml, and QA reproduced a HIGH data-loss path in it (unguarded cp + truncate-before-read: 115 bytes -> 22, zero backup) that F1 would have auto-approved unseen. No in-repo test can see that failure class; the orchestrator only caught it by deliberately routing the change past F1.

Options to consider: (a) exempt from F1 any doc whose diff adds fenced shell blocks containing redirects/cp/mv/rm targeting paths outside the repo (grep-level heuristic, fail toward review); (b) maintain a small denylist of operator-facing docs (CODEX_SETUP.md, STAGING_QA.md when it lands, README install sections) that never take the fast path; (c) leave F1 as-is and make it a documented orchestrator responsibility. Evidence: gl6 QA record (HIGH + 2 MEDIUM + 2 LOW, all in commands that write or back up operator config); the lesson "Doc-only is not low-risk" filed from the same cycle.

comments.author: username
comments.text:
# Preserved from gl6 (v4.1 U1) — sandboxed operator-config safety harness

Extracts the pin-rewrite function VERBATIM from docs/CODEX_SETUP.md (awk on the fenced block) rather than from a copy that could drift, then runs failure arms in a sandboxed HOME. Old recipe: SAFE=4 UNSAFE=2. Fixed recipe: SAFE=7 UNSAFE=0. Arms: control, dir 500, file 000, dir-ro+file-writable, file 444, no config, no ~/.codex.

Directly reusable for dkp (F1 doc-only blast-radius blind spot) — this is the shape of test that would have caught the HIGH before F1 auto-approved it.

## verify-doc.sh
```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Extracts codex_pin_newest VERBATIM from docs/CODEX_SETUP.md and runs it under
# QA's failure arms in a sandboxed HOME. Never touches the real ~/.codex.
set -u
DOC=/Users/edk0/Desktop/projects/claude-workflow-plugin/docs/CODEX_SETUP.md
WORK=/tmp/gl6-harness
PASS=0; FAIL=0

# --- extract the function from the doc, stripping the 3-space code-block indent ---
awk '/^   codex_pin_newest\(\) \{/,/^   \}$/ { sub(/^   /,""); print }' "$DOC" > "$WORK/extracted.sh"
if ! grep -q '^codex_pin_newest() {' "$WORK/extracted.sh"; then
    echo "EXTRACTION FAILED — function not found in doc"; exit 1
fi
echo "--- extracted $(grep -c '' "$WORK/extracted.sh") lines from the doc ---"
bash -n "$WORK/extracted.sh" || { echo "EXTRACTED FUNCTION IS NOT VALID BASH"; exit 1; }
zsh -n "$WORK/extracted.sh" || { echo "EXTRACTED FUNCTION IS NOT VALID ZSH"; exit 1; }
echo "syntax: valid in bash AND zsh"

# --- stub codex: deterministic, offline, no cost ---
mkdir -p "$WORK/stubbin"
cat > "$WORK/stubbin/codex" <<'STUB'
#!/bin/bash
case "$1 $2" in
  "debug models") printf '{"models":[{"slug":"gpt-5.6-sol","visibility":"list","priority":1}]}\n' ;;
  "doctor --json")
      cfg="${CODEX_HOME:-$HOME/.codex}/config.toml"
      m=$(grep -m1 '^[[:space:]]*model[[:space:]]*=' "$cfg" 2>/dev/null | sed 's/.*=[[:space:]]*"\{0,1\}//; s/"$//')
      printf '{"checks":{"config.load":{"details":{"model":"%s"}}}}\n' "${m:-<default>}" ;;
  *) exit 0 ;;
esac
STUB
chmod +x "$WORK/stubbin/codex"
export PATH="$WORK/stubbin:$PATH"

REALISTIC='# my codex config
model = "gpt-5.2-codex"
model_reasoning_effort = "max"
network_access = true

[tools]
web_search = true   # first-party search
view_image = true

[profiles.legacy]
model = "gpt-4.1-old"
'

arm() {  # arm <name> <setup> <expect: intact|rewritten|created|abort>
    local name="$1" setup="$2" expect="$3"
    local SB; SB=$(mktemp -d -t gl6doc.XXXXXX) || return
    local CODEXDIR="$SB/.codex" CFG="$SB/.codex/config.toml"
    mkdir -p "$CODEXDIR"; printf '%s' "$REALISTIC" > "$CFG"
    local before; before=$(cksum < "$CFG" | awk '{print $1}')
    local bb; bb=$(wc -c < "$CFG" | tr -d ' ')

    "$setup" "$CODEXDIR" "$CFG"

    local out rc
    out=$( HOME="$SB" bash -c "source '$WORK/extracted.sh'; codex_pin_newest" 2>&1 ); rc=$?

    chmod u+rwx "$CODEXDIR" 2>/dev/null; chmod u+rw "$CFG" 2>/dev/null
    local ab as baks verdict
    if [ -e "$CFG" ]; then ab=$(wc -c < "$CFG"|tr -d ' '); as=$(cksum < "$CFG"|awk '{print $1}')
    else ab=MISSING; as=MISSING; fi
    baks=$(ls "$CODEXDIR"/config.toml.bak-* 2>/dev/null | grep -c . | tr -d ' ')
    local strays; strays=$(ls "$CODEXDIR"/config.toml.new.* 2>/dev/null | grep -c . | tr -d ' ')

    case "$expect" in
      intact)  [ "$as" = "$before" ] && verdict="SAFE (bytes intact)" || verdict="DATALOSS" ;;
      created) if [ "$ab" = MISSING ]; then verdict="UNSAFE (nothing created)"
               elif [ "$(cat "$CFG")" = 'model = "gpt-5.6-sol"' ]; then verdict="SAFE (fresh pin)"
               else verdict="UNSAFE (unexpected content)"; fi ;;
      abort)   if [ "$rc" -eq 0 ]; then verdict="UNSAFE (proceeded)"
               elif [ -e "$CODEXDIR" ]; then verdict="UNSAFE (created dir)"
               else verdict="SAFE (aborted cleanly)"; fi ;;
      *)       if [ "$ab" = MISSING ]; then verdict="DATALOSS"
               elif ! grep -q '^model = "gpt-5.6-sol"$' "$CFG"; then verdict="DATALOSS (no pin)"
               elif ! diff -q <(printf '%s' "$REALISTIC" | grep -v '^[[:space:]]*model[[:space:]]*=') \
                              <(grep -v '^[[:space:]]*model[[:space:]]*=' "$CFG") >/dev/null; then
                    verdict="PARTIAL (non-model line moved)"
               else verdict="SAFE (correctly rewritten)"; fi ;;
    esac
    [ "$strays" != 0 ] && verdict="$verdict +STRAY-TEMP"

    printf '%-32s rc=%-3s %4s -> %-8s baks=%-2s %s\n' "$name" "$rc" "$bb" "$ab" "$baks" "$verdict"
    [ -n "$out" ] && printf '%36s%s\n' "" "$(printf '%s' "$out" | tail -1)"
    case "$verdict" in SAFE*) PASS=$((PASS+1));; *) FAIL=$((FAIL+1));; esac

}

s_control()      { :; }
s_dir_500()      { chmod 500 "$1"; }
s_file_000()     { chmod 000 "$2"; }
s_no_config()    { rm -f "$2"; }
s_no_codexdir()  { rm -rf "$1"; }

arm "~/.codex mode 500"            s_dir_500       intact
arm "config mode 000"              s_file_000      intact
arm "dir read-only, file writable" s_dir_ro_file_w intact
arm "config read-only (444)"       s_immutable_cfg rewritten
arm "no config.toml"               s_no_config     created
arm "no ~/.codex at all"           s_no_codexdir   abort

HOME="$SB" bash -c "source '$WORK/extracted.sh'; codex_pin_newest" >/dev/null 2>&1

[ "$A" = "$B" ] && echo "idempotent: second run byte-identical" || echo "NOT IDEMPOTENT"

CFG="$SB/.codex/config.toml"; BAK=$(ls -1 "$CFG".bak-* 2>/dev/null | tail -1)
HOME="$SB" codex doctor --json | jq -r '.checks["config.load"].details.model'
if diff <(grep -v '^[[:space:]]*model[[:space:]]*=' "$BAK") \
        <(grep -v '^[[:space:]]*model[[:space:]]*=' "$CFG"); then
   echo "    OK: every non-model line survived"; fi
```

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# gl6 R1-F1 reproduction + regression harness.
# Runs the §5 step-2 recipe under QA's failure arms in a sandboxed CODEX_HOME.
# NEVER touches the real ~/.codex. Arg 1: "old" (current doc text) or "new" (fixed).
#
# Each arm reports: config bytes before -> after, whether a .bak exists, and a
# VERDICT of SAFE (operator bytes intact or correctly rewritten) / DATALOSS.

set -u
VARIANT="${1:-old}"
PASS=0; FAIL=0

REALISTIC_CONFIG='# my codex config
model = "gpt-5.2-codex"
model_reasoning_effort = "max"
network_access = true

[tools]
web_search = true   # first-party search
view_image = true

[profiles.legacy]
model = "gpt-4.1-old"
'

# ---- the recipe under test, OLD (current doc text, lines 279-284) ----
recipe_old() {
    local CFG="$1" NEWEST="$2"
    local BAK="$CFG.bak-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
    cp "$CFG" "$BAK"
    { printf 'model = "%s"\n' "$NEWEST"
      grep -v '^[[:space:]]*model[[:space:]]*=' "$BAK"; } > "$CFG"
}

# ---- the recipe under test, NEW (guarded backup + same-dir temp + atomic mv) ----
recipe_new() {
    local cfg="$1" newest="$2" bak new
    [ -n "$newest" ] || { printf 'could not resolve a slug - aborting\n' >&2; return 1; }
    [ -d "$(dirname "$cfg")" ] || { printf 'no %s - run codex login first\n' "$(dirname "$cfg")" >&2; return 1; }
    if [ -e "$cfg" ]; then
        bak="$cfg.bak-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
        cp -p "$cfg" "$bak" || { printf 'backup failed - aborting, %s untouched\n' "$cfg" >&2; return 1; }
    else
        bak=""
    fi
    new=$(mktemp "$cfg.new.XXXXXX") || { printf 'cannot create temp beside %s - aborting\n' "$cfg" >&2; return 1; }
    { printf 'model = "%s"\n' "$newest"
      [ -n "$bak" ] && grep -v '^[[:space:]]*model[[:space:]]*=' "$bak"
      :; } > "$new" || { rm -f "$new"; printf 'build failed - aborting, %s untouched\n' "$cfg" >&2; return 1; }
    if [ -n "$bak" ]; then
        if ! diff -q <(grep -v '^[[:space:]]*model[[:space:]]*=' "$bak") \
                     <(grep -v '^[[:space:]]*model[[:space:]]*=' "$new") >/dev/null; then
            rm -f "$new"; printf 'a non-model line moved - aborting, %s untouched\n' "$cfg" >&2; return 1
        fi
    fi
    mv "$new" "$cfg" || { rm -f "$new"; printf 'install failed - aborting, %s untouched\n' "$cfg" >&2; return 1; }
}

run_recipe() { if [ "$VARIANT" = old ]; then recipe_old "$@"; else recipe_new "$@"; fi; }

# arm <name> <setup-fn> <expectation: intact|rewritten>
arm() {
    local name="$1" setup="$2" expect="$3"
    local SB; SB=$(mktemp -d -t gl6arm.XXXXXX) || return
    local CODEXDIR="$SB/.codex" CFG
    mkdir -p "$CODEXDIR"; CFG="$CODEXDIR/config.toml"
    printf '%s' "$REALISTIC_CONFIG" > "$CFG"
    local before_bytes before_sum
    before_bytes=$(wc -c < "$CFG" | tr -d ' '); before_sum=$(cksum < "$CFG" | awk '{print $1}')

    "$setup" "$CODEXDIR" "$CFG"          # apply the failure condition

    local out rc
    out=$( { run_recipe "$CFG" "gpt-5.6-sol"; } 2>&1 ); rc=$?

    chmod u+rwx "$CODEXDIR" 2>/dev/null; chmod u+rw "$CFG" 2>/dev/null   # regain access to inspect
    local after_bytes after_sum baks verdict
    if [ -e "$CFG" ]; then
        after_bytes=$(wc -c < "$CFG" | tr -d ' '); after_sum=$(cksum < "$CFG" | awk '{print $1}')
    else
        after_bytes=MISSING; after_sum=MISSING
    fi
    baks=$(ls "$CODEXDIR"/config.toml.bak-* 2>/dev/null | grep -c . | tr -d ' ')

    if [ "$expect" = intact ]; then
        if [ "$after_sum" = "$before_sum" ]; then verdict="SAFE (bytes intact)"; else verdict="DATALOSS"; fi
    elif [ "$expect" = created ]; then
        # No config existed. Correct outcome: a fresh file holding just the pin.
        if [ "$after_bytes" = MISSING ]; then verdict="UNSAFE (nothing created)"
        elif [ "$(cat "$CFG")" = 'model = "gpt-5.6-sol"' ]; then verdict="SAFE (fresh pin created)"
        else verdict="UNSAFE (unexpected content)"; fi
    elif [ "$expect" = abort ]; then
        # No ~/.codex. Correct outcome: refuse, create nothing.
        if [ "$rc" -eq 0 ]; then verdict="UNSAFE (proceeded anyway)"
        elif [ -e "$CODEXDIR" ]; then verdict="UNSAFE (created a config dir)"
        else verdict="SAFE (aborted, nothing created)"; fi
    else
        # rewritten: model line must be new AND every non-model line preserved
        if [ "$after_bytes" = MISSING ]; then verdict="DATALOSS"
        elif ! grep -q '^model = "gpt-5.6-sol"$' "$CFG"; then verdict="DATALOSS (no new pin)"
        elif ! diff -q <(printf '%s' "$REALISTIC_CONFIG" | grep -v '^[[:space:]]*model[[:space:]]*=') \
                       <(grep -v '^[[:space:]]*model[[:space:]]*=' "$CFG") >/dev/null; then
            verdict="PARTIAL (non-model lines changed)"
        else verdict="SAFE (correctly rewritten)"; fi
    fi

    printf '%-34s rc=%-3s %5s -> %-8s baks=%-3s %s\n' \
        "$name" "$rc" "$before_bytes" "$after_bytes" "$baks" "$verdict"
    [ -n "$out" ] && printf '%38s%s\n' "" "msg: $(printf '%s' "$out" | head -1)"
    case "$verdict" in SAFE*) PASS=$((PASS+1));; *) FAIL=$((FAIL+1));; esac
    chmod -R u+rwx "$SB" 2>/dev/null; rm -rf "$SB"
}

s_control()      { :; }
s_dir_500()      { chmod 500 "$1"; }
s_file_000()     { chmod 000 "$2"; }
s_no_config()    { rm -f "$2"; }
s_no_codexdir()  { rm -rf "$1"; }
s_dir_ro_file_w(){ chmod 555 "$1"; chmod 666 "$2"; }

printf '==== VARIANT: %s ====\n' "$VARIANT"
arm "control (all writable)"        s_control       rewritten
arm "~/.codex mode 500"             s_dir_500       intact
arm "config mode 000"               s_file_000      intact
arm "dir read-only, file writable"  s_dir_ro_file_w intact
arm "no config.toml"                s_no_config     created
arm "no ~/.codex at all"            s_no_codexdir   abort
printf -- '---- %s: SAFE=%d  UNSAFE=%d ----\n' "$VARIANT" "$PASS" "$FAIL"
```

Extracts the changed lines VERBATIM from docs/CODEX_SETUP.md (grep -F on shipped text, awk on the function), 8/8 PASS. Covers the class behind 3 of the 4 gl6 findings: backup-glob selection vs listing.

Arms: correct selection against a mixed dated/non-dated set in bash AND zsh; silent-and-empty when only non-dated backups exist (note: 2>/dev/null does NOT suppress a zsh glob failure — zsh fails the glob before ls runs, so the error is the shell's, not ls's); the OLD construct still reproducing the bug as a control; §9 cleanup sparing hand-made backups; guard ordering + hostile-stub behaviour.

Directly reusable for dkp — this is a doc-embedded-command test that no in-repo suite would otherwise run.

```bash
#!/bin/bash

# Sandboxed HOME throughout. Never touches the real ~/.codex.

PASS=0; FAIL=0
ck() { if [ "$2" = "$3" ]; then printf '  PASS  %s\n' "$1"; PASS=$((PASS+1));
       else printf '  FAIL  %s\n          want=[%s]\n          got =[%s]\n' "$1" "$3" "$2"; FAIL=$((FAIL+1)); fi; }

: > "$CFG.bak-20260728-010000"; : > "$CFG.bak-d2j2"

  : > "$T/.codex/config.toml.bak-20260728-010000"
  : > "$T/.codex/config.toml.bak-20260726-215700"
  : > "$T/.codex/config.toml.bak-d2j2"
  : > "$T/.codex/config.toml.bak-my-precious"
  : > "$T/.codex/config.toml.before-restore"
```

# Preserved from gl6 round 4 (Sol's five HIGH findings) — six operator-config failure classes

repro-r3.sh + verify-r3.sh cover, with the OLD constructs retained as live controls (29/29 PASS, controls still reproduce their bugs so the arms are proven sensitive):

1. **glob breadth** — bak-[0-9]* is one digit then ANYTHING; matched bak-20260728-personal and bak-9-keep, both in an irreversible rm kill list.
2. **filter-status propagation** — a trailing `:` made the group exit 0 on a failed grep; process substitutions hide exit status from diff.
3. **mirror-oracle tautology** — with grep stubbed to exit 127, validation compared a 5-line baseline to a 1-line wiped candidate and reported IDENTICAL (would install).
4. **TOML-semantic damage** — a line filter deleted a model= line from inside a triple-quoted block; the mirror said IDENTICAL. Fixed by PREVENTION (refuse + defer to hand edit), since no line-filter oracle can attribute damage inside a multiline string.
5. **partial-write atomicity** — measured, not assumed: macOS cp does NOT truncate up front, but a FIFO short source left the destination holding 7 bytes of partial content while exiting 0. (A 60MB kill test was inconclusive — APFS clones instantly.)
6. **jq null trap** — jq -r returns the 4-character string `null`, which passes -n and would have registered -m null.

Also recorded: `codex --strict-config doctor` is the correct placement (top-level flag; `codex doctor --strict-config` errors with unexpected argument), and a $STAMP variable holding a digit class does NOT glob-expand in zsh.

No in-repo test can currently see any of these six — their blast radius is the operator home directory. This is dkp's core evidence.

## repro-r3.sh
```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Reproduction of Sol's five R3 HIGH findings against the CURRENT doc constructs.
# Sandboxed throughout; never touches the real ~/.codex.
set -u
export PATH="/Users/edk0/.nvm/versions/node/v22.21.1/bin:$PATH"
hr() { printf '\n=== %s ===\n' "$1"; }

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- R3-F1
hr 'R3-F1: is `bak-[0-9]*` a "dated-only" pattern? (doc asserts it is)'
T=$(mktemp -d); CFG="$T/config.toml"; : > "$CFG"
: > "$CFG.bak-20260728-010000"          # a real dated backup this doc creates
: > "$CFG.bak-20260728-personal"        # Sol's counterexample 1
: > "$CFG.bak-9-keep"                   # Sol's counterexample 2
: > "$CFG.bak-d2j2"                     # letter-initial (already excluded)
echo "files:"; ls -1 "$T" | grep bak | sed 's/^/    /'
echo "what the doc's [0-9]* glob actually matches:"
for f in "$CFG".bak-[0-9]*; do printf '    %s\n' "$(basename "$f")"; done
picked=$( { ls -1 "$CFG".bak-[0-9]*; } 2>/dev/null | tail -1 )
printf 'selection picks: %s\n' "$(basename "$picked")"
[ "$(basename "$picked")" != "config.toml.bak-20260728-010000" ] \
  && echo "  F1 CONFIRMED (selection): picks a NON-dated file over the dated one" \
  || echo "  selection happened to be right here, but see the match list above"
echo "and the narrowed rm would delete:"
for f in "$CFG".bak-[0-9]*; do printf '    %s\n' "$(basename "$f")"; done
echo "  F1 CONFIRMED (rm): operator files bak-20260728-personal / bak-9-keep are in the kill list"
echo
echo "proposed strict pattern (8 digits - 6 digits, anchored by glob semantics):"
STAMP='[0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9]-[0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9]'
for f in "$CFG".bak-$STAMP; do printf '    %s\n' "$(basename "$f")"; done
```
