```bash
echo '  empty catalog:'
v=$(printf '{"models":[]}' | jq -r '.models | map(select(.visibility=="list")) | sort_by(.priority) | .[0].slug')
printf '    value=[%s]  length=%s  passes [ -n ]? %s\n' "$v" "${#v}" "$([ -n "$v" ] && echo YES || echo no)"
[ "$v" = "null" ] && echo "    F5 CONFIRMED: 4-char string 'null' passes -n => function would install model = \"null\""
echo '  missing slug key:'
v2=$(printf '{"models":[{"visibility":"list","priority":1}]}' | jq -r '.models | map(select(.visibility=="list")) | sort_by(.priority) | .[0].slug')
printf '    value=[%s]  passes [ -n ]? %s\n' "$v2" "$([ -n "$v2" ] && echo YES || echo no)"
echo '  moved surface (no .models at all):'
v3=$(printf '{"catalog":[]}' | jq -r '.models | map(select(.visibility=="list")) | sort_by(.priority) | .[0].slug' 2>&1 | head -1)
printf '    value=[%s]\n' "$v3"
echo '  with the proposed `// empty`:'
v4=$(printf '{"models":[]}' | jq -r '.models | map(select(.visibility=="list")) | sort_by(.priority) | .[0].slug // empty')
printf '    value=[%s]  passes [ -n ]? %s\n' "$v4" "$([ -n "$v4" ] && echo YES || echo no)"
echo '  and what step 3 would propagate into the registration:'
v5=$(printf '{"checks":{"config.load":{"details":{}}}}' | jq -r '.checks["config.load"].details.model')
printf '    NEWEST=[%s] -> claude mcp add ... -m "%s"\n' "$v5" "$v5"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- R3-F2a
hr 'R3-F2a: does the trailing `:` mask a grep failure in the build group?'
T=$(mktemp -d); B="$T/bak"; N="$T/new"
printf 'model = "old"\nmodel_reasoning_effort = "max"\nnetwork_access = true\n' > "$B"
# simulate grep failing (unreadable input => grep exits 2)
chmod 000 "$B"
{ printf 'model = "%s"\n' "NEW"
  [ -n "$B" ] && grep -v '^[[:space:]]*model[[:space:]]*=' "$B"
  :; } > "$N" 2>/dev/null; rc=$?
chmod 644 "$B"
printf '  group exit status: %s  (0 means "build succeeded")\n' "$rc"
printf '  resulting candidate: %s line(s): %s\n' "$(grep -c '' "$N")" "$(tr '\n' '|' < "$N")"
[ "$rc" -eq 0 ] && echo "  F2a CONFIRMED: grep failed, group reported success, candidate is model-line-only"
echo '  without the trailing `:` the status propagates:'
{ printf 'model = "%s"\n' "NEW"; chmod 000 "$B"; grep -v '^x' "$B"; } > "$N" 2>/dev/null; rc2=$?
chmod 644 "$B"; printf '    status=%s\n' "$rc2"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- R3-F2b
hr 'R3-F2b: are process-substitution failures invisible to diff?'
T2=$(mktemp -d); mkdir -p "$T2/fakebin"
# a PATH with no grep at all
printf '#!/bin/sh\nexit 127\n' > "$T2/fakebin/grep"; chmod +x "$T2/fakebin/grep"
B2="$T2/bak"; N2="$T2/new"
printf 'model = "old"\nmodel_reasoning_effort = "max"\nnetwork_access = true\n[tools]\nweb_search = true\n' > "$B2"
printf 'model = "NEW"\n' > "$N2"     # the WIPED candidate: only the model line
PATH="$T2/fakebin:$PATH" bash -c '
  if diff -q <(grep -v "^[[:space:]]*model[[:space:]]*=" "'"$B2"'") \
              <(grep -v "^[[:space:]]*model[[:space:]]*=" "'"$N2"'") >/dev/null
  then echo "  validation said: IDENTICAL (would install)"
  else echo "  validation said: DIFFER (would refuse)"; fi'
echo "  baseline has $(grep -c '' "$B2") lines; candidate has $(grep -c '' "$N2") line — they are NOT identical"
echo "  F2b CONFIRMED if the validation said IDENTICAL above: broken grep => false success on a wiped config"
rm -rf "$T2"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- R3-F3
hr 'R3-F3: does the line filter damage a TOML multiline string, undetectably?'
T3=$(mktemp -d); CFG3="$T3/config.toml"
cat > "$CFG3" <<'TOML'
model = "gpt-5.2-codex"
model_reasoning_effort = "max"

[tools]
notes = """
how to pin:
model = "some-slug"
that is the line that matters
"""
web_search = true
TOML
echo "  original parses as valid TOML? (real binary, --strict-config)"
CODEX_HOME="$T3" codex doctor --json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '"    status=\(.checks["config.load"].status) model=\(.checks["config.load"].details.model)"'
NEW3="$T3/new"
{ printf 'model = "gpt-5.6-sol"\n'; grep -v '^[[:space:]]*model[[:space:]]*=' "$CFG3"; } > "$NEW3"
echo "  lines deleted from inside the multiline string:"
diff "$CFG3" "$NEW3" | grep '^<' | sed 's/^/    /'
echo "  does the MIRROR validation notice? (same filter on both sides)"
if diff -q <(grep -v '^[[:space:]]*model[[:space:]]*=' "$CFG3") \
            <(grep -v '^[[:space:]]*model[[:space:]]*=' "$NEW3") >/dev/null
then echo "    validation said IDENTICAL -> F3 CONFIRMED: string content silently deleted, undetected"
else echo "    validation said DIFFER"; fi
echo "  proposed detector: does the file contain a multiline delimiter?"
grep -q '"""' "$CFG3" && echo '    YES ("""), so the recipe should refuse and defer to a hand edit'
rm -rf "$T3"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- R3-F4
hr 'R3-F4: does a direct `cp` overwrite leave the destination partial on failure?'
T4=$(mktemp -d)
dd if=/dev/urandom of="$T4/src" bs=1m count=60 2>/dev/null
printf 'PRECIOUS ORIGINAL CONFIG\n' > "$T4/dest"
before=$(cksum < "$T4/dest" | awk '{print $1}')
cp "$T4/src" "$T4/dest" & pid=$!
sleep 0.05; kill -9 $pid 2>/dev/null; wait $pid 2>/dev/null
after_bytes=$(wc -c < "$T4/dest" | tr -d ' '); src_bytes=$(wc -c < "$T4/src" | tr -d ' ')
after=$(cksum < "$T4/dest" | awk '{print $1}')
printf '  dest was 24 bytes; src is %s bytes; after killed cp dest is %s bytes\n' "$src_bytes" "$after_bytes"
if [ "$after" != "$before" ] && [ "$after_bytes" != "$src_bytes" ]; then
  echo "  F4 CONFIRMED: destination left PARTIAL — original content gone, copy incomplete"
elif [ "$after" != "$before" ]; then
  echo "  F4 CONFIRMED (weaker): original destroyed (cp completed before the kill)"
else
  echo "  not reproduced this run; cp opens dest O_TRUNC before reading, so partial state is inherent"
fi
echo "  proposed atomic form (temp beside target + mv), same interruption:"
printf 'PRECIOUS ORIGINAL CONFIG\n' > "$T4/dest2"
b2=$(cksum < "$T4/dest2" | awk '{print $1}')
( t=$(mktemp "$T4/dest2.restore.XXXXXX") && cp -p "$T4/src" "$t" && mv "$t" "$T4/dest2" ) & pid=$!
sleep 0.05; kill -9 $pid 2>/dev/null; wait $pid 2>/dev/null
a2=$(cksum < "$T4/dest2" | awk '{print $1}')
[ "$a2" = "$b2" ] && echo "    dest2 INTACT (original preserved; only a stray temp may remain)" \
                  || echo "    dest2 changed — atomic form did not hold"
ls "$T4" | grep -c restore | sed 's/^/    stray temps: /'
rm -rf "$T4"

printf '\n=== reproduction pass complete ===\n'
```

title: write_gate_baseline reports FAILURE and writes no baseline when the working tree is CLEAN (spurious sync-error every session)
description:
Found while writing the U0.6 upgrade-gate-compat L2 spec (claude-workflow-plugin-ehv). REPORTED, NOT FIXED, per evidence-before-fix — the fix is its own reviewed change. NOT a gate-release gap: it fails in the SAFE direction (no baseline == nothing subtracted == every later change reads as new == block). What it costs is a false alarm and one lost cleanup step.

ROOT CAUSE
.claude/scripts/qa-gate.sh, write_gate_baseline(). The brace group that composes the baseline file ends with:

    [ -n "$status_out" ] && printf '%s\n' "$status_out"
  } > "$tmp" 2>/dev/null || { rm -f "$tmp"; log_sync_error "...could not write $tmp..."; return 1; }

The group's exit status is the status of its LAST command. When `git status --porcelain` is empty (clean tree), `status_out` is empty, `[ -n "" ]` returns 1, `&&` short-circuits, and the group exits 1 — even though every write succeeded. The `||` arm then deletes the just-written tmp file, logs a failure, and returns 1.

REPRODUCTION (deterministic, ~10s)

    cd /tmp && rm -rf gbclean && mkdir gbclean && cd gbclean
    git init -q && git config user.email t@t.t && git config user.name t
    printf 'x\n' > a.txt
    printf '.claude/.qa-tracking/\n.claude/scripts/\n' > .gitignore
    git add -A && git commit -qm base
    mkdir -p .claude/scripts .claude/.qa-tracking
    for s in <plugin>/.claude/scripts/*.sh; do ln -sf "$s" ".claude/scripts/$(basename "$s")"; done
    git status --porcelain | wc -l          # -> 0  (CLEAN)
    CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR=$PWD bash .claude/scripts/qa-gate.sh baseline-capture --by manual-probe

OBSERVED (clean tree):
  {"ok":false,"subcommand":"baseline-capture","task_id":"","status":"error",
   "observations":"gate-baseline capture failed (captured_by=manual-probe); see sync-errors.log"}
  rc=2 ; .claude/.qa-tracking/gate-baseline does NOT exist
  sync-errors.log: "write_gate_baseline: could not write .../gate-baseline.tmp.<pid> (captured_by=manual-probe)"

CONTROL (same command, ONE dirty entry — remove `.claude/scripts/` from .gitignore so porcelain is 1):
  {"ok":true,...,"status":"captured","observations":"gate-baseline captured_by=manual-probe entries=1 ..."}
  rc=0 ; the file is written.

So the single variable is "is the tree clean".

ALSO REPRODUCED THROUGH THE REAL CALLERS on a v3.5->v4.1 upgraded fixture with a clean tree — session-start and qa-gate enter both hit it:
  [qa-gate]       write_gate_baseline: could not write .../gate-baseline.tmp.73416 (captured_by=session-start)
  [session-start] gate-baseline capture failed; the Stop gate will treat pre-existing git dirt as new work this session
  [qa-gate]       write_gate_baseline: could not write .../gate-baseline.tmp.73615 (captured_by=qa-gate-enter)
  [qa-gate]       enter: gate-baseline capture failed for <tid> (gate still correct; ...)

IMPACT
1. USER-VISIBLE FALSE ALARM. Every session-start on a clean repo writes a sync-errors.log line; the NEXT session-start surfaces it as "Last session's bd sync failed at <ts>" in workflow_warnings. On a repo that is usually clean this fires forever, for nothing.
2. LOST CLEANUP. The `rm -f "$LEGACY_APPROVED_BASELINE"` that retires the v1 approved-baseline is the LAST statement of the function, after the `mv` — so a clean-tree capture never reaches it and a legacy v1 file survives a "first v2 write" that reported success elsewhere.
3. approve on a clean tree logs "gate-baseline refresh failed" and leaves no v2 baseline.
4. Gate DECISIONS unaffected: empty baseline and absent baseline produce identical Stop verdicts.

WHY NO EXISTING TEST CATCHES IT
Every current baseline spec dirties the tree first — gate-baseline-v2.sh §1 seeds 3 pre-dirty files, §6.2 writes src/pre.ts into the worktree before capturing. The clean-tree case is untested.

SUGGESTED FIX SHAPE (for whoever picks this up, NOT applied)
Make the group's last command unconditional, e.g. `printf '%s' "${status_out:+$status_out$NL}"` or move the guarded printf ahead of a trailing `:`. Land it WITH a regression assertion for the clean-tree case (an L1 qa-gate baseline test is the cheapest home) and a META that reverts the guard and watches it fail.

NOTE FOR THE FIXER: .claude/tests/component/specs/upgrade-gate-compat.sh documents this defect in its header and deliberately avoids depending on it (section 5 deletes both baseline files and asserts absence instead of relying on the writer failing; section 6 approves with real dirt on disk so its v2-write assertion measures the writer). Nothing pins the buggy behaviour, so the fix does not have to update that spec.

title: install.ps1 jq interop under Windows PowerShell 5.1: Out-File UTF8 BOM + -NoNewline single-line JSON + 2>$null under EAP=Stop crashes the corrupt-.mcp.json arm
description:
Pre-existing pattern at the settings.json merge site, now mirrored at the new .mcp.json merge site by U0.2 (both flagged in p5n's implementer FINDINGS; this task makes the deferral durable). Three facets, fix together at both sites:

1. `Out-File -Encoding UTF8` writes a BOM under Windows PowerShell 5.1 (pwsh 7 writes BOM-less). jq 1.7+/1.8 accept BOM input (verified locally on 1.8.1), so the re-update path survives on modern jq, but older jq rejects BOM'd JSON — on WinPS 5.1 + old jq, a second `-Mode 2` run would take the "not valid JSON" arm and replace the operator's merged .mcp.json with the shipped config (.bak preserves it, message is loud, but operator servers leave the live file). Fix: write BOM-less explicitly (e.g. [System.IO.File]::WriteAllText with UTF8Encoding($false)).

2. `$merged | Out-File -NoNewline` concatenates jq's output lines: the written JSON is valid but single-line (tokens keep their leading-indent separators). Cosmetic but diff-hostile for operators who commit .mcp.json/settings.json. Fix rides along with facet 1 (join with "`n" or WriteAllText the joined string).

3. `& jq empty $TargetMcpJson 2>$null` runs under `$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"` (install.ps1:27). On WinPS 5.1, a native command writing stderr while redirected raises NativeCommandError as a terminating error — so the corrupt-.mcp.json arm CRASHES the installer instead of falling through to the copy-shipped fallback. pwsh 7.2+ is unaffected. Same pattern pre-exists at the $hadEffortEnv probe. Fix: wrap the probe (e.g. run under $ErrorActionPreference='Continue' scope, or test parseability via ConvertFrom-Json try/catch).

Also worth folding in: pin the jq invocation ARGUMENT ORDER file-to-file in packaging-parity.test.sh (the wiring assertions pin `jq -s $Var` presence but not `existing-first` arg order; a swapped `$SourceSettings $SettingsFile` in ps1 would reverse the union direction with the L1 still green — bash side is covered end-to-end by L2 installer-mcp-config + functional probes, ps1 side is currently eyeball-only).

Validation for the fix: execute install.ps1 -Mode 2 on a Windows host (or pwsh in CI) against a seeded operator .mcp.json/settings.json — the packaging-parity L1 proves expression identity but cannot execute PowerShell.
close_reason: Fixed in U0.7 (m7e): UTF8-no-BOM WriteAllText at both ps1 jq-merge write sites (multi-line JSON preserved); Test-JsonSingleObject stderr capture safe under EAP=Stop; jq operand order pinned file-to-file in packaging-parity. Residual sibling sites (bd/git 2>$null; gitignore/CLAUDE.md Out-File seeds) recorded on m7e as pre-existing, out of 3t1 scope.

comments.text:
<!-- BD-MCP-META: {"kind":"fix-reference","source":"devops-agent","fixed_in":"claude-workflow-plugin-m7e"} -->
FIX LANDED (uncommitted, awaiting QA) in claude-workflow-plugin-m7e — do not close until QA verifies. All three facets plus the folded-in jq-arg-order rider.

**Facet 1 + 2 (BOM / single-line JSON), BOTH write sites**: `$merged | Out-File -FilePath ... -Encoding UTF8 -NoNewline` replaced at the `.mcp.json` and `settings.json` merge sites with a single shared writer:
```powershell
function Write-LfFile {
    param([string]$FilePath, [string[]]$Lines)
    $utf8NoBom = New-Object System.Text.UTF8Encoding($false)
    [System.IO.File]::WriteAllText($FilePath, (($Lines -join "`n") + "`n"), $utf8NoBom)
}
```
jq's output arrives from `& jq` as an ARRAY of lines, so the `-join "`n"` restores exactly jq's multi-line shape (the `-NoNewline` concatenation is what flattened it), and UTF8Encoding($false) removes the 5.1 BOM. The same writer is used by the new `.claude/install-manifest` write, where LF is not cosmetic: install.sh reads the body with `awk -F'\t'` and `length($3) == 64`, so a CRLF body validates ZERO rows and silently degrades the next `-Mode 2` to the pre-v4.1 plain-copy Update.

**Facet 3 (2>$null under EAP=Stop)**: `Test-JsonSingleObject` now runs its jq probe under a FUNCTION-SCOPED `$ErrorActionPreference = 'Continue'` with `2>&1 | Out-Null` instead of `2>$null`. The scoped assignment reverts on return, so 'Stop' still governs everything else. The `$hadEffortEnv` probe named in the task description is fixed the same way, through a new `Get-JqScalar` helper — it runs BEFORE the validity gate, so on 5.1 a malformed settings.json crashed there first and the documented manual-review arm was unreachable. `Get-JqScalar` collects the full output and indexes it rather than using `Select-Object -First 1`, which stops the upstream pipeline and can leave `$LASTEXITCODE` stale.

**Rider (jq argument ORDER pinned file-to-file)**: packaging-parity.test.sh section 6j extracts the operand order from EACH installer's own invocation line and asserts "existing shipped" on both sides plus equality between them (`arg_role_order` maps `$SETTINGS_FILE`/`$SettingsFile` -> existing, `$SOURCE_SETTINGS`/`$SourceSettings` -> shipped; same for the .mcp.json pair). **META 10** swaps the ps1 operands in a copy and asserts the order flips to "shipped existing" and stops matching install.sh. Both call sites also carry a comment saying the operand order IS the union direction.

**Mechanical guards added (L1 section 6i/6j)**, each RED-proved:
- zero `Out-File` on a JSON/manifest write path (META 9 restores the exact pre-fix line -> 1, not 0);
- zero `-NoNewline` on those paths (same META);
- zero `jq ... 2>$null` anywhere in install.ps1 (RED-proved by restoring it);
- `Test-JsonSingleObject` carries the scoped 'Continue' and `2>&1`;
- the LF writer exists exactly once, uses WriteAllText + UTF8Encoding($false), and joins with `` `n `` (RED-proved by swapping in `[Environment]::NewLine`);
- both merge sites and the install-manifest write go through it.

**Validation caveat, unchanged**: this is EXPRESSION- and TEXT-level evidence. No PowerShell on the implementation host, so nothing here executed `install.ps1 -Mode 2` against a seeded operator config. `.github/workflows/windows-install.yml` remains dispatch-only and was not extended. The task's own "validation for the fix" line (execute on a Windows host / pwsh in CI) is still outstanding and is the reason to keep this open.

title: v4.1 U6: depth-3 migration gate check — PRE-CHECKED FAILING (2.1.219 published 2026-07-24, flip 3 days after 2.1.217; 30-day hold unmet). Execute deferral path: evidence + standing task + LESSONS entry + CHANGELOG deferred
close_reason: CLOSED, need-triggered — NOT deferred on a calendar. This retires the 2026-08-23 next-check date recorded in this task's earlier comment; do not treat that date as live. REASONING: depth-1 is not a limitation awaiting removal, it is itself an ENFORCEMENT MECHANISM. Because subagents cannot spawn subagents, an implementer structurally cannot procure its own review — the grader and reviewer spawns must come from the root, which is exactly the separation the gate's independence predicate exists to guarantee. Migrating to depth-3 would mean BUILDING a parent-role guard to restore, in software, a property the current platform default gives for free, in order to enable nesting no workflow in this plugin needs. That trade is backwards. The QA->grader relay is the only candidate edge, and it already works as a root-orchestrated relay (qa.md s6, orchestrator.md s5a), pinned by no-nested-spawn-instructions.test.sh. Standing task filed separately with the trigger stated as a condition rather than a date: raise the pin WHEN a concrete workflow requires nested spawn, not when a month elapses.

title: v4.1 U4 epic: vendored superpowers skills (pin 3dcbd5c, vendor/ reference docs, evidence-before-fix merge, LICENSE)
design:
## Scope decision (recorded 2026-07-30, task claude-workflow-plugin-kfe)

REDUCED from the original plan's five vendored skills to ONE vendored skill
plus a practice harvest. This decision previously lived only in the untracked
`docs/plans/v4.1-upgrade-wave.md`; that loss mode is one of this release's own
recorded lessons, so it is recorded here as the durable record.

### What is vendored

`brainstorming` ONLY, from `obra/superpowers` at pin
`3dcbd5c4b48e02263fbf4a3c01e3fe4f81d584d9` (MIT, Copyright (c) 2025 Jesse
Vincent). Lands at `.claude/vendor/superpowers/brainstorming/SKILL.md` with a
sibling `MANIFEST.md` and verbatim `LICENSE.upstream`.

### What is NOT vendored, and why

`writing-plans`, `test-driven-development`, `receiving-code-review`,
`systematic-debugging` are HARVESTED as practices into surfaces that already
exist, not vendored as files. The goal is that the plugin carries the best
practice from each source without importing five layers of ceremony. Each of
those four skills duplicates machinery the gates already enforce (TDD ->
`backend.md` TDD workflow + the Stop-hook test gate; receiving-code-review ->
the 5c/5d review relay and arbitration; systematic-debugging -> the
evidence-before-fix protocol; writing-plans -> orchestrator SS2/SS4a Beads
decomposition and the SPEC doc), and importing them wholesale would ship a
second, competing execution model alongside the plugin's own.

`systematic-debugging` specifically is MERGED into the existing
evidence-before-fix protocol rather than added beside it: one authoritative
debugging protocol, evidence-before-fix winning every conflict, with a
delimited byte-identical EBF-CORE region across the four carriers
(`qa.md`, `backend.md`, `frontend.md`, `devops.md`).

### Reference docs, NOT registered skills

The vendored tree lives under `.claude/vendor/`, not `.claude/skills/`.
Explicit `Read .claude/vendor/.../SKILL.md` instructions in agent prompts load
it exactly where it is wired; skill registration would surface it session-wide,
need frontmatter rewrites plus manifest entries plus a parity test, and would
not reach subagent prompts anyway. It also preserves "everything under
`.claude/skills/` is registered" as an exact invariant, and keeps
`platform-audit.test.sh`'s agents+commands+the-one-SKILL scan honest — a
registered second skill would silently escape that scan.

`.claude-plugin/plugin.json` `skills[]` therefore stays length 1, and that is
an assertion in `.claude/scripts/tests/vendored-skills.test.sh`.

### Do NOT install upstream from the marketplace

Upstream registers all 14 skills session-wide; 13 of them encode a competing
execution/approval model (user-approval gates, self-directed commits,
specialist-spawns-specialist relays that `no-nested-spawn-instructions.test.sh`
and the depth-1 spawn pin forbid).

### Also in scope for the epic

## FINDING — this task carries a `qa-approved` label that was NOT earned by any review of C5's work. Gate state left untouched; reporting, not fixing.

**What happened.** Comment 947 records:

```
QA-GATE APPROVED change_set_hash=9942b2bd... reviewed_by=none worktree=... at 2026-07-30T12:32:11Z:
Auto-approved: doc-only change-set detected (F1 fast path) — no reviewable source changed.
[review bypass: F1 doc-only fast path: no reviewable source changed]
```

That fired at **12:32:11Z — 22 seconds after the `IMPLEMENTER` record at 12:31:49Z**, i.e. at the
very start of this C5 session, over the change set C4 had left behind (`docs/plans/*.md`, all
`.md`, correctly classified doc-only). It also **closed the task**. The state I inherited on
spawn was `in_progress` / `[devops, qa-gate-entered, rubric-pending]`; the state now is
`closed` / `[devops, qa-approved]`, and **I did not close or approve it** — my only `bd update`
set `notes`.

**Why it matters.** C5's change set is NOT doc-only. It contains `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`,
which F1's own classifier treats as reviewable source — `verify-before-stop.sh:134-136` says so
in as many words: *".json/.yaml/.toml do NOT (they often influence behavior)"*. That file drives
the installer banner, the agent/skill/command registration and the MCP wiring. So Beads currently
reports a version bump plus a full release audit as approved by an F1 bypass with
`reviewed_by=none`.

**The gate itself is behaving correctly — measured, not assumed:**

| | value |
| --- | --- |
| hash bound by the F1 auto-approval | `9942b2bd2656804a57c7a95a41e8f10380f4fa820494917603771a604764322c` |
| hash of the current change set | `914ceeff413507cbf3d92d9b6290c727c303191da961ee778ae9891d7c3f7c73` |

They differ, so `verify-before-stop.sh` will emit `LABEL_WITHOUT_RECORD` and **re-block** rather
than release on the stale label — the same fail-closed direction this release's own UPGRADE NOTE
documents. And because `plugin.json` is reviewable source, **a second F1 auto-approval is not
possible**; the fast path cannot fire again over this change set.

**What I did NOT do, deliberately.** I did not remove `qa-approved`, did not reopen the task, did
not run `qa-gate.sh enter`, and did not approve. Removing or re-granting a gate label to tidy the
record is precisely the side channel `CLAUDE.md` forbids, and the stale-label-plus-moved-hash
state is the documented, recoverable one. The recovery is the standard three commands the block
reason prints (`enter` → `impact-report` → `approve`), run by a reviewer who is not me.

**Two things for the orchestrator to decide, both above a devops call:**

1. Whether the closed+`qa-approved` state should be corrected before the tag, so the release is
   not recorded as having shipped its version bump under a review bypass.
2. Whether F1 auto-approving *and closing* a task that is still actively being implemented is a
   defect worth its own follow-up. The trigger here was benign — an inherited doc-only change set
   at the moment of spawn — but the effect was to spend the task's approval on work that had not
   started yet. `wg6`'s UPGRADE NOTE already documents F1's doc-only fast path as auto-approving
   only WITH an active task; this session had one, so the guard held and the outcome was still
   wrong. Related in kind to `claude-workflow-plugin-dkp` (F1 doc-only fast path is blind to
   off-repo blast radius).

## Part 1: VERIFY the three original asks — ALL THREE PRESENT, no fix needed

Located by text in the current file. Coverage landed in 5297a8b (d2j.3) after gl6 was filed; gl6 was simply never closed. This task was gap-fill, exactly as the brief predicted.

1. **Model pin lives in `config.toml`, not the registration flag.** Covered in THREE places:
   - §4 registration table, the `codex -m <slug> mcp-server` fragment row: "**`-m` does not choose the model here** — in `mcp-server` mode the model comes from `~/.codex/config.toml`".
   - §5 point 2: "It does **not** select the model: verified live on codex-cli 0.145.0, `mcp-server` mode ignores the registration's `-m`, and a `-c model=…` override does not stick either. `config.toml` wins."
   - §7 subsection "The model pin lives in `config.toml`, not in the registration", fact 1.
2. **The 400 error text + fix.** §7 same subsection, fact 2 carries the verbatim string `400 invalid_request_error: The 'gpt-5.2-codex' model is not supported when using Codex with a ChatGPT account.` plus the observable symptom (exit 5, no artifact); fact 3 is the fix.
3. **How to verify the resolved model.** §7 fact 3 step 2: `codex doctor --json | jq -r '.checks["config.load"].details.model'`, with the `session_configured` event named as the definitive in-band check and doctor as the free version that does not start a session.

## Part 2: the six residual gaps — all fixed

1. **Revert procedure (was missing).** §7 fact 3 now uses a dated `$BAK` and gained a **Reverting** paragraph (`cp "$BAK" ~/.codex/config.toml` restores exact prior bytes, re-verify with step 2, `rm "$BAK"` when clean). §9 gained a full **step 3** that restores or hand-strips `~/.codex/config.toml`, plus the note that uninstalling the binary does NOT remove `~/.codex`.
2. **Model-update recipe was half-automated (the important one).** §5's snippet now writes the file that drives the RUN before touching the registration: resolve `$NEWEST` -> back up -> portable rewrite of the top-level `model` key -> `codex doctor` verify -> only then `claude mcp remove/add` -> re-probe. Explicit "running only the `claude mcp` half is how you end up in the mismatch state this paragraph is warning about."
3. **Two inconsistent config.toml examples.** Reconciled. §4 now shows the complete two-key file (`model` + `model_reasoning_effort`) at the point the operator first opens the file, with a warning box that effort-only leaves the model unpinned; §5's block is explicitly labelled "the same two-key file §4 already showed whole" and its `model` value became a placeholder so there is no competing literal.
4. **`gpt-5.6-sol` hardcoding: 11 -> 6.** Added a single "One slug, one source" statement at §4 that names the pin, its date, and where it comes from; six `<slug>` placeholders elsewhere. The 6 survivors are all load-bearing: the statement itself, the copy-pasteable registration command, §4's canonical config file, the dated catalog evidence, the dated resolver sample output, and the expected-output line in the §7 fix.
5. **Unpinned CLI surfaces.** New §5 subsection "If these commands or jq paths moved" — introspection ladder (`.schemaVersion`/`.codexVersion`, `.checks | keys`, `.details`, `.models[0] | keys`) plus two verified shape traps.
6. **Per-profile `model` key.** New §5 subsection "If you use Codex profiles" — see the contradiction below; the finding is stronger than the ask.

## Part 3: also added (this session's evidence)

New §7 subsection **"Exit 5 at the wall-clock cap"**: the verbatim driver line `[codex-review] codex tool call exceeded 300s wall-clock budget (or server exited); no artifact`; 8 of 9 cycles in the v4.1 wave (attributed to one maintainer's machine); automatic degradation to the Claude lane with the review still happening; the cap's home (`.claude/review-config` `timeout_seconds`, default 300); and `claude-workflow-plugin-xo8` as the tracked investigation. **No root cause claimed** — the doc states the size correlate explicitly does not hold (~103 KB succeeded, ~95 KB failed). Also cross-linked from the exit-5 troubleshooting row and the degradation table.

## CONTRADICTS THE TASK BRIEF — gap 6's premise is false on 0.145.0

The brief said: "Codex supports profiles ... add a note that a profile's `model` overrides the top-level one if the operator uses profiles." **On codex-cli 0.145.0 a profile cannot reach this lane at all**, so I documented the verified behaviour instead of the assumed one. Three findings, each reproduced in a sandboxed `CODEX_HOME` (the live `~/.codex` and the live registration were never mutated):

- `codex -p <name> mcp-server` **fails outright — the server never starts**: `Error: --profile only applies to runtime commands and \`codex mcp\`: \`codex\`, \`codex exec\`, \`codex review\`, \`codex resume\`, \`codex archive\`, \`codex delete\`, \`codex unarchive\`, \`codex fork\`, \`codex mcp\`, \`codex sandbox\`, and \`codex debug prompt-input\`.` `mcp-server` is not on that list. A `-p` in the registration therefore presents as `handshake-failed` with nothing visibly wrong at the `claude mcp get codex` level — this is now also called out in the `handshake-failed` troubleshooting row.
- A top-level `profile = "<name>"` selector key is a **hard config-load failure**: `legacy \`profile = "name"\` config is no longer supported; use \`--profile name\` with \`name.config.toml\` instead`. `codex doctor` reports `config could not be loaded` with `details: {}` — the lane dies with it.
- A legacy `[profiles.<name>]` **table parses without complaint and is inert** — the top-level `model` still wins and nothing warns you. Silent no-op, not an override.

Profiles on 0.145.0 are separate layered files (`$CODEX_HOME/<name>.config.toml` via `-p`), not `[profiles.x]` tables. Net effect: the doc's single-top-level-`model` model of the world is *correct*, and the note now defends it rather than qualifying it.

## Everything asserted was re-verified against the live binary

codex-cli 0.145.0 was on PATH, so no command in the diff is unverified. Confirmed working: both `codex debug models` jq paths (priority-head still resolves `gpt-5.6-sol`; `supported_reasoning_levels[].effort/.description` intact), `codex doctor --json`'s `.checks["config.load"].details.model` (report `schemaVersion: 1`), `claude mcp add/remove` flag syntax (read from `--help`, not executed), and the new config-rewrite recipe run verbatim in a sandbox — it preserves comments/tables/`model_reasoning_effort`, is idempotent, and `codex doctor` confirms the result.

Three unverifiable-by-inspection claims were hedged in the doc's own voice rather than asserted: the `CODEX_HOME`/`CODEX_MCP_MODEL` split-config seam is marked "read off the script rather than exercised end to end"; there is no local diagnostic for `model_reasoning_effort` (doctor does not expose it) and the doc says so; and the billing question for a turn killed mid-stream is explicitly left to the operator and OpenAI.

Two incidental verified details worth keeping: `details.model` reports the literal `<default>` (not `null`) when nothing is pinned — now used as the cheapest unpinned check in three places; and the §9 backup glob was loosened to `config.toml.bak*` so it still catches the plain `.bak` earlier revisions of this doc told operators to make, with a note that an unmatched glob is a hard error on zsh (verified: `zsh: no matches found`, rc=1).

- Change set: **`docs/CODEX_SETUP.md` only** (+239/-30). No code touched. No commit, no qa-gate approve/close, per brief.

QA-GATE BLOCKED at 2026-07-27T20:26:49Z: QA BLOCK — 1 HIGH + 2 MEDIUM + 2 LOW in the operator-facing commands that rewrite ~/.codex/config.toml. Everything else in the change verified correct (details in the qa-plan doc, v1). All findings reproduced in a sandboxed CODEX_HOME/HOME; live ~/.codex and live registration never mutated.

=== R1-F1 (HIGH) docs/CODEX_SETUP.md:280-284 — the backup can silently fail to exist while the config is destroyed, and the doc's own step-3 guard reports success ===

    CFG="$HOME/.codex/config.toml"
    BAK="$CFG.bak-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
    cp "$CFG" "$BAK"
    { printf 'model = "%s"\n' "$NEWEST"
      grep -v '^[[:space:]]*model[[:space:]]*=' "$BAK"; } > "$CFG"

`> "$CFG"` truncates the target BEFORE the group runs, and the group reads from $BAK, not $CFG. `cp` is unguarded. So whenever cp fails while $CFG itself stays writable, the config is rebuilt from a backup that does not exist.

REPRODUCED (~/.codex mode 500 — dir not writable, file writable; also reachable via ENOSPC/quota):
  115-byte config -> 22 bytes ("model = \"gpt-5.6-sol\"" only). model_reasoning_effort, network_access, [tools] and all comments gone. ZERO .bak files on disk.

Worst property: step 3 cannot catch it. `codex doctor ... .details.model` prints exactly $NEWEST, because the model pin IS correct — it is every OTHER key that is gone. The doc says "If this does not echo $NEWEST, stop and read the file" — it DOES echo it, so the operator proceeds to step 4 believing the sweep worked, with no backup to go back to. This is the same class this project graded HIGH on sibling task 36z this wave ("backup legs missing for the docs surface").

FIX (one line): guard the backup before the destructive filter, e.g.
    cp "$CFG" "$BAK" || { printf "backup failed - aborting\n" >&2; return 1; }
or safer still, build into a temp file and `mv` into place so $CFG is never truncated before the new content exists.

=== R1-F2 (MEDIUM) docs/CODEX_SETUP.md:277-279 — the comment claims [tables] are untouched; they are not ===

The comment promises the rewrite "replaces the top-level `model` key and leaves every other line — comments, [tables], your effort setting — untouched." `grep -v` is line-based and section-blind: it strips EVERY `model =` line in the file.

REPRODUCED: a config containing
    [profiles.legacy]
    model = "gpt-4.1-old"
lost that line silently (diff shows line 12 deleted). The rest of the claim IS accurate — model_reasoning_effort, model_provider, comments and other tables all survived.

The behaviour is arguably desirable (it implements the "hoist it to the top level" advice in your own new profiles subsection), so the cheapest fix is to correct the sentence rather than the pattern — say that it replaces every `model =` line in any table with a single top-level one, and that this is the hoist. What must not ship is a copy-pasteable destructive command whose adjacent comment tells the operator it will not touch something it does touch.

=== R1-F3 (MEDIUM) docs/CODEX_SETUP.md:185-191 — day-granularity backup + a false no-clobber claim ===

    cp ~/.codex/config.toml ~/.codex/config.toml.bak-$(date +%Y%m%d)
is introduced with "A dated suffix avoids clobbering an earlier one." It does not, within a day.

REPRODUCED: pristine backup made -> config edited -> §4 line re-run same day -> the only backup on disk now holds the EDITED content; the pristine pre-edit copy is unrecoverable.

This is the FIRST backup an operator makes (the pre-any-edit state) and the one §9's restore path leans on, so it is the most valuable one to preserve. §5 (:281) and §7 (:467) already use `%Y%m%d-%H%M%S`. Fix: use second granularity here too so all three backup legs agree.

=== R1-F4 (LOW) docs/CODEX_SETUP.md:438 — the one complete copy-pasteable command with a placeholder parses as two shell redirections ===

    claude mcp add --scope user codex -- "$(command -v codex)" -m <slug> mcp-server

The shell reads `<slug>` as `< slug` PLUS `>` whose target is the next word: `... -m < slug > mcp-server`.

REPRODUCED in zsh and bash — in a normal cwd it FAILS CLOSED ("no such file or directory: slug"; command not executed, no file created), which is why this is low and not high. But with a file named `slug` in the cwd, both shells execute `claude mcp add --scope user codex -- <path> -m` (model value AND the mcp-server subcommand both swallowed) and create a junk file named `mcp-server`.

This is the only one of the 12 placeholder occurrences sitting in a full command; the other 11 are prose, `#` comments, quoted TOML, or table fragments and are fine. Fix: `-m YOUR_SLUG` (or quote it) in that row only — keeping the literal slug in §4's runnable registration at :129 is correct and should stay.

=== R1-F5 (LOW) docs/CODEX_SETUP.md:332-333 — "Only `model` happens to be a bare word today" is inaccurate ===

Verified against 0.145.0: `.checks["config.load"].details` also exposes `cwd` and `CODEX_HOME` as bare words, and both resolve with dot syntax. The practical advice (use bracket-and-quote syntax) is correct and safe; only the parenthetical is wrong.

=== NOT findings — verified correct, do not change these ===
- All THREE original gl6 asks are genuinely present (L139/L255/L450; L458-460; L472+L486). The verify-and-close leg is satisfiable.
- The profile contradiction is CORRECT and understated: I reproduced all three facts verbatim AND found a fourth route you did not test — `-c profile=<name>` also hard-fails, so it is not a back door either. Control: plain `codex mcp-server` starts and exits 0 on stdin EOF.
- Exit-5 subsection is honest: 8-of-9 matches the tally recorded on gz3 this wave; p5n confirmed as the lone sol-codex success; xo8 data point 6 confirms 95,309 bytes failing below the ~103KB success; timeout_seconds=300 and the driver line match the scripts; no root cause claimed.
- Revert path restores byte-identically; tilde-in-assignment expands correctly in zsh and bash; rewrite is idempotent; §9 zsh-glob claim correct and its restore/rm lines are non-destructive with no backups present.
- Hardcoding 11 -> 6 verified; all six survivors load-bearing. No mismatch state from copy-pasting §4 in order. "No test asserts this doc text" verified.
- Suites re-run by QA: L1 26/26, L2 37/37 specs / 1567 assertions, lint rc=0, manifest OK, all 7 anchors resolve.

=== Process notes ===
1. The spawn brief's rubric set is WRONG: `bd show --json` reports issue_type=bug (header reads [BUG]), so per qa.md §6a the bugfix overlay APPLIES — default + devops + bugfix. Sibling gz3 recorded the same rule this wave. The next grading packet must include bugfix.md.
2. Review relay deliberately NOT initiated this cycle: lane is codex, but the change set must change, so a paid Sol turn now would be spent on a diff that will be rewritten and the request change_set_hash would go stale on the first edit. Deferred to the post-fix cycle, as is the rubric relay.
3. Suggested follow-up (not blocking): xo8's TITLE is stale ("2 of 3 reviews ... ~148KB x15 timed out") vs its own data point 6 (5-of-6) and the current 8-of-9.

<!-- BD-MCP-META: {"kind":"implementer-fix-note","source":"devops","review_iteration":1,"findings_addressed":5,"binary_verified":"codex-cli 0.145.0"} -->
DEVOPS FIX — QA review iteration 1: all 5 findings addressed + the systemic lesson applied doc-wide

Change set still `docs/CODEX_SETUP.md` only (now +335/-36). No commit, no qa-gate approve. The live `~/.codex` and the live registration were never mutated — re-confirmed after all testing: `config.toml` still 195 bytes / mtime Jul 26 21:57, content unchanged, no stray files in `~/.codex`, registration still `Args: -m gpt-5.6-sol mcp-server` / Connected.

## Reproduced before fixing (bug-typed task, so evidence first)

I did not take the findings on trust. Built a sandbox harness (`/tmp/gl6-harness/harness.sh`) that runs the recipe verbatim under each failure arm and reports bytes-before -> bytes-after plus backup count.

- **R1-F1 independently reproduced.** Old recipe, `~/.codex` mode 500: **204 bytes -> 22 bytes, `baks=0`**. Same on the `dir read-only, file writable` arm. QA measured 115 -> 22; mine is 204 -> 22 only because my fixture config is larger. Identical failure.
- **R1-F2 reproduced** — `diff` shows `model = "gpt-4.1-old"` deleted from `[profiles.legacy]`; everything else survived, exactly as QA described.
- **R1-F4 reproduced** in both shells. Clean cwd: fails closed (`no such file or directory: slug`). With a file named `slug` present: executes with mangled args **and creates a junk file named `mcp-server`** — confirmed by `ls`.
- **R1-F5 reproduced** against the binary: `.details.cwd` and `.details.CODEX_HOME` both resolve with dot syntax, so "only `model`" was wrong.

Root cause of F1, stated precisely: `> "$CFG"` is a redirection on the *group command*, so the shell truncates `$CFG` when it sets up the group — before `grep` inside the group reads `$BAK`. With `cp` unguarded, any failure that leaves `$CFG` writable but prevents backup creation (dir not writable, ENOSPC, quota) rebuilds the config from a file that does not exist. Evidence: the harness arms above, and `codex-review.sh`-style guard absence at the old lines 286-290.

## Per-finding fixes

**R1-F1 HIGH — fixed structurally, not just guarded.** §5 step 1 is now a `codex_pin_newest` function (a function so a failed step can `return` instead of falling through into the destructive part — loose lines in an interactive paste cannot do that, and `return` outside a function is itself an error). Four changes, each closing a different route to the same loss:
1. `cp -p "$cfg" "$bak" || { …; return 1; }` — the backup is checked.
2. The replacement is built into `mktemp "$cfg.new.XXXXXX"` and installed with `mv`. `$cfg` is never opened for writing until a complete replacement exists.
3. The temp file is created **beside** `config.toml`, not in `$TMPDIR`, so `mv` is a same-filesystem rename — all-or-nothing. Across filesystems `mv` degrades to copy-then-unlink, which opens the destination for writing and can leave it half-written; that would have reintroduced the same bug class through the back door. This is called out in the doc so a future editor does not "simplify" it into `$TMPDIR`.
4. A pre-install `diff` refuses to install if any non-`model` line moved.

Also handled: no `config.toml` (creates a fresh pin, no bogus backup), no `~/.codex` (refuses, creates nothing), unresolvable slug (refuses before touching anything).

**How the verification now detects a wiped config — the actual lesson.** The verification block (now step 2; QA's "step 3" in the old numbering) asks **two independent questions**:
- (a) `codex doctor … .details.model` — is the pin right?
- (b) `diff <(grep -v '^[[:space:]]*model[[:space:]]*=' "$BAK") <(grep -v … "$CFG")` — is the rest of the file still there?

Demonstrated rather than asserted. Against a deliberately wiped config (reduced to just the new `model` line, i.e. the exact R1-F1 end state):
```
pin check says: gpt-5.6-sol            <- cannot see the wipe, reports success
diff check: FAILED as intended - the wipe IS detected
```
That is the whole point: (a) provably cannot see this failure and (b) can. The prose says so explicitly, so the next editor does not delete (b) as redundant. The no-backup case prints `NO BACKUP ON DISK — fine if you had no config before, alarming otherwise` rather than a confusing `diff` error.

Bonus from restructuring: step 3 now derives `NEWEST` from the **resolved config** (`codex doctor`) rather than from a shell variable, so the RECORD side is read out of the RUN side and the two structurally cannot disagree. It also fixed a scope bug I introduced mid-edit (`newest` became `local`, so the old `$NEWEST` in the registration line would have been empty).

**R1-F2 MEDIUM — sentence fixed, pattern kept**, per QA's and my agreement that the behaviour is desirable. The comment now says it removes *every* `model =` line **including one inside a `[table]`**, writes a single top-level `model`, and that a pin living in `[profiles.…]` is thereby **hoisted to the top level — which is the fix the profiles subsection recommends anyway**. Verified the hoisted output still loads in the real binary: `status:ok, parse:ok, model:gpt-5.6-sol`, and it also passes `--strict-config`, even with the now-empty `[profiles.legacy]` table left behind.

**R1-F3 MEDIUM — fixed.** §4 now uses `%Y%m%d-%H%M%S` (all three backup legs agree), and the false no-clobber claim is replaced with the reason: "a same-day re-run of a day-stamped command overwrites the pristine copy with an already-edited one". Also added `cp -p … && ls -l … || echo "NO BACKUP — fix that before editing anything"`, because "a `cp` whose failure you did not read is indistinguishable from a backup you never made". `-p` keeps the source's mode — verified the backup lands `-rw-------`, not world-readable.

**R1-F4 LOW — fixed in that row only**, as QA scoped it: `-m YOUR_SLUG`. The §4 "One slug, one source" box now explains the convention and why (`<slug>` in a pasteable command is read as `< slug` plus `>`), so the inconsistency with the 6 remaining prose/fragment `<slug>`s is deliberate and documented rather than sloppy. §4's runnable registration keeps the literal slug, per QA.

**R1-F5 LOW — corrected and expanded.** Re-derived from the binary: 8 of the 12 `details` keys contain spaces; one more (`"config.toml"`) contains a **dot**, which dot syntax also cannot reach because `jq` reads it as two keys — a third category neither QA nor I had named. Only `model`, `cwd`, `CODEX_HOME` are plain enough for `.details.foo`. The bullet now says use bracket syntax throughout rather than remembering which category a key is in.

**Non-blocking tension you flagged — fixed.** §7 step 2's expected output no longer contradicts step 1: the edit line reads `model = "SOME_SLUG_YOUR_ACCOUNT_SUPPORTS"` (with a parenthetical noting this doc's own pin is `gpt-5.6-sol`, "yours depends on your account") and the expected output reads `# -> the slug you just set`.

## The lesson applied to every other recipe in the doc, not just §5

Per your instruction. Each of these was a guard-or-verify gap of the same shape:

- **§4 backup** — guarded + confirmed (above).
- **§7 fix recipe** — `cp -p … && ls -l "$BAK" || echo "NO BACKUP — do not edit yet"`, and step 2 gained `diff "$BAK" ~/.codex/config.toml # expect: only the model line differs`, because "a correct `model` line in an otherwise mangled file passes the first check and fails the lane".
- **§9 restore** — this had its own latent footgun that no finding named: it auto-restored `$(ls -t … | head -1)`, i.e. the *newest* backup, which after any edit is the edited one, not the pre-lane one. Worse, I had paired `ls -t` with `cp -p`, and `-p` preserves the source mtime, so `-t` ordering no longer means creation order at all. Now: list with `ls -l`, **name the file you want** (the dated suffix *is* the creation time; the earliest is your pre-lane state and "newest is usually the wrong choice here, which is why this is not automated"), a safety copy of the current file first with a load-bearing `&&` so no restore can happen without it, and a `diff` against that safety copy before the final `rm`.

Verified separately that `cp` with a missing source does **not** truncate its destination (18-byte dest intact), so §9's placeholder filename fails closed for an operator who pastes it without substituting.

## Sandbox arms run — all against the doc's real bytes

`/tmp/gl6-harness/verify-doc.sh` extracts `codex_pin_newest` **verbatim from `docs/CODEX_SETUP.md`** (awk on the code block, indent-stripped) rather than from a copy I might have drifted from, syntax-checks it, then runs the arms in a sandboxed `HOME` with a stub `codex`.

| arm | old recipe | new recipe |
| --- | --- | --- |
| control (all writable) | SAFE (rewritten) | SAFE (rewritten) |
| `~/.codex` mode 500 | **DATALOSS 204->22, baks=0** | SAFE (bytes intact, aborts) |
| config mode 000 | SAFE | SAFE (bytes intact, aborts) |
| dir read-only, file writable | **DATALOSS 204->22, baks=0** | SAFE (bytes intact, aborts) |
| config read-only (444) | n/a | SAFE (rewritten) |
| no `config.toml` | truncate-created a 22-byte file | SAFE (fresh pin, no bogus backup) |
| no `~/.codex` at all | **DATALOSS (dest gone)** | SAFE (aborts, creates nothing) |

**old: SAFE=4 / UNSAFE=2 -> new: SAFE=7 / UNSAFE=0.** No arm leaves a stray `config.toml.new.*` behind (checked explicitly). Idempotent: second run byte-identical. The extracted function is valid in **both bash and zsh** (`bash -n` + `zsh -n`).

I also fixed two wrong *expectations* in my own harness mid-run rather than let them pass — the "no config" and "no ~/.codex" arms were originally asserted against the wrong end state, which would have made the test lie in both directions.

## Doc-wide checks

- **All 17 `bash` blocks in the doc extracted and syntax-checked in bash AND zsh — all valid.** No remaining `<placeholder>` on a non-comment line inside any block (the one hit is `# -> <default> if unpinned`, expected *output* inside a trailing comment).
- 48 fence lines, balanced. All 7 internal anchors still resolve. `gpt-5.6-sol` still 6, all load-bearing. No PII/personal paths in the diff.
- **L1 `make test` 26/26 PASS. L2 `make test-component` 37/37 specs / 1567 assertions PASS. `make lint` rc=0. `make manifest-validate` OK.**

## R2-F1 reproduced, then fixed — with one extra wrinkle QA's fix would have left

Reproduced first. With `config.toml.bak-20260726-215700`, `config.toml.bak-20260728-010000` and `config.toml.bak-d2j2` all present, `ls -1 "$CFG".bak-* | tail -1` selects **`config.toml.bak-d2j2`**. Also confirmed `.bak-old`, `.bak-orig`, `.bak-keep`, `.bak-tmp` each win over every dated backup, for the reason given: digits sort before letters, so any letter-initial suffix sorts last.

The suggested `[0-9]*` is right and I took it, but on its own it introduces a cosmetic regression I caught while testing: **`2>/dev/null` does not suppress a zsh glob failure**, because zsh fails the glob *before* `ls` runs, so the error is the shell's, not `ls`'s, and the redirection on `ls` never sees it. On a machine with only non-dated backups, an operator on macOS/zsh would get

```
zsh:1: no matches found: /Users/…/.codex/config.toml.bak-[0-9]*
```

printed in the middle of the section that is teaching them to trust these checks. `$BAK` still ends up empty and the guarded branch still prints the right message, so it is noise rather than a defect — but noise exactly where credibility matters. Shipped line:

```bash
BAK=$( { ls -1 "$CFG".bak-[0-9]*; } 2>/dev/null | tail -1 )
```

The brace group puts the glob failure *inside* the redirected scope. Verified silent and correct in **both** bash and zsh, with and without dated backups present. (I also tested a `find -maxdepth 1 -name … | sort | tail -1` variant, which is equally correct and silent, and rejected it as less readable for an operator doc.) The comment is now true and says why, including the digits-before-letters reason, so the next editor does not "simplify" it back to `.bak-*`.

## Sweep result: yes, a third instance — and it fires on this machine today

Classified every backup glob in the doc by whether it **selects** (must be narrow) or **lists** (should be broad).

**THIRD INSTANCE — §9 cleanup, `rm -f ~/.codex/config.toml.bak*`.** Same class, different axis: not ordering but *breadth*. That glob deletes every `config.toml.bak…` file, including ones this doc never created. On this very machine it would have deleted `config.toml.bak-d2j2` — a file from task d2j.2 that the operator made for their own reasons — and `.bak-old` / `.bak-my-important-config` fare identically. A cleanup step should delete what the doc created and let the operator judge the rest. Now:

```bash
rm -f ~/.codex/config.toml.bak-[0-9]* ~/.codex/config.toml.before-restore
ls -l ~/.codex/config.toml.bak* 2>/dev/null   # anything still listed is yours to judge
```

Verified in a sandbox: dated backups and `before-restore` are removed; `.bak-d2j2` and `.bak-my-precious` survive and get listed.

**FOURTH (minor) — §4's confirmation glob.** `cp … && ls -l ~/.codex/config.toml.bak-*` listed *all* backups to confirm the one it had just written, so with `.bak-d2j2` present the operator could read reassurance off an unrelated file. Tightened to the §7 shape — `BAK=…; cp -p … "$BAK" && ls -l "$BAK" || echo …` — which confirms the single file it wrote and removes a glob entirely. Prose says why.

Also tightened §5's prose from "delete the backup" to `rm "$BAK"` — "named, not globbed, so you cannot take a hand-made backup with it" — since an unspecified instruction invites the operator to improvise the very glob we just removed.

**Final classification, deliberate and documented:** four *selections*, all narrow or explicit (§4 `"$BAK"`, §5 step 2 `bak-[0-9]*`, §7 `"$BAK"`, §9 rm `bak-[0-9]*`); two *listings*, deliberately loose because showing everything is the point (§9's inventory and the post-cleanup leftover review), each with a comment saying it is a listing and not a selection. No `ls -t` and no `| head -1` auto-pick survives anywhere — the §9 footgun from R1 is gone and did not come back in another guise.

## On the `[ -d "${cfg%/*}" ]` guard: QA's dead-code observation does not reproduce here

Tested directly on codex-cli 0.145.0, both routes:

- `CODEX_HOME=<absent dir> codex debug models` — dir still **ABSENT** afterwards.
- `env -u CODEX_HOME HOME=<sandbox with no .codex> codex debug models` — `.codex` still **ABSENT** afterwards, rc=0, and it still resolved `gpt-5.6-sol`.

So on this binary the guard is reachable, not dead. Rather than assert QA is wrong on a side-effect claim that may well be version- or path-dependent, I made the question moot: **the guard now runs before the catalog call.** That makes it live regardless of whose observation holds, and it fails faster (no catalog fetch when there is no `~/.codex`). Proved it with a deliberately hostile stub `codex` that *does* `mkdir -p "$HOME/.codex"` on every invocation — modelling QA's belief — and the guard still fires, rc=1, creating nothing. The comment records the ordering rationale so it is not reshuffled later.

`/tmp/gl6-harness/verify-r2.sh` — extracts the changed lines **verbatim from the doc** (`grep -F` on the shipped text, awk on the function block) rather than from a copy: **PASS=8 FAIL=0**.

first (`no …/.codex — run codex login first`), **the catalog is never called**, and
nothing is created.

## Two corrections to the implementer's claims (neither is a finding)

1. **Their non-reproduction of my dead-code note is half wrong — via the route the
   code actually takes, I was right.** Measured on 0.145.0:
   - `CODEX_HOME=<absent>`: dir NOT created, and the slug does **not** resolve (empty).
   - `HOME=<sandbox>` (so CODEX_HOME defaults to `$HOME/.codex`): slug resolves
     `gpt-5.6-sol` **and `~/.codex` IS created**.

   The function uses `$HOME/.codex`, i.e. the second route, so the directory was
   being recreated as I read it. **This has no consequence for the shipped doc**,
   because their comment does not assert the side-effect either way — it says the
   ordering "holds regardless of whether some future `codex` subcommand creates the
   directory as a side effect of running." That is the correct way to write it, and
   arm F's changed verdict is the observable proof the reorder mattered.
2. Minor: their note says the old selection form's zsh error appears "on a macOS
   machine with only non-dated backups". Confirmed — and it also appears on any
   machine with **no** backups at all, which is the more common first-run state.

The HIGH fix, the verify-and-close leg (all three original asks), the profile
contradiction (including the `-c profile=` fourth route I added), the exit-5
subsection, F2-F5, and the 11->6 hardcoding reduction are unchanged from where I
verified each against the live binary and the durable record in v1/v2.

## Doc-wide + suites (re-run by QA)
- 48 fence lines balanced; **17 bash blocks, 0 invalid in bash, 0 invalid in zsh**;
  7 anchors resolve; `gpt-5.6-sol` still exactly 6; 0 PII matches.
- L1 `make test` **26/26 PASS**. L2 / lint / manifest: see the closing comment.
- Live `~/.codex/config.toml` **byte-identical to my v2 record** (195 bytes, mtime
  2026-07-26 21:57:53, sha256 `14afff5cbaf3246a4035…`); `config.toml.bak-d2j2` present
  and untouched; registration args still `["-m","gpt-5.6-sol","mcp-server"]`.

## The label mechanism — REPRODUCED, evidence filed on l1r.3

Neither QA nor the implementer forgot to clear `qa-blocked`. The removal **works** and
is then **silently reverted**:
- `bd label remove … qa-blocked` -> `✓ Removed label …`, rc=0; DB (`bd show` and
  direct `sqlite3`) reflects the removal.
- `.beads/issues.jsonl` still lists `qa-blocked`, frozen at an older `updated_at`.
- `bd label remove` does not bump `updated_at` and does not flush; a following
  `bd update --notes` did not flush either (DB advanced, JSONL did not).
- SQLite is in **WAL** mode and the mtimes are the tell: `beads.db` 01:35:16 (stale),
  `beads.db-wal` 01:40:01 (real writes), `issues.jsonl` 01:35:16.
- bd's help documents `--no-auto-flush` ("automatic JSONL sync after CRUD") and
  `--no-auto-import` ("automatic JSONL import when newer than DB").

Root cause: the removal lands in the WAL and is not flushed; because `beads.db`'s
mtime does not advance while writes sit in the WAL, any later touch of the
git-tracked `issues.jsonl` makes it look newer than the DB and the pre-removal label
set is replayed over the newer state. Full write-up with the observed/inferred split
and a reproduction skeleton is on **`claude-workflow-plugin-l1r.3`**. The gate
contract was never at risk — this is fail-closed noise (a stale blocking label), not
a fail-open release.

DEVOPS FIX — all five R3 HIGH findings reproduced, fixed, and resolved

Change set still `docs/CODEX_SETUP.md` only (+486/-41). No commit, no approve. Five `resolve-finding` records posted (R3-F1…R3-F5), each citing real `--fix` line ranges and real `--test` arm names. Live `~/.codex/config.toml` unchanged throughout — 195 B, mtime Jul 26 21:57, sha256 `14afff5cbaf3246a4035…` (matches QA's v2/v3 record), `config.toml.bak-d2j2` present and untouched; registration unchanged.

Sol is right on all five, and the set-reading is right too: three of them share the root cause that **the validation was a mirror of the mutation**. Per-finding detail is in the five resolve-finding comments; below is what the set taught and what the reproductions turned up that the findings did not predict.

## Reproductions (`/tmp/gl6-harness/repro-r3.sh`), all against the pre-fix bytes

- **F1** — `bak-[0-9]*` matched `bak-20260728-personal` and `bak-9-keep`; the selection picked **`bak-9-keep`** over the real dated backup, and both operator files were in the irreversible `rm` kill list. Sol's reading of glob semantics is exactly right and both QA and I had reasoned about this pattern and got it wrong.
- **F2a** — with an unreadable input, the build group exited **0** because of the trailing `:`, leaving a model-line-only candidate. Without the `:`, status 2 propagates.
- **F2b** — with `grep` stubbed to exit 127, the mirror validation compared a 5-line baseline against a 1-line wiped candidate and reported **IDENTICAL (would install)**.
- **F3** — a `notes = """…"""` block containing a `model =` line: the filter deleted that line from inside the string, the original parsed fine (`status=ok`), and the mirror validation reported **IDENTICAL**.
- **F5** — `jq -r` returned the 4-character string `null` for both an empty catalog and a catalog entry lacking `.slug`; `[ -n ]` accepts it; step 3 would have propagated `-m null`.

**F4 needed two attempts and corrected my own framing.** A 60 MB kill test was inconclusive — macOS `cp` clones instantly on APFS. A FIFO source forced a streaming copy and gave a deterministic result, which was *not* what I assumed: `cp` does **not** truncate the destination up front on macOS (it still read 34 bytes while `cp` blocked on the fifo), but a short source left the destination holding **7 bytes of partial content while `cp` exited 0**. Silently truncated config, success code. That is worse than the O_TRUNC story I started with, and the doc now states the measured behaviour rather than my theory.

## What the set taught, and how the fix reflects it

The unifying error was building the oracle out of the same expression as the mutation. Two runs of one filter agree even when the filter is broken. So the filter now runs **once** into a baseline file whose `grep` status is explicitly checked (accepting exit 1 — legitimately "a config of nothing but `model =` lines" — and rejecting 2+), the candidate is built from that baseline, and validation splits into two questions that fail independently:

- **CHECK 1** compares the candidate against the baseline artifact actually written, with `cmp`, status visible, no process substitution. Catches a truncated or partial build.
- **CHECK 2** asks the **real TOML parser** — `codex --strict-config doctor` against a throwaway `CODEX_HOME`. The only check here that understands TOML rather than lines.

And the operator-facing step 2 stopped filtering altogether: it is now a **raw** `diff` of backup against config, filter-free by construction, which is both safer and easier to read.

Three corrections I made to my own or Sol's framing rather than shipping them unexamined:

1. **`--strict-config` is a top-level flag.** `codex doctor --strict-config` errors with `unexpected argument`; it must be `codex --strict-config doctor`. I hit this while implementing and documented it inline. Sol's brief said the doc "already uses `codex doctor --strict-config` … for exactly this purpose" — it did not; the flag appeared nowhere in the doc before this change, so this introduces it, with the correct placement.
2. **I could not substantiate my first draft of the independence claim.** I wrote that a broken table header "passes CHECK 1 and is caught only by the parser", then tested it end-to-end and found the function actually aborts earlier with `catalog gave no usable slug`, because `codex debug models` cannot load a broken config either. The paragraph now says what I measured: a wiped candidate **passes** the parser (so CHECK 1 is the only thing catching content loss), a broken header **is** refused by the parser while CHECK 1 would wave it through, and the parser check is honestly labelled defence-in-depth that is usually pre-empted by the catalog step. Keeping it is still right — it is the only TOML-aware check and it does not depend on a future `codex debug models` reading your config.
3. **F3 is fixed by prevention, not detection.** No oracle built from a line filter can attribute damage inside a multiline string, so the function refuses when the config contains either delimiter form and defers to a hand edit — verified refusal and byte-intactness for `"""` and `'''`. Placed before the catalog call so it costs nothing.

## Sweep results for the two classes Sol named

**`[0-9]*`-believed-to-mean-dated:** exactly one use survives (§9's irreversible `rm`) and it is now the literal 8-digit/dash/6-digit stamp, verified in bash **and** zsh. The §5 selection site was removed rather than fixed — the function exports `CODEX_PIN_BAK` and step 2 names it, because the safest selection is no selection. `grep` confirms no bare `bak-[0-9]*` is *used* anywhere; the single remaining occurrence is the comment citing it as wrong. A note on a rejected alternative: holding the digit class in a `$STAMP` variable **does not work in zsh**, which does not glob-expand the result of parameter expansion — so the pattern is written out literally at the one place it is needed.

**`jq -r` null trap:** every site audited. Values that flow into a command or file are guarded with `// empty` plus a shape check (`''|null|'<default>'` rejected, non-slug characters rejected). Values a human reads got `// empty` so "missing" reads blank rather than as a plausible value named `null`. The four lines in the paths-moved introspection block deliberately keep bare `null` — there a printed `null` is the answer you came for — and the doc now says so explicitly, with a warning to add `// empty` if you copy one of those lines into something that consumes the value.

## Verification

- `/tmp/gl6-harness/verify-r3.sh` — one arm per finding plus the old constructs as **live controls**, extracted verbatim from the doc: **PASS=29 FAIL=0**. Every control still reproduces its bug, so the arms are proven sensitive rather than vacuous.
- `/tmp/gl6-harness/verify-doc.sh` — the original 7-arm safety suite, re-run against the rewritten function (99 lines, clean under `bash -n` and `zsh -n`): **7 arms / 0 UNSAFE**, idempotent, and the two-question verification still catches F1's wipe state. Its stub needed updating to tolerate the new top-level `--strict-config`.
- Real-binary end-to-end on a healthy config: pin installed, all non-model content preserved, zero stray temps, `codex doctor` confirms `gpt-5.6-sol`.
- Doc-wide: **19** bash blocks, all valid in bash and zsh; 52 fence lines balanced; all anchors resolve; no PII.
- **L1 26/26 PASS. L2 37/37 specs / 1567 assertions PASS. `make lint` rc=0.**

One process note: `qa-gate.sh resolve-finding` rejected my R3-F3 invocation on a shell-quoting conflict with the triple-quote delimiters in the summary text; worked around by building the arguments in variables. Not a defect in the script, but worth knowing if a future finding summary needs to quote TOML delimiters.

The harness (`repro-r3.sh`, `verify-r3.sh`, `verify-doc.sh`, `verify-r2.sh`, `harness.sh`) remains uncommitted per the doc-only scope. `repro-r3.sh` and `verify-r3.sh` are the two worth salvaging for `claude-workflow-plugin-dkp`: between them they cover glob-breadth, filter-status propagation, mirror-oracle tautology, TOML-semantic damage, partial-write atomicity, and the `jq null` trap — six failure classes whose blast radius is the operator's home directory and which no in-repo test can currently see.

<!-- BD-MCP-DOC: qa-plan v4 -->
# QA review — claude-workflow-plugin-gl6 — v4 (review iteration 4: Sol's five HIGH resolutions verified)

Supersedes v3. **All five R3 HIGH resolutions verified against the current bytes with
my own arms.** Zero findings at or above the `high` threshold. Three non-blocking
LOW/INFO observations below. Returning `RUBRIC-RELAY`.

## First: my own miss, on the record

Sol found five HIGH findings on bytes I had cleared with "zero open findings" in v3 —
and **R3-F2/F3 is the tautology I predicted in v2 and then cleared on a bad test.** My
v2 note read: *"I predicted it was tautological (both sides derive from `$bak` through
the same filter, so it could only catch I/O corruption). It also catches injection
through the slug… stronger than I expected."* The error is visible in that sentence: I
tested the oracle with a **working** `grep`, and a mirror oracle is indistinguishable
from an independent one until the filter itself is broken. The correct test — the one I
ran this round — is to stub `grep` to fail and see whether the check still speaks. That
is the generalisable lesson, and it is why this round's centrepiece is a coverage
matrix rather than a pass/fail.

## Gate state
- Impact report regenerated: `server=code-graph`, files=6,
  `change_set_hash=6dde6bdf7b085d2f53703be3510317e916bd7e41c5373df1e0598d8218c3e414`,
  verified equal to `impact-report.sh --hash-only` after all activity including packet staging.
- `review-check.sh gate` -> `{"ok":true,"independent":true,"open_findings":0,"reviewer_identity":"sol-codex"}`.
  Sol's `REVIEW-ARTIFACT v1 iteration=3` is bound to hash `56758d90…` (the bytes it
  reviewed) and all five findings carry `RESOLVED` records with real `fix=`/`test=` refs.
- `qa-blocked` cleared by QA for the **third** time; the DB/JSONL divergence reproduced
  again (DB 4 labels, JSONL 5) — more confirmation for `l1r.3`.
- Grading packet staged: `.claude/.qa-tracking/grading-packet-gl6/` (~204 KB, 8 items),
  manifest in the `grading-packet` doc.

## Verification method
Extracted `codex_pin_newest` **verbatim from the current doc bytes** via awk:
**103 lines**, sha256 `25703fc2e9616839…`, clean under `bash -n` and `zsh -n`.
7 arms, **0 UNSAFE, 0 stray temps** (control, dir 500, file 000, file 444, no config,
no `~/.codex`, dir 555).

## The weighted question: are the two checks genuinely independent?

**Yes — measured, with a reachable case on each side.** I broke each mechanism
separately instead of trusting a happy-path run.

| Candidate | Reachable? | CHECK 1 (`cmp` vs baseline) | CHECK 2 (real TOML parser) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| healthy | yes | PASS | PASS |
| wiped — model line only | yes (stub `cat` to emit nothing) | **FAIL — catches** | PASS (blind) |
| top-level quoted-key duplicate | **yes** (real config, see below) | PASS (blind) | **FAIL — catches** |

- Broken-`grep` stub (exit 127): `filter failed (grep exit 127) — aborting`, config
  intact, 0 strays. The R3-F2 status-propagation fix works.
- Wiped candidate (working `grep`, stubbed `cat`): `candidate does not match the
  baseline — aborting`. CHECK 1 catches what the parser provably cannot.
- **The reachable parser-only case, which the implementer could not find.** A config of
  `"model" = "gpt-5.2-codex"` + `network_access = true`:
  - the ORIGINAL is valid and loadable (`status:ok model=gpt-5.2-codex`) and
    `codex debug models` resolves `gpt-5.6-sol` with it, so **the function does not
    abort at the catalog step** — this is the reachability the implementer's own hedge
    was missing;
  - the filter matches **0** lines (a quoted key is not `^model[[:space:]]*=`), so the
    candidate carries both `model = …` and `"model" = …` — a duplicate key;
  - CHECK 1 passes (candidate matches the baseline by construction);
  - the parser refuses: `parser rejected the candidate (resolved 'nothing')`, config intact.

  So the doc's "neither subsumes the other" is **empirically true in both directions**,
  and the parser check is load-bearing rather than merely defence-in-depth. My evidence
  strengthens the doc's claim; see LOW-2 for the wording nit.

## The weighted question: is §9's surviving `[0-9]*` really strict?

Yes, and identically in **bash and zsh**. The pattern is fully literal
(`bak-[0-9]x8-[0-9]x6`, no trailing wildcard, so it must match the whole name).
Removed: `bak-20260726-215700`, `bak-20260728-010000`, `before-restore`.
**Survived:** `bak-20260728-personal` and `bak-9-keep` (Sol's counterexamples),
`bak-d2j2`, `bak-my-precious`, plain `bak`, `bak-2026`, and the off-by-one stamps
`bak-20260728-01000` (5-digit) and `bak-20260728-0100000` (7-digit). No operator file
can match unless it is exactly an 8-6 stamp.

## The weighted question: does the F3 prevention path fail closed?

Yes, on **both** delimiter forms and **before** the catalog call. With a stub `codex`
that marks a file when invoked: for `"""` and for `'''` alike the function prints
`… contains a multiline string — edit it by hand, not with this`, the config is intact,
and **the catalog is never called**. Prevention rather than detection is the right
choice here — no line-oriented oracle can attribute damage inside a multiline string.

## The other two resolutions

- **R3-F5 (jq null / shape):** all four hostile catalog payloads abort with the config
  intact — empty `models` array and missing `slug` both give `catalog gave no usable
  slug`; the literal string `null` is rejected by the explicit case arm; a
  shell-metacharacter slug gives `implausible slug 'evil; rm -rf /'`. Swept the doc:
  every `jq -r` whose value flows into an action carries `// empty` (the two apparent
  gaps are continuation lines that do), and the four deliberately-bare introspection
  lines are documented with a rationale that even warns against copying them.
- **R3-F4 (atomic restore):** their FIFO finding reproduced **exactly** — direct `cp`
  from a short source exits **0** while leaving the destination holding 7 bytes of
  partial content, original lost. And the value of the fix demonstrated: with a copy
  killed mid-stream, direct `cp` leaves `dest=[AAAA]` (original gone) while
  temp+rename leaves the original intact. All three restore sites (§5 :464, §7 :685,
  §9 :818) are temp+rename behind `&&`, and §9's chains behind its safety copy.
- **`CODEX_PIN_BAK`** is deliberately not in the `local` list, so it survives into the
  caller — verified. The else-branch for "the function did not run in THIS shell"
  refuses to auto-select and tells the operator to read the name off `ls -l` and diff
  by hand: the safest selection is no selection, applied consistently.

## Three non-blocking observations (all LOW/INFO, none at/above `high`)

1. **LOW-1 — step 2's expected output is understated.** The doc says "Expect exactly
   two lines of output: the new `model = …` added at the top and the old one removed."
   A raw `diff` actually prints **four** lines — `0a1`, `> model = "gpt-5.6-sol"`,
   `2d2`, `< model = "gpt-5.2-codex"`. Two of those are the content lines described;
   the other two are diff's range markers. Since the next sentence is "Anything more
   means something else moved", an operator counting lines can false-alarm on a healthy
   sweep. Fix: say "two changed lines (plus diff's range markers)", or show the
   expected four-line block verbatim.
2. **LOW-2 — the parser-only example in the closing paragraph is the unreachable one.**
   It cites "a candidate with a broken table header", which per the implementer's own
   testing aborts earlier at the catalog step and so cannot arise through this
   function. My top-level quoted-key duplicate IS reachable and produces exactly the
   asymmetry the paragraph is arguing for. Swapping the example would make the claim
   demonstrable instead of illustrative. The paragraph's conclusion is correct either
   way — this is a strengthening, not a correction.
3. **INFO — a killed restore leaves an orphan temp.** `config.toml.restore.XXXXXX`
   remains in `~/.codex` if a restore is interrupted (observed in the F4b arm), and
   §9's cleanup line removes only the dated stamps and `before-restore`. Inert and
   rare, but this doc otherwise cares about exactly this ("how `~/.codex` fills with
   files you can no longer tell apart"). The function's own abort paths do clean up
   (`strays=0` on every arm) — it is only the operator-facing one-liners.
4. **INFO — the multiline guard is the one guard that fails OPEN.**
   `[ -e "$cfg" ] && grep -qe '"""' …` treats a broken `grep` (exit 127) as "no
   multiline string" and proceeds. No damage results, because the later
   filter-status check aborts on the same broken `grep` (verified). Worth knowing if
   that later check is ever refactored away.

## Doc-wide + suites (re-run by QA)
- 52 fence lines balanced; **19 bash blocks, 0 invalid in bash, 0 invalid in zsh**;
  7 anchors resolve; `gpt-5.6-sol` still exactly 6; 0 PII matches.
- Residual-construct sweep: **0** `ls -t`, **0** `head -1` auto-picks, **0** process
  substitutions inside a validation compare.
- L1 **26/26 PASS**; L2 **37/37 specs / 1567 assertions PASS**; `make lint` **rc=0**;
  `make manifest-validate` **rc=0**.
- Live `~/.codex/config.toml` **byte-identical across all four QA rounds** (195 bytes,
  mtime 2026-07-26 21:57:53, sha256 `14afff5cbaf3246a4035…`); `config.toml.bak-d2j2`
  untouched; registration args unchanged; **0** stray temps in the live `~/.codex`.

## Next
Returning `qa_status: needs-grading` (RUBRIC-RELAY), rubric iteration 1, rubric set
**default + devops + bugfix** (`issue_type=bug`), `iteration_cap=3`. Packet staged and
manifested. On `satisfied` I approve at hash `6dde6bdf…`, clearing `qa-blocked`
explicitly as on 36z.
