title: bd-compat's version range excludes the host's bd 1.2.1, so the spec fails on this machine and passes in the pinned container
description:
Measured during mdnc round 1, 2026-08-14, and it RETIRES A CLAIM the orchestrator has repeated for three
phases.

  host      : bd 1.2.1  -> bd-compat.sh fails 1 assertion
  container : bd 1.1.2  -> bd-compat.sh passes 75/75

The spec records a version range; the host's bd is above it because bd self-upgraded mid-session
(1.1.2 -> 1.2.1, which re-added the 'sync' command). THIS IS AN ENVIRONMENT FACT, NOT A CODE DEFECT.

WHAT IT CORRECTS. Every bar this session was reported as having 'two expected pre-existing reds'
(installer-v3-upgrade and bd-compat). That framing was wrong: it is ONE code carry plus ONE host
artifact, and the second one disappears the moment the tier runs against the pinned version. The
orchestrator repeated the wrong framing in several briefs and in two commit messages.

NEEDS a decision rather than a patch: either widen the recorded range as bd releases (and accept the
spec chases upstream), or pin the host expectation to the same version CI pins and treat a divergence as
a loud environment error rather than a test failure. The second matches how the tier already handles
docker's absence - a named skip, never a silent green.

RELATED: claude-workflow-plugin-3yux filed this as a defect earlier in the arc; that framing should be
corrected there too.

DISCOVERED-FROM: claude-workflow-plugin-mdnc round 1.

title: lessons.test.sh and mutation-harness.test.sh shell out to python3 with no availability guard, so a runner without it FAILS instead of skipping
description:
FOUND BY: the first Linux container run of the L1 tier (claude-workflow-plugin-mdnc), on an
image that had not yet provisioned python3.

MEASURED:
  /repo/.claude/scripts/tests/lessons.test.sh: line 609: python3: command not found
    FAIL: M1: broken normalizer appends both copies (BEFORE+2)   expected 113, actual 112
  /repo/.claude/scripts/tests/mutation-harness.test.sh: line 448: python3: command not found
    FAIL: META 2: cleanup-removed harness leaks at least one worktree   expected 0, actual 1
  cmd: bash .claude/tests/linux/run-linux-tier.sh --tiers l1   (before python3 was added to
       .claude/tests/linux/Dockerfile)

WHY IT MATTERS EVEN THOUGH CI HAS PYTHON3. Every other prerequisite in this tier is guarded:
`command -v bd` 39 times, `command -v jq` 22, `command -v node` 9. These two are not, so a
missing prerequisite produces a FAILING ASSERTION WITH A WRONG NUMBER rather than a skip marker
naming what is absent. That is strictly harder to diagnose than a skip - the number looks like a
regression in the thing under test - and it is the inverse of the a9hh standard (a skip must not
read as a pass; a missing prerequisite must not read as a defect either).

GitHub's ubuntu-24.04 runner ships python3, so CI has never seen it, and the l1-unit job's
"Verify dependencies" step does not check for python3 either - so a runner image change that
dropped it would surface as these two mystery failures.

FIX: either guard both call sites and print one of the tier's four skip-marker shapes (which
makes them PARTIAL and red under STRICT_SECTIONS=1, where python3 is provisioned), or replace
the python3 use with something already required. Also add python3 to the l1-unit job's
dependency-verification step so the absence fails where it is named.

.claude/tests/linux/Dockerfile now installs python3 and records this finding in the comment
above the package list.

title: post-edit.sh second-chance branch round-trips a tracked path through $(dirname)/$(basename)
description:
Third attacker-influenced site of the command-substitution path class censused during fkm.3 QA round 8; the sibling filings are jtni (reconcile_tracker) and w4ya (wtres_repo_relative).

post-edit.sh:388-389:
  _PE_DIR=$(cd "$(dirname "$_PE_CANDIDATE")" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P) || _PE_DIR=""
  [ -n "$_PE_DIR" ] && _PE_RESOLVED="${_PE_DIR%/}/$(basename "$_PE_CANDIDATE")"

$_PE_CANDIDATE derives from tool_input.file_path, so it is agent-chosen. Command substitution strips every trailing newline and cannot tell a command's output terminator from a filename's last byte, so a leaf named with a trailing newline is reattached under a different name and the tracker records a path that is not the one written. Reached only in the SECOND-CHANCE branch (fkm.1.15), i.e. after _pe_within has already rejected the path, so it additionally needs an ancestor symlink pointing back into the repo — stated as a precondition rather than dismissed, because tracking fidelity is what the whole gate reads.

Remedy is the one fkm.3 used in the design region: parameter expansion (${p%/*} with dirname's trailing-slash rule, ${p##*/}) instead of the subprocess round-trip. Both are pure bash, portable, byte-preserving, and delete two subprocesses.

NOT part of fkm.3's change set — pre-existing from fkm.1.15, filed per CONTRIBUTING (a defect found in closed work opens a new task).

title: wtres_repo_relative round-trips a path through $(dirname)/$(basename) (verify-before-stop.sh:4019-4020)
description:
Census finding from fkm.3 round 6. PRE-EXISTING (worktree-resolution / llh work), NOT introduced by fkm.3 — filed as a new task per CONTRIBUTING.md.

SITE: verify-before-stop.sh:4019-4020

    d=$(dirname "$p") || return 1
    b=$(basename "$p") || return 1

then `printf '%s%s' "$_WTRES_MEMO_PREFIX" "$b"`.

MECHANISM: the same class fkm.3 closed in qa-gate.sh's design region. Command substitution strips every trailing newline including one belonging to the pathname, so a path whose LAST COMPONENT ends in a newline is re-spelled one byte short, and a path whose PARENT ends in a newline resolves `d` to the wrong directory (which is then handed to `repo_identity` and `git -C`).

REACHABILITY: the inputs are tracker lines and `git status` output. changed-files.txt is line-delimited, so a path containing a newline cannot be one tracker line — which is what bounds this. It is reachable through the same indirection fkm.3 measured for the design predicate: an entry that RESOLVES through a component named with a trailing newline.

THE PORTABLE FIX IS PARAMETER EXPANSION, and it is not a one-liner: `${p%/*}` is not `dirname` (dirname strips trailing slashes FIRST) and `${p##*/}` is not `basename` for the same reason. fkm.3 ships a worked, measured spelling of both in `design_path_is_contained` — copy that, and red-before with a fixture whose component is newline-named.

title: reconcile_tracker's repo-root round-trip: git rev-parse --show-toplevel through $( ) loses a trailing newline
description:
Found while auditing the three areas QA named in fkm.3 round 6 (approve's re-hash, design_foreign_paths, the tracker reconcile). PRE-EXISTING, 94d work, NOT introduced by fkm.3 — filed as a new task per CONTRIBUTING.md rather than folded into a closed one.

SITES (qa-gate.sh):
- 686  `top=$(git -C "$PROJECT_DIR" rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)`
- 688  `canon_pd=$(cd "$PROJECT_DIR" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)`
- 689  `canon_top=$(cd "$top" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)`
- 1560 the same rev-parse capture in the second helper
and the same shape in verify-before-stop.sh at 1676, 4105-4106, 4137, 4147.

MECHANISM: identical to fkm.3's R5-F1 class. `$( )` strips every trailing newline and cannot tell a command's output terminator from a filename's last byte, so a repository whose ROOT DIRECTORY is named with a trailing newline yields a truncated `$top`, hence a truncated `$prefix`, hence `abs="$prefix/$p"` naming paths that do not exist. The tracker then under-covers the real change set — the same harm class 94d.1 exists to make visible.

NOT FIXED IN fkm.3, deliberately: (a) it is outside the D1 region and outside the declared surface of that task; (b) unlike the D1 sites there is no byte-preserving alternative — `git rev-parse` has no `-z`/NUL output for `--show-toplevel`, so the fix is either to stop asking git (which changes the nested-project semantics reconcile_tracker was built for) or to route through a sentinel-suffix capture idiom (`x=$(cmd; printf '|'); x=${x%|}`) at every producer and consumer.

REACHABILITY: requires the checkout's own root component to end in a newline. Lower than the D1 sites, which took only a sibling directory. Fail direction is a WRONG path spelling rather than a bypass, but a wrong spelling means a real changed file is absent from the tracker under its true name.

ANY FIX MUST BE RED-BEFORE: build a checkout under a root named with a trailing newline, observe reconcile spell the paths short, then fix.

title: sync-errors.log surfacing shows only head -1 then truncates, and now competes with informational F1 veto lines on ~42% of commits
description:
QA round-1 finding R1-F2 on claude-workflow-plugin-s5qf (LOW, non-blocking). NOT a defect in s5qf — s5qf follows the existing precedent exactly and its log message is the most informative in the file. This is about the pre-existing surfacing MECHANISM that message feeds, which s5qf materially amplifies.

THE MECHANISM. `log_sync_error` appends to .claude/.qa-tracking/sync-errors.log. session-start.sh:433-436 reads ONLY `head -1` and then TRUNCATES the whole file, and :680-684 reports it as:

    - Last session logged a Beads sync error at <ts>; see .claude/.qa-tracking/sync-errors.log

Two problems, both pre-existing:
  * only the FIRST line ever reaches the operator, and the rest are discarded
    unread on the same pass;
  * every line is labelled "a Beads sync error" whatever it actually was. The
    fkm.1.1 wording note at :673-679 already concedes the label "was never
    accurate anyway".

WHY s5qf MAKES IT MATTER MORE. Both F1 vetoes call log_sync_error on their
SUCCESS path — one line per vetoed path, on an ordinary successful Stop. Observed
live during the s5qf review at 2026-08-11T16:14:54Z: two informational lines
(.claude/agents/qa.md and docs/HOOKS.md), from a completely healthy run.

By the churn figure QA reproduced independently, 60 of 142 non-merge commits in
this repo touch a veto-reachable governing artifact. So on roughly 42% of
commits the FIRST line of sync-errors.log will now be an informational F1 veto
line rather than an error — and a genuine bd write failure sitting behind it is
truncated away unseen, having been announced (if at all) as somebody else's
timestamp.

The bbh content veto set this precedent and it was harmless there because an
executable file with a documentation name is rare. A governing artifact changing
is not rare; it is the normal case in this repo.

CANDIDATE DIRECTIONS (a decision, not a design):
  * Separate severity from the channel: let vetoes write an INFO-shaped line (or
    a different file) and keep sync-errors.log for actual write failures. This is
    the honest fix and the largest.
  * Or keep one file and make the surfacing read it properly: report the count
    and the most severe line rather than head -1, and stop calling every entry a
    Beads sync error. The :673-679 note already wants this.
  * Or, smallest: do not truncate what was never shown.

NOT URGENT. Nothing is lost that was ever reliably surfaced — the truncation
predates all of this. Filed so the amplification is on the record rather than
discovered later as "the error log is full of successes".

title: The F1 arm still swallows two failures it does not block on: qa-gate enter, and the classified-hash computation
description:
QA round-1 finding R1-F4 on claude-workflow-plugin-bbh (the qzv.3 half), recorded
in the qa-claude review artifact on that task. Filed to TRACK a residual the
implementer declared and deliberately did not fix — I agree with that decision;
the gap is only that the declaration lived in a completion-payload field and
nowhere a future reader will look.

THE TWO, both on the F1 fast-path arm of verify-before-stop.sh:

  :1586  "$QA_GATE" enter "$CURRENT_TASK" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
             || log_sync_error "qa-gate enter failed during F1 ..."
  :1272  F1_CLASSIFIED_HASH=$(current_change_set_hash) || true

Both are the shape qzv.3 just fixed one line below: a failure that is logged (or
not even logged) and then ignored.

WHY LEAVING THEM IS DEFENSIBLE, and why this is P3 rather than a re-open. The
implementer's argument, which I checked and accept: a failed `enter` almost
always surfaces THROUGH the approve refusal the same round now BLOCKS on —
`enter` regenerates the impact report, so an enter that failed leaves the report
missing or stale, and approve then refuses with impact_report_missing /
impact_report_stale and the F1-APPROVE-REFUSAL region turns that into a block
naming the error_key. The :1272 swallow degrades the same way: with no classified
hash the `--expect-hash` array collapses to zero arguments, and the same missing
impact-report.sh that caused it makes approve refuse anyway. Declining to patch
without a reproduction is the evidence-before-fix protocol working, not a
shortcut.

THE RESIDUAL, precisely. An `enter` failure that does NOT cause approve to fail —
i.e. one that leaves a fresh impact report, an entered label and a reconciled
tracker behind while still exiting non-zero. Then the Stop releases on an
approval whose preconditions were established by a call that reported failure,
and the only trace is one sync-errors.log line. Narrow, and nobody has produced
it.

WHAT THIS TASK WANTS, in order:
  1. A REPRODUCTION first. Do not patch on the argument above being wrong;
     establish an `enter` exit path that leaves every artifact approve checks
     intact. If none exists, that is a legitimate and valuable outcome — record
     it here and close, and the two lines become documented-safe rather than
     unexamined.
  2. Only then decide. The obvious change (block on a non-zero enter) has its own
     availability profile on the most-travelled fast path in the system, which is
     exactly the cost bbh and qzv.3 both had to measure. Measure it the same way.

NOT A REGRESSION FROM qzv.3. Both swallows predate it. qzv.3 made the situation
strictly better: before it, an enter failure AND the approve failure were both
swallowed and the Stop released over a wiped tracker.

title: cmd_block inherits approve's terminal-first ordering without re-deriving it — sweep-first is strictly safer for block
description:
Found during QA of claude-workflow-plugin-8zi (P3). NOT a regression — this strictly IMPROVES on the pre-8zi state and is filed as a design follow-up.

## The observation

set_terminal_label applies terminal-FIRST ordering to both callers, and the rationale in its header is gz3's:

  "the approval RECORD is written before this call, so from the moment the terminal label lands the {record, label} pair is coherent ... Sweeping first would instead open a window with NO terminal label, which those same readers resolve to `entered` or `none`."

That reasoning is correct FOR APPROVE. It was not re-derived for BLOCK, where both premises differ:

- block writes NO record before the transition (its comment is written AFTER the labels), so there is no {record, label} pair to keep coherent.
- a window with no terminal label is the SAFE direction for a block: readers resolve it to `entered`, and the Stop hook then requires approval rather than releasing.

## Consequence

Under terminal-first, cmd_block on a task carrying a prior qa-approved passes through a transient {qa-approved, qa-blocked} for the width of one bd call. All four label readers test qa-approved FIRST (cmd_status, epic-gate.sh qa_state_of, statusline.sh x2), so during that window a task being BLOCKED reports `approved`. If a Stop fires inside it and the prior approval record still binds the current change set, both halves of the release predicate hold.

## Why this is an improvement, not a defect

Before 8zi, block never removed qa-approved at all — the window was PERMANENT. 8zi shrinks it from permanent to one bd call. Reachability is narrow: it needs a concurrent Stop inside the window AND an unchanged change set (if the specialist edited anything, the record no longer binds and LABEL_WITHOUT_RECORD blocks instead).

## Suggested fix

Give set_terminal_label an ordering parameter, or a sibling entry point, so block sweeps first and approve keeps terminal-first. Do NOT flip approve — its ordering is load-bearing for gz3.

Any change needs a leg asserting the block-side window closes, plus the existing 8zi-3 legs (block clears qa-approved, every in-flight label survives, status flips approved -> blocked) staying green.

title: Fixture SKILL.md copies drift unguarded — sync-fixtures covers .claude/scripts/*.sh only, so 9 committed copies carry a stale SessionEnd row that a live e2e run injects into agents
description:
Found while landing qzv. Filed rather than fixed inside it, because healing it wholesale carries
an UNRELATED correction into 9 committed files and would make this task's diff unattributable.

WHAT IS UNGUARDED. `make sync-fixtures` copies `.claude/scripts/*.sh` into every
`.claude/tests/e2e/fixtures/*/.claude/scripts/`, and the drift guard measures exactly that set.
`.claude/skills/workflow-engine/SKILL.md` is ALSO committed per fixture (7 fixtures + 2
node-react-auth worktrees = 9 copies) and nothing syncs or compares it. `vendored-skills.test.sh`
META-6b deliberately PRUNES `.claude/tests/` copies from the shipped-skills scan, so they are
invisible there by design.

THE LIVE DRIFT, measured 2026-08-04 before qzv touched anything: all 9 copies still say the
SessionEnd row is "`bd sync` with error logging", while canonical says "Checks the Beads JSONL
ledger (read-only) and logs divergence" — the R4-F1 correction ("this hook no longer WRITES the
ledger"), which landed in canonical and never reached the fixtures.

WHY IT MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING COSMETIC. These copies are what a live e2e run injects into the
agents it drives, so a stale row is a false instruction in an agent packet, not a stale doc. It is
also invisible: the run-start sync heals SCRIPTS and reports success, so a reader has no signal
that the skill text the agents received is a release behind.

WHAT qzv DID DO: applied ONLY its own step-7 correction to the 9 copies (the Stop hook no longer
runs `bd update --status closed`), because shipping a claim the code contradicts into an agent
packet is worse than leaving a pre-existing row stale. The SessionEnd row was deliberately left
alone.

CANDIDATE FIX: extend `sync-fixtures` to `.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md` and add the pair to whatever
measures drift, so the count covers it. Check first whether any fixture INTENDS a divergent
SKILL.md (a degraded-install scenario, say) — if so the sync needs a per-fixture opt-out rather
than a blanket copy, and that opt-out is the actual deliverable.

NOT IN SCOPE: the recorded cassettes under `.claude/tests/e2e/cassettes/` also contain the old
text. Those are dated recordings of past runs and must not be retro-edited — same rule the
RELEASE_AUDIT addendum and CHANGELOG entries follow.

title: HOOKS.md cites QA's 54% figure against a parenthetical that cannot produce it

The 54% figure is also correct as QA's independent count, but HOOKS.md supports it with a parenthetical (60 git-visible, 29 byte-identical) from which 54% cannot be derived — 29/60 is 48%, and 54% comes from a different denominator. title: The impact report's nested JSON shape has produced four wrong-path reads across two agents — a silent zero looks identical to a dead index
description:
Observed FOUR times during the 94d review arc, by two different agents, on the same artifact:

  1. QA round 4 read .impact.nodes and saw 0 nodes for all 26 files — nearly recorded it as a code-graph degradation. Real path: .impact.data.nodes.
  2. QA round 5 read .ok instead of .impact.ok and saw '26 per-file errors'. Re-measured: 0 errors.
  3. QA round 6 made the SAME .impact.nodes vs .impact.data.nodes error again, and said so.
  4. A specialist hit the sibling shape while compacting item 7 for the grading packet.

Each time the wrong path returns a plausible-looking value — 0 nodes, 0 ok, an error count — rather than a jq error. So a query that never reached the data is indistinguishable from a query that found bad data. Every instance was caught only because the reader was suspicious of a convenient or alarming number and re-measured.

THIS IS NOT FOUR CARELESS AGENTS. Four independent instances on one artifact is a property of the artifact. The report nests per-file results under .impact.data.* while carrying sibling keys (.ok, .server, .change_set_hash) at the top level, so both nesting depths are locally plausible and the wrong one fails silently.

FIX DIRECTIONS, pick one:
  (a) Flatten the per-file entries so there is one nesting depth, or
  (b) ship a documented reader — impact-report.sh --nodes <file> / --ok — so consumers never hand-write the jq path, or
  (c) at minimum, document the canonical paths in the report header itself and in qa.md 6p.1 where the packet compaction is prescribed.

(b) is preferred: it is the same reasoning that made review-check.sh THE ONE validator. A hand-written jq path against a nested artifact is the analytic equivalent of a hand-mirrored list, and this repo already has the lesson about those.

RELATED, same defect family: fkm.1.11 (the Stop gate reports 'technical checks passed' while running only L1) and fkm.1.14 (codex-review.sh deletes its own error_key on a paid failure). All three are 'the measurement that did not happen looks exactly like the measurement that passed.' That family now has six recorded instances this session, four of them here.

title: qa.md:196 carries two statements that 94d made false: out-of-repo Write probes are now dropped, and .claude/.qa-tracking/ IS now denylisted
description:
Found by QA round 5 on 94d, recorded as R5-F3 (low). The specialist disclosed HALF of this as its residual 2; QA found the other half in the same paragraph.

The paragraph is `.claude/agents/qa.md:196` ("Keep your own scratch out of the change set"), and the same text is echoed in the three specialist prompts. It currently contains two sentences that 94d's own change set falsified:

FALSE SENTENCE 1 (disclosed by the specialist as residual 2).
  "a probe you Write to an absolute path — /tmp/enc-diff.sh, a mktemp -d directory,
   anything outside the repo — enters changed-files.txt, the change-set hash, and
   the Stop gate"
After fkm.1.15's CONTAINMENT-FILTER, an out-of-repo path is DROPPED at record time and logged to sync-errors.log. QA confirmed by probe: /tmp/enc-diff.sh, /etc/hosts, a foreign repo path, a mktemp -d probe, a sibling dir string-prefixed by the root, and a lexical .. escape are all dropped.

FALSE SENTENCE 2 (NOT disclosed — found by QA round 5).
  "Do NOT use .claude/.qa-tracking/ for scratch: despite what this line used to say,
   it is NOT denylisted — post-edit.sh tracks it and anything you write there enters
   the change set, which is how a review artifact ended up as a tracked entry of its
   own change set."
Rule 2 (WORKFLOW_SELF_WRITTEN_REGEX + workflow_self_written, landed earlier in this same change set as the R2-F5 fix) makes this false too. QA confirmed by probe that a write to $ROOT/.claude/.qa-tracking/r.json is dropped with no containment log — dropped by rule 2, one filter earlier. The paragraph's own cautionary anecdote (a review artifact becoming a tracked entry of its own change set) is exactly the defect that fix closed.

So: one paragraph, two false sentences, both created by the same change set, one disclosed and one not. Note the irony worth preserving in the rewrite — this is the paragraph that governs QA's own behaviour, and it now steers reviewers away from a directory that this very change set made safe.

BOTH stalenesses are in the CONSERVATIVE direction (the guidance still works; it is merely no longer the only mechanism), which is why this is low and not medium.

FIX. Rewrite the paragraph to say: the mechanism now DROPS an out-of-repo path and LOGS it to sync-errors.log, and .claude/.qa-tracking/ is filtered at the writer by rule 2 — so prefer the session scratchpad because there is then nothing to log, not because the alternatives are tracked. Keep the standing advice against deleting a stray tracker entry mid-cycle; that part is still true and still load-bearing.

NOT DOABLE INSIDE 94d: .claude/agents/qa.md and the three specialist prompts are not in 94d's change set, so editing them would move the graded hash 01296db9... . This must land after 94d's approval.

title: codex-review.sh leaks codex mcp-server processes — observed one pair running 2 days
description:

  68543 / 68550  elapsed 06:01:33
  36672 / 36696  elapsed 2 days 02:34:18

title: R7-F2: no gate runs sync-fixtures - CI detects fixture drift, nothing prevents it
description:
R7-F2 (low). make test-ci CATCHES fixture drift via _fixture-script-sync; only a human remembering to re-sync after the last canonical edit PREVENTS it. That discipline failed during fkm.1.1 (sync 00:27:08Z, canonical edit 01:36:39Z, no re-sync) and shipped stale contract text into seven committed files, turning the branch gate red.

Design tension to resolve, recorded by QA r7: an auto-syncing prerequisite would MUTATE COMMITTED FILES during a test run, which is presumably why the guard is a checker and not a fixer. A --check mode merely duplicates detection the guard already performs. The real gap is PREVENTION, so the fix belongs before the test run, not inside it.

Second occurrence of the class. Precedent: run 4 shipped a stale verify-before-stop.sh into a PAID live run (bd claude-workflow-plugin-366.10) - the incident _fixture-script-sync.unit.spec.ts:6-15 cites as its own reason for existing.

title: R7-F1: Makefile sync-fixtures skip list and runFixture.ts FIXTURE_SYNC_EXCLUDES are hand-mirrored with only a comment binding them
description:
R7-F1 (low). Verified scope, after two STRONGER claims were checked and found FALSE: both divergence directions ARE caught by the L3 guard (Makefile-excludes-more trips the per-pair existsSync at _fixture-script-sync.unit.spec.ts:157-160; TS-excludes-more trips the orphan assertion at :170-182), and the lists are NOT denylisted - Makefile, runFixture.ts and the guard spec are all tracked, so a divergence enters the change-set hash normally.

Genuine residual, narrower than first reported: a brand-new script added to FIXTURE_SYNC_EXCLUDES only, never synced, leaves the guard green while the live sync silently stops maintaining it - the over-exclusion class runFixture.ts:268-271 names in its own header. The window closes at the next make sync-fixtures.

Fix: a direct assertion binding the two lists, replacing the comment at Makefile:319-320. Scope to the residual; do not over-build. The 'sole observer' framing IS accurate: the guard is the only thing watching a denylisted class.

title: RELEASE_AUDIT self-consistency check: ADDENDUM row-range vs section header vs tally vs row-id grep
description:
All three findings from the C5 QA review of `docs/RELEASE_AUDIT.md` were MECHANICALLY DETECTABLE, and a cheap checker would have caught every one before review. Suggested by the C5 reviewer; filed rather than built, because the release closeout is not the place to add a new spec.

## The three defects a checker would have caught

1. **HIGH** — ADDENDUM 2 said A10 is "superseded by `UW9`". The correct row is `UW14`. `UW9` is the SessionStart row. This was the ONE pointer a reader follows to verify the A10 correction, so it defeated exactly the checkability the addendum exists to provide (`igp` defect class).
2. **MEDIUM** — ADDENDUM 2 said the ledger is `UW1`-`UW12`. It is `UW1`-`UW16`. The H3 header, the tally Total and the row-id grep all said 16.
3. **LOW** — ADDENDUM 2 named "0 NOT-PROVEN" as the verdict clause the un-re-scoped grep would falsify. Measured, NOT-PROVEN is 0 under BOTH forms; the clauses that actually break are PROVEN (14 -> 27) and PROVEN-WITH-CAVEAT (0 -> 3).

## Proposed checks (all offline, no network, L1-tier)

For each `## v<X> claims ledger` section in `docs/RELEASE_AUDIT.md`:

- the row-id range named in its ADDENDUM matches the `### v<X> claims (<PREFIX>1-<PREFIX>n)` header, matches the tally's `**Total**` cell, and matches `grep -cE '^\| <PREFIX>[0-9]+ \|'` over the section. All four must agree.
- every backticked `UW<n>` / `TM<n>` cross-reference in prose resolves to a row that EXISTS in the named section. Catches defect 1 as a dangling-pointer check; a stronger form asserts the cited row's text actually mentions the subject.
- every non-final ledger's five tally ranges terminate at the NEXT ledger's heading, not at `,0`. This is the recurring trap: v4.0.0 left it armed and v4.1.0 paid it. See the ADDENDUM 2 blockquote and the "TO WHOEVER APPENDS THE NEXT LEDGER" note in the v4.1.0 tally.
- the sum of the four status counts equals the row-id count, per section. This is the asymmetry the C5 reviewer noticed: the `Total` row greps `^\| TM[0-9]+ \|` and is IMMUNE to the range bug, so a corrupted table shows 27+3+0+0 = 30 statuses against a Total of 14. Preserve that asymmetry deliberately — an internally inconsistent table is a far better failure than a uniformly wrong one.

## Non-obvious detail for whoever builds this

The frozen v3.5.0 row-id grep needs `^\| [A-Z]+[0-9]+[a-z]? \|` — rows `P6a` and `P6b` carry a trailing letter, and without the optional suffix the count reads 119 instead of the documented 121. A checker hardcoding `[A-Z]+[0-9]+` would report a false failure on a correct file, which is the fastest way to get a guard deleted.

Needs a META proving each check can fail: plant a wrong row-range, a dangling `UW<n>` pointer, and a `,0` range into fixture copies and assert the checker flags each.

title: completion-contract-parity: assert context_coverage on the two unguarded carriers (MCP_SERVERS.md, invariants.ts)
description:
Found during QA review of claude-workflow-plugin-i17 (C2). The shipped documents are all CORRECT — every carrier really does carry `context_coverage`. This is a gap in the new L1 guard's future protection, not a defect in what shipped.

`.claude/scripts/tests/completion-contract-parity.test.sh` lists 12 files in `CARRIERS`. Section 5 scans all 12 for forbidden phrases, but Section 4's positive presence assertions cover only 10. Two carriers can be silently reverted with the spec still green.

## R1-F1 (medium) — docs/MCP_SERVERS.md:94

Reproduced in a sandbox: reverting the F7 tuple from `{..., llm_observations, context_coverage}` to `{..., llm_observations}` leaves the spec at Failed=0/45. The twin file `.claude/mcp/bd-mcp/README.md` carries the byte-identical tuple and IS asserted (same mutation there gives Failed=1/45).

This is exactly the drift i17's own implementation note named as the motivation: "docs/MCP_SERVERS.md (same tuple as bd-mcp README — updating one and not the other is the drift being guarded)". The guard covers one side of it.

## R1-F2 (low) — .claude/tests/e2e/lib/invariants.ts:435-437

Same shape. Reverting the doc comment to `carries all six F7 fields` and dropping `context_coverage` from the field list leaves the spec at Failed=0/45. The Section-5 needle `all six fields` does NOT match `all six F7 fields` — the `F7` infix breaks the fixed string — so the phrase scan does not incidentally cover it.

## R1-F3 (low) — META-TEST A discriminates via PARSE_ERROR

META-A strips the `context_coverage` line from a copy of `backend.md`. That is the fence's LAST key, so the preceding trailing comma is stranded and the block becomes invalid JSON — `fence_head7` returns PARSE_ERROR, not a six-key list. The assertion passes, but it demonstrates sensitivity to MALFORMATION rather than to the well-formed missing-seventh-key shape it names. The in-code comment says to "confirm the block still parses before concluding anything from the key list" and then never asserts that it parses.

## R1-F4 (info) — the census is a hardcoded five-entry list

A future specialist prompt added without a contract section would not appear in Section 1's census — the same "a named carrier nobody checked" shape the devops gap was.

Also worth tightening: the spec header's item 4 leads with "context_coverage reached every prose carrier" and then enumerates a list omitting these two files. LESSONS.md's rule applies — an invariant that is only nearly true is one a future change can break without failing a test; count the write or delete the claim.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Two new assert_eq lines in Section 4 asserting context_coverage presence in docs/MCP_SERVERS.md's F7 tuple and in invariants.ts's field list, mirroring the existing bd-mcp README assertion.
2. Both proven sensitive by sandbox mutation: reverting each file's field must fail EXACTLY ONE assertion, with a full-pass control before and after.
3. META-A's backend.md mutation removes the field AND the preceding comma so the stripped fence still parses, making the demonstration match its stated claim. Assert the mutated body parses before comparing keys.
4. Header item 4 either enumerates every carrier it asserts or drops the phrase "every prose carrier"; header notes that a new specialist prompt must be added to the Section 1 census list.
5. run-tests.sh green; the assertion total in the header updated to match.
notes: Evidence is reproducible. Build a minimal sandbox (docs/, .claude/agents/, .claude/rubrics/, the rubric-revision-loop fixture rubrics, .claude/tests/README.md, .claude/tests/e2e/lib/invariants.ts, .claude/mcp/bd-mcp/README.md), point `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` at it, and run the spec from its live path. A faithful sandbox scores 45/45 identically to the live repo — verified during the i17 review.

title: U3 harness (DEFERRED — evidence bar unmet): context-gathering ledger + frontier queue
description:
DEFERRED ON PURPOSE. This carries the full U3 design so it survives; it is NOT scheduled work. Do not pick it up off a ready queue — the acceptance criteria below are the criteria for OPENING it, not for closing it.

## Why it is deferred

U3 was originally scoped as a context-gathering ledger plus a frontier harness. It was cut to C2 (`claude-workflow-plugin-i17`): one contract field (`context_coverage`) and one rubric criterion (default C8). The motivating problem — a 14-PR speculative-fix chain where fourteen plausible patches could not be ranked because nobody had recorded which sources were consulted — is already addressed by the evidence-before-fix protocol, which is shipped, is mechanically guarded by `evidence-before-fix.test.sh`, and is demonstrably working.

Building the harness now would be machinery ahead of evidence: a ledger/frontier loop is a substantial, permanently-maintained surface (a config file, a shell harness, orchestrator and reviewer-lane wiring, L1 + L3 tests, a META-TEST) justified by a failure mode we have not yet observed the shipped cheap version failing to catch.

The cheap version is C2. `context_coverage` is a free-form string with a fixed three-part convention: what was read / what was deliberately NOT read and why / the largest remaining unknown. That convention is what makes the field gradeable, and it is also what gives this harness a real corpus if it is ever built — every completed task now leaves a machine-readable-ish record of what its author did and did not look at.

## Acceptance criteria for OPENING this task

Name **three closed tasks** whose `context_coverage` omitted the **same class of source**, where that omission is plausibly connected to a defect, a bounce, or a QA block. Cite the task ids and quote the relevant `context_coverage` text from each.

"Same class of source" means a recurring category, not three unrelated one-offs: e.g. "none of them read the installer's upgrade path before changing a shipped file's classification", or "none of them read the L2 component specs before changing a hook's stdin contract".

If the bar is not met, this stays deferred. If the field turns out to be honestly filled and the omissions turn out to be harmless, the correct outcome is to close this as unneeded and record that as a result — a null result on "do we need the harness" is worth more than the harness.

## The design, preserved in full

From `docs/plans/v4.1-upgrade-wave.md` Phase U3 (that file is UNTRACKED in git — this description is the durable copy):

- A **coverage ledger** (sources visited: files, symbols, docs, tickets, sibling repos) and a **frontier queue** (discovered-but-unvisited), maintained by a small harness the orchestrator and reviewer lanes call.
- **Termination is structural**: frontier empty, or a hard cap (frontier depth, source count) hit — with `stopped_by` recorded, reusing the V2 review-template convention (`review-check.sh`'s artifact carries the same field, so the vocabulary is already established).
- Every exhaustive-mode delegation carries the same mandatory `risk_threshold` and `stop_condition` fields as reviews; the harness **rejects requests missing them**. This is the mechanical answer to diligence-as-infinite-loop — the same shape `review-check.sh validate-request` already enforces for the review lane.
- Wire it into the **orchestrator's pre-decomposition step** and offer it to the **reviewer lane**. Caps live in ONE config file (`.claude/context-config`), matching the existing one-caps-file convention of `.claude/review-config` and `.claude/rubric-config`.
- Implementation surface named in the epic title: `.claude/context-config`, `.claude/scripts/context-ledger.sh`, orchestrator wiring in `.claude/agents/orchestrator.md`.

**Tests the design calls for:** L1 and L3 on the ledger/frontier harness — dedup (the same source visited twice is one ledger row), termination on empty frontier, termination on cap with the correct `stopped_by` value, and rejection of an uncapped request. **META-TEST:** mutate the cap check so the frontier can grow unbounded — the termination assertion must fail.

**Sequencing note from the plan:** U3's harness was placed before U5 (staging e2e QA loop) so staging verification could use bounded exhaustive mode. If U5 is built while U3 remains deferred, U5 must supply its own bound rather than assuming this harness exists.

## What C2 actually shipped instead

`claude-workflow-plugin-i17`: `context_coverage` added to the F7 contract (`docs/AGENTS.md`), to all four specialist prompts and qa.md's three contract blocks, to `grader.md`, to default rubric C3 (presence) and the new C8 (quality, on the empty / boilerplate / detached-from-the-work taxonomy), plus the qa.md section-3 review-checklist item that makes the contract's only claimed enforcement actually exist. Guarded by `.claude/scripts/tests/completion-contract-parity.test.sh`.

Honest ceiling, carried forward: C2 added **zero mechanical runtime enforcement**. Nothing rejects a payload at runtime; the e2e `completion-contract` invariant stays `skipped` on its documented trace gap. If the evidence bar above is ever met, that ceiling is part of the argument for building this.
design:
Deliberate deviation from the brief's wording: filed as `deferred` rather than `closed`. `bd ready` excludes deferred, so it is out of the work queue exactly as a closure would be, but the design text stays discoverable on an open-status listing rather than needing a `--include-closed` to find. The intent is identical to closed-as-unneeded: no work is scheduled, and the three-instance evidence bar is the trigger to change that.

Filed as a child of the U3 epic `claude-workflow-plugin-gio` rather than as a replacement for it — the epic is the orchestrator's, and reconciling it (close it, retitle it, or leave it blocked) is the orchestrator's call, not this specialist's.
acceptance_criteria: OPENING criteria (not closing criteria): three closed tasks named, with ids and quoted `context_coverage` text, whose coverage notes omitted the SAME class of source, and where that omission is plausibly connected to a defect, a bounce, or a QA block. Fewer than three, or three unrelated one-offs, means the bar is unmet and this stays deferred. A null result — the field is honestly filled and the omissions are harmless — closes this as unneeded and is a valid, valuable outcome.

title: worktree-sweep.test.sh A4: broaden the structural deletion ban beyond `rm` (find -delete and rmdir currently evade it)
description:
QA finding R1-F3 (low) from the C1b review. Regression-guard gap, not a live
defect — the shipped `worktree-sweep.sh` contains zero occurrences of
`-delete` / `rmdir` / `unlink` / `shred`.

## What was reproduced

`A4: zero 'rm' against ANY candidate/path variable` bans `rm` only:

    grep -cE '(^|[^[:alnum:]_])rm[[:space:]]'

Injecting `find "$SWEEP_CANON" -mindepth 1 -delete` into the removal path of
a sandbox copy leaves **all 34 L1 assertions PASSING**. Same for
`rmdir "$SWEEP_CANON"`. (A first attempt looked like it failed, but only
because the injected trailing comment contained the word "rm" — trailing
comments survive A4's whole-line comment strip. Re-run clean without it.)

No behavioural assertion catches these either: on a candidate that already
passed every gate, `find -delete` produces the same observable as
`git worktree remove` (directory gone), so L2's 7.x assertions stay green.

## Why it matters

Section A's header states the case for the text check: "A behavioural spec
can only prove this for the inputs it happens to try; the text check covers
every future edit at once." It covers `rm`-shaped future edits. For the one
script in the plugin that can delete an operator's working tree, the ban
should name the primitive class.

## Asked for

Broaden A4's pattern to something like `rm|rmdir|unlink|shred|-delete`
(keeping A6 for `--force`), and soften the header claim to match what the
assertion actually enforces. Add the two injections above to the sensitivity
list so the guard is shown to discriminate.

title: worktree-sweep: document that --apply deletes IGNORED files with the worktree (and why --ignored is not the fix)
description:
QA finding R1-F1 (medium) from the C1b review. Documentation only — the code is correct.

## What was reproduced

Gate 3 is `git status --porcelain`, which excludes **ignored** files. In an
independent fixture, a worktree whose only extra content was gitignored
(`.env` containing `SECRET=hunter2`, plus `ignored-stuff/cache.bin`) read
CLEAN, passed all six gates, and `--apply` DESTROYED the `.env`.
`git worktree remove` without `--force` does not count ignored files as
making a tree unclean, so nothing downstream stops it.

This is exactly `git worktree remove` semantics and it needs a manual
`--apply`; containment confines it to `.claude/worktrees/<name>`; dry-run is
the default and prints every path first; and committed work always survives
because branches are not deleted. So the behaviour is defensible — what is
missing is that the header comment and `docs/HOOKS.md` describe gate 3 as
"clean = `git status --porcelain` empty (untracked included)", which reads
as "nothing will be lost".

## Why the obvious tightening is NOT the fix

`git status --porcelain --ignored` returns `!! .claude/` even in a correctly
gitignored repo, because gate 6's own evidence file
(`.claude/.qa-tracking/current-task`) is itself ignored. Adding `--ignored`
to gate 3 would make the primary evidence path never yield a removal —
self-defeating. Measured, not assumed.

## Asked for

One sentence in `.claude/scripts/worktree-sweep.sh`'s gate-3 header line and
in the `docs/HOOKS.md` helper-table row: ignored content (`.env`, build
caches) inside a swept worktree is deleted with it, and `--ignored` is
deliberately not used because the gate-6 evidence file is itself ignored.

Optionally also R1-F4 (low): a git-LOCKED worktree that passes all six gates
is printed as REMOVABLE by the dry run, but `--apply` gets a git refusal
(REMOVE-FAILED, rc=1, directory survives — fail-safe). Reading the `locked`
marker from `git worktree list --porcelain` would let the dry run report a
`locked` keeper reason instead of promising a removal git will refuse.

And R1-F5 (info): `SWEEP_ROOT` is only required non-empty and not literally
`/`; it is never checked to be inside `CURRENT_TOP`. `contained_in
"$CURRENT_TOP" "$SWEEP_ROOT"` is one more line of a guard already written.

title: install.sh's generated .gitignore lacks .claude/worktrees/ (the repo's own .gitignore has it)
description:
Noticed during C1b (8xv) while tracing how the worktree sweeper's task-evidence gate interacts with the clean-tree gate.

install.sh's GENERATED_GITIGNORE block (install.sh ~:779-833, executed verbatim
by packaging-parity.test.sh) writes:

    .claude/.session-start
    .claude/.qa-tracking/
    .claude/.mutation-runs/
    .claude/.mutation-worktrees/

but NOT `.claude/worktrees/`. The plugin's own .gitignore gained that line in
C1a (wg6) with the rationale "a leftover worktree was invisible to the gate AND
visible in `git status`". A fresh install into a repo with no .gitignore
therefore reproduces exactly the condition wg6 closed here.

Two consequences, both in the parent checkout (never inside a worktree, which
has no .claude/worktrees/ of its own):
 - `git status` in a target project lists every subagent worktree as untracked.
 - The Stop gate's git-status fallback sees them as session dirt (the shared
   denylist does drop the PATHS, so the change-set hash is unaffected).

Fix is one line in the heredoc + the matching line in install.ps1's mirrored
list, and packaging-parity.test.sh compares the two line-for-line, so both must
move together. Out of scope for C1b, which deliberately shipped no installer
change.

title: settings.json omits the ^Bash$ PostToolUse hook (bd-github-link.sh) that hooks.json ships — decide and align
description:
Found by the C1b (8xv) generalisation of platform-audit.test.sh checker (f) from SubagentStart-only to full hook-surface parity. The FIRST run of the generalised checker reported a live drift:

  EVENT_DIFF:PostToolUse

.claude/hooks/hooks.json declares TWO PostToolUse matchers:
  1. ^(Write|Edit|MultiEdit)$ -> post-edit.sh        (also in settings.json)
  2. ^Bash$                   -> bd-github-link.sh   (NOT in settings.json)

.claude/settings.json declares only #1. settings.json is what a live session
loads, so the I3 Beads<->GitHub auto-link hook does NOT fire in this repo's own
sessions; it only reaches plugin-scoped installs that read hooks.json.

docs/HOOKS.md documents the difference as deliberate ("for plugin-scoped
installs"), BUT the same sentence also claimed SubagentStart was one of the
differences, which stopped being true at some point — so the doc's authority on
the remaining half is weakened. C1b did not change behaviour: it pinned the
allowance exactly (violation set must be exactly EVENT_DIFF:PostToolUse, AND
hooks.json PostToolUse must equal settings' list plus exactly that one entry)
and corrected the stale SubagentStart half of the sentence.

DECIDE:
 (a) intended -> nothing to do; the pin already guards it.
 (b) an omission -> add the ^Bash$ entry to settings.json (behaviour change:
     bd-github-link.sh would then run on EVERY Bash tool call in this repo) and
     drop the allowance from platform-audit checker (f), which will then require
     full equality.

Evidence to reproduce:
  jq -S '.hooks.PostToolUse' .claude/settings.json
  jq -S '.hooks.PostToolUse' .claude/hooks/hooks.json
  bash .claude/scripts/tests/platform-audit.test.sh   # section (f)

title: shellcheck CI job is permanently red (advisory/continue-on-error) — a check nobody can act on trains people to ignore it

comments.author: username
comments.text:
Observed 2026-07-30 on run 30503166302 (b38714b), the run that took the branch back to green after lv4.

  OVERALL: success
    L1 / L2 / L3 vitest / manifest validation: success
    shellcheck (advisory): FAILURE
    L3 live: skipped

The job is continue-on-error, so the run is correctly green. But the job itself has been
red for a long time and is red for reasons nobody is expected to fix:
  - SC2317 'Command appears to be unreachable' on trap handlers and on functions invoked
    indirectly. Two files already carry file-level disables for exactly this
    (workflow-doctor.sh, and install.sh after C0b added an explicit exit made
    cleanup_install_tmp look dead). Note shellcheck 0.11.0 emits SC2317 for a trap
    handler ONLY when the script ends in an explicit exit — reproduced in isolation
    during C0b, second instance of that quirk.
  - SC2015 'A && B || C is not if-then-else' on idioms that are deliberate.

WHY FILE IT:  is clean and is the gate the Stop hook enforces, so the repo's
real lint bar is met. The CI job runs a DIFFERENT, stricter invocation that includes
info-level findings, and it can never go green without either fixing ~dozens of
intentional idioms or suppressing them. A permanently-red check is worse than no check:
it is indistinguishable from a newly-broken one, so the next genuine shellcheck
regression will land in a job everyone already scrolls past.

OPTIONS (not chosen):
  a) Align the CI invocation with  — same severity threshold, same file set.
     Then the job means what the local gate means, and a red is actionable.
  b) Keep the stricter sweep but pin its expected finding COUNT, failing only on an
     increase. Preserves the signal without demanding a cleanup.
  c) Add the targeted per-file disables with rationale comments (the repo's existing
     convention) until the sweep is genuinely clean, then drop continue-on-error.
Prefer (a) or (b): (c) is a large diff across many files for an advisory signal.

RELATED: this is the same family as 2ty, 1nz, 94d and qzv — signals that report with
more confidence than their evidence supports, or that cannot be acted on. Worth naming
together in the release closeout rather than as four unrelated tickets.

title: track_path builds hook JSON without escaping — an environment-derived path containing a quote/backslash silently vacates D3's landing assertions
description:
Found during QA of wg6 (C1a). Flagged by the implementer and deliberately NOT fixed there; accepted as a follow-up rather than a release blocker.

SITE: `.claude/tests/component/specs/denylist-shared.sh:181`

    printf '{"tool_input":{"file_path":"%s"}}' "$p" | ... post-edit.sh

No escaping. `post-edit.sh:20` parses with `jq -r '.tool_input.file_path // ...' 2>/dev/null || echo ""`.

REPRODUCED (simulating the printf/jq path, not by creating such an account):
  home containing a double quote   -> jq exit 5, "Invalid numeric literal at line 1, column 6"
  home containing a backslash      -> jq exit 5, "Invalid escape at line 1, column 65"
  clean home                       -> parses correctly
On a jq failure FILE_PATH is empty, post-edit.sh returns early at line 55, nothing is
tracked, and `track_path` reports `skipped`.

WHY IT MATTERS NOW: section D is the FIRST caller to pass an environment-derived value —
`D_PLAN_ABS="${HOME:-/nonexistent-home}/.claude/plans/..."`. Every other caller passes a
literal or a `mktemp -d` path, neither of which can contain a quote.

FAILURE DIRECTIONS (asymmetric, which is what keeps this low):
  D2 expects "tracked" -> would get "skipped" -> FAILS LOUDLY. This fires first.
  D3 expects "skipped" -> would get "skipped" -> PASSES VACUOUSLY. The real hazard.
  D4 unaffected (literals + the mktemp fixture path).
So the spec goes red before the vacuous pass can mislead anyone — but a reader debugging
the loud D2 failure would be looking at the wrong assertion.

Note the same reasoning applies to `$HOME` in `denylist-source.test.sh` (L1), which uses
`dl_verdict` — that one is already safe, because wg6 rewrote it to pass the path as a
`bash -c` ARGUMENT rather than interpolating it into the script text.

SUGGESTED FIX: build the payload with `jq -n --arg p "$p" '{tool_input:{file_path:$p}}'`
(jq is already a hard dependency of the component runner — `run.sh` exits 2 without it),
or reuse the L1 argument-passing idiom. Add a D-section assertion that drives a path
containing a quote so the escaping is pinned, not just fixed.

SEVERITY: low. Dormant on every realistic host (HOME is clean on macOS dev boxes and on
ubuntu CI runners), test-harness only, no shipped-runtime impact.

title: Degraded-mode asymmetry: a missing awk silently costs the whole 13KB contract with no workflow_degraded block (C0c R1-F5)
description:
QA finding R1-F5 (low) from the C0c independent review.

C0c gives `bd`-off-PATH, missing `.beads/` and missing `jq` each a loud in-band `<workflow_degraded severity="high">` block at the top of `additionalContext`. A missing `awk` does not get one.

MEASURED, running the target's own hook with `awk`/`gawk`/`nawk`/`mawk` masked off PATH:

```
rc=0  valid JSON  exactly 1 object
<workflow_engine source=...>  present (carrying the stub)
<workflow_degraded ...>       0 occurrences
additionalContext = 6,201 bytes   (healthy control: 19,021 bytes)
```

So the entire ~13 KB delegation contract is replaced by the one-line stub, and nothing at the TOP of the context says the session is degraded. The stub itself is good — it names the cause and preserves `MUST delegate` — but it is buried inside `<workflow_engine>`, which is exactly the placement the rest of this change argues against ("an LLM that reads the workflow blocks before the warning has already decided how to behave by the time the warning arrives").

The code comment at `session-start.sh:681-690` defers to `workflow-doctor.sh`'s `skill` check ("real body ~13KB, stub ~200B"). That is true and it is a real catch — but it is out-of-band, and the design principle of this change is loud in-band.

Spec `installer-target-functional.sh` 6f pins the graceful behaviour and deliberately does not assert a degraded block, so this is a considered design decision rather than an oversight — filing it so the choice is revisited rather than inherited.

NOT a blocker: `awk` absence is far rarer than PATH divergence, the hook stays valid and exits 0, and the delegation rule survives.
acceptance_criteria: - Either a fourth `<workflow_degraded>` reason fires when `WORKFLOW_BODY` falls back to the stub, with its own `fix:` lines, and `installer-target-functional.sh` 6f asserts it; or the decision to keep it out-of-band is written down at the call site with the reasoning, so the next reader does not re-litigate it.

title: L2 test-lib hygiene: dead net_required_or_skip + node-dependent assertion outside its HAVE_NODE guard (C0c R1-F3/F4)
description:
Two low-severity QA findings from the C0c independent review.

**R1-F3 — dead code in a shared lib.** `net_required_or_skip()` was added to `.claude/tests/component/lib/fixture.sh:143-196` (~30 lines with comments) and has **zero callers** anywhere in the repo; `installer-target-functional.sh` uses only `net_available()`. It is also untested. Either wire it to a spec that needs it, or drop it — a shared-lib function with no caller drifts silently.

**R1-F4 — a node-dependent assertion escapes its guard.** `.claude/tests/component/specs/installer-target-functional.sh:895-896`:

```
assert_eq "installer-target-functional 7g: 9 passed, 0 failed after the METAs" \
    "9 0" "$(jq -r '"\(.passed) \(.failed)"' "$M7G" ...)"
```

sits **outside** the `if [ "$HAVE_NODE" = "yes" ]` guard that correctly wraps the adjacent exit-code assertion at 891-894. `workflow-doctor.sh:658` hard-requires `node` and `npm` for the `deps` check, so on a node-less host `deps` FAILs, the guarded assertion is skipped as designed, and this unguarded one fails with `8 1`. That contradicts the spec's own header promise that "a node-less host still gets the C0c regression coverage".

Not reachable on this machine or in CI (both have node), which is why it passed 40/40 twice.

**Also worth considering (R1-F6, info):** `make lint` covers `.claude/scripts/*.sh`, `.claude/scripts/tests/*.sh`, `.claude/tests/mutation/*.sh` and `.claude/tests/mutation/lib/*.sh` — but **not** `.claude/tests/component/specs/*.sh` or `.claude/tests/component/lib/*.sh`. The new 968-line spec is therefore unlinted by the project's own lint target. Run manually it is clean at `shellcheck -S warning`; `fixture.sh` carries 2 pre-existing SC2164s (identical count in HEAD, not introduced by C0c).
acceptance_criteria:
- `net_required_or_skip` either has a caller and a test, or is removed.
- `installer-target-functional.sh:895-896` is inside the same `HAVE_NODE` guard as 891-894; verified by running the spec with node/npm masked off PATH.
- Optional: `make lint` extended to cover `.claude/tests/component/{specs,lib}/*.sh`.

title: install.ps1 R3 machinery has zero executed evidence — dispatch windows-install.yml once
approve-idempotency.sh can hang when its parent is SIGTERM'd — 4 orphans at 5h/1d10h, stalled L2 ~90s

comments.author: username
comments.text:
THIRD instance of the 'absence of failure is not success' trap this release, and the first one I walked into myself as orchestrator — recording it here because this task is about the same family (a spec that misbehaves under full-suite conditions but not alone).

WHAT HAPPENED (2026-07-29, C0c verification): the full L2 run reported 40 specs / 39 passed / 1 failed, naming code-graph-mcp.sh, 1868 assertions passed and 1 failed. To diagnose I ran the spec DIRECTLY:

    bash .claude/tests/component/specs/code-graph-mcp.sh | grep -iE '^\s*(FAIL|SKIP)'

That printed nothing and exited 0, and I reported it as passing. It was not passing. L2 specs require the runner's pre-sourced lib, so run directly the file died immediately:

    line 38: mk_fixture: command not found
    line 39: COMPONENT_FIXTURE_PATH: unbound variable

Zero assertions ran. No FAIL line existed to grep BECAUSE nothing executed. Exit 0 came from the last command in the pipeline, not from success.

Run correctly through the runner (bash .claude/tests/component/run.sh --filter code-graph-mcp): 29/29 PASS, 0 fail. So the spec is healthy and the full-suite failure was transient.

WHY IT BELONGS ON THIS TASK: the transient failure is most plausibly resource contention during the full suite, and this task tracks approve-idempotency.sh hanging/stalling (~90s observed, 4 orphaned processes at 5h/1d10h). Whatever stalls the suite is a candidate cause for a neighbouring spec's MCP boot or fixture step timing out. Re-running L2 alone to get a trustworthy number.

THE GENERALISABLE POINT, now with three data points this release:
 1. an L2 run killed at a 10-minute cap reported '0 fails' from 38 of 39 specs (C0b);
 2. a summary pipeline over a truncated log reported 'total spec-level fails: 0' (C0b);
 3. this one — a grep for FAIL over a script that never started.
In all three the pass signal was 'I did not see a failure'. The existing lesson says to assert the completeness line (Total: N). That works for the runner. It does NOT cover invoking a spec outside its harness, where the correct control is to assert a POSITIVE result (a PASS count, a __SPEC_SUMMARY__ line) rather than the absence of a negative.

SUGGESTED, cheap and separate from the hang: give L2 specs a guard that fails loudly when sourced without the lib — e.g. an early check for mk_fixture with a one-line 'run me via component/run.sh' message and exit 2. That converts a silent 0 into an unmistakable usage error, and it would have prevented this misreport entirely.

title: Add a behavioural section to mcp-deps-preserve.test.sh for mcp_server_has_deps (R3-F1: semantic mutant -maxdepth 3->1 passes both suites)

comments.author: username
comments.text:
R3-F1 (medium), found by QA at C0b approval, 2026-07-29. PROVEN BY MUTATION.

mcp-deps-preserve.test.sh executes mcp_deps_install only. It never calls
mcp_server_has_deps, mcp_servers_runnable, or the tail block. Literal reintroduction of
the old predicate IS caught (1 packaging-parity assertion each for the [ -d ] and
reclaim mutants) — but that pins SPELLING, not semantics.

The demonstrating mutant: change -maxdepth 3 to -maxdepth 1 inside mcp_server_has_deps.
It keeps every grepped literal, so packaging-parity passes 623/0 AND mcp-deps-preserve
passes 49/0 — while producing a real, inverse, operator-facing false claim. Against a
target with 3,371 files and 92 package.json whose servers demonstrably boot, it printed
'NOT RUNNABLE YET' and 'has no dependencies installed; this server cannot boot' for
both servers. Depth 1 misses scoped packages (@scope/pkg/package.json is at depth 3).

FIX: add a behavioural section to mcp-deps-preserve.test.sh that SOURCES
mcp_server_has_deps from the shipped install.sh (the file already does this extraction
for the four preserve functions — reuse that machinery) and runs it against three
fixtures: (a) a real tree with pkg/package.json, (b) a scoped-only tree with
@scope/pkg/package.json to pin the depth, (c) a 94-empty-directory husk. Add a META
mutating -maxdepth 3 -> 1 and assert fixture (b) flips.

WHY QA DID NOT WRITE IT: authoring an untested change to the implementer's spec at
approval time is the same shape that produced the husk defect (fixing F1 introduced
it), and it would have invalidated the 1,648/49/623 counts the approval cites. Correct
call — recording it here so the reasoning is not lost.

Context: the husk predicate exists because [ -d node_modules ] answers TRUE for a tree
a failed npm ci left as 94 empty directories. Both arms of that failure exit 3, so no
exit code discriminates — this defect family lives entirely in the readout, which is
why a behavioural test on the predicate is worth more than its severity suggests.

title: workflow-doctor Section 5c: FALSE_CLAIMS negative check is line-bounded (sed 1,120p) — a falsified absolute below line 120 escapes it

comments.author: username
comments.text:
Found by QA in C0a review iteration 2 (R2-F1, low). PROVEN BY MUTATION, not inferred: mutation M8 reintroduced a falsified absolute non-mutation claim at line 1391 of workflow-doctor.sh, and Section 5c's FALSE_CLAIMS check did NOT flag it, because it reads the header surface via 'sed -n 1,120p'.

Why it matters beyond the narrow miss: Section 5c is the anti-drift guard for R1-F1 — the falsified safety claim that blocked review round 1. Its whole job is to stop the docs and the code diverging a second time. One half of that guard (the negative/FALSE_CLAIMS direction) is scoped to the first 120 lines; the positive/disclosure direction is not. A guard with one line-bounded half is exactly the shape that reads as covering more than it does.

It is also the single place the spec departs from its own stated convention, which .claude/tests/README.md and LESSONS.md:31 both give as 'anchor on TEXT patterns, never line numbers'.

FIX: scan the whole file for FALSE_CLAIMS instead of 'sed -n 1,120p'. One token. Restores consistency with the convention and closes the escape.

NOT BLOCKING: below risk_threshold=high, and both operator-facing surfaces (--help and .claude/commands/workflow-doctor.md) are fully covered — the gap is only in the script header below line 120.

title: make lint does not cover .claude/tests/component/specs/*.sh — every L2 spec is unlinted by the canonical target
description:
Found during bjx (v4.1 U1). The Makefile lint target enumerates .claude/scripts/*.sh, .claude/scripts/tests/*.sh, install.sh and uninstall.sh — but not .claude/tests/component/specs/*.sh. There are now 38 L2 specs totalling several thousand lines of bash, none of them shellchecked by make lint. Specs written this release were lint-clean only because their authors ran shellcheck manually and said so; nothing enforces it.

Fix is a one-line glob addition, but check first whether the specs pass cleanly as a set — the L2 idiom (pre-sourced lib functions, inherited PASS/FAIL counters, deliberate unquoted heredocs in fixture builders) may need targeted disable directives, and a lint target that everyone learns to ignore is worse than one that is honest about its scope. title: bd-mcp integration test 'qa-gate lifecycle' is stale: approve refused (exit 2) because the test skips impact-report + review records
description:
Found while verifying claude-workflow-plugin-gz3 (v4.1 U1).

## Symptom
`cd .claude/mcp/bd-mcp && npm test` -> 28/29, one failure:

```
not ok 7 - qa-gate lifecycle: enter -> status (entered) -> approve -> status (approved)
  error: tool call should succeed: qa-gate.sh approve failed (exit 2)
  location: tests/integration.test.js:333
```

## Not a gz3 regression (proven)
Reproduced byte-identically on a pristine pre-gz3 worktree (`git worktree add --detach /tmp/gz3-prefix ee75125`, node_modules symlinked): same test, same `exit 2`, same 28/29. The gz3 change cannot be involved — the first approve in that test runs with `had_approved=0`, i.e. the untouched path.

## Root cause
`tests/integration.test.js:333` drives `bd_qa_enter` -> `bd_qa_approve` on a temp Beads repo with NO impact report generated and NO IMPLEMENTER / REVIEW-ARTIFACT records seeded. Since G2.n6d (impact-report freshness) and V3/jio.1 (review separation) `approve` refuses in that state, on purpose. The test encodes a pre-G2.n6d contract.

## Why it rotted unnoticed
`make test-ci` = `test test-component test-e2e-unit manifest-validate`. The bd-mcp suite is in none of them, so nothing runs it in CI or in the normal local loop.

## Fix sketch
1. Bring the test up to the current gate contract: generate an impact report and seed the review records (the L2 tier's `seed_review_records` in `.claude/tests/component/lib/fixture.sh` is the reference model — it goes through the real writers rather than hand-crafting comment text), then assert approve succeeds. Alternatively assert the REFUSAL explicitly, if the intent is to cover the MCP wrapper rather than the gate's happy path.
2. Consider adding `bd-mcp` npm test to `make test-ci` so the next drift fails loudly. Weigh runtime: the suite takes ~14s and needs a real `bd`.

title: workflow-manifest.sh hardening: mirror install.sh mcp dir-only semantics (R1-F1) + propagate find failures in scans (R1-F2)
description:
Two LOW-severity findings from the independent QA review of U0.1 (REVIEW-ARTIFACT v1 r1, reviewer qa-claude, both below the high risk threshold — advisory, non-blocking; recorded on claude-workflow-plugin-gzc).

**R1-F1 — latent mcp surface divergence** (.claude/scripts/workflow-manifest.sh:306 vs install.sh:538)
`scan_tree workflow ".claude/mcp" ...` walks every regular file under .claude/mcp (node_modules/.tmp pruned), while install.sh iterates only directories (`for mcp_dir in .../*/`). A loose top-level file ever added directly under .claude/mcp/ would be enumerated by generate but never shipped by install.sh, making classify emit a permanent copy-new for a file the installer cannot deliver. Vacuous today: no such file exists in the repo or the v3.5.0 tag (verified during review). Fix direction: scan per-subdirectory of .claude/mcp to mirror the dir-only loop exactly, or add a paired warning comment at BOTH sites (the same-commit pairing discipline the file header already declares). Add an L1 assertion: a loose file at .claude/mcp/top-level.txt in the synthetic tree must NOT appear in generate output (or must, if the installer is changed to ship it — pick one and pin it).

**R1-F2 — find failures invisible in process substitution** (.claude/scripts/workflow-manifest.sh:249 and :282)
`find ... -print0 2>/dev/null` runs inside `< <(...)`; a find failure (e.g. unreadable subdirectory mid-walk) is discarded — set -e never sees it, and the affected rows are silently omitted. The unreadable-FILE case, by contrast, fails loud with zero stdout and is pinned by L1 Section 4c. This weakens the all-or-nothing manifest contract for pathological inputs only (generate sources are release archives/checkouts; the frozen-table cmp would catch omissions on the shipped surface). Fix direction: propagate find's status via an exit-marker file (e.g. `find ... || : > "$WORK_DIR/find-failed"` then die after the loop when the marker exists), or drop 2>/dev/null and assert stderr-clean in tests. Add an L1 case with an unreadable SUBDIRECTORY (chmod 000 dir, same root-skip probe as Section 4c).

Both fixes must keep the determinism contract (byte-identical output on the happy path) and re-run the frozen-table reproduction check (`git archive v3.5.0 | ... | cmp - manifests/v3.5.0.sha256`) since U0 later specs byte-compare generate output.
acceptance_criteria:
- R1-F1 closed one of two ways, decided and documented: scan mirrors install.sh's dir-only mcp loop (with L1 loose-file assertion), or paired warning comments landed at both sites in the same commit.
- R1-F2: a find failure during scan_flat/scan_tree aborts generate/classify with a named error and ZERO bytes on stdout (same contract as hash failure); L1 unreadable-subdirectory case added with root-skip probe.
- Happy-path output byte-identical to pre-change (frozen v3.5.0 table still cmp-clean against tag regeneration).
- Full make test + make lint green.

title: review-check.sh gate: greedy sed reads the LAST findings=[...] token on the artifact line (TS invariant reads the FIRST) — harden to first-token
description:
Found during jio.2 QA parity review of the shell predicate vs the new `approval-cites-independent-review` TS invariant.

`review-check.sh` line ~376 extracts the findings token with:

```
ART_FINDINGS=$(printf '%s' "$art" | sed -nE 's/.*findings=\[([^]]*)\].*/\1/p')
```

The greedy `.*` prefix means that if the artifact line ever contained a SECOND `findings=[...]` substring after the genuine one (grammar position: `findings=[...] at <ts>: <summary>`), the shell would read the LAST occurrence while the TS invariant (`invariants.ts`, `/findings=\[([^\]]*)\]/` first match) reads the FIRST — the genuine token per grammar.

NOT currently exploitable through the shipped writer: `qa-gate.sh review-record` generates the summary from fixed strings ("approve — no findings at/above <t>" / "findings — N finding(s) reported"), so no free-form text reaches the artifact line. A hand-written `bd comments add` forgery is the documented threat boundary (jio.1) and out of scope. This is defense-in-depth so the two implementations of the predicate agree even on adversarial input: change the sed to non-greedy first-token semantics (e.g. `grep -oE 'findings=\[[^]]*\]' | head -1`) and add an L1 case with a two-token line pinning first-token wins.

The live invariant would surface any real-world divergence as a shell-says-clean / TS-says-open disagreement — which is the designed second-witness effect, but the counter itself should not be spoofable.

title: Bug: signup route returns 404 instead of 500 when the data-access layer throws a falsy value
description:
Discovered during QA of 40c.1 via independent fault-injection probing (7 error shapes fuzzed through the 500 path).

ROOT CAUSE: server/src/routes/signup.js outer catch does 'return next(err)'. When the store (or any downstream) throws a FALSY value (null/undefined/0/''/false), Express treats next(falsy) as next() — i.e. 'continue routing' — so the request SKIPS the central error handler in app.js and falls through to the catch-all 404 (not_found) instead of the intended 500 (internal_error).

REACHABILITY: NOT reachable today. The in-memory store throws only EmailTakenError; validateSignup guarantees password is a string before hashPassword (so its TypeError cannot fire); and node-postgres rejects with Error objects. This is a defense-in-depth gap in the 'every unexpected failure funnels to a leak-free 500' invariant, most relevant when the Postgres-backed store lands (claude-workflow-plugin-5x8).

IMPACT: LOW. No information disclosure — the 404 body is a static structured envelope with no internals/stack/secret (fuzz-verified). Only the status code and error code are 'wrong' (404 not_found vs 500 internal_error).

FIX (one line): normalize non-Error throws in the route's outer catch, e.g. 'return next(err instanceof Error ? err : new Error("non-error thrown in signup"));'. Add a regression test that injects a falsy throw from store.insert and asserts 500 + internal_error. Best handled alongside 5x8.

title: Mutation sweep does not halt on SIGINT when slow test in flight; cleanup still correct
description:
Phase C.1 mutation harness usability finding (not a containment safety defect).

Behaviour: when the per-mutant test command is slow (e.g. sleep 30, an infinite-loop mutant), pressing Ctrl+C (SIGINT) on the sweep PID does NOT cause it to exit. The sweep continues processing all remaining mutants. The trap fires at script exit (via EXIT), and worktree cleanup IS correct — both the .claude/.mutation-worktrees/ dir and the git worktree registry end up clean.

Root cause: bash defers SIGINT delivery while waiting on a child process. The mutation-sweep's main for-loop calls run_mutant per mutant, which runs the test in a (subshell). When SIGINT arrives during the subshell wait, bash queues it; once the subshell returns, the INT trap fires (which is the same handler as EXIT — cleanup_worktrees), but then control returns to the for-loop because the trap handler did not exit. Loop continues.

Probe evidence (all timestamps UTC):
- t=0: sweep launched with --test-cmd 'sleep 30' --max-mutants 3
- t=3s: worktree m-...-1 visible
- t=5s: SIGINT sent
- t=35s: trap fired once (wt=1); but loop continued — second worktree created
- t=65s: trap fired again (wt=2)
- t=95s: sweep exited naturally after all 3 mutants done; final trap with wt=3

Containment guarantees HOLD: trap runs at exit, no leak. Main tree intact (HEAD + tracked file hashes unchanged across the run).

Fix: in run_mutant or the wrapping for-loop, after each iteration, check if SIGINT has been received and exit early. Bash-idiomatic approach:

  INT_FLAG=0
  trap 'INT_FLAG=1; cleanup_worktrees' INT
  trap 'cleanup_worktrees' EXIT TERM
  ...
  while IFS= read -r line; do
      [ "$INT_FLAG" = "1" ] && break
      ...
  done

User-facing impact: a developer pressing Ctrl+C expects the sweep to stop NOW. Currently they have to wait for all remaining mutants. With a 60-mutant cap and a 60s per-mutant timeout, that's up to an hour of unwanted work after Ctrl+C. Not a safety issue, but the spec brief asked us to probe SIGINT behavior and this is what we found.

title: post-edit.sh:137-140 justifies its -n guard with a set -e abort that bash does not perform
description:
R3-F2 (low), measured by QA at review round 4 of 94d.

The comment at post-edit.sh:137-140 states the -n guard on WORKFLOW_SELF_WRITTEN_REGEX is 'load-bearing, not defensive noise' because with the lib absent the function is undefined and set -e would abort the hook — and a hook that aborts prints no envelope.

set -e IS on at :14. But bash exempts if-CONDITION commands from errexit. QA measured it: undefined function in an if-condition under set -euo pipefail takes the else branch, the script continues, rc=0. Without the guard the hook prints one stderr line and TRACKS the path, which is already the documented missing-lib behaviour at :74-77.

KEEP THE GUARD — it is still correct for stderr hygiene and for the rule-2 coupling. Only the stated mechanism is wrong, and it is wrong in the confident direction.

Same defect class as R1-F2 and R1-F3, both of which were fixed in the very round that introduced this one: prose asserting something the code does not do. Worth noting for the LESSONS ledger — a fix round that corrects three false comments and writes a fourth is evidence that comment accuracy needs a mechanical check, not more care.

The LESSONS observation this task carried — a round that corrected three false comments and wrote a fourth is evidence comment accuracy needs a mechanical check, not more care — is owed to Phase P item P8 (LESSONS scoping) and does not need an open task to be written.

title: LESSONS.md meta-finding entry says 1nz has "four instances"; there are five — the ledger is stale against its own source task
description:
Found during QA review of docs/v4.1-closure.md (claude-workflow-plugin-q7n).

## The discrepancy

`LESSONS.md`'s v4.1 meta-finding entry (sourced `claude-workflow-plugin-uvk`,
recorded 2026-07-30) reads:

> "live-repo assertions fail under any concurrent writer, including the Stop
> hook racing its own implementer (1nz, **four instances**)"

`claude-workflow-plugin-1nz` has **five**. Its third comment
(2026-07-30T14:32:34Z) opens "FIFTH instance, 2026-07-30, and it settles the
diagnosis: the assertion cannot hold during a review cycle BY CONSTRUCTION, not
by bad luck", and says "the failure mode is now fully characterised across five
instances".

`docs/v4.1-closure.md` §7 and §8 both say five and are correct. The ledger is
the stale artifact, not the closure document.

## Why it is worth fixing despite being one word

`LESSONS.md` is read by the orchestrator before every non-trivial
decomposition and is shipped to the grader in the Phase A grading packet. It is
also an `operator`-class row in the frozen release manifest, so editing it has
the side effect described in `claude-workflow-plugin-ce5` — worth batching with
that work rather than doing as a standalone commit.

A stale count in the institutional-memory ledger is a small instance of the
exact family the entry itself is about: a record reporting confidently on
evidence it did not re-verify.

## Fix

Update the entry to "five instances". Do NOT hand-edit — `LESSONS.md`'s header
says entries are added via `.claude/scripts/lessons.sh`, and the helper
dedup-merges by normalized text, so a corrected re-add creates a second entry
rather than replacing the first. The header does allow one legitimate
hand-edit ("pruning entries that are no longer relevant"); a correction is
arguably in that spirit, but confirm the intended mechanism before editing,
since this is the file whose edit-path discipline the ledger itself documents.

## Also noted, already covered elsewhere

`claude-workflow-plugin-uvk` closed carrying `qa-gate-entered` alongside
`qa-approved` — that is `claude-workflow-plugin-8zi` visible in a released
task's record. No new task needed; 8zi already tracks it.

title: Raise CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH above 1 WHEN a concrete workflow needs nested spawn (need-triggered, no date)

comments.author: username
comments.text:
Converted from a 30-day timer to a NEED trigger when 7be closed (2026-07-30). The previously recorded next-check date of 2026-08-23 is RETIRED — not live, nobody should act on it.

THE TRIGGER, stated as a condition: open this only when a concrete workflow requires an agent to spawn an agent. Not when a month elapses, not when the platform default changes.

WHY DEPTH-1 IS NOT A LIMITATION TO REMOVE: it is an enforcement mechanism. Because subagents cannot spawn subagents, an implementer STRUCTURALLY CANNOT PROCURE ITS OWN REVIEW. Grader and reviewer spawns must originate at the root — precisely the separation the gate's independence predicate exists to guarantee. Raising the pin would mean writing a parent-role guard to restore in software a property the platform gives for free, to enable nesting no workflow here needs.

THE ONLY CANDIDATE EDGE is QA -> grader, and it already works as a root-orchestrated relay (qa.md section 6, orchestrator.md section 5a), pinned by no-nested-spawn-instructions.test.sh. Even the one plausible use case is already served.

PIN SITES if ever raised: settings.json:8, asserted by platform-audit.test.sh:79, warned by session-start.sh:259-271.

INSTABILITY RECORD — why a date was the wrong instrument: the platform default has moved three times in this project's lifetime (off -> a depth-1 assumption -> depth-3). A calendar check would have fired against whichever value happened to be current that week and told us nothing about whether we needed it. Re-date with 'npm view @anthropic-ai/claude-code time' if version history is needed; the changelog carries no dates.
